# Twine — public API reference for AI coding agents

> Generated by `cargo xtask llms-txt` from the rustdoc comments — do not edit by hand.
> Twine is a declarative, signal-driven GUI library in Rust for microcontrollers and
> desktops (`no_std` + `alloc`). Applications depend on the facade crate `twine`, which
> re-exports the other crates (`twine::view` = `twine_view`, `twine::widgets` =
> `twine_widgets`, …) and offers `twine::prelude::*`.

## How to use this file

This file is large: do not read it whole. Find the section you need, then read only it.

1. Pick a crate or module from the **Index** below; each entry gives the line where its
   section starts (`L1234`). Read from that line (e.g. offset 1234, limit 200).
2. Or search the headings, which always start a line and use full paths:
   - `^## crate twine_view` — a crate (its docs: concepts, features, an example)
   - `^### mod twine_view::modifiers` — a module
   - `^#### struct .*::Ui$`, `^#### trait .*::View$`, `^#### fn .*::run$`, `^#### enum`,
     `^#### const`, `^#### macro`, `^#### type` — one item
   - a method or field: search `fn <name>(` (methods) or `` `<name>: `` (fields).
3. An item section is: `#### <kind> <path>`, a signature in a code span, the first
   paragraph of its docs, then bullets for fields/variants/methods (signature — summary),
   with `Errors:`, `Panics:`, `Safety:` notes and the traits it implements.
4. Paths are where an item is defined or first re-exported; through the facade the same
   item is `twine::<module>::…` (see the facade's re-export list at the top).
5. Documented with each crate's user-facing features, in the default build profile (the
   `safety` profile removes some items and widens handles; see `twine_core`'s docs).

## crate twine

Documented with features: `full,std,embassy,drivers,platform-std,drivers-fbdev,drivers-evdev`.

**twine**

Twine: a declarative, signal-based, low-power GUI library for embedded devices with the
feature set of LVGL, `no_std` + `alloc`.

This is the facade crate: it re-exports every Twine crate under a short module name and
gathers everything an application needs in `prelude`.

```rust
use twine::prelude::*;

pub fn counter(cx: Scope) -> impl View {
    let count = cx.signal(0u32);
    column((
        label(text!("Clicked {} times", count.get())).test_id("count"),
        button(label("Click me")).on_click(move || count.update(|c| *c += 1)),
    ))
    .gap(12)
    .padding(16)
    .align_items(CrossAlign::Center)
}
```

An application is a function run **once** that describes its widgets; dynamic values are
fine-grained bindings, so a change updates exactly the affected widgets and redraws
exactly their pixels, and an idle UI uses no CPU at all.

**Guides**

- Writing a custom widget: a gauge with its own class and parts,
  drawing, keypad/encoder input, theming with design elements and theme modes, a typed
  view, animations within the motion preference, and tests (the `gauge` example).
- Application state: the store pattern for large applications — a
  `Copy` struct of signals and memos with action methods, provided as context and read by
  any component; scoped stores, testing with `TestUi`, stores fed by ports (the `todos`
  demo and the `todo_list` example).

**Features**

The facade is the one dependency an application needs: every feature below is forwarded
to every Twine crate that has it (`cargo xtask layers` checks the forwarding).

- default: `color-rgb565`, `color-rgb565-swapped`, `img-qoi`, `perf-monitor`, `log`.
- `std` (host, simulator, tests: the thread-local reactive runtime), `log`, `defmt`
  (logging backends), `perf-monitor` (on-screen performance overlay), `debug-checks`
  (expensive engine invariant checks), `test-ids` (keep test ids in release builds).
- `async`: the async runtime (`AsyncUi`, `Ui::builder_async`), the async HAL traits, async
  drivers and `Outbox::recv` (await commands from the UI in any executor).
- `color-*`: pixel formats the renderer is compiled for (`color-i1` also compiles `L8`);
  `img-*`: image decoders (`qoi`, `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `bmp`, `lz4`).
- `platform-cortex-m`, `platform-riscv`, `platform-std`, `platform-embassy`: ready-made
  `Platform` implementations in `platform` (none by default: Twine assumes
  no OS, executor or chip).
- `embassy`: `embassy` (the `twine-embassy` crate: the embassy run loop; implies `async`
  and `platform-embassy`).
- `drivers`: `drivers` (the `twine-drivers` crate); `drivers-<name>` for each driver, bus
  and input device (`drivers-spi`, `drivers-i2c`, `drivers-xpt2046`, `drivers-ft6x36`, …).
  A display panel's feature (`drivers-ili9341`, `drivers-st7789`, `drivers-ssd1306`, …)
  also enables the `color-*` feature its pixel format needs, so a panel can never be
  refused with `EngineError::FormatDisabled` for a missing format.
- Fonts of `fonts`: bundles `fonts-latin-small` (Montserrat 12–16 px),
  `fonts-latin-medium` (12–24 px), `fonts-latin-all`, `fonts-mono` (unscii), `fonts-rtl`
  (Hebrew, Arabic, Persian), `fonts-cjk`, `fonts-all`; and one feature per font
  (`montserrat-20`, `unscii-8`, …) for precise flash budgets.
- `include-assets`: `include_font!` and `include_image!`, bitmap fonts and images
  generated from TrueType/OpenType and PNG/JPEG/… files while the application compiles
  (host-only proc macros; a build script with the `twine-build` crate does the same for
  many assets, and subsets fonts to the characters of the translations).
- `bidi`, `arabic-shaping`: right-to-left and Arabic/Persian text; `ttf`: runtime TrueType
  fonts; `fs`: the file system (`fs` module) and file images; `vector`: vector graphics
  (`vector` module, `vector_canvas`); `svg`: SVG images drawn as vectors (implies
  `vector`).
- Themes (`theme`): `theme-lvgl` (default; `Lvgl`, LVGL's default theme), `theme-mono`
  (`Mono`, 1-bit displays), `theme-simple` (`Simple`). A display's theme is a `static`
  named in the application (`AppConfig::new().theme(&lvgl::THEME)`): a theme, a mode table
  or a style is linked only when it is named; the features only compile them.
- `full`: every optional, platform-neutral part above (all pixel formats, decoders, fonts,
  the three themes, `vector`, `svg`, `ttf`, `include-assets`, `fs`, `bidi`, `arabic-shaping`, `async`, `perf-monitor`, `display-integrity`) — for
  hosts, simulators, tests and documentation. It leaves out `std`, the logging backends,
  platforms, drivers and the debugging aids; firmware enables only what it uses.

- `safety`: the safety profile (not in `default` or `full`).
- `display-integrity`: frame observers, region checks against the panel's read-back,
  safety-critical nodes, the fail-safe screen and the `Validity` looks
  (`docs/safety/profile.md` § 11); in `full`, implied by `safety`, otherwise not linked.
- `no-panic-runtime`: reactive failures that can be skipped (a write to a disposed signal, a
  creation in a disposed scope or a full arena, a memo cycle) raise a fault instead of
  panicking (`reactive` crate docs § Failures); implied by `safety`.
- `partitions`: two partitioned runtimes instead of one
  (not in `default` or `full`, not implied by `safety`; zero cost without it).

Firmware that offers alternatives as its own cargo features (one display of several, at
most one touch controller) checks their combinations with `feature_rules!`.

**Safety profile**

The `safety` feature selects the profile for certifiable products (bounded, observable,
analysable behaviour; `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository is the reference):

- **Excluded parts are compile errors**, not silent omissions: the performance overlay
  (`perf-monitor`, a default feature, so depend on `twine` with `default-features = false`),
  the file system (`fs`, and the `twine-fs` crate), run-time TrueType fonts (`ttf`, a
  floating-point rasterizer), the JPEG decoder (`img-jpeg`), `full`, and the `twine-lottie`
  crate (floating point, run-time JSON). Everything else (drivers, platforms, `vector`,
  `svg`, the other decoders, fonts, `bidi`, `async`, `embassy`) is available.
- **Library code is linted** for panics, unchecked indexing, overflowing arithmetic and
  floating point (`clippy::{indexing_slicing, unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, unreachable,
  arithmetic_side_effects, float_arithmetic}` denied; crates with remaining sites carry a
  tracked allow-list whose counts the repository's CI ratchets down). Every remaining panic
  site is listed in the panic inventory (`docs/safety/panics.md`).
- **No panicking convenience APIs**: `UiBuilder::build`, `Scope::expect_context` and
  `expect_navigator` do not exist in the profile; use `try_build`, `use_context` and
  `use_navigator`, which return a `Result`.
- **No-panic reactive runtime** (`no-panic-runtime`): a write to a disposed signal, a
  creation in a disposed scope or beyond its limit and a memo cycle are skipped with a `warn!`
  and a fault (`FaultKind::DisposedHandle`,
  `Capacity`, `MemoCycle`, `ReentrantAccess`); a read that has no value to return still
  panics (after the fault), and the reactive `try_*` forms never do.
- **Bounded memory**: every growing structure is bounded by
  `AppConfig::limits` (`Limits`; reaching a
  bound is a `Capacity` fault naming it, never growth), and the profile requires
  `preallocated` limits, reserved when the `Ui` is built.
  `Ui::seal()` ends start-up: Twine's growth points then report any allocation as
  `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal`.
  `AppConfig::audit_report` dumps the whole configuration
  (limits, caches, timeouts, features) as audit evidence.
- **Bounded time**: `EngineConfig::step_budget` bounds
  what one update renders (chunks and/or time; the rest of a frame continues in the next
  update, and an update past its time raises
  `FaultKind::FrameOverrun`), `on_chunk` feeds a
  watchdog between chunks, `Ui::timing` reports the worst update,
  render and flush times, and the recursion of drawing, hit testing and layout is bounded
  by `Limits::max_tree_depth` with a measured stack cost per level (CI-checked budget).
- **Display integrity** (feature `display-integrity`, implied by `safety`; not linked
  without it): a frame observer sees every chunk sent to a
  panel (`UiBuilder::frame_observer`), `Engine::check_region` compares a cache-free
  off-screen re-render with what the panel reads back
  (`FaultKind::DisplayIntegrity`),
  `ObjFlags::SAFETY_CRITICAL` nodes are drawn whole, without caches, transitions or
  ancestors' opacity, `Ui::heartbeat` feeds an external watchdog, `Ui::enter_fail_safe`
  switches to a static screen built at start-up (no allocation), and `Validity<T>` values
  show dashes and a cross-hatch when invalid (`docs/safety/profile.md` § 11).
- **Fault reporting** (`Faults`, the fault hook) is always on, in every profile.
- The firmware builds with `overflow-checks = true` and `panic = "abort"`, and its panic
  handler follows the contract in `docs/safety/profile.md` (record, put the display and
  outputs in a safe state, reset; never resume Twine).

```rust
[dependencies]
twine = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["safety", "color-rgb565", "img-qoi", "defmt"] }

[profile.release]
overflow-checks = true
panic = "abort"
```

`core::SAFETY_PROFILE` tells code whether it is built in the profile. Further run-time
guarantees of the profile (wide arena generations, bounded time, …) are listed with their
status in `docs/safety/profile.md`.

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### macro twine::feature_rules!
```rust
macro_rules! feature_rules {
    (@rule exactly_one $group:literal [$($f:literal),+]) => { ... };
    (@rule at_most_one $group:literal [$($f:literal),+]) => { ... };
    (@rule requires $feature:literal [$($f:literal),+]) => { ... };
    (@rule excludes $feature:literal [$($f:literal),+]) => { ... };
    (@pairs $group:literal [$head:literal $(, $rest:literal)*]) => { ... };
    (@pairs $group:literal []) => { ... };
    ($($rule:ident $name:literal : [$($f:literal),+ $(,)?];)+) => { ... };
}
```
Checks combinations of the **calling crate's** cargo features at compile time: each rule expands to `#[cfg(..)] compile_error!(..)` items, evaluated in the crate that invokes the macro, so a wrong selection is a compile error naming the features — not a link error or a misbehaving board. Nothing is generated when the selection is valid (no code, no flash).

### mod twine::guide::app_state

Application state: the store pattern for large applications.

Small views keep their state in local signals (`let count = cx.signal(0)`). As an application
grows, state is shared by screens and components far apart in the tree — the current user,
settings, a list of alarms, the data a sensor task delivers — and handing it down as
arguments through every layer becomes noise. This guide shows the pattern Twine recommends for
that: a **store** — a `Copy` struct of signals and memos with **actions as methods** —
**provided once** by the root scope as a context value and **read by any component** with
`Scope::expect_context`. It costs nothing per frame
and keeps every rule of the state in one place.

The complete, runnable version is the `todos` demo (`twine_demos::todos`: a keyed list, a
"clear done" action, commands from a companion app through ports) with the `todo_list`
example (`cargo xtask sim todo_list`) and its tests (`crates/twine-demos/tests/todos.rs`).
Every code block below is compiled and run as a doctest.

**Contents:** 1. The store ·
2. Providing and reading it ·
3. Several stores, scoped stores ·
4. Testing · 5. Stores and ports ·
6. Cost and failure handling · Checklist

## crate twine_view

Documented with features: `std,async,svg,vector,theme-lvgl,theme-mono,theme-simple`.

**twine-view**

The declarative layer of the Twine GUI library: an application is a function
`fn app(cx: Scope) -> impl View` that runs **once** and describes a tree of widgets. `Ui`
builds that tree into the engine, and every dynamic value becomes a fine-grained binding —
a reactive effect that calls one idempotent widget setter — so a signal change runs exactly
the bindings that read it, invalidates exactly the pixels that change, and an idle UI does
no work at all (`Wake::Idle`).

```rust
use twine_view::prelude::*;

fn counter(cx: Scope) -> impl View {
    let count = cx.signal(0u32);
    column((
        label(text!("Clicked {} times", count.get())).test_id("count"),
        button(label("Click me")).on_click(move || count.update(|c| *c += 1)),
    ))
    .gap(12)
    .padding(16)
}
```

**Building blocks**

| Item | Role |
|------|------|
| `View`, `ViewSeq`, `AnyView` | descriptions consumed once by `View::build` |
| `BuildCx`, `WidgetView`, `widget_view` | building nodes; the generic widget builder every widget view wraps |
| `WidgetView::bind_after_children`, `bind_model`, `on_value_changed`, `event_value` | the pieces of a value widget's view: a value applied after its other settings, two-way binding, `.on_change` (the built-in views use them; so can custom widget views outside this crate) |
| `IntoProp`, `Prop`, `Icon`, `IntoText`, `text!`, `IntoModel`, `IntoVariant` | constant, signal, memo or closure property values (any type, converted with `From`); zero-allocation text; two-way bindings; a widget's variants |
| `#[component]`, `component::Modifiers` | components: a function becomes a view with a props builder, used like a built-in widget (`meter(rpm).range(0..=8000).padding(4)`) |
| `ViewExt` | flag, per-part / per-state style (`ViewExt::part`, `ViewExt::on_state`), style, theme class (`ViewExt::variant`, `ViewExt::role`), event and identity modifiers |
| `StyleExt`, `StyleScope` | one modifier per style property and shorthand (generated from the property table), on every view and in part/state scopes; colors, lengths, radii, opacities and fonts also take design elements (`design::SURFACE`) |
| `Scope::provide`, `Scope::expect_context` / `Scope::use_context`, `MissingContext` | context values: application stores (a `Copy` struct of signals and memos) provided by a scope and read by any component below it; allocation-free lookup, panicking or `Result` form (facade guide `twine::guide::app_state`) |
| `use_theme`, `ThemeHandle`, `AppConfig::theme` / `DisplayBuilder::theme` + `.mode(..)` | the display's `static` theme (fixed when the display is created); switch its mode (`set_mode`: light ↔ dark without rebuilding), read the mode and design element values (tracked) |
| `use_motion`, `MotionHandle`, `UiBuilder::motion` | the global motion preference (`Motion`: full, reduced, none), honoured by tweens, animations, style transitions, screen loads and scroll animations |
| `column()`, `row`, `grid`, `container`, `card`, `stack`, `spacer`, `scroll_view`, `Layout` | layout containers |
| `label`, `button`, `image`, `image_button`, `animimg` | core widget views |
| `bar`, `slider`, `switch`, `checkbox`, `arc`, `led`, `line()`, `spinner` | basic controls (value widgets take an `IntoModel`: two-way with a signal) |
| `textarea`, `keyboard`, `spinbox`, `buttonmatrix` + `btn`, `spangroup` + `span` | text and number entry (button matrix and keyboard maps are rows of buttons; a docked keyboard keeps the edited field visible), rich text |
| `dropdown`, `roller` (options: `IntoOptions`, `OptionsProp`; a `&'static` slice is stored without copying) | selection widgets (`twine-widgets-ext`) |
| `list`, `menu`, `tabview`, `tileview`, `window`, `msgbox` | containers (`twine-widgets-ext`) |
| `when`, `dynamic`, `for_each`, `virtual_list` (items: `IntoItems`, `Items`) | structural reactivity limited to one region; keyed collections with one item signal per row, updated in place |
| `NodeRef`, `ScopeExt` | the imperative escape hatch, tweens and animations of any `Interpolate` value (timed by an `AnimSpec`), timers, modals |
| `Ui`, `UiBuilder`, `UiCore` | the runtime: the update cycle, `Wake`, `StepBudget` |
| `Ui::timing`, `Ui::reset_worst`, `TimingReport` | worst-case update, render and flush times (bounded time evidence; the budget is `EngineConfig::step_budget`) |
| `UiBuilder::display`, `Ui::mount_on`, `DisplayBuilder`, `Ui::display_mut`, `DisplayMut` | several displays in one `Ui`: each with its own buffers, inputs, theme and application, updated by the same loop |
| `Ui::set_rotation`, `Ui::set_brightness`, `Ui::set_display_sleep`, `UiBuilder::display_commands`, `DisplayCmd` | display control at run time (rotation, brightness, sleep / wake), also from other tasks and interrupts through a command channel |
| `BuildReport`, `BuildFault`, `BuildError` | widgets that could not be created while mounting: the per-mount report and the error that fails the mount |
| `AppConfig`, `UiBuilder::app_config`, `UiCore::mount_configured`, `UiCore::mount_configured_with_waker` | the application's configuration (engine, limits, theme, motion, rotation, fault hook), one value for firmware, simulator and tests |
| `Limits`, `UiBuilder::limits`, `AppConfig::apply_limits`, `CapacityFault` | the memory bounds of everything that grows (nodes, tree depth, texts, handlers, timers, animations, reactive nodes and scopes, effects, queues, navigation, keyed lists, wakers, heap budget), enforced as `Capacity` faults, optionally preallocated |
| `Ui::partition`, `UiCore::partition`, `AppConfig::partition`, `Partition` | partitioned runtimes (feature `partitions`): independent UIs on runtimes of their own, sharing no state (`run` § Partitions) |
| `Ui::seal`, `UiCore::seal` | end of start-up: heap budget checked, then any allocation by Twine raises `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` (`twine_core::alloc_guard`) |
| `AppConfig::audit_report` | the complete configuration as stable `section.key=value` lines for audit evidence (`twine_core::audit`), ending with its CRC-32 digest |
| `Ui::heartbeat`; with the `display-integrity` feature `Ui::set_fail_safe`, `Ui::enter_fail_safe`, `UiBuilder::frame_observer`, `ViewExt::validity`, `ViewExt::safety_critical`, `ScopeExt::watch_fresh`, `INVALID_TEXT` (`Validity` texts) | display integrity: liveness, the static fail-safe screen, an independent frame monitor, data validity and its standard look (critical nodes and region checks: the engine's `ObjFlags::SAFETY_CRITICAL`, `Engine::check_region`) |
| `typestate` | the builder's required parts (runtime, clock / platform, draw buffers), checked at compile time |
| `run::blocking`, `run::blocking_with`, `run::LoopEvent` | the run loop over a `Platform` (bare metal, an RTOS task, a host thread) |
| `draw_buffers!`, `DrawBuffers` | `static` draw buffers sized at compile time and taken once (`UiBuilder::buffers`) |
| `LayerBuffer` | a `static` layer buffer taken once (`UiBuilder::layer_buf`), so the engine's layer buffer stays out of the heap |
| `Ui::memory_report`, `MemoryReport` | what the memory is used for: engine (tree, caches, layer and draw buffers), reactive runtime, command queues, waker pool |
| `navigator()`, `Navigator`, `expect_navigator` / `use_navigator`, `NavigatorView::restore`, `Leave`, `NavOutcome`, `ScreenAnim` | typed navigation: a stack of routes (an application enum) shown as screens with LVGL screen-load animations; push / pop / replace / pop-to / reset, leave guards, stack inspection and restore |

**How bindings reach the engine**

Views are built with the engine borrowed by the `BuildCx`. Later, handlers, effects and
timer callbacks reach it through `EngineAccess`: `Ui` lends the engine to the code it
runs (event handlers, effect flushes, timers, animations) and any code below borrows it
exclusively for a moment. A binding that runs without an engine (a signal written outside
`Ui::update`) re-queues itself for the next update.

**The rule:** the engine is available inside event handlers, effects, timers (and
animation and channel-message callbacks) and while building; elsewhere use the `Ui`
methods or post a message. Hooks that create something (timers, tweens, animations,
modals) and navigation defer their engine work to the next update. Engine side effects —
the cleanups of a scope disposed outside an update (stopping its animations, removing its
timers, closing its modals, deleting its navigator's pages), the `AnimController` methods,
`ThemeHandle::set_mode` and `MotionHandle::set` — are
queued on the `Ui` that owns the scope and applied at the start of its next update (a
bounded, allocation-free queue: see `UiCore` § Engine commands). The queue is bounded:
when it is full a command is dropped and the next update raises a
`FaultKind::Capacity` record with code
`CapacityFault::EngineQueue` (see `Ui::take_faults`); it never panics. Calls
that must return what the engine holds — `NodeRef::with_mut`,
`AnimController::is_playing` — return `None` / `false` without it and, in debug builds
(`debug_assertions`), log `warn!` once per call site (compiled out in release builds; see
`EngineAccess` § Diagnostics).

```rust
use twine_view::prelude::*;
use twine_widgets::label::Label;

static STATUS: Channel<&'static str, 4> = Channel::new();

fn app(cx: Scope) -> impl View {
    let r: NodeRef<Label> = cx.node_ref();
    // A message handler runs inside `Ui::update`: the engine is lent.
    cx.on_message(&STATUS, move |s| {
        r.with_mut(|l: &mut Label, cx| l.set_text(cx, s));
    });
    label("idle").node_ref(r)
}
// From another task or an ISR: post a message rather than calling `r.with_mut` there.
let _ = STATUS.try_send("busy");
```

**Allocation**

Views allocate while they are built (boxed closures, one reactive effect per dynamic
property) — once. Steady-state updates allocate nothing: text bindings format into the
label's own buffers (`text!`), setters that do not change a value do nothing.

**The runtime token**

The reactive runtime belongs to the execution context (UI thread or task) that took its
`Runtime` token: `Runtime::take()` once, early in `main`, and
hand it to the builder (`UiBuilder::runtime`); the `Ui` keeps it. The token is `!Send`,
so the compiler keeps the UI in its context — no `unsafe`, also without `std` (where the
runtime lives in a `static`). With `std` every thread has its own runtime, and
`Runtime::current_thread()` gives a test or host tool its thread's token at any time.

**Features**

`std`, `log`, `defmt`: as in every Twine crate.

`safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
`docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints, and no panicking
convenience APIs — `UiBuilder::build` (and the async builder's), `expect_navigator` and
`Scope::expect_context` are removed; use `UiBuilder::try_build`, `use_navigator` and
`Scope::use_context`, which return a `Result`. Implies `display-integrity`.

`display-integrity`: the fail-safe screen (`Ui::set_fail_safe`, `enter_fail_safe`), frame
observers (`UiBuilder::frame_observer`), `.safety_critical`, `.validity`, `Validity` texts
and `ScopeExt::watch_fresh` (`docs/safety/profile.md` § 11); off, none of it is compiled.

`partitions`: two partitioned runtimes (ADR-001): a `Ui` built with
`Runtime::take_partition(p)` runs in partition `p` with its own runtime, engine, limits,
faults, seal domain, step budget and heartbeat (`run` § Partitions,
`docs/safety/profile.md` § 13). Not implied by `safety`; without it there is one partition and
nothing of it is compiled into handles or the runtime.

#### struct twine_view::EffectCx
The context `Ui` passes to `Runtime::flush_effects_with`: a marker telling the runtime that this is a real flush (effects deferred earlier for lack of an engine are re-queued). The engine itself is reached through `EngineAccess`, which `Ui` provides for the whole flush.
Methods of `EffectCx`:
- `pub fn scoped<R>(rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_view::EffectCx) -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with a flush context while `engine` is provided through `EngineAccess`.
- `pub fn with_engine<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine) -> R) -> Option<R>` — Calls `f` with the engine (see `EngineAccess::with`).
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::EngineAccess
The scoped "current engine": lets code without an engine parameter — `NodeRef` `with_mut`, bindings, hooks — reach the engine while the `Ui` runs it.
Methods of `EngineAccess`:
- `pub fn provide<R>(rt: impl Into<twine_reactive::Runtime>, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Makes `engine` available to `with` while `f` runs (also when `f` panics, the previous state is restored). `rt` is the runtime of the calling context (a `Runtime` or a `Scope`). Allocates nothing.
  Panics: Never by itself; a panic of `f` propagates after the previous state is restored.
- `pub fn with<R>(rt: impl Into<twine_reactive::Runtime>, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine) -> R) -> Option<R>` — Calls `f` with the current engine, or returns `None` (without calling `f`) when there is none: outside `Ui`, or while an enclosing `with` holds it. `rt` is the runtime of the calling context (a `Runtime` or a `Scope`). Allocates nothing; never panics (unless `f` does).
- `pub fn available(rt: impl Into<twine_reactive::Runtime>) -> bool` — Whether an engine is available right now (one read of the ambient slot). `rt` is the runtime of the calling context. Never panics.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::AsyncUi<D: twine_hal::AsyncDisplayDriver, W: twine_hal::AsyncInputWait = twine_view::NoInputWait>
The declarative UI runtime on an async display: like `Ui`, but each frame is rendered chunk by chunk and flushed with `AsyncDisplayDriver::flush`; with two buffers the flush of one chunk (DMA) runs while the next chunk renders.
Methods of `AsyncUi`:
- `pub async fn update_async(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update (see `UiCore::update`), then the frame, if one is due: rendered chunk by chunk, each chunk's flush started before the next chunk renders. Returns when to run again. Never panics; a failed flush is reported to the engine (`FaultKind::FlushError`, `Engine::report_flush`) and its area redrawn later; a flush still pending after `EngineConfig::flush_timeout` is dropped and reported (`FaultKind::FlushTimeout`, `Engine::report_flush_timeout`; see `AsyncUi` § Bounded flushes).
- `pub async fn wait_input(&mut self)` — Completes when the input registered with `AsyncUiBuilder::input_wait` signals its interrupt (never without one, and never while the engine is still polling it — e.g. a pressed touch screen, which the engine reads on its own deadline); tells the next update to read the inputs.
- `pub fn waker(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The waker, set by channel sends and input notifications (`'static`, usable from interrupts and other tasks).
- `pub fn messages_per_channel(&self) -> usize` — Messages each channel delivers per update (see `Limits::messages_per_channel`).
- `pub fn set_messages_per_channel(&mut self, n: usize)` — Changes how many messages each channel delivers per update (see `Limits::messages_per_channel`; `0` counts as `1`). Never panics.
- `pub fn notify_input(&self)` — Tells the next update that an input device changed.
- `pub fn now(&self) -> twine_core::Instant` — The current time of the platform's clock (see `AsyncUiBuilder::platform`). Never panics itself (it calls the platform's `now`).
- `pub fn memory_report(&self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — What the UI's memory is used for, by part (`MemoryReport`), as `Ui::memory_report`; the async UI's own draw buffers are reported in `engine.draw_buffers_heap` / `draw_buffers_static`. Allocates nothing; never panics; O(nodes).
- `pub fn timing(&self) -> twine_engine::TimingReport` — The worst-case timings since start-up or the last `reset_worst` (see `Ui::timing`): the chunks this runtime renders count in `worst_render_us`, the flushes it awaits in `worst_flush_us`; `worst_update_us` is the update before them. Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn reset_worst(&mut self)` — Clears the high-water marks of `timing`. Never panics.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the UI belongs to, as `Ui::partition`. Never panics.
- `pub fn heartbeat(&self) -> u32` — The number of completed updates, as `Ui::heartbeat`. Never panics.
- `pub fn seal(&mut self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — Ends start-up, as `Ui::seal`: checks the heap budget against this report (draw buffers included), then seals the allocation guard of the UI's partition. Returns the report.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably.
- `pub fn take_faults(&mut self) -> twine_core::Faults` — The faults raised since the last call, clearing them (see `Ui::take_faults`).
- `pub fn fault_counts(&self) -> twine_core::FaultCounts` — Occurrences of every fault kind since start-up (see `Ui::fault_counts`).
- `pub fn last_fault(&self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> Option<&twine_engine::FaultRecord>` — The last record of `kind` (see `Ui::last_fault`).
- `pub fn set_fault_hook(&mut self, hook: Option<twine_engine::FaultHook>)` — Sets the function called for every fault (see `Ui::set_fault_hook`).
- `pub fn display_health(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayHealth>` — The flush health of the display (see `Ui::display_health`).
- `pub fn input_health(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_hal::DeviceHealth>` — The health of input device `id` (see `Engine::input_health`).
- `pub fn recover_display(&mut self)` — Recovers the display after flush failures (see `Ui::recover_display`).
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<(), twine_view::UiError>` — Rotates the display at the next update (see `Ui::set_rotation`): the async driver's `set_rotation`, or software rotation (needs `AsyncUiBuilder::reserve_rotation`). Wakes the UI.
  Errors: None in practice (an `AsyncUi` display is never a framebuffer display); the signature matches `Ui::set_rotation`.
- `pub fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction)` — Sets the panel brightness at the next update (see `Ui::set_brightness`). Wakes the UI. Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn set_display_sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool)` — Puts the display to sleep or wakes it at the next update (see `Ui::set_display_sleep`). Wakes the UI. Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn display_asleep(&self) -> bool` — Whether the display is asleep (a sleep request was applied by an update). Never panics.
- `pub fn display_info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — The description of the display: its current logical size and rotation. Never panics.
- `pub fn inactive_for(&self) -> twine_core::Duration` — The time since the last user input (see `Ui::inactive_for`), on the platform's clock. Never panics.
- `pub fn trigger_activity(&mut self)` — Records user input that did not come through an input device (see `Ui::trigger_activity`). Never panics.
- `pub fn display_driver_mut(&mut self) -> &mut D` — The display driver (e.g. to change the brightness of an AMOLED).
- `pub fn root_scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The application's root scope.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### struct twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, W = twine_view::NoInputWait, R = twine_view::NoRuntime, P = twine_view::NoPlatform, B = twine_view::NoBuffers>
Configures and builds an `AsyncUi` (see `Ui::builder_async`). The methods are those of `UiBuilder`, plus `input_wait`; the platform is an `AsyncPlatform` (`platform`) instead of a clock.
Methods of `AsyncUiBuilder`:
- `pub fn buffers(self, m: twine_engine::BufferMode) -> twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, W, R, P, twine_engine::BufferMode>` — The draw buffers, **required** (as for `Ui::builder`): `static` buffers declared with `draw_buffers!` and passed with `BufferMode::partial_double_from` (render one chunk while the other is transferred) or `BufferMode::partial_single_from`; any `'static` memory (`BufferMode::partial_double` / `partial_single`); or heap buffers (`BufferMode::alloc`, allocated only once the display has been accepted). Without buffers, `try_build` fails with `EngineError::InvalidConfig`; with `Full` / `Direct` it fails with `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch`.
- `pub fn input(self, d: impl twine_hal::InputDevice + 'static) -> Self` — Adds an input device read by the engine (see `UiBuilder::input`).
- `pub fn accel(self, accel: impl twine_render::DrawAccel + 'static) -> Self` — Attaches a draw accelerator that renders into the chunks of this UI (see `UiBuilder::accel`), taking ownership of it. Default: software only.
- `pub fn layer_buf(self, buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — Caller memory for the engine's layer buffer, as `UiBuilder::layer_buf` (typically a `LayerBuffer` static; without it the layer buffer is heap). A later call replaces it; shorter than 4 KiB fails the build. Never panics.
- `pub fn input_wait<T: twine_hal::InputDevice + twine_hal::AsyncInputWait + 'static>(self, d: T) -> twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, T, R, P, B>` — Adds the input device whose interrupt wakes the sleeping UI (e.g. a touch controller with its IRQ pin); it is also read by the engine like `input`. The device implements both `InputDevice` and `AsyncInputWait`; the `AsyncUi` waits for its interrupt in `AsyncUi::wait_input`.
- `pub fn platform<Q: twine_hal::AsyncPlatform + Clone + 'static>(self, platform: &Q) -> twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, W, R, Box<dyn twine_hal::AsyncPlatform>, B>` — The platform (required): a clone of `platform` becomes the `AsyncUi`'s clock and the timer that bounds every flush with `EngineConfig::flush_timeout` (see the `AsyncUi` § Bounded flushes), and `P::in_interrupt` the reactive runtime's interrupt probe (`twine_reactive::set_interrupt_probe`). Typically `twine_embassy`'s `EmbassyPlatform`; in tests, `twine_testing::MockPlatform`. A later call replaces it. Never panics; the clone is boxed once.
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — The theme of the display: a `static` theme, attached when the display is created (sets `AppConfig::theme`).
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — The mode the display starts in (sets `AppConfig::theme_mode`; example: see `theme`).
- `pub fn config(self, c: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — The engine configuration.
- `pub fn waker(self, waker: &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker) -> Self` — The `AsyncUi`'s waker, the application's own instead of a pooled one (see `UiBuilder::waker`).
- `pub fn fault_hook(self, hook: twine_engine::FaultHook) -> Self` — The function called for every fault (see `UiBuilder::fault_hook`).
- `pub fn limits(self, limits: twine_core::Limits) -> Self` — The memory bounds of the `AsyncUi` (sets `AppConfig::limits`; see `UiBuilder::limits`): applied when it is built, before anything is created.
- `pub fn motion(self, motion: twine_anim::Motion) -> Self` — The initial motion preference (see `UiBuilder::motion`).
- `pub fn runtime(self, rt: twine_reactive::Runtime) -> twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, W, twine_reactive::Runtime, P, B>` — The reactive runtime of the calling execution context (required; see `UiBuilder::runtime`): the `AsyncUi` keeps the token, which keeps it and every reactive handle of the application in this task. Never panics.
- `pub fn display_commands<const N: usize>(self, commands: &'static twine_reactive::Channel<twine_engine::DisplayCmd, N>) -> Self` — Applies the `DisplayCmd`s sent to `commands` from any context (see `UiBuilder::display_commands`); the `AsyncUi` applies them to its async driver between frames.
- `pub fn reserve_rotation(self) -> Self` — Reserves the memory software rotation needs in every rotation (see `UiBuilder::reserve_rotation`), for async drivers without hardware rotation.
- `pub fn app_config(self, config: twine_view::AppConfig) -> Self` — The application's configuration (see `UiBuilder::app_config`): replaces every setting it covers; the methods called afterwards refine it.
- `pub fn rotation(self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — The rotation the screens are designed for (see `UiBuilder::rotation`); the `AsyncUi` asks its driver before the first frame (software rotation needs `reserve_rotation`).
- `pub fn try_build<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::AsyncUi<D, W>, twine_view::UiError> where D: twine_hal::AsyncDisplayDriver + 'static, W: twine_hal::AsyncInputWait + 'static, R: twine_view::HasRuntime, P: twine_view::HasPlatform, B: twine_view::HasBuffers` — Builds the `AsyncUi` (engine, display, theme, inputs; `app` built once). Exists only once the runtime, the platform and the draw buffers are given (`typestate`).
  Errors: What only the device can tell: `UiError::Engine` with `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch` for `Full` / `Direct` buffers, `EngineError::BufferMisaligned` for misaligned caller memory, the engine's errors for the display and inputs. Heap buffers (`BufferMode::alloc`) are allocated only after the display has been accepted. `UiError::Build`: a widget of `app` could not be created (see `UiBuilder::try_build`).
- `pub fn build<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> twine_view::AsyncUi<D, W> where D: twine_hal::AsyncDisplayDriver + 'static, W: twine_hal::AsyncInputWait + 'static, R: twine_view::HasRuntime, P: twine_view::HasPlatform, B: twine_view::HasBuffers` — `try_build`, panicking on an error.
  Panics: When the engine rejects the display, buffers or inputs, or when a widget of `app` cannot be created. A missing runtime, platform or buffers is a compile error.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::NoInputWait
The input waited on by an `AsyncUi` without `input_wait`: never signals.

#### struct twine_view::BuildCx<'a>
The context views are built with: the engine, the parent new nodes go under, the reactive scope that owns the bindings created meanwhile, and the display.
Methods of `BuildCx`:
- `pub fn new(engine: &'a mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, scope: twine_reactive::Scope) -> Self` — A context building under `parent` with bindings owned by `scope`.
- `pub fn parent(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node new nodes are created under.
- `pub fn scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The scope owning the bindings and handlers created while building.
- `pub fn runtime(&self) -> twine_reactive::Runtime` — The reactive runtime the build runs in (the scope's: `Scope::runtime`), for `EngineAccess` and the runtime-wide operations of custom views. Free (zero-sized); never panics.
- `pub fn display(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayId>` — The display the nodes are built for (`None` for detached trees on an engine without displays).
- `pub fn engine(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn create<W: twine_engine::Widget>(&mut self, w: W) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — Creates `w` as the last child of `parent` (the theme styles it, then `Widget::init` runs) and returns its id.
- `pub fn is_dead(id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is `DEAD_NODE` (a widget whose creation failed; see `create`).
- `pub fn with_parent<R>(&mut self, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>) -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with `parent` as the parent of new nodes.
- `pub fn with_scope<R>(&mut self, scope: twine_reactive::Scope, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>) -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with `scope` owning the bindings created meanwhile.
- `pub fn build(&mut self, v: impl twine_view::View) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — Builds `v` under the current parent and returns its root node.
- `pub fn build_seq(&mut self, seq: impl twine_view::ViewSeq)` — Builds every view of `seq` under the current parent.
- `pub fn on_delete(&mut self, node: twine_engine::NodeId, f: impl FnOnce() + 'static)` — Runs `f` once when `node` is deleted (an engine `Delete` handler). The engine is available through `EngineAccess` while `f` runs (e.g. for cleanups that remove timers).
- `pub fn provide<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with the engine lent to `EngineAccess` (for code that reaches the engine indirectly while a build borrows it, e.g. creating effects that apply at once).
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::WidgetView<W: twine_engine::Widget>
The generic widget builder every widget view wraps: a constructor, build steps (modifiers) run in order right after the node is created, and children built last.
Methods of `WidgetView`:

When the node cannot be created (see `BuildCx::create`) no step runs and no child is built.

- `pub fn bind<T: 'static, M>(self, prop: impl twine_view::IntoProp<T, M>, set: impl Fn(&mut W, &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, T) + 'static) -> Self` — Wires any property value to a widget setter: constants are applied once, signals, memos and closures through a binding that calls `set` whenever they change.
- `pub fn after_children(self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>, twine_engine::NodeId) + 'static) -> Self` — Adds a build step run after the children are built (e.g. to arrange them).
- `pub fn bind_after_children<T: 'static, M>(self, prop: impl twine_view::IntoProp<T, M>, set: impl Fn(&mut W, &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, T) + 'static) -> Self` — Like `bind`, applied **late**: the value is first set (and its binding created) after every other build step and the children, in the order of the `bind_after_children` calls, wherever in the builder chain they were made.

- `pub fn range<M>(self, r: impl twine_view::IntoProp<RangeInclusive<i32>, M>) -> Self` — The value range.
- `pub fn angles<M1, M2>(self, start: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M1>, end: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M2>) -> Self` — The indicator's start and end angles (normally set from the value; for an arc used as a plain gauge).
- `pub fn bg_angles<M1, M2>(self, start: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M1>, end: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M2>) -> Self` — The background arc's start and end angles.
- `pub fn mode<M>(self, m: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets::arc::ArcMode, M>) -> Self` — Normal, symmetrical or reverse (the value grows counter-clockwise).
- `pub fn rotation<M>(self, r: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M>) -> Self` — The rotation of the whole arc (0° = 3 o'clock, clockwise).
- `pub fn knob<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — `false` removes the knob's styles and makes the arc not clickable (a display-only arc, LVGL `lv_obj_remove_style(arc, NULL, LV_PART_KNOB)`); `true` (the default) puts them back.
- `pub fn change_rate<M>(self, speed: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::AngularSpeed, M>) -> Self` — The maximum drag speed (LVGL default 720 °/s), e.g. `.change_rate(AngularSpeed::deg_per_s(360))`.
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(i32) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the new value whenever the user changes it.
- `pub fn color<M>(self, c: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::ColorValue, M>) -> Self` — The LED's color: a `Color` or a design element (default: the theme's `design::PRIMARY`, which follows the theme mode), constant, signal or closure.
- `pub fn brightness<M>(self, b: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Fraction, M>) -> Self` — The brightness while on, clamped to LVGL's `LV_LED_BRIGHT_MIN`…`MAX` (80…255 of 255, i.e. about 31 %…100 %: an LED is never fully black).
- `pub fn y_invert<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Mirrors the y coordinates (y grows upwards).
- `pub fn width<M>(self, w: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self` — The stroke width (`line_width`: pixels, a `Length` or a length design element). This shadows `StyleExt::width` on line views.
- `pub fn rounded<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Rounded line ends and joints (`line_rounded`).
- `pub fn dash<M1, M2>(self, w: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M1>, gap: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M2>) -> Self` — A dashed line: `w` px dashes with `gap` px gaps.
- `pub fn period<M>(self, d: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Duration, M>) -> Self` — The time of one turn (default 1 s).
- `pub fn arc_angle<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M>) -> Self` — The length of the chasing arc (default 200°).
- `pub fn long_mode<M>(self, m: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_text::LongMode, M>) -> Self` — What happens with text that does not fit (`LongMode`).
- `pub fn max_lines<M>(self, n: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — Limits the number of lines of a content-sized label (0 = unlimited). An `i32` like every count of the view API, so that literals infer (see `IntoProp` § Integer literals); a value outside `0..=u16::MAX` is warned about and clamped.
- `pub fn selectable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Lets the pointer select text: pressing and dragging over the label selects the characters between the press and the pointer (drawn with the `Selected` part's style). Turning it off clears the selection.
- `pub fn checkable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Makes the button toggle its checked state when clicked.
- `pub fn checked(self, checked: impl twine_view::IntoModel<bool>) -> Self` — The checked state: a plain value (the button owns it; see `on_change`) or a signal kept in sync both ways.
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(bool) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the new checked state whenever the user toggles it.
- `pub fn rotation<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M>) -> Self` — Rotation around the pivot.
- `pub fn scale<M>(self, s: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Scale, M>) -> Self` — Zoom (both axes; 256 = 1.0).
- `pub fn pivot<M>(self, p: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Point, M>) -> Self` — Pivot of rotation and zoom, relative to the image.
- `pub fn antialias<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Anti-aliasing of transformed images.
- `pub fn inner_align<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets::image::ImageAlign, M>) -> Self` — Alignment (and stretching, tiling) of the image inside the widget.
- `pub fn svg_cache<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Draws an SVG source from a raster cached once instead of from its vector paths (feature `svg`; faster redraws of static icons).
- `pub fn checked_images<M1, M2>(self, released: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_image::ImageSource, M1>, pressed: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_image::ImageSource, M2>) -> Self` — The images of the checked state (released and pressed).
- `pub fn disabled_image<M>(self, src: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_image::ImageSource, M>) -> Self` — The image of the disabled state.
- `pub fn three_slice<ML, M, MR>(self, state: twine_widgets::image_button::ImageButtonState, left: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_view::Icon, ML>, mid: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_image::ImageSource, M>, right: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_view::Icon, MR>) -> Self` — Three-slice images of `state`: `left` and `right` at the ends (optional: `()` for none, any `Icon`), `mid` tiled between them to fill the width.
- `pub fn checked(self, checked: impl twine_view::IntoModel<bool>) -> Self` — The checked state (with `checkable`): a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways.
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(bool) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the new checked state whenever the user toggles it.
- `pub fn repeat<M>(self, r: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_anim::Repeat, M>) -> Self` — How often the frames play (default: forever).
- `pub fn playing<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Plays while `true` (from the first frame each time it turns `true`), stops at the frame shown when `false`.
- `pub fn pages(self, pages: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> Self` — More pages (loaded by rows), kept hidden until loaded.
- `pub fn sidebar(self, page: impl twine_view::View) -> Self` — A sidebar page shown left of the main page; its rows loading pages are marked `CHECKED` while their page shows.
- `pub fn header_mode<M>(self, mode: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets_ext::menu::MenuHeaderMode, M>) -> Self` — Where the headers go.
- `pub fn root_back_button<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Whether the root page shows a back button.
- `pub fn title<MT>(self, title: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>) -> Self` — The title shown in the menu's header while the page is loaded (any `IntoText`; a dynamic title also updates the header of a loaded page).
- `pub fn page_ref(self, r: twine_view::MenuPageRef) -> Self` — Fills `r` with this page when it is built.
- `pub fn loads(self, page: twine_view::MenuPageRef) -> Self` — Clicking this row loads `page` (a `menu_cont` only; the reference may be filled after this row is built).
- `pub fn dir<M>(self, dir: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::Side, M>) -> Self` — The side the list opens to (`Side::Bottom` by default). It flips to the opposite side when that has more room.
- `pub fn symbol<M>(self, icon: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_view::Icon, M>) -> Self` — The symbol at the side (`Symbol::Down` by default): a `Symbol`, an image, or `()` for none (any `Icon`).
- `pub fn text<MT>(self, text: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>) -> Self` — A fixed text on the button instead of the selected option (e.g. a menu title; any `IntoText`).
- `pub fn highlight<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Highlights the selected option in the open list (on by default).
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(usize) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the index of the option the user chose.
- `pub fn mode<M>(self, mode: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode, M>) -> Self` — Normal (ends at the first and last option) or infinite (the options repeat).
- `pub fn visible_rows<M>(self, rows: impl twine_view::IntoProp<u8, M>) -> Self` — The height in rows (LVGL `lv_roller_set_visible_row_count`).
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(usize) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the index of the option the user chose.
- `pub fn mode<M>(self, m: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanMode, M>) -> Self` — Fixed size, content size on one line (`Expand`), or wrapping in a fixed width (`Break`). Sets the size styles like LVGL.
- `pub fn overflow<M>(self, o: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanOverflow, M>) -> Self` — Clip the text beyond the height, or end the last line with "...".
- `pub fn indent<M>(self, px: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — Indent of the first line in px.
- `pub fn max_lines<M>(self, n: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The maximum number of lines (`Break` mode; negative = unlimited).
- `pub fn bar_position<M>(self, side: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::Side, M>) -> Self` — Where the bar is (`Side::Top` by default).
- `pub fn bar_size<M>(self, size: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The bar's height (top / bottom) or width (left / right).
- `pub fn animated<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Whether switching tabs (by clicking or from the model) slides the pages (default on); off switches instantly.
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(usize) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the index of the tab the user switched to.
- `pub fn one_checked<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — At most one checkable button is checked at a time.
- `pub fn on_select(self, f: impl FnMut(usize) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the index of the button the user pressed (released, for `CLICK_TRIG` buttons).
- `pub fn selected(self, sel: impl twine_view::IntoModel<Option<u16>>) -> Self` — The selected button (the one pressed last, or highlighted by keys): a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways.
- `pub fn mode<M>(self, m: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_widgets::keyboard::KeyboardMode, M>) -> Self` — The key map shown: lower/upper case letters, special characters, a number pad or a user map.
- `pub fn custom_map(self, mode: twine_widgets::keyboard::KeyboardMode, map: &'static [&'static [twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::MapBtn]]) -> Self` — Replaces the map of `mode` for this keyboard: a `'static` table of rows of keys, each with its text and control bits (`MapBtn`; stored by reference).
- `pub fn docked<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Docks the keyboard to the bottom of its parent (keyboard avoidance): instead of covering the bottom of the parent, it reserves its height there, the parent's other children are laid out in the area above it (a page with `fill` shrinks), and the field being edited is scrolled into view after the layout pass that makes room — when the keyboard appears, when it changes size (a display rotation) and when it moves to another field (that causes no layout). Hiding the keyboard gives the area back. No engine code is needed in the application.
- `pub fn popovers<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Shows the pressed key enlarged above it.
- `pub fn on_ready<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self` — The OK key was pressed (`Ready`).
- `pub fn on_cancel<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self` — The close key was pressed (`Cancel`).
- `pub fn placeholder<MT>(self, text: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>) -> Self` — The text shown (greyed) while the field is empty.
- `pub fn one_line<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — One line: no line breaks, scrolls horizontally, Enter sends `Ready`.
- `pub fn password<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Shows bullets instead of the characters (the last typed one briefly).
- `pub fn max_length<M>(self, n: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The maximum number of characters (0 = unlimited). An `i32` like every count of the view API, so that literals infer (see `IntoProp` § Integer literals); a negative value is warned about and counts as 0.
- `pub fn accepted_chars<MT>(self, chars: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>) -> Self` — Accepts only the characters of `chars` (e.g. `"0123456789."`; any `IntoText`).
- `pub fn cursor_click_pos<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — A click moves the cursor to the clicked character (default on).
- `pub fn text_selection<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Dragging selects text.
- `pub fn on_ready<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self` — `Ready`: Enter in a one-line field, or the keyboard's OK key.
- `pub fn on_insert(self, f: impl FnMut(&str) -> Option<String> + 'static) -> Self` — Filters insertions: `f` gets the text about to be inserted and returns `None` to insert it, or `Some(replacement)` to insert that instead (an empty replacement inserts nothing). Deletions are not filtered.
- `pub fn range<M>(self, r: impl twine_view::IntoProp<RangeInclusive<i32>, M>) -> Self` — The value range.
- `pub fn digits<M1, M2>(self, total: impl twine_view::IntoProp<u8, M1>, sep_pos: impl twine_view::IntoProp<u8, M2>) -> Self` — `total` digits (1…10, leading zeros shown) with the decimal point after `sep_pos` digits (0 = none).
- `pub fn step<M>(self, step: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The step of one increment (a power of ten: the digit being edited). An `i32` like the value, so that literals infer; a value below 1 is warned about and counts as 1.
- `pub fn rollover<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Wraps around at the range ends instead of stopping.
- `pub fn on_change(self, f: impl FnMut(i32) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the new value whenever the user changes it.
- `pub fn header_height<M>(self, h: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The header height (default: the display's DPI / 2).
- `pub fn content_padding<M>(self, pad: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self` — The padding of the content area on all sides (the theme's by default), e.g. 0 for a tabview filling the window.
- `pub fn buttons<T: twine_view::IntoText<MT>, MT>(self, texts: impl IntoIterator<Item = T>) -> Self` — The footer buttons' texts (each any `IntoText`, e.g. a translation).
- `pub fn close_button<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — A close button in the header (a dynamic value creates the button and hides it while `false`).
- `pub fn on_button(self, f: impl FnMut(usize) + 'static) -> Self` — Called with the index of the footer button clicked.
- `pub fn on_close<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self` — Called when the close button closes the box.
Implements: Debug, View, ViewExt

#### fn twine_view::widget_view

#### struct twine_view::AppConfig
Everything about a UI that is the **application's** choice rather than the board's: the engine configuration, the memory bounds (`Limits`), the theme, the motion preference, the rotation the screens are designed for and the fault hook.
Fields:
- `engine: twine_engine::EngineConfig` — The engine configuration (refresh period, flush timeout and policy, caches, input timings, idle timeout, …). Default: `EngineConfig::default`.
- `limits: twine_core::Limits` — The memory bounds of the engine, the reactive runtime, the `Ui`'s queues, the navigation stack and the waker pool (see `Limits`), applied when the `Ui` is built (before anything is created, so preallocated storage is reserved first). Default `Limits::DEFAULT`. The runtime's share applies to the `Ui`'s partition only (every partition has its own runtime and bounds); the waker pool's share is process-wide (per thread with `std`): the last `Ui` built sets it.
- `partition: twine_core::Partition` — The partition this configuration is for (`Partition`, ADR-001): named in the audit report (`partition.index`) so each partition's evidence names itself. The `Ui` builders set it from the runtime token (`UiBuilder::runtime`); `apply_limits` refuses a configuration for another partition than the token's. Default `Partition::MAIN`.
- `theme: Option<&'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook>` — The theme of the (first) display: a `static` (one theme per display, fixed at compile time), attached when the display is created. Default `None`: no theme — set one, or the widgets get only their own styles (on every host alike). Further displays of a multi-display `Ui` bring their own (`DisplayBuilder::theme`).
- `theme_mode: Option<twine_style::ThemeMode>` — The mode the (first) display starts in. `None` (default): the theme's first listed mode (`ThemeHook::modes`). Switch it at run time with `ThemeHandle::set_mode` / `Engine::set_theme_mode`.
- `motion: twine_anim::Motion` — The initial motion preference (`Motion`). Default `Motion::Full`.
- `rotation: Option<twine_core::Rotation>` — The rotation the screens are designed for. `None` (default) keeps the display's own rotation (the one its driver was created with). `Some(r)` different from it is requested when the UI is built and applied before the first frame is drawn (`Engine::set_rotation`): by the driver in hardware (`MADCTL` panels), else in software — which needs `UiBuilder::reserve_rotation`, or the rotation is refused with `FaultKind::DisplayControl`. The simulator emulates it in hardware; `TestUi` rotates its in-memory panel.
- `fault_hook: Option<twine_engine::FaultHook>` — The function called for every fault (see `Engine::set_fault_hook`). Default `None`.
Methods of `AppConfig`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — The defaults: `EngineConfig::default`, `Limits::DEFAULT`, no theme, `Motion::Full`, the display's own rotation, no fault hook — exactly what a builder uses when it is given no `AppConfig`.
- `pub fn partition(self, p: twine_core::Partition) -> Self` — Sets `partition`: the partition this configuration is reviewed for. Needed only when the configuration is applied by hand (`apply_limits`, `UiCore::mount_configured`) to a runtime of another partition than `Partition::MAIN`; the builders set it from their token.
- `pub fn engine(self, engine: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — Sets `engine`.
- `pub fn limits(self, limits: twine_core::Limits) -> Self` — Sets `limits`.
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — Sets `theme`: a `static` theme (`static THEME: Lvgl = Lvgl::new();`).
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — Sets `theme_mode`: the mode the display starts in (a mode the theme does not list starts in its first mode instead, with a warning).
- `pub fn no_theme(self) -> Self` — Clears `theme`: the display gets no theme.
- `pub fn display_theme(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayTheme>` — The theme the (first) display is created with: `theme` starting in `theme_mode`. What hosts that create the engine themselves pass to `Engine::add_display` and its siblings (the builders, the simulator and the test harness do). `None` without a theme.
- `pub fn motion(self, motion: twine_anim::Motion) -> Self` — Sets `motion`.
- `pub fn rotation(self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — Sets `rotation` to `Some(rotation)`.
- `pub fn fault_hook(self, hook: twine_engine::FaultHook) -> Self` — Sets `fault_hook`.
- `pub fn configure_engine(&self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Applies the configuration to an engine and its `display`, for hosts that create the engine themselves (the simulator, test harnesses, custom loops; the builders call it): the fault hook, the motion preference and the rotation (requested only when it differs from the display's). The theme is not applied here: it is attached when the display is created (`display_theme`). `engine` is not applied here — it is what the host creates the engine with (`Engine::new`) — and neither are the `limits` (they need the runtime too: `apply_limits`, which `UiCore::mount_configured` calls).
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for an unknown display; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when a rotation is configured for a framebuffer display (see `Engine::set_rotation`).
- `pub fn apply_limits(&self, rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine) -> Result<(), twine_view::UiError>` — Puts `engine` into `rt`'s partition (`Engine::set_partition`: its growth is then noted in that partition's seal domain) and applies `limits`: the engine's share (`Engine::set_limits`), the reactive runtime's (`Runtime::set_limits`, for `rt`'s partition only) and the waker pool's heap bound (`WakerLease::set_heap_limit` from `Limits::max_heap_wakers`; process-wide, shared by every partition — the last `Ui` built sets it). With `Limits::preallocate` this reserves the bounded storage, so call it before anything is created (the builders and `UiCore::mount_configured` do). The `Ui`'s own bounds (engine queue, messages per channel) are applied by the mount. Idempotent; allocates only the reservation; never panics.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` with `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `Limits::validate` refuses the limits (nothing is applied) — in the `safety` profile also when they are not preallocated —, or when the configuration is for another partition than `rt`'s (`partition`: its audit evidence would name the wrong partition).
- `pub fn audit_report(&self) -> twine_core::audit::KeyValues<'_, twine_view::AppConfig>` — The complete configuration as `section.key=value` lines (see `twine_core::audit` for the format): `Display`, and `defmt::Format` with the `defmt` feature; or visit the entries with `Audit::audit` to store or transmit them without text. Sections, in order:
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Audit
