#### struct twine_view::Flex<W: twine_engine::Widget = twine_engine::Obj>
A flex container (`column()`, `row`, `flex`, `scroll_view`: a plain object; `card`: `Flex<Card>`). `Flex<Card>` (from `card`) is the same flex container on a `Card` node, so it takes the card look of the theme and every `Flex` method:
Methods of `Flex`:
- `pub fn wrap(self, on: bool) -> Self` — Items wrap into several tracks when they do not fit (`false` by default).
- `pub fn reverse(self, on: bool) -> Self` — Items are placed from the last child to the first (`false` by default).
- `pub fn justify<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::MainAlign, M>) -> Self` — Placement of the items on the main axis, like CSS `justify-content`.
- `pub fn align_items<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::CrossAlign, M>) -> Self` — Placement of the items across the main axis, like CSS `align-items`: inside their track and, with it, the track(s) in the container (LVGL's cross and track placement; use `align_content` afterwards to place the tracks differently).
- `pub fn align_content<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::MainAlign, M>) -> Self` — Placement of the tracks of a wrapping container, like CSS `align-content` (LVGL track placement).
Implements: Debug, View, ViewExt

#### struct twine_view::Grid
A grid container (`grid`).
Methods of `Grid`:
- `pub fn column_align<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridAlign, M>) -> Self` — How the columns are placed in the container.
- `pub fn row_align<M>(self, a: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridAlign, M>) -> Self` — How the rows are placed in the container.
Implements: Debug, View, ViewExt

#### enum twine_view::Layout
How a view arranges its children, set with `StyleExt::layout` on any view (typically a `container` or a `card`).
Variants:
- `None` — No layout: children are placed by their own position and alignment (`LayoutKind::None`).
- `Flex(twine_style::FlexFlow)` — A flex layout with this flow (`LayoutKind::Flex` + `flex_flow`).
- `Grid { columns: twine_style::GridTracks, rows: twine_style::GridTracks }` — A grid layout with these tracks (`LayoutKind::Grid` + the node's tracks).
Methods of `Layout`:
- `pub const fn none() -> Self` — No layout.
- `pub const fn row() -> Self` — A flex row without wrapping (like `row`).
- `pub const fn column() -> Self` — A flex column without wrapping (like `column`).
- `pub const fn flex(flow: twine_style::FlexFlow) -> Self` — A flex layout with any flow, e.g. `FlexFlow::ROW.wrap(true)` (like `flex`).
- `pub fn grid(columns: impl Into<twine_style::GridTracks>, rows: impl Into<twine_style::GridTracks>) -> Self` — A grid layout with `columns` × `rows` tracks, e.g. from `grid_tracks!` or `'static` slices (like `grid`).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_view::card
`pub fn card(children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Flex<twine_widgets::container::Card>`
A card: a `Card` node — the theme's card look (background, border, radius, padding and gap from the theme), applied by the theme to the card class explicitly, so a card looks like one whatever the theme does for plain containers — with its children in a column. It is a `Flex`, so `Flex::wrap`, `Flex::justify`, `Flex::align_items`, … and every modifier (`.padding(..)`, `.gap(..)`, `.layout(..)`) refine it. Applications restyle all cards with a recipe for `CARD_CLASS` in a design system extending their theme (`twine_engine::DesignSystem`, `type Base = Lvgl`).

#### fn twine_view::column
`pub fn column(children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Flex`
A flex column (no wrapping), transparent: no background, border or padding (LVGL `lv_obj` with the `transp` style), content-sized unless sized.

#### fn twine_view::container
`pub fn container(children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Container`
A plain object with the theme's container look (a card in the default theme) and no layout: children are positioned by their own position and alignment. Give it one with `.layout(..)`, e.g. `container(..).layout(Layout::row())`; for a card with a column of children use `card`.

#### fn twine_view::flex
`pub fn flex(direction: twine_style::FlexDirection, children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Flex`
A flex container along `direction`, transparent like `column()`; add wrapping and reverse order with `Flex::wrap` and `Flex::reverse`.

#### fn twine_view::grid
`pub fn grid<M1, M2>(columns: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridTracks, M1>, rows: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridTracks, M2>, children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Grid`
A grid container with `columns` × `rows` tracks, transparent like `column()`. The tracks are any track-list property: a `grid_tracks!` list, a vector, a `'static` slice, or a signal/closure (the grid is laid out again when they change). They are the local `grid_column_tracks` / `grid_row_tracks` style properties, so state styles and themes can override them. Place children with `grid_col` / `grid_row` and align them in their cell with `grid_align`.

#### fn twine_view::row
`pub fn row(children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Flex`
A flex row (no wrapping), transparent like `column()`.

#### fn twine_view::scroll_view
`pub fn scroll_view(axis: twine_style::Axis, children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Flex`
A scrollable column (`Axis::Vertical`, also for `Both`) or row (`Axis::Horizontal`) with scrollbars shown while needed, transparent like `column()`.

#### fn twine_view::spacer
`pub fn spacer() -> twine_view::Container`
An invisible item taking the free space of a flex container (`flex_grow(1)`).

#### fn twine_view::stack
`pub fn stack(children: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::Container`
A `container` whose children are all centered on top of each other.

#### struct twine_view::DisplayBuilder<S, B = twine_view::NoBuffers>
A display and what belongs to it: its draw buffers, input devices, theme, rotation reserve and `DisplayCmd` channel. `UiBuilder` configures its first display with the same methods; a `DisplayBuilder` describes a further one for `UiBuilder::display` or `Ui::mount_on`.
Methods of `DisplayBuilder`:
- `pub fn new(display: D) -> Self` — A display flushed from partial draw buffers (as `Ui::builder`): it needs `buffers` (checked at compile time).
- `pub fn framebuffer(display: D) -> Self` — A memory-mapped framebuffer display (as `Ui::builder_fb`); without `buffers` it uses `BufferMode::Full` (the driver's framebuffers).
- `pub fn buffers(self, m: twine_engine::BufferMode) -> twine_view::DisplayBuilder<S, twine_engine::BufferMode>` — The draw buffers (see `UiBuilder::buffers`: required for a partial display — at compile time —, never allocated implicitly). A later call replaces them.
- `pub fn input(self, d: impl twine_hal::InputDevice + 'static) -> Self` — Adds an input device of this display (any number; see `UiBuilder::input`). Pointer devices are fitted to this display and hit-test only its screens. Keypads and encoders join the `Ui`'s focus group (the engine's default group, created when the first one is added): the engine has one default group, so keypads of several displays share it.
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — The theme of this display (each display has its own theme and theme mode): a `static` theme, attached when the display is created and kept for its lifetime (one `static` can serve several displays). A later call replaces it. Without one, the first display of a `UiBuilder` takes `AppConfig::theme`; further displays get none.
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — The mode this display starts in (default: its theme's first listed mode; a mode the theme does not list starts in that one instead, with a warning). Switch it at run time with `DisplayMut::set_theme_mode`. (Example: see `theme`.)
- `pub fn reserve_rotation(self) -> Self` — Reserves the memory software rotation of this display needs (see `UiBuilder::reserve_rotation`).
- `pub fn display_commands<const N: usize>(self, commands: &'static twine_reactive::Channel<twine_engine::DisplayCmd, N>) -> Self` — Applies the `DisplayCmd`s sent to `commands` to **this** display (see `UiBuilder::display_commands`); every display can have its own channel. A later call replaces the channel.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::DisplayMut<'a>
Run-time control of one display of a `Ui` (`Ui::display_mut`): rotation, brightness, sleep, theme mode, health — independently of the `Ui`'s other displays. The setters record a request the engine applies at the next update between two frames, and wake the `Ui`. Never panics; allocates nothing.
Methods of `DisplayMut`:
- `pub fn id(&self) -> twine_engine::DisplayId` — The display's id in the engine. Never panics.
- `pub fn scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The scope of the application on this display (see `UiCore::display_scope`): the root scope for the first display. Never panics.
- `pub fn info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — The description of the display: its current logical size and rotation. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<(), twine_view::UiError>` — Rotates the display at the next update (see `Ui::set_rotation`). Never panics.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` with `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a framebuffer display.
- `pub fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction)` — Sets the panel brightness at the next update (see `Ui::set_brightness`). Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn set_sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool)` — Puts the display to sleep (`true`) or wakes it (`false`) at the next update (see `Ui::set_display_sleep`); the other displays keep drawing. Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn asleep(&self) -> bool` — Whether the display is asleep (a sleep request was applied by an update). Never panics.
- `pub fn set_theme_mode(&mut self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode)` — Switches the display's theme mode (`Engine::set_theme_mode`; e.g. dark on one display, night on another). The application on the display sees it through `use_theme`. Idempotent; never panics. (Example: see `Ui::display_mut`.)
- `pub fn theme_mode(&self) -> twine_style::ThemeMode` — The display's theme mode. Never panics.
- `pub fn health(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayHealth>` — The display's flush health (see `Engine::display_health`). Never panics.
- `pub fn recover(&mut self)` — Recovers the display after flush failures (see `Ui::recover_display`). Never panics.
Implements: Debug

#### type twine_view::DrawBuffers
`pub type DrawBuffers<const N: usize, const BYTES: usize> = twine_reactive::TakeOnce<[twine_hal::DrawBuffer<BYTES>; N]>`
`N` draw buffers of `BYTES` bytes each in a `static`, handed out once: the type `draw_buffers!` declares.

#### type twine_view::LayerBuffer
`pub type LayerBuffer<const BYTES: usize> = twine_reactive::TakeOnce<[u8; BYTES]>`
A `static` layer buffer of `BYTES` bytes, handed out once: give it to `UiBuilder::layer_buf` to keep the engine's layer buffer (opacity groups, transforms, blend modes) out of the heap.

#### struct twine_view::BuildError
Widgets could not be created while an application was built: each got `DEAD_NODE` (see `BuildCx::create`), and the mount's `BuildReport` recorded it. The parts that were created are removed again (see `UiCore::mount`).
Fields:
- `failures: u32` — How many widgets failed (each one's children were skipped and are not counted).
- `first: twine_view::BuildFault` — The first failure (usually the root cause).
- `last: twine_view::BuildFault` — The last failure.
Methods of `BuildError`:
- `pub const fn new(failures: u32, first: twine_view::BuildFault, last: twine_view::BuildFault) -> twine_view::BuildError` — An error for `failures` failed widgets, `first` and `last` among them.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error, From<twine_view::BuildError>

#### enum twine_view::BuildFailure
Why a widget could not be created while building: the stable `code` of its `BuildFailed` fault record.
Variants:
- `Capacity = 1` — A bound of the widget tree was reached (`Limits::max_nodes` or `Limits::max_tree_depth`); the engine raised a `Capacity` fault as well (its code tells which).
- `ParentGone = 2` — The parent does not exist (deleted while the view was being built).
- `Engine = 3` — Any other engine error.
Methods of `BuildFailure`:
- `pub fn of(e: &twine_engine::EngineError) -> twine_view::BuildFailure` — The failure of an `EngineError` returned by node creation.
- `pub const fn code(self) -> u32` — The stable numeric code (the fault record's `code`).
- `pub const fn from_code(code: u32) -> Option<twine_view::BuildFailure>` — The failure with code `code` (`None` for an unknown code).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_view::BuildFault
One widget that could not be created while building: why, and under which parent.
Fields:
- `cause: twine_view::BuildFailure` — Why the widget was not created.
- `parent: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The parent it was to be created under (`None` for a root).
Methods of `BuildFault`:
- `pub const fn new(cause: twine_view::BuildFailure, parent: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>) -> twine_view::BuildFault` — A failure for `cause` under `parent`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display

#### struct twine_view::BuildReport
The record of a build: how many widgets could not be created, and the first and the last failure. The mount of a `Ui` / `UiCore` owns one for the duration of the build, and every `BuildCx::create` failure under the application's root scope fills it — also the failures of nested builds that run while the application is mounted (e.g. the rows a `for_each` builds in its first run). A non-empty report fails the mount with a `BuildError` (`into_result`).
Methods of `BuildReport`:
- `pub const fn new() -> twine_view::BuildReport` — An empty report. `const`; never panics.
- `pub fn record(&mut self, fault: twine_view::BuildFault)` — Records one failed widget (the count saturates at `u32::MAX`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn failures(&self) -> u32` — How many widgets failed (each one's children were skipped and are not counted; saturates at `u32::MAX`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn first(&self) -> Option<twine_view::BuildFault>` — The first failure, if any. Never panics.
- `pub const fn last(&self) -> Option<twine_view::BuildFault>` — The last failure, if any. Never panics.
- `pub const fn is_ok(&self) -> bool` — Whether nothing failed. Never panics.
- `pub fn into_result(self) -> Result<(), twine_view::BuildError>` — `Ok(())` when nothing failed, the `BuildError` otherwise. Never panics.
  Errors: `BuildError` with the count and the first and last failure when any widget failed.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_view::UiError
Why a UI runtime could not be constructed: the engine rejected the configuration (display, buffers, inputs, rotation), or the application could not be built.
Variants:
- `Engine(twine_engine::EngineError)` — The engine rejected the configuration.
- `Build(twine_view::BuildError)` — The application could not be built.
Methods of `UiError`:
- `pub fn engine_error(&self) -> Option<&twine_engine::EngineError>` — The engine error, if this is one.
- `pub fn build_error(&self) -> Option<&twine_view::BuildError>` — The build error, if this is one.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, From<twine_engine::EngineError>, From<twine_view::BuildError>, Display, Error

The view of `dynamic`.

#### trait twine_view::IntoItems<T: 'static, M>
`pub trait IntoItems<T: 'static, M>`
The items of a `for_each` or a `virtual_list`: a `Signal`, `ReadSignal` or `Memo` of a `Vec<T>` (read in place with `with`: no clone of the list when it changes), a closure returning a `Vec<T>` (re-run when a signal it reads changes), or a constant `Vec<T>` or `&'static [T]` (e.g. a table in flash). `M` is an inferred marker, as for `IntoProp`.
Items:
- `fn into_items(self) -> twine_view::Items<T>` — The items.
Implemented by: twine_reactive::Signal<Vec<T>>, twine_reactive::ReadSignal<Vec<T>>, twine_reactive::Memo<Vec<T>>, F, Vec<T>, &'static [T], &'static [T; N], twine_view::Items<T>

#### struct twine_view::Items<T: 'static>
The items of a keyed collection (`for_each`, `virtual_list`), made by `IntoItems`.
Methods of `Items`:
- `pub fn new(read: impl Fn(&mut dyn FnMut(&[T])) + 'static) -> Self` — Items read by `read`, which calls its argument with the current items (the reads it makes are tracked by the collection's effect).
- `pub fn read(&self, f: impl FnMut(&[T]))` — Calls `f` with the current items (tracked when called inside an effect or memo). Never panics (beyond what the source panics with, e.g. a disposed signal).
Implements: Debug, IntoItems<T, twine_view::marker::Prop>

#### struct twine_view::WhenElse<V, V2>

#### fn twine_view::dynamic
`pub fn dynamic(f: impl Fn(twine_reactive::Scope) -> twine_view::AnyView + 'static) -> twine_view::Dynamic`
A region whose content is `f(scope)`, rebuilt whenever a signal read **by `f` itself** changes. Reads inside the built views (their bindings) do not rebuild the region.

#### fn twine_view::for_each
`pub fn for_each<T, K, V, M>(items: impl twine_view::IntoItems<T, M>, key: impl Fn(&T) -> K + 'static, view: impl Fn(twine_reactive::Scope, twine_reactive::ReadSignal<T>) -> V + 'static) -> twine_view::ForEach<T, K> where T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static, K: Eq + Hash + Clone + 'static, V: twine_view::View`
A keyed list: one row per item, identified by `key(item)`; `view` builds a row from a `ReadSignal` of its item.

#### fn twine_view::virtual_list
`pub fn virtual_list<T, K, V, M>(items: impl twine_view::IntoItems<T, M>, key: impl Fn(&T) -> K + 'static, row_height: i32, view: impl Fn(twine_reactive::Scope, twine_reactive::ReadSignal<T>) -> V + 'static) -> twine_view::VirtualList where T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static, K: PartialEq + 'static, V: twine_view::View`
A vertically scrolling keyed list of rows `row_height` pixels high, where only the visible rows (plus one) exist — the same API as `for_each`: `items` is any `IntoItems` (a signal or memo of a `Vec` is read in place, never cloned), `key` identifies an item, and `view` builds a row from a `ReadSignal` of its item.

#### fn twine_view::when
`pub fn when<V: twine_view::View>(cond: impl Fn() -> bool + 'static, then: impl Fn(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V + 'static) -> twine_view::When<V>`
Shows `then(scope)` while `cond()` is `true` (and nothing, or the `otherwise` branch, while it is `false`).

#### struct twine_view::AnimController
Controls a free-running animation created with `ScopeExt::animation`. `Copy`, like a signal; its state is owned by the scope that created the animation (once that scope is disposed every method does nothing and `is_playing` is `false`).
Methods of `AnimController`:
- `pub fn pause(&self)` — Pauses at the current value.
- `pub fn resume(&self)` — Continues after `pause`.
- `pub fn restart(&self)` — Starts again from the beginning (also after the animation ended or was stopped).
- `pub fn stop(&self)` — Stops the animation (the value stays where it is).
- `pub fn set_playing(&self, on: bool)` — Plays (`true`, resuming or restarting) or pauses (`false`).
- `pub fn is_playing(&self) -> bool` — Whether the animation exists and is not paused (`false` without the engine).
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug

#### struct twine_view::MotionHandle
The motion preference of the engine the `Ui` runs on (see `use_motion`): read it (tracked) and change it at run time. `Copy`.
Methods of `MotionHandle`:
- `pub fn get(&self) -> twine_anim::Motion` — The motion preference. **Tracked**: an effect, memo or closure property that calls it re-runs when it changes. Outside a `Ui` the engine's value is read untracked if the engine is available, else `Motion::Full`.
- `pub fn set(&self, motion: twine_anim::Motion)` — Sets the motion preference (`Engine::set_motion`): animations started from now on follow it, and running non-essential animations that would not end by themselves end when it becomes stricter. `get` returns the new value at once. Applied now where the `Ui` runs code (handlers, effects, timers, while building), else queued for the next `Ui::update`. Idempotent; never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### trait twine_view::ScopeExt
`pub trait ScopeExt: Copy`
Hooks tied to a `Scope`: everything they create is released when the scope is disposed.
Items:
- `fn node_ref<W: twine_engine::Widget>(self) -> twine_view::NodeRef<W>` — An empty `NodeRef`, filled by `.node_ref(r)` on a view.
- `fn tween<T: twine_anim::Interpolate + PartialEq + 'static>(self, source: impl Fn() -> T + 'static, spec: impl Into<twine_anim::AnimSpec>) -> twine_reactive::ReadSignal<T>` — A signal that animates towards `source()` whenever it changes, with the timing `spec` (an `AnimSpec`, or just a `Duration` for a linear one; its forward play is used: retargeting mid-flight continues from the current value). Any `Interpolate` value: numbers, colors, points, sizes, angles, scales, opacities. Idle once it arrived.
- `fn animation<T: twine_anim::Interpolate + PartialEq + 'static>(self, from: T, to: T, spec: impl Into<twine_anim::AnimSpec>) -> (twine_reactive::ReadSignal<T>, twine_view::AnimController)` — A free-running animation of any `Interpolate` value from `from` to `to` with the timing `spec` (duration, easing, delay, repetition, playback): its value as a signal and a controller. Starts when the scope is built (or at the next update).
- `fn interval(self, period: twine_core::Duration, f: impl FnMut() + 'static)` — Calls `f` every `period` (inside a batch) while the scope lives.
- `fn timeout(self, delay: twine_core::Duration, f: impl FnOnce() + 'static)` — Calls `f` once after `delay`, unless the scope is disposed before.
- `fn show_modal<V: twine_view::View>(self, view: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope, twine_view::ModalHandle) -> V + 'static) -> twine_view::ModalHandle` — Shows `view` in a modal on the display's top layer: a full-screen semi-transparent backdrop blocking the input below, the view centered, and a focus group of its own for keypads and encoders. Closed with `ModalHandle::close` (or when this scope is disposed).
- `fn use_theme(self) -> twine_view::ThemeHandle` — The theme switcher of the `Ui` (same as `use_theme`).
- `fn use_motion(self) -> twine_view::MotionHandle` — The motion preference of the `Ui` (same as `use_motion`).
- `fn menu_page_ref(self) -> twine_view::MenuPageRef` — An empty menu page reference, filled by `menu_page(..).page_ref(r)` (rows can load pages defined after them).
Implemented by: twine_reactive::Scope

#### struct twine_view::ThemeHandle
The theme of the `Ui`'s display (see `use_theme`): switch its mode, read the mode and the values of design elements. The theme itself is fixed when the display is created (one `static` theme per display, design §2.0a).
Methods of `ThemeHandle`:
- `pub fn set_mode(&self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode)` — Switches the theme to `mode` (light, dark, night, high contrast): the display takes the theme's design element table for `mode` and every node is re-resolved once (`Engine::set_theme_mode`); views are not rebuilt and no binding re-runs, except those that read `mode`, `modes` or `get`. Allocates nothing (the mode tables are `'static`). At once inside handlers, effects and timers run by the `Ui`; called elsewhere (between updates) it is queued and takes effect at the start of the next `Ui::update`. A mode the theme does not support (`modes`) is refused: the display keeps its current mode and a warning is logged; never panics.
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_style::ThemeMode` — The theme mode of the `Ui`'s display. **Tracked**: an effect, memo or closure property that calls it re-runs when the mode changes. Outside a `Ui` (a scope without one) the engine's default display is read untracked, if the engine is available; else `ThemeMode::Light`.
- `pub fn modes(&self) -> &'static [twine_style::ThemeMode]` — The modes the theme supports (`ThemeHook::modes`, e.g. all four for `Lvgl::new()`; empty without a theme). **Tracked** like `mode` (it is fixed for the display's theme), and read like it outside a `Ui` (empty if the engine is not available). Cycle through them with `ThemeMode::next_in` (example at `set_mode`).
- `pub fn get<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&self, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>) -> Option<T>` — The value the theme gives the design element `element` in its current mode (`None` if the theme does not define it, or the engine is not available — it is inside handlers, effects, bindings and while views are built). **Tracked** like `mode`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### fn twine_view::use_motion
`pub fn use_motion(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> twine_view::MotionHandle`
The motion preference of the `Ui` owning `cx`: read (tracked) and change it (`MotionHandle`). Set the initial preference with `UiBuilder::motion`.

#### fn twine_view::use_theme
`pub fn use_theme(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> twine_view::ThemeHandle`
The theme of the `Ui` owning `cx`: switch its mode, read the mode and design element values (`ThemeHandle`).

#### struct twine_view::MemoryReport
The memory of a UI by part: the engine (`EngineMemory`), the reactive runtime (`RuntimeMemory`), the engine command queues and the waker pool. From `Ui::memory_report`, `AsyncUi::memory_report` and `twine_testing::TestUi::memory_report`.
Fields:
- `engine: twine_engine::EngineMemory` — The engine: tree, render scratch and caches, glyph and image caches, layer buffer, draw buffers.
- `reactive: twine_reactive::RuntimeMemory` — The reactive runtime the UI runs on (shared by every UI on it).
- `engine_queues: usize` — The UI's engine command queues (one per display; see `Limits::engine_queue`).
- `waker_pool: usize` — Heap wakers of the process-wide waker pool (`WakerLease::heap_bytes`; 0 while every UI uses a static slot or its own `static` waker).
Methods of `MemoryReport`:
- `pub fn heap_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes of every part: the engine's heap, the reactive runtime, the command queues and the waker pool.
  Panics: Never for a report from `memory_report` (its parts are sizes of memory that exists); a hand-built value whose parts sum past `usize::MAX` overflows (a panic in debug builds).
- `pub fn static_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Caller memory (statics) the UI uses: a static layer buffer and static draw buffers (`EngineMemory::static_bytes`).
  Panics: As `heap_bytes`: never for a report from `memory_report`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### trait twine_view::IntoModel<T: 'static>
`pub trait IntoModel<T: 'static>`
Anything usable as the value of an editable widget: a plain value of type `T` (the widget owns the state) or a `Signal<T>` (two-way).
Items:
- `fn into_model(self) -> twine_view::Model<T>` — The model.
Implemented by: T, twine_reactive::Signal<T>, twine_view::Model<T>

#### enum twine_view::Model<T: 'static>
The value of an editable widget: owned by the widget (changes are reported through `.on_change`) or bound to a signal (the widget shows it and writes user changes back).
Variants:
- `Owned(T)` — The widget owns the state, starting at this value.
- `Bound(twine_reactive::Signal<T>)` — The widget displays the signal and writes changes back to it.
Implements: Default, Debug, IntoModel<T>

#### fn twine_view::bind_model
`pub fn bind_model<T: PartialEq + Clone + 'static>(cx: &mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>, node: twine_engine::NodeId, model: twine_view::Model<T>, show: impl Fn(&mut twine_engine::Engine, twine_engine::NodeId, T) + 'static, read: impl Fn(&twine_engine::Engine, twine_engine::NodeId, &twine_engine::Event) -> T + 'static)`
Wires a model to a widget: `show` displays the value (once for owned values, as a binding for bound signals); for bound signals, every `ValueChanged` of the node reads the widget's value with `read` (which also gets the event: widgets that send `ValueChanged` from their own event handler carry the new value in its parameter) and writes it back with `set_if_changed`. The widget setter's idempotency ends the round trip (the binding re-runs once and changes nothing).

#### fn twine_view::event_value
`pub fn event_value(ev: &twine_engine::Event) -> Option<i32>`
The value an event carries as `EventParam::Value`. Never panics; `None` for any other parameter.

#### fn twine_view::on_value_changed
`pub fn on_value_changed<T: 'static>(cx: &mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>, node: twine_engine::NodeId, map: impl Fn(&twine_engine::Engine, twine_engine::NodeId, &twine_engine::Event) -> Option<T> + 'static, f: impl FnMut(T) + 'static)`
Registers `f` for every `ValueChanged` sent to `node` itself, with `map(engine, node, event)` as argument (skipped when `map` returns `None`); the engine is lent to `f` through `EngineAccess` meanwhile.

#### trait twine_view::ViewExt
`pub trait ViewExt: twine_view::View + Sized`
The modifiers of every widget view: flags, per-part / per-state styles, relations, events and identity (the table of the view API). Every view also has the style modifiers of `StyleExt`: whole styles (`style`, static or heap) and the style-property modifiers (sizes and positions, spacing, colors, borders, shadows, text, visual effects, layout item properties), which set **local style properties** of the `Main` part; `part` / `on_state` give them a part or a state. Flag modifiers set object flags. Every value may be a constant, a signal, a memo or a closure (`IntoProp`); dynamic values become bindings whose re-runs with an unchanged value do nothing (the engine setters are idempotent).
Items:
- `type Widget: twine_engine::Widget` — The widget type of the view's root node (for `node_ref`).
- `fn push_op(self, op: twine_view::BuildOp) -> Self` — Appends a build step run right after the node is created.
- `fn op(self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_view::BuildCx<'_>, twine_engine::NodeId) + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Appends a build step `f(cx, node)`.
- `fn flag<M>(self, flag: twine_engine::ObjFlags, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Binds an object flag. A constant is set once; a signal, memo or closure becomes a binding. Never panics.
- `fn state<M>(self, state: twine_style::State, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Binds a state (added while the value is `true`). Never panics. See `on_state` for styling the state.
- `fn on_code<R>(self, code: twine_engine::EventCode, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Calls `f` for every event `code` of the node (the engine is available through `EngineAccess` meanwhile). Its result is ignored.
- `fn part(self, part: twine_style::Part, f: impl FnOnce(twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> Self (provided)` — Styles one part of the widget (e.g. `Part::Indicator` of a slider or bar, `Part::Knob`): `f` receives a `StyleScope` with every style modifier (`StyleExt`), setting local properties of that part. Constants are set once; signals, memos and closures become one binding each. Combine with a state through `StyleScope::on_state`. A view that uses no scope pays nothing for this; never panics (a part the widget does not draw is simply never read).
- `fn on_state(self, state: twine_style::State, f: impl FnOnce(twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> Self (provided)` — Styles the `Main` part while all of `state` is active, e.g. a pressed look (`State::PRESSED`) or a checked one: `f` receives a `StyleScope` with every style modifier (`StyleExt`). The look is applied when the node enters the state and removed when it leaves it. Never panics; a view without scopes pays nothing.
- `fn styled(self, selector: twine_style::Selector, f: impl FnOnce(twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> twine_view::StyleScope<Self>) -> Self (provided)` — Styles any part in any states (`Selector::part(Part::Knob).with_state(State::PRESSED)`): the general form of `part` and `on_state`. Never panics; costs one build step per modifier used in `f` and nothing otherwise.
- `fn align_to<W: twine_engine::Widget, MA, MX, MY>(self, base: twine_view::NodeRef<W>, anchor: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::Anchor, MA>, dx: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, MX>, dy: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, MY>) -> Self (provided)` — Places the node relative to the node of `base` (LVGL `lv_obj_align_to`), following it when it moves: next to it (`Anchor::BelowLeft`, …) or inside it (an `Align`, e.g. `Align::Center`). The reference must be filled (by `.node_ref(base)` on another view) before the layout runs; until then the relation is not set. `anchor`, `dx` and `dy` may be dynamic. Never panics.
- `fn hidden<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Not drawn, not hit-tested, ignored by layouts.
- `fn clickable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Receives pointer presses.
- `fn checkable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Toggles the `CHECKED` state when clicked.
- `fn scrollable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Can be scrolled.
- `fn scroll_momentum<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Scrolling continues with momentum after release.
- `fn scroll_elastic<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Elastic overscroll.
- `fn scroll_one<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Scrolls at most one snappable child per gesture.
- `fn scroll_on_focus<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Scrolls itself into view when focused.
- `fn floating<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Positioned by hand, ignored by the parent's layout and scroll extents.
- `fn ignore_layout<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Positioned by hand, ignored by the parent's layout.
- `fn event_bubble<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Events also go to the parent.
- `fn overflow_visible<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Children are not clipped to the node.
- `fn disabled<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Disabled: the `DISABLED` state (no input, disabled look).
- `fn scroll_dir<M>(self, axis: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::Axis, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Which directions can be scrolled (all by default; stop scrolling with `scrollable(false)`).
- `fn scrollbar<M>(self, m: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::ScrollbarMode, M>) -> Self (provided)` — When scrollbars are shown.
- `fn scroll_snap_x<M>(self, s: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::ScrollSnap, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Horizontal scroll snapping of the children.
- `fn scroll_snap_y<M>(self, s: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::ScrollSnap, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Vertical scroll snapping of the children.
- `fn focusable<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Keypad / encoder focusable: in the default focus group (and focused when clicked). Needs a default focus group (`Ui` creates one when a keypad or encoder is added); without one the node is only made click-focusable. Never panics.
- `fn on_click<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Clicked (released without scrolling).
- `fn on_press<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Pressed.
- `fn on_release<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Released.
- `fn on_long_press<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Long pressed.
- `fn on_long_press_repeat<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Repeated while long pressed.
- `fn on_focus<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Got the focus.
- `fn on_defocus<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Lost the focus.
- `fn on_value_changed<R>(self, f: impl FnMut() -> R + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — The widget's value changed (widgets with a value also have a typed `.on_change`).
- `fn on_gesture(self, f: impl FnMut(twine_style::Side) + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — A swipe gesture on the node, with the side it moved towards.
- `fn on_key(self, f: impl FnMut(twine_hal::Key) + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — A key sent to the focused node.
- `fn on_scroll(self, f: impl FnMut(twine_core::Point) + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — The node scrolled; `f` receives the new scroll offset.
- `fn on_event(self, code: twine_engine::EventCode, f: impl FnMut(&mut twine_engine::EventCx<'_>) + 'static) -> Self (provided)` — Any event with full access to the `EventCx` (the engine is reached through the context itself here, not through `EngineAccess`).
- `fn variant<M>(self, variant: impl twine_view::IntoVariant<Self::Widget, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Themes the widget as `variant` (design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.4): a typed choice among the theme classes of the widget type (`Variant`, e.g. `ButtonVariant::Tinted` on a button; a variant of another widget type does not compile). A theme that does not know the variant styles the widget like its own class. A constant is set once; a signal, memo or closure re-themes the node whenever the variant changes (an unchanged variant does nothing).
- `fn role(self, role: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Self (provided)` — Themes the node as `role`: a `WidgetClass` derived from the widget's class (its `base` chain reaches it), so a component or container gets a look of its own in every theme that knows the role, and its base's look in the others (design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.4). A role that does not derive from the widget's class is refused (warning; the node keeps its look).
- `fn test_id(self, id: &'static str) -> Self (provided)` — A test id for queries in tests and tree dumps.
- `fn node_ref(self, r: twine_view::NodeRef<Self::Widget>) -> Self (provided)` — Fills `r` with the node when it is built.
- `fn group(self, g: twine_engine::GroupId) -> Self (provided)` — Adds the node to focus group `g`.
Implemented by: twine_view::WidgetView<W>, twine_view::Flex<W>, twine_view::Grid, twine_view::Container, twine_view::VirtualList, twine_view::VectorCanvas

#### struct twine_view::ModalHandle
A modal opened with `ScopeExt::show_modal`, also passed to the modal's view closure (and provided as context in the modal's scope).
Methods of `ModalHandle`:
- `pub fn close(&self)` — Closes the modal (disposes its scope, deletes its nodes, restores the focus group) at the next effect flush. Closing twice, or after the opening scope was disposed, does nothing.
- `pub fn node(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The backdrop node (once shown).
- `pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool` — Whether the modal is open.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug

#### fn twine_view::expect_navigator
`pub fn expect_navigator<R: 'static>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> twine_view::Navigator<R>`
The `Navigator` over routes of type `R` provided by the enclosing `navigator`: the panicking form of `use_navigator`, a thin `#[track_caller]` wrapper for pages, which are always inside their navigator.
Panics: If `cx` is not inside a navigator over `R`, with `"context twine_view::navigator::Navigator<{R}> not provided"` at the caller's location (`MissingContext`).

#### enum twine_view::Leave
What a leave guard (`Navigator::on_leave`) decides about a navigation that would remove its page.
Variants:
- `Allow` — The page may be left (and deleted).
- `Deny` — The navigation is cancelled: nothing changes (`NavOutcome::Denied`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_view::NavOutcome
The outcome of a navigation request (`Navigator::push`, `pop`, …).
Variants:
- `Accepted` — The route stack changed (the screens follow at the next effect flush), or already was as requested (`pop_to` the current route).
- `Denied` — A leave guard of a page that would be removed returned `Leave::Deny`.
- `AtRoot` — `pop` / `pop_to_root` at the root page.
- `NotFound` — `pop_to`: the route is not on the stack.
- `Empty` — `reset` with no routes (the stack is never empty).
- `Busy` — Requested by a leave guard while it decides about another navigation (ignored).
- `Full` — The stack would be deeper than `Limits::max_nav_depth`: nothing changes, and a `Capacity` fault (code `NavDepth`) is raised.
- `Disposed` — The navigator's scope was disposed (logged with `warn!`).
Methods of `NavOutcome`:
- `pub const fn is_accepted(self) -> bool` — Whether the request was accepted (`NavOutcome::Accepted`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_view::Navigator<R: 'static>
A stack of typed routes shown as screens (see `navigator`), obtained with `expect_navigator` (or `use_navigator`, which returns a `Result`).
Methods of `Navigator`:
- `pub fn push(&self, route: R, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Shows the page of `route` on top of the current one with `anim`; the current page stays alive below (its state is kept for the way back).
- `pub fn pop(&self, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Goes back to the page below with `anim`. The top page's leave guards decide first; the page is deleted (its scope disposed) when the animation ends.
- `pub fn replace(&self, route: R, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Replaces the top page with the page of `route` (the old one is deleted after `anim`; its leave guards decide first). The depth stays the same.
- `pub fn pop_to(&self, route: &R, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Goes back to the topmost page whose route equals `route`, removing every page above it (their leave guards decide first, top first).
- `pub fn pop_to_root(&self, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Goes back to the root page, removing every page above it (their leave guards decide first, top first).
- `pub fn reset(&self, stack: impl IntoIterator<Item = R>, anim: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>) -> twine_view::NavOutcome` — Replaces the whole stack with `stack` (root first), e.g. after a logout, or to restore a saved stack at run time (`NavigatorView::restore` does it before the first page is built). Every current page is removed (their leave guards decide first, top first); only the new top page is built.
- `pub fn on_leave(&self, cx: twine_reactive::Scope, guard: impl FnMut(&R) -> twine_view::Leave + 'static)` — Registers a leave guard for the page that owns `cx` (the page's scope or one inside it): before a navigation removes that page (`pop`, `replace`, `pop_to`, `pop_to_root`, `reset`; not `push`, which keeps it), `guard` is called with the route that would be shown, and `Leave::Deny` cancels the navigation (`NavOutcome::Denied`).
- `pub fn depth(&self) -> usize` — Number of pages (0 once the navigator is disposed). Tracked.
- `pub fn current(&self) -> Option<R>` — The route of the top page (`None` once the navigator is disposed). Tracked; clones the route.
- `pub fn stack(&self) -> Vec<R>` — The route stack, root first (empty once the navigator is disposed): for tests and for saving the navigation state (restore it with `NavigatorView::restore` or `reset`). Tracked; clones the routes into a new `Vec`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug

#### struct twine_view::NavigatorView<R: 'static>
The view of `navigator`: an anchor node, plus `restore`.
Methods of `NavigatorView`:
- `pub fn restore(self, stack: impl IntoIterator<Item = R>) -> Self` — Starts with `stack` (root first) instead of the initial route, e.g. a stack saved before a reset of the device. Only the top page is built; the pages below are built when they are shown. An empty `stack` keeps the initial route. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, View

#### fn twine_view::navigator
`pub fn navigator<R, V>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope, initial: R, page: impl Fn(twine_reactive::Scope, R) -> V + 'static) -> twine_view::NavigatorView<R> where R: Clone + PartialEq + 'static, V: twine_view::View`
A navigation root over routes of type `R`: provides a `Navigator<R>` in `cx` (see `expect_navigator`) and shows the page of `initial` as the display's active screen. `page(scope, route)` builds the view of a route's page; it is called once per page, with the page's own scope, when the page is first shown. The view itself is an empty anchor node (the pages inherit their text style from it).

#### fn twine_view::use_navigator
`pub fn use_navigator<R: 'static>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> Result<twine_view::Navigator<R>, twine_reactive::MissingContext>`
The `Navigator` over routes of type `R` provided by the enclosing `navigator` (the innermost one for nested navigators of the same route type), or `MissingContext` naming `Navigator<R>` when `cx` is not inside one — the non-panicking form (see `expect_navigator` for application pages, and `Scope` § Context values for the convention and the lookup cost: a scope-chain walk, allocation-free). Look it up once when the page is built and move the `Copy` handle into its handlers.
Errors: `MissingContext` naming `Navigator<R>` when `cx` is not inside a navigator over `R`.

#### struct twine_view::NodeRef<W: twine_engine::Widget>
A reference to the node of a widget view, filled when the view is built (`.node_ref(r)`). `Copy`, like a signal (it is one: reading it with `get` inside a binding subscribes to it).
Methods of `NodeRef`:
- `pub fn new(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> Self` — An empty reference owned by `cx` (usually created with `cx.node_ref()`).
- `pub fn get(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node, once built (a tracked read).
- `pub fn get_untracked(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node without subscribing the running binding.
- `pub fn with_mut<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut W, &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>) -> R) -> Option<R>` — Calls `f` with the widget and a widget context for its node, inside handlers, effects and timer callbacks run by the `Ui` (the engine is taken from `EngineAccess`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### struct twine_view::Icon
An optional icon of a widget (a list button, a dropdown arrow, the side images of an image button…): `()` for none, a `Symbol`, an `ImageSource`, a `&'static` `Image`, or an `Option` of a symbol or an image source. Icon parameters are properties (`impl IntoProp<Icon, M>`), so a closure, signal or memo of any of these is a reactive icon (a dynamic `None` hides it).
Fields:
- `0: Option<twine_image::ImageSource>`
Methods of `Icon`:
- `const NONE: twine_view::Icon` — No icon.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, From<()>, From<twine_core::Symbol>, From<twine_image::ImageSource>, From<&'static twine_image::Image>, From<Option<twine_core::Symbol>>, From<Option<twine_image::ImageSource>>, From<twine_view::Icon>

#### trait twine_view::IntoProp<T, M>
`pub trait IntoProp<T, M>`
Anything usable as a property value of type `T`: a value converting into `T` (`Into`), or a closure, `Signal`, `ReadSignal` or `Memo` whose value converts into `T`.
Items:
- `fn into_prop(self) -> twine_view::Prop<T>` — The property value.
Implemented by: U, F, twine_reactive::Signal<U>, twine_reactive::ReadSignal<U>, twine_reactive::Memo<U>, &'static [T; N], twine_view::Prop<T>

#### trait twine_view::IntoVariant<W, M>
`pub trait IntoVariant<W, M>`
A variant of the widget type `W` for the views' `variant`: a `Variant` whose `Widget` is `W` (e.g. a `ButtonVariant` for a button), or a closure, `Signal`, `ReadSignal` or `Memo` of one. Like `IntoProp` (whose markers it shares), but the widget type picks the variant type, so `.variant(ButtonVariant::Plain)` needs no annotation and a variant of another widget does not compile.
Items:
- `fn into_variant(self) -> twine_view::Prop<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The variant's theme class, as a property.
Implemented by: V, F, twine_reactive::Signal<V>, twine_reactive::ReadSignal<V>, twine_reactive::Memo<V>

#### enum twine_view::Prop<T>
A property value: fixed, or computed by a closure that is re-run (as a binding) whenever a signal it reads changes.
Variants:
- `Static(T)` — Applied once, at build time (no binding is created).
- `Dynamic(Box<dyn Fn() -> T>)` — Re-evaluated by a binding effect.
Methods of `Prop`:
- `pub fn get(&self) -> T` — The current value: a clone of a constant, or the result of a dynamic prop's closure. Inside a binding, effect or memo the closure's reads are tracked like any other read, so a component can turn a property it uses in several places into a `Copy` memo:
- `pub fn map<U: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(T) -> U + 'static) -> twine_view::Prop<U>` — Maps the value (lazily for dynamic props).
Implements: Debug, Default, IntoProp<T, twine_view::marker::Prop>, IntoOptions<twine_view::marker::Prop>

#### trait twine_view::StyleExt
`pub trait StyleExt: Sized + Sealed`
The style modifiers: whole styles (`style`, `class_style`) and the style-property modifiers, one per style property and one per shorthand (generated from the property table of `twine-style`: the names are the `style!` keys and the `StyleBuf` builder methods, see `twine_style::PROPERTIES.md`), plus `fill` and the generic `style_prop` / `style_props`.
Items:
- `fn style(self, s: impl Into<twine_style::StyleRef>) -> Self (provided)` — Adds a whole style to the node: a `static` `Style` written with `style!` (`&CARD`, in flash), or a heap one — a `StyleBuf` (moved into an `Rc`) or a shared `Rc<StyleBuf>` / `StyleRef` (one style for many nodes, e.g. a theme's `styles()`). On a view it applies to the `Main` part in the default state; in a `StyleScope` to the scope's part and states (`.on_state(State::PRESSED, |s| s.style(&CARD_PRESSED))`).
- `fn class_style(self, s: impl Into<twine_style::StyleRef>) -> Self (provided)` — Adds a whole style with theme priority (below every `style` and local property, like the theme's own class styles), for the `Main` part on a view or the scope's selector in a `StyleScope`. Takes the same styles as `style`. Never panics.
- `fn style_prop<T: 'static, M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<T, M>, make: fn(T) -> twine_style::StyleProp) -> Self (provided)` — Binds a local style property built by `make` from the value (e.g. a `StyleProp` variant: `self.style_prop(w, StyleProp::LineWidth)`), for the `Main` part on a view or the scope's selector in a `StyleScope`.
- `fn style_props<T: 'static, M, const N: usize>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<T, M>, make: fn(T) -> [twine_style::StyleProp; N]) -> Self (provided)` — Binds several local style properties built by `make` from one value (a `fn` pointer, see `style_prop`).
- `fn width<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Width (`LV_STYLE_WIDTH`). Default `Content` (LVGL: widget class dependent).
- `fn min_width<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Minimal width (`LV_STYLE_MIN_WIDTH`); percent of the parent's content width.
- `fn max_width<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Maximal width (`LV_STYLE_MAX_WIDTH`).
- `fn height<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Height (`LV_STYLE_HEIGHT`). Default `Content` (LVGL: widget class dependent).
- `fn min_height<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Minimal height (`LV_STYLE_MIN_HEIGHT`).
- `fn max_height<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Maximal height (`LV_STYLE_MAX_HEIGHT`).
- `fn x<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — X position relative to the `Align` reference (`LV_STYLE_X`).
- `fn y<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Y position relative to the `Align` reference (`LV_STYLE_Y`).
- `fn align<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::Align, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Alignment in the parent (`LV_STYLE_ALIGN`).
- `fn transform_width<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Draws the object wider on both sides; percent of its width (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_WIDTH`).
- `fn transform_height<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Draws the object taller on both sides (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_HEIGHT`).
- `fn translate_x<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Moves the object after layout; percent of its width (`LV_STYLE_TRANSLATE_X`).
- `fn translate_y<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Moves the object after layout; percent of its height (`LV_STYLE_TRANSLATE_Y`).
- `fn translate_radial<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Moves radial items (e.g. scale labels) outward (`LV_STYLE_TRANSLATE_RADIAL`).
- `fn transform_scale_x<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Scale, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Horizontal zoom (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_SCALE_X`).
- `fn transform_scale_y<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Scale, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Vertical zoom (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_SCALE_Y`).
- `fn transform_rotation<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Angle, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Rotation (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_ROTATION`).
- `fn transform_pivot_x<M>(self, v: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, M>) -> Self (provided)` — Pivot of rotation/zoom from the left edge; percent of the width (`LV_STYLE_TRANSFORM_PIVOT_X`).

- `fn shadow_offset<X, Y>(self, x: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, X>, y: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::design::LengthValue, Y>) -> Self (provided)` — Shadow offset.
- `fn transform_scale<S>(self, scale: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Scale, S>) -> Self (provided)` — Scale of the rendered node on both axes.
- `fn transform_pivot<P>(self, point: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Point, P>) -> Self (provided)` — Pivot of the transformation in pixels, relative to the node.
- `fn grid_col<C>(self, columns: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridSpan, C>) -> Self (provided)` — Grid columns of the item: a column (`2`) or a range of columns (`0..2`), see `GridSpan`.
- `fn grid_row<R>(self, rows: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridSpan, R>) -> Self (provided)` — Grid rows of the item: a row (`1`) or a range of rows (`0..=1`), see `GridSpan`.
- `fn grid_align<X, Y>(self, x: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridAlign, X>, y: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_style::GridAlign, Y>) -> Self (provided)` — Alignment inside the grid cell (horizontal, vertical).
- `fn fill(self) -> Self (provided)` — Fills the parent: width and height 100 % of the parent's content area (padding excluded), i.e. `.size(Length::pct(100), Length::pct(100))`.
- `fn fill_width(self) -> Self (provided)` — Width 100 % of the parent's content area, i.e. `.width(Length::pct(100))` (a size, not a share of free space: see `fill`).
- `fn fill_height(self) -> Self (provided)` — Height 100 % of the parent's content area, i.e. `.height(Length::pct(100))` (a size, not a share of free space: see `fill`).
Implemented by: V, twine_view::StyleScope<V>

#### struct twine_view::StyleScope<V>
The style modifiers of a view for one part and/or state: what the closure of `ViewExt::part`, `ViewExt::on_state` and `ViewExt::styled` receives. It has exactly the modifiers of a view (`StyleExt`); they set local properties of the view's node for the scope's `Selector` instead of the `Main` part in the default state.
Methods of `StyleScope`:
- `pub fn selector(&self) -> twine_style::Selector` — The part and states the modifiers apply to.
- `pub fn part(self, part: twine_style::Part, f: impl FnOnce(Self) -> Self) -> Self` — Styles part `part` in the scope's states: `.on_state(State::PRESSED, |s| s.part(Part::Knob, ..))` is the same selector as `.part(Part::Knob, |s| s.on_state(State::PRESSED, ..))`. The innermost part applies (a part replaces the scope's part; states add up). The scope returned keeps its own selector. Never panics.
- `pub fn on_state(self, state: twine_style::State, f: impl FnOnce(Self) -> Self) -> Self` — Styles the scope's part while `state` is also active (the states add up: `.part(Part::Knob, |s| s.on_state(State::PRESSED, ..))` styles the pressed knob). The scope returned keeps its own selector, so modifiers after the call apply to it again. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, StyleExt

#### enum twine_view::TextProp
