#### struct twine_view::Ui
The declarative UI runtime: the engine, the application's root scope and the clock.
Methods of `Ui`:
- `pub fn builder_async<D: twine_hal::AsyncDisplayDriver + 'static>(display: D) -> twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D>` — A builder for an async display (`AsyncUi`): partial buffers (two for DMA overlap), flushed through `display` chunk by chunk.
- `pub fn builder<D: twine_hal::DisplayDriver + 'static>(display: D) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<twine_view::Partial<D>>` — A builder for a display flushed from partial draw buffers.
- `pub fn builder_fb<D: twine_hal::FramebufferDisplay + 'static>(display: D) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<twine_view::Framebuffer<D>, twine_view::NoRuntime, twine_view::NoClock, twine_engine::BufferMode>` — A builder for a memory-mapped framebuffer display (`Full` / `Direct` buffer modes).
- `pub fn update(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update (see `UiCore::update`) at the clock's current time, rendering within `AppConfig::engine`'s `step_budget` (default unlimited). Returns when to run again; `run::blocking` is the loop that honours it.
- `pub fn update_budgeted(&mut self, budget: twine_engine::StepBudget) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update that renders at most `budget` (`StepBudget`: chunks and/or time) instead of the configured `step_budget`: the hook for schedulers that bound how long a step may take (an RTOS time slice, a super-loop with other duties). When the frame is cut short the update returns `Wake::Now` and the next update — budgeted or not — continues it; the finished frame has exactly the pixels of the same frame rendered by one `update`. An update that uses up the budget's time raises `FaultKind::FrameOverrun`. Each update still runs the whole update cycle before rendering (messages, inputs, timers, animations, bindings, layout), so the UI stays responsive while a large frame is drawn.
- `pub fn now(&self) -> twine_core::Instant` — The current time of the `Ui`'s clock (or platform): the time base of the deadlines `update` returns. Never panics itself (it calls the clock's `now`).
- `pub fn notify_input(&self)` — Tells the next update that an input device changed (e.g. from a touch interrupt through `waker`).
- `pub fn waker(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The waker, set by channel sends and input notifications (`'static`, usable from interrupts and other tasks).
- `pub fn memory_report(&self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — What the UI's memory is used for, by part: the engine (tree, render scratch and caches, glyph and image caches, layer buffer, draw buffers), the reactive runtime, the engine command queues and the waker pool (`MemoryReport`: units, shared parts and what is not included).
- `pub fn timing(&self) -> twine_engine::TimingReport` — The worst-case timings since start-up or the last `reset_worst`: the longest update, chunk render and chunk flush in µs (`TimingReport`; measured with the engine's `hires_timer`, all `0` without one). Evidence for a time budget (`twine_core::audit::KeyValues(&ui.timing())` writes the `timing.*` audit lines). Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn reset_worst(&mut self)` — Clears the high-water marks of `timing` (`Engine::reset_worst`). Never panics.
- `pub fn heartbeat(&self) -> u32` — The number of completed updates (`Engine::heartbeat`), wrapping: an external watchdog reads it to see that the UI is alive. Never panics.
- `pub fn seal(&mut self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — Ends start-up: from now on every allocation by one of Twine's growth points raises `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` at the next update, after the heap budget is checked (see `UiCore::seal`). Returns the memory report at sealing time. Call it once the UI is built and has drawn its first frames (every screen it will show exists).
- `pub fn messages_per_channel(&self) -> usize` — Messages each channel delivers per update (see `Limits::messages_per_channel`).
- `pub fn set_messages_per_channel(&mut self, n: usize)` — Changes how many messages each channel delivers per update (see `Limits::messages_per_channel` and `UiBuilder::limits`; `0` counts as `1`). Never panics.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably (full LVGL-style control).
- `pub fn take_faults(&mut self) -> twine_core::Faults` — The faults raised since the last call, clearing them: the engine's (display flush errors, capacity, build failures, …) and the reactive runtime's (effect loop cuts, the depth guard, dropped channel messages). `Ui::update` forwards the runtime's faults to the engine, so the fault hook sees them too.
- `pub fn fault_counts(&self) -> twine_core::FaultCounts` — Occurrences of every fault kind since start-up (saturating, never reset).
- `pub fn last_fault(&self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> Option<&twine_engine::FaultRecord>` — The last record of `kind` (display, node, time, occurrences, detail code).
- `pub fn set_fault_hook(&mut self, hook: Option<twine_engine::FaultHook>)` — Sets the function called for every fault as it is raised (`None` removes it); see `FaultHook` for what it may do.
- `pub fn display_health(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayHealth>` — The flush health of the display (see `Engine::display_health` and `FlushPolicy`).
- `pub fn input_health(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_hal::DeviceHealth>` — The health of input device `id` as the engine last read it (see `Engine::input_health`; devices added with `UiBuilder::input` are numbered in the order they were added, see `Engine::inputs`). A device entering `Degraded` or `Failed` also raises `FaultKind::InputDevice`.
- `pub fn recover_display(&mut self)` — Recovers the display after flush failures: clears its error count, resumes a display halted by `FlushPolicy::Halt` and redraws it (see `Engine::recover_display`).
- `pub fn motion(&self) -> twine_anim::Motion` — The motion preference (see `set_motion`).
- `pub fn set_motion(&mut self, motion: twine_anim::Motion)` — Sets the motion preference at run time (e.g. when the user toggles "reduce motion" in the settings): `Engine::set_motion`, and the value `use_motion` reads (tracked) changes at once. Idempotent; never allocates or panics.
- `pub fn mount_on<S: twine_view::DisplaySetup, B: twine_view::HasBuffers, V: twine_view::View>(&mut self, display: twine_view::DisplayBuilder<S, B>, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_engine::DisplayId, twine_view::UiError>` — Adds a further display to the `Ui` and builds `app` on it (the run-time counterpart of `UiBuilder::display`); returns its id. `display` brings its own draw buffers, inputs, theme, rotation reserve and command channel. The application runs in a child scope of the root scope (contexts the first display's application provided there are visible to it), with its own theme state and engine-command queue; it is updated by this `Ui`'s `update` and woken by its `waker`, so the run loop that drives the `Ui` drives it too. Each display keeps its own dirty areas (an update redraws only what changed on each), inputs, theme mode, rotation and power state (`display_mut`). Wakes the `Ui`.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` when the engine refuses the display, its buffers or inputs (see `Engine::add_display`); `UiError::Build` when a widget of `app` cannot be created (see `UiCore::mount_on`: the application is taken down again; the display, already added to the engine, stays blank). The `Ui`'s other displays are unaffected.
- `pub fn displays(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_engine::DisplayId> + '_` — The displays of the `Ui`: the first one (`display`), then those added with `UiBuilder::display` and `mount_on`, in that order.
- `pub fn display_mut(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_view::DisplayMut<'_>>` — Run-time control of `display` (rotation, brightness, sleep, theme, theme mode, health; see `DisplayMut`); `None` for a display without an application of this `Ui`. The `Ui`'s own methods (`set_rotation`, …) act on the first display.
- `pub fn root_scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The root scope: the scope of the first display's application (the applications of further displays run in child scopes, `DisplayMut::scope`).
- `pub fn runtime(&self) -> twine_reactive::Runtime` — The reactive runtime the `Ui` runs in (the token given to `UiBuilder::runtime`): for code outside the view tree that batches writes, reads the runtime's statistics and memory, or takes its faults. Never panics.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the `Ui` belongs to: the partition of the token given to `UiBuilder::runtime` (ADR-001). A partition is one runtime and every `Ui` built on it; this `Ui`'s engine, seal domain (`seal`), faults, limits, step budget, frame observer, fail-safe screen and heartbeat are its own, so a `Ui` of another partition cannot interfere with them. Never panics.
- `pub fn display(&self) -> twine_engine::DisplayId` — The first display (the one given to `Ui::builder`; see `displays` for all).
- `pub fn display_info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — The description of the first display: its current logical size and rotation. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<(), twine_view::UiError>` — Rotates the display at the next update (`Engine::set_rotation`): the driver rotates in hardware, or the engine in software (needs `UiBuilder::reserve_rotation`); the draw format is checked again, the screens are laid out for the new size, the display is redrawn and touch input is fitted to the new rotation — all between two frames, without allocating. A rotation that does not fit raises `FaultKind::DisplayControl` and the display keeps its rotation. Wakes the `Ui`. Idempotent.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` with `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a framebuffer display.
- `pub fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction)` — Sets the panel brightness at the next update (`Engine::set_display_brightness`; a driver without brightness control raises `FaultKind::DisplayControl` — dim an LCD with its backlight instead). Wakes the `Ui`. Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn set_display_sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool)` — Puts the display to sleep (`true`) or wakes it (`false`) at the next update (`Engine::set_display_sleep`): asleep, the panel sleeps and nothing is drawn (the UI keeps running; what changes is drawn after the wake). Wakes the `Ui`. Idempotent; never panics.
- `pub fn display_asleep(&self) -> bool` — Whether the first display is asleep (`set_display_sleep`, `DisplayCmd::Sleep`): the sleep request was applied by an update. Never panics.
- `pub fn inactive_for(&self) -> twine_core::Duration` — The time since the last user input (`Engine::inactive_for` at the clock's current time): touch, keys, encoders, buttons, or `trigger_activity`. With `EngineConfig::idle_timeout` set, an update with nothing to do returns `Wake::IdleFor` once this exceeds the timeout.
- `pub fn trigger_activity(&mut self)` — Records user input that did not come through an input device (e.g. a hardware button the application handles itself): restarts `inactive_for` and the idle timeout. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### struct twine_view::UiBuilder<S, R = twine_view::NoRuntime, C = twine_view::NoClock, B = twine_view::NoBuffers>
Configures and builds a `Ui` (see `Ui::builder`).
Methods of `UiBuilder`:
- `pub fn app_config(self, config: twine_view::AppConfig) -> Self` — The application's configuration (`AppConfig`: engine configuration, limits, theme, motion, rotation, fault hook) — the same value the simulator and the tests are given, so they run what ships. **Replaces** every setting it covers, including those set before by `config`, `limits`, `theme`, `motion`, `rotation` and `fault_hook`; those methods called afterwards refine it (e.g. the board's `hires_timer`). Never panics.
- `pub fn display<S2: twine_view::DisplaySetup, B2: twine_view::HasBuffers + 'static, V: twine_view::View + 'static>(self, display: twine_view::DisplayBuilder<S2, B2>, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V + 'static) -> Self` — Adds a further display to the `Ui`, running `app` (see `Ui::mount_on`, which does the same on a built `Ui`): `display` brings its own draw buffers (required, checked at compile time), inputs, theme, rotation reserve and command channel. Displays are mounted after the first one's application, in the order they were added. One engine, one update cycle and one waker drive all of them, so one run loop does (`run::blocking`, `twine_embassy::run`); each display keeps its own dirty areas, inputs, theme mode, rotation and power state.
- `pub fn display_commands<const N: usize>(self, commands: &'static twine_reactive::Channel<twine_engine::DisplayCmd, N>) -> Self` — Applies the `DisplayCmd`s sent to `commands` from any context — another task, an interrupt, another thread or core (brightness, sleep, wake, rotation): each update delivers them (like any channel, see `Limits::messages_per_channel`) to `Engine::display_command` for the `Ui`'s display, and the engine applies them between frames (see `Ui::set_rotation`, `Ui::set_display_sleep`, `Ui::set_brightness`). A send wakes the `Ui`. The application owns the channel (the ports pattern: a `static` in firmware). A later call replaces the channel.
- `pub fn reserve_rotation(self) -> Self` — Reserves, at build time, the memory software rotation needs in every rotation (`Engine::reserve_rotation`), so `Ui::set_rotation` (and an `AppConfig::rotation`) works without allocating on a panel that cannot rotate in hardware. Not needed for drivers that rotate in hardware (MIPI DCS panels with `MADCTL`). Building fails for a framebuffer display.
- `pub fn buffers(self, m: twine_engine::BufferMode) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<S, R, C, twine_engine::BufferMode>` — The draw buffers of the display. **Required** for `Ui::builder` (partial displays): `build` does not exist until they are given (a compile error, see `typestate`) — the `Ui` never allocates heap buffers implicitly. `Ui::builder_fb` starts with `BufferMode::Full` (the driver's framebuffers). A later call replaces them.
- `pub fn input(self, d: impl twine_hal::InputDevice + 'static) -> Self` — Adds an input device (any number). Keypads and encoders are attached to a default focus group.
- `pub fn accel(self, accel: impl twine_render::DrawAccel + 'static) -> Self` — Attaches a draw accelerator, taking ownership of it — and with it of the peripheral it drives (e.g. `twine_accel_stm32::Dma2d::new(PacRegs::new(p.DMA2D)?)`): every rendered chunk offers its fills, blits and glyph blending to it, and what it declines is drawn in software (see `Engine::set_accel`). A later call replaces it. Default: software only.
- `pub fn layer_buf(self, buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — Caller memory for the engine's layer buffer (opacity groups, transforms, blend modes; ARGB8888) — typically a `LayerBuffer` static — so that firmware keeps the renderer's largest scratch buffer out of the heap. Without it the engine allocates `EngineConfig::layer_buf_bytes` on the heap. Like draw buffers, this is memory owned by the board, not part of the shared `AppConfig`. A later call replaces it.
- `pub fn clock(self, c: impl twine_hal::Clock + 'static) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<S, R, Box<dyn twine_hal::Clock>, B>` — The clock (required, unless `platform` provides it): the time of every update, timer and animation. A later `clock` or `platform` call replaces it. Boxed once.
- `pub fn platform<P: twine_hal::Platform + Clone + 'static>(self, platform: &P) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<S, R, Box<dyn twine_hal::Clock>, B>` — The platform the `Ui` runs on (see `Platform`), in one call:
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — The theme of the display: a `static` theme, attached when the display is created; sets `AppConfig::theme`. A later call replaces it.
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — The mode the display starts in; sets `AppConfig::theme_mode`. (Example: see `theme`.)
- `pub fn config(self, c: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — The engine configuration; sets `AppConfig::engine`.
- `pub fn rotation(self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — The rotation the screens are designed for; sets `AppConfig::rotation` (applied before the first frame, in hardware when the driver can, else in software with `reserve_rotation`).
- `pub fn fault_hook(self, hook: twine_engine::FaultHook) -> Self` — The function called for every fault (see `Ui::set_fault_hook`); sets `AppConfig::fault_hook`. Set here, it also sees the faults raised while the display is added and the application is built. The hook is a plain `fn` (see `FaultHook`): called synchronously for each fault, it must be short and must not panic.
- `pub fn waker(self, waker: &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker) -> Self` — The `Ui`'s waker: the application's own (typically a `static UiWaker` that interrupt handlers name directly) instead of one leased from the pool (see `UiCore::mount_with_waker`).
- `pub fn limits(self, limits: twine_core::Limits) -> Self` — The memory bounds of the `Ui` (sets `AppConfig::limits`; default `Limits::DEFAULT`), applied when it is built, before anything is created: the engine's (nodes, tree depth, text length, handlers, timers, animations), the reactive runtime's (nodes, scopes, pending effects), the `Ui`'s own and the waker pool's. Two of them shape the update cycle:
- `pub fn motion(self, motion: twine_anim::Motion) -> Self` — The initial motion preference (default `Motion::Full`; sets `AppConfig::motion`): how much the UI animates, e.g. the platform's "reduce motion" accessibility setting. Applied before the application is built, so even its first animations honour it; change it at run time with `Ui::set_motion` or `use_motion`. See `Motion` for what each level does to which animation.
- `pub fn runtime(self, rt: twine_reactive::Runtime) -> twine_view::UiBuilder<S, twine_reactive::Runtime, C, B>` — The reactive runtime of the calling execution context (required: `build` does not exist without it — a compile error): the token `Runtime::take` returned (or a copy of it). The `Ui` keeps it; because the token is `!Send`, the `Ui` and every reactive handle of the application stay in this context — interrupts and other tasks talk to it through `Channel` and the `waker`. A later call replaces the token. Never panics.
- `pub fn try_build<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::Ui, twine_view::UiError> where S: twine_view::DisplaySetup, R: twine_view::HasRuntime, C: twine_view::HasClock, B: twine_view::HasBuffers` — Builds the `Ui`: creates the engine, adds the display, the theme and the inputs, then builds `app` (once) on the active screen. Exists only once the runtime, the clock and the draw buffers are given (`typestate`).
  Errors: What only the device can tell: `UiError::Engine` with the engine's errors for the display, buffers and inputs (see `Engine::add_display`: a format not compiled in, buffers that do not fit the panel or are misaligned, too many displays or nodes) and for an `AppConfig::rotation` on a framebuffer display. Heap buffers (`BufferMode::alloc`) are allocated only once the display has been accepted. `UiError::Build`: a widget of `app` could not be created (e.g. more nodes than `Limits::max_nodes`); see `UiCore::mount`. The fault hook set with `fault_hook` has seen every fault by then.
- `pub fn build<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> twine_view::Ui where S: twine_view::DisplaySetup, R: twine_view::HasRuntime, C: twine_view::HasClock, B: twine_view::HasBuffers` — `try_build`, panicking on an error.
  Panics: When the engine rejects the display, buffers or inputs, or when a widget of `app` cannot be created (see `try_build` § Errors). A missing runtime, clock or buffers is a compile error, not a panic.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_view::UiCore
The reactive half of a `Ui` for hosts that own the engine themselves (test harnesses, simulators, custom loops): the root scope, the waker, and the update cycle run on an engine passed in.
Methods of `UiCore`:
- `pub fn memory_report(&self, engine: &twine_engine::Engine) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — The memory report of this UI on `engine` (`MemoryReport`). `Ui`, `AsyncUi` and `TestUi` call it with their engine. Allocates nothing; never panics; O(nodes).
- `pub fn seal(&self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — Ends start-up: from now on Twine is expected to allocate nothing, and every growth point that does allocate raises `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` at the next update (see `twine_core::alloc_guard` for how it is detected and what it covers). Call it once the UI is built and has run its first updates (every screen and buffer the product uses exists; with `Limits::preallocate` the bounded structures are reserved). Before sealing, it checks `Limits::heap_budget` against the report's `heap_bytes` (a `Capacity` fault with code `CapacityFault::HeapBudget` when exceeded). Returns the memory report at sealing time (evidence of the fixed memory).
- `pub fn mount<V: twine_view::View>(rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::UiCore, twine_view::BuildError>` — Builds `app` on the active screen of `display` (inside one batch, with the engine lent to `EngineAccess`), lays it out, and sets a waker leased from the pool (`UiWaker::lease`) on the root scope, so the application's channels wake this UI.
  Errors: `BuildError` when a widget could not be created while `app` was built: the mount owns a `BuildReport` that every `BuildCx::create` failure of the application fills, including nested builds that run during the mount (each failure is also raised as a `FaultKind::BuildFailed` fault, as telemetry). The application is then taken down again: its scope is disposed and the nodes it created are deleted, so the engine is left as before (apart from the fault stream).
- `pub fn mount_with_waker<V: twine_view::View>(rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, waker: &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::UiCore, twine_view::BuildError>` — `mount` with the application's own waker (typically a `static UiWaker`) instead of a pooled one. The waker should not be shared with another live UI (both would be woken by each other's channels).
  Errors: As `mount`.
- `pub fn mount_configured<V: twine_view::View>(rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, config: &twine_view::AppConfig, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::UiCore, twine_view::UiError>` — `mount` with the application's `AppConfig`, for hosts that create the engine themselves (the simulator, test harnesses, custom loops) and want exactly what `UiBuilder::app_config` gives a `Ui`: `AppConfig::apply_limits` (engine, runtime, waker pool), `AppConfig::configure_engine` on `display` (fault hook, motion, rotation; the display was created with `AppConfig::display_theme`), then the mount with the limits' engine-queue capacity and messages per channel. `AppConfig::engine` is what the host creates the engine with.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` from `AppConfig::apply_limits` (invalid limits) or `AppConfig::configure_engine` (unknown display, a rotation on a framebuffer display); `UiError::Build` as `mount`.
- `pub fn mount_configured_with_waker<V: twine_view::View>(rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, config: &twine_view::AppConfig, waker: &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_view::UiCore, twine_view::UiError>` — `mount_configured` with the application's own waker (typically a `static UiWaker`) instead of a pooled one, as `mount_with_waker` is to `mount`. Besides letting interrupt handlers name the waker, this makes the mount independent of the process-wide `WakerLease` pool: what it allocates does not depend on how many other UIs (of other threads, e.g. tests running in parallel) hold a lease.
  Errors: As `mount_configured`.
- `pub fn mount_on<V: twine_view::View>(&mut self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_reactive::Scope, twine_view::UiError>` — Builds `app` on a further display of the engine (added by the host, e.g. with `Engine::add_display`), in a new child scope of the root that is returned: the application gets the display's own theme state, design elements and engine-command queue (its `ThemeHandle` and `use_theme` work on its display), and runs in this `UiCore`'s update cycle and waker (see `UiCore` § Several displays). Contexts provided on the root scope (by the first display's application) are visible to it. Allocates the scope, the queue and the views once; updates allocate nothing more than with one display.
  Errors: `UiError::Engine` with `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for a display the engine does not have, `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a display that already runs an application of this `UiCore`; `UiError::Build` when a widget could not be created (see `mount`; the scope is disposed and its nodes deleted again, the other displays' applications are untouched).
- `pub fn displays(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_engine::DisplayId> + '_` — The displays this `UiCore` runs applications on: the one it was mounted on, then the ones added with `mount_on`, in that order. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn display_scope(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_reactive::Scope>` — The scope of the application on `display`: the root scope for the display the `UiCore` was mounted on, the child scope `mount_on` returned for a further one, `None` for a display without an application of this `UiCore`. Never panics.
- `pub fn update(&mut self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, now: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update at `now`, in the documented order: 1 time, then the engine commands queued since the last update (see `UiCore` § Engine commands; effects deferred for lack of an engine run first, as they were requested earlier: e.g. an animation created, then paused, between updates), 2 channel messages, 3 inputs, 4 timers, 5 animations (2–5 inside one batch, with the engine lent to the application code they run), 6 the effect flush (bindings), 7 layout, 8 refresh; returns 9 when to run again (the engine's deadline, or at once while effects, channel messages, engine commands or the waker are pending). The refresh (8) renders within the engine's `EngineConfig::step_budget` (default unlimited; see `update_budgeted`).
- `pub fn update_budgeted(&mut self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, now: twine_core::Instant, budget: twine_engine::StepBudget) -> twine_engine::Wake` — `update` whose refresh (8) renders at most `budget` (see `StepBudget`) instead of the configured one: a frame cut short continues in the next update, and this one returns `Wake::Now`. See `Ui::update_budgeted`.
- `pub fn set_motion(&mut self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, motion: twine_anim::Motion)` — Sets the engine's motion preference (`Engine::set_motion`) and the `Ui`'s tracked copy (`MotionHandle::get`) at once. Idempotent; never panics, allocates nothing.
- `pub fn set_engine_queue_capacity(&mut self, capacity: usize)` — Sets the number of engine commands the `UiCore` can queue (default `Limits::engine_queue`; see `UiCore` § Engine commands). Allocates the new ring now (configuration time), keeping the queued commands; queuing never allocates. Shrinking the ring below the number of commands already queued keeps the oldest ones that fit and drops the rest, reported at the next update like a full queue (`FaultKind::Capacity` with code `CapacityFault::EngineQueue`, the dropped commands as occurrences). A capacity of `0` drops every command issued without the engine. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_messages_per_channel(&mut self, n: usize)` — Sets how many messages each channel delivers per update (default `Limits::messages_per_channel`; `0` counts as `1`, so every update makes progress). Never panics.
- `pub fn messages_per_channel(&self) -> usize` — Messages each channel delivers per update (see `set_messages_per_channel`).
- `pub fn root_scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The root scope: the scope of the application on the display the `UiCore` was mounted on (further displays' applications run in child scopes, see `display_scope`). Its waker and channel registrations are the `UiCore`'s.
- `pub fn runtime(&self) -> twine_reactive::Runtime` — The reactive runtime the application runs in (the token it was mounted with).
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the `UiCore` belongs to: its runtime token's (ADR-001). Its engine, seal domain, faults, limits, step budget and heartbeat are that partition's. Never panics.
- `pub fn display(&self) -> twine_engine::DisplayId` — The display the `UiCore` was mounted on (see `displays` for all).
- `pub fn waker(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The waker: set by channel sends and `notify_input`; register a task `Waker` in it to be woken.
- `pub fn notify_input(&self)` — Tells the next update that an input device changed (callable from anywhere through the `waker`).
- `pub fn take_faults(&self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine) -> twine_core::Faults` — The faults raised since the last call (engine faults and the reactive runtime's, which are forwarded to the engine first), clearing them. See `Ui::take_faults`.
- `pub fn dispose(self, engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine)` — Disposes the application's scope with the engine lent to its cleanups (after applying the engine commands still queued), so it leaves no animation, timer or modal behind. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### struct twine_view::Btn

Methods of `Btn`:

- `pub fn checked(self) -> Self` — Starts checked.

- `pub fn no_repeat(self) -> Self` — No repeated selection while long pressed.

- `pub fn popover(self) -> Self` — Shows an enlarged copy above the button while pressed (selected on release).

#### fn twine_view::spangroup
`pub fn spangroup(spans: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanGroup>`
A paragraph of `span`s with their own text styles, wrapped as one text.

#### fn twine_view::spinbox
`pub fn spinbox(value: impl twine_view::IntoModel<i32>) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::spinbox::Spinbox>`
A number field editing `value` (a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways): keys, the encoder or `increment`/`decrement` change it digit by digit.

#### fn twine_view::spinner
`pub fn spinner() -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::spinner::Spinner>`
The loading spinner (an arc chasing around a ring; not clickable).

#### fn twine_view::switch
`pub fn switch(on: impl twine_view::IntoModel<bool>) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::switch::Switch>`
An on/off switch editing `on` (a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways).

#### fn twine_view::tab
`pub fn tab<MT>(title: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>, content: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::TabView`
A tab of a `tabview`: a button titled `title` in the bar and a page holding `content`. Outside a tabview it logs `warn!` and builds a plain container.

#### fn twine_view::tabview
`pub fn tabview(selected: impl twine_view::IntoModel<usize>, tabs: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets_ext::tabview::Tabview>`
Tabs: a button bar and swipeable pages, one per `tab` of `tabs`; the index of the active tab in `selected` (a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways).

#### fn twine_view::textarea
`pub fn textarea(text: impl twine_view::IntoModel<String>) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::textarea::Textarea>`
A text field editing `text`: a plain value or a `Signal<String>` kept in sync both ways.

#### fn twine_view::tile
`pub fn tile(pos: twine_view::TilePos, dirs: impl Into<twine_style::Sides>, content: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::TileView`
A tile of a `tileview()` at `pos` that the user may leave towards `dirs` (one `Side` or a set of `Sides`, e.g. `Sides::RIGHT | Sides::BOTTOM`), holding `content`. Outside a tileview it logs `warn!` and builds a plain container.

#### fn twine_view::tileview
`pub fn tileview(active: impl twine_view::IntoModel<twine_view::TilePos>, tiles: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets_ext::tileview::Tileview>`
A 2D grid of full-size `tile`s swiped in the directions each tile allows; the position of the tile in view in `active` (a plain value or a signal kept in sync both ways).

#### fn twine_view::window
`pub fn window<MT>(title: impl twine_view::IntoText<MT>, header_buttons: impl twine_view::ViewSeq, content: impl twine_view::ViewSeq) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets_ext::window::Window>`
A window: a header with `title` (cut with dots when too long) and `header_buttons` (usually `window_button`s), above `content`, which scrolls.

#### fn twine_view::window_button
`pub fn window_button<M1, M2>(icon: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_image::ImageSource, M1>, width: impl twine_view::IntoProp<i32, M2>) -> twine_view::WidgetView<twine_widgets::button::Button>`
A header button of a `window()`: `width` px wide, as high as the header, `icon` (a `Symbol` or an image) centered. Unlike the other icon setters (which take any `Icon`, so also `()` for none), `icon` is an `ImageSource`: a header button always shows one.

#### struct twine_view::VectorCanvas
The view of `vector_canvas`.
Implements: Debug, View, ViewExt

#### fn twine_view::vector_canvas
`pub fn vector_canvas(draw: impl Fn(&mut twine_vector::VectorScene) + 'static) -> twine_view::VectorCanvas`
A canvas of vector graphics: `draw` fills a `VectorScene` (in the canvas's coordinates, (0, 0) = top-left corner) and runs again whenever a signal it reads changes. Only the bounds of the old and the new scene are redrawn, and nothing happens when the new scene equals the old one.

#### macro twine_view::draw_buffers!
```rust
macro_rules! draw_buffers {
    ($(
        $(#[$attr:meta])*
        $vis:vis static $name:ident : $count:tt x $rows:tt rows x $width:tt px @ $format:ident
    );+ $(;)?) => { ... };
}
```
Declares `static` draw buffers sized at compile time, aligned by their type and handed out once — no `static mut`, no `unsafe`, no hand-computed sizes.

#### macro twine_view::text!
```rust
macro_rules! text {
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```
A dynamic text formatted like `format!`, re-run only when a signal read in its arguments changes, written in place into the label's own buffers: no allocation after warm-up, and nothing happens when the result equals the current text.

### mod twine_view::component

Components: functions describing a piece of UI, used like built-in widgets.

The attribute `#[component]` (re-exported from `twine-macros`)
turns a function into a view with a props builder — required props are arguments, optional
ones are methods, modifiers apply to the returned view's root:


This module holds what the generated code uses at run time: `Modifiers`, the modifiers
applied to a component, kept until it is built. Without the macro a component is a plain
function returning a view (see `component` § Without the macro).

#### struct twine_view::component::Modifiers
The modifiers (build steps) applied to a component before it is built, handed to the view its body returns when it is built — in order, after the body's own, exactly as if they were written at the end of the body.
Methods of `Modifiers`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — No modifiers (does not allocate).
- `pub fn push(&mut self, op: twine_view::BuildOp)` — Appends a modifier (a build step run on the root node, see `ViewExt::push_op`).
- `pub fn apply<V: twine_view::ViewExt>(self, view: V) -> V` — Hands every modifier, in order, to `view` (its `ViewExt::push_op`) and returns it.
Implements: Default, Debug

### mod twine_view::flow

Control flow: `when`, `dynamic`, `for_each`, `virtual_list` (the keyed collections
take their items as `IntoItems`).

Each region owns one **wrapper node** (a `LAYOUT_PASSTHROUGH` node: its children are laid
out as children of the wrapper's parent, it draws nothing and is invisible to hit tests)
and a child `Scope` per piece of content. Replacing content disposes that scope — with
every signal, effect, binding and handler created inside — and deletes its nodes; nothing
outside the region is rebuilt.

#### static twine_view::flow::WHEN_CLASS
`pub static WHEN_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Class of the `when` wrapper.

#### static twine_view::flow::DYNAMIC_CLASS
`pub static DYNAMIC_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Class of the `dynamic` wrapper.

#### static twine_view::flow::FOR_EACH_CLASS
`pub static FOR_EACH_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Class of the `for_each` wrapper.

#### static twine_view::flow::NAVIGATOR_CLASS
`pub static NAVIGATOR_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Class of the `navigator`) anchor.

#### struct twine_view::flow::Wrapper
The wrapper node of a control-flow region: no look, no input, transparent to layout.
Fields:
- `0: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Implements: Debug, Clone, Copy, Widget

Re-exports in `twine_view::flow`:

### mod twine_view::navigator

Typed screen navigation: `navigator`, `Navigator`, `expect_navigator` /
`use_navigator`, leave guards
(`Navigator::on_leave`, `Leave`) and the outcome of a request (`NavOutcome`).

**Model**

A navigator holds a **stack of routes** — values of an application type `R` (usually an
enum, `Clone + PartialEq`) — and one **page function** `Fn(Scope, R) -> V` that turns a
route into the view of its page. Each page is an engine screen of its own with its own child
`Scope`; the screens are switched with the engine's screen-load animations
(`Engine::load_screen_anim`, `ScreenAnim`).

Requests (`push`, `pop`,
`replace`, `pop_to`,
`pop_to_root`, `reset`) change the route
stack **at once** (so `stack` and `depth` see them)
and are applied to the engine at the `Ui`'s next effect flush: several requests in one
handler become one transition, with the animation of the last one. Only the top page is
built: a page under it is built when it becomes the top again (pages restored with
`NavigatorView::restore` or pushed twice in one handler cost nothing until shown). A page
that leaves the stack is deleted — its scope disposed with every signal, effect, timer and
guard created inside — at the end of its animation (at once when it is not shown). When the
navigator itself goes away (its scope is disposed, e.g. with a `when`
branch), its pages are deleted and the screen shown before it is shown again.
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

Re-exports in `twine_view::navigator`:
- `Leave` — same as `twine_view::Leave`
- `NavOutcome` — same as `twine_view::NavOutcome`
- `Navigator` — same as `twine_view::Navigator`
- `navigator` — same as `twine_view::navigator`
- `NavigatorView` — same as `twine_view::NavigatorView`
- `use_navigator` — same as `twine_view::use_navigator`
- `expect_navigator` — same as `twine_view::expect_navigator`

### mod twine_view::run

Run loops: thin, optional adapters that step a `Ui` and sleep as it asks.

Twine never owns the execution model: the UI is a step function (`Ui::update` returns a
`Wake`) plus wake-up signalling (`UiWaker`). A run loop is a
few lines on top, and an application may always write its own. This module has the
blocking one, for every context that can block: bare metal, an RTOS task, a host thread.

| Execution model | Adapter | Sleeps with |
|-----------------|---------|-------------|
| bare metal, RTOS task, host thread | `blocking`, `blocking_with` | a `Platform` (`WFE`, a task notification, a condition variable) |
| embassy (async) | `twine_embassy::run`, `twine_embassy::run_with` | the executor (timer, task waker, input interrupt) |
| anything else | your loop around `Ui::update` / `Ui::update_budgeted` | your choice |

**What the blocking loop does**


- **`Wake::Idle` never spins:** the loop waits with no deadline; only a wake-up ends the
  wait (a channel message, a `Latest` set, `Ui::notify_input`, an input interrupt calling the
  `waker`).
- **`Wake::At(t)`** waits until `t` on the platform's clock, or a wake-up.
- **`Wake::Now`** steps again at once, after `Platform::yield_now` (an RTOS yields to
  the other ready tasks of its priority; bare metal does nothing). It cannot starve the
  UI's own work or livelock: the UI returns `Now` only while work is pending, and every
  update makes progress on it (the rest of a frame — at least one chunk with a
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_view::run::LoopEvent
What a run loop is doing, reported to the callback of `blocking_with` (and of `twine_embassy::run_with`) together with the `Ui`, so the application keeps access to the UI, its engine and its display while the loop owns them: power management (backlight, panel sleep, clocks), fault handling, watchdogs. The display driver is `ui.engine_mut().driver_mut::<MyPanel>(ui.display())`.
Variants:
- `BeforeUpdate` — The loop is about to update the UI (every iteration, also after `Wake::Now`). Changes made here — signals, widgets, the theme — are part of this update.
- `Idle(Option<twine_core::Instant>)` — The update is done and the loop is about to sleep until the instant (on the `Ui`'s clock; `None`: until a wake-up). A signal written here wakes the `Ui` by itself (the bindings it changes defer to the next update and wake the `Ui`); other changes — the engine or display touched directly — are not drawn until the next wake-up: follow them with `Ui::notify_input` (or a `UiWaker::wake`), which makes the wait return at once.
- `Inactive(twine_core::Duration)` — Like `Idle(None)` (nothing scheduled, the loop sleeps until a wake-up), and there has been no user input for this long — at least `EngineConfig::idle_timeout` (`Wake::IdleFor`): the moment to pick a deep-sleep mode or put the display to sleep (`Ui::set_display_sleep`; follow it with `Ui::notify_input` so it is applied before the sleep). Reported instead of `Idle(None)`, only with an `idle_timeout`.
- `Woken` — The sleep ended: the deadline passed, the UI was woken, or (as platforms may) for no reason. The next event is `BeforeUpdate`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_view::run::blocking
`pub fn blocking<P: twine_hal::Platform>(ui: twine_view::Ui, platform: &mut P) -> never`
Runs `ui` forever on `platform`: `blocking_with` without a callback.

#### fn twine_view::run::blocking_with
`pub fn blocking_with<P, F>(ui: twine_view::Ui, platform: &mut P, on_event: F) -> never where P: twine_hal::Platform, F: FnMut(&mut twine_view::Ui, twine_view::run::LoopEvent)`
Runs `ui` forever on `platform`, reporting each step of the loop to `on_event` with the `Ui` (see `LoopEvent`): update, then sleep with `Platform::wait` as the returned `Wake` says — no deadline for `Wake::Idle` (no spinning), until `t` for `Wake::At(t)`, and no sleep for `Wake::Now` (after `Platform::yield_now`).

### mod twine_view::typestate

The parts a `UiBuilder` (and `AsyncUiBuilder`) must be given before it
can build, checked by the compiler.

A builder carries one type parameter per required part. It starts with the "missing"
marker (`NoRuntime`, `NoClock`, `NoBuffers`, and `NoPlatform` for the async
builder); the method that provides the part (`runtime`,
`clock` / `platform`,
`buffers`) replaces the marker by the part itself, and
`build` / `try_build` exist only once every part is there. Forgetting one is a compile
error that names the missing call — never a run-time `InvalidConfig` error on a device:

| Missing | Compile error says | Add |
|---------|--------------------|-----|
| runtime | "the `Ui` has no reactive runtime" | `.runtime(Runtime::take().expect(..))` |
| clock | "the `Ui` has no clock" | `.platform(&p)` or `.clock(c)` |
| draw buffers | "the display has no draw buffers" | `.buffers(BufferMode::partial_double_from(BUFS.take()..))` or `.buffers(BufferMode::alloc(..))` |
| async platform | "the `AsyncUi` has no platform" | `.platform(&EmbassyPlatform)` (or `.with_embassy_platform()`) |

What only the device can tell stays a run-time error of `try_build`
(`UiError`): a display the engine refuses (format not compiled in, too
many displays, node budget), buffers that do not fit the panel or are misaligned, inputs
the engine refuses, widgets that cannot be built.

**Cost.** None at run time: the markers are zero-sized, a provided part is stored exactly
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

Re-exports in `twine_view::typestate`:
- `NoRuntime` — same as `twine_view::NoRuntime`
- `NoClock` — same as `twine_view::NoClock`
- `NoBuffers` — same as `twine_view::NoBuffers`
- `NoPlatform` — same as `twine_view::NoPlatform`
- `HasRuntime` — same as `twine_view::HasRuntime`
- `HasClock` — same as `twine_view::HasClock`
- `HasBuffers` — same as `twine_view::HasBuffers`
- `HasPlatform` — same as `twine_view::HasPlatform`

## crate twine_widgets

Documented with features: `std,gif,svg,bidi,arabic-shaping`.

**twine-widgets**

The basic widgets of the Twine GUI library, each a port of the LVGL widget of the same
name:

| Widget | LVGL | Parts |
|--------|------|-------|
| `Container` | `lv_obj` | `Main`, `Scrollbar` |
| `Card` | `lv_obj` with the theme's card look | `Main`, `Scrollbar` |
| `Label` | `lv_label` | `Main`, `Scrollbar`, `Selected` |
| `Button` | `lv_button` | `Main`, `Scrollbar` |
| `Image` | `lv_image` | `Main` |
| `Bar` | `lv_bar` | `Main`, `Indicator` |
| `Slider` | `lv_slider` | `Main`, `Indicator`, `Knob` |
| `Switch` | `lv_switch` | `Main`, `Indicator`, `Knob` |
| `Checkbox` | `lv_checkbox` | `Main`, `Indicator` |
| `Arc` | `lv_arc` | `Main`, `Indicator`, `Knob` |
| `Spinner` | `lv_spinner` | `Main`, `Indicator`, `Knob` |
| `Led` | `lv_led` | `Main` |
| `Line` | `lv_line` | `Main` |
| `ImageButton` | `lv_imagebutton` | `Main` |
| `AnimImg` | `lv_animimg` | `Main` |
| `ButtonMatrix` | `lv_buttonmatrix` | `Main`, `Items` |
| `Keyboard` | `lv_keyboard` | `Main`, `Items` |
| `Textarea` | `lv_textarea` | `Main`, `Scrollbar`, `Selected`, `Cursor`, `PLACEHOLDER` |
| `Spinbox` | `lv_spinbox` | as the textarea |
| `SpanGroup` | `lv_spangroup` | `Main` |

They are
`Widget`s of `twine-engine`, usable imperatively (LVGL-style) and
wrapped by the declarative view layer.

**Conventions (every widget follows them)**

- A widget module `x` has `pub struct X` (the widget state), `pub static X_CLASS:
  WidgetClass` (name, parts, default flags, focus group default, as LVGL's
  `lv_x_class`) and `pub fn create(engine, parent) -> Result<NodeId, EngineError>`, the
  imperative constructor (LVGL `lv_x_create`): it creates the node, the display's theme
  styles it, then `Widget::init` runs.
- Setters are `pub fn set_*(&mut self, cx: &mut WidgetCx<'_>, v)` and are **idempotent**:
  setting the value a widget already has does nothing — no invalidation, no layout (P3).
  A change invalidates only the widget's own area (P2) and marks the layout only when the
  widget's content size can change. Call them through
  `Engine::with_widget_mut`:
  `engine.with_widget_mut(id, |l: &mut Label, cx| l.set_text(cx, "Hi"))`.
- Getters take `&self` (and a `MeasureCx` when they need
  styles or geometry).
- Every setter that changes something logs
  `trace!(target: "twine::engine", "<class>#<node> set_<name>")`.
- Look comes from styles only: widgets read their parts' resolved styles (themes set
  the LVGL look, applications override with styles or local properties). A widget's
  variants are theme classes derived from its class, chosen with a typed
  `Variant` (`ButtonVariant`).
- Invalid input never panics in release builds: it logs `warn!` and is ignored (P7).

**Example**

```rust
use twine_engine::Engine;
use twine_testing::EngineHarness;
use twine_widgets::prelude::*;

let mut h = EngineHarness::new(120, 60);
let screen = h.screen();
let e = h.engine_mut();
let btn = button::create(e, screen).unwrap();
let lbl = label::create(e, btn).unwrap();
e.with_widget_mut(lbl, |l: &mut Label, cx| l.set_text(cx, "OK"));
e.align(lbl, twine_style::Align::Center, 0, 0);
h.run_until_idle();
assert_eq!(h.engine().widget::<Label>(lbl).unwrap().text(), "OK");
```

Value widgets (slider, arc, spinbox, button matrix, keyboard, textarea) send `ValueChanged`
once the change is complete and the widget is back in its node
(`Engine::post_event`), so handlers can read it with
`engine.widget::<W>(ev.target)`. The new value (the button index for a button matrix) is
also carried as `EventParam::Value`. Checkable widgets
(switch, checkbox) use the engine's `State::CHECKED`; set it from code with their
`set_checked` so they redraw.

**Features**

- `gif`: `AnimImg::from_gif` plays animated GIFs.
- `std`, `log`, `defmt`: as in every Twine crate.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints; implies
  `display-integrity`.
- `display-integrity`: the value digests of bars, sliders, arcs and spinboxes
  (`Widget::value_digest`, display-integrity cross-checks).
- `partitions`: two partitioned runtimes instead of one (ADR-001); widgets note the growth
  of their own buffers in their engine's partition (`WidgetCx::partition`). Not implied by
  `safety`.

#### enum twine_widgets::Orientation
The direction of a bar, slider or switch (LVGL `lv_bar_orientation_t`, `lv_slider_orientation_t`, `lv_switch_orientation_t`).
Variants:
- `Auto` — Vertical when the widget is taller than wide, else horizontal.
- `Horizontal` — Left to right (right to left with an RTL base direction).
- `Vertical` — Bottom to top.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

Re-exports in `twine_widgets`:
- `LongMode` = `twine_text::LongMode`

#### struct twine_widgets::animimg::AnimImg
An animated image (LVGL `lv_animimg`): an `Image` whose source steps through `frames`.
Methods of `AnimImg`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An animated image without frames (30 ms, repeating forever, stopped).
- `pub fn image(&self) -> &twine_widgets::image::Image` — The image showing the frames (rotation, scale, alignment…).
- `pub fn image_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_widgets::image::Image` — The image, mutably (its setters change how every frame is drawn).
- `pub fn frames(&self) -> &'static [twine_image::ImageSource]` — The frames.
- `pub fn frame_index(&self) -> usize` — The index of the frame shown.
- `pub fn period(&self) -> twine_core::Duration` — The duration of one pass over the frames.
- `pub fn repeat(&self) -> twine_anim::Repeat` — How often the frames are played.
- `pub fn is_playing(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> bool` — Whether the animation is running.
- `pub fn set_frames(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, frames: &'static [twine_image::ImageSource])` — Sets the frames (LVGL `lv_animimg_set_src`) and shows the first one. A running animation restarts. Idempotent (same slice).
- `pub fn set_period(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, period: twine_core::Duration)` — Sets the duration of one pass (LVGL `lv_animimg_set_duration`). Idempotent; a running animation restarts.
- `pub fn set_repeat(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, repeat: twine_anim::Repeat)` — Sets how often the frames play (LVGL `lv_animimg_set_repeat_count`). Idempotent; a running animation restarts.
- `pub fn start(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Plays the frames from the first one (LVGL `lv_animimg_start`).
- `pub fn stop(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Stops at the frame shown (LVGL `lv_animimg_delete`).
- `pub fn from_gif(bytes: &'static [u8]) -> Result<Self, twine_image::Error>` — An animated image playing a GIF (feature `gif`): every frame is composited by the GIF player and shown for its own delay; the GIF's loop count applies. Call `start` to play it.
  Errors: The GIF cannot be parsed.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::animimg::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates an animated image without frames as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_animimg_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

### mod twine_widgets::arc

`Arc`: an arc slider with a knob (LVGL `lv_arc`).

Angles are `Angle`s (0.1°), clockwise from 3 o'clock like LVGL's. The widget keeps them in
tenths of a degree internally, so values map to angles like LVGL built with
`LV_USE_FLOAT` (the integer build rounds every angle to a whole degree).

#### enum twine_widgets::arc::ArcMode
How the indicator of an `Arc` grows with the value (LVGL `lv_arc_mode_t`).
Variants:
- `Normal` — Clockwise from the background's start angle.
- `Symmetrical` — From the middle of the background arc towards either end.
- `Reverse` — Counter-clockwise from the background's end angle.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### static twine_widgets::arc::ARC_CLASS
`pub static ARC_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Arc`: `"arc"`, parts `Main` (background arc), `Indicator` and `Knob`, editable with an encoder (LVGL `lv_arc_class`; not in the default group, like LVGL).

#### const twine_widgets::arc::ARC_DEFAULT_SIZE
`pub const ARC_DEFAULT_SIZE: i32 = util::DPI_DEF`
LVGL's default object size (`lv_obj_class.width_def = LV_DPI_DEF`), which arcs inherit.

#### struct twine_widgets::arc::Arc
An arc slider (LVGL `lv_arc`): a background arc (`Main`: `ArcWidth`, `ArcColor`, `ArcRounded`), an indicator arc (`Indicator`) showing the value and a knob (`Knob`) at its end.
Methods of `Arc`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An arc with LVGL's defaults: background 135° … 45°, indicator 135° … 270°, range 0…100, no value yet, change rate 720°/s.
- `pub fn value(&self) -> i32` — The value (the minimum while none was set).
- `pub fn min(&self) -> i32` — The minimum.
- `pub fn max(&self) -> i32` — The maximum.
- `pub fn angle_start(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The indicator's start angle.
- `pub fn angle_end(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The indicator's end angle.
- `pub fn bg_angle_start(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The background's start angle.
- `pub fn bg_angle_end(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The background's end angle.
- `pub fn rotation(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The rotation of the whole arc.
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_widgets::arc::ArcMode` — The mode.
- `pub fn change_rate(&self) -> twine_core::AngularSpeed` — The maximal drag speed.
- `pub fn knob_offset(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The knob's angular offset from the indicator's end.
- `pub fn is_dragging(&self) -> bool` — Whether the arc is being dragged.
- `pub fn set_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32)` — Sets the value, clamped to the range (LVGL `lv_arc_set_value`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_range(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, min: i32, max: i32)` — Sets the range (LVGL `lv_arc_set_range`); the value is clamped into it. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_angles(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, start: twine_core::Angle, end: twine_core::Angle)` — Sets the indicator's angles directly (LVGL `lv_arc_set_angles`; values are normalized to 0…360°). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_bg_angles(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, start: twine_core::Angle, end: twine_core::Angle)` — Sets the background's angles (LVGL `lv_arc_set_bg_angles`); the indicator follows the value. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, rotation: twine_core::Angle)` — Turns the whole arc (LVGL `lv_arc_set_rotation`; normalized to 0…360°). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets::arc::ArcMode)` — Sets the mode (LVGL `lv_arc_set_mode`): the indicator is re-anchored and the value re-applied. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_change_rate(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, rate: twine_core::AngularSpeed)` — Limits how fast dragging may turn the value (LVGL `lv_arc_set_change_rate`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_knob_offset(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, offset: twine_core::Angle)` — Moves the knob by `offset` along the arc (LVGL `lv_arc_set_knob_offset`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn center(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> (twine_core::Point, i32)` — The center and radius of the background arc (LVGL `get_center`).
- `pub fn knob_area(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> twine_core::Rect` — The knob's area (LVGL `get_knob_area`), centered on the indicator ring.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::arc::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`

### mod twine_widgets::bar

`Bar`: a progress bar (LVGL `lv_bar`).

#### const twine_widgets::bar::ANIM_VALUE

`pub const ANIM_START_VALUE: u16 = 1`
`AnimProp::Custom` id of the start value animation (LVGL `start_value_anim`).

#### enum twine_widgets::bar::BarMode
How a `Bar` (and a `Slider`) draws its indicator (LVGL `lv_bar_mode_t`).
Variants:
- `Normal` — From the minimum to the value.
- `Symmetrical` — From zero to the value when the range includes zero (e.g. −50…50).
- `Range` — From the start value to the value (both settable).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### static twine_widgets::bar::BAR_CLASS
`pub static BAR_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Bar`: `"bar"`, parts `Main` (background) and `Indicator`.

#### const twine_widgets::bar::BAR_DEFAULT_WIDTH

#### const twine_widgets::bar::BAR_DEFAULT_HEIGHT
`pub const BAR_DEFAULT_HEIGHT: i32`
LVGL `lv_bar_class.height_def`: `LV_DPI_DEF / 10`.

#### struct twine_widgets::bar::Bar
A progress bar (LVGL `lv_bar`): a background (`Part::Main`) and an indicator (`Part::Indicator`) showing a value within a range.
Methods of `Bar`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — A bar with range 0…100 and value 0 (LVGL `lv_bar_constructor`).
- `pub fn value(&self) -> i32` — The value (the target value while an animation runs, LVGL `lv_bar_get_value`).
- `pub fn start_value(&self) -> i32` — The start value (the minimum unless the mode is `BarMode::Range`).
- `pub fn min(&self) -> i32` — The minimum as set (LVGL returns the swapped value of a reversed range).
- `pub fn max(&self) -> i32` — The maximum as set.
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_widgets::bar::BarMode` — The mode.
- `pub fn orientation(&self) -> twine_widgets::Orientation` — The orientation.
- `pub fn is_animating(&self) -> bool` — Whether an animation of the value or the start value is running.
- `pub fn is_symmetrical(&self) -> bool` — Whether the indicator is drawn from zero (LVGL `lv_bar_is_symmetrical`): symmetrical mode with a range spanning zero.
- `pub fn set_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32, anim: bool)` — Sets the value, clamped to the range (and not below the start value). With `anim` the indicator moves there over the `AnimDuration` style of `Main` (LVGL `lv_bar_set_value`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_start_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32, anim: bool)` — Sets the start value in `BarMode::Range` (clamped to the range and not above the value; ignored in the other modes, like LVGL). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_range(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, min: i32, max: i32)` — Sets the range (LVGL `lv_bar_set_range`). `min > max` reverses the bar: the indicator grows from the other end. The value is clamped into the new range. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets::bar::BarMode)` — Sets the mode. Leaving `BarMode::Range` resets the start value to the minimum. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_orientation(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, o: twine_widgets::Orientation)` — Sets the orientation. Idempotent.
- `pub fn is_horizontal(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> bool` — Whether the bar is drawn horizontally.
- `pub fn indicator_area(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> twine_core::Rect` — The area the indicator is drawn in (empty when it is not drawn), as computed by LVGL's `draw_indic`.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`

#### enum twine_widgets::button::ButtonVariant
The look of a button, as a theme class (design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.4): the value of the view's `.variant(..)` (a constant or a signal), which calls `Engine::set_theme_class`. A theme that does not know a variant styles it like a plain button (lineage fallback): the built-in LVGL, Mono and Simple themes show every variant as their button.
Variants:
- `Filled` — The theme's button (the primary action).
- `Tinted` — Accent text on a light accent tint.
- `Gray` — A neutral gray fill.
- `Plain` — Text only, no fill.
- `Destructive` — A destructive action (the theme's danger color).
- `Custom(&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass)` — An application variant: a class derived from `BUTTON_CLASS`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Variant

#### struct twine_widgets::button::Button
A button: a container that is clickable, focusable and not scrollable. With the default theme it is a primary-colored rounded rectangle with a shadow (light mode) that darkens while pressed, turns secondary when checked and shows an outline on keyboard focus.
Methods of `Button`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — A button widget (insert it with `Engine::create` or use `create`).
- `pub const fn with_class(class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Self` — A button of another class: an LVGL subclass of the button that only changes the class (its name for themes and queries, flags, focus group default), e.g. `"list_button"`.
- `pub fn set_checkable(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Makes the button toggle `State::CHECKED` on click (the `CHECKABLE` flag). Idempotent.
- `pub fn is_checkable(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> bool` — Whether the button is checkable.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::button::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a button as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_button_create`). Its size is `Content` until set.

### mod twine_widgets::buttonmatrix

`ButtonMatrix`: a grid of text buttons drawn by one widget (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix`).

#### enum twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap
The buttons of a `ButtonMatrix`, row by row: each button has its text and the control bits it starts with. Rows are explicit (no `"\n"` entries, no `""` terminator: an empty text is a button without text).
Variants:
- `Static(&'static [&'static [twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::MapBtn]])` — A map in flash.
- `Owned(twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::OwnedMap)` — A map built at run time.
Methods of `BtnMap`:
- `pub fn btn_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of buttons.
- `pub fn row_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of rows.
- `pub fn row_lens(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> + '_` — The number of buttons of each row, top to bottom.
- `pub fn texts(&self) -> twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnTexts<'_>` — The texts of the buttons in reading order. Allocation-free.
- `pub fn text(&self, i: usize) -> Option<&str>` — The text of button `i` (in reading order).
- `pub fn initial_ctrl(&self, i: usize) -> Option<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>` — The control bits button `i` starts with.
Implements: From<&twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap>, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, From<&'static [&'static [twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::MapBtn]]>, From<&'static [&'static [twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::MapBtn]; N]>, From<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::OwnedMap>

#### struct twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnTexts<'a>
The texts of a `BtnMap` in reading order (`BtnMap::texts`).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Iterator

#### struct twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::MapBtn
A button of a static `BtnMap`: its text and initial control bits (relative width, checkable, …).
Fields:
- `text: &'static str` — The label (may be empty: a button without text).
- `ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl` — The control bits the button starts with.
Methods of `MapBtn`:
- `pub const fn new(text: &'static str, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl) -> Self` — A button showing `text` with control bits `ctrl`.
- `pub const fn text(text: &'static str) -> Self` — A button showing `text`, one width unit, no other control bits.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::OwnedMap
A button matrix map built at run time: the buttons' texts and initial control bits in reading order, and the number of buttons of each row. Each text is its own `String`, so a button's text can be replaced in place (`ButtonMatrix::set_btn_text` reuses its capacity).
Methods of `OwnedMap`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty map (no rows).
- `pub fn with_capacity(buttons: usize, rows: usize) -> Self` — An empty map with room for `buttons` buttons in `rows` rows.
- `pub fn push(&mut self, text: &str, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl)` — Appends a button to the last row (starting the first row of an empty map). A map holds at most `u16::MAX` buttons per row: more are ignored with a warning.
- `pub fn new_row(&mut self)` — Starts a new row: the buttons pushed next go there. A row without buttons takes its height but shows nothing.
- `pub fn btn_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of buttons.
- `pub fn row_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of rows.
- `pub fn text(&self, i: usize) -> Option<&str>` — The text of button `i`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<&twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap>, From<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::OwnedMap>

#### static twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::POPOVER_CLASS
`pub static POPOVER_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of the popover node: `"buttonmatrix_popover"`, no flags (not clickable, not scrollable, not focusable).

#### struct twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl
The control bits of one button (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_ctrl_t`, same values).
Methods of `BtnCtrl`:
- `const WIDTH_MASK: Self` — The relative width (`LV_BUTTONMATRIX_WIDTH_MASK`).
- `const HIDDEN: Self` — The button is not drawn and cannot be pressed; it still takes its width.
- `const NO_REPEAT: Self` — No repeated `ValueChanged` on long press.
- `const DISABLED: Self` — Drawn with the `DISABLED` styles and cannot be pressed.
- `const CHECKABLE: Self` — Toggles `CHECKED` when clicked.
- `const CHECKED: Self` — Checked (drawn with the `CHECKED` styles).
- `const CLICK_TRIG: Self` — `ValueChanged` on release instead of on press.
- `const POPOVER: Self` — Shows an enlarged key above the button while pressed (on the top layer); `ValueChanged` on release.
- `const RECOLOR: Self` — LVGL's text recoloring; kept for parity, ignored (logs a warning once).
- `const CUSTOM_1: Self` — Free for applications (the keyboard theme uses it for control keys).
- `const CUSTOM_2: Self` — Free for applications.
- `pub const fn empty() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all bits unset.
- `pub const fn all() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all known bits set.
- `pub const fn bits(&self) -> u16` — Get the underlying bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u16) -> Option<Self>` — Convert from a bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits_truncate(bits: u16) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value, unsetting any unknown bits.
- `pub const fn from_bits_retain(bits: u16) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value exactly.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self>` — Get a flags value with the bits of a flag with the given name set.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether all bits in `self` are unset.
- `pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool` — Whether all known bits in this flags value are set.
- `pub const fn intersects(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether any set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub const fn contains(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, other: Self)` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, other: Self, value: bool)` — Call `insert` when `value` is `true` or `remove` when `value` is `false`.
- `pub const fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise and (`&`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub const fn symmetric_difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn complement(self) -> Self` — The bitwise negation (`!`) of the bits in `self`, truncating the result.
- `pub const fn iter(&self) -> bitflags::iter::Iter<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>` — Yield a set of contained flags values.
- `pub const fn iter_names(&self) -> bitflags::iter::IterNames<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>` — Yield a set of contained named flags values.
- `pub const fn width(units: u8) -> twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl` — A relative width of `units` (clamped to 1…15).
- `pub const fn width_units(self) -> u32` — The relative width (LVGL `get_button_width`: 0 counts as 1).
- `pub const fn is_inactive(self) -> bool` — Hidden or disabled: the button cannot be selected (LVGL `button_is_hidden || button_is_inactive`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Flags, PublicFlags, Binary, Octal, LowerHex, UpperHex, BitOr, BitOrAssign, BitXor, BitXorAssign, BitAnd, BitAndAssign, Sub, SubAssign, Not, Extend<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>, FromIterator<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>, IntoIterator

#### struct twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::ButtonMatrix
A matrix of text buttons drawn by one widget (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix`): no node per button, so a keyboard of 40 keys costs one node.
Methods of `ButtonMatrix`:
- `pub fn new(map: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap) -> Self` — A button matrix with `map` (no areas until it is laid out).
- `pub fn map(&self) -> &twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap` — The map (the buttons' texts and initial control bits; the current bits are `btn_ctrl`).
- `pub fn btn_count(&self) -> u16` — The number of buttons.
- `pub fn row_count(&self) -> u16` — The number of rows.
- `pub fn btn_text(&self, idx: u16) -> Option<&str>` — The text of button `idx` (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_get_button_text`).
- `pub fn btn_ctrl(&self, idx: u16) -> Option<twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl>` — The control bits of button `idx`.
- `pub fn has_btn_ctrl(&self, idx: u16, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl) -> bool` — Whether button `idx` has every bit of `ctrl` (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_has_button_ctrl`).
- `pub fn selected_btn(&self) -> Option<u16>` — The selected (pressed or keyboard-selected) button (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_get_selected_button`).
- `pub fn one_checked(&self) -> bool` — Whether at most one button can be checked.
- `pub fn btn_area(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, idx: u16) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — The absolute area of button `idx` as of the last layout.
- `pub fn popover_node(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The popover node on the top layer, once one was shown.
- `pub fn set_map(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, map: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnMap)` — Sets the map (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_map` and `lv_buttonmatrix_set_ctrl_map` in one): the buttons, their texts and their control bits, which replace the current ones. Idempotent: the same map (the same static table, or an equal one) changes nothing, also not the control bits changed since. The selection is kept on the button that now occupies its position. The texts of an `OwnedMap` are cut to `Limits::max_text_len` like a label's text (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`, per cut text); a static map's texts are used as they are (in flash, never copied). The button tables are kept between maps: a map with more buttons than any before grows them. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_btn_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16, text: &str)` — Replaces the text of button `idx` in place (a static map is copied into an owned one first, once; after that the button's string is reused, so a text that fits its capacity allocates nothing — with `Limits::preallocate` a growing string is reserved for the full `max_text_len` at once). Cut to `Limits::max_text_len` like a label's text (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`). Redraws only that button; the layout is unchanged. Idempotent; an index out of range is ignored with a warning. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_btn_ctrl(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl)` — Adds `ctrl` bits to button `idx` (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_button_ctrl`); with `one_checked`, checking one unchecks the others. Idempotent.
- `pub fn clear_btn_ctrl(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl)` — Removes `ctrl` bits from button `idx` (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_clear_button_ctrl`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_btn_ctrl_all(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl)` — Adds `ctrl` to every button (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_button_ctrl_all`).
- `pub fn clear_btn_ctrl_all(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, ctrl: twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::BtnCtrl)` — Removes `ctrl` from every button (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_clear_button_ctrl_all`).
- `pub fn set_btn_width(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16, units: u8)` — Sets the relative width of button `idx` (1…15; LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_button_width`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_one_checked(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Allows at most one checked button (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_one_checked`: when enabled, only the first checked button stays checked). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_selected_btn(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: Option<u16>)` — Selects button `idx` (or none; LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_set_selected_button`). Idempotent; an index out of range is ignored with a warning.
- `pub fn btn_invalidation_area(&self, m: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, idx: u16) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — The absolute area redrawn when button `idx` changes (pressed, selected, checked): the button grown by the row and column gaps, at least `dpi / 10` (LVGL `invalidate_button_area`: outlines and shadows fit in the gaps).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::buttonmatrix::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a button matrix with LVGL's default map ("Btn1" … "Btn5"), 260 × 130 px, as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_buttonmatrix_create`).

### mod twine_widgets::container

`Container`: the base object (LVGL `lv_obj`), a styled rectangle holding children.

The engine's `Obj` is the container: class `"obj"`, parts `Main`
and `Scrollbar`, and LVGL's `lv_obj` default flags (`CLICKABLE`, `CLICK_FOCUSABLE`,
`SCROLLABLE`, `SCROLL_ELASTIC`, `SCROLL_MOMENTUM`, `SCROLL_WITH_ARROW`, `SCROLL_CHAIN`,
`SCROLL_ON_FOCUS`, `SNAPPABLE`, `PRESS_LOCK`, `GESTURE_BUBBLE`). The default theme draws it
as a card (white or dark background, grey border, rounded corners, padding).

`Card` is a container of its own class, `CARD_CLASS`: themes give it their card look
explicitly, whatever they do for plain objects (a theme that does not know it styles it
like a container, its `base`).

#### static twine_widgets::container::CARD_CLASS
`pub static CARD_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Card`: `"card"`, parts `Main` and `Scrollbar`, the base object's flags, base `CONTAINER_CLASS` (a theme without a card look styles it like a container).

#### struct twine_widgets::container::Card
A card: a `Container` that themes style with their card look (the default and mono themes' `card` style, the simple theme's white surface), so it looks like a card even where a theme draws plain containers differently. Behaves exactly like a container.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::container::create_card
`pub fn create_card(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a `Card` as the last child of `parent`. Its size is `Content` until set.
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

#### fn twine_widgets::container::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a container as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_obj_create`). Its size is `Content` (it wraps its children) until set.

- `CONTAINER_CLASS` = `twine_engine::OBJ_CLASS` (renamed)

#### enum twine_widgets::image::ImageAlign

Variants:

- `TopLeft` — Top left.
- `TopMid` — Top middle.
- `TopRight` — Top right.
- `BottomLeft` — Bottom left.
- `BottomMid` — Bottom middle.
- `BottomRight` — Bottom right.
- `LeftMid` — Left middle.
- `RightMid` — Right middle.

#### struct twine_widgets::image::Image
An image widget (LVGL `lv_image`): shows an `ImageSource` — a converted image in flash, encoded bytes (QOI, PNG, …) decoded through the engine's decoders and cache, a file read through `Engine::set_file_source`, or a symbol drawn as text.
Methods of `Image`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An image without a source.
- `pub fn src(&self) -> Option<&twine_image::ImageSource>` — The source.
- `pub fn header(&self) -> Option<twine_image::ImageHeader>` — The source's header (`None` without a source, for symbols and unreadable sources).
- `pub fn src_size(&self) -> twine_core::Size` — The source's size (0×0 without a readable source).
- `pub fn rotation(&self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The rotation.
- `pub fn scale_x(&self) -> twine_core::Scale` — The horizontal scale.
- `pub fn scale_y(&self) -> twine_core::Scale` — The vertical scale.
- `pub fn pivot(&self) -> twine_core::Point` — The pivot relative to the image's top-left corner.
- `pub fn antialias(&self) -> bool` — Whether transformed drawing is anti-aliased.
