- `pub fn offset(&self) -> twine_core::Point` — The offset of the image inside the widget.
- `pub fn blend_mode(&self) -> twine_render::BlendMode` — The blend mode.
- `pub fn set_src(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, src: twine_image::ImageSource)` — Sets the source. Idempotent (compared by identity: the same static image or byte slice, an equal path or symbol). The header is read right away (probing encoded data and files through the header cache) to size the widget; an unreadable source logs `warn!` and leaves an empty 0×0 image.
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, angle: twine_core::Angle)` — Sets the rotation around the pivot (normalized to 0…360°). Ignored (0) while the inner alignment scales the image itself. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_scale(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: twine_core::Scale)` — Sets both scales (256 = 1×; 0 counts as 1/256 and logs a warning). Ignored while the inner alignment scales the image itself. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_scale_x(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: twine_core::Scale)` — Sets the horizontal scale. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_scale_y(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: twine_core::Scale)` — Sets the vertical scale. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_pivot(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point)` — Sets the rotation / scale center relative to the image's top-left corner. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_antialias(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Bilinear filtering of transformed images. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_svg_cache(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Draws an SVG source from a copy rasterized once (at the source size) into the image cache instead of from the vector paths every time (faster redraws of static icons; scaling and rotating then resample the bitmap), feature `svg`. Idempotent.
- `pub fn svg_cache(&self) -> bool` — Whether SVG sources are drawn from a cached raster.
- `pub fn set_inner_align(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, align: twine_widgets::image::ImageAlign)` — Sets the inner alignment. `Stretch`, `Contain`, `Cover` and `Tile` set the scale (and reset rotation and pivot) themselves; leaving them resets the scale. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_offset(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point)` — Sets the offset of the image inside the widget. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_blend_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, m: twine_render::BlendMode)` — Sets the blend mode. Idempotent.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### enum twine_widgets::label::LabelText
Where a label's text lives: in flash (no allocation) or in an owned buffer whose capacity is reused by later texts.

- `Owned(String)` — An owned copy (LVGL `lv_label_set_text`).
Methods of `LabelText`:
- `pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str` — The text.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_widgets::label::Label
A text label (LVGL `lv_label`).
Methods of `Label`:
- `pub fn new(text: &'static str) -> Self` — A label showing `text` (a `'static` string, stored without copying).
- `pub fn with_class(self, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Self` — The label as a widget of another class: an LVGL subclass of the label that only changes the class (its name for themes and queries, flags), e.g. a list's text (`"list_text"`).
- `pub fn text(&self) -> &str` — The text.
- `pub fn text_storage(&self) -> &twine_widgets::label::LabelText` — The text storage.
- `pub fn shown_text(&self) -> &str` — The text as drawn: the `text`, or with a mask the bullets. Byte indices of `letter_pos`, `letter_on` and the selection refer to this text.
- `pub fn set_shaping(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Turns Arabic/Persian shaping of the drawn text on or off (feature `arabic-shaping`; default on, like LVGL's `LV_USE_ARABIC_PERSIAN_CHARS` labels). A textarea turns it off for its label. Idempotent.
- `pub fn is_masked(&self) -> bool` — Whether the text is masked.
- `pub fn set_mask(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, bullet: Option<&str>, reveal: Option<usize>)` — Masks the text (a Twine extension used by the textarea's password mode): every character is drawn as `bullet`, except the character at index `reveal` (and line breaks). `None` shows the text. `text` still returns the real text. Idempotent.
- `pub fn edit_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, f: impl FnOnce(&mut String))` — Edits the text in place with `f` (a Twine extension for the textarea: inserting or removing characters reuses the buffer's capacity). A `'static` text is copied into the owned buffer first. Always redraws and re-measures. The result is cut to `Limits::max_text_len` like `set_text`.
- `pub fn long_mode(&self) -> twine_text::LongMode` — The long mode.
- `pub fn max_lines(&self) -> u16` — The line limit (0 = unlimited).
- `pub fn selection(&self) -> Option<(usize, usize)>` — The selected byte range (start ≤ end), if any.
- `pub fn scroll_offset(&self) -> twine_core::Point` — The offset the text is drawn at (scrolling long modes).
- `pub fn dots_end(&self) -> Option<usize>` — In `Dots` mode when the text is cut: the byte index where the visible text ends and `"..."` follows.
- `pub fn text_size(&self) -> twine_core::Size` — Size of the laid-out text as of the last refresh (LVGL `text_size`).
- `pub fn set_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &str)` — Sets the text, copying it into the label's own buffer. Idempotent: an equal text does nothing. A different text overwrites the buffer in place (`clear` + `push_str`, so no allocation when it fits), invalidates the label and marks its layout if it is content-sized. A text longer than `Limits::max_text_len` is cut at a character boundary (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`); with `Limits::preallocate` the buffer is reserved to that length when it first grows.
- `pub fn set_text_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &'static str)` — Sets a `'static` text without copying (LVGL `lv_label_set_text_static`). Idempotent. An owned buffer is kept for later `set_text` calls.
- `pub fn write_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, f: impl FnOnce(&mut String)) -> bool` — Builds the text in place with `f` (which receives an empty buffer) and applies it if it differs from the current text; returns whether it changed. Two buffers are swapped, so formatting a text of a stable length never allocates (with `Limits::preallocate`, both are reserved to `Limits::max_text_len`). The result is cut to `Limits::max_text_len` like `set_text`.
- `pub fn set_long_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, m: twine_text::LongMode)` — Sets the long mode. Idempotent. Stops the scroll animations and resets the offset (LVGL `lv_label_set_long_mode`).
- `pub fn set_max_lines(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, n: u16)` — Limits the number of lines of a content-sized label (0 = unlimited). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_selection(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, start: usize, end: usize)` — Selects the bytes `start..end` (in any order; clamped to the text and rounded down to character boundaries). Idempotent; an empty range clears the selection.
- `pub fn clear_selection(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Removes the selection. Idempotent.
- `pub fn letter_pos(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, byte_idx: usize) -> twine_core::Point` — Position of the character at byte `byte_idx` relative to the top-left corner of the content area (LVGL `lv_label_get_letter_pos`).
- `pub fn letter_on(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point) -> usize` — Byte index of the character at `p` (relative to the top-left corner of the content area; LVGL `lv_label_get_letter_on`).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::label::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a label showing "Text" as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_label_create`).

LVGL `LV_LED_BRIGHT_MIN` (80 of 255): the brightness of an LED that is off.

#### const twine_widgets::led::LED_BRIGHT_MAX

LVGL `LV_LED_BRIGHT_MAX` (255 of 255): the brightness of an LED that is on.

#### const twine_widgets::led::LED_DEFAULT_SIZE

LVGL `lv_led_class.width_def` / `height_def`: `LV_DPI_DEF / 5`.

#### const twine_widgets::led::LED_DEFAULT_COLOR
`pub const LED_DEFAULT_COLOR: twine_core::Color`
The color an LED shows when its color is a design element its display's theme does not define (e.g. no theme): LVGL's default primary color (blue 500, `#2196F3`).

#### static twine_widgets::led::LED_CLASS
`pub static LED_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Led`: `"led"`, part `Main`, the base object's flags (LVGL `lv_led_class`).

#### struct twine_widgets::led::Led
An LED (LVGL `lv_led`): a circle (with the default theme) whose background, border, outline and shadow colors take the LED's color, darkened by its brightness; the shadow ("glow") shrinks with the brightness.
Methods of `Led`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An LED, on, in the theme's `design::PRIMARY` (LVGL `lv_led_constructor`); it shows `LED_DEFAULT_COLOR` until it is created (and where the theme does not define the element).
- `pub fn color(&self) -> twine_core::Color` — The color as drawn: `color_value` resolved for the LED's display.
- `pub fn color_value(&self) -> twine_style::design::ColorValue` — The color as set: a fixed color or a design element (default `design::PRIMARY`).
- `pub fn brightness(&self) -> twine_core::Fraction` — The brightness (`LED_BRIGHT_MIN ..= LED_BRIGHT_MAX`).
- `pub fn is_on(&self) -> bool` — Whether the LED is brighter than halfway (LVGL `lv_led_toggle`'s test).
- `pub fn set_color(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, c: impl Into<twine_style::design::ColorValue>)` — Sets the color: a `Color` or a design element such as `design::DANGER` (followed through theme mode switches). Idempotent; redraws only when the drawn color changes.
- `pub fn set_brightness(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, b: twine_core::Fraction)` — Sets the brightness, clamped to `LED_BRIGHT_MIN ..= LED_BRIGHT_MAX` (LVGL's 80…255 of 255: an LED is never fully black). Idempotent.
- `pub fn on(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Full brightness (LVGL `lv_led_on`).
- `pub fn off(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Minimal brightness (LVGL `lv_led_off`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Off when brighter than halfway, else on (LVGL `lv_led_toggle`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::led::color_brightness
`pub const fn color_brightness(c: twine_core::Color) -> u8`
LVGL `lv_color_brightness`: `(3 r + g + 4 b) / 8`.

#### fn twine_widgets::led::create

#### struct twine_widgets::slider::Slider
A slider (LVGL `lv_slider`): a `Bar` whose value is set by dragging a knob (`Part::Knob`), with the arrow keys, or by turning an encoder in edit mode.
Methods of `Slider`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A slider with range 0…100 and value 0.
- `pub fn bar(&self) -> &twine_widgets::bar::Bar` — The underlying bar state (range, mode, orientation, values).
- `pub fn value(&self) -> i32` — The value (of the right knob in range mode).

- `pub fn min(&self) -> i32` — The minimum.
- `pub fn max(&self) -> i32` — The maximum.
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_widgets::slider::SliderMode` — The mode.
- `pub fn is_dragged(&self) -> bool` — Whether a knob is being dragged (LVGL `lv_slider_is_dragged`).
- `pub fn left_knob_focused(&self) -> bool` — Whether the left knob has the keypad / encoder focus (range mode).
- `pub fn set_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32, anim: bool)` — Sets the value (see `Bar::set_value`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_left_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32, anim: bool)` — Sets the left knob's value in range mode (see `Bar::set_start_value`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_range(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, min: i32, max: i32)` — Sets the range (see `Bar::set_range`: any pair of `i32`s, mapped exactly). Dragging maps the pointer back in `i64` too (`(rel · (max − min) + len / 2) / len + min`, the pointer clamped to the track first). Idempotent. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets::slider::SliderMode)` — Sets the mode. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_orientation(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, o: twine_widgets::Orientation)` — Sets the orientation. Idempotent.
- `pub fn knob_areas(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> (twine_core::Rect, Option<twine_core::Rect>)` — The knob areas: `(right, left)`; the left one only in range mode (LVGL `draw_knob`, `position_knob`).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

### mod twine_widgets::spangroup

`SpanGroup`: rich text made of `Span`s with their own styles (LVGL `lv_spangroup`).

#### static twine_widgets::spangroup::SPANGROUP_CLASS
`pub static SPANGROUP_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `SpanGroup`: `"spangroup"`, part `Main`, the base object's flags (LVGL `lv_spangroup_class`).

#### struct twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId
The handle of a `Span` in its `SpanGroup` (stays valid while the span exists).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

#### enum twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanMode
How a `SpanGroup` sizes itself (LVGL `lv_span_mode_t`, derived from the size styles like LVGL master).
Variants:
- `Fixed` — Fixed width and height; text beyond them is clipped (or ellipsized).
- `Expand` — As wide and tall as the text on one line (width and height `Content`).
- `Break` — A fixed width, lines break, the height follows the text.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanOverflow
What a `SpanGroup` does with text beyond its height (LVGL `lv_span_overflow_t`).
Variants:
- `Clip` — Cut it off.
- `Ellipsis` — End the last visible line with "...".
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_widgets::spangroup::Span
One run of text with its own text style (LVGL `lv_span_t`). Unset properties fall back to the group's `Main` style (LVGL `lv_span_get_style_*`). Only the text properties are used: font, color, opacity, decoration, letter space.
Methods of `Span`:
- `pub fn text(&self) -> &str` — The text.
- `pub fn set_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &str) -> bool` — Sets the text (copied, reusing the buffer); returns whether it changed. Call `SpanGroup::refresh` afterwards (or use `SpanGroup::set_span_text`).
- `pub fn set_text_static(&mut self, s: &'static str) -> bool` — Sets a `'static` text without copying; returns whether it changed.
- `pub fn style(&self) -> &twine_style::StyleBuf` — The span's own style.
- `pub fn set_style(&mut self, p: twine_style::StyleProp) -> bool` — Sets a style property of the span (text properties only are used); returns whether it changed.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanLine
A line of a `SpanGroup`'s layout (see `SpanGroup::line_layout`).
Fields:
- `y: i32` — Top of the line relative to the content area.
- `height: i32` — The line height (the tallest span's line height plus the line space).
- `pieces: Vec<(twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId, Range<usize>, i32, i32)>` — The pieces on the line: span, byte range of its text, x (before alignment) and width.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanGroup
Rich text (LVGL `lv_spangroup`): `Span`s, each with its own font, color, opacity, decoration and letter space, flowed together like one paragraph.
Methods of `SpanGroup`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty group (clip overflow, no indent, no line limit).
- `pub fn span_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of spans.
- `pub fn span_ids(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId> + '_` — The span ids in order.
- `pub fn span(&self, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId) -> Option<&twine_widgets::spangroup::Span>` — A span.
- `pub fn span_mut(&mut self, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId) -> Option<&mut twine_widgets::spangroup::Span>` — A span, mutably: call `refresh` after changing it.
- `pub fn overflow(&self) -> twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanOverflow` — The overflow handling.
- `pub fn indent(&self) -> i32` — The first line's indent in px.
- `pub fn max_lines(&self) -> i32` — The line limit of `Break` mode (-1: none).
- `pub fn mode(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanMode` — The mode, derived from the size styles like LVGL master (`lv_spangroup_get_mode`).
- `pub fn add_span(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>) -> twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId` — Appends an empty span (LVGL `lv_spangroup_add_span`).
- `pub fn delete_span(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId)` — Removes a span (LVGL `lv_spangroup_delete_span`). Unknown ids are ignored.
- `pub fn set_span_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId, s: &str)` — Sets the text of a span (LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_span_text`), cut to `Limits::max_text_len` (`Span::set_text`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_span_text_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId, s: &'static str)` — Sets a `'static` span text without copying. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_span_style(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, id: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId, p: twine_style::StyleProp)` — Sets a style property of a span (LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_span_style`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanMode)` — Sets the mode (LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_mode`, which sets the size styles: `Expand` makes both `Content`, `Break` gives a content width a fixed 100 px and a `Content` height, `Fixed` gives `Content` sizes 100 px).
- `pub fn set_overflow(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, o: twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanOverflow)` — Sets the overflow handling (LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_overflow`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_indent(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, px: i32)` — Indents the first line by `px` (LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_indent`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_max_lines(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, n: i32)` — Limits `Break` mode to `n` lines (-1: no limit; LVGL `lv_spangroup_set_max_lines`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_align(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, align: twine_text::TextAlign)` — Sets the text alignment (the `TextAlign` style, like LVGL's deprecated `lv_spangroup_set_align`).
- `pub fn refresh(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Re-lays out and redraws the group after spans changed (LVGL `lv_spangroup_refresh`).
- `pub fn expand_width(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, max: i32) -> i32` — LVGL `lv_spangroup_get_expand_width`: the width of all spans on one line (plus the indent), at most `max` (0: no limit).
- `pub fn max_line_height(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> i32` — The tallest line height of the spans (LVGL `lv_spangroup_get_max_line_height`).
- `pub fn expand_height(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, width: i32) -> i32` — LVGL `lv_spangroup_get_expand_height`: the height of the text wrapped at `width` (at most `max_lines` lines).
- `pub fn line_layout(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> Vec<twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanLine>` — The line layout at the current width (for inspection; allocates).
- `pub fn span_by_point(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point) -> Option<twine_widgets::spangroup::SpanId>` — The span at the absolute point `p` (LVGL `lv_spangroup_get_span_by_point`; here the drawn pieces are hit exactly).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::spangroup::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates an empty span group (sized to its text) as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_spangroup_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

### mod twine_widgets::spinbox

#### const twine_widgets::spinbox::SPINBOX_MAX_DIGITS

The most digits a spinbox shows (the value is an `i32`).

#### static twine_widgets::spinbox::SPINBOX_CLASS
`pub static SPINBOX_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Spinbox`: `"spinbox"`, the textarea's parts, flags and focus behaviour (LVGL `lv_spinbox_class`, a subclass of `lv_textarea_class`).

#### const twine_widgets::spinbox::SPINBOX_DEFAULT_WIDTH

LVGL `lv_spinbox_class.width_def`: `LV_DPI_DEF`.

#### fn twine_widgets::spinbox::format_value
`pub fn format_value(buf: &mut [u8; 16], value: i32, digit_count: u8, dec_point_pos: u8, signed: bool, step: u32) -> (&str, usize)`
Formats `value` like LVGL `lv_spinbox_updatevalue` into `buf`: a sign when negative values are possible, leading zeros up to `digit_count`, a decimal point after `dec_point_pos` integer digits (0: none). Returns the text and the cursor position for `step`.

#### struct twine_widgets::spinbox::Spinbox
A numeric editor (LVGL `lv_spinbox`): a one-line `Textarea` showing an integer with a fixed number of digits, an optional sign and decimal point, and a cursor highlighting the digit that `increment` / `decrement` change.
Methods of `Spinbox`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A spinbox with LVGL's defaults: value 0, range −99 999…99 999, 5 digits, step 1, no rollover, digits stepping to the right.
- `pub fn textarea(&self) -> &twine_widgets::textarea::Textarea` — The textarea part.
- `pub fn textarea_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_widgets::textarea::Textarea` — The textarea part, mutably (text constraints, cursor…).
- `pub fn value(&self) -> i32` — The value.
- `pub fn range(&self) -> (i32, i32)` — The range `(min, max)`.
- `pub fn step(&self) -> u32` — The step (a power of ten: the digit the cursor is on).
- `pub fn digit_count(&self) -> u8` — The number of digits.
- `pub fn dec_point_pos(&self) -> u8` — The number of integer digits before the decimal point (0: none).
- `pub fn rollover(&self) -> bool` — Whether stepping past an end wraps to the other end.
- `pub fn digit_step_direction(&self) -> twine_style::Side` — The direction the step digit moves on an encoder click.
- `pub fn set_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32)` — Sets the value, clamped to the range (LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_value`; no `ValueChanged`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_range(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, min: i32, max: i32)` — Sets the range; the value is clamped (LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_range`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_digit_format(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, count: u8, sep_pos: u8)` — Sets the number of digits (1…10) and the integer digits before the decimal point (0: none; ≥ `count` also none). The range shrinks to what the digits can show (LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_digit_format`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_step(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, step: u32)` — Sets the step (LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_step`; use powers of ten). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_rollover(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Wrap around at the ends (LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_rollover`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_digit_step_direction(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, dir: twine_style::Side)` — The direction an encoder click moves the step digit (`Side::Right` or `Side::Left`; `Top`/`Bottom` act as `Left`; LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_digit_step_direction`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_cursor_pos(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, pos: u32)` — Puts the step on digit `pos` counted from the right (0 = ones; LVGL `lv_spinbox_set_cursor_pos`). Ignored when that digit exceeds the range.
- `pub fn step_next(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the step one digit right (÷ 10, at least 1; LVGL `lv_spinbox_step_next`).
- `pub fn step_prev(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the step one digit left (× 10 while within the range; LVGL `lv_spinbox_step_prev`).
- `pub fn increment(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Adds the step (LVGL `lv_spinbox_increment`: crossing zero keeps the digits, e.g. −3 + 10 = 3; at the maximum it wraps with rollover, else clamps). Sends `ValueChanged` when the value changes.
- `pub fn decrement(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Subtracts the step (LVGL `lv_spinbox_decrement`, mirrored). Sends `ValueChanged` when the value changes.
- `pub fn text<'e>(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'e>) -> &'e str` — The text as shown (read from the label).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets::spinbox::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a spinbox, 130 px wide and one line high, as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_spinbox_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

#### struct twine_widgets::textarea::Textarea
A text input (LVGL `lv_textarea`): a scrollable container holding a `Label` child with the text, a blinking cursor, an optional placeholder, a password mode and input constraints.
Methods of `Textarea`:
- `pub fn add_char(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, c: char)` — Inserts `c` at the cursor and moves the cursor after it (LVGL `lv_textarea_add_char`). Rejected characters (see the constraints) are ignored.
- `pub fn add_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &str)` — Inserts `s` at the cursor and moves the cursor after it (LVGL `lv_textarea_add_text`). With a length limit or an accepted list the characters are checked one by one.
- `pub fn delete_char(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Deletes the character before the cursor (backspace; LVGL `lv_textarea_delete_char`), or the selected text.
- `pub fn delete_char_forward(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Deletes the character at the cursor (the `Del` key; LVGL `lv_textarea_delete_char_forward`), or the selected text.
- `pub fn set_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &str)` — Replaces the text and puts the cursor at the end (LVGL `lv_textarea_set_text`; with a length limit or an accepted list the characters are checked one by one). Idempotent: the same text changes nothing (the cursor stays).
- `pub fn set_cursor_pos(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, pos: i32)` — Places the cursor before character `pos` (LVGL `lv_textarea_set_cursor_pos`): negative positions count from the end, `CURSOR_LAST` (or anything past the end) is the end. Scrolls to the cursor and restarts the blink. Idempotent.
- `pub fn cursor_right(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the cursor one character right (LVGL `lv_textarea_cursor_right`).
- `pub fn cursor_left(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the cursor one character left (LVGL `lv_textarea_cursor_left`).
- `pub fn cursor_down(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the cursor one line down, keeping its x (LVGL `lv_textarea_cursor_down`).
- `pub fn cursor_up(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Moves the cursor one line up, keeping its x (LVGL `lv_textarea_cursor_up`).
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty textarea (its label is created when it is inserted into a tree).
- `pub fn label(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The label node holding the text (LVGL `lv_textarea_get_label`).
- `pub fn text<'e>(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'e>) -> &'e str` — The text (the real text in password mode; LVGL `lv_textarea_get_text`).
- `pub fn cursor(&self) -> twine_widgets::textarea::CursorState` — The cursor state.
- `pub fn cursor_pos(&self) -> usize` — The cursor position in characters (LVGL `lv_textarea_get_cursor_pos`).
- `pub fn cursor_area(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> twine_core::Rect` — The cursor's absolute area as drawn.
- `pub fn placeholder_text(&self) -> &str` — The placeholder text (`""` when none).
- `pub fn password_mode(&self) -> bool` — Whether password mode is on.
- `pub fn password_bullet<'s>(&'s self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> &'s str` — The password bullet: the one set, else `PWD_BULLET` if the font has it, else `"*"` (LVGL `lv_textarea_get_password_bullet`).
- `pub fn password_show_time(&self) -> twine_core::Duration` — How long the last typed password character stays visible.
- `pub fn one_line(&self) -> bool` — Whether one-line mode is on.
- `pub fn accepted_chars(&self) -> Option<&twine_widgets::textarea::AcceptedChars>` — The accepted characters.
- `pub fn max_length(&self) -> u32` — The maximum length in characters (0 = unlimited).
- `pub fn cursor_click_pos(&self) -> bool` — Whether a press places the cursor.
- `pub fn text_selection(&self) -> bool` — Whether text selection with the pointer is enabled.
- `pub fn text_is_selected(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> bool` — Whether some text is selected (LVGL `lv_textarea_text_is_selected`).
- `pub fn selection(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> Option<(usize, usize)>` — The selected character range (start < end), if any.
- `pub fn current_char(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> Option<char>` — The character before the cursor (LVGL `lv_textarea_get_current_char`).
- `pub fn set_placeholder_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &str)` — Sets (or removes) the placeholder shown while the text is empty (LVGL `lv_textarea_set_placeholder_text`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_placeholder_text_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, s: &'static str)` — Sets a `'static` placeholder without copying. Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_cursor_click_pos(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Enables placing the cursor by pressing (LVGL `lv_textarea_set_cursor_click_pos`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_max_length(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, n: u32)` — Limits the text to `n` characters (0 = unlimited; LVGL `lv_textarea_set_max_length`). Idempotent; an existing longer text is kept.

## crate twine_widgets_ext

Documented with features: `std,vector,bidi,arabic-shaping`.

**twine-widgets-ext**

The complex widgets of the Twine GUI library, each a port of the LVGL widget of the same
name, built on the basic widgets of `twine-widgets`. The last column lists the
`WidgetClass::name` of each class (diagnostics only:
themes match the `*_CLASS` statics by identity, not by name):

| Widget | LVGL | Class names |
|--------|------|-----------------------|
| `Dropdown` | `lv_dropdown` | `dropdown`, `dropdown_list` |
| `Roller` | `lv_roller` | `roller` |
| `List` | `lv_list` | `list`, `list_text`, `list_button` |
| `Menu` | `lv_menu` | `menu`, `menu_page`, `menu_cont`, `menu_section`, `menu_separator`, `menu_main_container`, `menu_main_header_container`, `menu_sidebar_container`, `menu_sidebar_header_container` |
| `Tabview` | `lv_tabview` | `tabview`, `tabview_tab_bar`, `tabview_content` |
| `Tileview` | `lv_tileview` | `tileview`, `tileview_tile` |
| `Window` | `lv_win` | `win`, `win_header`, `win_content` |
| `VectorView` (feature `vector`) | `lv_draw_vector` in a canvas | `vector_view` |
| `Msgbox` | `lv_msgbox` | `msgbox`, `msgbox_backdrop`, `msgbox_header`, `msgbox_content`, `msgbox_footer`, `msgbox_header_button`, `msgbox_footer_button` |

**Conventions**

The conventions of `twine-widgets` apply: a module `x` has `pub struct X`, `pub static
X_CLASS: WidgetClass` and `pub fn create(engine, parent)`; setters take a
`WidgetCx`, are idempotent (P3) and log
`trace!(target: "twine::engine", "<class>#<node> set_<name>")`; the look comes from styles
only; invalid input logs `warn!` and is ignored (P7).

Composite widgets (a window's header, a menu's pages) are made of child nodes of their own
classes, so themes style each part by class identity (`&'static WidgetClass`, like LVGL's
`lv_obj_check_type`); `twine-theme` depends on this crate for the class statics. Popups (a
dropdown's option list) live on the display's top layer while open and are deleted when
closed.

**Features**

- `std`, `log`, `defmt`: as in every Twine crate.
- `vector`: `vector_view::VectorView` over `twine-vector`.
- `bidi`, `arabic-shaping`: right-to-left text; shaped dropdown and roller options.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints.

#### enum twine_widgets_ext::Options
The options of a `Dropdown` or a `Roller`: `'\n'`-separated options in flash (`Static`) or owned (`Owned`, one allocation reused by later lists), or a `&'static` slice of options (`Slice`: zero-copy, e.g. a table of translated names).
Variants:
- `Static(&'static str)` — A `'static` string of `'\n'`-separated options (LVGL `set_options_static`).
- `Slice(&'static [&'static str])` — A `'static` slice, one option per element (stored by reference).
- `Owned(String)` — An owned copy of `'\n'`-separated options (LVGL `set_options`); its capacity is reused by later option lists.
- `Shaped { source: twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions, shaped: String }` — `'static` options with Arabic/Persian letters, stored with their contextual forms (feature `arabic-shaping`, like LVGL's `LV_USE_ARABIC_PERSIAN_CHARS`).
Methods of `Options`:
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> twine_widgets_ext::OptionsIter<'_>` — The options in order (none for an empty list). Allocation-free.
- `pub fn count(&self) -> u16` — The number of options: `'\n'`s + 1 (0 for an empty string; LVGL `count_options_in_str`, whose empty list is `NULL`), or the slice's length — at most `u16::MAX`.
- `pub fn get(&self, i: u16) -> Option<&str>` — Option `i` (`None` past the end).
- `pub fn index_of(&self, option: &str) -> Option<u16>` — The index of the option equal to `option` (LVGL `get_option_index`).
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — The length in bytes of the options joined with `'\n'`.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether there are no options.
- `pub fn measure(&self, font: &'static twine_text::Font, letter_space: i32, line_space: i32) -> twine_core::Size` — The size of the options laid out one per line in `font`: the widest option, and `n × line_height + (n − 1) × line_space` (one empty line for no options), like a label of the joined text. Allocation-free.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, IntoIterator, Display, PartialEq<str>, PartialEq<&str>

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::OptionsIter<'a>
The options of an `Options`, in order (`Options::iter`).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Iterator

#### enum twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions
`'static` options handed to `set_options_static` of a `Dropdown` or a `Roller`: stored by reference, never copied (unless they need Arabic shaping).
Variants:
- `Str(&'static str)` — Options separated by `'\n'` (LVGL's format).
- `Slice(&'static [&'static str])` — One option per element (an option must not contain `'\n'`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<&'static str>, From<&'static [&'static str]>, From<&'static [&'static str; N]>

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::ClassObj
A plain container of its own class: the building block of composite widgets (LVGL `lv_obj` subclasses without data, e.g. a window's header or a menu's section).
Fields:
- `0: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass`
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Widget

### mod twine_widgets_ext::dropdown

#### static twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::DROPDOWN_LIST_CLASS
`pub static DROPDOWN_LIST_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `DropdownList`: `"dropdown_list"`, parts `Main`, `Scrollbar` and `Selected` (the selected and the pressed option), not click-focusable, no scroll on focus (LVGL `lv_dropdownlist_class` constructor). `Selected` is drawn per option in its own state.

#### const twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::DROPDOWN_DEFAULT_WIDTH

#### const twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::DROPDOWN_DEFAULT_SYMBOL
`pub const DROPDOWN_DEFAULT_SYMBOL: twine_image::ImageSource`
The default symbol: `SYMBOL_DOWN` (drawn as `SYMBOL_UP` when the list opens upwards).

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::Dropdown
A dropdown (LVGL `lv_dropdown`): shows the selected option (or a fixed `text`) and a symbol; a click opens the options as a `DropdownList` on the display's top layer, below the dropdown (or above, left, right: `set_dir`; it flips to the other side when there is more room there).
Methods of `Dropdown`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A dropdown with LVGL's defaults: three options ("Option 1" … "Option 3"), the first selected, opening downwards, `SYMBOL_DOWN`, selected highlight on.
- `pub fn with_options(options: impl Into<twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions>) -> Self` — A dropdown showing `options` (a `'\n'`-separated `&'static str` or a `&'static` slice of options, stored without copying).
- `pub fn options(&self) -> &twine_widgets_ext::Options` — The options (they compare equal to their `'\n'`-joined text and display as it).
- `pub fn option_count(&self) -> u16` — The number of options.
- `pub fn selected(&self) -> u16` — The index of the selected option (while the list is open with keys moving the highlight: the highlighted one, LVGL `lv_dropdown_get_selected`).
- `pub fn selected_str(&self, buf: &mut String)` — Writes the confirmed selected option into `buf` (cleared first; LVGL `lv_dropdown_get_selected_str`).
- `pub fn option_index(&self, option: &str) -> Option<u16>` — The index of the option equal to `option` (LVGL `lv_dropdown_get_option_index`).
- `pub fn dir(&self) -> twine_style::Side` — The direction the list opens to.
- `pub fn symbol(&self) -> Option<&twine_image::ImageSource>` — The symbol (`None`: no symbol).
- `pub fn text(&self) -> Option<&str>` — The fixed text shown instead of the selected option.
- `pub fn selected_highlight(&self) -> bool` — Whether the selected option is highlighted in the list.
- `pub fn list(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The list node while open.
- `pub fn is_open(&self, e: &twine_engine::Engine) -> bool` — Whether the list is open.
- `pub fn pressed_option(&self) -> Option<u16>` — The option pressed in the list, if any.
- `pub fn set_options(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, options: &str)` — Sets the options (`'\n'`-separated), copied into the owned buffer (its capacity is reused); the selection goes to the first option (LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_options`). The options are one widget text: cut to `Limits::max_text_len` bytes like a label's text (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`), and with `Limits::preallocate` the buffer is reserved for the limit when it first grows, so later option lists allocate nothing. Idempotent: the same options change nothing (and keep the selection).
- `pub fn set_options_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, options: impl Into<twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions>)` — Sets `'static` options — a `'\n'`-separated `&'static str` or a `&'static` slice of options — stored without copying (LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_options_static`); the selection goes to the first option. Idempotent (the same `'static` data changes nothing). Never panics.
- `pub fn add_option(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, option: &str, pos: u32)` — Inserts `option` before option `pos` (`u32::MAX` or any index past the end: at the end; LVGL `lv_dropdown_add_option`), in place in the owned buffer (static options are copied into it first). The selection index is kept. Refused (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`) when the options would exceed `Limits::max_text_len` bytes.
- `pub fn clear_options(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Removes every option (LVGL `lv_dropdown_clear_options`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_selected(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16)` — Selects option `idx` (clamped to the last one; LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_selected`, no `ValueChanged`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_dir(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, dir: twine_style::Side)` — The side the list opens to (`Side::Bottom` by default; LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_dir`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_symbol(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, symbol: Option<twine_image::ImageSource>)` — The symbol drawn at the side (`None` hides it; LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_symbol`). A `ImageSource::Symbol` is text in the `Indicator` font; other sources are images (rotated by the `Indicator`'s `transform_rotation`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_text(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, text: Option<&str>)` — A fixed text shown instead of the selected option (copied; `None`: the selected option; LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_text`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_text_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, text: Option<&'static str>)` — A fixed `'static` text (stored without copying; LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_text_static`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_selected_highlight(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Highlights the selected option in the list (LVGL `lv_dropdown_set_selected_highlight`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn open(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Opens the list (LVGL `lv_dropdown_open`): creates it on the top layer of the dropdown's display, sized to the options (at most the space to the screen edge and the list's `max_height`), placed on the side of `dir` (the opposite side when it has more room), scrolled to the selected option. Adds `CHECKED` to the dropdown and sends `Ready`. Opening an open list does nothing.
- `pub fn close(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Closes the list (LVGL `lv_dropdown_close`): deletes it (after a fade-out when the list has an `anim_duration`), removes `CHECKED` from the dropdown and sends `Cancel`. The selection is left as it is.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a dropdown, 130 px wide and content high, as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_dropdown_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::dropdown::DropdownList
The option list of an open `Dropdown` (LVGL `lv_dropdownlist`): a scrollable node on the top layer drawing the owner's options with the `Main` text style and the selected / pressed option with the `Selected` styles in the `CHECKED` / `PRESSED` states.

Implements: Debug, Widget

- `pub fn set_title_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, title: Option<&'static str>)` — Sets a `'static` title (LVGL `lv_menu_set_page_title_static`). Idempotent.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::menu::Menu
A menu (LVGL `lv_menu`). Build pages with `page_create`, fill them with `cont_create` rows (and `section_create`, `separator_create`), link rows to pages with `set_load_page_event` and show the root with `Menu::set_page`. Loading a page pushes it on the history; the header's back button pops it. With a sidebar page (`Menu::set_sidebar_page`) the menu has two columns, and the sidebar row whose page is loaded is `CHECKED`. Page switches are instant (LVGL).
Methods of `Menu`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A menu (its child nodes are created by `init`).
- `pub fn cur_main_page(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The page shown in the main area (LVGL `lv_menu_get_cur_main_page`).
- `pub fn cur_sidebar_page(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The page shown in the sidebar (LVGL `lv_menu_get_cur_sidebar_page`).
- `pub fn main_header(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The main header (LVGL `lv_menu_get_main_header`).
- `pub fn main_header_back_button(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The main header's back button (LVGL `lv_menu_get_main_header_back_button`).
- `pub fn main_header_title(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The main header's title label.
- `pub fn sidebar_header(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The sidebar header (LVGL `lv_menu_get_sidebar_header`), with a sidebar.
- `pub fn sidebar_header_back_button(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The sidebar header's back button (LVGL `lv_menu_get_sidebar_header_back_button`).
- `pub fn sidebar_container(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The sidebar column, with a sidebar.
- `pub fn main_container(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The main column (header and page).
- `pub fn storage(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The hidden node holding the pages not shown.
- `pub fn history(&self) -> &[twine_engine::NodeId]` — The loaded pages, the current one last.
- `pub fn mode_header(&self) -> twine_widgets_ext::menu::MenuHeaderMode` — The header mode.
- `pub fn mode_root_back_button(&self) -> bool` — Whether the root page shows a back button.
- `pub fn selected_tab(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The sidebar row whose page is loaded.
- `pub fn back_button_is_root(&self, btn: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether a click on `btn` goes nowhere back: the sidebar's back button, or the main back button on the root page (LVGL `lv_menu_back_button_is_root`; checked in a click handler of the back button, the depth before the click counts).
- `pub fn set_page(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, page: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>)` — Shows `page` in the main area and pushes it on the history (`None`: shows nothing and clears the history; LVGL `lv_menu_set_page`). Updates the header title and the back buttons, marks the selected sidebar row and sends `ValueChanged`.
- `pub fn refresh_titles(&self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Shows the titles of the loaded pages in the headers again, e.g. after the title of a loaded page changed (a page title shows when the page is loaded).
- `pub fn set_sidebar_page(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, page: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>)` — Shows `page` in a sidebar (created on first use) and reloads the main page (`None`: removes the sidebar; LVGL `lv_menu_set_sidebar_page`).
- `pub fn set_mode_header(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets_ext::menu::MenuHeaderMode)` — Where the headers go (LVGL `lv_menu_set_mode_header`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_mode_root_back_button(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Whether the root page shows a back button (LVGL `lv_menu_set_mode_root_back_button`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn clear_history(&mut self)` — Empties the history (LVGL `lv_menu_clear_history`): the next page loaded is a root.
- `pub fn load_page(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, row: twine_engine::NodeId, page: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Loads `page` because `row` was clicked (LVGL `lv_menu_load_page_event_cb`): a row of the sidebar becomes the selected one (`CHECKED`) and starts a new history; without a sidebar the focus moves on to the page.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets_ext::menu::create

### mod twine_widgets_ext::roller

`Roller`: a drum-style picker (LVGL `lv_roller`).

#### static twine_widgets_ext::roller::ROLLER_CLASS
`pub static ROLLER_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Roller`: `"roller"`, parts `Main` and `Selected` (the band in the middle and the text on it), the base object's flags without `SCROLLABLE` and `SCROLL_CHAIN_VER` (dragging moves the options, not a parent), always in the default focus group, editable (LVGL `lv_roller_class` and constructor).

#### const twine_widgets_ext::roller::ROLLER_DEFAULT_HEIGHT
`pub const ROLLER_DEFAULT_HEIGHT: i32 = util::DPI_DEF`
LVGL `lv_roller_class.height_def`: `LV_DPI_DEF`.

#### const twine_widgets_ext::roller::ROLLER_DEFAULT_OPTIONS
`pub const ROLLER_DEFAULT_OPTIONS: &str`
The options of a new roller (LVGL with `LV_WIDGETS_HAS_DEFAULT_VALUE`).

#### enum twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode
How a roller ends.
Variants:
- `Normal` — The first and the last option are the ends.
- `Infinite` — The options repeat endlessly (LVGL `LV_ROLLER_MODE_INFINITE`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::roller::Roller
A roller (LVGL `lv_roller`): the options in a column that the user drags (or steps with keys / an encoder) under a selection band in the middle; releasing snaps the nearest option into the band with an animation (the `Main` `anim_duration`, 200 ms in the default theme).
Methods of `Roller`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A roller with LVGL's defaults: five options ("Option 1" … "Option 5"), normal mode, the first selected.
- `pub fn with_options(options: impl Into<twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions>) -> Self` — A roller of `'static` options — a `'\n'`-separated `&'static str` or a `&'static` slice of options, stored without copying — in normal mode.
- `pub fn options(&self) -> &twine_widgets_ext::Options` — The options, once also in infinite mode (they compare equal to their `'\n'`-joined text and display as it; their storage is the options given, in both modes).
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode` — The mode.
- `pub fn option_count(&self) -> u16` — The number of options (LVGL `lv_roller_get_option_count`: the real ones in infinite mode).
- `pub fn selected(&self) -> u16` — The index of the selected option (LVGL `lv_roller_get_selected`).
- `pub fn selected_str(&self, buf: &mut String)` — Writes the selected option into `buf` (cleared first; LVGL `lv_roller_get_selected_str`).
- `pub fn visible_row_count(&self) -> u8` — The number of rows set with `set_visible_row_count` (0: the default height).
- `pub fn offset_y(&self) -> i32` — The vertical offset of the option column from the top of the content area.
- `pub fn page_count(&self) -> u16` — The number of virtual pages (1 in normal mode).
- `pub fn rows_drawn(&self) -> u32` — The rows the last draw visited (both text passes).
- `pub fn set_options(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, options: &str, mode: twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode)` — Sets the options (copied into the owned buffer, its capacity reused) and the mode; selects the first option (LVGL `lv_roller_set_options`). The options are one widget text: cut to `Limits::max_text_len` bytes like a label's text (a `Capacity` fault, code `TextLen`; reserved for the limit with `Limits::preallocate`). Idempotent: the same options and mode change nothing.
- `pub fn set_options_static(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, options: impl Into<twine_widgets_ext::StaticOptions>, mode: twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode)` — Sets `'static` options — a `'\n'`-separated `&'static str` or a `&'static` slice of options, stored without copying — and the mode; selects the first option. Idempotent. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_mode(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, mode: twine_widgets_ext::roller::RollerMode)` — Sets the mode, keeping the options; selects the first option. Idempotent. Never panics.
- `pub fn set_selected(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u16, anim: bool)` — Selects option `idx` (clamped), animated when `anim` (LVGL `lv_roller_set_selected`; no `ValueChanged`). In infinite mode the nearest copy of the option is chosen (a jump from the last to the first option rolls forward). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_visible_row_count(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, rows: u8)` — Sets the height to show `rows` rows: `(line height + line space) × rows + 2 × border` (LVGL `lv_roller_set_visible_row_count`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn height_for_rows(m: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, rows: u8) -> i32` — The height of `rows` rows (LVGL `lv_roller_set_visible_row_count`).
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets_ext::roller::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a roller, content wide and `LV_DPI_DEF` high, as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_roller_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::tabview::Tabview
A tabview (LVGL `lv_tabview`): a bar of buttons (one per tab) and a content area whose pages scroll horizontally (vertically with the bar at the left or right) and snap one page at a time.
Methods of `Tabview`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A tabview (its bar and content are created by `init`; the bar is at the top).
- `pub fn active(&self) -> u32` — The index of the active tab (LVGL `lv_tabview_get_tab_active`).
- `pub fn tab_bar(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The button bar (LVGL `lv_tabview_get_tab_bar`).
- `pub fn content(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The page container (LVGL `lv_tabview_get_content`).
- `pub fn tab_bar_position(&self) -> twine_style::Side` — The bar position.
- `pub fn tab_bar_size(&self) -> i32` — The bar size (height at the top or bottom, width at the side).
- `pub fn animated(&self) -> bool` — Whether clicking a tab scrolls to it with an animation.
- `pub fn tab_count(&self, e: &twine_engine::Engine) -> u32` — The number of tabs (LVGL `lv_tabview_get_tab_count`).
- `pub fn tab_button(&self, e: &twine_engine::Engine, idx: u32) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The button of tab `idx` (LVGL `lv_tabview_get_tab_button`).
- `pub fn tab_page(&self, e: &twine_engine::Engine, idx: u32) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The page of tab `idx`.
- `pub fn add_tab(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, name: &str) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — Adds a tab titled `name` (copied): a button in the bar and a page (returned) in the content (LVGL `lv_tabview_add_tab`). The first tab becomes active.
- `pub fn rename_tab(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u32, name: &str)` — Renames tab `idx` (LVGL `lv_tabview_set_tab_text`). Unknown tabs log `warn!`.
- `pub fn set_active(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, idx: u32, anim: bool)` — Switches to tab `idx`, scrolling the content to its page (animated when `anim`), and marks its button `CHECKED` (LVGL `lv_tabview_set_active`; no `ValueChanged`). An index past the last tab is remembered (it activates when that tab is added) but shows nothing.
- `pub fn set_animated(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Whether clicking a tab animates the switch (default on).
- `pub fn set_tab_bar_position(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, dir: twine_style::Side)` — Puts the bar at the top, bottom, left or right (LVGL `lv_tabview_set_tab_bar_position`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_tab_bar_size(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, size: i32)` — The bar's height (top / bottom) or width (left / right) (LVGL `lv_tabview_set_tab_bar_size`). Idempotent.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

### mod twine_widgets_ext::vector_view

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::vector_view::VectorView
Draws a `VectorScene` in its own coordinates: scene point (0, 0) is the top-left corner of the widget; drawing is clipped to the widget.
Methods of `VectorView`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty view.
- `pub fn scene(&self) -> &twine_vector::VectorScene` — The scene.
- `pub fn bounds(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — Bounds of the scene in scene coordinates (`None` when nothing is drawn).
- `pub fn set_scene(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, scene: twine_vector::VectorScene)` — Replaces the scene. Idempotent: an equal scene changes nothing; otherwise the old and the new bounds are invalidated.
- `pub fn swap_scene(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, scene: &mut twine_vector::VectorScene)` — Exchanges the scene with `scene` (which receives the old one, storage included). Idempotent like `set_scene`: an equal scene is not swapped.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### struct twine_widgets_ext::window::Window
A window (LVGL `lv_win`): a flex column of a header (a flex row: `add_title` and `add_button` fill it) and a content area that takes the rest and scrolls. The default theme draws the header grey with a small padding and the content like a screen.
Methods of `Window`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A window (its header and content are created by `init`).
- `pub fn header(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The header (LVGL `lv_win_get_header`).
- `pub fn content(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The content area (LVGL `lv_win_get_content`).
- `pub fn add_title(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, text: &str) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — Adds a title to the header (copied): a label taking the free width, cut with dots when too long (LVGL `lv_win_add_title`).
- `pub fn add_button(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, icon: twine_image::ImageSource, width: i32) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — Adds a button `width` px wide and as high as the header with `icon` centered (LVGL `lv_win_add_button`).
- `pub fn set_header_height(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, h: i32)` — The header height (default `dpi / 2`). Idempotent.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

#### fn twine_widgets_ext::window::init_title
`pub fn init_title(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine, label: twine_engine::NodeId)`
Sets up a window title label: one line cut with dots when too long, taking the free width (LVGL sets only the `Dots` long mode, so a content-high title wraps instead).

#### fn twine_widgets_ext::window::create
`pub fn create(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>`
Creates a window, 100 % × 100 % of its parent, as the last child of `parent` (LVGL `lv_win_create`).
Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` if `parent` does not exist (logged).

## crate twine_theme

Documented with features: `std,assets,lvgl,mono,simple`.

**twine-theme**

Themes for the Twine GUI library: they give every widget its default look, exactly like
LVGL's themes (`src/themes`). A theme is a `static` — **one theme per display, fixed at
compile time** (design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.0a) — given to a display when
it is created (`AppConfig::theme(&THEME)` / `DisplayBuilder::theme(&THEME)` in
`twine-view`, a `DisplayTheme` in the engine). The engine
then calls it for every node it creates, before the widget's own `init`, and the theme adds
styles with the lowest priority, so anything an application sets wins.

| Theme | Cargo feature | LVGL | Look |
|-------|---------------|------|------|
| `Lvgl` | `lvgl` (default) | `lv_theme_default` | material-like, light, dark, night or high contrast, primary/secondary colors, rounded cards and buttons with shadows, focus outlines, transitions, DPI-scaled |
| `Simple` | `simple` | `lv_theme_simple` | flat grey tones, minimal styling |
| `Mono` | `mono` | `lv_theme_mono` | pure black and white for 1-bit displays |

A theme is **data**: its styles are `static`s (`lvgl::styles`, `mono::styles`,
`simple::styles`), its colors, fonts and motion one `'static` [design
element](twine_style::design) table per `ThemeMode` (`lvgl::LIGHT`, …), and its per-class
looks `ComputedRecipe`s (`lvgl::ALL_RECIPES`, …, or the
ones the application lists with `.recipes(&[..])`). Only the
LVGL theme computes something at run time: the sizes it scales by the display's DPI and
size class, a small table per display built once when the display is created
(`lvgl::metrics`). Nothing is allocated when the mode switches.

```rust
use twine_style::ThemeMode;
use twine_theme::{Lvgl, Mono, Simple, ThemeHook};

static THEME: Lvgl = Lvgl::new(); // LVGL's look in all four modes
assert_eq!(ThemeHook::modes(&THEME).len(), 4);
static OLED: Mono = Mono::new();
static PLAIN: Simple = Simple::new();
assert_eq!(ThemeHook::modes(&PLAIN).len(), 4);
```

**Customization**

Everything is `const` (nothing is built at run time):

- **Tune** a theme's element set and list the modes the product shows:
  `static LIGHT: ElementTable = Lvgl::SET.primary(Palette::Teal.main()).table(ThemeMode::Light);`
  then `static THEME: Lvgl = Lvgl::new().modes(&[(ThemeMode::Light, &LIGHT)]);` — an
  unlisted mode's table is not linked. Application elements and overrides of single
  elements are `ElementTable`'s const builders on such a table.
- **Trim** a theme to the widget classes the product creates:
  `static THEME: Lvgl = Lvgl::new().recipes(&[&lvgl::OBJ, &lvgl::LABEL, &lvgl::BUTTON]);`
  — only the listed per-class recipes and the styles they use are linked (default: the
  theme's `ALL_RECIPES`). `twine_testing::assert_theme_covers` checks the list against a
  headless run of the UI, and `cargo xtask theme-recipes` prints the minimal list.
- **Extend** a theme with a `DesignSystem` whose
  `type Base = Lvgl;` (or `Mono`, `Simple`): its recipes (written with
  `recipe!`, reusing the theme's public `static` styles as `..`
  spreads) restyle the classes it names — custom widgets, variants and roles — and every
  other class keeps the base's look.

```rust
use twine_engine::{DesignSystem, Recipe, Theme, ThemeHook, WidgetClass, recipe};
use twine_style::design::ElementTable;
use twine_style::{Radius, Selector, State, ThemeMode};
use twine_theme::{Lvgl, lvgl};
use twine_widgets::button::BUTTON_CLASS;

/// A key of an on-screen numpad: themed like a button...
static KEY_CLASS: WidgetClass = WidgetClass::new("numpad_key").parts(BUTTON_CLASS.parts).base(&BUTTON_CLASS);

recipe! {
    // ...as a pill.
    static KEY for KEY_CLASS {
        Selector::MAIN => { ..lvgl::styles::BTN, ..lvgl::styles::BG_COLOR_PRIMARY, radius: Radius::Circle },
        State::PRESSED => { ..lvgl::styles::PRESSED },
    }
}
struct Numpad;
impl DesignSystem for Numpad {
    type Base = Lvgl;
    const NAME: &'static str = "numpad";
    const MODES: &'static [(ThemeMode, &'static ElementTable)] = lvgl::MODES;
    const RECIPES: &'static [&'static Recipe] = &[&KEY];
}
static THEME: Theme<Numpad> = Theme::new();
assert_eq!(THEME.recipe(&KEY_CLASS).map(|r| r.name()), Some("KEY"));
assert_eq!(THEME.recipe(&BUTTON_CLASS).map(|r| r.name()), Some("BUTTON")); // LVGL's
```

**Widget classes**

Themes recognise widget classes by **identity** (`&'static WidgetClass`, a pointer
comparison — this crate depends on `twine-widgets` and `twine-widgets-ext` for their class
statics), never by name. A class a theme does not know is styled like the nearest class of
its `WidgetClass::base` chain it knows, so a custom
widget with `base: Some(&BUTTON_CLASS)` looks like a button in every theme, and so do
variants (`ButtonVariant::Tinted`) and roles
(`Engine::set_theme_class`). Matching runs when a
node is created or re-themed — never while drawing — and allocates nothing.

**Theme modes for regulated displays**

| Theme | `Light` | `Dark` | `Night` | `HighContrast` |
|-------|---------|--------|---------|----------------|
| `Lvgl` | LVGL | LVGL | warm amber on near-black, ≤ 30 % luminance, blue ≤ red / 2 | white on black, yellow accent, opaque cyan focus ring |
| `Mono` | black on white | white on black | white on black | black on white |
| `Simple` | LVGL | flat greys inverted | dim warm amber, ≤ 30 % luminance, blue ≤ red / 2 | black on white, grey buttons with black text |

A mode a theme does not list is refused: the display keeps its mode (with a warning).
Each mode specifies minimum WCAG contrast ratios (`ThemeMode::min_contrast`:
text 4.5:1, 7:1 in `HighContrast`; text on accents 3:1 in `Light`/`Dark`, 4.5:1 at night,
7:1 in `HighContrast`; focus ring and disabled content 3:1 at night, 4.5:1 in
`HighContrast`), and every built-in theme meets them with its default colors (tested with
`ElementTable::check_contrast`). The
ratios (`Mono`: 21:1 for every pair in every mode):

| Theme, mode | on-surface / surface | / background | / surface-variant | muted / surface | on-primary / primary | on-secondary / secondary | focus ring / surface | disabled content / surface |
|-------------|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| lvgl, `Light` | 16.10 | 14.77 | 12.20 | 4.61 | 3.12 | 3.68 | 1.75 | 3.95 |
| lvgl, `Dark` | 13.61 | 17.21 | 12.33 | 7.56 | 3.12 | 3.68 | 2.14 | 6.33 |
| lvgl, `Night` | 6.15 | 6.63 | 5.04 | 4.87 | 4.92 | 4.93 | 6.09 | 3.53 |
| lvgl, `HighContrast` | 21.00 | 21.00 | 10.37 | 18.10 | 14.87 | 21.00 | 13.65 | 11.42 |
| simple, `Light` | 6.19 | 5.68 | 4.69 | 4.61 | 7.84 | 6.19 | 2.68 | 2.61 |
| simple, `Dark` | 12.63 | 14.19 | 8.62 | 6.22 | 4.61 | 14.19 | 6.22 | 5.02 |
| simple, `Night` | 6.15 | 6.63 | 5.70 | 4.87 | 4.89 | 6.63 | 4.87 | 3.53 |
| simple, `HighContrast` | 21.00 | 21.00 | 15.91 | 16.10 | 7.84 | 21.00 | 21.00 | 8.32 |

(`Light`/`Dark` focus rings are LVGL's 50 % translucent primary and are not specified.)

`Palette` is LVGL's material palette with identical values; DPI scaling is
`twine_style::dpx` (also used by the engine for `Length::dp` values).

**Features**

- `lvgl` (default), `mono`, `simple`: the themes. A theme's code and data are linked only
  when the application names it.
- `assets` (default): the default element sets (`Lvgl::SET`, `Mono::SET`, `Simple::SET`)
  and tables use the built-in Montserrat 14 font of `twine-assets`. Without it they have
  the empty font: give the set a font.
- `std`, `log`, `defmt`: as in every Twine crate.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints.

#### enum twine_theme::DisplaySize
The display size class LVGL's default theme scales radii and paddings with (`disp_size_t`).
Variants:
- `Small` — The larger side is at most 320 px (`DISP_SMALL`).
- `Medium` — The larger side is below 720 px (`DISP_MEDIUM`).
- `Large` — Larger displays (`DISP_LARGE`).
Methods of `DisplaySize`:
- `pub fn of(resolution: twine_core::Size) -> Self` — The class of a display of `resolution` (LVGL `lv_theme_default_init`).
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_theme::Lvgl
LVGL's default theme: material colors, rounded white (or dark) cards with a grey border, primary-colored buttons with a shadow that darken when pressed and turn secondary when checked, 50 % outlines on keyboard focus, and short transitions.
Methods of `Lvgl`:
- `const SET: twine_theme::LvglSet` — LVGL's element set: `Palette::Blue` / `Palette::Red`, Montserrat 14 (feature `assets`) for all three fonts (`lv_theme_default_init`'s defaults).
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — The theme with LVGL's defaults (see the table of `Lvgl`); LVGL `lv_theme_default_init`. `const`: `static THEME: Lvgl = Lvgl::new();`.
- `pub const fn modes(self, modes: &'static [(twine_style::ThemeMode, &'static twine_style::design::ElementTable)]) -> Self` — Lists the modes the theme supports, each with its `'static` table, in the order a mode switch cycles through them; the first is the start mode unless the display names another. Only the listed tables are linked; a switch to an unlisted mode is refused (the display keeps its mode). A mode listed twice counts once (its first table). Never panics.
- `pub const fn recipes(self, recipes: &'static [&'static twine_engine::ComputedRecipe]) -> Self` — Lists the per-class recipes the theme uses — **pay for what you use**: only the listed recipes (and the styles they add) are linked, so an image does not carry the looks of widget classes it never creates. Default: `ALL_RECIPES` (every class this theme styles).
- `pub const fn dpi(self, dpi: u16) -> Self` — Scales for `dpi` (at least 1) instead of each display's own DPI (LVGL uses the display's, `DEFAULT_DPI` = 130 by default). Never panics: `0` is taken as `1`.
- `pub const fn display_size(self, size: twine_theme::DisplaySize) -> Self` — Uses the size class `size` instead of deriving it from each display's resolution.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, ThemeHook, ThemeBase, Theme

#### struct twine_theme::LvglSet
The LVGL theme's element set: what its mode tables depend on — the primary and secondary colors (LVGL `color_primary` / `color_secondary`) and the fonts — tuned with `const` builders and turned into a mode's `'static` table with `table` (`Lvgl::SET` is LVGL's defaults).
Fields:
- `primary: twine_core::Color` — `design::PRIMARY` and `design::FOCUS_RING` in `ThemeMode::Light` and `ThemeMode::Dark`: buttons, sliders, focus rings.
- `secondary: twine_core::Color` — `design::SECONDARY` in `ThemeMode::Light` and `ThemeMode::Dark`: checked buttons, edit outlines.
- `fonts: twine_theme::FontScale` — `design::FONT_SMALL` / `FONT_BODY` / `FONT_LARGE` in every mode.
Methods of `LvglSet`:
- `pub const fn primary(self, color: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — The primary color (a `Palette` entry's `main` or any `Color`).
- `pub const fn secondary(self, color: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — The secondary color.
- `pub const fn fonts(self, fonts: twine_theme::FontScale) -> Self` — The small, normal and large fonts (LVGL `font_small` / `font_normal` / `font_large`).
- `pub const fn table(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> twine_style::design::ElementTable` — The `'static` element table of `mode` (see the module documentation for the values); `const`, so it lives in flash: `static T: ElementTable = Lvgl::SET.table(ThemeMode::Dark);`. Spacings, radii and elevations depend on the display and are in its `metrics` table instead. Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### struct twine_theme::Mono
LVGL's monochrome theme: black on white (or white on black), 1-px borders, pressed buttons get a thicker border, checked ones are inverted, focus and edit show outlines. Supports every `ThemeMode`, switchable at run time: a 1-bit panel can only invert, so `Night` is white on black like `Dark` and `HighContrast` black on white like `Light`.
Methods of `Mono`:
- `const SET: twine_theme::MonoSet` — The default element set (Montserrat 14 with the `assets` feature).
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — The theme in every mode with the default font (`MODES`); LVGL `lv_theme_mono_init`. `const`: `static THEME: Mono = Mono::new();`.
- `pub const fn modes(self, modes: &'static [(twine_style::ThemeMode, &'static twine_style::design::ElementTable)]) -> Self` — Lists the modes the theme supports, each with its `'static` table, in switching order (the first is the start mode). Only the listed tables are linked; a mode listed twice counts once. Never panics.
- `pub const fn recipes(self, recipes: &'static [&'static twine_engine::ComputedRecipe]) -> Self` — Lists the per-class recipes the theme uses — **pay for what you use**: only the listed recipes (and the styles they add) are linked, so an image does not carry the looks of widget classes it never creates. Default: `ALL_RECIPES` (every class this theme styles).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, ThemeHook, ThemeBase, Theme

#### struct twine_theme::MonoSet
The mono theme's element set: its one font (LVGL's mono theme has one), turned into a mode's `'static` table with `table` (`Mono::SET`: Montserrat 14 with the `assets` feature, else the empty font).
Fields:
- `font: &'static twine_text::Font` — The font of all text: `design::FONT_SMALL`, `FONT_BODY` and `FONT_LARGE`.
Methods of `MonoSet`:
- `pub const fn font(self, font: &'static twine_text::Font) -> Self` — The font of all text.
- `pub const fn table(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> twine_style::design::ElementTable` — The `'static` table of `mode`: `COLOR_FG` / `COLOR_BG` of LVGL (black and white, swapped in dark mode) for every color, `PAD_DEF`-based spacings, no shadows, no motion. A 1-bit panel can only invert: `Night` is white on black like `Dark` (dimming is the backlight's job), `HighContrast` black on white like `Light` (both already 21:1). Tints and fills have no intermediate shade: `ACCENT_TINT` is 20 % foreground on the background, `FILL_1..3` the background. `const`; never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### enum twine_theme::Palette
The 19 material colors of LVGL's `lv_palette_t`, in LVGL order. Each has ten `Tone`s: `tone` (LVGL `lv_palette_lighten` / `lv_palette_darken`), `main` for the middle one. A palette entry converts into its main `Color` (`Color::from(Palette::Teal)`), so theme builders take either.
Variants:
- `Red` — `LV_PALETTE_RED`.
- `Pink` — `LV_PALETTE_PINK`.
- `Purple` — `LV_PALETTE_PURPLE`.
- `DeepPurple` — `LV_PALETTE_DEEP_PURPLE`.
- `Indigo` — `LV_PALETTE_INDIGO`.
- `Blue` — `LV_PALETTE_BLUE`.
- `LightBlue` — `LV_PALETTE_LIGHT_BLUE`.
- `Cyan` — `LV_PALETTE_CYAN`.
- `Teal` — `LV_PALETTE_TEAL`.
- `Green` — `LV_PALETTE_GREEN`.
- `LightGreen` — `LV_PALETTE_LIGHT_GREEN`.
- `Lime` — `LV_PALETTE_LIME`.
- `Yellow` — `LV_PALETTE_YELLOW`.
- `Amber` — `LV_PALETTE_AMBER`.
- `Orange` — `LV_PALETTE_ORANGE`.
- `DeepOrange` — `LV_PALETTE_DEEP_ORANGE`.
- `Brown` — `LV_PALETTE_BROWN`.
- `BlueGrey` — `LV_PALETTE_BLUE_GREY`.
- `Grey` — `LV_PALETTE_GREY`.
Methods of `Palette`:
- `const ALL: [twine_theme::Palette; 19]` — Every palette entry, in LVGL order.
- `pub const fn main(self) -> twine_core::Color` — The main color (LVGL `lv_palette_main`).
- `pub const fn tone(self, tone: twine_theme::Tone) -> twine_core::Color` — The color of `tone`: `Tone::L1`…`Tone::L5` are LVGL's `lv_palette_lighten(p, 1..=5)`, `Tone::D1`…`Tone::D4` `lv_palette_darken(p, 1..=4)`, `Tone::Main` `lv_palette_main(p)`. Every tone exists for every palette entry: no level can be out of range.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<twine_theme::Palette>

#### enum twine_theme::Tone
A tone of a `Palette` color, lightest to darkest (Material's 50…900 shades).
Variants:
- `L5` — Lightest (`lv_palette_lighten(p, 5)`, Material 50).
- `L4` — `lv_palette_lighten(p, 4)` (Material 100).
- `L3` — `lv_palette_lighten(p, 3)` (Material 200).
- `L2` — `lv_palette_lighten(p, 2)` (Material 300).
- `L1` — `lv_palette_lighten(p, 1)` (Material 400).
- `Main` — The main color (`lv_palette_main`, Material 500).
- `D1` — `lv_palette_darken(p, 1)` (Material 600).
- `D2` — `lv_palette_darken(p, 2)` (Material 700).
- `D3` — `lv_palette_darken(p, 3)` (Material 800).
- `D4` — Darkest (`lv_palette_darken(p, 4)`, Material 900).
Methods of `Tone`:
- `const ALL: [twine_theme::Tone; 10]` — Every tone, lightest to darkest.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

### mod twine_theme::lvgl

`Lvgl`: a faithful port of LVGL's default theme
(`src/themes/default/lv_theme_default.c`), light and dark, plus Twine's night and
high-contrast modes — as `static` data.

- **Styles** (`styles`) are LVGL's `style_init()` as `static` `Style`s.
- **Colors, fonts and motion** are design elements in one `'static`
  table per mode (`LIGHT`, `DARK`, `NIGHT`, `HIGH_CONTRAST`, or the application's
  own made with `LvglSet::table`); the styles are the same in every mode, so
  `Engine::set_theme_mode` switches modes by
  swapping a pointer.
- **Sizes** follow the display like LVGL's: every pixel value is scaled with
  `dpx` by the display's DPI, and radii and paddings follow the display
  size class (`DisplaySize`: the larger side ≤ 320 px is small, < 720 px medium, else
  large). They are the elements of a small per-display table (`metrics`) computed once
  when the display is created.
- **Per-class looks** are LVGL's `theme_apply()` branches, one
  `ComputedRecipe` per widget class (`ALL_RECIPES`, or the ones the application
  lists with `Lvgl::recipes`: only those are linked),
  found along the node's theme-class lineage: a
  custom class whose `base` is `BUTTON_CLASS` is styled
  like a button.

The mode tables (LVGL's light and dark colors; Twine's night and high-contrast palettes):

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_theme::lvgl::MOTION
`pub const MOTION: twine_style::design::MotionSet`
The motion timings of the LVGL theme (`MOTION_*` design elements): `MOTION_FAST` is LVGL's theme transition (`TRANSITION_TIME`, linear); the longer ones follow LVGL's widget animation lengths (200–300 ms, ease in-out; exits ease out).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::LIGHT
`pub static LIGHT: twine_style::design::ElementTable`
LVGL's light mode with LVGL's colors and fonts (`Lvgl::SET.table(ThemeMode::Light)`).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::DARK
`pub static DARK: twine_style::design::ElementTable`
LVGL's dark mode (`Lvgl::SET.table(ThemeMode::Dark)`).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::NIGHT
`pub static NIGHT: twine_style::design::ElementTable`
Twine's night mode (`Lvgl::SET.table(ThemeMode::Night)`).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::HIGH_CONTRAST
`pub static HIGH_CONTRAST: twine_style::design::ElementTable`
Twine's high-contrast mode (`Lvgl::SET.table(ThemeMode::HighContrast)`).

#### const twine_theme::lvgl::MODES
`pub const MODES: &[(twine_style::ThemeMode, &twine_style::design::ElementTable)]`
Every mode with LVGL's colors and fonts, in switching order: what `Lvgl::new` lists. An image that only shows some modes lists only their tables (`Lvgl::modes`), so the others are not linked.

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::THEME
`pub static THEME: twine_theme::Lvgl`
The LVGL theme with its defaults (`Lvgl::new`: every mode, LVGL's colors and fonts), ready to give to a display: `AppConfig::new().theme(&lvgl::THEME)`. Linked only when named; a product that lists its modes or tunes its sizes declares its own `static`.

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::LABEL
`pub static LABEL: twine_engine::ComputedRecipe`
Labels: no styles (they inherit their text style).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::TEXTAREA_LABEL
`pub static TEXTAREA_LABEL: twine_engine::ComputedRecipe`
A textarea's text: a primary selection (lines 1086-1090).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::OBJ
`pub static OBJ: twine_engine::ComputedRecipe`
Plain objects: screens, else cards (lines 758-808).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::TABVIEW_PAGE
`pub static TABVIEW_PAGE: twine_engine::ComputedRecipe`
Tabview pages: padded, not cards (lines 758-808).

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::CARD
`pub static CARD: twine_engine::ComputedRecipe`
Twine's card: LVGL's look of a plain object, explicitly.

#### static twine_theme::lvgl::BUTTON
