- `pub fn set_partition(&mut self, p: twine_core::Partition)` — Moves the style to partition `p`'s seal domain: a property set for the first time after `p` was sealed is noted there (`AllocSite::StyleProps`). A style starts in `Partition::MAIN`; the engine moves the styles it owns (node-local styles) to its own partition. Never panics.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition set with `set_partition`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, p: twine_style::StyleProp) -> bool` — Sets a property, replacing an existing value of the same property in place. Returns `true` if the style changed (new property or different value).
- `pub fn set_tracks(&mut self, id: twine_style::PropId, tracks: twine_style::GridTracks) -> bool` — Sets the grid template property `id` (`GridColumnTracks` / `GridRowTracks`): a `'static` list is stored as is, a run-time one is held by the buffer (and released when the property is replaced or removed, or the buffer is dropped). Returns `true` if the style changed: equal tracks change nothing. Another property is ignored with a warning. The builder methods `grid_column_tracks` / `grid_row_tracks` call it.
- `pub fn set_transition(&mut self, t: twine_style::TransitionValue) -> bool` — Sets the `transition` property: a `'static` transition is stored as a reference, a run-time one is held by the buffer (released when the property is replaced or removed, or the buffer is dropped; the buffer's clones share it). Returns `true` if the style changed: an equal transition changes nothing. The `transition` builder method calls it. Allocates only to hold a run-time transition (at build time); never panics.
- `pub fn get_transition(&self) -> Option<&twine_style::Transition>` — The `transition` property, borrowed from the style (a `'static` transition or the run-time one the buffer holds), if set.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, id: twine_style::PropId) -> bool` — Removes a property (and the run-time grid template or transition it held). Returns `true` if it was set.
- `pub fn holds_tracks(&self, id: twine_style::PropId, r: twine_style::TracksRef) -> bool` — Whether this buffer sets the grid template property `id` to the template `r` (a value resolved from it).
- `pub fn copy_tracks_to(&self, id: twine_style::PropId, dst: &mut twine_style::StyleBuf) -> bool` — Sets the grid template property `id` of `dst` to this buffer's template for it, sharing a run-time template (`dst` takes its own reference). Returns whether `dst` changed. Transitions use it to keep the template they show alive.
- `pub fn get(&self, id: twine_style::PropId) -> Option<twine_style::StyleValue>` — The value of `id`, if set.
- `pub fn grid_tracks(&self, id: twine_style::PropId) -> Option<&[twine_style::GridTrack]>` — The tracks of the grid template property `id` (`GridColumnTracks` / `GridRowTracks`), borrowed from the style, if set.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every property (keeps the allocation) and releases the run-time templates and transition.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of properties.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether no property is set.
- `pub fn keys(&self) -> twine_style::Props` — The set of properties this style sets (O(properties)).
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &twine_style::StyleProp>` — The properties in insertion order.
- `pub const fn has_group(&self) -> u16` — Bit `g` is set iff a property of group `g` is present.
- `pub fn extend_from(&mut self, src: &impl twine_style::StyleContainer) -> bool` — Composes at run time: sets every property of `src` (a `Style`, a `StyleBuf` or a `StyleRef`) on this buffer, in `src`'s order, with the semantics of `set`: a property this buffer already has is replaced in place (`src` wins), the others are appended. Returns `true` if the buffer changed.
Implements: StyleContainer, Clone, Debug, Default, From<&twine_style::Style>, IntoIterator, FromIterator<twine_style::StyleProp>, From<twine_style::StyleBuf>

#### trait twine_style::StyleContainer
`pub trait StyleContainer: Sealed`
A style container whose properties can be composed into a `StyleBuf`: a flash `Style`, a heap `StyleBuf` or a `StyleRef` (either). Taken by `StyleBuf::extend_from` and `Style::merge`; sealed (implemented by these three only).
Implemented by: twine_style::Style, twine_style::StyleBuf, twine_style::StyleRef

#### enum twine_style::StyleRef
A style attached to a node: a `static` `Style` or a shared `StyleBuf` (themes share their runtime styles between many nodes).
Variants:
- `Static(&'static twine_style::Style)` — A style in flash.
- `Shared(Rc<twine_style::StyleBuf>)` — A heap style shared by reference counting.
Methods of `StyleRef`:
- `pub fn get(&self, id: twine_style::PropId) -> Option<twine_style::StyleValue>` — The value of `id`, if set.
- `pub fn has_group(&self) -> u16` — The group mask (see `Style::has_group`).
- `pub fn grid_tracks(&self, id: twine_style::PropId) -> Option<&[twine_style::GridTrack]>` — The tracks of the grid template property `id` of this style, borrowed from it (a `'static` list, or the run-time template a `StyleBuf` holds).
- `pub fn keys(&self) -> twine_style::Props` — The set of properties this style sets (O(properties)).
- `pub fn get_transition(&self) -> Option<&twine_style::Transition>` — The `transition` property of this style, borrowed from it (a `'static` transition, or the run-time one a `StyleBuf` holds).
- `pub fn ptr_eq(&self, other: &twine_style::StyleRef) -> bool` — Whether both refer to the same style object.
Implements: StyleContainer, Clone, Debug, From<&'static twine_style::Style>, From<Rc<twine_style::StyleBuf>>, From<twine_style::StyleBuf>

#### enum twine_style::GridTracks
A grid template to set: a `'static` list (stored as is) or a list built at run time (shared by reference counting; the style that holds it keeps it alive). Every grid template setter takes `impl Into<GridTracks>`: a `'static` slice or array, a `Vec` or a `SharedTracks`. Equality compares the tracks.
Variants:
- `Static(&'static [twine_style::GridTrack])` — A list in flash (or leaked).
- `Shared(twine_style::SharedTracks)` — A list built at run time.
Methods of `GridTracks`:
- `pub const fn from_static(tracks: &'static [twine_style::GridTrack]) -> Self` — A `'static` template (usable in `const` context).
- `pub fn tracks(&self) -> &[twine_style::GridTrack]` — The tracks.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, From<&'static [twine_style::GridTrack]>, From<&'static [twine_style::GridTrack; N]>, From<Vec<twine_style::GridTrack>>, From<twine_style::SharedTracks>

#### struct twine_style::SharedTracks
A grid template built at run time: an immutable, reference-counted list of tracks (cloning shares it; the last clone frees it). One word.
Methods of `SharedTracks`:
- `pub fn strong_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of holders (style containers and your own clones).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Deref, From<Vec<twine_style::GridTrack>>, PartialEq, Eq, From<twine_style::SharedTracks>

#### struct twine_style::TrackId
The identity of a run-time template held by a container (opaque: it only identifies, it cannot be dereferenced).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_style::TracksRef

#### struct twine_style::Transition
Which properties animate when a node enters a state, and how (LVGL `lv_style_transition_dsc_t`). Set as the `transition` property of the *target* state's style: `.on_state(State::PRESSED, |s| s.transition(..).bg(..))`, or on the default state to animate every state change.
Fields:
- `props: Option<twine_style::Props>` — The animated properties: `Some(set)` exactly these, `None` the properties the state change alters (see `Transition::all`).
- `spec: twine_anim::AnimSpec` — The timing (forward play only).
Methods of `Transition`:
- `pub const fn all(duration: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Animates every property the state change alters (interpolable ones), over `duration`, linear, without delay. See `Transition`.
- `pub const fn of(props: twine_style::Props, duration: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Animates the properties of `props` over `duration`, linear, without delay.
- `pub const fn props(self, props: twine_style::Props) -> Self` — Restricts the transition to `props` (an explicit list instead of the derived one).
- `pub const fn spec(self, spec: twine_anim::AnimSpec) -> Self` — Replaces the whole timing.
- `pub const fn duration(self, d: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Sets the duration.
- `pub const fn delay(self, d: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Sets the delay before the transition starts.
- `pub const fn easing(self, e: twine_anim::Easing) -> Self` — Sets the easing curve.
- `pub const fn linear(self) -> Self` — Constant speed (the default).
- `pub const fn ease_in(self) -> Self` — Slow start.
- `pub const fn ease_out(self) -> Self` — Slow end.
- `pub const fn ease_in_out(self) -> Self` — Slow start and end.
- `pub const fn essential(self) -> Self` — Marks the transition as essential: the `Motion` preference leaves it unchanged (for a transition that conveys a state, e.g. an alarm color fading in).
- `pub const fn animated(&self, changed: twine_style::Props) -> twine_style::Props` — The properties this transition animates for a state change that alters `changed` (the keys of the styles that start or stop applying): its list, or the interpolable members of `changed`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<&'static twine_style::Transition>, From<&'static twine_style::Transition>, From<twine_style::Transition>

#### struct twine_style::TransitionId

#### fn twine_style::is_interpolable

#### struct twine_style::DurationMs

#### enum twine_style::Length
A size, position or spacing that may depend on the display density, the parent or the content (LVGL coordinates with `LV_PCT(x)` / `LV_SIZE_CONTENT` / `LV_DPX(x)`).
Variants:
- `Px(i32)` — Pixels.
- `Pct(i16)` — Percent of the reference size (usually the parent's content area); values above 100 are allowed.
- `Content` — Sized by the content (LVGL `LV_SIZE_CONTENT`).
- `Dp(i32)` — Density-independent pixels: pixels on a `REFERENCE_DPI` (160 DPI) display, scaled to the display's DPI when the style is resolved (LVGL `LV_DPX`).
Methods of `Length`:
- `pub const fn px(v: i32) -> Self` — `v` pixels.
- `pub const fn pct(p: i16) -> Self` — `p` percent (LVGL `lv_pct`).
- `pub const fn dp(v: i32) -> Self` — `v` density-independent pixels (see `Length::Dp`).
- `pub const fn from_i32(v: i32) -> Self` — `v` pixels (`const` counterpart of `From<i32>`).
- `pub const fn with_dpi(self, dpi: u16) -> Self` — The length with a `Dp` value converted to pixels for a `dpi` display (see `dpx`); other lengths are unchanged.
- `pub const fn resolve(self, parent: i32, content: i32) -> i32` — The length in pixels: `Pct` is relative to `parent` (truncated like LVGL `lv_pct_to_px`, saturating), `Content` is `content`. A `Dp` that was not converted with `with_dpi` counts at the reference 160 DPI (1 dp = 1 px); style resolution converts `Dp` with the DPI of the source (`StyleSource::dpi`).
- `pub const fn as_px(self) -> Option<i32>` — The pixel value of a `Px` length.
Implements: ElementType, PropValue, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, From<i32>

#### enum twine_style::MainAlign
Placement of flex items along the main axis (`flex_main_align`, `justify`) and of the tracks of a wrapping flex container (`flex_track_align`, `align_content`) — LVGL `lv_flex_align_t`, same discriminants.
Variants:
- `Start = 0` — At the start.
- `End = 1` — At the end.
- `Center = 2` — Centered.
- `SpaceEvenly = 3` — Equal space before, between and after the items.
- `SpaceAround = 4` — Equal space around every item (half of it at the edges).
- `SpaceBetween = 5` — Equal space between the items, none at the edges.

#### enum twine_style::Radius
A corner radius (the `radius` style property): pixels, density-independent pixels, or fully round.
Variants:
- `Px(i32)` — Pixels. Drawn clamped to `0..=` half the shorter side of the node, so a negative value draws square corners and a large one a fully round shape. A value at or above the renderer's circle marker (`twine_render::RADIUS_CIRCLE`, 32 767) is stored like `Circle` and reads back as `Circle` (it draws the same).
- `Dp(i32)` — Density-independent pixels (see `Length::Dp`).
- `Circle` — Fully round: a circle for a square node, a pill otherwise (LVGL `LV_RADIUS_CIRCLE`).
Methods of `Radius`:
- `pub const fn to_length(self) -> twine_style::Length` — The radius as the pixel `Length` stored in styles (`Circle` → the renderer's circle marker).
- `pub const fn from_length(l: twine_style::Length) -> Option<twine_style::Radius>` — The radius stored as `l` (`None` for `Pct`/`Content`, which a radius cannot be).
Implements: ElementType, PropValue, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, From<i32>

#### enum twine_style::ScrollbarMode

#### struct twine_style::Sides

#### fn twine_style::dpx
`pub const fn dpx(dp: i32, dpi: u16) -> i32`
`dp` density-independent pixels in pixels on a `dpi` display (LVGL `LV_DPX_CALC`): `(dpi · dp + 80) / 160`, at least 1 for positive values, 0 for 0; negative values are scaled symmetrically. One multiply and one divide by a constant; saturating.

macro_rules! elements {

### mod twine_style::design

Design elements: named, typed values (colors, spacings, radii, opacities, fonts, motion
timings, icons) that a style refers to by name and the **theme** supplies, resolved when the
style is resolved.

A style that says `bg_color: design::SURFACE` instead of `bg_color: Color::WHITE` follows
the theme of its display: switching the theme's `ThemeMode` (light → dark) swaps the
theme's `ElementTable` and every node that uses a design element is re-resolved — no view
is rebuilt, no binding re-runs, nothing is allocated.


**Kinds**

| Element type | Value | Accepted by |
|--------------|-------|-------------|
| `ColorElement` | `Color` | every color property (`bg_color`, `text_color`, `border_color`, …, the `bg`, `border`, `outline` shorthands) |
| `LengthElement` | `Length` (`Px` or `Dp`) | every length property (`width`, `x`, `padding_*`, `margin_*`, `row_gap`, `border_width`, …) |
| `RadiusElement` | `Radius` | `radius` |
| `OpacityElement` | `Opa` | every opacity property (`bg_opacity`, `opacity`, …) |
| `FontElement` | `&'static Font` | `font` |
| `MotionElement` | `&'static AnimSpec` | `anim` (the timing of a widget's own animations) |
| `IconElement` | `&'static ImageSource` | `bg_image` |

A property of type `Color` stores a `ColorValue` (= `DesignValue<Color>`): a fixed
color or a color element. `Color` and `ColorElement` both convert into it, so the
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

`pub trait ElementType: twine_style::PropValue + Copy + 'static + Sealed`
A value type that design elements can have: `Color`, `Length`, `Radius`, `Opa`, `&'static Font`, `&'static AnimSpec`, `&'static ImageSource` and `Scale` (sealed).
Items:

Implemented by: twine_core::Color, twine_style::Length, twine_style::Radius, twine_core::Opa, &'static twine_text::Font, &'static twine_anim::AnimSpec, &'static twine_image::ImageSource, twine_core::Scale

#### struct twine_style::design::Element<T>
A design element whose value is a `T`: a typed name the theme gives a value (see the module documentation). `Copy`, 2 bytes.
Methods of `Element`:
- `const MAX_INDEX: u16` — The largest index of an application or theme-private element (16 383): larger numbers given to `custom` and `private` saturate to it.
- `pub const fn custom(n: u16) -> Self` — Application element number `n`: an element of the application (a brand color, a gauge zone color, …), which it gives a value in each mode of its theme; until then it resolves to the property's default (see the module documentation).
- `pub const fn private(n: u16) -> Self` — Theme-private element number `n`: an element a theme defines for its own styles and components (e.g. sizes it computes per display), outside the standard set. Applications use `custom` instead; private and application elements never collide, so a theme's private elements cannot overwrite an application's values (or the other way round). Numbering is shared by all kinds, like `custom`'s; a huge `n` saturates at `MAX_INDEX`. `const`; never panics.
- `pub const fn is_custom(self) -> bool` — Whether this is an application element (`custom`).
- `pub const fn is_private(self) -> bool` — Whether this is a theme-private element (`private`).
- `pub const fn index(self) -> u16` — The element's number within its id space: the standard element's index, or the `n` of `custom` / `private`.
- `pub const fn id(self) -> u16` — The raw id: the standard element's index (below 16 384), or the index with bit 14 set (application elements) or bit 15 set (theme-private elements). Stable within a build; for logs and tables, not for persisting.
- `pub const fn erase(self) -> twine_style::design::ElementRef` — The element without its value type, as styles store it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, From<twine_style::design::Element<T>>

#### enum twine_style::design::DesignValue<T>

Every color, length, radius, opacity and font property, the `anim` property and the `bg_image` property store one (as `ColorValue`, `LengthValue`, `RadiusValue`, `OpacityValue`, `FontValue`, `MotionValue`, `IconValue`), so it can be set to either:
Variants:
- `Fixed(T)` — A fixed value.
- `Element(twine_style::design::Element<T>)` — The value the theme gives the element.

- `pub fn fixed(self) -> Option<T>` — The fixed value (`None` for an element).

#### struct twine_style::design::ElementTable
The values a theme gives the design elements in one `ThemeMode`: the standard elements of every kind (fixed-size arrays, one slot per standard element), the application's elements (`Element::custom`) and the theme's private ones (`Element::private`).
Methods of `ElementTable`:
- `pub const fn colors(self, c: twine_style::design::SystemColors) -> Self` — Sets every element of `c` (`const` builder; see `SystemColors`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn spacing(self, s: twine_style::design::Spacing) -> Self` — Sets every element of `s` (`const` builder; see `Spacing`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn shape(self, s: twine_style::design::Shape) -> Self` — Sets every element of `s` (`const` builder; see `Shape`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn elevation(self, e: twine_style::design::Elevation) -> Self` — Sets every element of `e` (`const` builder; see `Elevation`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn motions(self, m: twine_style::design::MotionSet) -> Self` — Sets every element of `m` (`const` builder; see `MotionSet`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn icons(self, i: twine_style::design::IconSet) -> Self` — Sets the icons `i` lists, clearing the others (`const` builder; see `IconSet`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn fonts(self, f: twine_style::design::FontSet) -> Self` — Sets every element of `f` (`const` builder; see `FontSet`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty table (`const`; no allocation).
- `pub const fn color(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<twine_core::Color>, value: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — Sets the standard color element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn length(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<twine_style::Length>, value: twine_style::Length) -> Self` — Sets the standard length element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn radius(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<twine_style::Radius>, value: twine_style::Radius) -> Self` — Sets the standard radius element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn opacity(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<twine_core::Opa>, value: twine_core::Opa) -> Self` — Sets the standard opacity element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn font(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<&'static twine_text::Font>, value: &'static twine_text::Font) -> Self` — Sets the standard font element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn motion(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<&'static twine_anim::AnimSpec>, value: &'static twine_anim::AnimSpec) -> Self` — Sets the standard motion element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn icon(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<&'static twine_image::ImageSource>, value: &'static twine_image::ImageSource) -> Self` — Sets the standard icon element `element` (builder style).
- `pub const fn custom(self, values: &'static [Option<twine_style::StyleValue>]) -> Self` — Uses `values` for the application's elements (`Element::custom`): slot `n` is the value of `custom(n)`, as made by the `elements!` macro's `slots` (`const`; replaces the table's `'static` application values; values given with `set` stay on top of them).
- `pub const fn private(self, values: &'static [Option<twine_style::StyleValue>]) -> Self` — Uses `values` for the theme's private elements (`Element::private`): slot `n` is the value of `private(n)` (`const`; replaces the table's `'static` private values; values given with `set` stay on top of them).
- `pub fn with<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(self, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>, value: T) -> Self` — Sets the value of `element` and returns the table (builder style; run time, see `set`).
- `pub fn set<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&mut self, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>, value: T)` — Sets the value of `element`.
- `pub fn get<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&self, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>) -> Option<T>` — The value of `element` (`None` if the table does not define it).
- `pub fn value(&self, element: twine_style::design::ElementRef) -> Option<twine_style::StyleValue>` — The value of `element` as a `StyleValue` (what the resolver substitutes); `None` if the table does not define it (an application or private slot holding a value of another kind counts as not defined).
- `pub fn overlay(&mut self, other: &twine_style::design::ElementTable)` — Copies every value `other` defines into this table (replacing this table's values of those elements): layers application elements or overrides over a theme's table.
- `pub fn missing_standard(&self) -> Option<twine_style::design::ElementRef>` — The first required standard element the table does not define (`None` if it defines all of them): a check for theme authors. Icons are optional (an `IconSet` maps only the icons an application uses) and are not required.
- `pub fn check_contrast(&self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Result<(), twine_style::design::ContrastViolation>` — Checks every `ContrastPair` that `mode` specifies (`ThemeMode::min_contrast`) and returns the first that falls short: a check for theme authors and for applications that override standard elements (run it in a test; it is not meant for rendering).
  Errors: The first pair (in `ContrastPair::ALL` order) whose ratio is below the minimum, or whose elements the table lacks.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default

#### struct twine_style::design::FlatElements
The element values a display resolves with, finished for it (`Dp` lengths in pixels for its DPI) and flattened into **one indexed array**: every standard element, then the application's, then the theme-private ones — a table `top` (the theme's table of the current mode) merged over a table `base` (the display's metrics). What the resolver reads for every design element of a node (the engine keeps one per themed display): one bounds-checked read instead of a search through two tables.
Methods of `FlatElements`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — Empty: every element undefined (no allocation).
- `pub fn reserve(&mut self, base: Option<&twine_style::design::ElementTable>, top: &twine_style::design::ElementTable)` — Makes room for `fill``(base, top)`, so that it allocates nothing. Call it for every `top` the array will be filled from (every mode a display lists). Never panics.
- `pub fn fill(&mut self, base: Option<&twine_style::design::ElementTable>, top: &twine_style::design::ElementTable, dpi: u16)` — Rebuilds the array in place: every element `top` defines with `top`'s value, every other one `base` defines with `base`'s, each **finished for the display**: a `Length::Dp` value is stored in pixels for `dpi`, so a read returns the value the resolver uses as is. Allocates only when `reserve` was not called for this pair; never panics.
- `pub fn value(&self, element: twine_style::design::ElementRef) -> Option<twine_style::StyleValue>` — The value of `element` as a `StyleValue` (`None` if undefined; an application or private slot holding a value of another kind counts as undefined). One bounds-checked read; never panics.
- `pub fn get<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&self, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>) -> Option<T>` — The value of `element` (`None` if undefined). Never panics.
- `pub fn heap_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Bytes of heap the array holds (its capacity).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default

#### enum twine_style::design::ContrastPair
A foreground / background pair of standard elements whose legibility a `ThemeMode` specifies (`ThemeMode::min_contrast`). `colors` gives the two colors as they are displayed: translucent elements (the focus ring, the disabled overlay) are blended with their opacity element first.
Variants:
- `OnSurface` — `ON_SURFACE` on `SURFACE`: body text on cards and containers.
- `OnBackground` — `ON_SURFACE` on `BACKGROUND`: text on the screen.
- `OnSurfaceVariant` — `ON_SURFACE` on `SURFACE_VARIANT`: text on neutral buttons.
- `OnSurfaceMuted` — `ON_SURFACE_MUTED` on `SURFACE`: secondary text (hints, captions, units).
- `OnPrimary` — `ON_PRIMARY` on `PRIMARY`: text on accent buttons.
- `OnSecondary` — `ON_SECONDARY` on `SECONDARY`: text on checked buttons.
- `FocusRing` — `FOCUS_RING` at `FOCUS_RING_OPACITY` over `SURFACE`, against `SURFACE`: the focused widget must be identifiable.
- `DisabledContent` — `ON_SURFACE` recolored with `DISABLED` at `DISABLED_OPACITY` (how the themes draw disabled widgets), against `SURFACE`: disabled content stays readable.
Methods of `ContrastPair`:
- `const ALL: [twine_style::design::ContrastPair; 8]` — Every pair.
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — A short name for messages (`"on-surface/surface"`).
- `pub fn colors(self, t: &twine_style::design::ElementTable) -> Option<(twine_core::Color, twine_core::Color)>` — The foreground and background colors of the pair as `t` displays them (blended with their opacity elements, see the variants); `None` if `t` lacks one of the elements. Never panics.
- `pub fn ratio(self, t: &twine_style::design::ElementTable) -> Option<twine_core::color::ContrastRatio>` — The WCAG contrast ratio of the pair in `t` (`None` if `t` lacks one of the elements). Never panics.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_style::design::ContrastViolation
A pair that does not reach its mode's minimum contrast (`ElementTable::check_contrast`).
Fields:
- `pair: twine_style::design::ContrastPair` — The pair.
- `ratio: Option<twine_core::color::ContrastRatio>` — Its ratio in the table (`None`: the table lacks one of its elements).
- `min: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — The mode's minimum.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display

## crate twine_engine

Documented with features: `std,fs,svg,perf-monitor,color-argb8888,color-i1,color-l8,color-rgb565,color-rgb565-swapped,color-rgb888,color-xrgb8888`.

**twine-engine**

The core of the Twine GUI library: the retained widget tree, the `Widget` trait, styles
attached to nodes, precise invalidation, displays with screens and layers, and the refresh
pipeline that turns dirty areas into pixels on a panel with as little work as possible.

`twine-engine` sits above the renderer (`twine-render`), text, images and styles, and below
themes, widgets and the declarative view layer. It is fully usable on its own, imperatively
(LVGL-style); it does not depend on the reactive runtime.

**How a frame happens**

1. Changes invalidate exactly the affected area: a node's coordinates plus its extra draw
   size (shadow, outline, transform), clipped by its ancestors (P2). Setters that do not
   change anything invalidate nothing (P3).
2. Layout-affecting changes (sizes, positions, flex/grid properties, children, flags) mark
   the node dirty; `Engine::update_layout` (run by `step`) lays out only the dirty
   subtrees with `twine-layout`, moves unchanged subtrees by delta and invalidates the old
   and new areas of the nodes that actually moved.
3. `Engine::step` refreshes each display at most once per
   `EngineConfig::refr_period`: dirty areas are merged, rounded to the display's alignment
   and split into chunks that fit the draw buffer.
4. Each chunk is drawn starting from the topmost node that covers it opaquely (nodes hidden
   below are skipped), back to front, with opacity groups, transforms and blend modes
   rendered through layers.
5. With two draw buffers the next chunk is rendered while the driver still transfers the
   previous one (DMA pipelining); framebuffer displays render into a back buffer and swap.
6. Input devices are read first in each step: devices with an interrupt only after
   `Engine::notify_input` and while held, so an idle touch UI never wakes the CPU.
7. Timers and animations run right after the inputs, on wall-clock time: a late frame
   jumps to the right value. Animations write node properties through the same setters as
   user code; while one plays `step` asks for the next frame, and once they end (or are
   paused) it asks for nothing (`Engine::anim_start`, `Engine::timer_add`, style
   transitions on state changes, `Engine::load_screen_anim`).
8. Scrolling moves a container's children by its scroll offset without a layout pass and
   redraws only the container (`Engine::scroll_by`, drag / throw / snap by pointers,
   scrollbars in `Part::Scrollbar`).
9. When nothing is dirty, `step` returns `Wake::Idle` and does nothing at all (P1). A
   steady-state frame performs no heap allocation (P4).

| Module concept | Items |
|----------------|-------|
| tree | `Tree`, `Node`, `NodeId`, iterators, `Tree::check_invariants` |

| audit | `impl Audit for EngineConfig` (`twine_core::audit`), `audit_features`, `ThemeHook::audit` |
| draw acceleration | `Engine::set_accel`, `Engine::clear_accel` |

**Features**

- `std`, `log`, `defmt`: as in every Twine crate.
- `debug-checks`: tree invariants after every mutation, style cache verification, the
  invalidation log and the render hook (tests enable it).
- `perf-monitor`: the on-screen performance overlay.
- `test-ids`: keep node test ids in release builds.
- `color-*`: pixel formats compiled into the renderer.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints; it refuses `perf-monitor`
  and `fs`; it implies `display-integrity`.
- `display-integrity`: frame observers, region re-render / read-back / checks,
  `ObjFlags::SAFETY_CRITICAL`, the stale / invalid marks and the fail-safe screen
  (`docs/safety/profile.md` § 11). Off (the default), none of it is compiled: no flag test
  per drawn node, no observer branch per chunk.
- `partitions`: two partitions instead of one (`Engine::set_partition`; ADR-001).
  Everything else an engine owns — limits, step budget and timing, faults, observer,
  critical registry, fail-safe screens, heartbeat — is per engine anyway, so engines of two
  partitions share nothing. Not implied by `safety`.

**Example**

```rust
use twine_core::{Color, ColorFormat, Instant, Opa, Rect};
use twine_engine::{BufferMode, Engine, EngineConfig, Obj, Wake};
use twine_hal::DisplayInfo;
use twine_style::{Selector, StyleProp};

let mut engine = Engine::new(EngineConfig::default()).unwrap();
let buf: &'static mut [u8] = Box::leak(vec![0u8; 64 * 2 * 8].into_boxed_slice());
let display = engine.add_display(Panel(None), BufferMode::partial_single(buf), None).unwrap();
let screen = engine.active_screen(display).unwrap();
let boxed = engine.create(screen, Box::new(Obj)).unwrap();
engine.set_pos(boxed, 8, 8); // laid out by the next `step`
engine.set_size(boxed, 20, 10);
engine.set_local_prop(boxed, Selector::MAIN, StyleProp::BgColor(Color::RED.into()));
engine.set_local_prop(boxed, Selector::MAIN, StyleProp::BgOpacity(Opa::COVER.into()));
assert!(matches!(engine.step(Instant::from_millis(0)), Wake::Idle)); // rendered, nothing left
assert_eq!(engine.step(Instant::from_millis(100)), Wake::Idle);      // idle: no work at all
```

#### enum twine_engine::AnimProp
The node property an engine animation writes (`Engine::anim_start`).
Variants:
- `X` — Local X position.
- `Y` — Local Y position.
- `Width` — Width.
- `Height` — Height.
- `Opa` — Opacity of the part (`part_opacity`).
- `TranslateX` — Horizontal translation.
- `TranslateY` — Vertical translation.
- `ScaleX` — Horizontal transform scale.
- `ScaleY` — Vertical transform scale.
- `Rotation` — Transform rotation.
- `Style(twine_style::PropId)` — Any integer-like style property (integers, pixel lengths, opacities, angles, scales) of the `Main` part, set as a local property.
- `ScrollX` — Horizontal scroll position.
- `ScrollY` — Vertical scroll position.
- `Value` — A widget-defined value (e.g. a bar's value).
- `Custom(u16)` — A widget-defined custom property.
Methods of `AnimProp`:
- `pub const fn key(self) -> twine_anim::PropKey` — The property's code in a `AnimTarget::Node` target.
- `pub const fn from_key(key: twine_anim::PropKey) -> Option<twine_engine::AnimProp>` — The property of a code made by `key` (`None` for any other number).
- `pub const fn target(self, node: twine_anim::NodeKey) -> twine_anim::AnimTarget` — The `AnimTarget::Node` target of this property of node `node`. For code driving a `Timeline` or matching the targets of the engine's animations by hand. Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_engine::Deferred
The context of the engine's animation and timer callbacks: a queue of work executed with the engine right after the timeline or the timers have run.
Methods of `Deferred`:
- `pub fn defer(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine) + 'static)` — Runs `f` with the engine once the current animation or timer step is done (in queue order, after the values computed before). Allocates the boxed closure.
Implements: Default, Debug, TickSink

#### fn twine_engine::defer
`pub fn defer(cx: &mut twine_anim::AnimCx<'_>, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine) + 'static) -> bool`
Runs `f` with the engine after the animation step of the callback `cx` belongs to (see `Deferred`). Returns `false` (and logs `warn!`) if `cx` does not come from an engine animation.

#### struct twine_engine::EngineConfig
Engine configuration. Construct with `EngineConfig::default()` and change fields:
Fields:
- `refr_period: twine_core::Duration` — Minimum time between two frames of a display (default 16 ms). Invalidations in between accumulate.
- `max_dirty_areas: usize` — Dirty areas kept per display before they collapse into their bounding box (1..=32, default 32).
- `cooperative_flush: bool` — When no draw buffer is free because the driver still flushes them all (or a framebuffer swap is pending), return `Wake::Now` from `step` instead of waiting inside it. Default `false`.
- `flush_timeout: Option<twine_core::Duration>` — Longest wait for a display driver to finish a flush (to hand a draw buffer back through `poll_flush`) or a framebuffer swap (`present_done`), measured from the start of the flush. `None`: wait forever (a hung DMA transfer freezes the UI). Default 500 ms — far above any chunk transfer on a working bus; raise it for very slow panels (e.g. e-paper drivers whose flush includes the panel refresh).
- `flush_policy: twine_engine::FlushPolicy` — What happens when a display driver reports a failed flush or present (default `FlushPolicy::Reinvalidate`: the area is redrawn on the next frame). Every failure raises `FaultKind::FlushError` whatever the policy.
- `max_consecutive_flush_errors: u16` — Consecutive failed flushes or presents of a display (each chunk counts) after which it is `DisplayState::Failed` — and, with `FlushPolicy::Halt`, stops refreshing (≥ 1, default 8). See `Engine::display_health`.
- `debug_refresh: bool` — Tint every refreshed area with a color that changes per frame (LVGL `LV_USE_REFR_DEBUG`). Default `false`.
- `layer_buf_bytes: usize` — Bytes of the ARGB8888 layer buffer used for opacity groups, transforms and blend modes (≥ 4 KiB, default 24 KiB), allocated on the heap by `Engine::new`. To keep it out of the heap, give the engine a `static` buffer instead (`Engine::with_layer_buf`, `UiBuilder::layer_buf`); this field then reports that buffer's size.
- `glyph_cache_bytes: usize` — Glyph cache budget in bytes (default 8 KiB).
- `image_cache_bytes: usize` — Decoded image cache budget in bytes (default 0: only uncompressed static images).
- `circle_cache_entries: u8` — Quarter-circle coverage cache entries (default 4).
- `gradient_cache_entries: u8` — Gradient color map cache entries (default 4).
- `shadow_cache_entries: u8` — Blurred shadow corner cache entries (default 1).
- `default_font: Option<&'static twine_text::Font>` — The default `Font` when no style sets one (the engine cannot depend on the built-in fonts; `None` = `twine_text::EMPTY_FONT`, which draws nothing).
- `perf_log_period: twine_core::Duration` — Period of the `twine::perf` log line (default 5 s).
- `mem_info: Option<fn() -> twine_engine::MemInfo>` — Memory statistics provider for `RefreshStats` and the `twine::perf` log line (the heap allocator's counters; see `MemInfo` for the pattern with `embedded-alloc` / `esp-alloc` and `HeapPeak`). Default `None`.
- `hires_timer: Option<fn() -> twine_core::Instant>` — High-resolution time source for intra-frame timing (render / flush durations, the worst-case timings of `Engine::timing`, the time limit of `step_budget`). `None`: the timing fields of `RefreshStats` and `TimingReport` stay 0 and nothing is measured.
- `step_budget: twine_engine::StepBudget` — How much one `Engine::step` (the view layer's `Ui::update`) may render: a chunk limit and/or a time limit (`StepBudget`); the rest of a frame continues in the next step (`Wake::Now`), and a step that uses up its time raises `FaultKind::FrameOverrun`. `Engine::step_budgeted` / `Ui::update_budgeted` override it per call. Default `StepBudget::UNLIMITED`. A time limit needs `hires_timer` (checked by `validate`).
- `on_chunk: Option<fn()>` — Called between the chunks of a frame — after each chunk is rendered and handed to the driver (and after each chunk of the chunk-level API): the place to feed a watchdog or yield to a scheduler during a long frame. A plain `fn` (no allocation, no state in the engine); it must not touch the engine. Default `None` (one branch per chunk).
- `long_press_time: twine_core::Duration` — Press duration that triggers a long press (default 400 ms).
- `long_press_repeat: twine_core::Duration` — Repeat period of long-press-repeat events (default 100 ms).
- `scroll_limit: i32` — Pointer movement in pixels that starts scrolling (default 10).
- `scroll_throw: NonZeroU8` — Momentum decay of a scroll throw in percent per input read (default 10): each read keeps `100 − scroll_throw` percent of the throw vector; 100 or more stops a throw at once. Non-zero by its type: a throw always decays, so it always ends (a snapped throw's predicted distance is finite). Never panics.
- `gesture_limit: i32` — Movement in pixels that makes a gesture (default 50).
- `gesture_min_velocity: i32` — Minimum velocity of a gesture in pixels per read period (default 3).
- `multi_click_time: twine_core::Duration` — Maximum gap between clicks of a double / triple click (default 300 ms).
- `multi_click_distance: i32` — Maximum distance in pixels between clicks of a multi-click (default 5).
- `read_period: twine_core::Duration` — Input device read period while pressed or for polled devices (default 30 ms).
- `idle_timeout: Option<twine_core::Duration>` — After this long without user input (see `Engine::inactive_for`), a step that has nothing to do returns `Wake::IdleFor` instead of `Wake::Idle`, so the run loop can pick a deep-sleep mode or put the display to sleep. Until then, an otherwise idle step asks to be woken once, when the timeout passes (one wake-up per inactive period; no polling). Default `None`: never (no extra wake-up). Must be > 0 when set.
Methods of `EngineConfig`:
- `pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Checks the values: `refr_period > 0`, `max_dirty_areas` in `1..=32`, `layer_buf_bytes ≥ 4096`, `max_consecutive_flush_errors ≥ 1`, `flush_timeout > 0` and `idle_timeout > 0` (when set), and that a time limit in `step_budget` has a `hires_timer` to measure it with. `Engine::new` calls it.
  Errors: `EngineError::InvalidConfig` naming the first value out of range. Never panics.
- `pub fn render_config(&self) -> twine_render::RenderConfig` — The renderer's cache budgets derived from this configuration (the cache entry counts and `layer_buf_bytes`, saturated to `u32::MAX`; the other fields keep the renderer's defaults).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Audit

#### trait twine_engine::DesignSystem
`pub trait DesignSystem: Sync + 'static`
A theme described as `const` data (design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.5): the design element table of each mode it ships and the recipes of the widget classes it styles. Implemented on a unit struct and installed as `Theme<Self>`, which costs no heap and runs no start-up code.
Items:
- `type Base: twine_engine::ThemeBase` — The theme this design system extends: a class the design system has no recipe for is styled by it, and its per-display metrics are the display's (a built-in theme, e.g. `twine_theme::Lvgl`, or another design system's `Theme<D>`). `NoBase` for a design system of its own.
- `const NAME: &'static str` — A short name for logs and audit reports (`ThemeHook::name`).
- `const MODES: &'static [(twine_style::ThemeMode, &'static twine_style::design::ElementTable)]` — The modes the theme supports, each with its design element table (`const`, in flash), in the order a mode switch cycles through them; the first is the mode the theme starts in. List only the modes the product shows: an unlisted table is not linked, and a switch to an unlisted mode is refused (the display keeps its mode). Each mode at most once, at most `ThemeMode::ALL``.len()` entries (checked at compile time). A table should define every standard element (`ElementTable::missing_standard`); the display's default font is the first table's `design::FONT_BODY`.
- `const RECIPES: &'static [&'static twine_engine::Recipe]` — The recipes the default `recipe` chooses from (default: none). The first recipe for a class wins.
- `fn recipe(class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Option<twine_engine::RecipeRef> (provided)` — The recipe for exactly `class` (no lineage walk: `Theme<D>` walks the lineage and asks for each class), or `None` (then the `Base` is asked). The default searches `RECIPES` (`Recipe::find`); override it to compute the choice. Called when a node is created or re-themed, never while drawing; must not panic.

#### struct twine_engine::NoBase
The base of a `DesignSystem` that extends no theme (`type Base = NoBase;`): styles nothing, has no design elements, no metrics and the empty font.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, ThemeHook, ThemeBase

#### struct twine_engine::Theme<D: twine_engine::DesignSystem>
A `DesignSystem` installed as a theme: zero-sized, no heap, no start-up code, `Sync`, so it is a `static` (`static THEME: Theme<Clinic> = Theme::new();`) given to a display when it is created (`AppConfig::theme(&THEME)`, `DisplayTheme`). Implements `ThemeHook`:
Methods of `Theme`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — The theme of design system `D`.
Implements: Default, Debug, ThemeHook, ThemeBase

#### trait twine_engine::ThemeBase
`pub trait ThemeBase: twine_engine::ThemeHook + Sync + 'static`
A theme a `DesignSystem` can extend (`DesignSystem::Base`): a theme type with one `'static` instance. Implemented by the built-in themes of `twine-theme` (their default configuration), by every `Theme<D>` (so design systems extend each other) and by `NoBase`.
Items:
- `const THEME: &'static Self` — The instance a design system extending this theme falls back to.
Implemented by: twine_engine::NoBase, twine_engine::Theme<D>

#### trait twine_engine::Variant
`pub trait Variant: Copy + 'static`
A typed choice among the theme classes of one widget type: the value of the view's `.variant(..)` (constant or reactive). Each value names a `WidgetClass` derived from the widget's class (its `base` chain reaches it), set with `Engine::set_theme_class`; a theme that does not know the variant styles the node like the widget's class (lineage fallback).
Items:
- `type Widget: twine_engine::Widget` — The widget type whose views take this variant.
- `fn class(self) -> &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass` — The theme class of this variant (the widget's own class for the default variant).

#### enum twine_engine::BufferMode
The draw buffers of a display (LVGL's render modes): one concept for caller-provided memory, heap allocation and driver-owned framebuffers.
Variants:
- `Partial { a: twine_hal::DrawBufferMem, b: Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem> }` — One or two partial draw buffers provided by the caller.
- `Alloc(twine_engine::BufferSpec)` — Partial draw buffers the engine allocates on the heap (and never frees, like `'static` memory) once the display has been accepted.
- `Full` — Two full framebuffers owned by a `FramebufferDisplay`.
- `Direct` — One full framebuffer owned by a `FramebufferDisplay`, rendered in place.
Methods of `BufferMode`:
- `const ALLOC_PADDING: usize` — Bytes of alignment padding each buffer of `Alloc` carries on the heap (a buffer of `n` bytes takes `n + ALLOC_PADDING`), as counted by `Engine::memory_report`.
- `pub fn partial_single(buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — One partial buffer from caller memory (any `&'static mut [u8]`; prefer `partial_single_from` for `draw_buffers!` statics). The alignment is checked when the display is added.
- `pub fn partial_double(a: &'static mut [u8], b: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — Two partial buffers from caller memory (rendering overlaps flushing); prefer `partial_double_from` for `draw_buffers!` statics. The alignment is checked when the display is added.
- `pub fn partial_single_from<const BYTES: usize>(bufs: &'static mut [twine_hal::DrawBuffer<BYTES>; 1]) -> Self` — One partial buffer from a `twine::draw_buffers!` static of one buffer (`BUF.take()`), aligned by its type.
- `pub fn partial_double_from<const BYTES: usize>(bufs: &'static mut [twine_hal::DrawBuffer<BYTES>; 2]) -> Self` — Two partial buffers from a `twine::draw_buffers!` static of two buffers (`BUFS.take()`), aligned by their type: rendering one overlaps flushing the other.
- `pub const fn alloc(spec: twine_engine::BufferSpec) -> Self` — Partial buffers on the heap, allocated by the engine as `spec` describes once the display has been accepted (nothing is allocated for a refused display).
- `pub const fn full() -> Self` — Double framebuffer with area sync (framebuffer displays).
- `pub const fn direct() -> Self` — Single framebuffer rendered in place (framebuffer displays).
- `pub fn partial_bytes(&self, info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> Result<usize, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Bytes of the (smaller) partial buffer this mode provides for the display `info`: the caller's buffers' length, or what `Alloc` will allocate. Allocates nothing; used to size chunked rendering before the buffers exist.
  Errors: `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch` for `Full` / `Direct`; `EngineError::BufferMisaligned` for caller memory that is not 4-byte aligned.
- `pub fn into_partial(self, info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> Result<(twine_hal::DrawBufferMem, Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem>), twine_engine::EngineError>` — The partial buffers of this mode for the display `info`: the caller's (checked for alignment) or, for `Alloc`, freshly allocated ones (zeroed, 4-byte aligned, leaked). Call it only once the display has been accepted, so that a refused display allocates nothing — `Engine::add_display` does; integrations that render through `Engine::add_chunked_display` call it after that succeeded.
  Errors: `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch` for `Full` / `Direct`; `EngineError::BufferMisaligned` for misaligned caller memory; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for an `Alloc` on a display without pixels, `EngineError::BufferTooSmall` for an `Alloc` on a display whose row alignment exceeds its height. Nothing is allocated on error.
Implements: Debug

#### enum twine_engine::BufferSpec
A request for partial draw buffers on the heap: how many (one or two) and how many full-width rows each (`BufferMode::Alloc`).
Variants:
- `PartialSingle { rows: u16 }` — One partial buffer of `rows` full-width rows: render, flush, wait, repeat.
- `PartialDouble { rows: u16 }` — Two partial buffers of `rows` rows each (rendering overlaps flushing, e.g. DMA).
Methods of `BufferSpec`:
- `pub const fn buffer_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of buffers (1 or 2).
- `pub const fn rows(&self) -> u16` — Rows per buffer as requested.
- `pub fn bytes_per_buffer(&self, info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> usize` — Bytes of **one** buffer for the display `info` (`buffer_bytes` of its logical width).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### const twine_engine::MAX_DISPLAYS
`pub const MAX_DISPLAYS: usize = 4`
Maximum number of displays per engine.

#### enum twine_engine::DisplayCmd
A display command from any context (a task, an interrupt, another thread): send it through a `Channel<DisplayCmd, N>` that the view layer's `UiBuilder::display_commands` registers, or apply it directly with `Engine::display_command` (or the `Engine::set_*` method it names).
Variants:
- `Brightness(twine_core::Fraction)` — Set the panel brightness (`Engine::set_display_brightness`).
- `Sleep` — Put the display to sleep: the panel sleeps and nothing is drawn (`Engine::set_display_sleep` with `true`).
- `Wake` — Wake the display and draw what changed meanwhile (`Engine::set_display_sleep` with `false`).
- `Rotate(twine_core::Rotation)` — Rotate the display (`Engine::set_rotation`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_engine::DisplayControlFault
The `code` of a `FaultKind::DisplayControl` fault: which request failed, and why.
Variants:
- `BrightnessUnsupported = 1` — The driver cannot set the brightness (e.g. an LCD dimmed by its backlight pin, which the application drives).
- `BrightnessFailed = 2` — The driver failed to set the brightness.
- `SleepUnsupported = 3` — The driver cannot sleep; the display is not drawn while "asleep" anyway.
- `SleepFailed = 4` — The driver failed to put the panel to sleep; the display is not drawn while "asleep".
- `WakeFailed = 5` — The driver failed to wake the panel; the display is drawn again anyway (the panel may stay dark until it recovers).
- `RotationFailed = 6` — The driver failed to rotate; the display keeps its rotation.
- `RotationNotReserved = 7` — The rotation needs software rotation and its scratch memory was not reserved (`Engine::reserve_rotation`); the display keeps its rotation.
- `RotationRefused = 8` — The rotated display does not fit its buffers or its draw format is not compiled in (a `FaultKind::FormatDisabled` fault is raised as well); the display keeps its rotation.
Methods of `DisplayControlFault`:
- `pub const fn code(self) -> u32` — The fault record's `code`.
- `pub fn from_code(code: u32) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayControlFault>` — The fault for a record's `code` (`None` for unknown codes).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_engine::DisplayRequests
Requests waiting to be applied to a display's driver (the latest of each kind).
Fields:
- `brightness: Option<twine_core::Fraction>` — A new brightness.
- `sleep: Option<bool>` — Sleep (`true`) or wake (`false`).
- `rotation: Option<twine_core::Rotation>` — A new rotation.
Methods of `DisplayRequests`:
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether nothing is requested.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::DisplayResponses
What the driver answered to the `DisplayRequests` taken with `Engine::take_display_requests`: one entry per request, in the driver's words (errors as their `DriverErrorCode`).
Fields:
- `brightness: Option<Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>>>` — The answer of `set_brightness`.
- `sleep: Option<Result<twine_core::Duration, twine_hal::ControlError<twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>>>` — The answer of `sleep` (the settle time).
- `rotation: Option<Result<twine_hal::DisplayInfo, twine_hal::ControlError<twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>>>` — The answer of `set_rotation` (the new description).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::DrawCx<'a, 'p>
Drawing context of one node: the `Painter` (clipped to what the node may draw), the engine for style lookups, and helpers building draw descriptors from the node's styles.
Methods of `DrawCx`:
- `pub fn painter(&mut self) -> &mut twine_render::Painter<'p>` — The painter (its clip is `clip`).
- `pub fn node(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node being drawn.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &'a twine_engine::Engine` — The engine (styles, tree).
- `pub fn coords(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — Absolute coordinates of the node.
- `pub fn content_area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The coordinates minus padding and border width of `Part::Main`.
- `pub fn clip(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — What the node may draw into (the chunk, clipped by its ancestors).
- `pub fn state(&self) -> twine_style::State` — The node's state.
- `pub fn opa(&self) -> twine_core::Opa` — The node's effective opacity (own `Opa` × ancestors').
- `pub fn style(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — A resolved style property of the node.
- `pub fn style_i32(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> i32` — A resolved integer property.
- `pub fn rect_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` (LVGL `lv_obj_init_draw_rect_dsc`): background (color, gradient), border, outline, shadow and radius, from the resolved styles (`Main` reads the node's style cache), with the node's opacity and recolor applied.
- `pub fn line_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::LineDsc` — The line style of `part` (`Line*` properties).
- `pub fn arc_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ArcDsc<'static>` — The arc style of `part` (`Arc*` properties; an arc image source is not resolved here).
- `pub fn text_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` (`Text*` properties, inherited ones included), with the surface behind the text as its `background` (`Engine::text_background`), which picks the run's text gamma.
- `pub fn rect_dsc_for_state(&self, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` as if the node were in `state` (transitions ignored; see `Engine::rect_dsc_for_state`), with the node's opacity and recolor applied.
- `pub fn text_dsc_for_state(&self, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` as if the node were in `state` (see `Engine::text_dsc_for_state`).
- `pub fn image_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ImageDsc<'static>` — The image style of `part` (`Image*` properties).
- `pub fn with_images<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_render::Painter<'p>, &mut twine_image::ImageContext<'_>) -> R) -> R` — The image context (caches, decoders, file source) for drawing image sources, with the painter: `f(painter, image_context)`.
- `pub fn with_svg<R>(&mut self, bytes: &'static [u8], f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_render::Painter<'p>, &twine_vector::SvgDocument) -> R) -> Result<R, twine_vector::SvgError>` — Calls `f` with the painter and the parsed SVG document of `bytes` (parsed once and cached; `ImageSource::Svg`), feature `svg`.
  Errors: The parse error of a malformed document (logged once when parsed).
- `pub fn with_svg_images<R>(&mut self, bytes: &'static [u8], f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_render::Painter<'p>, &twine_vector::SvgDocument, &mut twine_image::ImageContext<'_>) -> R) -> Result<R, twine_vector::SvgError>` — Calls `f` with the painter, the parsed SVG document of `bytes` and the image context (to cache a rasterized copy), feature `svg`.
  Errors: The parse error of a malformed document.
- `pub fn with_clip<R>(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::DrawCx<'_, 'p>) -> R) -> Option<R>` — Runs `f` with the clip narrowed to `area` (intersected with the current clip).
- `pub fn draw_text(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, text: &str, dsc: &twine_text::TextDsc)` — Draws `text` in `area` with `dsc` (uses the engine's glyph cache).
- `pub fn draw_base(&mut self, part: twine_style::Part)` — Draws the styled rectangle of `part` over the node's coordinates, like LVGL's `lv_obj` draw: shadow → background (color or gradient) → background image → border (unless `BorderPost`) → outline. Invisible elements are skipped.
- `pub fn draw_rect_style(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, part: twine_style::Part)` — Like `draw_base` over `area` instead of the node's coordinates.
- `pub fn draw_border_post(&mut self, part: twine_style::Part)` — Draws the border of `part` when it has `BorderPost` (called by the engine after the children).
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_engine::RectStyle
The resolved rectangle style of a part: a `RectDsc` plus the owned simple gradient (`BgGradDir` + `BgGradColor`) it may refer to. Get the descriptor with `RectStyle::dsc`.
Fields:
- `base: twine_render::RectDsc<'static>` — Everything except a simple gradient.
- `simple_grad: Option<twine_render::Gradient>` — The simple gradient built from `BgGradDir`/`BgGradColor`/stops, if any.
Methods of `RectStyle`:
- `pub fn dsc(&self) -> twine_render::RectDsc<'_>` — The descriptor to pass to `Painter::rect`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### struct twine_engine::Engine
The engine: the widget tree, up to `MAX_DISPLAYS` displays with their screens, layers and refreshers, the render caches (allocated once) and the configuration.
Methods of `Engine`:
- `pub fn set_accel(&mut self, accel: impl twine_render::DrawAccel + 'static)` — Attaches a draw accelerator (e.g. `twine_accel_stm32::Dma2d`), taking ownership of it (and so of the peripheral it drives): every chunk the engine renders passes it to the `Painter`, which offloads fills, blits and glyph blending and draws whatever the accelerator reports `Unsupported` in software. The painter waits for queued operations before a chunk is flushed or presented. Replaces (drops) any previous accelerator.
- `pub fn clear_accel(&mut self)` — Detaches (drops) the draw accelerator: rendering returns to software only. No-op without one. Never panics (dropping the accelerator runs its `Drop`, if any).
- `pub fn has_accel(&self) -> bool` — Whether a draw accelerator is attached.
- `pub fn anim_start(&mut self, node: twine_engine::NodeId, prop: twine_engine::AnimProp, anim: twine_anim::Anim) -> twine_anim::AnimId` — Starts `anim` on property `prop` of `node` (its target is set to `AnimTarget::Node`); a running animation of the same node and property is replaced (LVGL). Values are written through the idempotent setters:
- `pub fn anim_start_fn(&mut self, anim: twine_anim::Anim, exec: impl FnMut(&mut twine_engine::Engine, i32) + 'static) -> twine_anim::AnimId` — Starts `anim` with a closure receiving the engine and each new value (LVGL `exec_cb`). The closure runs right after the animation step, like every engine animation write.
- `pub fn anim_stop(&mut self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Stops an animation (no callbacks). Returns `false` for a finished or unknown id.
- `pub fn anim_pause(&mut self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Pauses an animation at its current value. Returns `false` for a finished or unknown id.
- `pub fn anim_resume(&mut self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Continues a paused animation where it stopped. Returns `false` for a finished or unknown id.
- `pub fn anim_restart(&mut self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Restarts an animation from its beginning (delay included). Returns `false` for a finished or unknown id. A restart is a start: the current `motion` preference is applied to the animation's timing again (a stricter preference set since shortens it; a timing shortened by an earlier preference stays short — start a new animation to play the full timing again).
- `pub fn anim_exists(&self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is a live animation (running or paused).
- `pub fn anim_is_paused(&self, id: twine_anim::AnimId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is a paused animation.
- `pub fn anims_of(&self, node: twine_engine::NodeId) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_anim::AnimId> + '_` — The animations running on properties of `node` (started with `anim_start`).
- `pub fn motion(&self) -> twine_anim::Motion` — The motion preference (default `Motion::Full`): see `set_motion`.
- `pub fn set_motion(&mut self, motion: twine_anim::Motion)` — Sets the global motion preference (the platform's "reduce motion" accessibility setting; `Motion` documents what each level does and which animations are essential). It is applied once when an animation starts — every animation of the engine: those of `anim_start` / `anim_start_fn` (and so the view layer's tweens), style transitions (with `Motion::None` they are not created at all), screen load animations and scroll animations — never per frame.
- `pub fn anim_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of live animations (running or paused, including style transitions and screen load animations).
- `pub fn timer_add(&mut self, period: twine_core::Duration, cb: impl FnMut(&mut twine_engine::Engine, twine_anim::TimerId) + 'static) -> twine_anim::TimerId` — Adds a timer calling `cb(engine, id)` every `period` (LVGL `lv_timer_create`), first one period after the current update (or after the next update when called between updates). A timer late by several periods runs once. `step` wakes up exactly when the next timer is due. When `Limits::max_timers` timers exist already, it is not added: the result is `TimerId::DANGLING` and a `FaultKind::Capacity` fault (code `Timers`) is raised.
- `pub fn timer_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of timers (running or paused).
- `pub fn timer_remove(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Removes a timer (also from inside its own callback). Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_pause(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Pauses a timer. Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_resume(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Resumes a paused timer; its period keeps counting from its last run (LVGL). Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_set_period(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId, period: twine_core::Duration) -> bool` — Changes a timer's period. Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_ready(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Runs a timer at the next update regardless of its period. Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_reset(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Restarts a timer's period from now (from the next update when called between updates). Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_set_repeat_count(&mut self, id: twine_anim::TimerId, count: Option<u32>) -> bool` — Limits the number of remaining runs of a timer (`None` = forever); at zero it is removed. Returns `false` for an unknown id.
- `pub fn timer_exists(&self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is a timer of the engine (running or paused).
- `pub fn timer_is_paused(&self, id: twine_anim::TimerId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is a paused timer (`timer_pause`; `false` for running and unknown timers).
- `pub fn run_timers(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant)` — Runs the due timers at `now` (update cycle step 4; called by `step`).
- `pub fn run_anims(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant)` — Advances every animation to `now` and applies the new values (update cycle step 5; called by `step`). Animations started by the applied values or callbacks get their first values in the same call.
- `pub fn now(&self) -> twine_core::Instant` — The engine's current time: the time of the running step (`step`, `Ui::update` — the platform clock's reading), else the last one it knew. Timers and animations run on it; view-layer hooks timestamp data with it (`ScopeExt::watch_fresh`). Never panics.
- `pub fn add_display(&mut self, driver: impl twine_hal::DisplayDriver + 'static, buffers: twine_engine::BufferMode, theme: Option<twine_engine::DisplayTheme>) -> Result<twine_engine::DisplayId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Registers a display with an embedded frame memory (SPI/i80 panels). `buffers` must be `BufferMode::Partial` or `BufferMode::Alloc`. Creates the display's bottom layer, first screen, top layer and system layer, and schedules a full redraw. The first display becomes the default one.
  Errors: `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch` for `Full` / `Direct`; `EngineError::TooManyDisplays`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` (and `FaultKind::Capacity` is raised) when `Limits::max_nodes` leaves no room for the display's 4 layer and screen nodes; `EngineError::FormatDisabled` (and `FaultKind::FormatDisabled` is raised) when the renderer for the display's colour format is not compiled in; `EngineError::BufferMisaligned` for caller buffers that are not 4-byte aligned; `EngineError::BufferTooSmall` for buffers shorter than `DisplayInfo::align` rows (at least one); `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a display without pixels.
- `pub fn add_chunked_display(&mut self, info: twine_hal::DisplayInfo, chunk_bytes: usize, theme: Option<twine_engine::DisplayTheme>) -> Result<twine_engine::DisplayId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Registers a display without a driver, rendered through the chunk-level refresh API (`refresh_begin`, `render_chunk`, `refresh_end`): the caller owns the draw buffers (at least `chunk_bytes` each) and flushes each rendered chunk itself, e.g. through an async driver. Rotation, alignment and mono conversion work as with `add_display`.
  Errors: `EngineError::TooManyDisplays`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when `Limits::max_nodes` leaves no room for the display's layer and screen nodes; `EngineError::FormatDisabled` (see above); `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a display without pixels.
- `pub fn add_framebuffer_display(&mut self, driver: impl twine_hal::FramebufferDisplay + 'static, buffers: twine_engine::BufferMode, theme: Option<twine_engine::DisplayTheme>) -> Result<twine_engine::DisplayId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Registers a memory-mapped display (LTDC, RGB, Linux fb). `buffers` must be `BufferMode::Full` (the driver must hand out two framebuffers) or `BufferMode::Direct`. Each framebuffer must hold exactly `width × height` pixels. Software rotation is not available in these modes.
  Errors: `EngineError::BufferModeMismatch` for a partial or `Alloc` buffer mode, or a `Full` driver that hands out one framebuffer; `EngineError::TooManyDisplays`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when `Limits::max_nodes` leaves no room for the display's layer and screen nodes; `EngineError::FormatDisabled` (see above); `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a software rotation or an `I1` width that is not a multiple of 8; `EngineError::BufferTooSmall` for a framebuffer that is not exactly `width × height` pixels.
- `pub fn default_display(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayId>` — The first registered display.
- `pub fn displays(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_engine::DisplayId> + '_` — Every registered display.
- `pub fn display_info(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_hal::DisplayInfo>` — The description of `display`.
- `pub fn driver<D: 'static>(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<&D>` — The driver of `display` as `D` (e.g. to read a test display's pixels).
- `pub fn driver_mut<D: 'static>(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<&mut D>` — The driver of `display` as `&mut D`.
- `pub fn create_screen(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Creates a new (inactive) screen on `display`: a root `Obj` covering the display.
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for an unknown `display`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when `Limits::max_nodes` is reached (a capacity fault is raised).
- `pub fn load_screen(&mut self, screen: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Makes `screen` the active screen of its display (instantly) and redraws the display (`ScreenUnloadStart`, `ScreenLoadStart`, `ScreenLoaded`, `ScreenUnloaded`). A screen load animation in progress is finished first. Same as `load_screen_anim` with `ScreenAnim::None`.
- `pub fn active_screen(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The active screen of `display`.
- `pub fn screens(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> &[twine_engine::NodeId]` — The screens of `display`.
- `pub fn bottom_layer(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The layer below every screen (LVGL `lv_layer_bottom`).
- `pub fn top_layer(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The layer above the screens, for popups (LVGL `lv_layer_top`).
- `pub fn sys_layer(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The topmost layer, for the performance overlay and cursors (LVGL `lv_layer_sys`).
- `pub fn display_of(&self, node: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayId>` — The display `node` belongs to (walks to the root).
- `pub fn set_display_vsync(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, on: bool)` — Calls `wait_vsync` on the driver before the first flush of every frame of `display` (tear-effect synchronization).
- `pub fn framebuffer(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, index: u8) -> Option<&[u8]>` — The bytes of framebuffer `index` of a framebuffer display (`None` for other displays or while the buffer is lent out).
- `pub fn create(&mut self, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, widget: Box<dyn twine_engine::Widget>) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Creates a node for `widget` as the last child of `parent`, then calls `Widget::init`. Unknown parents log `warn!` and fail with `EngineError::NodeNotFound`.
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `parent`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when `Limits::max_nodes` is reached (a capacity fault is raised); `EngineError::TooDeep` when the node would be deeper than `Limits::max_tree_depth` (a capacity fault is raised).
- `pub fn create_root(&mut self, widget: Box<dyn twine_engine::Widget>) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Creates a root node that belongs to no display (LVGL `lv_obj_create(NULL)` before the screen is used). Useful for tests and for building trees off-screen.
  Errors: `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when `Limits::max_nodes` is reached (a capacity fault is raised).
- `pub fn widget<W: twine_engine::Widget>(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&W>` — The widget of `id` as `W` (`None` for unknown ids or other widget types).
- `pub fn with_widget_mut<W: twine_engine::Widget, R>(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, f: impl FnOnce(&mut W, &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>) -> R) -> Option<R>` — Calls `f` with the widget of `id` as `&mut W` and a `WidgetCx` for the node: the way to call a widget's setters (LVGL `lv_<widget>_set_*`). Returns `None` (and logs `warn!`) when the node does not exist or holds another widget type.
- `pub fn delete(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Deletes `id` and its subtree. Every node of the subtree receives `Delete` (children before their parent) while it still exists; then the nodes leave their focus groups, the area is invalidated, the nodes are freed and the parent receives `ChildDeleted` (with the deleted node as target). Layers and active screens cannot be deleted. The animations and style transitions of the deleted nodes stop.
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `id`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a layer, an active screen or (with `display-integrity`) the fail-safe screen. Nothing is deleted on error.
- `pub fn set_display_brightness(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, level: twine_core::Fraction) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Requests the panel brightness `level` (`Fraction::ZERO` darkest, `ONE` brightest) of `display`: applied by the next step between frames (see the `DisplayCmd` docs). Idempotent. A driver without brightness control raises `FaultKind::DisplayControl` (`DisplayControlFault::BrightnessUnsupported`).
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound`.
- `pub fn set_display_sleep(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, sleep: bool) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Requests sleep (`true`) or wake (`false`) for `display`, applied by the next step (see the `DisplayCmd` docs): asleep, the panel sleeps and nothing is drawn; after a wake, what changed meanwhile is drawn once the panel's settle time has passed. Idempotent.
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound`.
- `pub fn set_rotation(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Requests the rotation `rotation` for `display`, applied by the next step between frames: hardware rotation through the driver, or software rotation (needs `reserve_rotation`); then a re-layout, a full redraw and the input devices fitted again (see the `DisplayCmd` docs). Idempotent: the current rotation cancels a pending request. Allocates nothing.
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a framebuffer display (they cannot be rotated at run time). A rotation that turns out not to fit when it is applied raises `FaultKind::DisplayControl` instead.
- `pub fn display_command(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, cmd: twine_engine::DisplayCmd) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Applies a `DisplayCmd` to `display` (the `set_*` method it names).
  Errors: As the method it calls.
- `pub fn display_asleep(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> bool` — Whether `display` is asleep (a sleep request was applied, and no wake since). `false` for unknown displays. Never panics.
- `pub fn display_brightness(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_core::Fraction>` — The brightness last applied to `display` (`None` before any, or for unknown displays). Never panics.
- `pub fn display_requests_pending(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> bool` — Whether requests for `display` wait to be applied (`false` for unknown displays). Never panics.
- `pub fn reserve_rotation(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Reserves, once, the memory software rotation of `display` needs in **every** rotation: rotation scratch buffers sized for its draw buffers (and, for mono and chunked displays, their shadow buffers). Call it at start-up for a display that may be rotated at run time by a driver without hardware rotation; later `set_rotation` calls then allocate nothing. Allocates nothing for memory the display already has (a display added in software rotation has it for that geometry). Without it, such a rotation is refused (`DisplayControlFault::RotationNotReserved`) — memory is never allocated silently while the UI runs.
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` for a framebuffer display.
- `pub fn take_display_requests(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, now: twine_core::Instant) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayRequests>` — For a display added with `add_chunked_display`: takes the requests to apply now, if any and if the display is ready for them (no frame in progress, the panel's settle time passed). The caller applies them to its driver in the order rotation, brightness, sleep, and reports with `complete_display_requests` before the next frame. `None` for other displays (the engine applies their requests itself).
- `pub fn complete_display_requests(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, requests: twine_engine::DisplayRequests, responses: twine_engine::DisplayResponses, now: twine_core::Instant) -> Option<twine_core::Rotation>` — Applies the driver's answers to the requests taken with `take_display_requests` (see the `DisplayCmd` docs): records brightness and sleep state, the settle time, and for a rotation re-checks, re-lays out and redraws the display, raising `FaultKind::DisplayControl` for what failed. Returns the rotation the caller must restore on its driver when a hardware rotation had to be refused (the engine keeps the old one), `None` otherwise. Unknown displays are ignored (`None`). Never panics.
- `pub fn opa_recursive(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Opa` — The effective opacity of `id`: its `Opa` times every ancestor's.
- `pub fn transform_size(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> (i32, i32)` — The extra size `TransformWidth` / `TransformHeight` add to each side of `id` (LVGL `lv_area_increase(&coords, w, h)` in the object's drawing).
- `pub fn draw_area(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Rect` — The area the object's rectangle is drawn in: its coordinates grown by `transform_size`.
- `pub fn rect_dsc(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` of `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_init_draw_rect_dsc`): background (color or gradient), border, outline, shadow and radius, every opacity multiplied by `opa` and every color recolored.
- `pub fn rect_dsc_for_state(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` of `id` as if the node were in `state`, with running transitions ignored (LVGL sets `obj->state` and `skip_trans` around `lv_obj_init_draw_rect_dsc`): for widgets that draw several items of one part in their own states, like the buttons of a button matrix. Opacity and recolor are applied as in `rect_dsc` (ancestors in their current state).
- `pub fn text_dsc(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` of `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_init_draw_label_dsc`): `Text*` properties (inherited ones included), opacity multiplied by `opa`, color recolored, and `TextDsc::background` set to the surface the text is drawn over (see `text_background`), so the run gets the text gamma of its real polarity.
- `pub fn text_background(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part) -> Option<twine_core::Color>` — The color of the surface the text of `part` of `id` is drawn over: the background of `part` itself when it is opaque (a button-matrix item, a selected option, a block cursor), else the `Main` background of the nearest node — `id` itself first, then its ancestors — whose background is opaque (`BgOpacity` ≥ 253, LVGL's `LV_OPA_MAX`), with `id`'s recolor applied like the text's. `None` when nothing behind the text is opaque (the text color alone then decides its polarity).
