- `pub fn text_dsc_for_state(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` of `id` as if the node were in `state`, with transitions ignored (see `rect_dsc_for_state`); the `background` is `part`'s or the node's `Main` background in `state` when opaque, else the nearest opaque ancestor's (see `text_background`).
- `pub fn image_dsc(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_render::ImageDsc<'static>` — The image style of `part` of `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_init_draw_image_dsc`): `ImageOpa` multiplied by `opa`, `ImageRecolor` combined with the style recolor.
- `pub fn line_dsc(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_render::LineDsc` — The line style of `part` of `id` (`Line*` properties).
- `pub fn arc_dsc(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_render::ArcDsc<'static>` — The arc style of `part` of `id` (`Arc*` properties; an arc image source is not resolved here).
- `pub fn new(config: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Result<twine_engine::Engine, twine_engine::EngineError>` — An engine with `config` (validated). Allocates the render caches once, the layer buffer of `EngineConfig::layer_buf_bytes` included (see `with_layer_buf` to keep it out of the heap).
  Errors: `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `config` is out of range (`EngineConfig::validate`). Never panics.
- `pub fn with_layer_buf(config: twine_engine::EngineConfig, layer_buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Result<twine_engine::Engine, twine_engine::EngineError>` — An engine like `new` whose layer buffer — the renderer's largest scratch buffer (opacity groups, transforms, blend modes; ARGB8888) — is `layer_buf`, caller memory such as a `static`, instead of `EngineConfig::layer_buf_bytes` bytes of heap. `config().layer_buf_bytes` then reports `layer_buf.len()`, and `memory_report` lists it as static. The bytes need no alignment or initial content. `Ui::builder(..).layer_buf(..)` passes it on.
  Errors: `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `config` is out of range or `layer_buf` is shorter than 4 KiB (the minimum of `layer_buf_bytes`). Allocates nothing on error; never panics.
- `pub fn tree(&self) -> &twine_engine::Tree` — The widget tree.
- `pub fn config(&self) -> &twine_engine::EngineConfig` — The configuration.
- `pub fn set_limits(&mut self, limits: &twine_core::Limits) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Applies the engine's share of `limits`: `max_nodes` (screens and layers included), `max_tree_depth`, `max_text_len`, `max_handlers`, `max_theme_classes`, `max_timers` and `max_anims` bound creations from now on (each refusal raises `FaultKind::Capacity` with its `CapacityFault` code). With `preallocate` it also reserves the node arena, the delete scratch, the theme-class table and the timer and animation tables, so staying within the limits allocates nothing there. Lowering a bound below the current count refuses further creations until enough are deleted — except `max_tree_depth`: drawing, hit testing and layout recurse over the tree, and their stack bound (`docs/safety/profile.md` § 10.4) holds only if no node is deeper than the limit, so a depth limit below the current tree's depth is refused. The `Ui` builders call it with `AppConfig::limits`; an engine created on its own starts with `Limits::DEFAULT`.
  Errors: `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `Limits::validate` refuses `limits`, or when the tree already has nodes deeper than `max_tree_depth`; nothing is applied.
- `pub fn set_partition(&mut self, p: twine_core::Partition)` — Puts the engine into partition `p` (ADR-001): from now on every growth point of the engine — its node arena, animation and timer tables, node-local styles, scratch buffers and its widgets' buffers (`WidgetCx::partition`) — notes allocations after a seal in `p`'s seal domain (`twine_core::alloc_guard`), and `raise_alloc_after_seal` reports `p`'s growth only. An engine starts in `Partition::MAIN`; `AppConfig::apply_limits(rt, engine)` sets the partition of the `Ui`'s runtime token, right after the engine is created and before any display or node. Call it before the start-up allocations it should attribute (growth before the call stays in the previous partition's domain). Idempotent; allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the engine belongs to (`set_partition`): whose seal domain its growth is noted in. Free; never panics.
- `pub fn limits(&self) -> &twine_core::Limits` — The limits applied with `set_limits` (default `Limits::DEFAULT`).
- `pub fn config_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::EngineConfig` — The configuration, mutably (cache sizes cannot change after `new`).
- `pub fn render_cache_stats(&self) -> twine_render::RenderCacheStats` — Hit/miss counters of the render caches.
- `pub fn set_file_source(&mut self, fs: Option<Box<dyn twine_image::FileSource>>)` — Sets where `ImageSource::File` images are read from (`None`: file images are not found). The file system crate provides an implementation over its virtual file system; any `FileSource` works.
- `pub fn set_vfs(&mut self, vfs: twine_fs::Vfs)` — Reads `ImageSource::File` images from `vfs` (paths like `"A:/img/logo.qoi"`), replacing any file source (feature `fs`). Headers are probed from the first `HEADER_PROBE_BYTES` of a file; pixels are decoded on first draw into the image cache (`EngineConfig::image_cache_bytes`).
- `pub fn vfs_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut twine_fs::Vfs>` — The virtual file system installed with `set_vfs` (e.g. to mount more drives), feature `fs`.
- `pub fn image_cache_invalidate(&mut self, src: &twine_image::ImageSource)` — Drops the decoded pixels and the cached header of `src` (LVGL `lv_image_cache_drop`), e.g. after the file changed: the next draw reads and decodes it again. Widgets showing `src` are not invalidated (invalidate them to redraw).
- `pub fn set_image_cache_budget(&mut self, bytes: usize)` — Changes the image cache budget (`EngineConfig::image_cache_bytes` at creation; LVGL `lv_image_cache_resize`), evicting least recently used images that no longer fit.
- `pub fn svg_parse_count(&self) -> u32` — How many SVG documents were parsed so far (feature `svg`; a cached document is not parsed again).
- `pub fn image_warn_once(&mut self, src: &twine_image::ImageSource) -> bool` — `true` the first time it is called for `src`: lets widgets log one warning per source (e.g. a missing file) instead of one per frame.
- `pub fn image_header(&mut self, src: &twine_image::ImageSource) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>` — The header (size, format) of an image source, read through the header cache and the decoder registry (encoded data and files are probed, not decoded).
  Errors: `twine_image::Error::NotFound` for missing files (or without a file source), `twine_image::Error::InvalidHeader` for unknown formats, `twine_image::Error::UnsupportedSource` for symbols and SVG (not raster images).
- `pub fn perf_monitor(&self) -> &twine_engine::PerfMonitor` — The performance monitor (fps and CPU of the last one-second window).
- `pub fn set_bounds_overlay(&mut self, on: bool)` — Toggles the layout bounds overlay (every node's coordinates outlined in magenta, drawn above the system layer) and redraws every display.
- `pub fn bounds_overlay(&self) -> bool` — Whether the layout bounds overlay is on.
- `pub fn invalidate_all(&mut self)` — Schedules a full redraw of every display.
- `pub fn dump(&self) -> String` — A dump of every root of every display (see `Tree::dump`), bottom layer first.
- `pub fn raise_fault(&mut self, record: twine_engine::FaultRecord)` — Raises a fault: stamps it with the current time, records it (pending set, counters, last record of its kind) and calls the `FaultHook`.
- `pub fn take_faults(&mut self) -> twine_core::Faults` — The kinds raised since the last call, clearing them (for applications that poll, e.g. once per update). O(1); never panics.
- `pub fn raise_alloc_after_seal(&mut self)` — Raises `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` for the allocations Twine's growth points noted in this engine's partition (`partition`) since the last call while it was sealed (`twine_core::alloc_guard`): one record, `code` = the last `AllocSite`, `occurrences` = their number. Does nothing when there were none (a few loads). `Ui` calls it at every update, and `take_faults` before it reports. Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn pending_faults(&self) -> twine_core::Faults` — The kinds raised since the last `take_faults`, without clearing them. Never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn fault_counts(&self) -> twine_core::FaultCounts` — Occurrences of every kind since the engine was created (saturating at `u32::MAX`, never reset; `take_faults` does not clear them). Never panics.
- `pub fn last_fault(&self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> Option<&twine_engine::FaultRecord>` — The last record raised of `kind` (kept until another one of that kind replaces it; `take_faults` does not clear it). Never panics.
- `pub fn set_fault_hook(&mut self, hook: Option<twine_engine::FaultHook>)` — Sets the function called for every raised fault (`None` removes it; a new hook replaces the previous one). The hook runs synchronously inside `raise_fault`, wherever the fault is detected (see `FaultHook`); it receives no engine, so it cannot re-enter this engine. Never panics, allocates nothing.
- `pub fn create_group(&mut self) -> Result<twine_engine::GroupId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Creates an empty focus group (wrapping, not editing, `RefocusPolicy::Prev`).
  Errors: `EngineError::TooManyGroups` when `MAX_GROUPS` groups exist (a capacity fault is raised).
- `pub fn delete_group(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId)` — Deletes a group: the focused node is defocused, the members leave the group, inputs using it get no group, and it stops being the default group.
- `pub fn set_default_group(&mut self, g: Option<twine_engine::GroupId>)` — Sets the group new widgets of classes with `GroupDef::True` join automatically.
- `pub fn default_group(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::GroupId>` — The default group.
- `pub fn group_add(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Appends `id` to group `g` (leaving its previous group first). The first node of a group gets the focus.
- `pub fn group_remove(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Removes `id` from its group. If it was focused, the focus moves on according to the group's `RefocusPolicy` (or the group ends up without focus).
- `pub fn group_remove_all(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId)` — Removes every node from group `g` (the focused one is defocused).
- `pub fn focus(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Focuses `id` in its group (LVGL `lv_group_focus_obj`): leaves edit mode, defocuses the previous node. Ignored when the group is frozen or `id` is in no group.
- `pub fn focus_next(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId)` — Focuses the next focusable node of `g` (skipping hidden and disabled nodes; wrapping if enabled, else calling the edge callback at the end).
- `pub fn focus_prev(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId)` — Focuses the previous focusable node of `g` (see `focus_next`).
- `pub fn focus_freeze(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, frozen: bool)` — Freezes (`true`) the focus of `g`: focus changes are ignored until unfrozen.
- `pub fn set_editing(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, editing: bool)` — Enters or leaves edit mode (encoder). The focused node receives `Focused` again, which adds or removes its `EDITED` state.
- `pub fn group_editing(&self, g: twine_engine::GroupId) -> bool` — Whether `g` is in edit mode.
- `pub fn set_wrap(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, wrap: bool)` — Whether `focus_next`/`focus_prev` wrap around at the ends (default `true`).
- `pub fn set_focus_cb(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, cb: Option<twine_engine::FocusCb>)` — Sets the callback run after the focus moved (it may use the engine).
- `pub fn set_edge_cb(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, cb: Option<twine_engine::EdgeCb>)` — Sets the callback run when a non-wrapping group hits its end.
- `pub fn set_refocus_policy(&mut self, g: twine_engine::GroupId, policy: twine_engine::RefocusPolicy)` — Sets where the focus goes when the focused node leaves the group.
- `pub fn focused(&self, g: twine_engine::GroupId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The focused node of `g`.
- `pub fn group_of(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::GroupId>` — The group `id` belongs to.
- `pub fn group_count(&self, g: twine_engine::GroupId) -> usize` — Number of nodes in `g`.
- `pub fn group_nodes(&self, g: twine_engine::GroupId) -> &[twine_engine::NodeId]` — The nodes of `g` in focus order.
- `pub fn set_input_group(&mut self, input: twine_engine::InputId, g: Option<twine_engine::GroupId>)` — Attaches a keypad or encoder to group `g` (`None` detaches it).
- `pub fn add_event_handler(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, filter: twine_engine::EventFilter, h: impl FnMut(&mut twine_engine::EventCx<'_>, &twine_engine::Event) -> twine_engine::EventResult + 'static) -> twine_engine::HandlerId` — Registers a user handler on `id` for the events selected by `filter`. Handlers run in registration order, after the widget's own `Widget::event`. A handler added while an event is being dispatched runs from the next dispatch on. While a handler runs it is taken out of its node: events sent to the same node from inside it (nested dispatch) reach the node's other handlers, not the running one.
- `pub fn remove_event_handler(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, h: twine_engine::HandlerId) -> bool` — Removes the handler `h` of `id` (also allowed from inside the handler itself). Returns whether it existed.
- `pub fn remove_all_event_handlers(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Removes every user handler of `id`.
- `pub fn event_handler_count(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> usize` — Number of user handlers of `id`.
- `pub fn register_event_code(&mut self) -> twine_engine::EventCode` — A new event code for application events (LVGL `lv_event_register_id`): `Custom(0)`, `Custom(1)`, …
- `pub fn post_event(&mut self, target: twine_engine::NodeId, code: twine_engine::EventCode, param: twine_engine::EventParam)` — Sends an event to `target` once its widget can take part (LVGL-style notifications such as `ValueChanged` sent by the widget itself).
- `pub fn send_event_text(&mut self, target: twine_engine::NodeId, code: twine_engine::EventCode, text: &str) -> twine_engine::EventResult` — Sends an event carrying `text` (`EventParam::Text`) and returns the result like `send_event`. The text is copied into a buffer of the engine (reused: no allocation once it is large enough) and readable by the handlers with `EventCx::text` while the event is dispatched.
- `pub fn event_text(&self, param: &twine_engine::EventParam) -> Option<&str>` — The text of an `EventParam::Text` while its event is being dispatched (`None` for other parameters and for handles of finished dispatches).
- `pub fn send_event(&mut self, target: twine_engine::NodeId, code: twine_engine::EventCode, param: twine_engine::EventParam) -> twine_engine::EventResult` — Sends an event to `target` and returns the most decisive result of its handlers.
- `pub fn display_health(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::DisplayHealth>` — The flush health of `display` (`None` for unknown displays): state, consecutive errors, last success and last error code. See `FlushPolicy`. Never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn recover_display(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Recovers `display` after a failure (typically once the application has reset the panel or its bus): clears the consecutive error count, resumes refreshing a `Halted` display and redraws the whole display (its content is unknown). The display is `Healthy` again until the next failure. A no-op for the counters of a healthy display (it is still redrawn).
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for unknown displays (never panics).
- `pub fn report_flush(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, area: twine_core::Rect, result: Result<(), twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>)` — Reports the outcome of a flush of a display added with `add_chunked_display`: `area` as returned by `render_chunk` (physical coordinates under software rotation), `result` the driver's outcome. Applies the `FlushPolicy` and updates the `DisplayHealth` exactly as for the engine's own flushes (the failed area is redrawn by a later frame). Call it for every flush, successful or not, also after `refresh_end`. Other displays report their flushes themselves; a call for them logs `warn!` and is ignored. Never panics (an unknown display is ignored with a `warn!`).
- `pub fn report_flush_timeout(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, areas: &[twine_core::Rect], waited: twine_core::Duration)` — Reports that a flush of a display added with `add_chunked_display` did not complete within `EngineConfig::flush_timeout` and was abandoned after `waited` (the caller dropped the flush): the async runtime's counterpart of the engine's own bounded wait, with the same effects. Raises `FaultKind::FlushTimeout` once (`code`: ms waited), marks the display `DisplayState::Failed` (halted under `FlushPolicy::Halt`), marks `areas` dirty again unless `FlushPolicy::Ignore` — the hung chunk and any chunk rendered but not flushed, each as returned by `render_chunk` — and, when the display's frame is open, abandons it: its unrendered rest stays dirty, `render_chunk` returns `None`, and the next frame starts no earlier than `refr_period` later. The next successful `report_flush` makes the display healthy again. Displays with their own driver, and unknown displays, are ignored with a `warn!`. Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn hit_test(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, p: twine_core::Point) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node a press at `p` on `display` would go to: the topmost `CLICKABLE` node whose hit test accepts `p` (children of a node are searched only where the node itself contains `p`, unless it has `OVERFLOW_VISIBLE`); non-clickable nodes pass the press to their parent. `None` when nothing is hit or the node hit is `DISABLED` (disabled nodes block the press and receive nothing).
- `pub fn add_input(&mut self, dev: impl twine_hal::InputDevice + 'static, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Result<twine_engine::InputId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Registers an input device for `display`. At most `MAX_INPUTS` devices; more fail with `EngineError::TooManyInputs`, an unknown display with `EngineError::DisplayNotFound`.
  Errors: `EngineError::TooManyInputs` when `MAX_INPUTS` devices are registered; `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for an unknown `display`.
- `pub fn remove_input(&mut self, id: twine_engine::InputId)` — Removes an input device (it is dropped; a scroll it was doing ends without events).
- `pub fn set_input_enabled(&mut self, id: twine_engine::InputId, on: bool)` — Enables or disables a device. A disabled device is not read at all.
- `pub fn input_enabled(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> bool` — Whether the device exists and is enabled.
- `pub fn input_kind(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_hal::InputKind>` — The kind of a device.
- `pub fn input_group(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_engine::GroupId>` — The group a keypad or encoder sends its keys to.
- `pub fn inputs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_engine::InputId> + '_` — Every registered device.
- `pub fn notify_input(&mut self, id: twine_engine::InputId)` — Marks an interrupt device as having new input: the next `read_inputs` reads it. Call this from the main loop after the device's interrupt woke it.
- `pub fn notify_input_all(&mut self)` — Marks every device as notified (for a shared interrupt line).
- `pub fn set_button_points(&mut self, id: twine_engine::InputId, points: &'static [twine_core::Point])` — Maps the buttons of a `InputKind::Button` device to screen points: button `n` presses like a pointer at `points[n]`.
- `pub fn gesture_dir(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_style::Side>` — The direction of the last gesture of a pointer (cleared by the next press).
- `pub fn set_gesture_limits(&mut self, limit: i32, min_velocity: i32)` — Changes the gesture thresholds: movement in pixels that makes a gesture and the minimum movement per read.
- `pub fn input_reset(&mut self, id: Option<twine_engine::InputId>, obj: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>)` — Resets the processing state of device `id` (`None`: every device), like LVGL `lv_indev_reset`: the pressed node is forgotten and a device that is held is ignored until it is released. With `obj`, only references to `obj` among the last pressed and hovered nodes are dropped; without, all of them.
- `pub fn input_wait_release(&mut self, id: twine_engine::InputId)` — Ignores device `id` until it is released (LVGL `lv_indev_wait_release`).
- `pub fn active_input(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::InputId>` — The device being processed.
- `pub fn input_scroll_obj(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node pointer `id` is scrolling (dragging or throwing) since its press turned into a scroll, if any (LVGL `lv_indev_get_scroll_obj`). Widgets check it on `Released` to tell a tap from the end of a drag.
- `pub fn input_pressed(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> bool` — Whether device `id` is pressed in its last sample (a pointer touching, a key or the encoder button down; LVGL `indev->state == LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED`).
- `pub fn input_health(&self, id: twine_engine::InputId) -> Option<twine_hal::DeviceHealth>` — The health device `id` reported with its last read (`DeviceHealth::Ok` before the first read), `None` for unknown devices.
- `pub fn read_inputs(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant)` — Reads the devices that need it at `now` and turns their samples into events (design order: the first thing `step` does).
- `pub fn inactive_for(&self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_core::Duration` — The time since the last user input: a changed sample of any input device, a device held down (pressed pointer, key or button), or `trigger_activity` — LVGL's `lv_display_get_inactive_time`. Before any input, the time since the first step. Costs nothing on the input path beyond one store per changed or held sample.
- `pub fn trigger_activity(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant)` — Records user input at `now` that did not come through an input device (e.g. a hardware button the application handles itself), restarting `inactive_for` and the `EngineConfig::idle_timeout`. Never panics.
- `pub fn input_deadline(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Instant>` — The earliest instant an input device needs to be read (polling period, held devices, long press timers). `None`: no device needs the CPU.
- `pub fn invalidate(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, reason: twine_engine::InvalidateReason)` — Invalidates the area of `id` (its coordinates plus extra draw size, clipped by its ancestors) so it is redrawn in the next frame. Hidden nodes and nodes of inactive screens are skipped. Unknown ids are ignored.
- `pub fn invalidate_node_area(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, area: twine_core::Rect, reason: twine_engine::InvalidateReason)` — Invalidates `area` (absolute) as far as it is visible through `id`'s clipping. A safety-critical node (`ObjFlags::SAFETY_CRITICAL`, feature `display-integrity`) is invalidated whole: it is never redrawn in parts.
- `pub fn invalidate_area(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, area: twine_core::Rect, reason: twine_engine::InvalidateReason)` — Invalidates an absolute area of a display (clipped to the screen).
- `pub fn frame_invalidation_log(&self) -> &[(twine_core::Rect, twine_engine::InvalidateReason)]` — The invalidations rendered by the last frame that started (feature `debug-checks`; empty otherwise): everything invalidated between the start of the frame before it and its own start.
- `pub fn invalidation_log(&self) -> &[(twine_core::Rect, twine_engine::InvalidateReason)]` — Every invalidation since the last frame started (feature `debug-checks`; empty otherwise).
- `pub fn coords(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Rect` — Absolute coordinates of `id` (`Rect::ZERO` for unknown ids).
- `pub fn content_area(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Rect` — Coordinates minus padding and border width of `Part::Main`.
- `pub fn place(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, rect: twine_core::Rect)` — Places `id` at the absolute rectangle `rect` right away (low-level placement). The subtree moves with it. No-op when unchanged (P3); otherwise the old and the new area are invalidated and a resize sends `SizeChanged`.
- `pub fn has_transform(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is drawn with a rotation, scale or skew.
- `pub fn needs_layer(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id` and its children must be rendered into a layer first: `opa_layered` below cover, a transform, a blend mode other than normal, or a bitmap mask.
- `pub fn compute_ext_draw(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> u16` — The extra draw size of `id` from its styles and widget (LVGL `lv_obj_refresh_ext_draw_size`): the maximum of the shadow extent, outline width + pad, the growth caused by the transform and transform size, and `Widget::ext_draw_size`.
- `pub fn set_flag(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, flags: twine_engine::ObjFlags, on: bool)` — Sets (`on`) or clears flags of `id`. Idempotent. Hiding invalidates the area before, showing after; both mark the parent's layout.
- `pub fn has_flag(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, flags: twine_engine::ObjFlags) -> bool` — Whether `id` has all of `flags`.
- `pub fn set_test_id(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, test_id: &'static str)` — Sets the test id used by queries and dumps (kept only in debug builds or with the `test-ids` feature).
- `pub fn mark_layout_dirty(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Schedules a layout of `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_mark_layout_as_dirty`), e.g. after a widget's content size changed. Layout properties set through styles do this automatically.
- `pub fn layout_pending(&self) -> bool` — Whether a layout pass is pending (some node is marked dirty).
- `pub fn layout_stats(&self) -> twine_engine::LayoutStats` — Statistics of the last `update_layout` that had work to do.
- `pub fn layout_visited(&self) -> Vec<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The nodes whose children were laid out by the last layout pass (feature `debug-checks`; empty otherwise). Lets tests check that only dirty subtrees are processed.
- `pub fn update_layout(&mut self)` — Runs the layout pass (update cycle step 7, called by `step`): every dirty subtree is laid out once, top-down, from its topmost dirty node (whose own rectangle is kept: its parent was not affected). Nodes whose rectangle changed then invalidate their old and new area (their subtree moves along without a relayout of its own), resized nodes get `SizeChanged` (`EventParam::Area` = old coordinates) and their parents `LayoutChanged`. When event handlers change the layout again the pass repeats, at most `MAX_LAYOUT_ITERATIONS` times (then `warn!` and the rest waits for the next update). Nothing dirty: returns immediately.
- `pub fn scroll_to_view_after_layout(&mut self, node: twine_engine::NodeId, anim: bool)` — Scrolls `node` into view through every scrollable ancestor (like `scroll_to_view_recursive`) once the layout is final: at the end of the next layout pass (`update_layout`, run by every `step` before drawing), or of the pass in progress when called from an event handler during one (e.g. on `SizeChanged`). Unlike `scroll_to_view_recursive`, it never lays out synchronously: a change that moves `node` (a docked keyboard appearing, a rotation) and the scroll are laid out once, in the same step.
- `pub fn layout_passes(&self) -> u32` — How many layout passes had work to do since the engine was created (wrapping): a `update_layout` with nothing dirty does not count, one with work counts once however many iterations it needed. Lets tests check that an operation caused no layout.
- `pub fn set_size(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, w: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>, h: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the width and height (`Px`, `Dp`, `Pct` of the parent's content area, `Content`, or a design element such as `design::SPACE_L`). Idempotent, like every setter here: an unchanged value does nothing.
- `pub fn set_width(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, w: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the width.    /// The value is anything that converts into a `LengthValue`: an `i32` (pixels), a `Length` (`Px`, `Pct`, `Dp` — density-independent, converted for the DPI of the node's display —, `Content`), or a length design element the theme supplies (e.g. `design::SPACE_M`, resolved for the theme's current mode). A local `Main` property: idempotent, a state style can still override it. Never panics (an unknown node is ignored).
- `pub fn set_height(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, h: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the height (units as for `set_width`).
- `pub fn set_pos(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, x: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>, y: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the position relative to the alignment point in the parent's content area (`Pct` of the parent's content size). Units as for `set_width`: pixels, `Length` (`Dp` included) or a design length element.
- `pub fn set_x(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, x: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the x position (see `set_pos`).
- `pub fn set_y(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, y: impl Into<twine_style::design::LengthValue>)` — Sets the y position (see `set_pos`).
- `pub fn set_align(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, align: twine_style::Align)` — Sets the alignment in the parent (the position becomes an offset from it).
- `pub fn align(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, align: twine_style::Align, x: i32, y: i32)` — Sets the alignment and the offset from it.
- `pub fn align_to(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, base: twine_engine::NodeId, anchor: impl Into<twine_style::Anchor>, x: i32, y: i32)` — Aligns `id` to another node `base` (LVGL `lv_obj_align_to`): an `Align` (or `Anchor::Inside`) places `id` in the base's content area, the other `Anchor`s next to the base. Unlike LVGL the relation is kept: `id` follows `base` when it moves. Flex and grid parents ignore it for their items. `align_to` a deleted node is ignored.
- `pub fn clear_align_to(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Removes an `align_to` relation (the node is positioned by its `X`/`Y`/`Align` styles again).
- `pub fn set_layout(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, kind: twine_style::LayoutKind)` — Sets the layout of the children (`None`, `Flex`, `Grid`).
- `pub fn set_flex_flow(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, flow: twine_style::FlexFlow)` — Sets the flex flow (direction, wrapping, reverse), e.g. `FlexFlow::COLUMN.wrap(true)`.
- `pub fn set_flex_align(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, main: twine_style::MainAlign, cross: twine_style::CrossAlign, track: twine_style::MainAlign)` — Sets the placement of the items on the main axis, across it (in their track) and of the tracks of a wrapping container.
- `pub fn set_flex_grow(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, grow: u16)` — Sets the weight of a flex item's share of the free main-axis space (0 = none; items share it in proportion to their weights).
- `pub fn set_grid_tracks(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, columns: impl Into<twine_style::GridTracks>, rows: impl Into<twine_style::GridTracks>)` — Sets the grid column and row templates of `id` as local `Main` style properties (see `set_local_grid_tracks`).
- `pub fn set_local_grid_tracks(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, selector: twine_style::Selector, prop: twine_style::PropId, tracks: impl Into<twine_style::GridTracks>)` — Sets a grid template property (`prop` is `PropId::GridColumnTracks` or `PropId::GridRowTracks`) of `id` as a local property for `selector`, so state styles, classes and themes interact with it by the usual precedence (a `PRESSED` style's template wins over a `Main` local one while pressed).
- `pub fn grid_column_tracks(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&[twine_style::GridTrack]>` — The grid column template of `id` as the layout uses it: the resolved `GridColumnTracks` property (state, local, normal and theme styles by precedence), in the node's current state, borrowed from the style that wins. `None` when no style sets it or the node is unknown.
- `pub fn grid_row_tracks(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&[twine_style::GridTrack]>` — The grid row template of `id` (like `grid_column_tracks`).
- `pub fn set_grid_align(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, column_align: twine_style::GridAlign, row_align: twine_style::GridAlign)` — Sets how the grid tracks are placed in the container (columns, rows).
- `pub fn set_grid_cell(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, columns: impl Into<twine_style::GridSpan>, rows: impl Into<twine_style::GridSpan>, x_align: twine_style::GridAlign, y_align: twine_style::GridAlign)` — Places a grid item: its columns and rows (a track `2` or a range `0..2`, see `GridSpan`) and its alignment in the cell (horizontal, vertical).
- `pub fn memory_report(&self) -> twine_engine::EngineMemory` — What the engine's memory is used for, by part (`EngineMemory`: units, and what is not included). For budgeting a device (which part to shrink), for a debug console, and for tests that pin the memory of a scene.
- `pub fn on_outside_press(&mut self, node: twine_engine::NodeId, cb: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine, Option<twine_engine::NodeId>) + 'static)` — Runs `cb` once, when the next pointer press on `node`'s display starts outside `node` and its descendants (including presses that hit nothing). `cb` receives the node the press goes to; it runs before that node receives `Pressed`, so it may delete `node` (a popup closing itself). Deleting `node` drops the callback unused.
- `pub fn outside_press_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of pending `on_outside_press` callbacks.
- `pub fn set_perf_overlay(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, on: bool) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Shows or hides the performance overlay of `display` (bottom-right corner of the system layer). Its own redraws are excluded from the frame statistics.
  Errors: `EngineError::DisplayNotFound` for an unknown `display`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when there is no room for the overlay node.
- `pub fn perf_overlay(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The overlay node of `display`, if shown.
- `pub fn last_sync_px(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> u64` — Pixels copied by the last area sync of a `Full` display (0 otherwise).
- `pub fn refresh(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_engine::RefreshOutcome` — Renders and flushes every display whose dirty areas are due at `now` (at most one frame per `refr_period` per display). Called by `step`.
- `pub fn step(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One step of the engine (the update cycle): `read_inputs`, `run_timers`, `run_anims`, the layout pass (`update_layout`, only dirty subtrees), then `refresh` every display that is due. Returns when to call again: the earliest of the next frame, the next animation frame (at most one per `refr_period` while an animation plays), the end of an animation delay, the next due timer, the next input read (polled devices, held devices, long press timers) and pending flushes; `Wake::Idle` when nothing is pending — an idle UI costs no CPU at all.
- `pub fn step_budgeted(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant, budget: twine_engine::StepBudget) -> twine_engine::Wake` — `step` rendering at most `budget` (see `StepBudget`) instead of the configured `step_budget`: when a frame is cut short, the step returns `Wake::Now` and the next step continues it. The pixels of a frame finished over several steps are those of the same frame rendered at once. A step that uses up the budget's time raises `FaultKind::FrameOverrun`.
- `pub fn begin_step(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant)` — Starts an update at `now` (the first part of `step`, for callers that run the steps one by one — the view layer's `Ui::update`): records the time used by animations and timers started before the next animation step, and (with a `hires_timer`) the moment the update starts, from which its `StepBudget` time and `TimingReport::worst_update_us` count.
- `pub fn finish_step(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Finishes an update (the last part of `step`, after `read_inputs`, `run_timers` and `run_anims`): the layout pass, the refresh of every due display and the performance bookkeeping. Returns when to call again (see `step`). Renders within `EngineConfig::step_budget`.
- `pub fn finish_step_budgeted(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant, budget: twine_engine::StepBudget) -> twine_engine::Wake` — `finish_step` rendering at most `budget` (see `StepBudget` and `step_budgeted`): returns `Wake::Now` when a frame was cut short.
- `pub fn flush_pending(&self) -> bool` — Whether a display driver still holds a draw buffer or a framebuffer swap is pending.
- `pub fn heartbeat(&self) -> u32` — The number of completed steps (`step`, `finish_step` and their budgeted forms; every `Ui::update`), wrapping at `u32::MAX`: a value an external watchdog reads to see that the UI is alive — it changes as long as updates complete, whatever they draw. Never panics.
- `pub fn last_stats(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> twine_engine::RefreshStats` — Statistics of the last frame of `display` (default values for unknown displays).
- `pub fn refresh_due(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Instant>` — The earliest instant a display that is not rendering a frame and has dirty areas may start its next frame (`None` when no display waits; halted displays never wait). The async runtime uses it after reporting its flushes, which can mark areas dirty again.
- `pub fn refresh_begin(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> Option<twine_engine::FrameInfo>` — Starts the next frame of a display added with `add_chunked_display`, if one is due at `now` (dirty areas and at least `refr_period` since the previous frame). Render it with `render_chunk` until that returns `None`, then call `refresh_end`. Call it after the update step (`Engine::step` / `finish_step`), which lays out and reports when the next frame is due.
- `pub fn render_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — Renders the next chunk of the frame started by `refresh_begin` into `buf` (at least the display's `chunk_bytes`), in the layout to flush: rows of the returned area, rotated and format-converted as the display needs. Returns the area to flush, or `None` when the frame is complete.
- `pub fn refresh_add_flush_time(&mut self, flush_us: u32, wait_us: u32)` — Adds the caller's measured transfer times to the statistics of the frame started by `refresh_begin`: `flush_us` of transfer, of which `wait_us` the CPU only waited (the rest overlapped rendering). `flush_us` also raises `TimingReport::worst_flush_us` (one chunk's flush per call).
- `pub fn refresh_end(&mut self)` — Ends the frame started by `refresh_begin`: statistics, the performance monitor and the `twine::refresh` log line. Chunks not rendered are dropped (their areas are redrawn by the next frame).
- `pub fn move_node(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, before: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Moves `id` (with its subtree) under `parent`, right before `parent`'s child `before` (`None`: as the last child). The old area is invalidated, the old and new parents are laid out again (the node gets its new rectangle in the next layout pass, which invalidates the new area), and both parents receive `ChildChanged`.
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for unknown nodes; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `before` is not a child of `parent` or `parent` is inside `id`'s subtree (all logged); `EngineError::TooDeep` (with a `FaultKind::Capacity` fault, code `TreeDepth`) when a node of the moved subtree would end up deeper than `Limits::max_tree_depth` — checked only when the parent changes (O(subtree)); the node stays where it was.
- `pub fn load_screen_anim(&mut self, screen: twine_engine::NodeId, load: impl Into<twine_engine::ScreenLoad>)` — Loads `screen` with an animation (LVGL `lv_screen_load_anim`):
- `pub fn screen_anim_running(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> bool` — Whether a screen load animation (or its delay) is in progress on `display`.
- `pub fn finish_screen_anim(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId)` — Finishes the screen load animation of `display` at once, if one runs (or waits for its delay): the new screen becomes active and every event and the `auto_delete` of the end are applied now, as if the animation had ended. `load_screen_anim` does this itself before it starts another animation; call it first when the caller needs to know which screen the next load will leave (the active screen afterwards), as the view layer's navigator does. Does nothing without an animation or for an unknown display. Never panics.
- `pub fn prev_screen(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The screen shown below or above the active one during a screen load animation (LVGL `lv_screen_prev`).
- `pub fn set_scroll_dir(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, dir: impl Into<twine_style::Sides>)` — Sets the directions `id` can be scrolled in (default `Sides::ALL`): an `Axis` or any set of `Sides` (e.g. only `Sides::LEFT`; the empty set disables scrolling). Idempotent.
- `pub fn scroll_dir(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_style::Sides` — The directions `id` can be scrolled in.
- `pub fn set_scrollbar_mode(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, mode: twine_style::ScrollbarMode)` — Sets when the scrollbars of `id` are shown (default `ScrollbarMode::Auto`). A change redraws the node; an unchanged mode does nothing.
- `pub fn scrollbar_mode(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_style::ScrollbarMode` — When the scrollbars of `id` are shown.
- `pub fn set_scroll_snap_x(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, snap: twine_style::ScrollSnap)` — Sets where `SNAPPABLE` children align horizontally when scrolling stops (default `ScrollSnap::None`). Idempotent; does not scroll by itself (see `update_snap`).
- `pub fn set_scroll_snap_y(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, snap: twine_style::ScrollSnap)` — Sets where `SNAPPABLE` children align vertically when scrolling stops.
- `pub fn scroll_snap_x(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_style::ScrollSnap` — The horizontal snapping of `id`.
- `pub fn scroll_snap_y(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_style::ScrollSnap` — The vertical snapping of `id`.
- `pub fn scroll_offset(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Point` — The scroll offset of `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_x/y`): how far the content is scrolled from its start (positive once it moved up / left).
- `pub fn scroll_end(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_core::Point` — The scroll offset `id` ends at: the target of a running scroll animation, else the current offset (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_end`).
- `pub fn scroll_top(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> i32` — How far the content of `id` can be scrolled down, i.e. the part above the top edge (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_top`) = the vertical scroll offset.
- `pub fn scroll_bottom(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> i32` — How much content is below the bottom of the content area (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_bottom`): the lowest child edge (plus its bottom margin) plus the bottom padding and border, minus the node's bottom edge; at least the widget's own content beyond the content area. Negative when scrolled beyond the end (elastic).
- `pub fn scroll_left(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> i32` — How much content is left of the content area (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_left`): the horizontal offset, or for right-to-left nodes the leftmost child edge beyond the content area.
- `pub fn scroll_right(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> i32` — How much content is right of the content area (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scroll_right`); for right-to-left nodes the negated horizontal offset.
- `pub fn scroll_by(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, dx: i32, dy: i32, anim: bool)` — Scrolls the content of `id` by `(dx, dy)` (LVGL `lv_obj_scroll_by`; positive `dy` moves the content **down**, reducing the offset). Not bounded: see `scroll_by_bounded`.
- `pub fn stop_scroll_anim(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Stops the scroll animations of `id` where they are (LVGL `lv_obj_stop_scroll_anim`), sending `ScrollEnd` for each.
- `pub fn scroll_by_bounded(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, dx: i32, dy: i32, anim: bool)` — Scrolls by `(dx, dy)` but not further than the content allows (LVGL `lv_obj_scroll_by_bounded`; the layout is updated first).
- `pub fn scroll_to(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, x: i32, y: i32, anim: bool)` — Scrolls to the offset `(x, y)`, bounded by the content (LVGL `lv_obj_scroll_to`). Scrolling to the current position does nothing.
- `pub fn scroll_to_x(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, x: i32, anim: bool)` — Scrolls horizontally to offset `x` (bounded; a running horizontal scroll animation stops first).
- `pub fn scroll_to_y(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, y: i32, anim: bool)` — Scrolls vertically to offset `y` (bounded; a running vertical scroll animation stops first).
- `pub fn scroll_to_view(&mut self, child: twine_engine::NodeId, anim: bool)` — Scrolls the parent of `child` so that `child` becomes visible in its content area, by the smallest distance; with snapping on the parent the child is aligned to the snap position instead (LVGL `lv_obj_scroll_to_view`). The layout is updated first.
- `pub fn scroll_to_view_recursive(&mut self, child: twine_engine::NodeId, anim: bool)` — Like `scroll_to_view` for every ancestor, from the parent outwards, so that `child` becomes visible through nested scrollable containers (LVGL `lv_obj_scroll_to_view_recursive`).
- `pub fn is_scrolling(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id` is being scrolled: dragged or thrown by a pointer, or animated (LVGL `lv_obj_is_scrolling`).
- `pub fn update_snap(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, anim: bool)` — Scrolls `id` so that its nearest `SNAPPABLE` child inside its area aligns with the snap position of each snapping axis (LVGL `lv_obj_update_snap`).
- `pub fn scrollbar_areas(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> (Option<twine_core::Rect>, Option<twine_core::Rect>)` — The horizontal and the vertical scrollbar of `id` in absolute coordinates, `None` for a bar that is not shown (LVGL `lv_obj_get_scrollbar_area`).
- `pub fn scrollbar_invalidate(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Invalidates the scrollbars of `id` as they are now (LVGL `lv_obj_scrollbar_invalidate`).
- `pub fn timing(&self) -> twine_engine::TimingReport` — The worst-case timings measured so far (`TimingReport`; all `0` without a `hires_timer`). Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn reset_worst(&mut self)` — Clears the high-water marks of `timing` (e.g. after start-up, so the first frames' one-off work — caches, the first full redraw — does not count, or at the start of each reporting period). Never panics.
- `pub fn add_style(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, style: impl Into<twine_style::StyleRef>, selector: twine_style::Selector)` — Adds `style` for `selector` to `id` (LVGL `lv_obj_add_style`): it has priority over every style added before and over theme styles.
- `pub fn add_theme_style(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, style: impl Into<twine_style::StyleRef>, selector: twine_style::Selector)` — Adds a theme style (lowest priority), used by themes.
- `pub fn remove_style(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, style: Option<&twine_style::StyleRef>, selector: Option<twine_style::Selector>)` — Removes normal and theme styles (LVGL `lv_obj_remove_style`): those equal to `style` (`None` = any style) whose selector matches `selector` (`None` = any; a selector with `Part::Any` / `State::ANY` matches every part / state).
- `pub fn remove_all_styles(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Removes every style of `id`: normal, theme and local styles, and the running style transitions (LVGL `lv_obj_remove_style_all`).
- `pub fn set_local_prop(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, selector: twine_style::Selector, prop: twine_style::StyleProp)` — Sets a local style property for `selector` (LVGL `lv_obj_set_style_*`). Idempotent (P3): setting the value it already has does nothing (no invalidation, no layout). A running style transition of the property is stopped (LVGL).
- `pub fn set_local_transition(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, selector: twine_style::Selector, t: impl Into<twine_style::TransitionValue>)` — Sets the local `transition` property for `selector`: which properties animate when the node enters the selector's state, and how (`Transition`). A `&'static Transition` is stored as a reference; a `Transition` value is moved into an `Rc` held by the node's local style (released with it). Idempotent (P3): an equal transition does nothing; nothing is redrawn (a transition only matters at the next state change). Allocates only to hold a run-time transition (build time); never panics.
- `pub fn remove_local_prop(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, prop: twine_style::PropId, selector: twine_style::Selector) -> bool` — Removes a local property; returns whether it was set.
- `pub fn style_prop(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — The value of `prop` for `part` of `id` with full LVGL resolution (state weights, priority, inheritance, defaults). Unknown ids give the default. A density-independent length (`Length::Dp`) comes back in pixels for the DPI of `id`'s display (`node_dpi`), converted by the resolver (`StyleSource::dpi`).
- `pub fn finish_style_value(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, prop: twine_style::PropId, v: twine_style::StyleValue) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — Finishes a value read straight from a style of `id` (outside the cascade) like `style_prop` finishes what it resolves: a design element becomes its theme value, a `Dp` length pixels (`twine_style::resolve_value`); any other value is returned unchanged.
- `pub fn node_dpi(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> u16` — The DPI that density-independent lengths of `id` resolve with: the DPI of the display showing `id` (`DisplayInfo::dpi`), else of the default display, else `twine_style::DEFAULT_DPI`. With one display this is a direct read; the resolver asks only when it finds a `Dp` value.
- `pub fn style_i32(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> i32` — An integer property in pixels (`Int`, pixel lengths and `Dp` lengths; other kinds give 0).
- `pub fn style_color(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_core::Color` — A color property (black if the property is not a color).
- `pub fn style_opa(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_core::Opa` — An opacity property (cover if the property is not an opacity).
- `pub fn style_font(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, part: twine_style::Part) -> &'static twine_text::Font` — The font of `part` (`Font`, inherited, default from the configuration).
- `pub fn cached_main(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::MainStyle` — The hot `Main` properties of `id` in its current state, from the node's cache (filled on first use after a style or state change). Unknown ids give the defaults.
- `pub fn style_cache_valid(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id`'s style cache holds values for the current epoch (for tests).
- `pub fn add_state(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, s: twine_style::State)` — Adds states to `id` (idempotent).
- `pub fn clear_state(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, s: twine_style::State)` — Removes states from `id` (idempotent).
- `pub fn set_state(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, s: twine_style::State, on: bool)` — Adds (`on`) or removes states. Idempotent; when the change selects the same style entries as before nothing is invalidated (LVGL `lv_obj_style_state_compare`). Otherwise the style transitions of the new state start (see `twine_style::Transition`; only on nodes that were drawn already). Every actual change sends `StateChanged` with the previous state (posted: a busy widget gets it once it is back, see `post_event`).
- `pub fn report_style_change(&mut self, style: &Rc<twine_style::StyleBuf>)` — Refreshes every node that uses the shared style `style` after it was mutated (scans the whole tree; rare).
- `pub fn set_style_parent(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, from: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>)` — Makes `id` inherit style properties (text font and color, base direction, …) from `from` instead of its parent; `None` inherits from the parent again. For nodes created on a display layer on behalf of a widget elsewhere: a dropdown's list inherits from its dropdown, so a font set on the dropdown's ancestors reaches the list.
- `pub fn theme(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<&'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook>` — The theme `display` was created with (`None` without a theme or for an unknown display). Never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn set_theme_mode(&mut self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode)` — Switches the theme of `display` to `mode` (e.g. light → dark): the display takes the theme's `'static` design element table for `mode` (`ThemeHook::design`: a pointer swap), and every node of the display is re-resolved once (style caches, extra draw sizes, layout, one `StyleChanged` event each) and the display is redrawn. The theme's styles are **not** re-applied: everything styled with design elements changes, nothing else does, so no view is rebuilt and nothing is allocated. The display's metrics table is kept.
- `pub fn theme_modes(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> &'static [twine_style::ThemeMode]` — The modes the theme of `display` supports (`ThemeHook::modes`; empty for a display without a theme or an unknown display). Cycle through them with `ThemeMode::next_in`:
- `pub fn theme_mode(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> twine_style::ThemeMode` — The theme mode of `display` (`ThemeMode::Light` for a display without a theme or an unknown display). Never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn design_epoch(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> u32` — A number that changes whenever the theme mode (and so the design element table) of `display` changes (`set_theme_mode`): lets a cache of design element values (e.g. a reactive layer) notice that it is stale. 0 for an unknown display.
- `pub fn design_table(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> Option<&'static twine_style::design::ElementTable>` — The design element table of `display`'s current mode (its theme's `'static` table; `None` without a theme, for a theme without design elements, or for an unknown display). Elements the display's metrics table defines are not in it: `design_value` reads both. Never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn design_value<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, element: twine_style::design::Element<T>) -> Option<T>` — The value `display`'s theme gives `element` in its current mode: the mode's table first, then the display's metrics table (`None` if neither defines it). Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn default_font(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> &'static twine_text::Font` — The default font of `display`: its theme's `ThemeHook::font_normal`, else `EngineConfig::default_font`, else `twine_text::EMPTY_FONT`.
- `pub fn theme_of(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook>` — The theme of the display showing `id` (on a screen or a layer), if any.
- `pub fn resolve_design_value<T: twine_style::design::ElementType>(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, value: twine_style::design::DesignValue<T>) -> Option<T>` — The value of a design value for node `id`: a fixed value as is, an element looked up in the design element tables of the display showing `id` (its theme's table for the current mode, then the display's metrics table; with one display a direct read). `None` when the element is not defined there (no theme, or a theme without it): the caller picks its fallback.
- `pub fn themed_nodes(&self, display: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> twine_engine::ThemedNodes<'_>` — The nodes of `display` its theme styles, parents first: every node of its screens and every node on its layers (not the layers themselves). Empty for an unknown display. Allocates nothing; never panics. For tools and tests that inspect a theme's coverage (`twine_testing::assert_theme_covers`).
- `pub fn set_theme_class(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass)` — Themes node `id` as `class` from now on (a variant or a role, design `docs/plan/r7-theming-design.md` §2.4): its theme styles are removed and the display's theme is applied again with `class` instead of the widget's class (`reapply_theme`). A theme that does not know `class` styles the node like the nearest class of `class`'s `lineage` it knows, so an unknown variant looks like its widget. Passing the widget's own class removes the override.
- `pub fn theme_class(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The class node `id` is themed as: its theme class if it has one, else its widget's class; `None` for an unknown node. Never panics.
- `pub fn reapply_theme(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId)` — Re-themes node `id`: removes its theme styles and applies its display's theme again with the node's theme class, then refreshes the node once (style caches, extra draw size, layout, redraw, one `StyleChanged` event). Its own, normal and local styles are kept; its children are not re-themed (a change of inherited properties still reaches them, but a theme that styles children by their parent's class — `ThemeCx::parent_class` — sees the new class only for children created afterwards). What `set_theme_class` runs; also for a theme whose look depends on something it reads in `apply` that changed.
- `pub fn transition_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of running style transitions (all nodes).
Implements: Debug, StyleSource

#### struct twine_engine::DriverErrorCode
A display driver's numeric error code (from `DisplayDriver::error_code` and the matching methods of the other driver traits; `0` means the driver gives none). Carried by `EngineError::Driver` and, for flush faults, by `FaultRecord::code`.
Methods of `DriverErrorCode`:
- `const NONE: twine_engine::DriverErrorCode` — No code (the driver does not classify its errors).
- `pub const fn new(code: u32) -> twine_engine::DriverErrorCode` — The code `code`.
- `pub const fn get(self) -> u32` — The numeric value.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, From<u32>, Display

#### enum twine_engine::EngineError
Errors of the engine API.
Variants:
- `NodeNotFound(twine_engine::NodeId)` — The node does not exist (never created, or deleted).
- `DisplayNotFound(twine_engine::DisplayId)` — The display does not exist.
- `TooManyDisplays` — More than `MAX_DISPLAYS` displays.
- `TooManyInputs` — More than `MAX_INPUTS` input devices.
- `TooManyGroups` — More than `MAX_GROUPS` focus groups.
- `TooManyNodes` — The widget tree is full: `Limits::max_nodes` live nodes (at most 65 535).
- `TooDeep` — The node would be deeper than `Limits::max_tree_depth` levels below its root (creation or move refused).
- `BufferTooSmall { needed: usize, got: usize }` — A draw buffer or framebuffer is smaller than needed.
- `BufferMisaligned` — A caller-provided draw buffer does not start at a 4-byte aligned address. Buffers declared with `twine::draw_buffers!` (or allocated with `BufferMode::alloc`) are aligned by construction.
- `BufferModeMismatch` — Partial or heap (`Alloc`) buffers were given for a framebuffer display, `Full`/`Direct` for a flush display, or a framebuffer display could not provide the buffers the mode needs.
- `InvalidConfig(&'static str)` — A configuration value or argument is invalid.
- `FormatDisabled(twine_core::ColorFormat)` — A display's pixels would have to be drawn in a colour format whose renderer is not compiled in: its `color-*` feature (of `twine`, `twine-engine` or `twine-render`) is disabled, or the format can never be a draw format (e.g. `A8`). Returned by `Engine::add_display`, `add_framebuffer_display` and `add_chunked_display` instead of adding a display that would stay blank; the display is not added, and `FaultKind::FormatDisabled` is raised.
- `NotVisible(twine_engine::NodeId)` — The node is not shown (hidden, clipped away, or not on an active screen or layer of a display), so it has no region on a display (`Engine::render_region_to`, `Engine::check_region`).
- `Unsupported(&'static str)` — The display or its driver cannot do what was asked (e.g. a driver without `DisplayDriver::read_back`, an integrity check on a software-rotated display); the text names what.
- `Busy` — The display is busy with something the request must not interleave with: a frame is in progress, a flush is in flight, or the region still has areas waiting to be drawn. Retry after the next update.
- `Driver { code: twine_engine::DriverErrorCode, message: heapless::string::String<64> }` — A display driver reported an error.
Methods of `EngineError`:
- `pub fn driver_code(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>` — The driver's error code of an `EngineError::Driver` (`None` for other errors).
- `pub fn driver(code: twine_engine::DriverErrorCode, e: &dyn Debug) -> Self` — An `EngineError::Driver` with `code` and the `Debug` output of the driver error `e` (truncated; formatting allocates nothing).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Display

#### struct twine_engine::InvariantError
A violated tree invariant, found by `Tree::check_invariants`.
Fields:
- `node: twine_engine::NodeId` — The node where the violation was found.
- `what: &'static str` — What is wrong.
- `other: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — Another node involved (e.g. the parent), if any.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Display

#### struct twine_engine::Event
One event as seen by a handler.
Fields:
- `code: twine_engine::EventCode` — What happened.
- `target: twine_engine::NodeId` — The node the event was sent to.
- `current_target: twine_engine::NodeId` — The node whose handlers are running (differs from `target` while bubbling).
- `param: twine_engine::EventParam` — The parameter.
Methods of `Event`:
- `pub fn key(&self) -> Option<twine_hal::Key>` — The key of a `Key` event.
- `pub fn dir(&self) -> Option<twine_style::Side>` — The direction of a `Gesture` event.
- `pub fn value(&self) -> Option<i32>` — The value of an event with `EventParam::Value` (e.g. `ValueChanged` of a slider).
- `pub fn prev_state(&self) -> Option<twine_style::State>` — The previous state of a `StateChanged` event.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_engine::EventCode
What happened (LVGL `lv_event_code_t`).
Variants:
- `Pressed` — The node was pressed.
- `Pressing` — The node is being pressed (sent on every read while pressed).
- `PressLost` — The pointer slid off the node while pressed (and the node lost the press).
- `ShortClicked` — Released before the long press time, without scrolling.
- `SingleClicked` — First short click of a series.
- `DoubleClicked` — Second short click within the multi-click time and distance.
- `TripleClicked` — Third short click within the multi-click time and distance.
- `LongPressed` — Pressed for the long press time.
- `LongPressedRepeat` — Sent every long press repeat period after `LongPressed`.
- `Clicked` — Released without scrolling (also after a long press).
- `Released` — Released (always sent on release).
- `ScrollBegin` — Scrolling started.
- `ScrollThrowBegin` — A scroll throw (momentum) started.
- `ScrollEnd` — Scrolling ended.
- `Scroll` — The node scrolled.
- `Gesture` — A swipe gesture (`EventParam::Dir`).
- `Key` — A key for the focused node (`EventParam::Key`).
- `Rotary` — A rotation by `n` steps (`EventParam::Rotary`), e.g. a mouse wheel over the node, sent by the application. Encoders do not send it: in edit mode their rotation arrives as `Key(Right)` / `Key(Left)` per step, like in LVGL, so widgets handle one input path.
- `Focused` — The node got the focus.
- `Defocused` — The node lost the focus.
- `Leave` — The node lost the focus to a node of another group (pointer click focus).
- `HitTest` — Advanced hit test (`EventParam::Point`); a handler returning `Stop` vetoes the hit.
- `HoverOver` — A mouse pointer moved over the node.
- `HoverLeave` — A mouse pointer left the node.
- `CoverCheck` — Cover check (custom draw hooks).
- `RefreshExtDrawSize` — Extra draw size request (custom draw hooks).
- `DrawMainBegin` — Before the main drawing.
- `DrawMain` — Main drawing.
- `DrawMainEnd` — After the main drawing.
- `DrawPostBegin` — Before the post drawing.
- `DrawPost` — Post drawing (after the children).
- `DrawPostEnd` — After the post drawing.
- `ValueChanged` — The widget's value changed (e.g. `CHECKED` toggled).
- `Insert` — Text is being inserted.
- `Refresh` — Request to refresh the widget.
- `Ready` — A process finished.
- `Cancel` — A process was cancelled (e.g. `Esc`).
- `Create` — The node was created (sent after `Widget::init`).
- `Delete` — The node is being deleted (sent bottom-up, before it is freed).
- `ChildChanged` — A child was added, removed or moved.
- `ChildCreated` — A child was created (sent to the parent; `Event::target` is the child).
- `ChildDeleted` — A child was deleted (sent to the parent; `Event::target` is the deleted child).
- `ScreenUnloadStart` — The screen starts unloading.
- `ScreenLoadStart` — The screen starts loading.
- `ScreenLoaded` — The screen was loaded.
- `ScreenUnloaded` — The screen was unloaded.
- `SizeChanged` — The size changed (`EventParam::Area` holds the old coordinates).
- `StyleChanged` — A style of the node changed.
- `StateChanged` — The node's state changed (`EventParam::State` holds the previous state; LVGL `LV_EVENT_STATE_CHANGED`). Sent after the new state is set, including for `Engine::add_state` / `Engine::clear_state` called directly; when the node's widget is busy (its own `event` or setter is running) it arrives right after that returns (see `Engine::post_event`).
- `LayoutChanged` — The layout of the node changed.
- `GetSelfSize` — Content size request.
- `Custom(u16)` — An application-defined event (see `Engine::register_event_code`).
Methods of `EventCode`:
- `pub const fn is_input(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is an input event (pressing, clicking, keys, focus, hover, scrolling).
- `pub const fn is_draw(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is a drawing event.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_engine::EventCx<'a>
The context of an event handler: the engine (mutably) on behalf of the node whose handlers run.
Methods of `EventCx`:
- `pub fn node(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node whose handlers run (the current target).
- `pub fn target(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node the event was sent to.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably.
- `pub fn widget_cx(&mut self) -> twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>` — A widget context for the current node.
- `pub fn stop_bubbling(&mut self)` — Stops bubbling to the parent after this node's handlers.
- `pub fn prevent_default(&mut self)` — Skips the remaining handlers of this node (and bubbling).
- `pub fn point(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Point>` — The last point of the pointer device being processed (`None` outside pointer input).
- `pub fn input(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::InputId>` — The input device being processed (`None` for events not caused by input).
- `pub fn send(&mut self, target: twine_engine::NodeId, code: twine_engine::EventCode, param: twine_engine::EventParam) -> twine_engine::EventResult` — Sends another event (nested dispatch) and returns its result.
- `pub fn post(&mut self, target: twine_engine::NodeId, code: twine_engine::EventCode, param: twine_engine::EventParam)` — Sends an event once `target`'s widget is back in its node (see `Engine::post_event`): from a widget's `event`, a `ValueChanged` posted to its own node reaches the handlers right after `event` returns, and they can read the widget.
- `pub fn text(&self, ev: &twine_engine::Event) -> Option<&str>` — The text of `ev` when it carries one (`EventParam::Text`), e.g. the text being inserted into a textarea (`Insert`).
Implements: Debug

#### enum twine_engine::EventParam
The parameter of an event. Every variant is `Copy`.
Variants:
- `None` — No parameter.
- `Point(twine_core::Point)` — A point (e.g. `HitTest`).
- `Key(twine_hal::Key)` — A key (`Key`).
- `Dir(twine_style::Side)` — A direction (`Gesture`: the side the swipe moved towards).
- `Rotary(i32)` — Encoder steps (`Rotary`).
- `Value(i32)` — A value.
- `Text(twine_engine::EventText)` — A text (e.g. `Insert`), sent with `Engine::send_event_text` and read with `EventCx::text` or `Engine::event_text` while the event is being dispatched.
- `State(twine_style::State)` — A state (`StateChanged`: the previous state).
- `Area(twine_core::Rect)` — An area (`SizeChanged`: the old coordinates).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_engine::EventResult
What a handler asks the dispatcher to do next.
Variants:
- `Continue` — Go on: remaining handlers run and the event bubbles (if enabled).
- `Stop` — Remaining handlers of this node run, but the event does not bubble to the parent.
- `Consumed` — Nothing else runs: no further handlers, no bubbling. From a widget's `event`, the user handlers are skipped too ("prevent default").
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_engine::EventText
Handle of the text of an event sent with `Engine::send_event_text`. The text itself is kept by the engine (in a reused buffer, so sending text allocates nothing in steady state) only while the event is being dispatched; read it with `EventCx::text` or `Engine::event_text`. A handle kept longer reads as `None`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### type twine_engine::FaultHook
`pub type FaultHook = fn(&twine_engine::FaultRecord)`
Called for every raised fault. A plain function (it cannot capture state, and setting it allocates nothing): record the fault, bump a counter, or signal a supervisor through a `static`. It runs where the fault is detected — possibly in the middle of rendering or flushing — so it must be short and must not panic.

#### struct twine_engine::FaultRecord
One fault: what happened, where, when and how often.
Fields:
- `kind: twine_core::FaultKind` — What happened.
- `display: Option<twine_engine::DisplayId>` — The display concerned, if any.
- `node: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node concerned, if any (e.g. the parent a node could not be created under).
- `input: Option<twine_engine::InputId>` — The input device concerned, if any (`FaultKind::InputDevice`).
- `at: twine_core::Instant` — When the engine raised it (the engine's current time: the running update's time, else the last known one).
- `occurrences: u32` — How many occurrences this record stands for (≥ 1; e.g. the number of dropped channel messages, or faults merged by the view layer since the last update).
- `code: u32` — A detail code whose meaning depends on the source (e.g. a driver error code), `0` when there is none.
Methods of `FaultRecord`:
- `pub const fn new(kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — A record of one occurrence of `kind`, with no display, node, input or code (`at` is set by `Engine::raise_fault`).
- `pub const fn display(self, d: twine_engine::DisplayId) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — Sets the display concerned.
- `pub const fn node(self, n: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — Sets the node concerned.
- `pub const fn input(self, i: twine_engine::InputId) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — Sets the input device concerned (input ids come from `Engine::add_input`).
- `pub const fn occurrences(self, n: u32) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — Sets the number of occurrences (`0` is stored as `1`: a record always stands for at least one occurrence).
- `pub const fn code(self, code: u32) -> twine_engine::FaultRecord` — Sets the detail code (its meaning per kind is documented on each `FaultKind` variant).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::VfsFileSource
A `twine_fs::Vfs` as an image `FileSource` (paths like `"A:/img/logo.qoi"`), feature `fs`. `Engine::set_vfs` installs one; code resolving images without an engine (`twine_image::with_pixels`) can use it directly.
Fields:
- `0: twine_fs::Vfs`
Implements: Debug, FileSource

#### struct twine_engine::LayoutDirty
Layout work pending on a node (consumed by the layout pass).
Methods of `LayoutDirty`:
- `const SELF: Self` — The node's own size/position must be recomputed.
- `const CHILDREN: Self` — The node's children must be laid out again.
- `const DESCENDANTS: Self` — A descendant has pending layout work (guides the layout pass to it).
- `pub const fn empty() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all bits unset.
- `pub const fn all() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all known bits set.
- `pub const fn bits(&self) -> u8` — Get the underlying bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Option<Self>` — Convert from a bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits_truncate(bits: u8) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value, unsetting any unknown bits.
- `pub const fn from_bits_retain(bits: u8) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value exactly.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self>` — Get a flags value with the bits of a flag with the given name set.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether all bits in `self` are unset.
- `pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool` — Whether all known bits in this flags value are set.
- `pub const fn intersects(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether any set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub const fn contains(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, other: Self)` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, other: Self, value: bool)` — Call `insert` when `value` is `true` or `remove` when `value` is `false`.
- `pub const fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise and (`&`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub const fn symmetric_difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn complement(self) -> Self` — The bitwise negation (`!`) of the bits in `self`, truncating the result.
- `pub const fn iter(&self) -> bitflags::iter::Iter<twine_engine::LayoutDirty>` — Yield a set of contained flags values.
- `pub const fn iter_names(&self) -> bitflags::iter::IterNames<twine_engine::LayoutDirty>` — Yield a set of contained named flags values.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Flags, PublicFlags, Binary, Octal, LowerHex, UpperHex, BitOr, BitOrAssign, BitXor, BitXorAssign, BitAnd, BitAndAssign, Sub, SubAssign, Not, Extend<twine_engine::LayoutDirty>, FromIterator<twine_engine::LayoutDirty>, IntoIterator

#### struct twine_engine::ObjFlags
Behaviour flags of a node, with the names of LVGL 9's `LV_OBJ_FLAG_*`.
Methods of `ObjFlags`:
- `const HIDDEN: Self` — Not drawn, not hit-tested, ignored by layouts.
- `const CLICKABLE: Self` — Receives pointer presses.
- `const CLICK_FOCUSABLE: Self` — Gets the `FOCUSED` state when clicked.
- `const CHECKABLE: Self` — Toggles the `CHECKED` state when clicked.
- `const SCROLLABLE: Self` — Can be scrolled.
- `const SCROLL_ELASTIC: Self` — Elastic overscroll.
- `const SCROLL_MOMENTUM: Self` — Scrolling continues with momentum after release.
- `const SCROLL_ONE: Self` — Scrolls at most one snappable child per gesture.
- `const SCROLL_CHAIN_HOR: Self` — Propagates horizontal scrolling to the parent at the edge.
- `const SCROLL_CHAIN_VER: Self` — Propagates vertical scrolling to the parent at the edge.
- `const SCROLL_ON_FOCUS: Self` — Scrolls to make itself visible when focused.
- `const SCROLL_WITH_ARROW: Self` — Scrolls with the arrow keys (keypad / encoder).
- `const SNAPPABLE: Self` — Can be a snap target of the parent's scroll snapping.
- `const PRESS_LOCK: Self` — Keeps being pressed while the pointer slides off.
- `const EVENT_BUBBLE: Self` — Events also go to the parent.
- `const GESTURE_BUBBLE: Self` — Gestures also go to the parent.
- `const ADV_HITTEST: Self` — Precise hit test (rounded corners, custom `Widget::hit_test`).
- `const IGNORE_LAYOUT: Self` — Positioned by hand, ignored by the parent's layout.
- `const FLOATING: Self` — Ignored by layouts and by the parent's scroll bounds.
- `const SEND_DRAW_TASK_EVENTS: Self` — Sends draw task events.
- `const OVERFLOW_VISIBLE: Self` — Children are not clipped to this node's area.
- `const FLEX_IN_NEW_TRACK: Self` — Starts a new flex track.
- `const LAYOUT_PASSTHROUGH: Self` — A transparent wrapper (not in LVGL; used by the declarative control-flow views): the layout lays out its children as if they were children of its parent (flex and grid positions, `%` sizes and content sizes are unchanged), its coordinates become the bounding box of its children, it draws nothing, does not clip its children and is transparent to hit-testing.
- `const WIDGET_1: Self` — Reserved for widgets.
- `const WIDGET_2: Self` — Reserved for widgets.
- `const USER_1: Self` — Free for the application.
- `const USER_2: Self` — Free for the application.
- `const USER_3: Self` — Free for the application.
- `const USER_4: Self` — Free for the application.
- `const DOCK_BOTTOM: Self` — Docked to the bottom of the parent (not in LVGL; an on-screen keyboard reserving its height, see `Keyboard::set_docked` in `twine-widgets`): the node gets the full width of the parent's content area and its own height, at the bottom of that area, and the parent's other children are laid out in the area above it (`Pct` sizes, `Align`, flex and grid; see `twine_layout::LayoutFlags::DOCK_BOTTOM`). Like `FLOATING`, it is not a flex/grid item, does not scroll with the parent and does not count for the parent's content size or scroll extents. A `HIDDEN` node reserves nothing.
- `const SCROLL_CHAIN: Self` — Both scroll chain directions.
- `pub const fn empty() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all bits unset.
