- `pub const fn all() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all known bits set.
- `pub const fn bits(&self) -> u32` — Get the underlying bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Option<Self>` — Convert from a bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits_truncate(bits: u32) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value, unsetting any unknown bits.
- `pub const fn from_bits_retain(bits: u32) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value exactly.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self>` — Get a flags value with the bits of a flag with the given name set.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether all bits in `self` are unset.
- `pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool` — Whether all known bits in this flags value are set.
- `pub const fn intersects(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether any set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub const fn contains(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, other: Self)` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, other: Self, value: bool)` — Call `insert` when `value` is `true` or `remove` when `value` is `false`.
- `pub const fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise and (`&`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.

#### struct twine_engine::DisplayHealth
The flush health of a display (`Engine::display_health`).
Fields:
- `state: twine_engine::DisplayState` — The state.
- `consecutive_errors: u32` — Failed flushes / presents in a row (each chunk counts; `0` after a success). A flush timeout raises it to at least `max_consecutive_flush_errors`.
- `last_ok: Option<twine_core::Instant>` — When the last flush succeeded (engine time), `None` before the first one.
- `last_error: Option<twine_engine::DriverErrorCode>` — The driver's code of the last failure, `None` if none failed yet.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_engine::DisplayState
The state of a display, derived from its consecutive flush errors (see `DisplayHealth`).
Variants:
- `Healthy` — The last flush succeeded (or none failed yet).
- `Degraded` — The last flush failed, fewer than `max_consecutive_flush_errors` times in a row.
- `Failed` — At least `max_consecutive_flush_errors` flushes failed in a row, or a flush did not finish within `flush_timeout`. The display keeps refreshing (unless `FlushPolicy::Halt`); one successful flush makes it healthy.
- `Halted` — Failed under `FlushPolicy::Halt`: not refreshed until `Engine::recover_display`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_engine::FlushPolicy
The engine's reaction to a failed flush or present.
Variants:
- `Reinvalidate` — Mark the failed area dirty again: it is redrawn and flushed on the next frame (at most one frame per `refr_period`), for as long as the driver keeps failing. A later successful flush makes the display healthy again on its own.
- `Halt` — Like `Reinvalidate` until the display is `Failed`; then stop refreshing it (the frame in progress is abandoned, invalidations accumulate) and report `DisplayState::Halted` until the application calls `Engine::recover_display`. For products whose fail-safe reaction must not be fought by the engine retrying a broken bus.
- `Ignore` — Drop the failed area (the panel shows stale pixels there until the area changes again). The fault is still raised and the health still tracked.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_engine::DEAD_NODE

A `NodeId` that is never valid in any tree: the node id of a widget that could not be created (the view layer returns it from `BuildCx::create` instead of aliasing another node).

#### struct twine_engine::EngineMemory
The memory an `Engine` holds, by part — from `Engine::memory_report`.
Fields:
- `nodes: usize` — Live nodes (a count, not bytes): widgets, screens and display layers.
- `tree: usize` — The widget tree: the node arena (every slot, by capacity, and its free lists), the root and style-link vectors, and per node its boxed widget, style entry vector, layout extension and event handlers.
- `node_slots: usize` — Node slots of the arena (a count: live, free and retired slots, by capacity).
- `render_scratch: usize` — The renderer's per-span scratch buffers (`8 ×` the widest span; see `RenderCaches::scratch_bytes`).
- `render_caches: usize` — The renderer's quarter-circle, shadow and gradient caches (fixed arenas).
- `glyph_cache: usize` — The glyph cache with the text renderer's scratch rows (`EngineConfig::glyph_cache_bytes` plus tables).
- `image_cache: usize` — Decoded images in the image cache and its entry table (bounded by `EngineConfig::image_cache_bytes` plus the table).
- `layer_buf: usize` — The ARGB8888 layer buffer (opacity groups, transforms, blend modes), wherever it lives.
- `layer_buf_static: bool` — The layer buffer is caller memory (`Engine::with_layer_buf`) instead of heap.
- `draw_buffers_heap: usize` — Partial draw buffers the engine allocated (`BufferMode::Alloc`; alignment padding included). Heap draw buffers live as long as the program, like statics.
- `draw_buffers_static: usize` — Partial draw buffers in caller memory (`BufferMode::Partial`, e.g. `draw_buffers!` statics).
Methods of `EngineMemory`:
- `pub fn heap_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes of the engine: the tree, the renderer's scratch buffers and caches, the glyph and image caches, a heap layer buffer and heap draw buffers.
- `pub fn static_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Caller memory the engine uses (a static layer buffer and static draw buffers): RAM the linker placed, not the heap. See `heap_bytes`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::ComputedRecipe
A recipe computed when a node is themed: a plain function that adds styles through the `ThemeCx`, for looks that depend on the node's place (its parent's class, its index, the display's DPI) — what a static `Recipe` cannot express. Prefer a static recipe where the look is fixed: it is data in flash and costs no code.
Fields:
- `name: &'static str` — The recipe's name (logs, coverage reports).
- `class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass` — The widget class the recipe styles.
- `apply: fn(&mut twine_engine::ThemeCx<'_>)` — Adds the styles to the node of the context.
Methods of `ComputedRecipe`:
- `pub const fn new(name: &'static str, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass, apply: fn(&mut twine_engine::ThemeCx<'_>)) -> Self` — A computed recipe named `name` for `class`.
- `pub fn for_class(&'static self, class: &twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Option<twine_engine::RecipeRef>` — `Some(self)` if the recipe is for exactly `class` (see `Recipe::for_class`).
Implements: Debug, From<&'static twine_engine::ComputedRecipe>

#### struct twine_engine::Recipe
The look of one widget class as data: a `Style` per `Selector` (part and states), all `'static` (in flash). Written with `recipe!`, which builds every style with `style!` (so `..BASE` spreads compose styles at compile time).
Fields:
- `name: &'static str` — The recipe's name (the `static`'s name with `recipe!`): shown in logs, coverage reports (`twine_testing::assert_theme_covers`) and `cargo xtask theme-recipes`. Not an identity.
- `class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass` — The widget class the recipe styles (a theme class: a widget's class, a variant or a role, see `Engine::set_theme_class`).
- `entries: &'static [(twine_style::Selector, &'static twine_style::Style)]` — The styles, in the order they are added to a node.
Methods of `Recipe`:
- `pub const fn new(name: &'static str, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass, entries: &'static [(twine_style::Selector, &'static twine_style::Style)]) -> Self` — A recipe named `name` for `class` with `entries` (what `recipe!` writes).
- `pub fn for_class(&'static self, class: &twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Option<twine_engine::RecipeRef>` — `Some(self)` if the recipe is for exactly `class` (an identity comparison: a recipe for `BUTTON_CLASS` does not match a class derived from it — the theme's lineage walk does that, see `DesignSystem`). Chains in a `DesignSystem::recipe` written by hand: `CARD.for_class(c).or_else(|| BUTTON.for_class(c))`. Never panics.
- `pub fn find(list: &[&'static twine_engine::Recipe], class: &twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Option<twine_engine::RecipeRef>` — The first recipe of `list` for exactly `class` (earlier entries win, so an application's override is listed before the base theme's recipes). O(`list`), never panics.
Implements: Debug, From<&'static twine_engine::Recipe>

#### enum twine_engine::RecipeRef

- `pub fn ptr_eq(self, other: twine_engine::RecipeRef) -> bool` — Whether both name the same recipe (an identity comparison).

#### enum twine_engine::ScreenAnim
How a new screen replaces the active one (LVGL `lv_screen_load_anim_t`); every variant but `None` carries the animation time.
Variants:
- `None` — Switch at once (after the delay).
- `OverLeft(twine_core::Duration)` — The new screen slides in from the right, over the old one.
- `OverRight(twine_core::Duration)` — The new screen slides in from the left, over the old one.
- `OverTop(twine_core::Duration)` — The new screen slides in from the bottom, over the old one.
- `OverBottom(twine_core::Duration)` — The new screen slides in from the top, over the old one.
- `MoveLeft(twine_core::Duration)` — Both screens move to the left.
- `MoveRight(twine_core::Duration)` — Both screens move to the right.
- `MoveTop(twine_core::Duration)` — Both screens move up.
- `MoveBottom(twine_core::Duration)` — Both screens move down.
- `FadeIn(twine_core::Duration)` — The new screen fades in over the old one.
- `FadeOut(twine_core::Duration)` — The old screen fades out, revealing the new one.
- `OutLeft(twine_core::Duration)` — The old screen slides out to the left, revealing the new one.
- `OutRight(twine_core::Duration)` — The old screen slides out to the right, revealing the new one.
- `OutTop(twine_core::Duration)` — The old screen slides out to the top, revealing the new one.
- `OutBottom(twine_core::Duration)` — The old screen slides out to the bottom, revealing the new one.
Methods of `ScreenAnim`:
- `pub const fn all(d: twine_core::Duration) -> [twine_engine::ScreenAnim; 15]` — Every animated variant (with `d`), in LVGL enum order, then `None`.
- `pub const fn duration(self) -> twine_core::Duration` — The animation time (zero for `None`).
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — A short lowercase name (`"over_left"`, `"fade_in"`, …) for logs and file names.
- `pub const fn old_on_top(self) -> bool` — Whether the old screen is drawn above the new one (LVGL `is_out_anim`).
- `pub const fn delay(self, d: twine_core::Duration) -> twine_engine::ScreenLoad` — This animation after a delay.
- `pub const fn auto_delete(self, on: bool) -> twine_engine::ScreenLoad` — This animation, deleting the old screen at the end (`auto_delete`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<twine_engine::ScreenAnim>

#### struct twine_engine::ScreenLoad

#### struct twine_engine::HeapPeak
The highest heap use seen, kept in a `static` next to a `MemInfo` provider (see the example there): `sample` turns an allocator's `used()`/`free()` into a `MemInfo` with a peak.
Methods of `HeapPeak`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — A tracker that has seen nothing (`peak` 0). `const`, for `static` items. Never panics.
- `pub fn sample(&self, used: usize, free: usize) -> twine_engine::MemInfo` — The statistics for a heap with `used` and `free` bytes, raising the peak if `used` is above it. Values above `u32::MAX` saturate. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn peak(&self) -> u32` — The highest `used` sampled so far (0 before the first `sample`). Never panics.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### struct twine_engine::MemInfo
Memory statistics reported by the application's allocator, through `EngineConfig::mem_info` (a plain `fn() -> MemInfo`: the allocator is the application's choice, so the engine only asks). Values are bytes, saturated to `u32::MAX`.
Fields:
- `used: u32` — Bytes in use.
- `peak: u32` — Highest `used` so far.
- `free: u32` — Bytes still free.
Methods of `MemInfo`:
- `pub fn used_percent(&self) -> u8` — `used` in percent of the heap (`used + free`), 0 for an empty heap. Never panics.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::PerfMonitor
Accumulates frames and busy time over one-second windows (LVGL's `sysmon` performance monitor): `fps` = frames per window, `cpu_percent` = busy time / wall time.
Methods of `PerfMonitor`:
- `const WINDOW: twine_core::Duration` — The window length.
- `pub fn frame(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant, busy_us: u64)` — Records a frame at `now` that kept the CPU busy for `busy_us`.
- `pub fn window_done(&mut self, now: twine_core::Instant) -> bool` — Closes the window if it is at least one second old at `now`: computes `fps` and `cpu_percent` and starts a new window. Returns whether a window was closed.
- `pub fn fps(&self) -> u16` — Frames per second of the last closed window.
- `pub fn cpu_percent(&self) -> u8` — CPU load in percent of the last closed window.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::RefreshStats
Statistics of the most recent frame of a display (see `Engine::last_stats`).
Fields:
- `frame: u32` — Frame number (1 = first frame of the display).
- `frame_time_us: u32` — Time from the start of the frame to the last chunk handed to the driver.
- `render_us: u32` — Time spent drawing.
- `flush_us: u32` — Time spent in the driver's flush calls (plus rotation / format conversion).
- `flush_wait_us: u32` — Time spent waiting for a draw buffer to come back from the driver.
- `dirty_areas: u16` — Dirty areas rendered (after merging).
- `dirty_px: u32` — Pixels rendered (sum of the dirty areas after rounding).
- `chunks: u16` — Chunks flushed (partial modes) or areas drawn (framebuffer modes).
- `nodes_drawn: u32` — Nodes drawn (after culling and the top-cover search).
- `fps: u16` — Frames per second over the last complete one-second window.
- `cpu_percent: u8` — Busy time (render + flush wait) in percent of the last window.
- `mem_used: u32` — Memory in use (from `EngineConfig::mem_info`).
- `mem_peak: u32` — Peak memory use.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_engine::TimingReport
The longest update, chunk render and chunk flush the engine has measured since it was created or since `Engine::reset_worst` (high-water marks, in µs): evidence for a time budget, and the numbers to size `StepBudget`'s time limit and an external watchdog with. Read with `Engine::timing` (the view layer's `Ui::timing`).
Fields:
- `worst_update_us: u32` — The longest update: from `Engine::begin_step` (the start of `Ui::update`, so messages, timers, animations and bindings count) to the end of `finish_step` (layout and refresh). Displays added with `add_chunked_display` are rendered by their caller after the update and count in `worst_render_us` only.
- `worst_render_us: u32` — The longest drawing of one chunk (a partial buffer's rows, a framebuffer area, or a chunk of the chunk-level API), software re-renders after an accelerator timeout included: the indivisible unit of rendering, by which a step can overrun its time budget.
- `worst_flush_us: u32` — The longest flush of one chunk as the step sees it: waiting for a free draw buffer, rotating / converting the chunk and handing it to the driver (with a blocking driver, the whole transfer); for framebuffer displays the present at the end of a frame; for chunk-level displays (`AsyncUi`) the transfer time their caller reports (`refresh_add_flush_time`).
Implements: Copy, Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Audit

#### struct twine_engine::DisplayTheme
The theme a display is created with: a `&'static` theme (fixed at compile time, design §2.0a) and the mode the display starts in. Fields:

#### struct twine_engine::ThemeCx<'a>
Access to one node for a theme's `ThemeHook::apply`: its tree position, its display's resolution and DPI, `add_style` and `add_recipe`.
Methods of `ThemeCx`:
- `pub fn new(tree: &'a mut twine_engine::Tree, node: twine_engine::NodeId, display: twine_engine::DisplayId, dpi: u16, resolution: twine_core::Size) -> Self` — A context for `node` of `display` (with its DPI and logical resolution).
- `pub fn node(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node being styled.
- `pub fn parent(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node's parent (`None` for screens).
- `pub fn parent_class(&self) -> Option<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The class the node's parent is themed as (themes style e.g. list items differently): its theme class — a variant or role — if it has one, else its widget's class.
- `pub fn grandparent_class(&self) -> Option<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The class the node's grandparent is themed as (see `parent_class`).
- `pub fn index(&self) -> Option<usize>` — The node's position among its siblings.
- `pub fn tree(&self) -> &twine_engine::Tree` — The tree (read-only).
- `pub fn add_style(&mut self, selector: twine_style::Selector, style: impl Into<twine_style::StyleRef>)` — Adds `style` for `selector` as a theme style (lowest priority; among theme styles the latest added wins, as with LVGL's `lv_obj_add_style` in a theme's apply callback).
- `pub fn add_recipe(&mut self, recipe: impl Into<twine_engine::RecipeRef>)` — Adds `recipe` (a `Recipe` or a `ComputedRecipe`) to the node: a static recipe's entries in order, each as a theme style (`add_style` with a `StyleRef::Static`: no reference counting); a computed recipe's function runs with this context. Allocates only the node's entry list growth; never panics.
- `pub fn dpx(&self, px: i32) -> i32` — `px` pixels at 160 DPI scaled to the display's DPI (LVGL `LV_DPX_CALC`): `(px · dpi + 80) / 160`, at least 1 for positive `px`; negative values are scaled symmetrically.
- `pub fn dpi(&self) -> u16` — The display's DPI.
- `pub fn resolution(&self) -> twine_core::Size` — The display's logical resolution.
- `pub fn display(&self) -> twine_engine::DisplayId` — The display the node belongs to.
Implements: Debug

#### trait twine_engine::ThemeHook
`pub trait ThemeHook`
What the engine needs from a theme (LVGL `lv_theme_t`): styling a node when it is created, the default font, and the design element values of each `ThemeMode` it lists (the theme's colors: `design::PRIMARY`, `design::SECONDARY`, …; LVGL's `color_primary` / `color_secondary`).
Items:
- `fn apply(&self, cx: &mut twine_engine::ThemeCx<'_>, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass)` — Adds the theme's styles to the node of `cx`, whose theme class is `class`.
- `fn font_normal(&self) -> &'static twine_text::Font` — The default font of text on the display (the default `Font`).
- `fn name(&self) -> &'static str (provided)` — A short name for logs (default `"theme"`).
- `fn modes(&self) -> &[twine_style::ThemeMode] (provided)` — The modes the theme supports, in the order a mode switch cycles through them (`ThemeMode::next_in`): exactly the modes for which `design` returns a table. The first is the mode a display starts in unless its `DisplayTheme` names another. Default: `ThemeMode::Light` only.
- `fn design(&self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Option<&'static twine_style::design::ElementTable> (provided)` — The values of the design elements in `mode`: a `'static` table (`const`, in flash, no heap), or `None` if the theme does not support `mode` (the default: a theme without design elements).
- `fn metrics(&self, dpi: u16, resolution: twine_core::Size) -> Option<twine_style::design::ElementTable> (provided)` — The display's own design element values: elements whose values depend on the display (sizes scaled by its DPI, paddings by its size class — the LVGL theme's), the same in every mode. Computed **once, when the display is created** (before the application builds its UI, so before `seal`), kept by the display and never rebuilt: a mode switch does not touch it. An element the mode's `design` table does not define is taken from here: the display merges the mode's table over this one into a single indexed array of finished values (`FlatElements`, refilled in place on a mode switch), which is what the resolver reads. Default `None` (a theme whose values do not depend on the display).
- `fn audit(&self, out: &mut dyn twine_core::audit::AuditSink) (provided)` — Describes the theme for an audit report (`AppConfig::audit_report`, section `theme`): the hook a certification file uses to pin the exact theme a product runs. The default writes `theme.name` (`name`), the first listed mode and the supported modes' count; a theme can add entries (a content digest of its tables, its version). Must not allocate; never panics.
- `fn recipe(&self, class: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Option<twine_engine::RecipeRef> (provided)` — The recipe the theme styles nodes of theme class `class` with — after its lineage fallback, so for a variant it does not know, the recipe of the variant's base — or `None`: no recipe for `class` or any of its bases, or a theme that styles in code (`apply`) and has no recipes (the default).
Implemented by: twine_engine::NoBase, twine_engine::Theme<D>

#### struct twine_engine::Node
One node of the tree: links, the widget, flags, state, styles and geometry.

- `pub fn parent(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The parent (`None` for screens and layers).
- `pub fn first_child(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The first child.

- `pub fn next_sibling(&self) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The next sibling.

- `pub fn styles(&self) -> &twine_engine::StyleList` — The style list.

- `pub fn is_hidden(&self) -> bool` — Whether the node has the `HIDDEN` flag.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_engine::Tree
The widget tree: an arena of `Node`s plus the list of roots (screens and layers).
Methods of `Tree`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty tree.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the tree's growth is noted in (see `Engine::set_partition`).
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of live nodes.
- `pub fn theme_class(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The class `id` is themed as: its theme class (`Engine::set_theme_class`) if it has one, else its widget's class; `None` for an unknown node. One branch without theme classes, else O(nodes with a theme class).
- `pub fn retired_slots(&self) -> usize` — Number of retired node slots: slots that used up their generations (65 535 by default, ≈ 2.8 × 10¹⁴ in the safety profile) and are never reused (`Arena::retired`). Stays 0 unless the tree's working set is tiny compared to its create/delete churn (see the arena's generation budget); a growing value means node memory is slowly being lost to wear. In the safety profile it stays 0 in practice.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the tree has no nodes.
- `pub fn style_epoch(&self) -> u32` — The style epoch: incremented whenever an inherited style property may have changed anywhere (invalidates every node's cached inherited values at once).
- `pub fn create(&mut self, parent: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>, widget: Box<dyn twine_engine::Widget>) -> Result<twine_engine::NodeId, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Creates a node for `widget` as the last child of `parent` (or as a new root), with the class's default flags, state `DEFAULT` and zero coordinates. O(1).
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `parent`; `EngineError::TooManyNodes` when the node arena is full.
- `pub fn delete(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<usize, twine_engine::EngineError>` — Deletes `id` and its whole subtree; returns the number of nodes deleted. O(subtree). The post-order (children before their parent) is built in the tree's delete scratch, which keeps its capacity: deleting allocates nothing once the scratch is large enough (reserved for `Limits::max_nodes` with `Limits::preallocate`).
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown node. Never panics.
- `pub fn move_to(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, new_parent: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>, index: Option<usize>) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Moves `id` under `new_parent` (`None` = make it a root) at `index` (`None` = last). Moving a node into its own subtree is rejected (`InvalidConfig("cycle")`).
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `id` or `new_parent`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `new_parent` lies in `id`'s subtree. Nothing moves on error.
- `pub fn move_before(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, before: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Moves `id` under `parent`, right before its child `before` (`None`: as the last child). Unlike `move_to` this needs no index lookup (O(1) apart from the cycle check). `before == Some(id)` keeps the node where it is when it already is a child of `parent`.
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `id` or `parent`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when `before` is not a child of `parent` (or is `id` while `id` is not yet a child of `parent`), or when `parent` lies in `id`'s subtree. Nothing moves on error.
- `pub fn set_index(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, index: usize) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Moves `id` to position `index` among its siblings (clamped to the last position).
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `id`.
- `pub fn swap(&mut self, a: twine_engine::NodeId, b: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Result<(), twine_engine::EngineError>` — Swaps the positions of `a` and `b` in their parents (LVGL `lv_obj_swap`; they may have different parents). Rejected if one is an ancestor of the other.
  Errors: `EngineError::NodeNotFound` for an unknown `a` or `b`; `EngineError::InvalidConfig` when one is an ancestor of the other.
- `pub fn index(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<usize>` — Position of `id` among its siblings (or among the roots). O(siblings).
- `pub fn contains(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether `id` refers to a live node.
- `pub fn node(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&twine_engine::Node>` — The node `id`.
- `pub fn get<W: twine_engine::Widget>(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&W>` — The widget of `id` as `W`.
- `pub fn get_mut<W: twine_engine::Widget>(&mut self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&mut W>` — The widget of `id` as `&mut W`. Changing widget data this way does not invalidate anything; prefer the widget's setters.
- `pub fn widget_dyn(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<&dyn twine_engine::Widget>` — The widget of `id`.
- `pub fn parent(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The parent of `id`.
- `pub fn style_parent(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The node `id` inherits style properties from: its style link when one is set (see `Engine::set_style_parent`), else its parent. O(links), usually 0 or 1.
- `pub fn style_link(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The style link of `id` (`None`: it inherits from its parent).
- `pub fn children(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::Children<'_>` — Children of `id`, first to last (paint order). No allocation.
- `pub fn children_rev(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::ChildrenRev<'_>` — Children of `id`, last to first (topmost first).
- `pub fn ancestors(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::Ancestors<'_>` — Ancestors of `id` from the parent up to the root (excluding `id`).
- `pub fn descendants(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_engine::Descendants<'_>` — `id` and all its descendants in pre-order (paint order), walking the links only: no stack, no allocation.
- `pub fn roots(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_engine::NodeId> + '_` — The roots (screens and layers) in creation order.
- `pub fn child(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId, index: i32) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The child at `index`; a negative index counts from the end (`-1` = last), like LVGL.
- `pub fn root_of(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>` — The root of `id`'s tree (itself for a root).
- `pub fn check_invariants(&self) -> Result<(), twine_engine::InvariantError>` — Checks every structural invariant: parent/child links are consistent, `child_count` matches, `prev`/`next` are symmetric, there are no cycles, roots have no parent, every parentless node is a root, and style links join live nodes without a cycle.
  Errors: The first violated invariant, as an `InvariantError` naming the node, the broken rule and the related node (if any).
- `pub fn dump(&self, root: twine_engine::NodeId, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result` — Writes an indented dump of `root`'s subtree, one node per line: `obj n3g1 "test_id" [x0,y0 → x1,y1] state=PRESSED flags=CLICKABLE|… text="…"` (states as `State`'s `Display`: application states by their `set_custom_name` names, `DEFAULT` for none).
  Errors: Only the errors of `out`.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### struct twine_engine::StepBudget
How much rendering one step may do: at most `max_chunks` chunks (a partial buffer's rows, or one dirty area of a framebuffer display) over all displays, and at most `max_time` of the step's time. The hook for schedulers that must bound the time a step takes (an RTOS time slice, a cooperative super-loop, a frame budget): the rest of a frame continues in the next step, which the step requests by returning `Wake::Now` — work is deferred, never dropped.
Methods of `StepBudget`:
- `const UNLIMITED: twine_engine::StepBudget` — No limit: a step renders every frame that is due completely (unless it has to wait for a draw buffer, see `EngineConfig::cooperative_flush`).
- `pub const fn chunks(n: u16) -> twine_engine::StepBudget` — At most `n` chunks per step (`0` counts as `1`: every step makes progress, so a loop stepping on `Wake::Now` always finishes the frame). Never panics.
- `pub const fn time(t: twine_core::Duration) -> twine_engine::StepBudget` — At most `t` of time per step, measured with the `hires_timer` (see the type's docs: a step that reaches it renders no further chunk and raises `FrameOverrun`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn with_chunks(self, n: u16) -> twine_engine::StepBudget` — This budget with at most `n` chunks per step (`0` counts as `1`). Never panics.
- `pub const fn with_time(self, t: twine_core::Duration) -> twine_engine::StepBudget` — This budget with at most `t` of time per step. Never panics.
- `pub const fn max_chunks(self) -> Option<u16>` — The chunk limit (`None`: unlimited). Never panics.
- `pub const fn max_time(self) -> Option<twine_core::Duration>` — The time limit (`None`: unlimited). Never panics.
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_engine::Wake
When `Engine::step` (or the view layer's `Ui::update`) must be called again. The caller may sleep until then (P1: an idle UI returns `Wake::Idle` and needs no CPU at all until an input interrupt or a new signal value arrives).
Variants:
- `Idle` — Nothing is pending: sleep until an external event.
- `At(twine_core::Instant)` — Call again at (or after) this instant.
- `Now` — Call again as soon as possible (work is pending, e.g. a partially rendered frame).
- `IdleFor(twine_core::Duration)` — Nothing is pending (like `Idle`), and there has been no user input for this long — at least `EngineConfig::idle_timeout`: a candidate for deep sleep.
Methods of `Wake`:
- `pub fn min(self, other: twine_engine::Wake) -> twine_engine::Wake` — The more urgent of `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn is_idle(self) -> bool` — Whether nothing is pending: `Wake::Idle` or `Wake::IdleFor`.
- `pub const fn inactive_for(self) -> Option<twine_core::Duration>` — The inactivity `Wake::IdleFor` reports (`None` for the other variants).
Implements: Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_engine::AsAny
`pub trait AsAny: Any`
Access to `self` as `Any`, implemented for every `'static` type. It lets `dyn Widget` be downcast (`<dyn Widget>::downcast_ref`).

- `fn as_any_mut(&mut self) -> &mut dyn Any` — `self` as `&mut dyn Any`.

#### const twine_engine::MAX_CLASS_DEPTH
`pub const MAX_CLASS_DEPTH: usize = 8`
How many classes `WidgetClass::lineage` visits at most (the class itself and its bases). Deeper chains (or a cycle of `static`s naming each other as base) are cut there: a lookup along the chain always ends.

- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &'a twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn coords(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — Absolute coordinates of the node.
- `pub fn content_area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The coordinates minus padding and border width of `Part::Main`.
- `pub fn state(&self) -> twine_style::State` — The node's state.
- `pub fn flags(&self) -> twine_engine::ObjFlags` — The node's flags.
- `pub fn style(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — A resolved style property.
- `pub fn style_i32(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> i32` — A resolved integer property (0 if it is not an integer).
- `pub fn finish_style_value(&self, prop: twine_style::PropId, v: twine_style::StyleValue) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — Finishes a value the widget read from a style it keeps itself (outside the node's cascade): a design element becomes the value of the node's theme, a `Dp` length pixels (see `Engine::finish_style_value`, which also gives the cost). Never panics.
- `pub fn font(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> &'static twine_text::Font` — The resolved font of `part`.
- `pub fn padding(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_core::Insets` — Padding of `part`.
- `pub fn style_color(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_core::Color` — A resolved color property (black if the property is not a color).
- `pub fn rect_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` (with the node's effective opacity and recolor), as `DrawCx::rect_dsc` would build it.
- `pub fn text_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part`, as `DrawCx::text_dsc` would build it but without the `background` (`None`): measuring and hit testing need no colors, so layout does not look for the surface behind the text.
- `pub fn rect_dsc_for_state(&self, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` as if the node were in `state`, as `DrawCx::rect_dsc_for_state` would build it.
- `pub fn text_dsc_for_state(&self, part: twine_style::Part, state: twine_style::State) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` as if the node were in `state`, as `DrawCx::text_dsc_for_state` would build it.
- `pub fn image_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ImageDsc<'static>` — The image style of `part`, as `DrawCx::image_dsc` would build it.
- `pub fn line_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::LineDsc` — The line style of `part`, as `DrawCx::line_dsc` would build it.
- `pub fn arc_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ArcDsc<'static>` — The arc style of `part`, as `DrawCx::arc_dsc` would build it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### trait twine_engine::Widget
`pub trait Widget: twine_engine::AsAny`
A widget: the behaviour of one node of the tree (LVGL's object class).
Items:
- `fn class(&self) -> &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass` — The widget's class (name, parts, default flags…).
- `fn init(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>) (provided)` — Called once right after the node was inserted into the tree (set default flags, local styles, create child nodes).
- `fn content_size(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> twine_core::Size (provided)` — Size of the content for `Length::Content` sizing, excluding padding. Default: zero.
- `fn draw(&self, cx: &mut twine_engine::DrawCx<'_, '_>) (provided)` — Draws the node before its children. Default: `DrawCx::draw_base` of `Part::Main`.
- `fn draw_post(&self, cx: &mut twine_engine::DrawCx<'_, '_>) (provided)` — Draws after the children (scrollbars are drawn by the engine afterwards).
- `fn ext_draw_size(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>) -> u16 (provided)` — Extra area outside the node's coordinates the widget draws into, beyond what the engine derives from the styles (shadow, outline, transforms). Default 0.
- `fn hit_test(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point) -> bool (provided)` — Whether the absolute point `p` hits the node. Default: `default_hit_test`.
- `fn covers(&self, cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect) -> bool (provided)` — Whether the node fully covers `area` with opaque pixels, so nothing below needs to be drawn. Default: `default_covers`.
- `fn text(&self) -> Option<&str> (provided)` — Text content for queries and tree dumps. Default `None`.
- `fn event(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::EventCx<'_>, ev: &twine_engine::Event) -> twine_engine::EventResult (provided)` — Reacts to an event sent to (or bubbling through) the node, after the built-in object behaviour (pressed / checked / focused states) and before the user handlers. Returning `EventResult::Consumed` skips the user handlers. Default: `EventResult::Continue`.
- `fn anim_value(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, v: i32) (provided)` — Applies a value of an `AnimProp::Value` animation started with `Engine::anim_start` (e.g. a bar's value). Default: ignored.
- `fn anim_custom(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, id: u16, v: i32) (provided)` — Applies a value of an `AnimProp::Custom(id)` animation started with `Engine::anim_start`. Default: ignored.
Implemented by: twine_engine::Obj, twine_engine::PerfOverlay

#### struct twine_engine::WidgetClass
Static description of a widget type (LVGL `lv_obj_class_t`), usually a `static`.
Fields:
- `name: &'static str` — Class name (`"obj"`, `"button"`…), shown in dumps, logs and test queries. Not an identity: compare classes with `is` / `is_a`.
- `parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]` — The parts the widget draws.
- `default_flags: twine_engine::ObjFlags` — Flags of a new node of this class.
- `group_def: twine_engine::GroupDef` — Default focus group membership.
- `editable: twine_engine::Editable` — Encoder edit mode.
- `base: Option<&'static twine_engine::WidgetClass>` — The class themes style this one like when they do not know it (default `None`: a theme that does not know the class gives it no styles). E.g. a custom button with `base: Some(&BUTTON_CLASS)` looks like a button in every theme, and a theme (or the application through a theme's `.class(..)` registration) may still style it on top. Only theming and `is_a` follow it: parts, flags and behaviour are the class's own.
- `item_parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]` — Parts the widget draws as several items, each in its own state (with `Engine::rect_dsc_for_state`), like the buttons (`Items`) of a button matrix. A state change of the node ignores the styles of these parts: it neither redraws the whole node for them nor starts their transitions. The widget invalidates the affected items itself (on `EventCode::StateChanged`). Default: none.
- `draw_parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]` — Parts whose styles only change how the widget draws, never its size or its children's layout, like a text field's `Cursor`. A state change that changes layout properties (paddings, border width, …) of these parts redraws the node (refreshing its extra draw size) instead of laying it out again — so moving the focus between text fields lays nothing out. Only for parts the widget's `content_size` does not read; the widget refreshes whatever it derives from their styles (e.g. the cursor's area) on `EventCode::StateChanged`, as no `StyleChanged` follows. Default: none (every part's layout properties lay the node out again, as in LVGL).
Methods of `WidgetClass`:
- `pub const fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self` — A class with parts `[Main]`, no flags, `GroupDef::Default`, `Editable::Inherit`, no base, no item parts and no draw-only parts.
- `pub const fn parts(self, parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]) -> Self` — With these parts.
- `pub const fn default_flags(self, flags: twine_engine::ObjFlags) -> Self` — With these default flags.
- `pub const fn group_def(self, g: twine_engine::GroupDef) -> Self` — With this group default.
- `pub const fn editable(self, e: twine_engine::Editable) -> Self` — With this edit mode.
- `pub const fn base(self, base: &'static twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> Self` — Themed like `base` where a theme does not know this class (see `WidgetClass::base`).
- `pub const fn item_parts(self, parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]) -> Self` — With these item parts (see `WidgetClass::item_parts`).
- `pub const fn draw_parts(self, parts: &'static [twine_style::Part]) -> Self` — With these draw-only parts (see `WidgetClass::draw_parts`).
- `pub fn is(&self, other: &twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> bool` — Whether `self` is the class `other` (the same `static`; a pointer comparison).
- `pub fn is_a(&'static self, other: &twine_engine::WidgetClass) -> bool` — Whether `self` is `other` or has it as a (direct or indirect) `base`, within `MAX_CLASS_DEPTH` steps. Never loops, never panics.
- `pub fn lineage(&'static self) -> twine_engine::Lineage` — The class, then its `base`, the base's base, … — at most `MAX_CLASS_DEPTH` classes (a longer chain, or a cycle, is cut and logged once per walk with `warn!`). Allocates nothing.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### struct twine_engine::WidgetCx<'a>
Mutable access to the engine on behalf of one node (widget `init` and setters).
Methods of `WidgetCx`:
- `pub fn new(engine: &'a mut twine_engine::Engine, node: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Self` — A context for `node`.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The engine's partition (`Engine::partition`): the seal domain a widget notes the growth of its own buffers in (`twine_core::alloc_guard::grew(cx.partition(), ..)`). Free; never panics.
- `pub fn node(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The node.
- `pub fn invalidate(&mut self)` — Invalidates the node's area (coords + extra draw size).
- `pub fn invalidate_for(&mut self, setter: &'static str)` — Invalidates the node's area for a setter named `setter` (shown in the invalidation log).
- `pub fn invalidate_area(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect)` — Invalidates an absolute area on the node's display, clipped to the node's visible area.
- `pub fn post_event(&mut self, code: twine_engine::EventCode, param: twine_engine::EventParam)` — Sends an event to the node once the widget is back in it (see `Engine::post_event`): the way a setter or `init` notifies handlers (`ValueChanged`) so that they can read the widget.
- `pub fn mark_layout(&mut self)` — Marks the node's size/position for the layout pass.
- `pub fn state(&self) -> twine_style::State` — The node's state.
- `pub fn add_state(&mut self, s: twine_style::State)` — Adds states (idempotent).
- `pub fn clear_state(&mut self, s: twine_style::State)` — Removes states (idempotent).
- `pub fn measure(&self) -> twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>` — A read-only view of the node (styles, coordinates, draw descriptors).
- `pub fn coords(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — Absolute coordinates of the node.
- `pub fn content_area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The coordinates minus padding and border width of `Part::Main`.
- `pub fn style(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_style::StyleValue` — A resolved style property.
- `pub fn style_i32(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> i32` — A resolved integer property (0 if it is not an integer).
- `pub fn style_color(&self, part: twine_style::Part, prop: twine_style::PropId) -> twine_core::Color` — A resolved color property.
- `pub fn font(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> &'static twine_text::Font` — The resolved font of `part`.
- `pub fn rect_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_engine::RectStyle` — The rectangle style of `part` (see `MeasureCx::rect_dsc`).
- `pub fn text_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_text::TextDsc` — The text style of `part` (see `MeasureCx::text_dsc`).
- `pub fn image_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ImageDsc<'static>` — The image style of `part` (see `MeasureCx::image_dsc`).
- `pub fn line_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::LineDsc` — The line style of `part` (see `MeasureCx::line_dsc`).
- `pub fn arc_dsc(&self, part: twine_style::Part) -> twine_render::ArcDsc<'static>` — The arc style of `part` (see `MeasureCx::arc_dsc`).
- `pub fn refresh_ext_draw_with(&mut self, widget_ext: u16) -> bool` — Recomputes the node's extra draw size after a widget property that changes `Widget::ext_draw_size` changed, with `widget_ext` as the value the widget now reports (the widget is taken out of its node while its setters run, so the engine cannot ask it). Returns whether the node's extra draw size changed; nothing is invalidated.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably.
- `pub fn fit_text<'s>(&mut self, s: &'s str) -> &'s str` — `s` within `Limits::max_text_len` bytes: `s` itself, or its longest prefix ending on a character boundary within the limit — then a `FaultKind::Capacity` fault (code `TextLen`, with the node) is raised. For widgets that store texts (label, checkbox, span, button-matrix button, dropdown/roller options). One comparison when the text fits; never panics, allocates nothing.
- `pub fn text_len_fits(&mut self, len: usize) -> bool` — Whether a text of `len` bytes is within `Limits::max_text_len`; when it is not, a `FaultKind::Capacity` fault (code `TextLen`, with the node) is raised. For edits that cannot be cut (e.g. inserting a dropdown option): the caller refuses them. One comparison when the text fits; never panics.
- `pub fn store_text(&mut self, buf: &mut String, s: &str)` — Replaces the content of the text buffer `buf` with `s` (call `fit_text` first). Allocates only when `buf` is too small; with `Limits::preallocate` a buffer below the full `max_text_len` is reserved to it at once, so a text set at start-up leaves room for every later text. Growth is noted for the allocation guard (`AllocSite::Text`). Never panics.
- `pub fn limit_text(&mut self, buf: &mut String, cap_before: usize)` — After a text buffer was edited in place (formatted or edited by a closure): notes its growth since its capacity was `cap_before` for the allocation guard, and cuts it to `Limits::max_text_len` as `fit_text` would (raising the same fault). Never panics.
- `pub fn reserve_text(&mut self, buf: &mut String)` — Reserves an empty text buffer for `max_text_len` bytes when the limits are preallocated and it is smaller (e.g. a formatting buffer before its first use, so formatting after a seal allocates nothing). Nothing otherwise; never panics.
Implements: Debug

#### fn twine_engine::default_covers
`pub fn default_covers(cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect) -> bool`
The default cover check (LVGL `lv_obj` cover check): the node covers `area` when it has no transform, `opa`, `opa_layered` and `bg_opa` are fully opaque, the blend mode is normal, no gradient stop is translucent, and `area` lies inside the coordinates without touching the rounded corners (inside the rectangle minus the `radius × radius` corner squares).

#### fn twine_engine::default_hit_test
`pub fn default_hit_test(cx: &twine_engine::MeasureCx<'_>, p: twine_core::Point) -> bool`
The default hit test: `p` inside the coordinates; with `ObjFlags::ADV_HITTEST` the rounded corners (`Radius` of `Part::Main`) are excluded.

#### fn twine_engine::audit_features

### mod twine_engine::gridnav

Grid navigation (LVGL `lv_gridnav`): arrow keys move the focus among the children of a
container by their position on screen.

The container is the member of the focus group; its children are not. The container keeps
track of a "focused child" that gets `FOCUSED | FOCUS_KEY` while the container is focused.
`Left`/`Right`/`Up`/`Down` keys pick the nearest child in that direction; other keys and the
press / click events of keypads and encoders are forwarded to the focused child.

#### fn twine_engine::gridnav::gridnav_add
`pub fn gridnav_add(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, container: twine_engine::NodeId, ctrl: twine_engine::GridnavCtrl)`
Enables grid navigation on `container` (replacing an earlier gridnav on it). Removes the container's `SCROLL_WITH_ARROW` flag (the arrows now move the focus).

#### fn twine_engine::gridnav::gridnav_remove
`pub fn gridnav_remove(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, container: twine_engine::NodeId)`
Disables grid navigation on `container`.

#### fn twine_engine::gridnav::gridnav_set_focused
`pub fn gridnav_set_focused(engine: &mut twine_engine::Engine, container: twine_engine::NodeId, child: Option<twine_engine::NodeId>, anim: bool)`
Makes `child` the focused child of the gridnav `container` (it gets `FOCUSED | FOCUS_KEY`) and scrolls it into view (animated with `anim`).

#### fn twine_engine::gridnav::gridnav_focused
`pub fn gridnav_focused(engine: &twine_engine::Engine, container: twine_engine::NodeId) -> Option<twine_engine::NodeId>`
The focused child of the gridnav `container`.

Re-exports in `twine_engine::gridnav`:
- `GridnavCtrl` — same as `twine_engine::GridnavCtrl`

## crate twine_reactive

Documented with features: `std,async`.

**twine-reactive**

Fine-grained, push-pull, glitch-free reactive signals for a single UI thread
The declarative view layer (`twine-view`) builds on it: every
widget property bound to a signal is an effect that writes that one
property, so a signal change runs exactly the bindings that depend on it (P2).

It sits directly above `twine-core` in the layering: `no_std` + `alloc`, depends only on
`twine-core`, `critical-section`, `portable-atomic` and `heapless`, and uses no `Arc` or CAS
atomics (it builds for thumbv6m).

```rust
use twine_reactive::Runtime;

let rt = Runtime::take().expect("runtime already taken"); // once, in the UI context
let cx = rt.create_root();
let (a, b) = (cx.signal(1), cx.signal(2));
let sum = cx.memo(move || a.get() + b.get());
let parity = sum.map(|s| s % 2);
cx.effect(move || println!("sum = {}, parity = {}", sum.get(), parity.get()));
a.set(3); // effect runs once: sum = 5, parity = 1
rt.batch(|| {
    a.set(1);
    b.set(1);
}); // effect runs once for both writes
assert_eq!(sum.get(), 2);
cx.dispose();
```

**Primitives**

| Item | Role |
|------|------|
| `Runtime` | the token of the UI context's runtime (`Runtime::take`); root scopes (`Runtime::create_root`) and every runtime-wide operation |
| `Runtime::take_partition`, `Runtime::partition`, `Scope::partition`, `Partition` | partitioned runtimes (feature `partitions`): independent runtimes for independent UIs (§ Partitions) |
| `Scope` | owns nodes, child scopes, cleanups, context values |
| `Scope::provide`, `Scope::use_context`, `Scope::expect_context`, `MissingContext` | context values: provided by a scope for its descendants, found by type (allocation-free scope-chain walk); `Result` or panicking lookup (not in the `safety` profile) |
| `Signal`, `ReadSignal`, `WriteSignal` | reactive values |
| `Memo` | lazy, cached, equality-checked derived values |
| `StoredValue` | a plain, non-reactive value owned by a scope (`Copy` handle) |
| `EffectId` | side effects re-run when their dependencies change |
| `Runtime::batch`, `Runtime::untrack` | group writes; read without subscribing |
| `Channel`, `Overflow` | ISR/task-safe FIFO into the UI (`Scope::on_message`); full-queue policy |
| `Latest` | ISR/task-safe latest-value cell into the UI (`Scope::watch`, `Scope::on_latest`): no queue, nothing dropped |
| `Outbox` | FIFO from the UI to a task: `try_recv`, or `recv().await` (feature `async`) |
| `UiWaker`, `WakerLease` | wake-ups of the UI loop (and of an `Outbox` consumer); one waker per root scope (`Scope::set_ui_waker`); `WakerLease::set_heap_limit` caps the heap the waker pool may grow to |
| `Runtime::take_faults`, `Runtime::take_capacity_faults`, `Runtime::set_fault_hook`, `Runtime::stats` | faults the runtime recovered from (capacity faults per bound), counters |
| `Runtime::set_limits` | the runtime's share of `Limits`: nodes, scopes, pending effects; preallocation |
| `audit_features` | the runtime's cargo features for an audit report |
| `Runtime::memory`, `RuntimeMemory` | the runtime's heap use, by part (arenas, values, scope data, queues) |
| `TakeOnce` | a `static` value handed out once as `&'static mut` (draw buffers, DMA memory), from any context |
| `set_interrupt_probe`, `in_interrupt` | the platform's "am I in an interrupt?" answer, for diagnostics |

| `ReactiveError`, `HandleKind` | why an operation on a handle failed (the `try_*` forms) |

All handles are `Copy` and `!Send`/`!Sync`.

**Failures**

Operations on handles fail only through programming errors — a handle used after its scope
was disposed, a write inside a read of the same value, a memo that reads itself — or an
exhausted bound (`Limits::max_reactive_nodes` or
`Limits::max_scopes`, see `Runtime::set_limits`); never because of input data. Each
fallible operation comes in two forms:

- **`try_*`** (`Signal::try_get`, `Signal::try_with`, `Signal::try_set`,
  `Signal::try_update`, `Memo::try_get`, `StoredValue::try_set`,
  `Scope::try_signal`, `Scope::try_memo`, `Scope::try_effect`, `Scope::try_child`,
  `Runtime::try_create_root`, …) returns `Result<_, ReactiveError>`, never panics and
  raises no fault: the caller decides. Use them (or `is_alive`) for handles that may
  outlive their scope.
- **The usual form** (`get`, `with`, `set`, `update`, `signal`, `memo`, `effect`, `child`,
  …) is a thin `#[track_caller]` wrapper over the same code. The success path costs the
  same as before the split (one `match`), and the failure path is a `#[cold]
**[inline(never)]` function, so the hot path carries no extra code.**

What the usual form does on failure depends on the `no-panic-runtime` feature (implied by
`safety`):

| Failure | Default | `no-panic-runtime` |
|---------|---------|--------------------|
| write to a disposed signal / stored value (`set`, `update`, `set_if_changed`) | panic | skipped (the value is dropped), `warn!` + `FaultKind::DisposedHandle` |
| write inside a read of the same value | panic | skipped, `warn!` + `FaultKind::ReentrantAccess` |
| creation in a disposed scope (`signal`, `memo`, `effect`, `child`, `map`, …) | panic | a handle that is never alive, `warn!` + `FaultKind::DisposedHandle` |
| creation beyond `Limits::max_reactive_nodes` / `max_scopes` | panic | a handle that is never alive, `warn!` + `FaultKind::Capacity` (code `ReactiveNodes` / `ReactiveScopes`) |
| a memo that reads itself (cycle) | panic | the memo's previous value, `warn!` + `FaultKind::MemoCycle` |
| a read that has no value: disposed handle, value mutably borrowed, cycle on a memo's first computation | panic | fault raised, then panic |

Reads that have no value to return still panic in every profile: they must return a `T`,
and inventing one (a default, another value of the type) would show wrong data without
anyone noticing. With `no-panic-runtime` the fault is raised first, so the application's
fault hook runs before its panic handler (`docs/safety/panics.md` in the repository lists
this site). Code that must not panic reads with the `try_*` forms.

Faults raised by `no-panic-runtime` are counted, reported to the
fault hook and kept for `Runtime::take_faults` like the
runtime's other faults (§ Faults); a `Ui` forwards them to its fault stream.

**Algorithm (push-pull coloring)**

A write **pushes** colors: direct subscribers become `Dirty`, their descendants `Check`
(descent stops at nodes already colored); effects reached are queued once. Reading a memo,
or flushing a queued effect, **pulls**: a `Check` node first brings its sources up to date
in read order and only recomputes if one of them actually changed; a memo whose new value
equals the old one does not mark its subscribers, so propagation stops there.

```rust
  a.set(3)                         a ──► sum ──► parity ──► E2
                                         │
  push:  sum = Dirty                     └────────────────► E1
         parity, E1, E2 = Check;  E1, E2 queued

  flush E1: Check → pull sum (recompute, changed) → E1 Dirty → run E1
  flush E2: Check → pull parity → pull sum (Clean) → recompute parity
            parity unchanged → E2 stays Check → Clean, not run
```

Every computation therefore runs at most once per change and never observes a mix of old
and new values (glitch-free: in a diamond `a → b, a → c, b + c → d`, `d` runs once per
write of `a`). Memos are lazy: they compute on first read, not at creation.

**Deep chains.** The pull is recursive. Beyond a depth of 256 nested checks a node is
recomputed without checking its sources (an `error!` is logged; results stay correct,
only extra work is done). Computing a long chain for the first time still recurses once
per memo through user code, so keep memo chains shallow on MCUs with small stacks.

**Effects and the view layer**

Effects receive a `&mut dyn Any` context (`Scope::effect_with_cx`). The view layer uses
three entry points:

1. **Creation**: an effect created outside a flush runs immediately with a `()` context;
   created during a flush, it runs later in that same flush with the flush's context.
2. **Automatic flush**: a write outside any batch or flush flushes at once with `()`.
   `Ui` wraps event dispatch and `Runtime::drain_channels` in `Runtime::batch`, so this mostly happens in
   tests that call `set` directly.
3. **`Runtime::flush_effects_with`** at the `Ui`'s fixed point in the update cycle, with the engine
   as context. A binding that finds no engine (`downcast_mut` fails) calls
   `Runtime::defer_current_effect`; deferred effects are re-queued by the next flush with a
   non-`()` context. `Runtime::has_pending_effects` reports pending or deferred work.

Code that runs without a context parameter (event handlers, user effects, timer
callbacks) reaches the engine through the *ambient* slot: `Runtime::provide_ambient` lends a
`&mut dyn Any` for the duration of a call, `Runtime::with_ambient` borrows it exclusively
(taking it out of the slot, so nested borrows see `None`) and `Runtime::ambient_is` tests its type
without borrowing it. A binding whose widget was deleted disposes itself with
`Runtime::dispose_current_effect`.

**Several UIs on one runtime: roots**

Each `Ui` owns one root scope, and its update runs as that root's update
(`Scope::activate`). While a root is active, only its effects run with the flush context and
the ambient value; an effect of another root that a shared signal triggers meanwhile runs
with `()` and an empty ambient slot (a binding defers itself, and
`Runtime::defer_current_effect` wakes its root's waker so its own UI runs it), and a flush
with a context re-queues only the active root's deferred effects. Channel handlers are
delivered per root (`Scope::drain_channels`, `Scope::any_channel_pending`) and pending
work is asked per root (`Scope::has_pending_effects`). So a binding only ever writes into
the engine it was built for. Outside every update no root is active and nothing is
filtered. Cost: one comparison per effect run; the rare foreign effect runs out of line.
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### struct twine_reactive::Channel<T, const N: usize>
A bounded, `const`-constructible, allocation-free FIFO queue from interrupts, tasks, threads or other cores **to the UI**.
Methods of `Channel`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty channel with room for `N` values; a full channel refuses new values (`Overflow::DropNewest`; see `on_full`).
- `pub const fn on_full(self, policy: twine_reactive::Overflow) -> Self` — The channel with overflow policy `policy` (see `Overflow`); `const`, so a `static` states its policy where it is declared. Default: `Overflow::DropNewest`.
- `pub const fn overflow(&self) -> twine_reactive::Overflow` — The overflow policy (see `on_full`). Never panics.
- `pub fn try_send(&self, v: T) -> Result<(), T>` — Queues `v` and wakes the UI. Interrupt- and thread-safe; never blocks, never allocates, never panics (unless a notify function or task waker does, see `UiWaker::wake`).
  Errors: `Err(v)` when the channel is full and its policy is `Overflow::DropNewest` (the UI is not woken). With `Overflow::DropOldest` a full channel evicts its oldest value instead (dropped in the caller's context) and `try_send` succeeds. Either way the lost value is counted (`take_dropped`).
- `pub fn try_recv(&self) -> Option<T>` — Dequeues the oldest value (`None` when empty). Any context; allocation-free; never panics. The UI normally receives through `Scope::on_message` instead.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of queued values.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether no value is queued.
- `pub fn waker(&self) -> &twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The waker signalled by `try_send` (the routing to the UI's waker is set up by `Scope::on_message`).
- `pub fn take_dropped(&self) -> u32` — Returns and resets the number of values lost because the channel was full (refused or evicted, see `Overflow`). The `on_message` drain calls it and reports the count as a `FaultKind::ChannelOverflow` fault; call it yourself only for a channel without a handler.
Implements: Default, Debug

#### struct twine_reactive::UiWaker
Wakes the UI loop. A `wake` does three things, each optional for the loop that runs the UI:
Methods of `UiWaker`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — A waker with the flag cleared and no registered task.
- `pub fn wake(&self)` — Sets the flag, then wakes the registered task and calls the notify function, if any.
- `pub fn set_notify(&self, notify: fn())` — Sets the function every `wake` calls (replacing the previous one): the hook for run loops that sleep on something other than the flag or an async task — an RTOS task notification or semaphore, an RTIC `pend`, a `Platform`'s notify (e.g. `twine_hal::Platform::notify`, installed by `UiBuilder::platform`).
- `pub fn clear_notify(&self)` — Removes the notify function (see `set_notify`); later wakes only set the flag and wake the task. Interrupt-safe, allocation-free, never panics.
- `pub fn register(&self, w: &Waker)` — Registers the task to wake (replacing a different one).
- `pub fn take(&self) -> bool` — Reads and clears the flag.
- `pub fn is_set(&self) -> bool` — Whether the flag is set (not clearing it).
- `pub fn unregister(&self, w: &Waker) -> bool` — Removes the registered task if it is `w` (or wakes the same task); returns whether it was removed. Another registered task is left in place; the flag is not touched.
- `pub fn reset(&self)` — Clears the flag and removes the registered task and the notify function (a waker handed to a new owner, e.g. when a pooled waker goes back to the pool).
- `pub fn task_waker(&'static self) -> Waker` — A task `Waker` that wakes this `UiWaker` (sets its flag and wakes the task registered in it). It allocates nothing: the waker points to `self`, so cloning and dropping it are no-ops, and it may be woken from any thread or interrupt.
- `pub fn lease() -> twine_reactive::WakerLease` — A `'static` waker for a new owner (a `Ui`), returned to a process-wide pool when the `WakerLease` is dropped. See `WakerLease` for where the waker lives: no allocation for the first `WakerLease::STATIC_SLOTS` leases alive at once, a bounded number of heap wakers beyond, and a shared waker (`WakerLease::is_shared`) once the pool is exhausted. Callable from any context; never panics.
- `pub fn lease_in(p: twine_core::Partition) -> twine_reactive::WakerLease` — `lease` for an owner in partition `p`: a heap waker allocated after `p` was sealed is noted in `p`'s seal domain (the `Ui` of a partition leases its waker this way). The pool itself is process-wide and shared by every partition (ADR-001 N6): give a critical partition a dedicated `static` waker (`UiBuilder::waker`) so the pool cannot affect it. Callable from any context; never panics.
Implements: Default, Debug

#### struct twine_reactive::WakerLease
A `'static` `UiWaker` lent to one owner at a time (`UiWaker::lease`); returned (and `reset`) when dropped.
Methods of `WakerLease`:
- `const STATIC_SLOTS: usize` — Leases served from `static` memory before the heap is used.
- `const DEFAULT_HEAP_LIMIT: u16` — The default of `heap_limit`: heap wakers that may be allocated beyond the `STATIC_SLOTS` (so up to 64 UIs alive at once get a waker of their own). Devices run a handful of UIs; the bound turns a leak — UIs that are never dropped — into a reported fault instead of unbounded heap growth. Equal to `Limits::DEFAULT.max_heap_wakers`.
- `pub fn set_heap_limit(limit: u16)` — Sets how many wakers the pool may allocate on the heap in total (process-wide; `0` forbids heap wakers, e.g. for a profile without dynamic allocation after start-up). Wakers already allocated stay in the pool and are still reused; lowering the limit below their number only stops further allocations. The `Ui` builders set it from `Limits::max_heap_wakers` (`AppConfig::limits`). Callable from any context (one critical section); never panics.
- `pub fn heap_limit() -> u16` — The limit set with `set_heap_limit` (default `DEFAULT_HEAP_LIMIT`). Never panics.
- `pub fn heap_allocated() -> u16` — The number of wakers the pool allocated on the heap so far (never decreases: heap wakers are reused, not freed). Never panics.
- `pub fn heap_bytes() -> usize` — Heap bytes of the wakers the pool allocated so far (`heap_allocated` × the size of one heap waker). Process-wide, never decreases; the `STATIC_SLOTS` static wakers are not heap. Never panics.
- `const HEAP_WAKER_BYTES: usize` — Size in bytes of one heap-allocated waker of the pool.
- `pub fn get(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The leased waker. The reference outlives the lease (it is `'static`), but once the lease is dropped the waker may belong to another owner.
- `pub fn is_shared(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is the shared fallback of an exhausted pool (see `WakerLease` § Exhausted pool): the waker is not this owner's alone. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### struct twine_reactive::MissingContext
No value of the asked type was provided by the scope or any of its ancestors (or the scope was disposed: a disposed scope provides nothing). Returned by `Scope::use_context`; `type_name` names the missing type.
Methods of `MissingContext`:
- `pub fn of<T: ?Sized + 'static>() -> Self` — The error for a missing `T`.
- `pub fn type_name(&self) -> &'static str` — The name of the missing type, as `core::any::type_name` spells it (meant for diagnostics: the exact text is not stable across compiler versions).
- `pub fn panic(self) -> never` — Panics with this error's message at the caller's location (the shared, out-of-line panic path of `Scope::expect_context` and the `expect_*` hooks).
  Panics: Always, with `"context {type_name} not provided"`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error

#### struct twine_reactive::EffectId
Handle to an effect (`Copy`, `!Send`, `!Sync`).
Methods of `EffectId`:
- `pub fn dispose(self)` — Stops the effect and releases its closure. Disposing twice is a no-op.
- `pub fn is_alive(self) -> bool` — Whether the effect is still alive (not disposed, scope alive).
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug

#### enum twine_reactive::HandleKind
The kind of reactive handle a `ReactiveError` is about.
Variants:
- `Signal` — A `Signal`, `ReadSignal` or `WriteSignal`.
- `Memo` — A `Memo`.
- `StoredValue` — A `StoredValue`.
- `Effect` — An effect (`EffectId`).
- `Scope` — A `Scope`.
Methods of `HandleKind`:
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The kind's name as messages spell it (`"signal"`, `"memo"`, `"stored value"`, `"effect"`, `"scope"`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### enum twine_reactive::ReactiveError
Why an operation on a reactive handle failed: the error of the `try_*` forms (`Signal::try_set`, `Memo::try_get`, `Scope::try_signal`, …).
Variants:
- `Disposed(twine_reactive::HandleKind)` — The handle's scope was disposed (for `HandleKind::Scope`: the scope itself, e.g. when creating a node in it). Handles returned by a creation that was skipped under `no-panic-runtime` are never alive and fail the same way.
- `Borrowed(twine_reactive::HandleKind)` — The value is borrowed by an enclosing access of the same value: a write inside `with`, or any access inside `update` / `with_mut`, on the same handle.
- `Capacity(twine_reactive::HandleKind)` — The runtime's bound is reached: `Limits::max_scopes` live scopes (`HandleKind::Scope`) or `Limits::max_reactive_nodes` live nodes (signals, memos, stored values and effects together); both at most 65 535 (see `Runtime::set_limits`).
- `Cycle` — A memo read itself, directly or through other memos (a dependency cycle).
Methods of `ReactiveError`:
- `pub const fn fault_kind(self) -> twine_core::FaultKind` — The fault the `no-panic-runtime` feature raises when it skips an operation that failed with this error: `FaultKind::DisposedHandle`, `FaultKind::ReentrantAccess`, `FaultKind::Capacity` or `FaultKind::MemoCycle`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, Error

#### struct twine_reactive::Runtime
The proof that the calling execution context owns a reactive runtime — a **partition**'s runtime: the token every runtime-wide operation needs (creating a root scope, batching, flushing, draining channels, the ambient slot, statistics and faults).
Methods of `Runtime`:
- `pub fn ambient_is<T: Any>(self) -> bool` — Whether the ambient slot holds a `T` that `with_ambient` could borrow right now: `false` outside a `provide_ambient`, while an enclosing `with_ambient` borrows the value, or when it is of another type. It neither takes the value out of the slot nor puts it back (one read of the slot instead of `with_ambient`'s two writes), so it is the cheap way to ask before doing work that needs the value. Never panics; allocates nothing.
- `pub fn provide_ambient<R>(self, value: &mut dyn Any, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Makes `value` available to `with_ambient` calls made (directly or indirectly) by `f`, then restores the previous ambient value (also when `f` panics). Nested calls shadow the outer value until they return. Allocates nothing.
- `pub fn with_ambient<R>(self, f: impl FnOnce(Option<&mut dyn Any>) -> R) -> R` — Calls `f` with the value of the innermost active `provide_ambient` (`None` when there is none, or while it is already borrowed by an enclosing `with_ambient`). The value is taken out of the slot while `f` runs and put back afterwards (also when `f` panics). Allocates nothing.
  Panics: Only when `f` panics (the panic propagates after the value was put back).
- `pub fn batch<R>(self, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with effects deferred until it returns; returns `f`'s result.
- `pub fn untrack<R>(self, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` without dependency tracking: reads inside `f` do not subscribe the running memo or effect. Allocates nothing.
- `pub fn flush_effects_with(self, ctx: &mut dyn Any)` — Runs all pending effects, passing `ctx` to each (see `Scope::effect_with_cx`).
- `pub fn set_flush_iterations_limit(self, n: u32)` — Sets how many rounds of effects re-triggering each other a flush runs before cutting the loop (default 100, minimum 1: `0` is taken as `1`). Never panics.
- `pub fn defer_current_effect(self)` — Called from inside a running effect: re-queues it to run again at the next flush with a real (non-`()`) context.
- `pub fn dispose_current_effect(self)` — Called from inside a running effect: disposes it (its closure is released after this run).
- `pub fn has_pending_effects(self) -> bool` — Whether effects of any root are waiting to run (pending, or deferred until a real context). A `Ui` asks `Scope::has_pending_effects` for its own root instead. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn drain_channels(self, max_per_channel: usize) -> usize` — Delivers queued channel messages to their `Scope::on_message` handlers — of **every** root —, at most `max_per_channel` per registration, inside one `batch`. Returns the number of messages handled.
- `pub fn any_channel_pending(self) -> bool` — Whether any channel with an `on_message` registration (of any root) has queued messages. Allocates nothing; never panics. A `Ui` asks `Scope::any_channel_pending` for its own root instead.
- `pub fn take() -> Option<twine_reactive::Runtime>` — Takes the runtime of `Partition::MAIN` for the calling execution context: `Some` the first time, `None` afterwards (without `std`: once per process; with `std`: once per thread). The same as `take_partition(Partition::MAIN)`: an application with one partition never names one.
- `pub fn take_partition(p: twine_core::Partition) -> Option<twine_reactive::Runtime>` — Takes the runtime of partition `p` for the calling execution context: `Some` the first time, `None` afterwards — once per partition and process without `std`, once per partition and thread with it. Each partition can be taken by a different context (two cores, two RTOS tasks, two executors), or several by one context (a super-loop stepping both UIs). Without the `partitions` feature only `Partition::MAIN` exists, so every other partition is `None` (it cannot be named: `Partition::new(1)` is `None` too).
- `pub const fn partition(self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition this token is the runtime of. Free; never panics.
- `pub fn current_thread() -> twine_reactive::Runtime` — The calling thread's runtime of `Partition::MAIN` (`std` only), whether or not `take` was called on this thread; it does not claim it either. With `std` every thread has its own runtimes, so a token for them can be handed out at any time: this is the convenience for tests, test harnesses, simulators and host tools. Portable code uses `take`. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn current_thread_partition(p: twine_core::Partition) -> twine_reactive::Runtime` — The calling thread's runtime of partition `p` (`std` only), without claiming it: like `current_thread` for another partition (tests that run two partitions on one thread, `TestUi` on a chosen partition, the simulator). Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn create_root(self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — Creates a new root scope.
  Panics: Only when the runtime already holds `Limits::max_scopes` live scopes. With `no-panic-runtime` it never panics: it returns a scope that is never alive after a `warn!` and a `Capacity` fault. `try_create_root` returns the error instead.
- `pub fn try_create_root(self) -> Result<twine_reactive::Scope, twine_reactive::ReactiveError>` — Like `create_root`, returning `ReactiveError::Capacity` (`HandleKind::Scope`) when the runtime already holds `Limits::max_scopes` live scopes instead of panicking. Raises no fault.
  Errors: `ReactiveError::Capacity`, as above.
- `pub fn stats(self) -> twine_reactive::Stats` — Live object counts and counters of the runtime (diagnostics, tests and fault analysis). Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn memory(self) -> twine_reactive::RuntimeMemory` — What the runtime's heap is used for, by part (`RuntimeMemory`: units and what is not included). Allocates nothing; never panics; O(nodes + scopes), so call it on demand (diagnostics, budgeting, tests), not every frame.
- `pub fn take_faults(self) -> twine_core::FaultCounts` — The faults the runtime recorded since the last call (occurrences per kind), clearing them. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn take_capacity_faults(self) -> [(twine_core::fault::CapacityFault, u32); 3]` — Which bound the runtime's `FaultKind::Capacity` faults since the last call were about: the occurrences per bound (`CapacityFault::ReactiveNodes`, `ReactiveScopes`, `PendingEffects`), clearing them. Their sum is the `Capacity` count of `take_faults`; `Ui` forwards each as a record with its code. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn set_limits(self, limits: &twine_core::Limits) -> Result<(), twine_core::Error>` — Applies the runtime's share of `limits` to this partition's runtime (other partitions keep their own bounds; per thread with `std`): `max_reactive_nodes`, `max_scopes` and `max_pending_effects` bound creations and the effect queues from now on (a creation beyond them fails with `ReactiveError::Capacity`; an effect beyond the queue bound is not queued and raises a `Capacity` fault with code `CapacityFault::PendingEffects`). With `preallocate` it also reserves the node and scope arenas, both effect queues and the propagation stack, so staying within the bounds allocates nothing there. Lowering a bound below the current count refuses further creations until enough are disposed. The `Ui` builders call it with `AppConfig::limits`.
  Errors: `twine_core::Error::InvalidArgument` from `Limits::validate`; nothing is applied.
- `pub fn set_fault_hook(self, hook: Option<twine_reactive::FaultHook>)` — Sets the function called for every fault the runtime records (`None` removes it), with the kind and the number of occurrences. It runs where the fault is detected — possibly in the middle of an effect flush — so keep it short: record, count or signal a supervisor. A new hook replaces the previous one.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<twine_reactive::Scope>

#### fn twine_reactive::in_interrupt
`pub fn in_interrupt() -> bool`
Whether the caller runs in interrupt context according to the probe set with `set_interrupt_probe` (`false` without one). Callable from any context; allocates nothing; never panics.

#### fn twine_reactive::interrupt_probe
`pub fn interrupt_probe() -> Option<fn() -> bool>`
The probe set with `set_interrupt_probe`, if any. Callable from any context; allocates nothing; never panics.

#### fn twine_reactive::set_interrupt_probe
`pub fn set_interrupt_probe(probe: Option<fn() -> bool>)`
Sets the function that tells whether the caller runs in interrupt context (`None` removes it): the platform's answer (`twine_hal::Platform::in_interrupt`, installed by `UiBuilder::platform`), typically reading an interrupt-status register.

#### struct twine_reactive::Latest<T>
A latest-value cell from interrupts, tasks, threads or other cores **to the UI**: a sensor reading, a connection state, a battery level — data where only the newest value matters.
Methods of `Latest`:
- `pub const fn new(initial: T) -> Self` — A cell holding `initial` (version 0). `const`, so it can initialise a `static`.
- `pub fn set(&self, value: T)` — Overwrites the value and wakes the UI. Interrupt- and thread-safe; never blocks, never fails, never allocates. The previous value is dropped after the critical section, in the caller's context.
  Panics: Only if called from the `Clone` implementation of `T` while that clone runs for this same cell (a re-entrant borrow), or if the waker's notify function or task waker panics.
- `pub fn replace(&self, value: T) -> T` — `set`, returning the previous value instead of dropping it.
  Panics: As `set`.
- `pub fn version(&self) -> u32` — The number of `set`s so far (wrapping at `u32::MAX`). A consumer that polls instead of registering with the UI compares it with the version it last saw. Never panics.
