#### trait twine_render::DrawAccel
`pub trait DrawAccel`
A hardware accelerator for common operations. The software renderer is always complete; an accelerator only speeds up what it supports.
Items:
- `fn fill(&mut self, dst: &mut twine_render::DrawBuf<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, color: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_render::AccelResult` — Fills `area` (inside `dst` and the clip) with `color` at `opa`.
- `fn blit(&mut self, dst: &mut twine_render::DrawBuf<'_>, dst_area: twine_core::Rect, src: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_render::AccelResult` — Copies/blends `src` onto `dst_area` (same size as `src`).
- `fn blend_a8(&mut self, dst: &mut twine_render::DrawBuf<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, color: twine_core::Color, alpha: &[u8], stride: usize) -> twine_render::AccelResult` — Blends `color` through an 8-bit alpha map (`stride` bytes per row) onto `area`.
- `fn wait(&mut self)` — Waits until all queued operations have finished.
- `fn take_timeouts(&mut self) -> u32 (provided)` — Operations that did not finish within the accelerator's own bound since the last call (clearing the count). Their pixels may be missing (a queued operation is only found to have timed out at a later `wait`). The engine polls this after every rendered chunk; when non-zero it renders the chunk again in software and raises `FaultKind::AccelTimeout`. Default: `0` (an accelerator that cannot time out).

#### struct twine_render::ArcDsc<'a>
Arc parameters.
Fields:
- `color: twine_core::Color` — Color (unless `image` is set).
- `opa: twine_core::Opa` — Opacity.
- `width: i32` — Ring width (`≥ radius`: a pie sector).
- `rounded: bool` — Rounded ends.
- `image: Option<&'a twine_render::ImagePixels<'a>>` — Fill the ring with this image, placed with its top-left corner at `center − (radius, radius)` (normally a `2·radius` square). Pixels outside the image are not drawn.
- `blend_mode: twine_render::BlendMode` — Blend mode.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default

#### enum twine_render::BlendMode
How source colors combine with the destination before alpha mixing (the LVGL set).
Variants:
- `Normal` — The source replaces the destination (mixed by alpha).
- `Additive` — Channels are added (saturating).
- `Subtractive` — Source channels are subtracted from the destination (saturating at 0).
- `Multiply` — Channels are multiplied.
- `Difference` — Absolute channel difference.
Methods of `BlendMode`:
- `const ALL: [twine_render::BlendMode; 5]` — Every mode, in declaration order.
- `pub fn channel(self, s: u8, d: u8) -> u8` — Combines one channel of the source `s` with the destination `d`.
- `pub fn color(self, s: twine_core::Color, d: twine_core::Color) -> twine_core::Color` — Combines the source color `s` with the destination color `d` channel by channel.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_render::Source<'s>
What a span is painted with.
Variants:
- `Solid(twine_core::Color)` — One color.
- `Pixels { data: &'s [u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat }` — Pixels of a byte-aligned format, starting with the span's first pixel (`Rgb565`, `Rgb565Swapped`, `Rgb888`, `Xrgb8888`, `Argb8888`, `L8`).
- `Argb(&'s [u8])` — Straight-alpha `Argb8888` pixels (memory `B, G, R, A`), starting with the span's first pixel.
Methods of `Source`:
- `pub fn offset(self, px: usize) -> twine_render::Source<'s>` — The source advanced by `px` pixels.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — How many pixels the source can provide (`usize::MAX` for a solid color).
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the source provides no pixels.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_render::argb_raw
`pub fn argb_raw(c: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> u32`
The raw `Argb8888` value of `c` with alpha `opa` (helper for building layer rows).

#### fn twine_render::blend_span
`pub fn blend_span<F: twine_core::PixelFormat>(dst: &mut [u8], n: usize, src: twine_render::Source<'_>, mask: Option<&[u8]>, opa: twine_core::Opa, mode: twine_render::BlendMode)`
Blends `n` pixels of `src` onto `dst` (row bytes of format `F`).

#### fn twine_render::mix_color
`pub fn mix_color(fg: twine_core::Color, bg: twine_core::Color, a: twine_core::Opa, mode: twine_render::BlendMode) -> twine_core::Color`
Mixes `fg` over `bg` with alpha `a` and blend `mode`, like `blend_span` does for one pixel of an alpha-less destination (without quantization).

#### struct twine_render::DrawBuf<'a>
Pixel memory in one `ColorFormat` representing the screen rectangle `area`.
Methods of `DrawBuf`:
- `pub fn new(data: &'a mut [u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat, stride: usize, area: twine_core::Rect) -> Result<Self, twine_render::RenderError>` — Wraps `data` as the pixels of `area` (screen coordinates) with rows `stride` bytes apart.
  Errors: `RenderError::UnsupportedFormat` for formats that cannot be drawn into; `RenderError::FormatDisabled` for draw formats whose renderer is not compiled in (see `is_format_enabled`: drawing never meets a disabled format); `RenderError::InvalidArea` for an empty area, a stride shorter than a row, or an `I1` area whose `x0`/`x1` are not multiples of 8; `RenderError::BufferTooSmall` when `data` cannot hold the area.
- `pub fn new_packed(data: &'a mut [u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat, area: twine_core::Rect) -> Result<Self, twine_render::RenderError>` — Like `new` with `stride = width · bpp / 8` (rows packed).
  Errors: As `new`.
- `pub fn format(&self) -> twine_core::ColorFormat` — The pixel format.
- `pub fn area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The screen rectangle the buffer represents.
- `pub fn stride(&self) -> usize` — Bytes between rows.
- `pub fn data(&self) -> &[u8]` — The whole underlying memory.
- `pub fn data_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8]` — The whole underlying memory, mutably.
- `pub fn row_mut(&mut self, y: i32, x0: i32, x1: i32) -> &mut [u8]` — Bytes of pixels `[x0, x1)` of row `y`, in absolute coordinates that must lie inside `area`. For `I1` the bytes containing the pixels are returned (`x0` rounded down, `x1` up to a multiple of 8).
- `pub fn row(&self, y: i32, x0: i32, x1: i32) -> &[u8]` — Shared version of `row_mut` (outside the area: an empty slice).
- `pub fn clear(&mut self, color: twine_core::Color)` — Fills the whole buffer with `color` (opaque). Formats whose `color-*` feature is disabled are left unchanged (with a warning).
- `pub fn reborrow(&mut self) -> twine_render::DrawBuf<'_>` — A shorter-lived `DrawBuf` over the same memory.
Implements: Debug

#### fn twine_render::is_draw_format
`pub const fn is_draw_format(format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> bool`
Whether `format` can be the format of a `DrawBuf` (independent of enabled features).

#### struct twine_render::CacheStats
Hit and miss counters of one cache.
Fields:
- `hits: u32` — Lookups served from the cache.
- `misses: u32` — Lookups that computed the entry.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_render::RenderCacheStats
Counters of every cache (for tests and the performance monitor).
Fields:
- `circle: twine_render::CacheStats` — Quarter-circle coverage.
- `shadow: twine_render::CacheStats` — Blurred shadow corners.
- `gradient: twine_render::CacheStats` — Gradient color maps.
- `image_copy_rows: u32` — Image rows drawn by the same-format copy path of `Painter::image`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_render::RenderCaches
All scratch memory and caches of the renderer, created once (e.g. when the engine is built) with `RenderConfig` budgets and reused by every `Painter`.
Methods of `RenderCaches`:
- `pub fn new(cfg: &twine_render::RenderConfig) -> Self` — Allocates every buffer and cache arena of `cfg`, the layer buffer (`cfg.layer_buf_bytes`) included.
- `pub fn with_layer_buf(cfg: &twine_render::RenderConfig, layer_buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — Like `new`, but the layer buffer is `layer_buf` — caller memory, typically a `static`, so the largest scratch buffer of the renderer stays out of the heap. `cfg.layer_buf_bytes` is ignored; `config` reports `layer_buf.len()` (saturated to `u32::MAX`). The bytes need no particular alignment or initial content (every layer clears what it uses).
- `pub fn config(&self) -> &twine_render::RenderConfig` — The configuration.
- `pub fn max_span(&self) -> usize` — Widest span processed at once.
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes reserved by the scratch buffers, the caches and a heap layer buffer: `scratch_bytes` + `cache_bytes` + the layer buffer unless it is static. The extension slot (`put_extension`) is not included.
- `pub fn scratch_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes of the per-span scratch buffers (coverage, mask, ARGB samples and 16-bit accumulators: `8 × max_span` bytes by capacity). Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn cache_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes of the quarter-circle, shadow and gradient caches (their fixed arenas). Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn layer_buf_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Size of the layer buffer in bytes, wherever it lives (0 while a layer is being drawn, which is never observable from outside a draw).
- `pub fn layer_buf_is_static(&self) -> bool` — Whether the layer buffer is caller memory (`with_layer_buf`) rather than heap.
- `pub fn gradient_color_map(&mut self, g: &twine_render::Gradient) -> &[u32]` — The cached 256-entry color map (packed `0xAARRGGBB`, see `build_color_map`) of `g`'s stops, built on a miss (evicting the least recently used map). Counts in `stats().gradient`.
- `pub fn take_extension<T: Any>(&mut self) -> Option<Box<T>>` — Takes the extension scratch state of type `T` out of the caches, if it is stored there.
- `pub fn put_extension<T: Any>(&mut self, v: Box<T>)` — Stores extension scratch state (see `take_extension`).
- `pub fn stats(&self) -> twine_render::RenderCacheStats` — Hit/miss counters.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### struct twine_render::RenderConfig
Budgets of the renderer's caches and scratch buffers.
Fields:
- `circle_cache_entries: u8` — Quarter-circle coverage entries (default 4).
- `shadow_cache_entries: u8` — Blurred shadow corners (default 1; 4 KiB each).
- `gradient_cache_entries: u8` — Gradient color maps (default 4; 1 KiB each).
- `max_span: u16` — Widest span in pixels processed at once (default 480). Wider spans are split.
- `layer_buf_bytes: u32` — Bytes of the ARGB8888 layer buffer (default 24 KiB).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### struct twine_render::CircleCache
LRU cache of quarter-circle coverage rows (fixed entry count and arena size, never grows).
Implements: Debug, Default

#### const twine_render::MAX_CACHED_RADIUS
`pub const MAX_CACHED_RADIUS: i32 = 256`
Largest radius the cache stores; larger radii are computed per row.

#### type twine_render::PixelFn
`pub type PixelFn<'s> = &'s dyn Fn(i32, i32, &mut [u8])`
Fills `out` (straight-alpha `Argb8888` bytes, memory `B, G, R, A`, `out.len() / 4` pixels) with the colors of row `y` starting at screen x `x0`.

#### enum twine_render::SpanSource<'s>
What a coverage span is painted with.
Variants:
- `Solid(twine_core::Color, twine_core::Opa)` — One color at an opacity.
- `Pixels(twine_render::PixelFn<'s>, twine_core::Opa)` — Colors computed per pixel (gradients, image patterns) at an opacity. The function is called once per chunk of at most `RenderCaches::max_span` pixels, only for the part of the span inside the clip.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### fn twine_render::is_format_enabled

Whether drawing into `format` is compiled in.

#### enum twine_render::RenderError
Errors reported when creating draw buffers or running buffer utilities.
Variants:
- `BufferTooSmall { needed: usize, got: usize }` — The byte slice is shorter than the described pixels.
- `UnsupportedFormat(twine_core::ColorFormat)` — The color format cannot be used here.
- `FormatDisabled(twine_core::ColorFormat)` — The color format is a draw format, but its renderer is not compiled in (enable the matching `color-*` feature of `twine-render`); see `is_format_enabled`.
- `InvalidArea` — The area is empty, the stride is too small, or a sub-byte format is not byte-aligned.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Error, Display

#### enum twine_render::SubpxOrder
Channel order of the three coverage values per pixel of subpixel glyphs (the panel's subpixel layout).

- `Rgb` — Red, green, blue (left to right, or top to bottom for vertical layouts).
- `Bgr` — Blue, green, red.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_render::GradExtend
What happens outside `t ∈ [0, 1]`.
Variants:
- `Pad` — The end colors continue.
- `Repeat` — The gradient repeats.
- `Reflect` — The gradient repeats mirrored.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_render::GradKind
Gradient geometry (relative to the drawn area's top-left). Coordinates and radii are clamped (never panicking) to `±2^26` px when the gradient is drawn (far beyond any screen; it keeps the sampling arithmetic exact).
Variants:
- `Hor` — Left to right over the area's width.
- `Ver` — Top to bottom over the area's height.
- `Linear { start: twine_core::Point, end: twine_core::Point }` — Along the line from `start` to `end`.
- `Radial { center: twine_core::Point, radius: i32, focal: twine_core::Point, focal_radius: i32 }` — Two-point radial gradient: `t = 0` on the focal circle (`focal`, `focal_radius`), `t = 1` on the end circle (`center`, `radius`).
- `Conical { center: twine_core::Point, start_angle: twine_core::Angle, end_angle: twine_core::Angle }` — Sweep around `center` from `start_angle` clockwise to `end_angle`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_render::MAX_STOPS
`pub const MAX_STOPS: usize = 8`
Maximum number of stops of a `Gradient`.

#### fn twine_render::build_color_map
`pub fn build_color_map(stops: &[twine_render::GradStop], map: &mut [u32])`
Fills `map` (256 entries) with samples of `stops`, packed `0xAARRGGBB`: entry `i` is the color at gradient position `i / 255` (the color map every gradient is drawn with).

#### fn twine_render::read_row_argb
`pub fn read_row_argb(px: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, y: u16, x0: u16, w: u16, out: &mut [u8])`
Reads `w` pixels of row `y` of `px`, starting at column `x0`, as straight-alpha `Argb8888` bytes (`B, G, R, A`) into `out` (at least `4 · w` bytes; shorter `out` reads fewer pixels).

#### struct twine_render::ImageDsc<'a>
How `Painter::image` draws an image (LVGL `lv_draw_image_dsc_t`).
Fields:
- `opa: twine_core::Opa` — Overall opacity.
- `recolor: twine_core::Color` — Recolor target. Alpha-only images (`A1`…`A8`) are drawn in this color when `recolor_opa` is not transparent, else in black.
- `recolor_opa: twine_core::Opa` — How strongly colors are mixed towards `recolor` (transparent = no recolor).
- `chroma_key: Option<twine_core::Color>` — Pixels of exactly this color (compared as 24-bit RGB after reading the pixel) are transparent.
- `tile: bool` — Repeat the image to fill the whole area (untransformed images only).
- `clip_radius: i32` — Corner radius of a rounded clip on the draw area (0 = none).
- `antialias: bool` — Bilinear filtering when transformed (else nearest neighbour).
- `angle: twine_core::Angle` — Clockwise rotation around `pivot`.
- `scale_x: twine_core::Scale` — Horizontal scale (256 = 1×).
- `scale_y: twine_core::Scale` — Vertical scale (256 = 1×).
- `pivot: twine_core::Point` — Rotation / scale center, relative to the draw area's top-left corner.
- `blend_mode: twine_render::BlendMode` — Blend mode.
- `bitmap_mask: Option<twine_render::ImagePixels<'a>>` — Alpha mask (`A1`…`A8` or `L8`) placed at the draw area's top-left corner; pixels outside it are transparent.
Methods of `ImageDsc`:
- `pub fn is_transformed(&self) -> bool` — Whether the image is rotated or scaled (`angle` is taken modulo 360°).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default

#### fn twine_render::transformed_area
`pub fn transformed_area(area: twine_core::Rect, angle: twine_core::Angle, scale_x: twine_core::Scale, scale_y: twine_core::Scale, pivot: twine_core::Point) -> twine_core::Rect`
Bounding box of `area` rotated by `angle` and scaled by `scale_x`/`scale_y` around `pivot` (relative to `area`'s top-left corner), rounded outwards. Widgets use it to enlarge their drawing area for transformed images.

#### struct twine_render::ImagePixels<'a>
A borrowed block of decoded pixels.
Fields:
- `format: twine_core::ColorFormat` — Format of `data`.
- `w: u16` — Width in pixels.
- `h: u16` — Height in pixels.
- `stride: u16` — Bytes between rows of `data`.
- `data: &'a [u8]` — Pixel rows.
- `palette: Option<&'a [u8]>` — Palette of indexed formats (`Argb8888` entries).
- `alpha: Option<&'a [u8]>` — Alpha plane of `Rgb565A8` (`w` bytes per row).
- `premultiplied: bool` — The color channels are premultiplied by alpha (`Argb8888`, `Rgb565A8`). Implied by `ColorFormat::Argb8888Premultiplied`.
Methods of `ImagePixels`:
- `pub fn new(format: twine_core::ColorFormat, w: u16, h: u16, data: &'a [u8]) -> Self` — Packed rows of `format` (stride = `w · bpp / 8` rounded up).
- `pub fn from_parts(format: twine_core::ColorFormat, w: u16, h: u16, stride: u16, data: &'a [u8], palette: Option<&'a [u8]>, alpha: Option<&'a [u8]>, premultiplied: bool) -> Result<Self, twine_render::RenderError>` — Pixels described part by part, validated: the stride must hold a row, `data` must hold `h` rows, indexed formats need a palette of at least `palette_len` entries, and `Rgb565A8` needs `w · h` alpha bytes (in `alpha`, or after the main plane in `data`).
  Errors: `RenderError::InvalidArea` when `stride` is shorter than a row; `RenderError::BufferTooSmall` when `data`, the palette or the alpha plane is too short.
- `pub fn row(&self, y: u16) -> &'a [u8]` — Bytes of row `y` (up to `stride` bytes; empty when out of range or the data is short).
- `pub fn alpha_row(&self, y: u16) -> &'a [u8]` — The `w` alpha bytes of row `y` of an `Rgb565A8` image (empty for other formats, out of range rows or short data).
- `pub fn rect_at(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> twine_core::Rect` — The image rectangle when its top-left corner is at `(x, y)`.
- `pub fn texel(&self, x: u16, y: u16) -> u32` — Texel `(x, y)` as straight-alpha packed `0xAARRGGBB` (every format: palettes, alpha planes and premultiplied pixels are resolved; alpha-only formats give black with the texel's alpha). Outside the image, or when the data is short, the result is `0` (transparent).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### const twine_render::MAX_MASKS
`pub const MAX_MASKS: usize = 16`
Maximum number of simultaneously pushed masks.

#### enum twine_render::Mask<'a>
A coverage mask.
Variants:
- `Radius { area: twine_core::Rect, radius: i32, outer: bool }` — A rounded rectangle; `outer = false` keeps the inside, `true` the outside. The radius is clamped to half the shorter side and to 2^22 px (never panics).
- `Angle { center: twine_core::Point, start: twine_core::Angle, end: twine_core::Angle }` — Keeps the sector from `start` clockwise to `end` around the point `center` (the top-left corner of pixel `center`). Angles are clockwise from 3 o'clock; `end − start ≥ 360°` keeps everything, `start == end` nothing.
- `Line { p1: twine_core::Point, p2: twine_core::Point, side: twine_render::LineSide }` — Keeps one side of the infinite line through `p1` and `p2` (a direction longer than 2^23 px is clamped by scaling it down, which keeps the line and rounds its slope; never panics).
- `Fade { area: twine_core::Rect, y_top: i32, y_bottom: i32, opa_top: twine_core::Opa, opa_bottom: twine_core::Opa }` — Vertical fade inside `area` (pixels outside `area` are unchanged): rows above `y_top` get `opa_top`, rows below `y_bottom` get `opa_bottom`, rows in between are interpolated.
- `Map { area: twine_core::Rect, alpha: &'a [u8] }` — An 8-bit alpha map covering `area` (row stride = `area.width()`); pixels outside `area` become transparent.
Methods of `Mask`:
- `pub fn apply(&self, y: i32, x0: i32, cov: &mut [u8]) -> twine_render::MaskResult` — Multiplies the coverage of the span starting at `(x0, y)` in place.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_render::MaskId
Identifies a pushed mask for `Painter::pop_mask`.
Methods of `MaskId`:
- `const INVALID: twine_render::MaskId` — The id returned when the stack is full; popping it does nothing.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_render::MaskResult
What `Mask::apply` did to a span.
Variants:
- `Transparent` — The whole span is now 0 (callers skip it).
- `FullCover` — The span was left unchanged.
- `Changed` — Some values changed.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_render::MaskStack<'a>
A fixed-capacity stack of masks (no allocation).
Methods of `MaskStack`:
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether no mask is pushed.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of pushed masks.
- `pub fn push(&mut self, m: twine_render::Mask<'a>) -> Option<twine_render::MaskId>` — Pushes `m`; `None` when the stack is full.
- `pub fn pop(&mut self, id: twine_render::MaskId) -> bool` — Removes the mask `id` (unknown ids are ignored). Returns whether a mask was removed.
- `pub fn apply(&self, y: i32, x0: i32, cov: &mut [u8]) -> twine_render::MaskResult` — Applies every mask to the span; stops early when it becomes transparent. Returns `MaskResult::FullCover` if no mask changed anything.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default

#### const twine_render::ACCEL_MIN_PX
`pub const ACCEL_MIN_PX: u64 = 1024`
Smallest area (in pixels) handed to `DrawAccel` operations.

#### struct twine_render::Painter<'a>
Draws into a `DrawBuf` with a clip rectangle, a mask stack and an optional accelerator.
Methods of `Painter`:
- `pub fn arc(&mut self, center: twine_core::Point, radius: i32, start: twine_core::Angle, end: twine_core::Angle, dsc: &twine_render::ArcDsc<'_>)` — Draws an arc from `start` clockwise to `end` (angles clockwise from 3 o'clock). `start == end` draws nothing; `|end − start| ≥ 360°` draws the full ring. Radii above 2^22 px are clamped to 2^22 px. Never panics.
- `pub fn coverage_span(&mut self, y: i32, x0: i32, coverage: &[u8], src: &twine_render::SpanSource<'_>)` — Blends the coverage row `coverage` (one byte per pixel, 255 = fully covered) starting at screen `(x0, y)` with `src`, after clipping and applying the mask stack.
- `pub fn coverage_span_mode(&mut self, y: i32, x0: i32, coverage: &[u8], src: &twine_render::SpanSource<'_>, mode: twine_render::BlendMode)` — `coverage_span` with a blend mode.
- `pub fn glyph_a8(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, alpha: &[u8], stride: usize, color: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa)` — Blends an A8 coverage block in `color` at `opa`: `alpha` holds `area.width()` values per row with a row stride of `stride` bytes. Clipped, masked, never allocates.
- `pub fn glyph_lcd(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, cov: &[u8], stride: usize, color: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa, order: twine_render::SubpxOrder)` — Blends a subpixel (LCD) glyph: `cov` holds 3 coverage values per destination pixel (in `order`), `area.width() × 3` per row, row stride `stride`. Each channel is mixed separately: `dst.c = mix(color.c, dst.c, cov_c × opa / 255)`. `L8`, `I1` and `Argb8888` (layer) buffers use the average of the three values as ordinary coverage.
- `pub fn image(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, px: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, dsc: &twine_render::ImageDsc<'_>)` — Draws the image `px` into `area` with `dsc`.
- `pub fn layer(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, dsc: &twine_render::LayerDsc, f: impl FnMut(&mut twine_render::Painter<'_>))` — Renders `f` into an `Argb8888` layer and composites it with `dsc`. `f` draws in screen coordinates and may be called several times (once per strip) for large layers.
- `pub fn line(&mut self, p1: twine_core::Point, p2: twine_core::Point, dsc: &twine_render::LineDsc)` — Draws a line from `p1` to `p2`. Widths above 2^22 px are clamped to 2^22 px; any `i32` end points are accepted. Never panics.
- `pub fn polyline(&mut self, pts: &[twine_core::Point], dsc: &twine_render::LineDsc)` — Draws connected segments. Interior vertices get a round join when `width > 2` and a round cap is requested. Overlapping parts of translucent polylines are blended twice; wrap the call in `Painter::layer` for an exact result.
- `pub fn new(buf: twine_render::DrawBuf<'a>, caches: &'a mut twine_render::RenderCaches) -> Self` — A painter over `buf` whose clip is the buffer's area.
- `pub fn with_accel(self, accel: &'a mut dyn twine_render::DrawAccel) -> Self` — Uses `accel` for the operations it supports.
- `pub fn clip(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The current clip rectangle (may be empty).
- `pub fn layer_available(&self) -> bool` — Whether `layer` would render into the layer buffer now: `false` inside another layer's content (the buffer is in use) or without a layer buffer, where `layer` draws its content directly, without opacity, blend mode or transform. Lets a recursive caller skip the layer set-up for such nested layers. Never panics.
- `pub fn with_clip<R>(&mut self, clip: twine_core::Rect, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` with the clip intersected with `clip`, then restores the previous clip.
- `pub fn buf(&self) -> &twine_render::DrawBuf<'a>` — The draw buffer. Call `sync_accel` before reading pixels if an accelerator may still be working.
- `pub fn buf_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_render::DrawBuf<'a>` — The draw buffer, mutably (waits for queued accelerator work first).
- `pub fn caches(&mut self) -> &mut twine_render::RenderCaches` — The caches.
- `pub fn sync_accel(&mut self)` — Waits for queued accelerator operations (called before every software write).
- `pub fn touched_area(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — Union of all areas drawn since the painter was created (`None` if nothing was drawn).
- `pub fn push_mask(&mut self, m: twine_render::Mask<'a>) -> twine_render::MaskId` — Pushes a mask applied to everything drawn until it is popped. When the stack is full (`MAX_MASKS`) a warning is logged and `MaskId::INVALID` returned.
- `pub fn pop_mask(&mut self, id: twine_render::MaskId)` — Removes a mask pushed with `push_mask` (unknown ids are ignored).
- `pub fn has_masks(&self) -> bool` — Whether masks are active.
- `pub fn fill(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, color: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa)` — Fills `area` with `color` at `opa` (clipped, masked). Large unmasked fills use the accelerator when one is set and supports it.
- `pub fn fill_mode(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, color: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa, mode: twine_render::BlendMode)` — `fill` with a blend mode.
- `pub fn triangle(&mut self, pts: [twine_core::Point; 3], dsc: &twine_render::TriangleDsc<'_>)` — Fills a triangle (collinear points draw nothing).
- `pub fn polygon(&mut self, pts: &[twine_core::Point], dsc: &twine_render::PolygonDsc<'_>)` — Fills a polygon with the non-zero rule.
- `pub fn polygon_with_rule(&mut self, pts: &[twine_core::Point], rule: twine_render::FillRule, dsc: &twine_render::PolygonDsc<'_>)` — Fills a polygon with the given fill rule.
- `pub fn rect(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, dsc: &twine_render::RectDsc<'_>)` — Draws a rectangle: shadow, background (color or gradient), border (unless `border_post`), outline — in this order, like LVGL.
- `pub fn rect_border_post(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, dsc: &twine_render::RectDsc<'_>)` — Draws only the border of `dsc` (for `border_post`: the engine calls this after the children).
- `pub fn fill_gradient(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, grad: &twine_render::Gradient, opa: twine_core::Opa)` — Fills `area` with a gradient (geometry relative to `area`).
- `pub fn blit(&mut self, pos: twine_core::Point, src: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, opa: twine_core::Opa, blend_mode: twine_render::BlendMode)` — Draws `src` with its top-left corner at `pos` (no transform). Same-format opaque copies use `copy_from_slice`; unmasked, fully visible normal blits try the accelerator first.
- `pub fn blit_recolor(&mut self, pos: twine_core::Point, src: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, opa: twine_core::Opa, blend_mode: twine_render::BlendMode, rc: Option<(twine_core::Color, twine_core::Opa)>)` — `blit` with an optional recolor.
- `pub fn blit_transformed(&mut self, src: &twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>, dsc: &twine_render::BlitDsc)` — Draws `src` mapped by `dsc.transform` (source pixel coordinates → screen). A singular transform draws nothing.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### fn twine_render::convert_l8_to_i1
`pub fn convert_l8_to_i1(src: &[u8], dst: &mut [u8], w: usize, h: usize) -> Result<(), twine_render::RenderError>`
Converts a `w × h` block of 8-bit luminance (`src`, stride `w`) into packed 1-bit pixels (`dst`, MSB first, stride `⌈w / 8⌉`): a pixel is 1 (white) when its luminance is ≥ 128, the same threshold the renderer uses when blending into `I1` buffers. Padding bits of the last byte of a row are 0.
Errors: `RenderError::BufferTooSmall` when `src` or `dst` cannot hold the block.

#### fn twine_render::rotate_area
`pub fn rotate_area(area: twine_core::Rect, panel: twine_core::Size, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> twine_core::Rect`
Where a logical `area` lands on a panel whose logical size is `panel` (the size before rotation, i.e. as the application sees it) — the same mapping as `Rect::rotate_in`.

#### fn twine_render::rotate_buffer
`pub fn rotate_buffer(src: &[u8], src_stride: usize, dst: &mut [u8], dst_stride: usize, w: usize, h: usize, rotation: twine_core::Rotation, bytes_per_px: usize) -> Result<(), twine_render::RenderError>`
Rotates a `w × h` pixel block (`bytes_per_px` ∈ 1..=4) from `src` into `dst`. For 90° and 270° the destination block is `h × w`. The pixel mapping is the one of `Rect::rotate_in` (and `rotate_area`): 90° maps `(x, y)` to `(y, w − 1 − x)`.
Errors: `RenderError::UnsupportedFormat` for `bytes_per_px` outside `1..=4`; `RenderError::InvalidArea` for a stride shorter than a row; `RenderError::BufferTooSmall` when `src` or `dst` cannot hold the block. An empty block is `Ok` and copies nothing.

- `ofs_y: i32` — Vertical offset.
- `spread: i32` — Growth of the shape (negative shrinks).
- `color: twine_core::Color` — Shadow color.
- `opa: twine_core::Opa` — Shadow opacity.
Methods of `ShadowDsc`:

Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### fn twine_render::shadow_ext_size
`pub fn shadow_ext_size(dsc: &twine_render::ShadowDsc) -> i32`
How far a shadow can reach outside its object (for the engine's extra draw area): `width / 2 + max(|ofs_x|, |ofs_y|) + spread` (never negative).

#### struct twine_render::BlitDsc

Fields:

- `opa: twine_core::Opa` — Overall opacity.
- `antialias: bool` — Bilinear filtering (else nearest neighbour).
- `blend_mode: twine_render::BlendMode` — Blend mode.
- `recolor: Option<(twine_core::Color, twine_core::Opa)>` — Mixes sampled colors towards this color by this opacity. Alpha-only sources (`A1`…`A8`) are black unless recolored.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default

## crate twine_text

Documented with features: `std,ttf,bidi,arabic-shaping`.

**twine-text**

Fonts, text layout and text drawing for the Twine GUI library (layer 3, above the renderer).

- **Fonts.** A `Font` holds line metrics, a `GlyphProvider` and an optional fallback
  font. The built-in provider is `BitmapFont`, a bitmap format with the same capabilities
  and semantics as LVGL's `lv_font_fmt_txt` (LVGL `src/font/lv_font_fmt_txt.h`): 1/2/4/8
  bits per pixel (a typed `Bpp`, so no other depth can reach the glyph readers), four
  cmap kinds, pair and class kerning, optional RLE compression with an XOR row prefilter,
  and subpixel (`Subpx`) glyphs, and per-font text gamma (`TextGamma`).
  Ready-made fonts (Montserrat with Font Awesome
  `Symbol`s, unscii) live in the `twine-assets` crate; applications generate their own
  from TrueType/OpenType files with the `twine-build` crate in `build.rs` (subset to the
  characters of their translations and string literals), the `include_font!` macro of the
  `twine` facade, or the `twine font` command (`twine-cli`).
- **Glyph cache.** `GlyphCache` keeps decoded glyphs of compressed fonts in a fixed byte
  budget (LRU) and owns the scratch memory of text drawing, so drawing never allocates.
- **Layout.** `TextLayout` breaks text into lines (LVGL rules), measures it, aligns lines,
  ellipsizes and hit-tests (`TextLayout::char_at` / `TextLayout::pos_of`).
- **Drawing.** `draw_text` draws text through a `Painter` with
  letter/line spacing, alignment, underline, strikethrough, selection, ellipsis and
  subpixel fonts, processing only the lines inside the clip.
- **Text gamma.** Stored coverage becomes opacity through the font's `TextGamma`: one
  16-entry table per `Polarity` (dark-on-light, light-on-dark), picked once per text run
  from the text and background colors (the engine passes the surface behind each text),
  so thin light-on-dark text keeps its weight at no
  per-pixel cost (module `gamma`).

All metrics are integers: glyph advances are stored in 1/16 px and rounded **per glyph** to
whole pixels exactly like LVGL (`(adv + 8) >> 4`), so layout and rendering are identical on
every target. The crate is `no_std` + `alloc` and float-free.

**Example**

```rust
use twine_assets::fonts::MONTSERRAT_14;
use twine_core::{Color, ColorFormat, Point, Rect};
use twine_render::{DrawBuf, Painter, RenderCaches};
use twine_text::{GlyphCache, TextAlign, TextDecor, TextDsc, TextLayout, draw_text};

// Measure and hit-test.
let mut layout = TextLayout::new("Hello wide world", &MONTSERRAT_14);
layout.max_width = 60;
assert_eq!(layout.line_count(), 3);
let cursor = layout.pos_of(6, TextAlign::Left, 60); // before "wide"
assert_eq!(cursor.y, i32::from(MONTSERRAT_14.line_height));
assert_eq!(layout.char_at(cursor, TextAlign::Left, 60), 6);

// Draw (once per frame / chunk; the caches are created once).
let mut caches = RenderCaches::default();
let mut glyphs = GlyphCache::default();
let mut px = vec![0u8; 120 * 40 * 2];
let area = Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 120, 40);
let buf = DrawBuf::new_packed(&mut px, ColorFormat::Rgb565, area).unwrap();
let mut painter = Painter::new(buf, &mut caches);
let mut dsc = TextDsc::new(&MONTSERRAT_14);
dsc.color = Color::WHITE;
dsc.align = TextAlign::Center;
dsc.decor = TextDecor::UNDERLINE;
draw_text(&mut painter, area, "Hello", &dsc, &mut glyphs);
```

**Bitmap format**

Plain bitmaps are bit-packed rows without padding (MSB first); compressed bitmaps use LVGL's
RLE scheme with an optional XOR prefilter. The bit-level format is documented in the
`decode` module source, and the encoder (feature `std`, module `encode`) is its exact
inverse.

**Features**

`std` (std conveniences and the `encode` module used by font generators), `log` / `defmt`
(logging backend, target `"twine::text"`).

`safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
`docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints; it refuses `ttf` (a
floating-point rasterizer); implies `display-integrity`.

`display-integrity`: `GlyphCache::set_fresh` (every glyph decoded again), for the engine's
display-integrity mechanisms; off, glyph lookups pay no fresh-mode test.

#### fn twine_text::mirror
`pub const fn mirror(c: char) -> char`
The mirrored form of a bracket drawn inside a right-to-left run (`(` ↔ `)`, `[` ↔ `]`, `{` ↔ `}`, `<` ↔ `>`, `«` ↔ `»`); other characters are returned unchanged.

#### fn twine_text::resolve_dir

#### struct twine_text::BitmapFont
A bitmap font (LVGL `lv_font_fmt_txt_dsc_t`), normally generated by the font generator.
Fields:
- `bpp: twine_text::Bpp` — Bit depth of every glyph's coverage values.
- `bitmap: &'static [u8]` — All glyph bitmaps.
- `glyphs: &'static [twine_text::GlyphDsc]` — Glyph descriptors indexed by glyph id (entry 0 is the reserved empty glyph).
- `cmaps: &'static [twine_text::Cmap]` — Code point → glyph id maps, searched in order.
- `kern: twine_text::Kern` — Kerning.
- `kern_scale: u16` — Kerning scale in 12.4 fixed point (16 = 1.0).
- `format: twine_text::BitmapFormat` — Bitmap storage format.
- `gamma: &'static twine_text::TextGamma` — Coverage → opacity curves, one per `Polarity` (see `gamma`): `gamma::DEFAULT` for generated fonts, `gamma::LINEAR` for LVGL's mapping.
Methods of `BitmapFont`:
- `pub fn glyph_id(&self, cp: char) -> Option<u16>` — The glyph id of `cp` (`None` when missing).
- `pub fn kern(&self, left: u16, right: u16) -> i32` — Raw kerning value between two glyph ids in 1/16 px, `kern_scale` applied (`(value × kern_scale) >> 4`, arithmetic shift).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, GlyphProvider

#### enum twine_text::BitmapFormat
How glyph bitmaps are stored.
Variants:
- `Plain` — Bit-packed rows without padding.
- `Compressed` — LVGL RLE with the XOR row prefilter.
- `CompressedNoPrefilter` — LVGL RLE without the prefilter.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_text::Cmap
A code point range mapped to glyph ids (LVGL `lv_font_fmt_txt_cmap_t`).
Fields:
- `range_start: u32` — First code point of the range.
- `range_length: u16` — Number of code points in the range.
- `glyph_id_start: u16` — Glyph id of the first mapped code point.
- `unicode_list: &'static [u16]` — Sorted code points relative to `range_start` (sparse kinds).
- `glyph_id_ofs_list: twine_text::GlyphIdOfs` — Glyph id offsets (full kinds).
- `kind: twine_text::CmapKind` — Mapping kind.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_text::CmapKind
How a `Cmap` maps code points to glyph ids (LVGL `lv_font_fmt_txt_cmap_type_t`).
Variants:
- `Format0Tiny` — Contiguous range: `glyph_id_start + rcp`.
- `Format0Full` — Contiguous range with a per-code-point `u8` offset list; offset 0 (other than for the range's first code point) means "missing".
- `SparseTiny` — Sparse code points (`unicode_list`, sorted): `glyph_id_start + index`.
- `SparseFull` — Sparse code points with a `u16` offset list: `glyph_id_start + glyph_id_ofs_list[index]`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_text::GlyphDsc
Metrics and bitmap location of one glyph (LVGL `lv_font_fmt_txt_glyph_dsc_t`).
Fields:
- `bitmap_index: u32` — Byte offset of the glyph's bitmap in `BitmapFont::bitmap`.
- `adv_w: u16` — Advance width in 1/16 px.
- `box_w: u8` — Bitmap width in px (subpixels for horizontal subpixel fonts).
- `box_h: u8` — Bitmap height in px (subpixels for vertical subpixel fonts).
- `ofs_x: i8` — Offset of the bitmap's left edge from the pen position.
- `ofs_y: i8` — Offset of the bitmap's bottom edge above the baseline.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_text::BLOCK_BYTES

#### struct twine_text::CacheStats
Statistics of a `GlyphCache`.

- `misses: u64` — Lookups that did not.
- `evictions: u64` — Entries evicted to make room.
- `bytes_used: usize` — Bytes of the arena currently occupied (whole blocks).
- `glyph_renders: u64` — Glyph bitmaps drawn by the text renderer (cached or not).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### const twine_text::DEFAULT_BUDGET
`pub const DEFAULT_BUDGET: usize`
Default budget (`EngineConfig::glyph_cache_bytes`).

#### struct twine_text::GlyphCache
LRU cache of decoded glyphs and the scratch buffers of the text renderer.
Methods of `GlyphCache`:
- `pub fn new(budget_bytes: usize) -> Self` — A cache of `budget_bytes` (rounded down to whole 64-byte blocks; 0 disables caching).
- `pub fn budget(&self) -> usize` — The arena size in bytes (0 when caching is disabled).
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes the cache reserves: the glyph arena and its block map, the entry table and the text renderer's scratch rows (by capacity; the glyph scratch grows once to the largest glyph drawn). Allocates nothing; never panics; O(1).
- `pub fn is_enabled(&self) -> bool` — Whether glyphs can be cached at all.
- `pub fn stats(&self) -> twine_text::CacheStats` — The statistics.
- `pub fn reset_stats(&mut self)` — Resets the statistics counters (not the contents).
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of cached glyphs.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether no glyph is cached.
- `pub fn get(&mut self, key: twine_text::GlyphKey) -> Option<&[u8]>` — The cached bitmap of `key` (marks it most recently used), counting a hit or a miss. Always a miss in fresh mode (`set_fresh`, feature `display-integrity`).
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, key: twine_text::GlyphKey, w: usize, h: usize) -> Option<&mut [u8]>` — Reserves space for a `w × h` bitmap of `key` (replacing an existing entry), evicting least recently used entries until it fits. Returns the zeroed-length-exact slot to fill, or `None` when caching is disabled or the glyph alone exceeds the budget (the caller then decodes into its own buffer).
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, key: twine_text::GlyphKey)` — Removes the entry of `key` (if cached).
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every entry (statistics are kept).
- `pub fn take_glyph_scratch(&mut self, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` — Takes the glyph scratch buffer out, sized to exactly `len` bytes (grown once if needed). `None` (with a warning) above `MAX_GLYPH_BYTES`. Return it with `put_glyph_scratch`.
- `pub fn put_glyph_scratch(&mut self, buf: Vec<u8>)` — Returns the buffer taken with `take_glyph_scratch`.
- `pub fn first_warning(&mut self, key: twine_text::GlyphKey) -> bool` — Records `key` (e.g. `(provider key, code point)`) in the "already warned" set; `true` if it was not there yet, i.e. the caller should log. Used to warn once per missing glyph or corrupt font. After `WARN_CAP` distinct keys the set is full: one last "further warnings suppressed" message is logged and every later call returns `false`.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### type twine_text::GlyphKey
`pub type GlyphKey = (usize, u32)`
Cache key: `(provider address, glyph id)`.

#### const twine_text::MAX_ENTRIES
`pub const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 256`
Maximum number of cached glyphs.

#### const twine_text::MAX_GLYPH_BYTES
`pub const MAX_GLYPH_BYTES: usize`
Largest glyph (in coverage bytes) the glyph scratch buffer grows to.

#### const twine_text::MAX_ROW
`pub const MAX_ROW: usize = 255`
Width of the row scratch buffers: the widest glyph row (in coverage values) that is decoded row by row.

#### const twine_text::WARN_CAP
`pub const WARN_CAP: usize = 32`
Capacity of the "already warned" set for missing glyphs and corrupt fonts; once it is full, no further such warnings are logged.

#### enum twine_text::Bpp
The bit depth of a bitmap font's coverage values (LVGL `bpp`): 1, 2, 4 or 8 bits per pixel.
Variants:
- `One = 1` — 1 bit per pixel: on or off.
- `Two = 2` — 2 bits per pixel: 4 coverage levels.
- `Four = 4` — 4 bits per pixel: 16 coverage levels (the default).
- `Eight = 8` — 8 bits per pixel: 256 coverage levels.
Methods of `Bpp`:
- `const ALL: [twine_text::Bpp; 4]` — Every depth, from 1 to 8 bits.
- `pub const fn new(bits: u8) -> Option<twine_text::Bpp>` — The depth of `bits` bits per pixel, or `None` unless `bits` is 1, 2, 4 or 8.
- `pub const fn bits(self) -> u8` — The number of bits per pixel: 1, 2, 4 or 8.
- `pub const fn max_value(self) -> u8` — The largest coverage value of this depth (`2^bits − 1`: 1, 3, 15 or 255).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

#### enum twine_text::TextDir
Base direction of text (LVGL `lv_base_dir_t` subset; widgets map the style's base direction to it).
Variants:
- `Ltr` — Left to right.
- `Rtl` — Right to left.
- `Auto` — From the first strong character (feature `bidi`; left to right without it).
Methods of `TextDir`:
- `pub fn resolved(self, text: &str) -> twine_text::TextDir` — The direction `text` is laid out in: `TextDir::Auto` detects it from the first strong character with the `bidi` feature and means left to right without it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_text::TextDrawFlags
Layout flags of a `TextDsc`.
Methods of `TextDrawFlags`:
- `const EXPAND: Self` — No wrapping: only newlines break lines.
- `const BREAK_ALL: Self` — Lines may break between any two characters.
- `pub const fn empty() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all bits unset.
- `pub const fn all() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all known bits set.
- `pub const fn bits(&self) -> u8` — Get the underlying bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Option<Self>` — Convert from a bits value.
- `pub const fn from_bits_truncate(bits: u8) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value, unsetting any unknown bits.
- `pub const fn from_bits_retain(bits: u8) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value exactly.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self>` — Get a flags value with the bits of a flag with the given name set.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether all bits in `self` are unset.
- `pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool` — Whether all known bits in this flags value are set.
- `pub const fn intersects(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether any set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub const fn contains(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, other: Self)` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, other: Self, value: bool)` — Call `insert` when `value` is `true` or `remove` when `value` is `false`.
- `pub const fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise and (`&`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub const fn symmetric_difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn complement(self) -> Self` — The bitwise negation (`!`) of the bits in `self`, truncating the result.
- `pub const fn iter(&self) -> bitflags::iter::Iter<twine_text::TextDrawFlags>` — Yield a set of contained flags values.
- `pub const fn iter_names(&self) -> bitflags::iter::IterNames<twine_text::TextDrawFlags>` — Yield a set of contained named flags values.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Flags, PublicFlags, Binary, Octal, LowerHex, UpperHex, BitOr, BitOrAssign, BitXor, BitXorAssign, BitAnd, BitAndAssign, Sub, SubAssign, Not, Extend<twine_text::TextDrawFlags>, FromIterator<twine_text::TextDrawFlags>, IntoIterator

#### struct twine_text::TextDsc
How to draw a text (LVGL `lv_draw_label_dsc_t`).
Fields:
- `font: &'static twine_text::Font` — The font (its fallback chain is used for missing characters).
- `color: twine_core::Color` — Text color.
- `background: Option<twine_core::Color>` — The color the text is drawn over, when the caller knows it (default `None`): with `color` it decides the run's `Polarity`, which picks the font's text gamma curve (`Polarity::of`). Without it the text color alone decides (light text is taken to be on a dark background). Widgets drawing through the engine get it filled in: `twine_engine::DrawCx::text_dsc` sets the nearest opaque background behind the text. Selected characters use `sel_color` over `sel_bg_color`.
- `opa: twine_core::Opa` — Opacity of everything drawn.
- `align: twine_text::TextAlign` — Line alignment inside the area.
- `decor: twine_text::TextDecor` — Underline / strikethrough.
- `letter_space: i32` — Extra space after each glyph.
- `line_space: i32` — Extra space between lines.
- `sel_start: Option<usize>` — Selection start (byte index; with `sel_end`, the order does not matter).
- `sel_end: Option<usize>` — Selection end (exclusive).
- `sel_color: twine_core::Color` — Text color of selected characters.
- `sel_bg_color: twine_core::Color` — Background of selected characters.
- `flags: twine_text::TextDrawFlags` — Layout flags.
- `ellipsis_lines: Option<usize>` — Draw at most this many lines; the last one ends with `"..."` when text is cut.
- `ofs: twine_core::Point` — Offset of the text inside the area (scrolling long modes).
- `subpx_order: twine_render::SubpxOrder` — Subpixel order of the panel (used by subpixel fonts).
- `base_dir: twine_text::TextDir` — Base direction: resolves `TextAlign::Auto` and, with the `bidi` feature, orders mixed-direction lines visually (`TextDir::Auto` detects it from the text; without `bidi` it means left to right).
Methods of `TextDsc`:
- `pub fn new(font: &'static twine_text::Font) -> Self` — Black, opaque, left-aligned text without decorations, spacing or selection, over an unknown background.
- `pub fn layout<'a>(&self, text: &'a str, width: i32) -> twine_text::TextLayout<'a>` — The layout this descriptor gives `text` in an area `width` px wide.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### fn twine_text::draw_text
`pub fn draw_text(p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, text: &str, dsc: &twine_text::TextDsc, cache: &mut twine_text::GlyphCache)`
Draws `text` into `area` (clipped to it) with `dsc`.

#### static twine_text::EMPTY_FONT
`pub static EMPTY_FONT: twine_text::Font`
A font without glyphs and with zero line height: the style default when no theme font is supplied. Every character is drawn as a (tiny) replacement box.

#### struct twine_text::Font
A font: line metrics plus a `GlyphProvider` and an optional fallback font.
Fields:
- `line_height: i16` — Height of one line in px.
- `base_line: i16` — Distance of the baseline from the bottom of the line in px.
- `underline_position: i8` — Underline position relative to the baseline (negative = below the baseline).
- `underline_thickness: u8` — Underline thickness in px (0 is drawn as 1).
- `provider: &'static dyn twine_text::GlyphProvider` — Glyph metrics and bitmaps.
- `fallback: Option<&'static twine_text::Font>` — Font consulted for characters the provider lacks.
- `subpx: twine_text::Subpx` — Subpixel layout of the glyph bitmaps.
Methods of `Font`:
- `pub fn glyph(&'static self, cp: char, next: Option<char>) -> Option<(&'static twine_text::Font, twine_text::GlyphInfo)>` — Resolves `cp` through this font, then its fallback chain; returns the font that has it and the glyph's metrics.
- `pub fn advance_px(&'static self, cp: char, next: Option<char>) -> i32` — Advance of `cp` in whole pixels (LVGL rounding), including kerning with `next`.
- `pub const fn ascent(&self) -> i32` — Distance from the top of a line to the baseline: `line_height - base_line`.
- `pub const fn placeholder_width(&self) -> i32` — Width of the replacement box drawn for missing characters: `line_height / 2`.
- `pub fn provider_key(&self) -> usize` — The glyph provider's address, used as the glyph-cache key of this font's provider.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_text::GlyphInfo
Metrics of one glyph, as returned by `GlyphProvider::glyph_info`.
Fields:
- `adv_w: u16` — Advance width in 1/16 px, kerning with the next character included.
- `box_w: u16` — Bitmap width in px (in subpixels for `Subpx::Hor` fonts).
- `box_h: u16` — Bitmap height in px (in subpixels for `Subpx::Ver` fonts).
- `ofs_x: i16` — Horizontal offset of the bitmap from the pen position.
- `ofs_y: i16` — Vertical offset of the bitmap's bottom edge above the baseline.
- `bpp: Option<twine_text::Bpp>` — Bit depth of the stored coverage bitmap, or `None` for an image glyph drawn from `GlyphProvider::glyph_image` (image fonts, LVGL `imgfont`).
- `id: u32` — Provider-specific glyph id (the glyph index for `BitmapFont`).
- `is_placeholder: bool` — `true` for a replacement glyph drawn when a character is missing.
Methods of `GlyphInfo`:
- `pub const fn advance_px(&self) -> i32` — The advance in whole pixels, rounded like LVGL: `(adv_w + 8) >> 4`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_text::GlyphProvider
`pub trait GlyphProvider: Sync`
Source of glyph metrics and coverage bitmaps: a `BitmapFont`, a runtime TrueType font (feature `ttf`) or an `ImageFontProvider`.
Items:
- `fn glyph_info(&self, cp: char, next: Option<char>) -> Option<twine_text::GlyphInfo>` — Metrics of `cp`, with kerning against `next` included in `adv_w` (only when `next` is also provided by this provider). `None` when the character is missing: the caller then tries the font's fallback and finally draws a replacement box.
- `fn render_a8(&self, info: &twine_text::GlyphInfo, polarity: twine_text::Polarity, out: &mut [u8], cache: &mut twine_text::GlyphCache) -> bool` — Writes the glyph's A8 opacity (`box_w × box_h`, stride `box_w`) into `out`: its coverage mapped through the provider's text gamma for `polarity` (see `gamma`; providers without gamma tables, such as 8-bit run-time TrueType glyphs, ignore it).
- `fn render_rows(&self, info: &twine_text::GlyphInfo, polarity: twine_text::Polarity, cache: &mut twine_text::GlyphCache, sink: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, &[u8])) -> bool (provided)` — Streams the glyph's A8 opacity row by row to `sink(row_index, row)` (each row `box_w` bytes; `polarity` as for `render_a8`). Returns `false` if the glyph could not be decoded.
- `fn glyph_image(&self, cp: char, next: Option<char>) -> Option<&'static twine_render::ImagePixels<'static>> (provided)` — The image of an image glyph (one whose `GlyphInfo::bpp` is 0), drawn instead of A8 coverage. `cp` and `next` are the arguments `glyph_info` was called with. The default (coverage-only providers) returns `None`.
Implemented by: twine_text::BitmapFont, twine_text::ImageFontProvider, twine_text::TtfProvider

#### const twine_text::MAX_FALLBACK_DEPTH
`pub const MAX_FALLBACK_DEPTH: usize = 8`
Maximum number of fonts consulted for one character (the font plus 7 fallbacks). Longer chains are assumed to be cycles: they are cut and logged once.

#### enum twine_text::Subpx
Subpixel rendering of a font's glyphs (LVGL `lv_font_subpx_t`).
Variants:
- `None` — Ordinary grayscale anti-aliasing.
- `Hor` — Horizontal subpixels (R, G, B side by side): glyph boxes are three times as wide.
- `Ver` — Vertical subpixels (R, G, B stacked): glyph boxes are three times as tall.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### fn twine_text::has_placeholder
`pub const fn has_placeholder(cp: char) -> bool`
Whether a character missing from every font is drawn as a replacement box (LVGL rule): not for control characters (below U+0020), U+F8FF (`Symbol::Dummy`) and U+200C (zero-width non-joiner), which stay invisible and take no space.

#### fn twine_text::provider_key
`pub fn provider_key(p: &dyn twine_text::GlyphProvider) -> usize`
Glyph-cache key of a provider: its address.

#### struct twine_text::GammaRamp
Coverage → opacity tables of one curve, for 2 and 4 bpp glyphs (1 bpp maps to `0, 255`, 8 bpp is used as stored).
Methods of `GammaRamp`:
- `const LINEAR: twine_text::GammaRamp` — LVGL's linear mapping: 4 bpp `v × 17`, 2 bpp `v × 85`.
- `pub const fn new(a4: [u8; 16]) -> twine_text::GammaRamp` — The ramp of the 4 bpp table `a4` (opacity of each coverage level `0..=15`); the 2 bpp table is `[a4[0], a4[5], a4[10], a4[15]]`.
- `pub const fn table4(&self) -> &[u8; 16]` — The 4 bpp table: opacity of coverage level `v` (`0..=15`).
- `pub const fn table2(&self) -> &[u8; 4]` — The 2 bpp table: opacity of coverage level `v` (`0..=3`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_text::Polarity
Which way a text run's contrast goes: the input of the gamma choice (see the module docs).
Variants:
- `DarkOnLight` — Text darker than its background (the usual light theme).
- `LightOnDark` — Text lighter than its background (dark themes, text on filled buttons).
Methods of `Polarity`:
- `pub const fn of(text: twine_core::Color, background: Option<twine_core::Color>) -> twine_text::Polarity` — The polarity of `text` drawn over `background`: `LightOnDark` when the text is brighter (`Color::luminance`). Without a known background the text alone decides: light text (luminance ≥ 128) is taken to be drawn on a dark background.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_text::Line

#### struct twine_text::TextFlags
Line-breaking flags.

- `pub const fn all() -> Self` — Get a flags value with all known bits set.
- `pub const fn bits(&self) -> u8` — Get the underlying bits value.

- `pub const fn from_bits_retain(bits: u8) -> Self` — Convert from a bits value exactly.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self>` — Get a flags value with the bits of a flag with the given name set.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether all bits in `self` are unset.
- `pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool` — Whether all known bits in this flags value are set.

- `pub const fn contains(&self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all set bits in `other` are also set in `self`.

- `pub fn remove(&mut self, other: Self)` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub fn toggle(&mut self, other: Self)` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub fn set(&mut self, other: Self, value: bool)` — Call `insert` when `value` is `true` or `remove` when `value` is `false`.
- `pub const fn intersection(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise and (`&`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise or (`|`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The intersection of `self` with the complement of `other` (`&!`).
- `pub const fn symmetric_difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — The bitwise exclusive-or (`^`) of the bits in `self` and `other`.
- `pub const fn complement(self) -> Self` — The bitwise negation (`!`) of the bits in `self`, truncating the result.
- `pub const fn iter(&self) -> bitflags::iter::Iter<twine_text::TextFlags>` — Yield a set of contained flags values.
- `pub const fn iter_names(&self) -> bitflags::iter::IterNames<twine_text::TextFlags>` — Yield a set of contained named flags values.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Flags, PublicFlags, Binary, Octal, LowerHex, UpperHex, BitOr, BitOrAssign, BitXor, BitXorAssign, BitAnd, BitAndAssign, Sub, SubAssign, Not, Extend<twine_text::TextFlags>, FromIterator<twine_text::TextFlags>, IntoIterator

#### struct twine_text::TextLayout<'a>
Text plus the parameters that determine its layout.
Fields:
- `text: &'a str` — The UTF-8 text.
- `font: &'static twine_text::Font` — The font.
- `letter_space: i32` — Extra space after every glyph (px, may be negative).
- `line_space: i32` — Extra space between lines (px, may be negative).
- `max_width: i32` — Width available for a line (ignored with `TextFlags::EXPAND`).
- `flags: twine_text::TextFlags` — Breaking flags.
Methods of `TextLayout`:
- `pub fn pos_of_bidi(&self, byte_index: usize, align: twine_text::TextAlign, area_w: i32, base: twine_text::TextDir) -> twine_core::Point` — Like `pos_of` for bidirectional text laid out with base direction `base`: the cursor before logical byte `byte_index` is at the left edge of its glyph in an LTR run and at the right edge in an RTL run; the end of a line is at the line's right end (LTR base) or left end (RTL base). `TextAlign::Auto` follows the base.
- `pub fn char_at_bidi(&self, p: twine_core::Point, align: twine_text::TextAlign, area_w: i32, base: twine_text::TextDir) -> usize` — Like `char_at` for bidirectional text: the logical byte index of the cursor position closest to `p` (inside an RTL glyph, the left half is after the character and the right half before it).
- `pub fn line_x(&self, line: &twine_text::Line, area_w: i32, align: twine_text::TextAlign) -> i32` — X of `line`'s left edge in an area `area_w` wide. Left: 0, Center: `(area_w − width).div_euclid(2)`, Right: `area_w − width`. Like LVGL, the result is not clamped: it is negative when the line is wider than the area.
- `pub fn dots_width(&self) -> i32` — Width of `"..."` (letter spacing included).
- `pub fn ellipsize(&self, max_lines: usize) -> Option<twine_text::Ellipsis>` — If the text needs more than `max_lines` lines (at least 1), the last visible line keeps its longest prefix for which `width(prefix) + letter_space + width("...") ≤ max_width`, without trailing spaces. `None` when the text fits.
- `pub fn line_of(&self, byte_index: usize) -> usize` — Index of the line containing byte `byte_index` (rounded down to a char boundary). An index at the end of a wrapped line belongs to the next line; one inside a line's newline belongs to that line.
- `pub fn char_at(&self, p: twine_core::Point, align: twine_text::TextAlign, area_w: i32) -> usize` — Byte index of the char boundary closest to `p` (relative to the area's top-left): the line is chosen by `y` (clamped to the first/last line), then the glyphs are walked; past a glyph's midpoint the boundary after it is returned.
- `pub fn pos_of(&self, byte_index: usize, align: twine_text::TextAlign, area_w: i32) -> twine_core::Point` — Top-left of the cursor before byte `byte_index` (rounded down to a char boundary): the start x of that glyph, or the line's end x at the end of a line.
- `pub fn new(text: &'a str, font: &'static twine_text::Font) -> Self` — A layout of `text` in `font` with no letter/line spacing, unlimited width and no flags.
- `pub fn lines(&self) -> twine_text::LineIter<'_, 'a>` — The lines (always at least one; an empty text is one empty line).
- `pub fn line_width(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> i32` — Width of the slice `range` laid out on one line (kerning against the character after the slice included). Indices are rounded down to char boundaries.
- `pub fn measure(&self) -> twine_core::Size` — Size of the laid-out text: the widest line and the total height (`n × line_height + (n − 1) × line_space`).
- `pub fn line_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of lines (≥ 1).
- `pub fn line_height(&self) -> i32` — Distance between the tops of two lines: `line_height + line_space`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

### mod twine_text::gamma

Text gamma: how a glyph's stored coverage becomes opacity, chosen per text run by polarity.

Blending anti-aliased coverage linearly in the panel's (sRGB-like) color space makes
partially covered pixels look lighter than their coverage: dark text on a light background
keeps its weight, light text on a dark background reads thin. A `TextGamma` holds one
coverage → opacity table per `Polarity`; `draw_text` picks the
polarity once per run from the text and background colors (`Polarity::of`) and the glyph
decoder maps each stored value through the table **instead of** the fixed LVGL expansion
(4 bpp `v × 17`, 2 bpp `v × 85`). The per-pixel work is the same (one table lookup instead
of one multiplication); nothing is computed per run beyond a luminance comparison.

Each table is `round(255 · (v / max)^(1 / γ))`: identity at both ends (0 stays transparent,
full coverage stays opaque), monotonic, and heavier in between for `γ > 1`. A bitmap font
carries its tables (`BitmapFont::gamma`), so the curve
strengths are tuned per font when the font is generated (`twine-build`'s `Font::gamma`);
the built-in fonts use `DEFAULT` (γ = 1.2 dark-on-light, 1.8 light-on-dark), and
`LINEAR` reproduces LVGL's mapping exactly.

| Depth | Mapping |
|-------|---------|
| 1 bpp | `0, 255` (no levels in between) |
| 2 bpp | `GammaRamp::table2` |
| 4 bpp | `GammaRamp::table4` |
| 8 bpp | identity (8-bit coverage is used as stored; run-time TrueType glyphs likewise) |
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### static twine_text::gamma::LINEAR
`pub static LINEAR: twine_text::TextGamma`
LVGL's linear mapping for both polarities (fonts generated without text gamma).

#### static twine_text::gamma::DEFAULT
`pub static DEFAULT: twine_text::TextGamma`
The default curves of generated fonts: γ = 1.2 dark-on-light (already heavy with linear blending: a mild lift) and γ = 1.8 light-on-dark (thin without it: a strong lift). The built-in fonts use these.

Re-exports in `twine_text::gamma`:
- `Polarity` — same as `twine_text::Polarity`
- `GammaRamp` — same as `twine_text::GammaRamp`
- `TextGamma` — same as `twine_text::TextGamma`

## crate twine_image

Documented with features: `std,img-bmp,img-gif,img-jpeg,img-lz4,img-png,img-qoi`.

**twine-image**

Images for the Twine GUI library: the `Image` data model (every `ColorFormat` of the
renderer, palettes, `Rgb565A8` alpha planes, premultiplied alpha), compressed images (LVGL
RLE, LZ4), decoders for encoded files (QOI, PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF and the raw `.tbin`
format of `decoders::tbin`), a byte-budgeted
`ImageCache` and the resolution of any `ImageSource` to drawable
`ImagePixels`.

Drawing itself is done by `twine-render` (`Painter::image`); this crate only produces
pixels. It is `no_std` + `alloc`.

**Features**

| Feature | Enables |
|---------|---------|
| `img-qoi` | in-house QOI decoder |
| `img-png` | in-house PNG decoder over `miniz_oxide` (all color types, Adam7) |
| `img-jpeg` | JPEG decoder (`zune-jpeg`, baseline + progressive) |
| `img-bmp` | in-house BMP decoder |
| `img-gif` | in-house GIF decoder and `GifPlayer` animation |
| `img-lz4` | LZ4-compressed images |
| `std` | encoders used by tools and tests |
| `log` / `defmt` | logging backend (target `"twine::image"`) |
| `safety` | the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints; refuses `img-jpeg` |

#### struct twine_image::ImageCache
Decoded images, least-recently-used first out, within a byte budget.
Methods of `ImageCache`:
- `pub fn new(budget_bytes: usize, max_entries: usize) -> Self` — A cache holding at most `max_entries` images and `budget_bytes` bytes of pixels.
- `pub fn budget(&self) -> usize` — The byte budget.
- `pub fn get_or_decode(&mut self, key: twine_image::SourceKey, decode: impl FnOnce(&mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>) -> Result<twine_image::CachedImage<'_>, twine_image::Error>` — Returns the cached pixels of `key`, or runs `decode` (which fills the buffer it gets and returns the header) and caches the result, evicting least recently used entries as needed. Cache hits do not allocate.
  Errors: The error of `decode`; nothing is cached then. An image larger than the cache budget is not an error: it is decoded on every call (logged once).
- `pub fn set_budget(&mut self, budget_bytes: usize)` — Changes the byte budget (LVGL `lv_image_cache_resize`), evicting least recently used images until the cached ones fit.
- `pub fn contains(&self, key: &twine_image::SourceKey) -> bool` — Whether `key` is cached (does not count as a use).
- `pub fn invalidate(&mut self, key: &twine_image::SourceKey)` — Drops the entry of `key` (e.g. after the file changed).
- `pub fn warn_once(&mut self, key: &twine_image::SourceKey) -> bool` — `true` the first time it is called for `key` (then `false`): lets callers log one warning per source (missing files, oversize images). Once 16 sources are remembered, every call returns `true` again for new sources.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Drops every entry.
- `pub fn stats(&self) -> twine_image::CacheStats` — Counters.
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes the cache holds: its entry table and the decoded pixels of every cached image (and of the transient image decoded for the current draw, if any), by capacity. At most the budget plus the table once the cache is full. Allocates nothing; never panics; O(entries).
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_image::ImageHeaderCache

- `pub fn insert(&mut self, key: twine_image::SourceKey, header: twine_image::ImageHeader)` — Caches `header` for `key` (replacing the oldest entry when full).
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &twine_image::SourceKey)` — Drops the header of `key`.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Drops every entry.

#### trait twine_image::Decoder
`pub trait Decoder`
Decodes one encoded image format.
Items:
- `fn name(&self) -> &'static str` — Short name for logs, e.g. `"qoi"`.
- `fn probe(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<twine_image::ImageHeader>` — Reads only the header of `bytes`; `None` when the bytes are not this format (or the header is invalid).
- `fn decode(&self, bytes: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>` — Decodes `bytes` into `out` (cleared first, reserved once; allocation failure is `Error::Decode("out of memory")`, never an abort).
  Errors: `Error::InvalidHeader` for data this decoder does not recognise, `Error::Decode` for corrupt data or when `out` cannot be allocated.
Implemented by: twine_image::decoders::bmp::BmpDecoder, twine_image::decoders::gif::GifDecoder, twine_image::decoders::jpeg::JpegDecoder, twine_image::decoders::png::PngDecoder, twine_image::decoders::qoi::QoiDecoder, twine_image::decoders::tbin::BinDecoder

#### struct twine_image::DecoderRegistry
An ordered list of decoders; the first whose `Decoder::probe` accepts the bytes decodes them.
Methods of `DecoderRegistry`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty registry.
- `pub fn with_defaults() -> Self` — The `.tbin` decoder, then every decoder enabled by features, in the order qoi, png, jpeg, bmp, gif.
- `pub fn register(&mut self, d: &'static dyn twine_image::Decoder) -> Result<(), twine_image::Error>` — Appends a decoder (probed after the existing ones); `Error::CacheFull` when `MAX_DECODERS` are registered.
  Errors: `Error::CacheFull` when `MAX_DECODERS` are registered.
- `pub fn names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> + '_` — Names of the registered decoders, in probe order.
- `pub fn probe(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<(&'static dyn twine_image::Decoder, twine_image::ImageHeader)>` — The first decoder that recognises `bytes`, with the image header.
- `pub fn decode(&self, bytes: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>` — Decodes `bytes` with the first decoder that recognises them; `Error::InvalidHeader` when none does.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidHeader` when no decoder recognises `bytes`, and the error of the decoder that does.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### const twine_image::MAX_DECODERS
`pub const MAX_DECODERS: usize = 8`
Maximum number of decoders in a `DecoderRegistry`.

#### enum twine_image::Error
Errors of `twine-image`.
Variants:
- `InvalidHeader` — The header is inconsistent (e.g. the stride cannot hold a row) or not recognised.
- `SizeMismatch { expected: usize, got: usize }` — The data length does not match the header.
- `Unsupported(twine_core::ColorFormat)` — The color format cannot be used here.
- `UnsupportedSource(&'static str)` — The kind of source cannot be resolved to pixels here (symbols, SVG).
- `Decode(&'static str)` — Encoded or compressed data is malformed, or decoding ran out of memory.
- `CacheFull` — The cache or registry has no room left.
- `NotFound` — A file source could not be found (or no file system is available).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Error, Display

#### enum twine_image::Compression
Compression method of `ImageData::Compressed`.
Variants:
- `Rle` — LVGL 9 run-length encoding (blocks of one pixel; 1 byte for sub-byte and indexed formats).
- `Lz4` — LZ4 block format (feature `img-lz4`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_image::Image
An image: header plus pixel data. Converted images from `twine image` are `pub static NAME: Image`.
Fields:
- `header: twine_image::ImageHeader` — Header.
- `data: twine_image::ImageData` — Pixel data.
Methods of `Image`:
- `pub fn decompress_into(&self, out: &mut [u8]) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>` — Decompresses (or copies) the pixel data into `out` (at least `ImageHeader::data_size` bytes) and returns the header of the result (without `ImageFlags::COMPRESSED`).
  Errors: `Error::SizeMismatch` when `out` is smaller than `ImageHeader::data_size` or the data decompresses to fewer bytes; `Error::Decode` for corrupt data or LZ4 data without the `img-lz4` feature.
- `pub const fn new_static(header: twine_image::ImageHeader, data: &'static [u8]) -> Self` — An image over static, uncompressed bytes.
- `pub fn new_owned(header: twine_image::ImageHeader, data: Box<[u8]>) -> Self` — An image over heap bytes.
- `pub fn bytes(&self) -> Option<&[u8]>` — The uncompressed bytes (`None` for compressed data).
- `pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), twine_image::Error>` — Checks that the data is consistent with the header.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidHeader` for an inconsistent header; `Error::SizeMismatch` when the data is shorter than the header requires.
- `pub fn palette(&self) -> Option<&[u8]>` — The palette of an indexed image (`palette_len · 4` bytes; `None` for other formats, compressed or short data).
- `pub fn pixels(&self) -> Option<twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>>` — Drawable pixels (`None` for compressed images, which need the cache, and for invalid images).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, From<&'static twine_image::Image>

#### enum twine_image::ImageData
Where an image's bytes live.
Variants:
- `Static(&'static [u8])` — Uncompressed bytes in flash/ROM.
- `Owned(Box<[u8]>)` — Uncompressed bytes on the heap. (A `Box`, not an `Rc`, so that `Image` stays `Sync` and can be a `static`; share an owned image by wrapping the whole `Image` in an `Rc`.)
- `Compressed { method: twine_image::Compression, data: &'static [u8], decompressed_size: u32 }` — Compressed bytes; decompressed into the image cache before drawing.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

- `pub const fn iter(&self) -> bitflags::iter::Iter<twine_image::ImageFlags>` — Yield a set of contained flags values.
- `pub const fn iter_names(&self) -> bitflags::iter::IterNames<twine_image::ImageFlags>` — Yield a set of contained named flags values.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Flags, PublicFlags, Binary, Octal, LowerHex, UpperHex, BitOr, BitOrAssign, BitXor, BitXorAssign, BitAnd, BitAndAssign, Sub, SubAssign, Not, Extend<twine_image::ImageFlags>, FromIterator<twine_image::ImageFlags>, IntoIterator

#### enum twine_image::ImageSource
What an image widget shows.

  Errors: `Error::NotFound` when the file does not exist or cannot be read.

#### fn twine_image::header_of
`pub fn header_of(src: &twine_image::ImageSource, cx: &mut twine_image::ImageContext<'_>) -> Result<twine_image::ImageHeader, twine_image::Error>`

#### fn twine_image::with_pixels

Calls `f` with the pixels of `src`.

#### fn twine_image::lz4_decompress
`pub fn lz4_decompress(input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, twine_image::Error>`
Decompresses an LZ4 block into `output` and returns the number of bytes written. Corrupt input or a too small `output` is an error (never a panic).
Errors: `Error::Decode` for corrupt input or an `output` too small for the data.

#### fn twine_image::rle_compress
`pub fn rle_compress(input: &[u8], blk_size: usize) -> Vec<u8>`
Compresses `input` (greedy: runs of two or more equal blocks become repeat packets of up to 127 blocks, everything else literal packets of up to 127 blocks). A trailing partial block is padded with zeros (which `rle_decompress` tolerates).

#### fn twine_image::rle_block_size
`pub const fn rle_block_size(format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> usize`
RLE block size of a format: bytes per pixel, or 1 for sub-byte and indexed formats (whose whole data, palette included, is compressed as one byte stream).

#### fn twine_image::rle_decompress
`pub fn rle_decompress(input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], blk_size: usize) -> Result<usize, twine_image::Error>`
Decompresses `input` into `output` and returns the number of bytes written.
Errors: `Error::Decode` for truncated input or an overflow of `output` by a block or more.

Re-exports in `twine_image`:
- `ColorFormat` = `twine_core::ColorFormat`
- `Symbol` = `twine_core::Symbol`

### mod twine_image::decoders

Built-in decoders (each behind its `img-*` feature, except the raw `.tbin` format).

### mod twine_image::decoders::bmp

In-house BMP decoder: 1, 4, 8 bpp paletted (uncompressed, RLE4, RLE8), 16 bpp
(RGB555 or bit fields), 24 bpp and 32 bpp (with optional alpha mask); bottom-up and
top-down rows; every DIB header version from `BITMAPCOREHEADER` to `BITMAPV5HEADER`.
Malformed data returns an error, never panics.

#### const twine_image::decoders::bmp::BMP_MAX_DIM
`pub const BMP_MAX_DIM: u32 = 16384`
Largest accepted width or height.

#### struct twine_image::decoders::bmp::BmpDecoder
Decodes BMP files (`BM` magic).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Decoder

### mod twine_image::decoders::gif

In-house GIF decoder: `GifDecoder` (first frame, for static use) and `GifPlayer`
(animation with frame compositing).

Supports GIF87a/GIF89a, global and local palettes, transparency, interlaced frames,
frames smaller than the canvas, the disposal methods *none*, *background* (cleared to
transparent, like browsers) and *previous*, per-frame delays and the NETSCAPE2.0 loop count.
Malformed data never panics: decoding stops at the first error.

#### const twine_image::decoders::gif::GIF_MAX_DIM
`pub const GIF_MAX_DIM: u16 = 16384`
Largest accepted canvas width or height.

#### const twine_image::decoders::gif::GIF_DEFAULT_DELAY
`pub const GIF_DEFAULT_DELAY: twine_core::Duration`
Delay used for frames that specify none (like browsers).

#### struct twine_image::decoders::gif::GifDecoder
Decodes the first frame of GIF files (static use; see `GifPlayer` for animation).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Decoder

#### struct twine_image::decoders::gif::GifPlayer<'a>
Plays an animated GIF: `advance` composites the next frame onto an `Argb8888` canvas and returns how long to show it.
Methods of `GifPlayer`:
- `pub fn new(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, twine_image::Error>` — Parses the GIF and allocates everything needed to play it. The canvas starts transparent; call `advance` to show the first frame.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidHeader` or `Error::Decode` for data that is not a playable GIF (including one without frames); `Error::Decode` when the canvas cannot be allocated.
- `pub fn header(&self) -> twine_image::ImageHeader` — Canvas header (`Argb8888`, canvas size).
- `pub fn frame_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of frames.
- `pub fn frame_index(&self) -> usize` — Index of the frame on the canvas (0-based; 0 before the first `advance`).
- `pub fn loop_count(&self) -> Option<u16>` — The NETSCAPE2.0 loop count: `None` without the extension (play once), `Some(0)` loops forever, `Some(n)` repeats `n` more times.
- `pub fn is_finished(&self) -> bool` — Whether the last loop has ended (the last frame stays on the canvas).
- `pub fn pixels(&self) -> twine_render::ImagePixels<'_>` — The canvas.
- `pub fn reset(&mut self)` — Restarts from the first frame with a transparent canvas.
- `pub fn advance(&mut self) -> twine_core::Duration` — Composites the next frame onto the canvas and returns its delay (0 → 100 ms). After the last loop the canvas is left unchanged and `GIF_DEFAULT_DELAY` returned.
Implements: Clone, Debug

### mod twine_image::decoders::jpeg

JPEG decoder over `zune-jpeg` (baseline and progressive, gray / YCbCr / CMYK input, all
chroma subsamplings). Output is always opaque `Xrgb8888`.

Each decode parses the headers twice (probe, then decode); that is cheap next to the
entropy decoding.
