### mod twine_image::decoders::png

In-house PNG decoder over `miniz_oxide` (zlib inflate).

Supports every standard PNG: gray, gray + alpha, RGB, RGBA and indexed images at every
legal bit depth (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), Adam7 interlacing, palette transparency and `tRNS` color
keys. Ancillary chunks and CRCs are ignored. Malformed data returns an error, never panics.

#### const twine_image::decoders::png::PNG_MAX_DIM

### mod twine_image::decoders::qoi

In-house QOI decoder (<https://qoiformat.org/qoi-specification.pdf>), plus an encoder
(feature `std`) for tools and tests.

Decoding allocates nothing but the output buffer: the 64-entry color index lives on the
stack.

#### const twine_image::decoders::qoi::QOI_MAX_DIM

#### fn twine_image::decoders::qoi::qoi_encode

Encodes `w × h` pixels given as `R, G, B, A` bytes into a QOI file with `channels` (3 or 4; with 3 the alpha bytes are ignored).

### mod twine_image::decoders::tbin

The raw twine binary image file (`.tbin`, written by `twine image --bin`): pixels in any
`ColorFormat`, stored as they are drawn, optionally RLE- or LZ4-compressed. Decoding is a
copy (or a decompression), so file images in the display's format cost no conversion.

Layout (little endian), 12-byte header then the data:

| Offset | Size | Field |
|-------:|-----:|-------|
| 0 | 4 | magic `b"TWIN"` |
| 4 | 1 | bits 0–3: version (1); bits 4–5: compression (0 none, 1 RLE, 2 LZ4); bit 6: premultiplied alpha |
| 5 | 1 | `ColorFormat` (`ColorFormat as u8`) |
| 6 | 2 | width |
| 8 | 2 | height |
| 10 | 2 | stride (bytes per row) |
| 12 | … | pixel data: `ImageHeader::data_size` bytes (palette first for indexed formats), or the compressed stream |

#### const twine_image::decoders::tbin::TBIN_MAGIC
`pub const TBIN_MAGIC: [u8; 4]`
Magic bytes of a `.tbin` file.

#### const twine_image::decoders::tbin::TBIN_HEADER_LEN
`pub const TBIN_HEADER_LEN: usize = 12`
Size of the `.tbin` header.

#### const twine_image::decoders::tbin::TBIN_VERSION
`pub const TBIN_VERSION: u8 = 1`
Format version written by `encode_tbin`.

#### struct twine_image::decoders::tbin::BinDecoder
Decoder of `.tbin` files (always available: it only copies or decompresses).
Implements: Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Decoder

#### fn twine_image::decoders::tbin::encode_tbin
`pub fn encode_tbin(header: twine_image::ImageHeader, compression: Option<twine_image::Compression>, stored: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`
Writes a `.tbin` file: the header of `header` (its `PREMULTIPLIED` flag is kept) and `stored`, the pixel data already compressed with `compression` (`None`: raw pixels, `ImageHeader::data_size` bytes).

## crate twine_vector

Documented with features: `std,svg`.

**twine-vector**

Vector graphics for the Twine GUI library (the equivalent of LVGL's `lv_vector` API and SVG
support): paths, curve flattening, an integer anti-aliasing rasterizer with non-zero and
even-odd fill rules, strokes (joins, caps, dashes), paints (solid, linear and radial
gradients, image patterns), transforms, and — with the `svg` feature — an SVG Tiny subset
parser.

Everything is fixed-point (coordinates are 16.16 `Fx`, the rasterizer
works in 24.8), so results are bit-identical on every target. Drawing goes through
`twine-render`'s `Painter`: the rasterizer produces anti-aliased
coverage rows for the rows inside the painter's clip only and hands them to
`Painter::coverage_span`, which applies masks and
blends. Rendering a path in horizontal chunks (partial display buffers) is pixel-identical
to rendering it at once.

**Pipeline**

```rust
 Path ──(transform, flatten 0.25 px)──► lines ──► rasterizer (clip rows) ──► coverage rows
  └──(flatten in path space)──► polylines ──► stroker (joins, caps, dashes) ──┘      │
                                                 Paint ──► SpanSource ──► Painter::coverage_span
```

**Memory**

Scratch buffers live in `VectorCaches`; they grow to the largest path drawn and are then
reused, so steady-state drawing does not allocate. `PainterVectorExt::vector` keeps them
in the painter's `RenderCaches` extension slot; `PainterVectorExt::vector_with` takes
them explicitly.

**Example**

```rust
use twine_core::{Color, ColorFormat, Fx, Rect};
use twine_render::{DrawBuf, FillRule, Painter, RenderCaches};
use twine_vector::{FxPoint, Paint, PainterVectorExt, Path, Stroke, VectorDsc};

let mut caches = RenderCaches::default();
let mut px = vec![0u8; 64 * 64 * 2];
let buf = DrawBuf::new_packed(&mut px, ColorFormat::Rgb565, Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 64, 64)).unwrap();
let mut p = Painter::new(buf, &mut caches);

let mut star = Path::new();
star.move_to(FxPoint::from_int(32, 4))
    .line_to(FxPoint::from_int(50, 60))
    .line_to(FxPoint::from_int(4, 24))
    .line_to(FxPoint::from_int(60, 24))
    .line_to(FxPoint::from_int(14, 60))
    .close();
p.vector(
    &star,
    &VectorDsc {
        fill: Some((Paint::Solid(Color::RED), FillRule::EvenOdd)),
        stroke: Some((Paint::Solid(Color::BLACK), Stroke { width: Fx::from_int(2), ..Stroke::default() })),
        ..VectorDsc::default()
    },
);
```

**Features**

- `svg`: `parse_svg` and `SvgDocument` in the `svg` module (SVG Tiny subset).
- `log` / `defmt`: logging backend (target `"twine::vector"`); `std`: std conveniences.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints.

#### struct twine_vector::DrawParams

#### trait twine_vector::PainterVectorExt

- `fn vector_with(&mut self, caches: &mut twine_vector::VectorCaches, path: &twine_vector::Path, dsc: &twine_vector::VectorDsc)` — Draws `path` with `dsc` using explicit `caches`.

#### struct twine_vector::VectorCaches
Reusable scratch memory of vector drawing: flattened lines and polylines, the rasterizer's edge list and row accumulators, and one 256-entry gradient color map.
Methods of `VectorCaches`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — Empty caches (the buffers grow on first use).
- `pub fn with_capacity(max_width: usize, segments: usize) -> Self` — Caches pre-sized for rows up to `max_width` pixels and paths of up to `segments` line segments, so even the first draw does not allocate for such paths.
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Bytes currently reserved by all buffers.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### struct twine_vector::VectorDsc

#### enum twine_vector::Paint
How a path is filled or stroked.
Variants:
- `Solid(twine_core::Color)` — One color.
- `Linear { start: twine_vector::FxPoint, end: twine_vector::FxPoint, stops: twine_vector::Stops, extend: twine_render::GradExtend, transform: twine_core::Transform }` — Linear gradient: `t = 0` at `start`, `t = 1` at `end`, constant along perpendiculars.
- `Radial { center: twine_vector::FxPoint, radius: twine_core::Fx, focal: Option<twine_vector::FxPoint>, stops: twine_vector::Stops, extend: twine_render::GradExtend, transform: twine_core::Transform }` — Radial gradient: `t = 0` at the focal point (default: the center), `t = 1` on the circle `(center, radius)`. A focal point outside the circle is moved just inside.
- `Image { image: twine_render::ImagePixels<'static>, transform: twine_core::Transform, extend: twine_render::GradExtend, antialias: bool }` — Image pattern: image pixel `(x, y)` covers `[x, x+1) × [y, y+1)` of paint space.
Methods of `Paint`:
- `pub fn is_solid(&self) -> bool` — Whether the paint is a single color.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, From<twine_core::Color>

#### enum twine_vector::Stops

- `Static(&'static [twine_render::GradStop])` — Stops in static memory.
- `Owned(Vec<twine_render::GradStop>)` — Stops owned by the paint.

#### const twine_vector::KAPPA
`pub const KAPPA: twine_core::Fx`
Cubic Bézier circle constant `4/3 · (√2 − 1) ≈ 0.5523` in 16.16.

#### struct twine_vector::Path
A vector path: sub-paths of lines and Bézier curves in 16.16 fixed point.
Methods of `Path`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty path.
- `pub fn with_capacity(verbs: usize, points: usize) -> Self` — An empty path with room for `verbs` verbs and `points` points.
- `pub fn verbs(&self) -> &[twine_vector::Verb]` — The verbs.
- `pub fn points(&self) -> &[twine_vector::FxPoint]` — The points (see `Verb` for how many each verb uses).
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the path has no verbs.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every command, keeping the capacity.
- `pub fn current_point(&self) -> twine_vector::FxPoint` — The current point: the end of the last command (the sub-path start after `close`).
- `pub fn move_to(&mut self, p: twine_vector::FxPoint) -> &mut Self` — Starts a new sub-path at `p`.
- `pub fn line_to(&mut self, p: twine_vector::FxPoint) -> &mut Self` — Straight line to `p`.
- `pub fn quad_to(&mut self, c: twine_vector::FxPoint, p: twine_vector::FxPoint) -> &mut Self` — Quadratic Bézier with control point `c` to `p`.
- `pub fn cubic_to(&mut self, c1: twine_vector::FxPoint, c2: twine_vector::FxPoint, p: twine_vector::FxPoint) -> &mut Self` — Cubic Bézier with control points `c1`, `c2` to `p`.
- `pub fn close(&mut self) -> &mut Self` — Closes the current sub-path (no-op when none is open).
- `pub fn arc_to(&mut self, radii: twine_vector::FxPoint, x_rot: twine_core::Angle, large: bool, sweep: bool, p: twine_vector::FxPoint) -> &mut Self` — SVG elliptical arc from the current point to `p` with radii `radii`, x-axis rotation `x_rot` and the SVG `large-arc` / `sweep` flags (W3C SVG 1.1 appendix F.6), converted to cubic Béziers of at most 90° each. Radii that are too small are scaled up; a zero radius draws a line; `p` equal to the current point draws nothing. The end point is exact.
- `pub fn rect(&mut self, r: twine_core::Rect, radius: i32) -> &mut Self` — Appends the closed rectangle `r` with corner radius `radius` (clamped to half the shorter side). Rounded corners are cubic quarter circles (`KAPPA`), so a rounded rectangle has 4 lines and 4 cubics.
- `pub fn rounded_rect(&mut self, r: twine_vector::FxRect, rx: twine_core::Fx, ry: twine_core::Fx) -> &mut Self` — Appends the closed rectangle `r` with elliptic corners `(rx, ry)` (each clamped to half the side, SVG `<rect>` semantics).
- `pub fn circle(&mut self, c: twine_vector::FxPoint, r: twine_core::Fx) -> &mut Self` — Appends a closed circle (4 cubics, clockwise on screen, starting at 3 o'clock).
- `pub fn ellipse(&mut self, c: twine_vector::FxPoint, rx: twine_core::Fx, ry: twine_core::Fx) -> &mut Self` — Appends a closed axis-aligned ellipse (4 cubics, clockwise on screen).
- `pub fn bounds(&self) -> twine_vector::FxRect` — Bounding box of all points (control points included, so it contains the curves). An empty path gives `FxRect::ZERO`.
- `pub fn transform(&mut self, t: &twine_core::Transform)` — Maps every point by `t` (Bézier curves are affine invariant).
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> twine_vector::PathIter<'_>` — Iterates the commands as `PathEl`s with their points.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, IntoIterator

#### enum twine_vector::PathEl
One path command with its points (see `Path::iter`).
Variants:
- `MoveTo(twine_vector::FxPoint)` — Start of a sub-path.
- `LineTo(twine_vector::FxPoint)` — Line to the point.
- `QuadTo(twine_vector::FxPoint, twine_vector::FxPoint)` — Quadratic curve (control, end).
- `CubicTo(twine_vector::FxPoint, twine_vector::FxPoint, twine_vector::FxPoint)` — Cubic curve (control 1, control 2, end).
- `Close` — Close the sub-path.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_vector::PathIter<'a>
Iterator over the commands of a `Path`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Iterator

#### enum twine_vector::Verb
A path command. Each verb consumes points from `Path::points`: `MoveTo`/`LineTo` one, `QuadTo` two (control, end), `CubicTo` three (control 1, control 2, end), `Close` none.
Variants:
- `MoveTo` — Starts a new sub-path.
- `LineTo` — Straight line.
- `QuadTo` — Quadratic Bézier curve.
- `CubicTo` — Cubic Bézier curve.
- `Close` — Closes the current sub-path (back to its start).
Methods of `Verb`:
- `pub const fn points(self) -> usize` — Number of points the verb consumes.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_vector::VectorScene
Paths with their descriptors, drawn in order.
Methods of `VectorScene`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty scene.
- `pub fn add(&mut self, path: twine_vector::Path, dsc: twine_vector::VectorDsc)` — Appends `path` drawn with `dsc`.
- `pub fn path_mut(&mut self) -> Option<(&mut twine_vector::Path, &mut twine_vector::VectorDsc)>` — Appends an item and returns its (cleared, capacity-keeping) path and descriptor for filling in place: the allocation-free way to rebuild a scene. A spare item left by `clear` is reused; otherwise the storage grows by one item.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every item (the storage is kept for reuse).
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of items.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the scene has no items.
- `pub fn items(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&twine_vector::Path, &twine_vector::VectorDsc)> + '_` — The items.
- `pub fn bounds(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — Screen bounds of all items (`None` when nothing is drawn).
- `pub fn bounds_with(&self, t: &twine_core::Transform) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — Screen bounds when drawn with `draw``(…, t)`.
- `pub fn draw(&self, p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, t: &twine_core::Transform)` — Draws every item, with `t` applied after each item's own transform. Items outside the painter's clip are skipped cheaply; nothing is allocated once the painter's `VectorCaches` have grown.
- `pub fn draw_with(&self, p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, params: &twine_vector::DrawParams)` — Draws every item with scene-wide `params` (transform, opacity, recolor).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

### mod twine_vector::svg

SVG Tiny subset parser (feature `svg`): `parse_svg` turns SVG bytes into an
`SvgDocument` holding a `VectorScene`, drawn scaled into any rectangle with
`SvgDocument::render`.

Supported:

- elements `svg` (`width`, `height`, `viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`), `g`, `path` (the
  full `d` grammar), `rect` (`rx`/`ry`), `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline`,
  `polygon`, and `linearGradient` / `radialGradient` with `stop`s (anywhere, usually in
  `defs`), referenced as `url(#id)`;
- presentation attributes and inline `style="…"` declarations: `fill`, `stroke`,
  `stroke-width`, `stroke-linejoin`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-miterlimit`,
  `stroke-dasharray`, `stroke-dashoffset`, `opacity`, `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`,
  `fill-rule`, `color` (for `currentColor`), `display="none"`, and `transform`
  (`matrix`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, `skewX`, `skewY`);
- gradients with `gradientUnits`, `gradientTransform`, `spreadMethod`, `x1 y1 x2 y2`,
  `cx cy r fx fy`, `stop` `offset`/`stop-color`/`stop-opacity` and `href` / `xlink:href`
  inheritance;
- colors `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `rgb()`, the 147 color keywords, `none`, `currentColor`.

Everything else (text, `use`, clipping, masks, filters, CSS style sheets, …) is ignored
with a `debug!` log. Group `opacity` is multiplied into the elements (no offscreen layer).

The parser is iterative (element nesting is limited to `MAX_DEPTH`), never panics, and
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_vector::svg::MAX_DEPTH
`pub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 32`
Deepest element nesting accepted.

#### enum twine_vector::svg::Align
`preserveAspectRatio` alignment.
Variants:
- `None` — Scale non-uniformly to fill the viewport.
- `XMinYMin` — Align min x / min y.
- `XMidYMin` — Align mid x / min y.
- `XMaxYMin` — Align max x / min y.
- `XMinYMid` — Align min x / mid y.
- `XMidYMid` — Center (the default).
- `XMaxYMid` — Align max x / mid y.
- `XMinYMax` — Align min x / max y.
- `XMidYMax` — Align mid x / max y.
- `XMaxYMax` — Align max x / max y.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_vector::svg::AspectRatio
`preserveAspectRatio`: alignment and `meet` (fit inside, the default) or `slice` (cover).
Fields:

- `slice: bool` — `slice` instead of `meet`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

Re-exports in `twine_vector::svg`:
- `SvgError` — same as `twine_vector::SvgError`
- `SvgDocument` — same as `twine_vector::SvgDocument`
- `parse_svg` — same as `twine_vector::parse_svg`

## crate twine_fs

Documented with features: `std,fs-std,fs-fat`.

**twine-fs**

File system abstraction of the Twine GUI library, the equivalent of LVGL's `lv_fs`: images,
fonts and other assets can be loaded from storage through drive-letter paths such as
`"A:/img/logo.qoi"`.

- `FileSystem` is the driver interface (open / read / write / seek / tell / close /
  directory listing / metadata), addressed by `FileHandle`s.
- `Vfs` mounts up to `MAX_DRIVES` file systems under drive letters and resolves full
  paths; `File` is an RAII wrapper that closes itself when dropped.
- Drivers: `MemoryFs` (files compiled into flash plus optional RAM files, always
  available), `StdFs` (a host directory, feature `fs-std`) and `FatFs` (FAT volumes on SD
  cards through `embedded-sdmmc`, feature `fs-fat`).

The crate is `no_std` + `alloc`. Opening files is logged at debug level with target
`"twine::fs"`.

```rust
use twine_fs::{MemoryFs, Vfs};

static ASSETS: &[(&str, &[u8])] = &[("greeting.txt", b"hello")];
let mut vfs = Vfs::new();
vfs.mount('A', Box::new(MemoryFs::new(ASSETS))).unwrap();
assert_eq!(vfs.read_to_vec("A:/greeting.txt").unwrap(), b"hello");
assert!(vfs.read_to_vec("B:/greeting.txt").is_err());
```

**Features**

`std` (`std` conveniences), `fs-std` (`StdFs`), `fs-fat` (`FatFs`), `log` / `defmt`
(logging backend).

#### struct twine_fs::FatFs<D: embedded_sdmmc::blockdevice::BlockDevice, T: embedded_sdmmc::filesystem::timestamp::TimeSource, const MAX_FILES: usize>
The first partition (MBR volume 0, FAT16 or FAT32) of a block device such as an SD card.
Methods of `FatFs`:
- `pub fn new(device: D, time: T) -> Result<Self, twine_fs::Error>` — Opens volume 0 of `device` (MBR partition table) and its root directory.
  Errors: `Error::Io` for a device error, `Error::NotFound` or `Error::Unsupported` when the card has no usable FAT volume 0, `Error::OutOfMemory`.
- `pub fn open_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of currently open files.
Implements: Debug, FileSystem, Drop

Implements: Debug, FileSystem

#### struct twine_fs::DirEntry<'a>
One entry of a directory listing (see `FileSystem::read_dir`).
Fields:
- `name: &'a str` — The entry's name (no path, no trailing `/`).
- `is_dir: bool` — Whether the entry is a directory.
- `size: u64` — Size in bytes (0 for directories).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_fs::Error
File-system errors.
Variants:
- `NotFound` — The file or directory does not exist.
- `NotADirectory` — A path component that must be a directory is a file.
- `IsADirectory` — A file operation was attempted on a directory.
- `PermissionDenied` — The file system or the open mode does not allow the operation.
- `InvalidPath` — The path is malformed (no drive letter, `..` escaping the root, unsupported name).
- `UnknownDrive(char)` — No file system is mounted at this drive letter.
- `TooManyOpenFiles` — The file system's open-file limit is reached.
- `Io` — A device or driver error.
- `Unsupported` — The file system does not support the operation.
- `OutOfMemory` — Memory could not be allocated.
- `TooManyDrives` — Every drive letter slot of the `Vfs` is taken.
- `InvalidSeek` — A seek before the start of the file (or past the addressable size).
- `BadHandle` — The handle is not an open file of this file system.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Error, Display

#### struct twine_fs::FileHandle
An open file of one `FileSystem`; only meaningful to the file system that returned it.
Fields:
- `0: u16`
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

#### trait twine_fs::FileSystem
`pub trait FileSystem`
A file system (LVGL `lv_fs_drv_t`): a driver mounted in a `Vfs` under a drive letter, or used directly.
Items:
- `fn open(&mut self, path: &str, mode: twine_fs::OpenMode) -> Result<twine_fs::FileHandle, twine_fs::Error>` — Opens `path` in `mode`.
  Errors: `Error::NotFound` for a missing file opened for reading, `Error::IsADirectory`, `Error::PermissionDenied` for a mode the file system does not allow, `Error::TooManyOpenFiles`, `Error::InvalidPath`, `Error::Io`.
- `fn read(&mut self, f: twine_fs::FileHandle, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, twine_fs::Error>` — Reads up to `buf.len()` bytes at the cursor; returns the number read (0 at the end).
  Errors: the file system's error: typically `Error::BadHandle` for a handle that is not open, `Error::Io` for a device failure.
- `fn write(&mut self, f: twine_fs::FileHandle, buf: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, twine_fs::Error>` — Writes `buf` at the cursor (at the end for `OpenMode::Append`); returns the number of bytes written.
  Errors: the file system's error: typically `Error::BadHandle` for a handle that is not open, `Error::Io` for a device failure, `Error::PermissionDenied` for a file opened read-only.
- `fn seek(&mut self, f: twine_fs::FileHandle, pos: twine_fs::SeekFrom) -> Result<u64, twine_fs::Error>` — Moves the cursor; returns the new absolute position. Seeking past the end is allowed (a later write fills the gap with zeros where the file system supports it).
  Errors: `Error::InvalidSeek` for a position before the start; the file system's error: typically `Error::BadHandle` for a handle that is not open, `Error::Io` for a device failure.
- `fn tell(&mut self, f: twine_fs::FileHandle) -> Result<u64, twine_fs::Error>` — The cursor position.
  Errors: the file system's error: typically `Error::BadHandle` for a handle that is not open, `Error::Io` for a device failure.
- `fn close(&mut self, f: twine_fs::FileHandle) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Closes the file (flushing written data).
  Errors: the file system's error: typically `Error::BadHandle` for a handle that is not open, `Error::Io` for a device failure (written data may be lost). The handle is closed either way.
- `fn read_dir(&mut self, path: &str, out: &mut dyn FnMut(twine_fs::DirEntry<'_>)) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Calls `out` once for every entry of the directory `path` (not for `.` and `..`).
  Errors: `Error::NotFound`, `Error::NotADirectory`, `Error::InvalidPath`, `Error::Io`, `Error::Unsupported` for file systems without directories.
- `fn metadata(&mut self, path: &str) -> Result<twine_fs::Metadata, twine_fs::Error>` — Metadata of `path`.
  Errors: `Error::NotFound`, `Error::InvalidPath`, `Error::Io`.
Implemented by: twine_fs::FatFs<D, T, MAX_FILES>, twine_fs::MemoryFs, twine_fs::StdFs, &mut F, Box<F>

#### struct twine_fs::Metadata
File or directory metadata (see `FileSystem::metadata`).
Fields:
- `size: u64` — Size in bytes (0 for directories).
- `is_dir: bool` — Whether the path is a directory.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_fs::OpenMode
How a file is opened (LVGL `lv_fs_mode_t`, plus the usual create/append variants).
Variants:
- `Read` — Read an existing file.
- `Write` — Create the file or truncate an existing one, then write.
- `ReadWrite` — Read and write an existing file (created empty when missing); not truncated.
- `Append` — Write at the end of the file (created when missing); every write appends.
Methods of `OpenMode`:
- `pub const fn can_read(self) -> bool` — Whether the mode allows reading.
- `pub const fn can_write(self) -> bool` — Whether the mode allows writing.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_fs::SeekFrom
A seek target, like `std::io::SeekFrom`.
Variants:
- `Start(u64)` — Absolute position.
- `End(i64)` — Relative to the end of the file.
- `Current(i64)` — Relative to the current position.
Methods of `SeekFrom`:
- `pub fn resolve(self, pos: u64, len: u64) -> Result<u64, twine_fs::Error>` — The absolute position this target resolves to for a file of `len` bytes whose cursor is at `pos`; `Error::InvalidSeek` before the start or on overflow.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidSeek` for a position before the start of the file or past `u64::MAX`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_fs::File<'a>
An open file that closes itself when dropped (errors on drop are logged; call `close` to observe them).
Methods of `File`:
- `pub fn open(fs: &'a mut dyn twine_fs::FileSystem, path: &str, mode: twine_fs::OpenMode) -> Result<Self, twine_fs::Error>` — Opens `path` (a driver path, without drive letter) on `fs`.
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::open`.
- `pub fn handle(&self) -> twine_fs::FileHandle` — The file system's handle of this file.
- `pub fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, twine_fs::Error>` — Reads up to `buf.len()` bytes; returns the number read (0 at the end).
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::read`.
- `pub fn read_exact(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Reads exactly `buf.len()` bytes; `Error::Io` if the file ends first.
  Errors: `Error::Io` when the file ends first, and the errors of `read`.
- `pub fn read_to_end(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<usize, twine_fs::Error>` — Appends the rest of the file to `out`; returns the number of bytes read.
  Errors: `Error::OutOfMemory` when `out` cannot grow (bytes read so far stay in `out`), and the errors of `read`, `seek` and `tell`.
- `pub fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, twine_fs::Error>` — Writes `buf`; returns the number of bytes written.
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::write`.
- `pub fn write_all(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Writes all of `buf`; `Error::Io` if the file system stops accepting data.
  Errors: `Error::Io` when a write accepts no bytes, and the errors of `write`.
- `pub fn seek(&mut self, pos: twine_fs::SeekFrom) -> Result<u64, twine_fs::Error>` — Moves the cursor; returns the new position.
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::seek`.
- `pub fn tell(&mut self) -> Result<u64, twine_fs::Error>` — The cursor position.
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::tell`.
- `pub fn close(self) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Closes the file, reporting errors (dropping closes too, but only logs them).
  Errors: The errors of `FileSystem::close`.
Implements: Debug, Drop

#### const twine_fs::MAX_DRIVES
`pub const MAX_DRIVES: usize = 8`
Maximum number of mounted drives.

#### struct twine_fs::Vfs
A set of file systems mounted under drive letters.
Methods of `Vfs`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty registry.
- `pub fn mount(&mut self, letter: char, fs: Box<dyn twine_fs::FileSystem>) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn twine_fs::FileSystem>>, twine_fs::Error>` — Mounts `fs` as drive `letter` (an ASCII letter), replacing (and returning) a file system already mounted there. `Error::TooManyDrives` when `MAX_DRIVES` are mounted.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidPath` when `letter` is not an ASCII letter; `Error::TooManyDrives` when `MAX_DRIVES` are mounted.
- `pub fn unmount(&mut self, letter: char) -> Option<Box<dyn twine_fs::FileSystem>>` — Unmounts drive `letter`, returning its file system.
- `pub fn letters(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = char> + '_` — The mounted drive letters.
- `pub fn drive_mut(&mut self, letter: char) -> Option<&mut dyn twine_fs::FileSystem + 'static>` — The file system mounted at `letter`.
- `pub fn open(&mut self, path: &str, mode: twine_fs::OpenMode) -> Result<twine_fs::File<'_>, twine_fs::Error>` — Opens `path` (`"A:/dir/file"`); the returned `File` closes itself when dropped.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidPath` without a drive letter, `Error::UnknownDrive` when nothing is mounted at it, and the errors of `FileSystem::open`.
- `pub fn read_dir(&mut self, path: &str, out: &mut dyn FnMut(twine_fs::DirEntry<'_>)) -> Result<(), twine_fs::Error>` — Lists the directory `path` (see `FileSystem::read_dir`).
  Errors: `Error::InvalidPath`, `Error::UnknownDrive`, and the errors of `FileSystem::read_dir`.
- `pub fn metadata(&mut self, path: &str) -> Result<twine_fs::Metadata, twine_fs::Error>` — Metadata of `path`.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidPath`, `Error::UnknownDrive`, and the errors of `FileSystem::metadata`.
- `pub fn read_to_vec(&mut self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, twine_fs::Error>` — Reads the whole file `path` into a new vector.
  Errors: The errors of `open` and `File::read_to_end`.
Implements: Default, Debug

#### fn twine_fs::parse_path
`pub fn parse_path(path: &str) -> Result<(char, &str), twine_fs::Error>`
Splits `"A:/dir/file.png"` into the drive letter and the driver path (`"/dir/file.png"`).
Errors: `Error::InvalidPath` when `path` does not start with an ASCII letter and `:`.

Re-exports in `twine_fs`:
- `twine_fs::embedded_sdmmc` → crate `embedded_sdmmc` (section `## crate embedded_sdmmc`)

## crate twine_assets

Documented with features: `fonts-all`.

**twine-assets**

Built-in fonts of the Twine GUI library as `static` `Font`s, one cargo
feature per font (`default = ["montserrat-14"]`) plus bundles of them (see Bundles;
`fonts-all` enables every font). Fonts that are not enabled cost nothing.

- **Montserrat Medium** 8–48 px (even sizes), 4 bpp: ASCII, `°`, `•` and every
  `twine_text::Symbol` icon (Font Awesome Free). Up to 16 px the bitmaps are stored
  plain (fastest to draw), larger sizes are RLE-compressed (smaller; decoded glyphs are
  kept in the glyph cache). Kerning from the font's `GPOS` table is included.
- **Montserrat Medium 14 px subpixel** (`montserrat-14-subpx`): horizontal RGB subpixel
  glyphs for LCD panels with a known subpixel order.
- **unscii** 8 and 16 px, 1 bpp, ASCII: pixel-exact bitmap fonts.
- **`DejaVu` Sans 16 px** (`dejavu-16-persian-hebrew`), 4 bpp, compressed: ASCII, Hebrew,
  Arabic and Persian letters plus the Arabic presentation forms that
  `twine_text::shape_into` (feature `arabic-shaping`) produces, and the symbols.
- **Source Han Sans SC 14 / 16 px** (`source-han-sans-sc-14-cjk`, `…-16-cjk`), 4 bpp,
  compressed: ASCII, CJK punctuation, Hiragana/Katakana, full-width forms, the ~1 300
  common Chinese/Japanese characters of LVGL's CJK fonts, and the symbols.

The files in `src/fonts/` are generated by `cargo xtask fonts` from
`assets/fonts/fonts.toml` (sources, licenses and SHA-256 hashes of the TTF files are in
`assets/fonts/SOURCES.md`); never edit them by hand. They are grid-fitted with full
hinting (`twine_build::font::Hinting::Full`: one-pixel stems, whole-pixel advances) and
carry the default text gamma (`twine_text::gamma::DEFAULT`: γ 1.2 dark-on-light, 1.8
light-on-dark), so small text stays crisp on low-DPI panels. Applications that need other sizes,
scripts or a subset of characters generate their own fonts with the same generator: the
`twine-build` crate in `build.rs` (`twine_build::font::Font`, e.g. subset to the characters
of the application's translations), `twine::include_font!`, or the `twine font` command.

Besides the fonts, the feature `safety` selects the safety profile (enabled by the `twine`
facade's `safety` feature, see `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository).

**Bundles**

Sets of fonts for applications that do not want to list sizes one by one (the individual
features stay for precise flash budgets; bundles only add fonts and combine freely):

| bundle | fonts | flash bytes |
|---|---|---:|
| `fonts-latin-small` | Montserrat 12, 14, 16 | ~58 K |
| `fonts-latin-medium` | `fonts-latin-small` + Montserrat 18, 20, 22, 24 | ~147 K |
| `fonts-latin-all` | every Montserrat size, `montserrat-14-subpx`, `montserrat-16-latin-ext` | ~666 K |
| `fonts-mono` | unscii 8, 16 | ~4 K |
| `fonts-rtl` | `dejavu-16-persian-hebrew` | ~38 K |
| `fonts-cjk` | Source Han Sans SC 14, 16 | ~289 K |
| `fonts-all` | every built-in font | ~1 M |

**Sizes**

Static data per font (bitmaps, glyph descriptors, cmaps, kerning; descriptor sizes as on a
64-bit host):

| feature | glyphs | line height | flash bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `montserrat-8` | 157 | 11 | 13785 |
| `montserrat-10` | 157 | 13 | 15486 |
| `montserrat-12` | 157 | 16 | 17377 |
| `montserrat-14` | 157 | 18 | 19581 |
| `montserrat-16` | 157 | 21 | 21871 |
| `montserrat-18` | 157 | 23 | 20600 |
| `montserrat-20` | 157 | 26 | 21965 |
| `montserrat-22` | 157 | 28 | 23746 |
| `montserrat-24` | 157 | 31 | 24986 |
| `montserrat-26` | 157 | 33 | 27200 |
| `montserrat-28` | 157 | 36 | 28917 |
| `montserrat-30` | 157 | 38 | 30697 |
| `montserrat-32` | 157 | 40 | 32115 |
| `montserrat-34` | 157 | 42 | 34820 |
| `montserrat-36` | 157 | 45 | 36610 |
| `montserrat-38` | 157 | 47 | 38471 |
| `montserrat-40` | 157 | 50 | 39955 |
| `montserrat-42` | 157 | 52 | 42323 |
| `montserrat-44` | 157 | 55 | 44050 |
| `montserrat-46` | 157 | 57 | 46113 |
| `montserrat-48` | 157 | 60 | 46977 |
| `montserrat-14-subpx` | 157 | 18 | 40998 |

| `source-han-sans-sc-16-cjk` | 1630 | 24 | 164904 |

**Example**

```rust
use twine_assets::fonts::MONTSERRAT_14;
use twine_text::TextLayout;

let size = TextLayout::new("Hello", &MONTSERRAT_14).measure();
assert_eq!(size.h, i32::from(MONTSERRAT_14.line_height));
assert!(size.w > 20);
```

## crate twine_extra

Documented with features: `std,i18n,qrcode,barcode`.

**twine-extra**

Extras for the Twine GUI library, the equivalent of LVGL's "others" and "libs": QR codes,
Code 128 barcodes, and (later) a file explorer, a Pinyin IME, a monkey tester, snapshots and a
system monitor. Every module sits behind a cargo feature of the same name; no feature is
enabled by default.

**Modules**

- `qrcode` (feature `qrcode`): `QrMatrix` encodes bytes into a QR code module matrix
  (versions 1–40, error correction levels L/M/Q/H, numeric/alphanumeric/byte mode chosen
  automatically); `draw_qr` paints it with a `twine_render::Painter`, scaled to whole pixels
  per module.
- `barcode` (feature `barcode`): `Code128` encodes ASCII text into a Code 128 symbol with
  automatic code set selection; `draw_barcode` paints it horizontally or vertically.
- `i18n` (feature `i18n`): the runtime of compile-time translations — catalogs generated by
  `twine-build` from Fluent / `.po` / TOML files implement `Language` (`enum Lang`) and
  `MessageKey` (`enum Key`); a reactive current language (`provide_i18n`, `use_i18n` /
  `expect_i18n`, `I18n::set_language`, `I18n::base_dir`, `I18n::font`); translated texts
  with compile-time checked arguments (`tr!(Key::Greeting, name = user)`); CLDR plural
  rules (`i18n::plural`).

Encoders are pure (`no_std` + `alloc`, no floating point) and allocate only when encoding.
Drawing never allocates and touches only the rows inside the painter's clip, so drawing in
horizontal chunks (partial display buffers) is pixel-identical to drawing at once.

**Other features**

- `log` / `defmt`: logging backend (target `"twine::extra"`); `std`: std conveniences.

#### macro twine_extra::tr!
```rust
macro_rules! tr {
    ($key:expr $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($key:expr, $($rest:tt)+) => { ... };
}
```
A translated text for a label (or any text property), in the current language of `provide_i18n`:

### mod twine_extra::barcode

Code 128 barcodes (LVGL `lv_barcode`): an encoder producing the symbol and drawing helpers.

`Code128::encode` turns ASCII text into Code 128 symbols with automatic code set selection
(B by default, C for runs of 4 or more digits, A for control characters), the modulo-103
check symbol and the start/stop patterns. `draw_barcode` paints the bars with a
`Painter`, horizontally or vertically.

#### struct twine_extra::barcode::Bars<'a>
Iterator over the bars of a `Code128`, see `Code128::bars`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Iterator

#### struct twine_extra::barcode::Code128
A Code 128 symbol: the sequence of symbol values from the start code to the stop code.
Methods of `Code128`:
- `pub fn encode(text: &str) -> Result<Self, twine_extra::barcode::Code128Error>` — Encodes ASCII `text`.
  Errors: `Code128Error::Empty` for empty `text`; `Code128Error::InvalidChar` naming the first character that is not ASCII.
- `pub fn symbols(&self) -> &[u8]` — Symbol values: start code, data (including code set switches and shifts), check symbol, stop code (106).
- `pub fn check_symbol(&self) -> u8` — The modulo-103 check symbol.
- `pub fn module_count(&self) -> u32` — Width of the symbol in modules, without quiet zones.
- `pub fn widths(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = u8> + '_` — Bar and space widths in modules, alternating, bar first (the pattern of every symbol in order).
- `pub fn bars(&self) -> twine_extra::barcode::Bars<'_>` — The bars as `(first module, width in modules)`, left to right.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_extra::barcode::Code128Error
Why text could not be encoded.
Variants:
- `Empty` — The text is empty.
- `InvalidChar { index: usize, ch: char }` — The text contains a character outside ASCII (Code 128 encodes code points 0–127).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Display

#### struct twine_extra::barcode::BarcodeStyle
Colors, module size, direction and quiet zone used by `draw_barcode`.
Fields:
- `dark: twine_core::Color` — Color of the bars.
- `light: twine_core::Color` — Color of the spaces, the quiet zones and the rest of the area.
- `scale: u8` — Pixels per module (0 is treated as 1).
- `orientation: twine_extra::barcode::Orientation` — Reading direction.
- `quiet_zone: u8` — Light margin before and after the symbol in modules (Code 128 needs at least 10).
Methods of `BarcodeStyle`:
- `pub fn length_px(&self, code: &twine_extra::barcode::Code128) -> i32` — Length in pixels along the reading direction: `(modules + 2 × quiet_zone) × scale`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### enum twine_extra::barcode::Orientation
Direction in which a barcode is read.
Variants:
- `Horizontal` — Read left to right; bars are vertical.
- `Vertical` — Read top to bottom; bars are horizontal.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### fn twine_extra::barcode::draw_barcode
`pub fn draw_barcode(p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, code: &twine_extra::barcode::Code128, style: &twine_extra::barcode::BarcodeStyle)`
Draws `code` in `area`: the area is filled with `style.light` once, then the bars span the whole area across the reading direction. Along it the symbol (with its quiet zones) is centred; a symbol longer than the area is clipped at both ends (make the area at least `BarcodeStyle::length_px` long). Only bars inside the painter's clip are drawn.

### mod twine_extra::i18n

Compile-time translations (the role of LVGL's `lv_translation`): a catalog generated at
build time from translation files, a reactive current language, and `tr!`
texts that follow it.

**The catalog**

`twine-build` (in `build.rs`) or `twine i18n` (the `twine-cli` tool) reads Fluent (`.ftl`),
gettext (`.po`) or TOML files — one per language — checks them and generates Rust:

- `enum Key`: one variant per message (`Key::Greeting`), with `const fn args()` (the
  argument names `tr!` checks at compile time) and `const fn id()`;
- `enum Lang`: one variant per language (`Lang::De`), with `code()`, `from_code()`,
  `base_dir()` (right to left for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, …), `font()` (the language's
  font, if the catalog names one), `ALL` and `DEFAULT`;
- one static message table per language, indexed by `Key` — every key in every language
  (missing translations were filled from fallback languages at build time), so nothing is
  searched, sorted or missing at run time.

The enums implement `MessageKey` and `Language`; `Message`, `Segment`,
`Plural`, `Variant` and `Selector` are the table's types. Include the generated
file in a module of its own:


**Showing texts**
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::Decimal
An integer or fixed-point number to format: `magnitude / 10^scale`, with a sign and display options. `Copy`; integers convert with `From`.
Methods of `Decimal`:
- `pub const fn new(mantissa: i64, scale: u8) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — `mantissa / 10^scale` (`Decimal::new(12345, 2)` is 123.45); `scale` is clamped to `MAX_SCALE`.
- `pub const fn unsigned(n: u64) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — A non-negative integer.
- `pub const fn min_fraction_digits(self, n: u8) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — Shows at least `n` fraction digits (padding with zeros; at most `MAX_SCALE`).
- `pub const fn max_fraction_digits(self, n: u8) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — Shows at most `n` fraction digits (rounding half to even, then dropping trailing zeros down to the minimum).
- `pub const fn percent(self) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — Formats as a percentage of 1 (`0.25` → `25%`, with the language's pattern).
- `pub const fn without_grouping(self) -> twine_extra::i18n::Decimal` — Writes the integer part without grouping separators.
- `pub fn operands(&self) -> Option<twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands>` — The CLDR plural operands of the number as `write` shows it (`1.0` has `v` = 1 and is `other` in English, `1` is `one`). `None` only beyond `u64`.
- `pub fn write(&self, format: &twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat, w: &mut dyn Write) -> Result` — Writes the number with `format`. Allocation-free.
  Errors: Only those of `w`.
- `pub const fn with(self, format: &twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat) -> twine_extra::i18n::number::Localized<'_>` — A `Display` of the number in `format` (for `text!`, `format!` or a `Write`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, From<i8>, From<i16>, From<i32>, From<i64>, From<u8>, From<u16>, From<u32>, From<u64>, From<isize>, From<usize>

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat
How one language writes numbers (CLDR symbols and patterns of its default numbering system).
Fields:
- `decimal: &'static str` — Decimal separator (`"."`, `","`, `"٫"`).
- `group: &'static str` — Grouping separator (`","`, `"."`, `"\u{202F}"`, `"٬"`).
- `primary_group: u8` — Digits in the group nearest the decimal separator (3); 0 = never group.
- `secondary_group: u8` — Digits in the further groups (3, or 2 for the Indian `12,34,567`).
- `min_grouping: u8` — Grouping starts only when the integer part has at least `primary_group + min_grouping` digits (Spanish and Polish: 2, so `1234` but `12 345`).
- `minus: &'static str` — Minus sign, with any bidi marks (`"-"`, `"−"`, `"\u{61C}-"`).
- `percent_prefix: &'static str` — Text before a percentage (`""`, Turkish `"%"`).
- `percent_suffix: &'static str` — Text after a percentage (`"%"`, German `"\u{A0}%"`).
- `zero: char` — The digit zero of the numbering system (`'0'`, Arabic-Indic `'٠'`, Extended Arabic-Indic `'۰'`); digits 1–9 follow it in Unicode.
Methods of `NumberFormat`:
- `const ROOT: twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat` — CLDR's root locale: `1,234.5`, `-1`, `12%`, ASCII digits.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory
A CLDR plural category.
Variants:
- `Zero` — `zero` (e.g. Arabic 0, Latvian 10).
- `One` — `one` (e.g. English 1, French 0 and 1, Russian 21).
- `Two` — `two` (e.g. Arabic and Hebrew 2).
- `Few` — `few` (e.g. Russian 2–4, Polish 22).
- `Many` — `many` (e.g. Russian 5–20, French 1 000 000).
- `Other` — `other`: everything else (every language has it).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands
The CLDR operands of a number: its absolute integer part `i`, the number of visible fraction digits `v` and the visible fraction digits `f` as an integer (`"1.50"`: i = 1, v = 2, f = 50). `n` (the absolute value) is `i` when `f` is 0; `t` is `f` without trailing zeros.
Methods of `PluralOperands`:
- `pub const fn integer(n: u64) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands` — The operands of a non-negative integer.
- `pub fn decimal(negative: bool, i: u64, v: u8, f: u64) -> Option<twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands>` — The operands of a decimal number with absolute integer part `i` and `v` visible fraction digits `f` (`1.50`: `i` = 1, `v` = 2, `f` = 50); what a formatted `Decimal` shows. `None` when `v` > 18 or `f` has more than `v` digits.
- `pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands>` — The operands of a number written in plain decimal notation (`"3"`, `"-2"`, `"1.50"`; no grouping separators, no exponent): what CLDR rules are defined on. `None` for any other text, or when the number does not fit (more than 18 fraction digits or an integer part above `u64::MAX`).
- `pub fn of(value: &dyn Display) -> Option<twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands>` — The operands of `value` as it displays (formatted into a 40-byte stack buffer, no allocation): `None` when the text is not a plain decimal number (see `parse`). This is how `tr!` reads the argument a plural message chooses on, so the category always matches the digits shown.
- `pub const fn i(&self) -> u64` — The absolute integer part `i`.
- `pub const fn v(&self) -> u8` — The number of visible fraction digits `v`.
- `pub const fn f(&self) -> u64` — The visible fraction digits `f` (with trailing zeros).
- `pub const fn t(&self) -> u64` — The visible fraction digits without trailing zeros `t`.
- `pub const fn is_negative(&self) -> bool` — Whether the number is negative (the rules use the absolute value).
- `pub const fn n_integer(&self) -> Option<u64>` — `n` when it is an integer (`f` = 0), else `None`: CLDR conditions on `n` (`n = 1`, `n % 10 = 3..9`) only hold for integral values.
- `pub const fn is_exactly(&self, n: u64) -> bool` — Whether the value is exactly the non-negative integer `n` (what a `[0]` variant matches).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### type twine_extra::i18n::PluralRule
`pub type PluralRule = fn(twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
A plural rule: the category of a number in one language.

#### const twine_extra::i18n::MAX_ARGS
`pub const MAX_ARGS: usize = 8`
The most arguments a message may have (the generator refuses more).

#### enum twine_extra::i18n::Arg<'a>
The value of one message argument.

- `Text(&'a dyn Display)` — Any other value, shown as it displays.
Methods of `Arg`:
- `pub fn operands(&self) -> Option<twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands>` — The CLDR plural operands of the value as shown in language `lang` (`None`: not a plain number).
- `pub fn write(&self, lang: usize, w: &mut dyn Write) -> Result` — Writes the value as shown in language number `lang` (an index into `Language::ALL`).
  Errors: Only those of `w`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### enum twine_extra::i18n::Segment
One piece of a message: literal text or an argument's value.
Variants:
- `Text(&'static str)` — Literal text.
- `Arg(u8)` — The argument at this index of the key's `args()`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_extra::i18n::Selector
What a plural `Variant` matches.
Variants:
- `Exact(u64)` — Exactly this non-negative integer (`[0]` in Fluent, `"0" = …` in TOML); checked before the categories.
- `Category(twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory)` — A CLDR category of the language's rule.

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::Variant
One variant of a `Plural` message.

- `segments: &'static [twine_extra::i18n::Segment]` — Its text.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::Plural
A message that chooses its text by the plural category of an argument.
Fields:
- `arg: u8` — Index (in the key's `args()`) of the argument it chooses on.
- `variants: &'static [twine_extra::i18n::Variant]` — The variants, exact values first.
- `other: &'static [twine_extra::i18n::Segment]` — The text when no variant matches (or the argument is not a plain number).
Methods of `Plural`:
- `pub fn select(&self, arg: Option<&twine_extra::i18n::Arg<'_>>, rule: twine_extra::i18n::PluralRule) -> &'static [twine_extra::i18n::Segment]` — The variant for the value `arg` (its plural operands as shown) under `rule`: an exact match, else the category's variant, else `other`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_extra::i18n::Message
One message of one language in a generated catalog.
Variants:
- `Text(&'static str)` — A text without arguments.
- `Format(&'static [twine_extra::i18n::Segment])` — A text with arguments.
- `Plural(&'static twine_extra::i18n::Plural)` — A plural choice.
Methods of `Message`:
- `pub const fn as_static(&self) -> Option<&'static str>` — The text when the message has no arguments, else `None`.
- `pub fn write(&self, w: &mut dyn Write, args: &[twine_extra::i18n::Arg<'_>], lang: usize, rule: twine_extra::i18n::PluralRule)` — Writes the message with `args` (the key's arguments in `args()` order) in language number `lang` (index into `Language::ALL`, for number formats) with its plural `rule`. A missing argument writes nothing.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### trait twine_extra::i18n::Language
`pub trait Language: Copy + PartialEq + 'static`
A language of a generated catalog (the generated `Lang` enum implements it).
Items:
- `const DEFAULT: Self` — The default language (the others fall back to it).
- `const ALL: &'static [Self]` — Every language, in declaration order.
- `fn index(self) -> usize` — Position in `ALL`.
- `fn code(self) -> &'static str` — The language code (`"en"`, `"pt-BR"`).
- `fn base_dir(self) -> twine_style::BaseDir` — The base text direction.
- `fn font(self) -> Option<&'static twine_text::Font>` — The language's font, if the catalog names one.
- `fn plural_rule(self) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralRule` — The CLDR plural rule.
- `const NUMBER_FORMATS: &'static [twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat]` — How each language writes numbers, indexed by `index` (CLDR data generated for the catalog's languages; linked only when a number is formatted).
- `fn number_format(self) -> &'static twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat (provided)` — How this language writes numbers.
- `fn messages(self) -> &'static [twine_extra::i18n::Message]` — The messages, indexed by `MessageKey::index`.

#### trait twine_extra::i18n::MessageKey
`pub trait MessageKey: Copy + 'static`
A message key of a generated catalog (the generated `Key` enum implements it).
Items:
- `type Lang: twine_extra::i18n::Language` — The catalog's language type.
- `fn index(self) -> usize` — Position in each language's `messages`.
- `fn id(self) -> &'static str` — The identifier in the translation files (shown when a message is missing).

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::I18n<L: twine_extra::i18n::Language>
The current language of a catalog, provided as a context by `provide_i18n`. `Copy`: capture it in event handlers.
Methods of `I18n`:
- `pub fn set_language(&self, lang: L)` — Switches to `lang`; every `tr!` text follows (only bindings re-run, no allocation). Idempotent: the same language changes nothing.
- `pub fn language(&self) -> L` — The current language (tracked: a binding reading it re-runs on a switch).
- `pub fn language_untracked(&self) -> L` — The current language without tracking.
- `pub fn base_dir(&self) -> twine_style::BaseDir` — The current language's base direction (tracked): `.base_dir(move || i18n.base_dir())`.
- `pub fn font(&self) -> Option<&'static twine_text::Font>` — The current language's font, if the catalog names one (tracked).
- `pub fn number(&self, value: impl Into<twine_extra::i18n::Decimal>) -> twine_extra::i18n::number::Localized<'static>` — `value` localized in the current language (tracked): a `Display` for `text!` or `format!` (`label(text!("{}", i18n.number(n.get())))`).
- `pub fn text<K: twine_extra::i18n::MessageKey<Lang = L>>(&self, key: K) -> &'static str` — The text of `key` (a message without arguments) in the current language (tracked). A key with arguments gives its identifier and logs a warning: show those with `tr!`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::provide_i18n
`pub fn provide_i18n<L: twine_extra::i18n::Language>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope, initial: L) -> twine_extra::i18n::I18n<L>`
Provides language `initial` of catalog `L` to `cx` and its descendants, for `tr!`, `use_i18n` and `expect_i18n`.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::use_i18n
`pub fn use_i18n<L: twine_extra::i18n::Language>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> Result<twine_extra::i18n::I18n<L>, twine_reactive::MissingContext>`
The `I18n` of catalog `L` provided to `cx` or an ancestor by `provide_i18n`, or `MissingContext` naming it when there is none — the non-panicking form (`.ok()` for code that works with and without translations; see `expect_i18n`). A scope-chain walk without allocation (`Scope` § Context values): look it up once while building.
Errors: `MissingContext` naming `I18n<L>` when no ancestor provides one.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::expect_i18n
`pub fn expect_i18n<L: twine_extra::i18n::Language>(cx: twine_reactive::Scope) -> twine_extra::i18n::I18n<L>`
The `I18n` of catalog `L` provided to `cx` or an ancestor by `provide_i18n`: the panicking form of `use_i18n`, a thin `#[track_caller]` wrapper for application code below `provide_i18n` (e.g. a language picker).
Panics: If no ancestor of `cx` called `provide_i18n` for `L`, with `"context twine_extra::i18n::I18n<…> not provided"` at the caller's location (`MissingContext`).

Re-exports in `twine_extra::i18n`:
- `BaseDir` = `twine_style::BaseDir`
- `Font` = `twine_text::Font`

### mod twine_extra::i18n::number

Locale-aware number formatting without floating point or allocation: `Decimal` (an
integer or a fixed-point value with fraction-digit options) written with a language's
`NumberFormat` (decimal and grouping separators, grouping sizes — Indian `12,34,567`
included —, minus sign, percent pattern and native digits such as Arabic-Indic `٠١٢`).

The generated catalog holds one `NumberFormat` per language (CLDR data, chosen at build
time; `Language::NUMBER_FORMATS`), and `tr!` formats integer and `Decimal`
arguments with the current language's. Nothing of it is linked unless a number is
formatted.

#### const twine_extra::i18n::number::MAX_SCALE
`pub const MAX_SCALE: u8 = 18`
The largest scale (fraction digits) a `Decimal` carries.

#### struct twine_extra::i18n::number::Localized<'a>
A `Decimal` with its `NumberFormat`: `Display` writes it localized.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Display

Re-exports in `twine_extra::i18n::number`:
- `NumberFormat` — same as `twine_extra::i18n::NumberFormat`
- `Decimal` — same as `twine_extra::i18n::Decimal`

### mod twine_extra::i18n::plural

CLDR plural rules: `PluralCategory`, the operands of a number (`PluralOperands`) and one
function per rule (named after a language that uses it; the generated catalog picks the
function of each language, `twine_build::i18n::RULES` lists which languages use which).

The rules are CLDR 44 cardinal rules evaluated on integer operands (no floating point):
decimals are described by their visible fraction digits, exactly as CLDR defines them
(`"1.0"` and `"1"` differ: in English `1 item` but `1.0 items`).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::other
`pub fn other(_: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
No plural distinction: always `other` (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, …).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::en
`pub fn en(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
`one: i = 1 and v = 0` (English, German, Dutch, Swedish, Finnish, Estonian, Urdu, …).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::tr
`pub fn tr(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
`one: n = 1` (Turkish, Greek, Hungarian, Bulgarian, Norwegian, Albanian, …).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::fr
`pub fn fr(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
`one: i = 0,1`; `many`: millions (French, Brazilian Portuguese).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::es
`pub fn es(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
`one: n = 1`; `many`: millions (Spanish).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::it
`pub fn it(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
`one: i = 1 and v = 0`; `many`: millions (Italian, Catalan, European Portuguese).

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::ru

Russian and Ukrainian: `one` 1, 21, 31…; `few` 2–4, 22–24…; `many` 0, 5–20, 25–30…; `other` decimals.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::ar
`pub fn ar(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`
Arabic: `zero` 0; `one` 1; `two` 2; `few` 3–10, 103–110…; `many` 11–99, 111–199…; `other` 100–102, decimals.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::he

Hebrew: `one` 1 (and 0.x); `two` 2; `other` everything else.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::hi

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::da

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::is

Icelandic: `one: t = 0 and i % 10 = 1 and i % 100 != 11 or t % 10 = 1 and t % 100 != 11`.

#### fn twine_extra::i18n::plural::lt
`pub fn lt(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`

`pub fn ro(o: twine_extra::i18n::PluralOperands) -> twine_extra::i18n::PluralCategory`

Filipino: `one` unless the last digit is 4, 6 or 9 (1, 2, 3 always `one`).

### mod twine_extra::qrcode

QR codes (LVGL `lv_qrcode`): an encoder producing a module matrix and drawing helpers.

`QrMatrix::encode` turns bytes into the smallest QR code (versions 1–40) that holds them at
the requested error correction level. Numeric, alphanumeric or byte mode is chosen
automatically, and the level is raised while the data still fits the same version (like
LVGL). `draw_qr` paints a matrix into an area with a `Painter`.


The encoder is Nayuki's QR Code generator (`qrcodegen-no-heap`, MIT), which needs no heap by
itself; this module allocates its scratch buffers only while encoding (≈ 2 × 3.9 KiB for the
largest version, less for small codes) and keeps just the packed matrix (≤ 4 KiB).

#### struct twine_extra::qrcode::QrLayout
Where a QR code lands in an area: whole pixels per module, centred.
Fields:
- `scale: i32` — Pixels per module (at least 1).
- `origin: twine_core::Point` — Top-left corner of module (0, 0) (inside the quiet zone).
Methods of `QrLayout`:
- `pub fn fit(area: twine_core::Rect, modules: u8, quiet_zone: u8) -> Option<Self>` — Fits a code of `modules` modules per side plus `quiet_zone` modules on each side into `area`: `scale = floor(min(w, h) / (modules + 2 × quiet_zone))`, centred. `None` when not even one pixel per module fits.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_extra::qrcode::QrStyle
Colors and quiet zone used by `draw_qr`.
Fields:
- `dark: twine_core::Color` — Color of dark modules.
- `light: twine_core::Color` — Color of light modules, the quiet zone and the rest of the area.
- `quiet_zone: u8` — Width of the light margin around the code in modules. The standard asks for 4; phones read codes with 1–2 as long as the surrounding area is light.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### fn twine_extra::qrcode::draw_qr
`pub fn draw_qr(p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, qr: &twine_extra::qrcode::QrMatrix, style: &twine_extra::qrcode::QrStyle) -> Option<twine_extra::qrcode::QrLayout>`
Draws `qr` centred in `area`: the whole area is filled with `style.light` once, then every run of dark modules becomes one filled rectangle. Only rows inside the painter's clip are visited. Returns the layout used, or `None` (after a warning, drawing `draw_qr_placeholder` instead) when the area is too small for one pixel per module.

#### fn twine_extra::qrcode::draw_qr_placeholder
`pub fn draw_qr_placeholder(p: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, area: twine_core::Rect, style: &twine_extra::qrcode::QrStyle)`
Draws the stand-in for a code that cannot be shown (data too long, area too small): the area filled with `style.light` and outlined with `style.dark` (1/16 of the shorter side, at least 1 px).

#### struct twine_extra::qrcode::DarkRuns<'a>
Iterator over the dark runs of one matrix row, see `QrMatrix::dark_runs`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Iterator

#### enum twine_extra::qrcode::Ecc
Error correction level. Higher levels survive more damage but need a larger code.
Variants:
- `Low` — About 7 % of the codewords can be restored.
- `Medium` — About 15 % of the codewords can be restored (the default, like LVGL).
- `Quartile` — About 25 % of the codewords can be restored.
- `High` — About 30 % of the codewords can be restored.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

#### enum twine_extra::qrcode::QrError
Why data could not be encoded.
Variants:
- `DataTooLong { len: usize }` — The data does not fit in a version 40 code at the requested error correction level.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Display

#### struct twine_extra::qrcode::QrMatrix
A QR code as a square matrix of dark and light modules.
Methods of `QrMatrix`:
- `pub fn encode(data: &[u8], ecc: twine_extra::qrcode::Ecc) -> Result<Self, twine_extra::qrcode::QrError>` — Encodes `data` into the smallest QR code that holds it with at least the error correction level `ecc`.
  Errors: `QrError::DataTooLong` when `data` does not fit the largest QR code (version 40) at level `ecc`.
- `pub fn size(&self) -> u8` — Modules per side, `17 + 4 × version` (21–177).
- `pub fn version(&self) -> u8` — The QR code version (1–40).
- `pub fn ecc(&self) -> twine_extra::qrcode::Ecc` — The error correction level actually used: at least the requested one, possibly higher when the data fits the same version at a higher level.
- `pub fn get(&self, x: u8, y: u8) -> bool` — Whether the module at column `x`, row `y` is dark (`false` outside the matrix).
- `pub fn row(&self, y: u8) -> &[u8]` — The packed modules of row `y` (MSB first, `ceil(size / 8)` bytes; bits past `size` are 0).
  Panics: If `y >= size`.
- `pub fn dark_runs(&self, y: u8) -> twine_extra::qrcode::DarkRuns<'_>` — The runs of dark modules in row `y` as `(first column, length)`, left to right (empty outside the matrix).
Implements: Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug

## crate twine_lottie

Documented with features: `std`.

**twine-lottie**

Plays Lottie (Bodymovin JSON) animations for the Twine GUI library: `load` parses a file
into a typed `Composition`, and `LottiePlayer` renders any frame of
it into a `twine-render` `Painter` through `twine-vector`
(anti-aliased fills and strokes, gradients, layers).

**Supported subset**

- Layers: shape, solid, null (as parents), precomposition (with time remapping `tm`, time
  stretch, start offset and a size clip); layer opacity, parenting, hidden layers, in/out
  points.
- Shapes: group (with transform and opacity), rectangle (rounded), ellipse, path, fill (fill
  rule), stroke (width, caps, joins, miter limit, dashes), gradient fill and stroke (linear;
  radial with highlight), trim paths (simultaneous and individual), repeater (copies,
  offset, transform, start/end opacity, stacking order).
- Animated properties with linear, hold and cubic-bezier keyframes (per-axis easing),
  spatial tangents for positions, old files with end values `e`.
- Masks (add, subtract, intersect, none; opacity; inverted) and alpha track mattes (normal
  and inverted).

Not supported: expressions, text, image and audio layers, effects, blend modes, luma mattes,
mask expansion, 3-D layers, auto-orient, merge paths, rounded corners, offset paths,
polystars and other shape modifiers. They are ignored and reported once per file with
`warn!(target: "twine::lottie", "lottie: unsupported {}", what)` and listed in
`Composition::unsupported`.

**Widget**

`widget::Lottie` plays a composition in the engine: an animation drives the frame, and
the widget re-renders its own `Argb8888` buffer only when the integer frame changes.
`view::lottie` is its declarative view (`.playing`, `.looping`, `.frame`, `.speed`,
`.on_complete`).

**Floating point**

Lottie data is float-based, so this crate uses `f32` (it is the documented exception to
Twine's fixed-point rule): an FPU is needed for good performance. Geometry is converted to
16.16 fixed point before it reaches `twine-vector`, so rasterization stays integer and
deterministic; MCUs without an FPU (RP2040, ESP32-C3) run it with soft-float, only slower.
The small math functions needed (`sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `sqrt`, `exp`, `ln`) are implemented
in the crate, so no `libm` is required.

**Memory**

The composition model lives on the heap (roughly the size of the JSON). Rendering reuses
scratch buffers owned by the player: the contours of the largest shape layer, and per
offscreen nesting level an `Argb8888` strip of at most
`RenderConfig::layer_buf_bytes` bytes plus coverage strips
(¼ of that per mask/matte buffer). Nothing is allocated per frame once they have grown.

**Example**

```rust
use twine_core::{ColorFormat, Rect};
use twine_render::{DrawBuf, Painter, RenderCaches};
use twine_lottie::{LottiePlayer, load};

let json = br#"{"fr":30,"ip":0,"op":60,"w":64,"h":64,"layers":[
  {"ty":4,"ks":{"r":{"a":1,"k":[{"t":0,"s":[0]},{"t":60,"s":[360]}]},
                "p":{"k":[32,32]}},
   "shapes":[
    {"ty":"rc","p":{"k":[0,0]},"s":{"k":[30,30]},"r":{"k":4}},
    {"ty":"fl","c":{"k":[0.2,0.5,1,1]},"o":{"k":100}}]}]}"#;
let mut player = LottiePlayer::new(load(json)?);
let mut caches = RenderCaches::default();
let mut px = vec![0u8; 64 * 64 * 2];
let area = Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 64, 64);
let mut p = Painter::new(DrawBuf::new_packed(&mut px, ColorFormat::Rgb565, area)?, &mut caches);
player.render_frame(15.0, &mut p, area); // the square rotated by 90°
```

#### enum twine_lottie::LottieError
Why a Lottie file could not be loaded.
Variants:
- `Json { line: usize, column: usize }` — The data is not valid JSON (1-based position of the error).
- `Invalid(&'static str)` — The JSON is valid but not a usable Lottie composition.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, Error

#### fn twine_lottie::load
`pub fn load(json: &[u8]) -> Result<twine_lottie::Composition, twine_lottie::LottieError>`
Parses a Lottie (Bodymovin JSON) file.
Errors: A `LottieError` for input that is not valid Lottie JSON (syntax errors, missing required fields, values out of range).

#### struct twine_lottie::Composition
A whole animation: the root layers, the precomposition assets and the timing.
Fields:
- `w: f32` — Width in composition units.
- `h: f32` — Height in composition units.
- `fr: f32` — Frame rate (frames per second, > 0).
- `ip: f32` — First frame.
- `op: f32` — Frame after the last one (`op > ip`).
- `layers: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Layer>` — Root layers, top-most first (as in the file).
- `assets: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Asset>` — Precomposition assets referenced by precomp layers (`Layer::asset`).
- `unsupported: Vec<String>` — Unsupported features found in the file (sorted, each listed once).
Methods of `Composition`:
- `pub fn frame_count(&self) -> f32` — Number of frames (`op − ip`).
- `pub fn duration_secs(&self) -> f32` — Duration in seconds.
- `pub fn unsupported(&self) -> &[String]` — Unsupported features found in the file (each listed once).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::LottiePlayer
Plays a `Composition`: renders any frame into a `Painter`.
Methods of `LottiePlayer`:
- `pub fn new(comp: twine_lottie::Composition) -> Self` — A player for `comp`.
- `pub fn composition(&self) -> &twine_lottie::Composition` — The composition.
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Bytes of scratch memory currently reserved (contours, paths, offscreen buffers).
- `pub fn fit(&self, dst: twine_core::Rect) -> (f32, f32, f32)` — The composition → screen transform that fits the composition into `dst` (contain, centered), as `(scale, offset_x, offset_y)`.
- `pub fn render_frame(&mut self, frame: f32, painter: &mut twine_render::Painter<'_>, dst: twine_core::Rect)` — Renders `frame` (composition frame number, fractional allowed) fitted into `dst` (contain, centered) and clipped to it. Allocates nothing once the scratch buffers have grown to the largest frame.
Implements: Debug

#### const twine_lottie::MAX_LAYER_DRAWS
`pub const MAX_LAYER_DRAWS: u32 = 4096`
Most layers drawn per frame (precomps can reference the same asset many times; this bounds the work of hostile files).

#### const twine_lottie::MAX_OFFSCREEN_DEPTH
`pub const MAX_OFFSCREEN_DEPTH: usize = 4`
Deepest nesting of offscreen layers (layers with opacity, masks or mattes inside each other).

#### const twine_lottie::MAX_PRECOMP_DEPTH
`pub const MAX_PRECOMP_DEPTH: u8 = 8`
Deepest nesting of precompositions (also stops reference cycles).

### mod twine_lottie::eval

Evaluating animated properties at a frame: `Lerp`, keyframe segment lookup (cached for
sequential playback), hold and cubic-bezier easing (per axis), spatial position tangents, and
layer time mapping.

Evaluation never allocates once the output buffers have their capacity: values are written
into caller-owned outputs (`Animatable::eval_into`).

#### struct twine_lottie::eval::Progress
Progress of an interpolation, one value per component (Lottie eases each axis separately). Components beyond the fourth use the fourth value.
Fields:
- `0: [f32; 4]`
Methods of `Progress`:
- `pub const fn uniform(t: f32) -> Self` — The same progress for every component.
- `pub fn get(&self, i: usize) -> f32` — Progress of component `i`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq

#### trait twine_lottie::eval::Lerp
`pub trait Lerp: Clone`
Values that can be interpolated between keyframes.
Items:
- `fn lerp_into(a: &Self, b: &Self, t: twine_lottie::eval::Progress, out: &mut Self)` — Writes the interpolation between `a` (progress 0) and `b` (progress 1) into `out`. Must not allocate once `out` has the needed capacity.
- `fn lerp_spatial(_a: &Self, _b: &Self, _to: twine_lottie::model::Vec2, _ti: twine_lottie::model::Vec2, _t: f32, _out: &mut Self) -> bool (provided)` — Spatial interpolation along the cubic `a, a + to, b + ti, b` (positions); returns `false` when the type has no spatial interpolation.
- `fn assign(out: &mut Self, src: &Self) (provided)` — Copies `src` into `out` (reusing `out`'s storage).
Implemented by: f32, twine_lottie::model::Vec2, [f32; 3], twine_lottie::model::Rgba, Vec<f32>, twine_lottie::model::PathData

#### fn twine_lottie::eval::cubic_bezier_ease
`pub fn cubic_bezier_ease(x1: f32, y1: f32, x2: f32, y2: f32, x: f32) -> f32`
CSS-style cubic-bezier easing `(x1, y1, x2, y2)` at time progress `x ∈ [0, 1]`: solves `bx(u) = x` with 4 Newton iterations, falling back to bisection, then returns `by(u)`.

### mod twine_lottie::model

The typed Lottie (Bodymovin JSON) model produced by `load`.

Field names follow the JSON keys where they are well known (`w`, `h`, `fr`,
`ip`, `op`, `ks`, …) so the model can be read side by side with a Lottie file. Only the
supported subset is represented; everything else is recorded in
`Composition::unsupported` and ignored.

Colors are `0..=1` floats, opacities and percentages `0..=100`, angles degrees, times frames.

#### type twine_lottie::model::Vec2
`pub type Vec2 = [f32; 2]`
A 2-D value (point, size, scale in percent).

#### type twine_lottie::model::Rgba
`pub type Rgba = [f32; 4]`
An RGBA color with `0..=1` channels (Lottie ignores the alpha channel of shape colors).

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Asset
A precomposition: a list of layers used by precomp layers.
Fields:
- `id: String` — Asset id (`id`), referenced by `Layer::ref_id`.
- `layers: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Layer>` — The layers, top-most first.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### enum twine_lottie::model::LayerKind
Layer type (`ty`).
Variants:
- `Precomp` — `0`: renders a precomposition asset.
- `Solid` — `1`: a solid color rectangle.
- `Null` — `3`: invisible, used as a parent.
- `Shape` — `4`: vector shapes.
- `Unsupported(u8)` — Any other type (image, text, audio, …): not rendered.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Layer
One layer.
Fields:
- `ty: twine_lottie::model::LayerKind` — Layer type.
- `name: String` — Name (`nm`), for logs.
- `ind: Option<i32>` — Index used by `parent` and `tp` references.
- `parent: Option<i32>` — `ind` of the parent layer.
- `parent_index: Option<usize>` — Resolved index of the parent in the same layer list.
- `ip: f32` — First visible frame (in the containing composition's time).
- `op: f32` — Frame after the last visible one.
- `st: f32` — Start time offset: the layer's local time is `(frame − st) / sr`.
- `sr: f32` — Time stretch (`sr`, 1 = normal).
- `ks: twine_lottie::model::Transform` — Layer transform.
- `shapes: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Shape>` — Shapes (shape layers), top-most first.
- `masks: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Mask>` — Masks, applied in order.
- `tt: Option<u8>` — Track matte type of this layer (`1` alpha, `2` inverted alpha; `3`/`4` luma are unsupported).
- `td: Option<u8>` — `1` if this layer is the track matte of the next layer (not rendered by itself).
- `tp: Option<i32>` — `ind` of the matte layer (newer files); `None` = the layer above.
- `matte_index: Option<usize>` — Resolved index of the matte source layer in the same list.
- `ref_id: Option<String>` — Precomp asset id (`refId`).
- `asset: Option<usize>` — Resolved index of the asset in `Composition::assets`.
- `w: f32` — Precomp width (clip).
- `h: f32` — Precomp height (clip).
- `tm: Option<twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>>` — Time remapping of a precomp in seconds (`tm`).
- `sc: twine_lottie::model::Rgba` — Solid color (`sc`, RGB `0..=1`).
- `sw: f32` — Solid width.
- `sh: f32` — Solid height.
- `hidden: bool` — Hidden layers are not rendered (`hd`).
Methods of `Layer`:
- `pub fn local_frame(&self, frame: f32) -> f32` — The layer's local time for the containing composition's `frame`: `(frame − st) / sr`.
- `pub fn is_visible_at(&self, frame: f32) -> bool` — Whether the layer is visible at the containing composition's `frame` (`ip ≤ frame < op` and not hidden).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Transform
A transform (layer `ks`, group `tr`, repeater `tr`).
Fields:
- `anchor: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Anchor point `a`.
- `position: twine_lottie::model::Position` — Position `p` (or split `px`/`py`).
- `scale: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Scale `s` in percent.
- `rotation: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Rotation `r` (or `rz`) in degrees, clockwise.
- `opacity: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Opacity `o` in percent.
- `skew: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Skew `sk` in degrees.
- `skew_axis: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Skew axis `sa` in degrees.
- `start_opacity: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Repeater start opacity `so` (percent; repeater transforms only).
- `end_opacity: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>` — Repeater end opacity `eo` (percent; repeater transforms only).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Default

#### enum twine_lottie::model::Position
A position: one 2-D property or separate x and y properties.
Variants:
- `Combined(twine_lottie::model::Animatable<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>)` — `p` as one (possibly spatially interpolated) value.
- `Split(twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>, twine_lottie::model::Animatable<f32>)` — `p.s == true`: separate `x` and `y`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### enum twine_lottie::model::Animatable<T>
A property that is either constant or animated by keyframes.
Variants:
- `Static(T)` — A constant value.
- `Keyframed(twine_lottie::model::Keyframes<T>)` — Keyframes (at least two).
Methods of `Animatable`:
- `pub fn eval_into(&self, frame: f32, out: &mut T)` — Writes the value at `frame` into `out` (reusing its storage).
- `pub fn value(&self, frame: f32) -> T` — The value at `frame`.
- `pub fn is_animated(&self) -> bool` — Whether the value changes over time.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Keyframes<T>
Keyframes of an animated property, sorted by time, plus the index of the segment used last (so sequential playback finds the segment in O(1)).
Fields:
- `frames: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Keyframe<T>>` — The keyframes (at least two).
Methods of `Keyframes`:
- `pub fn eval_into(&self, frame: f32, out: &mut T)` — Writes the value at `frame` into `out`.
- `pub fn new(frames: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Keyframe<T>>) -> Self` — Keyframes from a list sorted by time.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Keyframe<T>
One keyframe: the value at time `t` and how it moves on to the next keyframe.
Fields:
- `t: f32` — Time (frame, in the layer's local time).
- `s: T` — Start value `s`.
- `e: Option<T>` — End value `e` of older files; `None` = the next keyframe's `s`.
- `hold: bool` — Hold keyframe (`h: 1`): the value jumps at the next keyframe.
- `ease: Option<twine_lottie::model::Ease>` — Easing towards the next keyframe (`o`/`i`); `None` = linear.
- `to: Option<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Spatial out tangent `to` (positions), relative to `s`.
- `ti: Option<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Spatial in tangent `ti` (positions), relative to the end value.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Ease
Cubic-bezier easing of one keyframe segment, per axis (Lottie allows a different curve per dimension). `x` is time progress, `y` value progress.
Fields:
- `out: [twine_lottie::model::Vec2; 4]` — Out control point `(x1, y1)` per axis (`o`).
- `inn: [twine_lottie::model::Vec2; 4]` — In control point `(x2, y2)` per axis (`i`).
- `axes: u8` — Number of axes given (1..=4); later axes reuse the last one.
Methods of `Ease`:
- `pub fn progress(&self, x: f32) -> twine_lottie::eval::Progress` — Eased progress of every axis for linear progress `x`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::PathData
A bezier path: vertices with in/out tangents (relative to their vertex).
Fields:
- `closed: bool` — Closed path (`c`).
- `v: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Vertices `v`.
- `i: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — In tangents `i`.
- `o: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Out tangents `o`.
Implements: Lerp, Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq

#### enum twine_lottie::model::Shape
A shape item (`shapes` / group `it`).
Variants:
- `Group(twine_lottie::model::Group)` — `gr`: a group with its own transform.
- `Rect(twine_lottie::model::Rectangle)` — `rc`: rectangle.
- `Ellipse(twine_lottie::model::Ellipse)` — `el`: ellipse.
- `Path(twine_lottie::model::PathShape)` — `sh`: bezier path.
- `Fill(twine_lottie::model::Fill)` — `fl`: solid fill.
- `Stroke(twine_lottie::model::Stroke)` — `st`: solid stroke.
- `GradientFill(twine_lottie::model::GradientFill)` — `gf`: gradient fill.
- `GradientStroke(twine_lottie::model::GradientStroke)` — `gs`: gradient stroke.
- `Trim(twine_lottie::model::TrimPaths)` — `tm`: trim paths.
- `Repeater(twine_lottie::model::Repeater)` — `rp`: repeater.
- `Unsupported(String)` — Any other item type (ignored; name recorded in `Composition::unsupported`).
Methods of `Shape`:
- `pub fn size(&self) -> u32` — Number of items in this item's subtree, itself included (group transforms are not items). Used to number items in depth-first order.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Group
A shape group.
Fields:
- `items: Vec<twine_lottie::model::Shape>` — The items (without the transform), top-most first.
- `transform: twine_lottie::model::Transform` — The group transform (`tr` item).
- `size: u32` — 1 + the sizes of all items.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq

#### struct twine_lottie::model::Rectangle
`rc`: a rectangle centred on `p`.
Fields:
- `p: twine_lottie::model::Animatable<twine_lottie::model::Vec2>` — Center.
