### mod twine_lottie::view

`lottie`: the declarative view of the `Lottie` widget.

#### fn twine_lottie::view::lottie
`pub fn lottie(src: &'static [u8], w: i32, h: i32) -> twine_lottie::view::LottieView`
A Lottie animation of `w × h` pixels (fitted, centered) from the JSON `src` (parsed once, never copied). It loops and starts paused; bind `playing`, `looping`, `frame` and `speed` to control it.

#### struct twine_lottie::view::LottieView
The view of `lottie`.
Methods of `LottieView`:
- `pub fn playing<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Plays (`true`) or pauses (`false`); default paused. Never panics. Playback is an essential animation: the motion preference does not stop it (see `Lottie`).
- `pub fn looping<M>(self, on: impl twine_view::IntoProp<bool, M>) -> Self` — Loops (default) or stops at the last frame. (`loop` is a Rust keyword.) Never panics.
- `pub fn frame(self, frame: impl twine_view::IntoModel<u32>) -> Self` — The current frame, two-way: a bound signal follows playback and seeks when set.
- `pub fn speed<M>(self, s: impl twine_view::IntoProp<twine_core::Scale, M>) -> Self` — The playback speed (256 = 1×). Range: any non-zero `Scale` — `Scale::pct(50)` half speed, `Scale::pct(200)` twice as fast, up to `u16::MAX / 256` ≈ 256× (a playback lasts at least 1 ms whatever the speed). `0` is ignored with a warning (use `playing(false)` to stop). While playing, a new speed restarts the playback animation from the current frame. Never panics.
- `pub fn on_complete(self, f: impl Fn() + 'static) -> Self` — Called when a non-looping animation reaches its last frame (once per playback).
Implements: Debug, View, ViewExt

### mod twine_lottie::widget

`Lottie`: an engine widget playing a Lottie animation (LVGL `lv_lottie`), redrawing only
when the frame changes.

#### static twine_lottie::widget::LOTTIE_CLASS
`pub static LOTTIE_CLASS: twine_engine::WidgetClass`
The class of `Lottie`.

#### const twine_lottie::widget::ANIM_FRAME
`pub const ANIM_FRAME: u16 = 0x4C54`
`AnimProp::Custom` id of the playback animation (its values are frame numbers).

#### struct twine_lottie::widget::Lottie
Plays a Lottie animation fitted (contain, centered) into its content area.
Methods of `Lottie`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A widget without an animation; playback loops by default (like LVGL).
- `pub fn set_src(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, data: &'static [u8])` — Loads the Lottie JSON `data` (parsed once; stored without copying). Idempotent for the same bytes. Invalid data logs a warning and shows a placeholder. The frame goes back to the first one; playback continues when it was playing.
- `pub fn total_frames(&self) -> u32` — Number of frames (`op − ip` of the composition; 0 without a valid source).
- `pub fn current_frame(&self) -> u32` — The current frame (`0..total_frames`).
- `pub fn is_playing(&self) -> bool` — Whether the animation is playing.
- `pub fn is_looping(&self) -> bool` — Whether playback loops.
- `pub fn speed(&self) -> twine_core::Scale` — The playback speed (256 = 1×).
- `pub fn frame_rate(&self) -> u32` — Frames per second of the composition (0 without a valid source).
- `pub fn set_frame(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, f: u32)` — Shows frame `f` (clamped to the last frame). Idempotent: the same frame neither re-renders nor invalidates. While playing, playback continues from `f`.
- `pub fn play(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Starts (or resumes) playback. Idempotent. A finished, non-looping animation starts again from the first frame.
- `pub fn pause(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>)` — Pauses playback at the current frame. Idempotent. The UI is idle while paused.
- `pub fn set_loop(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, on: bool)` — Sets whether playback loops (default `true`). Idempotent.
- `pub fn set_speed(&mut self, cx: &mut twine_engine::WidgetCx<'_>, speed: twine_core::Scale)` — Sets the playback speed (256 = 1×; 0 is ignored with a warning). Idempotent.
Implements: Debug, Default, Widget

## crate twine_hal

Documented with features: `async,platform-std`.

**twine-hal**

The hardware abstraction of the Twine GUI library: the traits a display, input device,
clock or platform (sleeping, waking, interrupt context) implements, and the plain data
types exchanged with the engine.

`twine-hal` sits directly above `twine-core` in the crate layering. It depends only on
`twine-core` (plus, behind the opt-in `platform-*` features, the one crate each platform
implementation needs), is `no_std` and **allocation-free**, so drivers (`twine-drivers`,
firmware crates) can implement it on any microcontroller. The engine (`twine-engine`), the desktop
simulator (`twine-sim`) and the test harness (`twine-testing`) consume it.

| Trait | Implemented by | Purpose |
|-------|----------------|---------|
| `DisplayDriver` | SPI/i80 panel drivers, `SimDisplay`, `MemoryDisplay` | blocking or DMA flush of rendered chunks (`begin_flush` / `poll_flush`) |
| `AsyncDisplayDriver` | async panel drivers (feature `async`) | `async fn flush` for embassy |
| `FramebufferDisplay` | memory-mapped panels (LTDC, RGB, DSI) | hands out framebuffers, `present` at vsync |
| `InputDevice` | touch, keypad, encoder, button drivers; mocks | non-blocking `read` of `InputData` |
| `AsyncInputWait` | IRQ-driven input drivers (feature `async`) | `wait_for_interrupt` |
| `Clock` | platform timers, `MockClock` | monotonic `Instant` |
| `Platform` | bare metal, RTOS and OS ports (`platform`) | wait for a deadline or a wake-up; `notify`; `in_interrupt` |
| `AsyncPlatform` | async runtimes (feature `async`), `EmbassyPlatform` | the async UI's clock and timer (bounded flushes) |

Touch drivers share `Calibration` (3-point affine mapping of raw resistive-touch readings)
and `TouchTransform` / `TouchMount` (raw capacitive-panel coordinates to the rotated
screen, derived from the display with `TouchTransform::for_display` when the engine calls
`InputDevice::fit_to_display`).

Data types: `DisplayInfo`, `ControlError`, `DrawBufferMem`, `DrawBuffer` (and `buffer_bytes`), `Calibration`,
`TouchTransform`, `TouchMount`, `Rotation` (from
`twine-core`), `InputKind`, `InputData`, `PointerData`, `KeypadData`,
`EncoderData`, `ButtonData`, `Key`, `PollHint`, `DeviceHealth`.

**Features**

- `async`: `AsyncDisplayDriver`, `AsyncInputWait` and `AsyncPlatform`.
- `platform-cortex-m`: `CortexMPlatform` (`WFE`/`SEV`, `SCB::vect_active`; adds `cortex-m`).
- `platform-riscv`: `RiscvPlatform` (`WFI`; adds `riscv` and `critical-section`).
- `platform-std`: `StdPlatform` (condition variable; needs `std`).
- `platform-embassy`: `EmbassyPlatform`, an `AsyncPlatform` over `embassy-time` (implies
  `async`).

No platform implementation is enabled by default: the application chooses (or writes) its
own, so no OS, executor or chip is assumed (see `platform`).
- `defmt`: `defmt::Format` for every public type (and `defmt` logging in `twine-core`).
- `log`: `log` backend of the `twine-core` logging macros.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints.

```rust
use twine_core::ColorFormat;
use twine_hal::{DisplayInfo, Key, buffer_bytes};

let info = DisplayInfo::new(320, 240, ColorFormat::Rgb565Swapped);
const BYTES: usize = buffer_bytes(320, 24, ColorFormat::Rgb565Swapped); // compile time
assert_eq!(BYTES, info.bytes_per_row() * 24);
assert_eq!(Key::from_name("Next"), Some(Key::Next));
```

#### struct twine_hal::DrawBuffer<const BYTES: usize>
The storage of one draw buffer: `BYTES` zeroed bytes, 4-byte aligned **by its type** (the alignment the engine requires of draw buffers; word-wise renderers and most DMA engines need it too).
Methods of `DrawBuffer`:
- `const ALIGN: usize` — The alignment of every `DrawBuffer` in bytes (4).
- `const ZEROED: Self` — A zeroed buffer (a constant, so `[DrawBuffer::ZEROED; N]` initialises a `static` array in `.bss`).
- `pub const fn len(&self) -> usize` — Length in bytes (`BYTES`).
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the buffer has no bytes (`BYTES == 0`).
- `pub const fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8]` — The bytes of the buffer.
- `pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [u8]` — The bytes of the buffer, mutably.
Implements: Debug, From<&'static mut twine_hal::DrawBuffer<BYTES>>

#### struct twine_hal::DrawBufferMem
An exclusively owned, `'static` byte buffer that the engine renders into and hands to a display driver for flushing.
Methods of `DrawBufferMem`:
- `pub fn new(buf: &'static mut [u8]) -> Self` — Wraps a `'static` buffer.
- `pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8]` — The bytes of the buffer.
- `pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [u8]` — The bytes of the buffer, mutably.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Length in bytes.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether the buffer has no bytes.
- `pub fn into_inner(self) -> &'static mut [u8]` — Unwraps the underlying `'static` slice.
- `pub fn is_aligned(&self, align: usize) -> bool` — Whether the start address is a multiple of `align` (some DMA engines require 4).
- `pub fn addr(&self) -> usize` — The start address, used to identify buffers in logs and tests (e.g. which of the two ping-pong buffers a flush used).
Implements: From<&'static mut twine_hal::DrawBuffer<BYTES>>, Debug, AsRef<[u8]>, AsMut<[u8]>

#### fn twine_hal::buffer_bytes
`pub const fn buffer_bytes(width: u16, rows: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> usize`
Bytes of one partial draw buffer of `rows` full-width rows of a `width`-pixel display in `format`: `rows × ⌈width × bpp / 8⌉` (sub-byte formats round each row up to whole bytes, exactly as the engine lays out a chunk; see `ColorFormat::stride`).

#### struct twine_hal::Calibration
A 3-point affine touch calibration.
Fields:
- `a: i64` — `x` coefficient of `x'`.
- `b: i64` — `y` coefficient of `x'`.
- `c: i64` — Constant term of `x'`.
- `d: i64` — `x` coefficient of `y'`.
- `e: i64` — `y` coefficient of `y'`.
- `f: i64` — Constant term of `y'`.
- `div: i64` — Common divisor (> 0).
Methods of `Calibration`:
- `const IDENTITY: Self` — The identity mapping (raw coordinates are passed through), e.g. for a calibration screen that needs raw values.
- `const DEFAULT_240X320: Self` — A typical calibration of the common 2.8" ILI9341 + XPT2046 module, in the panel's native 240 × 320 portrait coordinates: raw X (≈ 3900…200) runs along the native x axis (reversed), raw Y (≈ 200…3900) along the native y axis. Valid in every rotation (landscape `Rotation::Deg90` is the usual one).
- `pub fn from_points(raw: [(i32, i32); 3], screen: [(i32, i32); 3]) -> Option<Self>` — Solves the affine mapping that sends the three `raw` points to the three `screen` points (the classic 3-point solution, e.g. TI application report SLYT277).
- `pub fn apply(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> (i32, i32)` — Maps a raw point to screen coordinates (rounded to the nearest pixel, saturated to `i32`). Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### trait twine_hal::Clock
`pub trait Clock`
A monotonic clock with microsecond resolution.
Items:
- `fn now(&self) -> twine_core::Instant` — The current time.
Implemented by: &C, twine_hal::StdPlatform

#### trait twine_hal::AsyncDisplayDriver
`pub trait AsyncDisplayDriver`
Async display driver (embassy / embedded-hal-async), feature `async`.
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The driver's error type.
- `fn info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — Static description of the display.
- `async fn flush(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, buf: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Sends the pixels of `area` (layout as for `DisplayDriver::begin_flush`) and completes when the transfer has finished; `buf` is borrowed for the whole transfer.
- `async fn wait_vsync(&mut self) (provided)` — Waits for the tearing-effect / vsync signal. Default: completes immediately.
- `fn error_code(&self, error: &Self::Error) -> u32 (provided)` — A numeric code for `error` (see `DisplayDriver::error_code`). Default: `0`.
- `async fn idle(&mut self) (provided)` — Called when the UI has nothing more to draw (after a frame that left nothing due), for power saving; the next `flush` must wake the bus again. Default: completes immediately. Same contract as `DisplayDriver::idle`.
- `async fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction) -> Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sets the panel brightness (see `DisplayDriver::set_brightness`). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`.
  Errors: As `DisplayDriver::set_brightness`.
- `async fn sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool) -> Result<twine_core::Duration, twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sleeps (`true`) or wakes (`false`) the panel and returns its settle time (see `DisplayDriver::sleep`). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`.
  Errors: As `DisplayDriver::sleep`.
- `async fn set_rotation(&mut self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<twine_hal::DisplayInfo, twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Rotates in hardware and returns the new description (see `DisplayDriver::set_rotation`). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported` (software rotation).
  Errors: As `DisplayDriver::set_rotation`.

#### enum twine_hal::ControlError<E>
Why a display control (`DisplayDriver::set_brightness`, `DisplayDriver::sleep`, `DisplayDriver::set_rotation` and their async and framebuffer counterparts) was not applied.
Variants:
- `Unsupported` — The panel or driver cannot do this (the provided methods' answer). Nothing was sent.
- `Driver(E)` — The driver tried and failed (bus error, …); the panel's state is unknown.
Methods of `ControlError`:
- `pub fn map<F>(self, f: impl FnOnce(E) -> F) -> twine_hal::ControlError<F>` — Maps the driver error with `f` (e.g. to an error code); `Unsupported` stays.
- `pub const fn is_unsupported(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is `ControlError::Unsupported`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_hal::DisplayDriver
`pub trait DisplayDriver`
A blocking or DMA-capable display driver with an embedded frame memory (GRAM).
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The driver's error type (bus errors, invalid areas…).
- `fn info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — Static description of the display. Must not change while the engine runs, except through `set_rotation` (which returns the new description).
- `fn begin_flush(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, buf: twine_hal::DrawBufferMem) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Starts sending `buf` (the pixels of `area`, row-major, native format, `stride = area.width() * bpp / 8`) to the panel.
  Errors: The driver's error (`Self::Error`) when the transfer cannot start; see above for how the engine recovers.
- `fn poll_flush(&mut self) -> Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem>` — Polls for completion of the oldest flush in progress.
- `fn wait_vsync(&mut self) (provided)` — Blocks until the panel's tearing-effect / vsync signal. Default: no-op.
- `fn idle(&mut self) (provided)` — Called when the refresher becomes idle, for power saving (e.g. put the bus to sleep). Default: no-op. The next `begin_flush` must wake the bus again.
- `fn error_code(&self, error: &Self::Error) -> u32 (provided)` — A numeric code for `error`, reported with the flush fault (the engine's `FaultRecord` `code` and its `DriverErrorCode`) so the application can tell errors apart without parsing text. Default: `0` (no code). Called only on the error path.
- `fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction) -> Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sets the panel brightness (`Fraction::ZERO` = darkest the panel allows, `ONE` = brightest), for panels that dim themselves (AMOLED/OLED: MIPI DCS `WRDISBV`, SSD1306 contrast). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported` — LCDs are dimmed by their backlight, which the application drives (PWM).
  Errors: `ControlError::Unsupported` (default), or `ControlError::Driver` when sending failed.
- `fn sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool) -> Result<twine_core::Duration, twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Puts the panel to sleep (`true`: e.g. MIPI DCS `SLPIN`, frame memory kept) or wakes it (`false`: `SLPOUT`). Returns the settle time: how long the panel needs before it accepts the next command or pixels (MIPI DCS: 5 ms after `SLPIN`, 120 ms after `SLPOUT`). The engine sends nothing to the driver before it has passed, so the driver never blocks. Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`.
  Errors: `ControlError::Unsupported` (default), or `ControlError::Driver` when sending failed.
- `fn set_rotation(&mut self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Result<twine_hal::DisplayInfo, twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Rotates the picture in hardware (e.g. MIPI DCS `MADCTL`) and returns the new description: logical size and `rotation` of `rotation`, and `hw_rotation` telling whether flush areas are now logical (`true`) or still native. The format may not change. Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`, and the engine rotates in software instead (with the scratch buffers `Engine::reserve_rotation` allocated at start-up).
  Errors: `ControlError::Unsupported` (default), or `ControlError::Driver` when sending failed (the driver must then keep reporting its previous rotation).
- `fn read_back(&mut self, area: twine_core::Rect, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Reads the pixels of `area` back from the panel's frame memory (GRAM; MIPI DCS `RAMRD`) into `buf`, in the layout of a flush (see § Pixel layout: rows of `area`, tightly packed, in `DisplayInfo::format`; `area` in the same coordinates as a flush). It is the "actual" half of a display-integrity check: the engine compares a checksum of what the panel holds with a checksum of an independent re-render (`Engine::check_region`). Optional — the default answers `ControlError::Unsupported`; panels without a readable frame memory (no MISO line, write-only interfaces) keep it.
  Errors: `ControlError::Unsupported` (default), or `ControlError::Driver` when reading failed (bus error, `area` outside the panel, `buf` too short).

#### struct twine_hal::DisplayInfo
Static description of a display, returned by the drivers' `info()`.
Fields:
- `width: u16` — Width in pixels, **after** rotation (logical).
- `height: u16` — Height in pixels, **after** rotation (logical).
- `format: twine_core::ColorFormat` — Native pixel format (e.g. `Rgb565Swapped` for SPI MIPI panels).
- `rotation: twine_core::Rotation` — Rotation of the logical screen relative to the panel.
- `hw_rotation: bool` — `true`: the panel rotates in hardware and flush areas are logical; `false`: the engine rotates each chunk in software before flushing.
- `align: u8` — Flush areas' x, y, width and height must be multiples of this (1, 2, 8…; 0 is treated as 1 by the engine).
- `dpi: u16` — Dots per inch (used to scale default sizes, LVGL default 130).
Methods of `DisplayInfo`:
- `pub const fn new(width: u16, height: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Self` — A display of `width × height` in `format` with defaults: rotation `Deg0`, `hw_rotation = false`, `align = 1`, `dpi = 130`.
- `pub const fn with_rotation(self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — Sets the rotation.
- `pub const fn with_hw_rotation(self, hw_rotation: bool) -> Self` — Sets whether the panel rotates in hardware.
- `pub const fn with_align(self, align: u8) -> Self` — Sets the flush area alignment.
- `pub const fn with_dpi(self, dpi: u16) -> Self` — Sets the DPI.
- `pub const fn bytes_per_row(&self) -> usize` — Bytes of one full-width row in `format` (sub-byte formats round up).
- `pub const fn area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The whole (logical) screen as a rectangle at the origin.
- `pub const fn native_size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The panel's native (unrotated) size `(width, height)`: the logical size with the axes swapped back for `Rotation::Deg90` and `Rotation::Deg270`. Touch transforms (`TouchTransform::for_display`) and anything else that works in panel coordinates start from it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_hal::FramebufferDisplay
`pub trait FramebufferDisplay`
A memory-mapped panel with one or two framebuffers owned by the driver / display controller (STM32 LTDC, ESP32 RGB/DSI, Linux framebuffer).
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The driver's error type.
- `fn info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — Static description of the display.
- `fn framebuffers(&mut self) -> Option<(twine_hal::DrawBufferMem, Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem>)>` — Hands out the framebuffers: `Some((front, back))` on the **first** call, `None` on every later call (handing them out once avoids aliasing `&'static mut` memory). Each buffer holds `info().bytes_per_row() * info().height` bytes.
- `fn present(&mut self, index: u8) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Scans out framebuffer `index` (0 = first, 1 = second) from the next vsync on. Non-blocking.
  Errors: The driver's error (`Self::Error`) when the buffer cannot be scanned out; see above for how the engine recovers.
- `fn present_done(&mut self) -> bool` — `true` once the last `present` has taken effect (the buffer swap happened and the previous buffer may be drawn into).
- `fn error_code(&self, error: &Self::Error) -> u32 (provided)` — A numeric code for `error` (see `DisplayDriver::error_code`). Default: `0`.
- `fn set_brightness(&mut self, level: twine_core::Fraction) -> Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sets the panel brightness (see `DisplayDriver::set_brightness`). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`. Framebuffer displays cannot be rotated at run time.
  Errors: As `DisplayDriver::set_brightness`.
- `fn sleep(&mut self, sleep: bool) -> Result<twine_core::Duration, twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sleeps (`true`) or wakes (`false`) the panel and returns its settle time (see `DisplayDriver::sleep`). Default: `ControlError::Unsupported`.
  Errors: As `DisplayDriver::sleep`.

#### struct twine_hal::ButtonData

#### enum twine_hal::DeviceHealth
The health of an input device, as reported by `InputDevice::health`.
Variants:
- `Ok` — The last read succeeded (or the driver cannot detect failures).
- `Degraded { errors: u16 }` — The last `errors` reads failed; the driver reports its last good sample meanwhile.
- `Failed` — Too many consecutive reads failed: the device's samples are not trusted. The engine processes them as released until the device reports `Ok` or `Degraded` again.
Methods of `DeviceHealth`:
- `const DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER: u16` — Consecutive failed reads after which the drivers of `twine-drivers` report `Failed` by default (each driver has a `with_fail_after` builder).
- `pub const fn after_error(self, fail_after: u16) -> twine_hal::DeviceHealth` — The health after one more failed read: `Degraded { errors + 1 }`, or `Failed` once `errors` reaches `fail_after` (a `fail_after` of 0 or 1 fails at the first error). `Failed` stays `Failed`.
- `pub const fn is_failed(self) -> bool` — Whether the device is `Failed`.
- `pub const fn is_ok(self) -> bool` — Whether the device is `Ok`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_hal::EncoderData
Sample of a rotary encoder.
Fields:
- `diff: i16` — Steps rotated since the last read (positive = clockwise / down).
- `pressed: bool` — Whether the encoder's button is pressed.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_hal::InputData
Data read from an input device; the variant matches `InputDevice::kind`.
Variants:
- `Pointer(twine_hal::PointerData)` — Pointer sample.
- `Keypad(twine_hal::KeypadData)` — Keypad event.
- `Encoder(twine_hal::EncoderData)` — Encoder sample.
- `Button(twine_hal::ButtonData)` — Button sample.
Methods of `InputData`:
- `pub const fn kind(&self) -> twine_hal::InputKind` — The kind of device this data comes from.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_hal::InputDevice
`pub trait InputDevice`
An input device (LVGL `lv_indev` driver side).
Items:
- `fn kind(&self) -> twine_hal::InputKind` — The kind of the device; `read` returns the matching `InputData` variant.
- `fn read(&mut self) -> twine_hal::InputData` — Returns the current state without blocking (drivers cache the last sample).
- `fn poll_hint(&self) -> twine_hal::PollHint (provided)` — How the engine should schedule reads. Default: `PollHint::Periodic`.
- `fn rearm(&mut self) (provided)` — Called by the engine after processing, lets IRQ-based drivers re-arm their interrupt. Default: no-op.
- `fn health(&self) -> twine_hal::DeviceHealth (provided)` — The device's health after the last `read`. Default: `DeviceHealth::Ok` (a driver that cannot detect failures).
- `fn fit_to_display(&mut self, info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) (provided)` — Fits the device to the display it is registered for. The engine calls it once when the device is added (`Engine::add_input`, hence `UiBuilder::input`), before the first `read`, with that display's `DisplayInfo`. Default: no-op (keypads, encoders, buttons, and pointers that already report logical coordinates).

#### enum twine_hal::InputKind
The kind of an input device, which decides how the engine processes its data.
Variants:
- `Pointer` — Touch panel or mouse: a point plus pressed state.
- `Keypad` — Keyboard or keypad: `Key` presses.
- `Encoder` — Rotary encoder with a push button.
- `Button` — Physical buttons mapped to screen points.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_hal::Key
A key of a keypad (LVGL `LV_KEY_*` plus text characters).
Variants:
- `Up` — Arrow up.
- `Down` — Arrow down.
- `Left` — Arrow left.
- `Right` — Arrow right.
- `Esc` — Escape / cancel.
- `Del` — Delete the character after the cursor.
- `Backspace` — Delete the character before the cursor.
- `Enter` — Enter / confirm.
- `Next` — Focus the next widget.
- `Prev` — Focus the previous widget.
- `Home` — Home.
- `End` — End.
- `Char(char)` — A text character.
Methods of `Key`:
- `const NAMED: [twine_hal::Key; 12]` — Every named (non-`Char`) key.
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<twine_hal::Key>` — Parses a key name: a variant name (`"Up"`, `"Enter"`, … — case-sensitive) or a string of exactly one character (→ `Key::Char`).
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The variant name (`"Char"` for every `Key::Char`; use `Display` to get the character).

#### struct twine_hal::KeypadData

#### enum twine_hal::PollHint
How the engine should schedule reads of a device (power saving).
Variants:
- `Interrupt` — The device signals input by an interrupt (the app calls `Ui::notify_input()` from the IRQ); the engine reads it only after a wake, and continuously while pressed.
- `Periodic` — No interrupt: the engine wakes every `read_period` to poll it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### trait twine_hal::Platform
`pub trait Platform: twine_hal::Clock`
Sleeping and waking for a blocking run loop (bare metal, an RTOS task, a host thread), on top of the platform's `Clock`.
Items:
- `fn wait(&mut self, deadline: Option<twine_core::Instant>)` — Blocks (or yields the CPU) until `deadline` (on this platform's `Clock`; `None`: no deadline) or a `notify`, whichever comes first; may return earlier (see the contract on `Platform`). Returns at once when `deadline` has passed or a `notify` happened since the previous `wait` returned. Never panics.
- `fn yield_now(&mut self) (provided)` — Lets other work of equal priority run before the loop steps the UI again: called by run loops (`twine::run::blocking`) between two steps when the UI has more work at once (`Wake::Now`, e.g. the rest of a frame rendered in budgeted chunks). Unlike `wait` it never sleeps: it only gives up the rest of the time slice.
- `fn notify() where Self: Sized` — Wakes a `wait` in progress, or makes the next one return at once. Interrupt-safe, non-blocking and allocation-free: called from the context that wakes the UI (interrupt handler, task, thread, core) through `UiWaker::set_notify`.
- `fn in_interrupt() -> bool where Self: Sized (provided)` — Whether the caller runs in interrupt (exception) context. Default: `false`.
Implemented by: twine_hal::StdPlatform

#### struct twine_hal::StdPlatform
`Platform` for hosted operating systems with `std` (feature `platform-std`: Linux, QNX, macOS, Windows, the simulator, tests): a UI loop on a thread.
Methods of `StdPlatform`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A platform for the calling thread's UI loop. Notifications made before this call do not count for its first `wait`. Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Clock, Platform

#### trait twine_hal::AsyncPlatform
`pub trait AsyncPlatform: twine_hal::Clock`
Waiting for a deadline in an async runtime (feature `async`), on top of the platform's `Clock`: the time source and timer of the async UI (`AsyncUi`), which bounds every display flush with `EngineConfig::flush_timeout` by racing the flush against `poll_wait_until`.
Items:
- `fn poll_wait_until(&mut self, deadline: twine_core::Instant, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<()>` — `Ready` once `deadline` (on this platform's `Clock`) has passed; otherwise arranges for `cx.waker()` to be woken at `deadline` and returns `Pending`. May be polled any number of times, with any deadline (each poll stands alone; no state is kept between polls). Never panics.
- `fn wait_until(&mut self, deadline: twine_core::Instant) -> twine_hal::WaitUntil<'_, Self> where Self: Sized (provided)` — A future that completes at `deadline` (a `poll_wait_until` loop).
- `fn in_interrupt() -> bool where Self: Sized (provided)` — Whether the caller runs in interrupt context (see `Platform::in_interrupt`). Default: `false`.

#### struct twine_hal::WaitUntil<'a, P: twine_hal::AsyncPlatform + ?Sized>
The future of `AsyncPlatform::wait_until`: completes at its deadline.
Implements: Debug, Future

#### struct twine_hal::TouchMount
How a touch panel's raw axes relate to the display's native (unrotated) axes.
Fields:
- `swap_xy: bool` — The raw X axis runs along the native rows (raw X and Y swapped).
- `mirror_x: bool` — The (swapped) raw X axis runs opposite to the native columns.
- `mirror_y: bool` — The (swapped) raw Y axis runs opposite to the native rows.
Methods of `TouchMount`:
- `const ALIGNED: Self` — Raw axes aligned with the native display axes (no swap, no mirror).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_hal::TouchTransform
Maps raw panel coordinates of a touch controller to logical screen coordinates.
Fields:
- `swap_xy: bool` — Swap the raw X and Y axes.
- `invert_x: bool` — Mirror X after the swap.
- `invert_y: bool` — Mirror Y after the swap.
- `width: u16` — Logical screen width.
- `height: u16` — Logical screen height.
Methods of `TouchTransform`:
- `const PASS_THROUGH: Self` — Raw coordinates passed through unchanged (only clamped to `0..u16::MAX`): what a pointer driver reports before it is fitted to a display.
- `pub const fn identity(width: u16, height: u16) -> Self` — No swap or mirroring, clamped to `width × height`.
- `pub const fn for_rotation(rotation: twine_core::Rotation, native_w: u16, native_h: u16) -> Self` — The transform of an aligned touch panel (`TouchMount::ALIGNED`) on a display rotated by `rotation` whose native (unrotated) size is `native_w × native_h`. Software rotation and the `MADCTL` tables of `twine-drivers` turn the picture the same way, so this holds for both. Prefer `for_display`, which reads both from the display.
- `pub const fn for_display(info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> Self` — The transform of an aligned touch panel on the display described by `info`: its rotation and native size (`DisplayInfo::native_size`) select the axes, its logical size is the clamp. Compose a mounted panel with `with_mount`. Never panics.
- `pub const fn with_mount(self, mount: twine_hal::TouchMount) -> Self` — This transform with a touch panel mounted as `mount` in front of it: raw points are first mapped to the display's native axes by `mount`, then by `self` (a transform of an aligned panel, e.g. from `for_display`). The result is still one swap and two mirrors, so `apply` costs the same.
- `pub const fn inverse(self) -> Self` — The inverse transform: maps logical screen coordinates back to the raw (native, for an aligned panel) coordinates this transform maps from, clamped to the native size. Used where a known logical point must be expressed in panel coordinates, e.g. the targets of a touch calibration (`Calibration` maps to native coordinates, so it survives a rotation). Never panics.
- `pub fn apply(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> twine_core::Point` — Transforms a raw point. Never panics (a zero size counts as 1).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

Re-exports in `twine_hal`:
- `Rotation` = `twine_core::Rotation`

### mod twine_hal::buffer

Draw buffer memory: `DrawBufferMem` (an owned `'static` buffer), `DrawBuffer` (the
storage of one buffer, 4-byte aligned by its type) and `buffer_bytes` (the size of a
partial buffer, computed at compile time).

**Why `'static`**

A DMA transfer keeps reading a buffer after the call that started it has returned. If the
buffer were a borrowed `&mut [u8]` with a shorter lifetime, the borrow could end (and the memory
be reused) while the DMA engine is still reading it — undefined behaviour that the borrow
checker cannot see. Requiring `&'static mut [u8]` and **moving** the buffer into the driver
for the duration of a flush (`DisplayDriver::begin_flush` takes it by value,
`DisplayDriver::poll_flush` hands it back) makes this safe without any `unsafe` in user code:

- the memory lives forever, so it can never be freed under the DMA;
- while the driver owns the `DrawBufferMem`, nobody else can write to it.

**Where the memory comes from**

- **Firmware:** `twine::draw_buffers!` declares a `static` of `DrawBuffer`s sized with
  `buffer_bytes` at compile time and hands them out once
  (`BufferMode::partial_double_from(BUFS.take()..)` in `twine-engine`). The alignment the
  engine needs is a property of the type, the buffers are zeroed `.bss` (no flash), and no
  `static mut` or `unsafe` is involved.
- **Heap:** `BufferMode::alloc(..)` lets the engine allocate (and leak) the buffers once the
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

Re-exports in `twine_hal::buffer`:
- `buffer_bytes` — same as `twine_hal::buffer_bytes`
- `DrawBuffer` — same as `twine_hal::DrawBuffer`
- `DrawBufferMem` — same as `twine_hal::DrawBufferMem`

### mod twine_hal::display

Display traits and descriptions: `DisplayDriver`, `AsyncDisplayDriver` (feature `async`),
`FramebufferDisplay`, `DisplayInfo`.

This module is the complete contract between the Twine engine and a display driver. A driver
author needs nothing else.

**Which trait to implement**

| Panel | Trait |
|-------|-------|
| Panel with its own frame memory (GRAM) on SPI / i80, blocking or DMA | `DisplayDriver` |
| Same, driven from an async executor (embassy) | `AsyncDisplayDriver` (feature `async`) |
| Memory-mapped panel scanned out of MCU RAM (LTDC, RGB, DSI, Linux fb) | `FramebufferDisplay` |

**Pixel layout of a flush**

The pixels of `area` are row-major and tightly packed: row `r` starts at byte
`r * stride` with `stride = area.width() * bpp / 8` (for sub-byte formats rounded up to whole
bytes per row, see `ColorFormat::stride`). The format is `DisplayInfo::format`. The buffer
may be longer than `stride * area.height()`; trailing bytes are ignored.

**Coordinates and rotation**

Areas use `Rect` (half-open). When `DisplayInfo::hw_rotation` is `true`,
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_hal::input

Input devices: `InputDevice`, `InputData`, `Key`, `PollHint`, `DeviceHealth` and
the per-kind data.

Reading is always **non-blocking**: a driver caches its last sample (updated from an IRQ or
when read) and `InputDevice::read` returns it. Drivers whose reading depends on time
(debounced GPIO encoders, the monkey tester) take a `Clock` at
construction; the trait itself is time-free.

- `ButtonData` — same as `twine_hal::ButtonData`
- `InputData` — same as `twine_hal::InputData`
- `PollHint` — same as `twine_hal::PollHint`
- `DeviceHealth` — same as `twine_hal::DeviceHealth`
- `InputDevice` — same as `twine_hal::InputDevice`
- `AsyncInputWait` — same as `twine_hal::AsyncInputWait`

### mod twine_hal::platform

Platform services: `Platform` (wait for a deadline or a wake-up, blocking) and
`AsyncPlatform` (the same for async runtimes, feature `async`), plus opt-in
implementations behind cargo features.

Twine never owns the execution model: the UI is a step function (`Ui::update` returns
when to run again) plus wake-up signalling (`UiWaker`). A run loop needs three platform
services, all supplied by the application:

| Service | Item | Bare metal | RTOS | Hosted OS |
|---------|------|------------|------|-----------|
| time | `Clock` (the supertrait) | a hardware timer | the kernel tick | `std::time` |
| sleep until a deadline or a wake-up | `Platform::wait` | `WFE` / `WFI` | task notification with timeout | condition variable with timeout |
| wake the sleeping loop | `Platform::notify`, installed with `UiWaker::set_notify` | `SEV` / a flag | give the notification | notify the condition variable |
| "am I in an interrupt?" | `Platform::in_interrupt` | an interrupt-status register | the kernel's ISR query | `false` |

**One time source.** A platform *is* the clock of the loop it runs: the `Ui` is built with
a clone of it (`UiBuilder::platform(&platform)`, which also installs `notify` on the `Ui`'s
waker and registers `in_interrupt`), and the loop waits with the platform itself, so the
deadlines the `Ui` returns and the time the platform waits for are on the same clock.
Clones of every platform here read the same time base.

**Implementations (opt-in features, none by default)**

| Feature | Type | `wait` | `notify` | `in_interrupt` |
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

Re-exports in `twine_hal::platform`:
- `StdPlatform` — same as `twine_hal::StdPlatform`
- `Platform` — same as `twine_hal::Platform`
- `AsyncPlatform` — same as `twine_hal::AsyncPlatform`
- `WaitUntil` — same as `twine_hal::WaitUntil`

### mod twine_hal::touch

Touch coordinates: `TouchTransform` maps raw panel coordinates of a touch controller to the
logical (rotated) screen, `TouchMount` describes how the touch panel sits on the display.

A touch controller reports points in its own axes. Two things turn them into logical screen
coordinates:

1. the **mount** (`TouchMount`): how the raw axes relate to the display's *native* (unrotated)
   axes — a property of the module (some panels are glued with an axis mirrored or swapped);
2. the **display rotation** (`DisplayInfo::rotation`): how the logical screen is turned
   relative to the native panel — a property of the display configuration.

`TouchTransform::for_display` derives (2) from the display's `DisplayInfo`, and
`TouchTransform::with_mount` composes (1) in front of it. Pointer drivers do this in
`InputDevice::fit_to_display`, which the engine calls
when the device is registered for a display, so applications never derive native sizes or
rotation tables by hand.

Re-exports in `twine_hal::touch`:
- `TouchMount` — same as `twine_hal::TouchMount`
- `TouchTransform` — same as `twine_hal::TouchTransform`

## crate twine_drivers

Documented with features: `all,std,async,testkit`.

**twine-drivers**

Display, touch and input drivers of the Twine GUI library, implementing the `twine-hal`
traits on top of `embedded-hal` 1.0 buses. Everything is `no_std` and allocation-free and
works on any microcontroller HAL (the hosted Linux drivers `fbdev` / `evdev` use `std`).

| Module | Devices |
|--------|---------|
| `interface` | transports: `SpiInterface` (SPI + DC), `QspiInterface` (quad SPI) and friends |
| `interface` (DMA) | `DmaSpiInterface` over a chip's `DmaSpiBus` (feature `spi-dma`): SPI + CS + DC whose pixel transfers run by DMA while the next chunk renders, for blocking runtimes |
| `mipi_dcs` | generic MIPI DCS panel driver `MipiDcs` |
| `ili9341` | ILI9341 240 × 320 |
| `ili9342` | ILI9342C 320 × 240 |
| `ili9488` | ILI9488 320 × 480 (RGB666 over SPI) |
| `st7789` | ST7789 240 × 320, 240 × 240, 135 × 240 |
| `st7735` | ST7735R/S 128 × 160 (green/red/black tab), 80 × 160 |
| `st7796` | ST7796S 320 × 480 |
| `gc9a01` | GC9A01 240 × 240 round |
| `jd9853` | JD9853 172 × 320 IPS |
| `co5300`, `sh8601`, `rm67162` | QSPI AMOLED controllers (410 × 502, 368 × 448, 240 × 536) |
| `ssd1306`, `sh1106` | monochrome OLEDs (I2C/SPI, `I1` page conversion in `mono`) |
| `touch` | touch: XPT2046, `FT6x36`, `FT5x06`, GT911, CST816S, AXS5106L, STMPE811 |
| `encoder` | rotary encoder on GPIOs (quadrature + button) |
| `keypad` | key matrix on GPIOs |
| `fbdev`, `evdev` | hosted Linux: framebuffer display (`/dev/fbN`) and input events (`/dev/input/eventN`), with `std` |

Every display driver has a blocking flavour (`DisplayDriver`) and, with feature `async`, an
async flavour (`AsyncDisplayDriver`) that overlaps DMA transfers with rendering when the HAL
provides an async, DMA-backed `SpiDevice`.

**Atomics on chips without compare-and-swap**

The crate uses `portable-atomic` and does not choose its fallback: the application does. On
targets without atomic read-modify-write instructions — `thumbv6m` (RP2040, Cortex-M0/M0+)
and single-core `riscv32imc` (ESP32-C3) — add one of:

- `portable-atomic = { version = "1", features = ["critical-section"] }` plus a
  critical-section implementation (e.g. `embassy-rp`'s `critical-section-impl`,
  `cortex-m`'s `critical-section-single-core`), or
- `--cfg portable_atomic_unsafe_assume_single_core` in `RUSTFLAGS` (single-core chips only;
  esp-hal already enables `portable-atomic`'s `unsafe-assume-single-core` on the ESP32-C3).

Not both: `portable-atomic` rejects the combination. Other targets need nothing.

**Features**

Every driver and bus interface is behind its own cargo feature and nothing is enabled by
default: enable exactly what your board has, e.g. `features = ["ili9341", "xpt2046",
"async"]` (a panel feature enables the interface and the MIPI DCS core it needs). `all`
enables everything. No driver knows about pins or boards: constructors take the HAL's bus,
pin and delay objects.

- Interfaces: `spi`, `i2c`, `i80`, `qspi`; `mipi-dcs` (generic panel core for your own
  `PanelSpec`).
- Displays: `ili9341`, `ili9342`, `ili9488`, `st7789`, `st7735`, `st7796`, `gc9a01`,
  `jd9853`, `co5300`, `sh8601`, `rm67162`, `ssd1306`, `sh1106`.
- Touch and input: `xpt2046`, `ft6x36` (also `FT5x06`, FT3168), `gt911`, `cst816s`,
  `axs5106l`, `stmpe811`, `encoder`, `keypad`.
- Hosted Linux (need `std`, not in `all`): `fbdev` (`FbDev`), `evdev` (`Evdev`); see the
  `linux_fbdev` example of the `twine` crate.
- `async`: async interfaces and drivers (`embedded-hal-async`), `AsyncInputWait` for IRQ pins.
- `testkit`: recording mock buses (module `testkit`) for host tests of code built on these drivers.
- `defmt` / `log`: logging backends (target `twine::driver`).
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature, see
  `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository): the profile's lints.

```rust
use twine_core::Rect;
use twine_drivers::ili9341;
use twine_drivers::testkit::{BusOp, Recorder};
use twine_hal::{DisplayDriver, DrawBufferMem, Rotation};

// On hardware: `spi` is an `embedded_hal::spi::SpiDevice`, `dc`/`rst` are output pins and
// `delay` implements `DelayNs`. Here the recording mocks stand in for them.
let rec = Recorder::new();
let mut lcd = ili9341::new(rec.spi(), rec.quiet_pin("dc"), Some(rec.pin("rst")), Rotation::Deg90, &mut rec.delay()).unwrap();
let buf = DrawBufferMem::new(Box::leak(Box::new([0u8; 320 * 2])));
lcd.begin_flush(Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 320, 1), buf).unwrap();
assert_eq!(rec.ops().last(), Some(&BusOp::Pixels(640)));
```

### mod twine_drivers::co5300

CO5300 AMOLED controller on quad SPI (Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06: 410 × 502).

| | |
|-|-|
| Reference | Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06 BSP (`Arduino_CO5300`, `Arduino_GFX`, BSD) |
| Interface | QSPI (`QspiInterface`), up to 80 MHz on ESP32-S3 |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x55` → `Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | no row/column exchange (software 90°/270°), even flush areas (`align = 2`), visible area starts at column 22 on the 2.06" glass, brightness via `0x51` |

`0x63 0xFF`, `WRDISBV 0xD0`, `WCE 0x00`. The column offset of 22 is the vendor example's
`col_offset1`.

| Panel pin | Driver argument |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `SCLK`, `SDIO0`–`SDIO3`, `CS` | `bus`, your HAL's quad-SPI implementing `QspiBus` / `AsyncQspiBus` (on ESP32-S3: `twine-esp`) |
| `RESET` | `rst`: `Some(OutputPin)`, or `None` (software reset); some boards route it through an I/O expander that the firmware releases first |
| `TE` | optional, not used |

There is no backlight: set the brightness with `set_brightness` (DCS `0x51`).

### mod twine_drivers::encoder

Rotary encoder on two GPIOs (quadrature A/B) plus an optional push button:
`QuadratureDecoder` and `GpioQuadrature` (`InputKind::Encoder`).

**Decoding**

`QuadratureDecoder` runs the standard Gray-code state machine on every edge: of the 16
`(previous, current)` A/B combinations, the 8 valid single-bit steps count ±1, everything
else (no change, or both lines changed = a missed or bouncing edge) counts 0. Contact bounce
on one line therefore cancels out (+1 −1). Steps are accumulated and reported in detents
(`steps_per_detent`, default 4 for the common EC11-style encoders).

The decoder keeps its state in atomics (`portable-atomic`: plain loads/stores plus a
critical-section `fetch_add` on targets without CAS such as the RP2040), so it can live in a
`static` and be fed from a GPIO interrupt while the UI task reads it.

**Usage**

Polled (call `update` often enough not to miss edges — ≥ 1 kHz
for hand-turned encoders; `read()` calls it too):


Interrupt driven (RP2040 example wiring: A = GPIO 14, B = GPIO 15, button = GPIO 13, all
with pull-ups, common pin to GND): put the decoder in a `static`, call
`DECODER.on_edge(a.is_high(), b.is_high())` from the GPIO interrupt of both lines (any
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### struct twine_drivers::encoder::QuadratureDecoder
Lock-free quadrature state machine (see the module docs). Safe to share between an interrupt handler (`on_edge`) and the UI (`take`).
Methods of `QuadratureDecoder`:
- `pub const fn new(steps_per_detent: u8) -> Self` — A decoder reporting one detent every `steps_per_detent` valid steps (≥ 1; 4 for most encoders, 2 or 1 for half/quarter-step types). Starts in state `00`.
- `pub fn on_edge(&self, a: bool, b: bool)` — Feeds the current levels of A and B (call on every edge of either line).
- `pub fn take(&self) -> i16` — Takes the whole detents turned since the last call (positive = clockwise); partial steps are kept.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_drivers::encoder::GpioQuadrature<'d, A, B, BTN, C>
Rotary encoder with optional push button, implementing `InputDevice` (`Encoder`).
Methods of `GpioQuadrature`:
- `pub fn new(decoder: &'d twine_drivers::encoder::QuadratureDecoder, a: A, b: B, btn: Option<BTN>, clock: C) -> Self` — A polled encoder: `update` (and `read`) sample A and B.
- `pub fn new_isr(decoder: &'d twine_drivers::encoder::QuadratureDecoder, btn: Option<BTN>, clock: C) -> Self` — An encoder whose A/B edges are fed to `decoder` from an interrupt handler (`QuadratureDecoder::on_edge`); `update` only samples the button.
- `pub fn with_debounce(self, debounce: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Sets the button debounce time.
- `pub fn with_fail_after(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Reports the encoder `Failed` after `n` consecutive `update`s with pin errors (default `DeviceHealth::DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER`; see `health`). MCU pins that cannot fail (`Error = Infallible`) compile the checks away.
- `pub fn with_button_active_high(self, active_high: bool) -> Self` — Treats the button as active high (switch to VCC with pull-down).
- `pub fn update(&mut self)` — Samples A/B (polled mode) and the button. Call from a periodic task (≥ 1 kHz when polling A/B) or rely on `read`.
- `pub fn release(self) -> (A, B, Option<BTN>, C)` — Returns the pins and the clock.
Implements: Debug, InputDevice

### mod twine_drivers::ili9341

ILI9341 240 × 320 TFT controller (the common 2.4"/2.8"/3.2" SPI modules).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | ILITEK ILI9341 V1.11 |
| Max SPI clock | 10 MHz write per datasheet (t<sub>scycw</sub> = 100 ns); modules routinely run at 40–62.5 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x55` (RGB565) → `ColorFormat::Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | BGR glass (`MADCTL.BGR`); mirrored columns at `Deg0` (Adafruit mapping), no offsets, no inversion |

The init table is the one of `Adafruit_ILI9341` (`initcmd`, BSD license,
<https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit_ILI9341>), minus the commands the generic
`MipiDcs` init sends itself (`MADCTL`, `COLMOD`, `SLPOUT`,
`DISPON`). Every command was cross-checked against the ILI9341 datasheet V1.11 (register
names and parameter counts noted per entry; `0xEF` is undocumented but required by many
panels).

**Rotation**

`MADCTL` per rotation (Adafruit's `setRotation` values, with 90° and 270° exchanged so that
`Deg90` turns the picture like the engine's software rotation: the module is held turned
90° clockwise): `Deg0 = MX|BGR` (240 × 320 portrait), `Deg90 = MX|MY|MV|BGR` (320 × 240
landscape), `Deg180 = MY|BGR`, `Deg270 = MV|BGR`.

**Frame rate and tearing**
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::ili9488

ILI9488 320 × 480 TFT controller over SPI (18-bit colour only).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | ILITEK ILI9488 V1.00 |
| Max SPI clock | 20 MHz write per datasheet (t<sub>scycw</sub> = 50 ns); modules often run at 40 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x66` (RGB666, 3 bytes/pixel) → `ColorFormat::Rgb888` |
| Quirks | **slow**: the SPI interface has no 16-bit mode, so every pixel costs 3 bytes (1.5× RGB565) |

**Colour format**

The panel takes 3 bytes per pixel and uses the upper 6 bits of each. The engine renders
`Rgb888`, whose bytes are `B, G, R` in memory, and the driver sends them unchanged; the
panel's `MADCTL.BGR` bit swaps red and blue, so the spec **clears** it for the common modules
(whose glass needs `BGR` for `R, G, B` data). If red and blue appear swapped, use
`ILI9488.with_bgr(true)`.

The application must enable `Rgb888` rendering (the `color-rgb888` feature of the `twine`
crate); the engine rejects a display whose format it cannot render.

Init as mipidsi's `ili948x::init_common`: display function control `0xB6 [02 02 3B]`, `NORON`,
plus the generic sequence. Rotation uses `standard_madctl`.

**Wiring**
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

ILI9488 320 × 480, RGB666 over SPI, `BGR` bit clear (see the module docs).

A ILI9488 on 4-wire SPI (blocking): `MipiDcs` over `SpiInterface`.

#### type twine_drivers::ili9488::AsyncIli9488
`pub type AsyncIli9488<SPI, DC, RST> = twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::AsyncMipiDcs<twine_drivers::interface::SpiInterface<SPI, DC>, RST>`

### mod twine_drivers::interface

Byte-level transports for command/data display controllers: `DcsInterface` (blocking),
`AsyncDcsInterface` (feature `async`) and their implementations.

| Interface | Bus | Notes |
|-----------|-----|-------|
| `SpiInterface` | 4-wire SPI (`SpiDevice` + DC pin) | the usual MIPI DCS panel wiring; DMA happens inside the HAL's `SpiDevice` |
| `I2cInterface` | I2C (control byte `0x00` / `0x40`) | SSD1306 / SH1106 OLEDs |
| `I80Interface8`, `I80Interface16` | Intel 8080 parallel via GPIO bit-banging | slow (~1–3 MB/s), for completeness |
| `QspiInterface` | quad SPI (`QspiBus`, no DC pin) | AMOLED controllers (CO5300, SH8601, RM67162) |
| `DmaSpiInterface` | 4-wire SPI over a `DmaSpiBus` + CS and DC pins (feature `spi-dma`) | blocking runtimes with DMA: the pixel transfer of a flush runs while the next chunk renders |

A panel driver (`MipiDcs`, `Ssd1306`,
…) is generic over the interface, so the same panel works over any of them.

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::I2cInterface<I2C>
I2C transport for controllers that prefix every write with a control byte: `0x00` for commands (parameters are sent as command bytes), `0x40` for display data (SSD1306 datasheet §8.1.5, SH1106 datasheet "I2C-bus write data").
Methods of `I2cInterface`:
- `const DEFAULT_ADDR: u8` — The usual address of SSD1306/SH1106 modules (SA0 low).
- `pub const fn new(i2c: I2C, addr: u8) -> Self` — Wraps an I2C bus; `addr` is the 7-bit device address.
- `pub const fn addr(&self) -> u8` — The device address.
- `pub fn release(self) -> I2C` — Returns the bus.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface, AsyncDcsInterface

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface8<D, WR, DC>
8-bit i80 interface: `D0`…`D7` plus `WR` and `DC`; one WR strobe per byte.
Methods of `I80Interface8`:
- `pub fn new(data: [D; 8], wr: WR, dc: DC) -> Self` — Creates the interface; `data[i]` drives `Di`. WR is driven high (idle) on first use.
- `pub fn release(self) -> ([D; 8], WR, DC)` — Returns the pins.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface, AsyncDcsInterface

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface16<D, WR, DC>
16-bit i80 interface: `D0`…`D15` plus `WR` and `DC`.
Methods of `I80Interface16`:
- `pub fn new(data: [D; 16], wr: WR, dc: DC) -> Self` — Creates the interface; `data[i]` drives `Di`.
- `pub fn release(self) -> ([D; 16], WR, DC)` — Returns the pins.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface, AsyncDcsInterface

#### trait twine_drivers::interface::AsyncQspiBus
`pub trait AsyncQspiBus`
An async quad-SPI bus (feature `async`); same semantics as `QspiBus`. The future starts the transfer (DMA) on its first poll.
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The bus error type.
- `async fn write(&mut self, instr: u8, addr: u32, data: &[u8], lines: twine_drivers::interface::QspiLines) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — See `QspiBus::write`.
Implemented by: twine_drivers::testkit::RecordingQspi

#### trait twine_drivers::interface::QspiBus
`pub trait QspiBus`
A blocking quad-SPI bus with chip select: one call is one transaction.
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The bus error type.
- `fn write(&mut self, instr: u8, addr: u32, data: &[u8], lines: twine_drivers::interface::QspiLines) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Writes `instr` (8 bits) and `addr` (low 24 bits, most significant byte first) on one line, then `data` on `lines`, with chip select asserted for the whole transaction.
  Errors: The bus error (`Self::Error`) when the transaction fails.
Implemented by: &mut T, twine_drivers::testkit::RecordingQspi

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::QspiInterface<B>
The DCS transport over a `QspiBus` (see the module docs for the framing).
Methods of `QspiInterface`:
- `pub const fn new(bus: B) -> Self` — Wraps a QSPI bus.
- `pub fn release(self) -> B` — Returns the bus.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface, AsyncDcsInterface

#### enum twine_drivers::interface::QspiLines
Width of a transaction's data phase (instruction and address always use one line).
Variants:
- `Single` — Data on `D0` only (register writes).
- `Quad` — Data on `D0`–`D3` (pixel writes).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::SpiInterface<SPI, DC>
4-wire SPI transport: an `SpiDevice` (which owns chip select) plus a DC pin.
Methods of `SpiInterface`:
- `pub const fn new(spi: SPI, dc: DC) -> Self` — Wraps an SPI device and the DC pin.
- `pub fn release(self) -> (SPI, DC)` — Returns the SPI device and the DC pin.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface, AsyncDcsInterface

#### trait twine_drivers::interface::DmaSpiBus
`pub trait DmaSpiBus`
The chip-specific half of `DmaSpiInterface`: an SPI peripheral that writes bytes (blocking) and transfers a draw buffer by DMA (non-blocking). Implement it for your MCU in a few register writes (DMA channel paced by the SPI's TX request, read address incrementing, write address the SPI data register); the interface does the rest (CS, DC, ordering, buffer hand-back).
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The bus error.
- `fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Writes `bytes` and returns once the last bit has left the bus (commands and their parameters).
  Errors: The bus error.
- `fn start_dma(&mut self, buf: twine_hal::DrawBufferMem, len: usize) -> Result<(), (Self::Error, twine_hal::DrawBufferMem)>` — Starts a DMA transfer of the first `len` bytes of `buf` (`len` ≤ `buf.len()`) and returns at once; the bus keeps `buf` until `finish_dma` returns it.
  Errors: The bus error, with the buffer (nothing was started).
- `fn finish_dma(&mut self) -> Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem>` — The buffer of the transfer started by `start_dma` once it has completely left the bus (the DMA channel is done **and** the SPI has shifted out its last bit, so CS and DC may change); `None` while it runs or when none was started. Non-blocking.

#### enum twine_drivers::interface::DmaSpiError<B, P>
The error of a `DmaSpiInterface`.
Variants:
- `Bus(B)` — The bus failed.
- `Pin(P)` — The CS or DC pin failed.
- `Timeout` — A DMA transfer did not finish within the interface's poll limit (`DmaSpiInterface::with_max_polls`); it is still considered running.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_drivers::interface::DmaSpiInterface<B, CS, DC>
A command/data transport (`DcsInterface`) over a `DmaSpiBus` with CS and DC pins, whose pixel transfers run by DMA: `start_pixels` only starts them, so a panel driver's `begin_flush` returns at once and the engine renders the next chunk into its second draw buffer while the first one is sent (the blocking runtime's `begin_flush` / `poll_flush` contract; use two draw buffers to get the overlap). `poll_pixels` hands a buffer back once its transfer is done.
Methods of `DmaSpiInterface`:
- `pub fn new(bus: B, cs: CS, dc: DC) -> Self` — The interface over `bus`, with the chip select `cs` (active low) and the data/command pin `dc`. Never panics.
- `pub fn with_max_polls(self, polls: u32) -> Self` — Polls of `DmaSpiBus::finish_dma` a command waits for a running transfer before it fails with `DmaSpiError::Timeout` (default `u32::MAX`; size it from the longest transfer, e.g. a whole draw buffer at the SPI clock, times a safety factor). `0` counts as `1`. Never panics.
- `pub fn release(self) -> (B, CS, DC)` — Returns the bus and the pins, e.g. to share the SPI with another device or to put it to sleep. It does not wait for a running transfer: call it once the last transfer has finished (the engine got its buffers back); buffers still queued are dropped. Never panics.
Implements: Debug, DcsInterface

#### enum twine_drivers::interface::InterfaceError<S, P>
Error of an interface that drives a bus plus GPIO pins.
Variants:
- `Spi(S)` — The bus (SPI) failed.
- `Pin(P)` — A GPIO pin (DC, WR, data line) failed.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### trait twine_drivers::interface::DcsInterface
`pub trait DcsInterface`
A blocking command/data transport to a display controller.
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The transport's error type.
- `fn command(&mut self, cmd: u8, params: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Sends command `cmd` followed by its parameter bytes.
  Errors: The bus error (`Self::Error`) when the transfer fails.
- `fn write_pixels(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Sends pixel data (the controller must be in memory-write mode, e.g. after `RAMWR`).
  Errors: The bus error (`Self::Error`) when the transfer fails.
- `fn command_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> (provided)` — Sends every byte of `bytes` as a command byte (controllers such as the SSD1306 take their parameters as command bytes). Default: one `command` per byte.
  Errors: The first bus error (`Self::Error`); the bytes after it are not sent.
- `fn start_pixels(&mut self, buf: twine_hal::DrawBufferMem, len: usize) -> Result<Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem>, (Self::Error, twine_hal::DrawBufferMem)> (provided)` — Starts sending the first `len` bytes of a draw buffer as pixel data, like `write_pixels`, but may return before the transfer is done: the non-blocking half of `DisplayDriver::begin_flush` (panel drivers such as `MipiDcs` call it). Returns `Ok(Some(buf))` when the transfer is already complete, or `Ok(None)` when the interface keeps `buf` until the transfer is done and `poll_pixels` hands it back (a DMA interface such as `DmaSpiInterface`). Every other method of the interface first waits for a transfer in progress.
  Errors: The transport's error, with the buffer (it is not in flight).
- `fn poll_pixels(&mut self) -> Option<twine_hal::DrawBufferMem> (provided)` — The buffer of a `start_pixels` transfer that has finished (each once, oldest first); `None` while it runs. Non-blocking. Default: `None` (the default `start_pixels` never keeps a buffer).
- `const CAN_READ: bool` — Whether `read_pixels` works on this interface (default `false`). Panel drivers check it before sending anything for a read-back, so an interface that cannot read answers "unsupported" without touching the panel.
- `fn read_pixels(&mut self, cmd: u8, out: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), twine_hal::ControlError<Self::Error>> (provided)` — Sends the read command `cmd` (MIPI DCS `RAMRD` after the address window is set) and fills `out` with the pixels that follow, **in the write format** of the panel (the format pixels are flushed in): the interface drops the controller's dummy read cycle and converts its read format (often 18-bit RGB666 even in 16-bit mode) — it is board- and controller-specific, so it lives with the interface. The basis of `DisplayDriver::read_back` (display integrity). Requires `CAN_READ`.
  Errors: `ControlError::Unsupported` (the default: nothing is sent), or the transport's error.
Implemented by: twine_drivers::interface::I2cInterface<I2C>, twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface8<D, WR, DC>, twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface16<D, WR, DC>, twine_drivers::interface::QspiInterface<B>, twine_drivers::interface::SpiInterface<SPI, DC>, twine_drivers::interface::DmaSpiInterface<B, CS, DC>

#### trait twine_drivers::interface::AsyncDcsInterface
`pub trait AsyncDcsInterface`
An async command/data transport (feature `async`); same semantics as `DcsInterface`.
Items:
- `type Error: Debug` — The transport's error type.
- `async fn command(&mut self, cmd: u8, params: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Sends command `cmd` followed by its parameter bytes.
- `async fn write_pixels(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>` — Sends pixel data (after `RAMWR`), in one bus transaction where possible.
- `async fn command_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> (provided)` — Sends every byte of `bytes` as a command byte. Default: one command per byte.
Implemented by: twine_drivers::interface::I2cInterface<I2C>, twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface8<D, WR, DC>, twine_drivers::interface::I80Interface16<D, WR, DC>, twine_drivers::interface::QspiInterface<B>, twine_drivers::interface::SpiInterface<SPI, DC>

### mod twine_drivers::interface::qspi

`QspiInterface`: quad-SPI transport of AMOLED controllers (CO5300, SH8601, RM67162, …).

QSPI panels have no DC pin. Every transaction starts with an 8-bit instruction and a 24-bit
address, both on one data line; the address carries the DCS command in its middle byte:

| Purpose | Instruction | Address | Data |
|---------|-------------|---------|------|
| register write (command + parameters) | `0x02` | `0x00, cmd, 0x00` | parameters, 1 line |
| pixel write (`RAMWR`) | `0x32` | `0x00, 0x2C, 0x00` | pixels, 4 lines |
| pixel write, continued (`RAMWRC`) | `0x32` | `0x00, 0x3C, 0x00` | pixels, 4 lines |

This is the framing of the vendors' reference code (Espressif `esp_lcd` QSPI panel IO,
Waveshare and `LilyGO` board support packages). The MCU side is a `QspiBus` (blocking) or
`AsyncQspiBus` (feature `async`) implemented by the firmware over its HAL's half-duplex
SPI (on ESP32-S3: `esp_hal::spi::master::SpiDmaBus::half_duplex_write` with a single-line
command/address phase and `DataMode::Quad` data).

#### fn twine_drivers::interface::qspi::split_write
`pub fn split_write(instr: u8, addr: u32, data: &[u8], max: usize) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u32, &[u8])>`
Splits a QSPI write for a bus whose transactions carry at most `max` data bytes: returns `(address, bytes)` per transaction. Register writes are never split; a pixel write (`opcode::WRITE_PIXELS`) is cut into pieces of `max` rounded down to an even count (no RGB565 pixel is cut), and every piece after the first uses `RAMWRC` so the panel continues where the previous one stopped.

Re-exports in `twine_drivers::interface::qspi`:
- `QspiLines` — same as `twine_drivers::interface::QspiLines`
- `QspiBus` — same as `twine_drivers::interface::QspiBus`
- `AsyncQspiBus` — same as `twine_drivers::interface::AsyncQspiBus`
- `QspiInterface` — same as `twine_drivers::interface::QspiInterface`

### mod twine_drivers::interface::qspi::opcode

QSPI instructions and DCS commands of the panel framing.

#### const twine_drivers::interface::qspi::opcode::WRITE_CMD
`pub const WRITE_CMD: u8 = 0x02`
Register write: command in the address, parameters on one line.

#### const twine_drivers::interface::qspi::opcode::WRITE_PIXELS
`pub const WRITE_PIXELS: u8 = 0x32`
Pixel write: `RAMWR`/`RAMWRC` in the address, pixels on four lines.

#### const twine_drivers::interface::qspi::opcode::RAMWR
`pub const RAMWR: u8 = 0x2C`
DCS memory write (start at the window origin).

#### const twine_drivers::interface::qspi::opcode::RAMWRC
`pub const RAMWRC: u8 = 0x3C`
DCS memory write continue.

### mod twine_drivers::jd9853

JD9853 IPS controller with a 172 × 320 panel (1.47" modules, e.g. Waveshare
ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47).

| | |
|-|-|
| Reference | Waveshare ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47 demo, ESP-IDF component `esp_lcd_jd9853` (Apache-2.0) |
| Max SPI clock | the vendor demo runs it at 80 MHz |

| Spec | Visible | Offset (`Deg0`, `Deg180`) | Offset (`Deg90`, `Deg270`) |
|------|---------|---------------------------|----------------------------|

`ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47-Demo.zip`, `ESP-IDF/01_factory/components/esp_lcd_jd9853`, from
<https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47>; SPDX `Apache-2.0`, Copyright

MIPI `MADCTL` bits (the Arduino demo drives it as an ST7789), so rotation uses
`standard_madctl`.
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::keypad

Key matrix scanned over GPIOs: `GpioMatrix` (`InputKind::Keypad`).

**Scanning**

Rows are outputs, idle **high**; columns are inputs with pull-ups. A scan drives one row low
at a time and reads the columns: a column reading low means the key at (row, column) is
pressed. Every key is debounced separately (default 20 ms, using the clock given at
construction) and each debounced change is queued as a key event (queue of 8; the engine
reads them one by one, `KeypadData::more` tells it to read again).

**Failures**

A scan in which a pin reports an error (e.g. pins on an I/O expander whose bus failed)
counts as a failed read for `health`: `Degraded` after one,
`Failed` after `with_fail_after` consecutive ones (default
`DeviceHealth::DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER`), `Ok` after a clean scan. MCU pins that cannot fail
(`Error = Infallible`) compile the checks away.

**Ghosting**

Without a diode per key, pressing three keys at three corners of a rectangle makes the
fourth corner read as pressed (current flows back through the pressed keys). Two keys are
always reported correctly. Use diodes (cathode towards the row) or only rely on single keys
and pairs. Configure rows as open-drain outputs if several keys in one column may be pressed
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_drivers::keypad::QUEUE_LEN
`pub const QUEUE_LEN: usize = 8`
Capacity of the event queue.

#### struct twine_drivers::keypad::GpioMatrix<ROW, COL, C, const R: usize, const N: usize>
A `R × C` key matrix implementing `InputDevice` (`Keypad`).
Methods of `GpioMatrix`:
- `pub fn new(rows: [ROW; R], cols: [COL; N], keymap: [[twine_hal::Key; N]; R], clock: C) -> Self` — A matrix with `keymap[row][column]`; drives every row high (idle).
- `pub fn with_fail_after(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Reports the keypad `Failed` after `n` consecutive scans with pin errors (default `DeviceHealth::DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER`).
- `pub fn with_debounce(self, debounce: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — Sets the per-key debounce time.
- `pub fn scan(&mut self)` — Scans the matrix once and queues debounced changes. `read` scans too; call this from a periodic task if the engine reads less often than the debounce time.
- `pub fn release(self) -> ([ROW; R], [COL; N], C)` — Returns the pins and the clock.
Implements: Debug, InputDevice

### mod twine_drivers::mipi_dcs

The generic MIPI DCS panel driver shared by every MIPI panel: `MipiDcs` (blocking,
`DisplayDriver`) and `AsyncMipiDcs` (feature `async`, `AsyncDisplayDriver`).

A panel model is a `PanelSpec`: size, controller memory size and offsets, `MADCTL` value
per rotation, `COLMOD`, inversion and a vendor init table. The per-panel modules
(`ili9341`, `st7789`, …) provide specs and constructors.

**Initialization**

1. Hardware reset (RST low 10 µs, high, wait 120 ms) or, without a reset pin, `SWRESET` and
   150 ms.
2. The spec's vendor `init` table.
3. `COLMOD`, `MADCTL` for the rotation, `INVON`/`INVOFF`, `SLPOUT` + 120 ms, `DISPON`.

**Byte order**

RGB565 panels report `ColorFormat::Rgb565Swapped`: the engine renders big-endian RGB565,
exactly the byte order the panel expects over SPI, so pixel buffers are sent **as-is**
(no per-pixel work in the driver). RGB666 panels (`COLMOD` `0x66`, ILI9488) report
`ColorFormat::Rgb888` and also receive the rendered bytes unchanged.

**Rotation**

Rotation is done by the controller (`MADCTL`), so `DisplayInfo::hw_rotation` is `true` and
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### struct twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl
`MADCTL` (memory access control) bits.
Methods of `Madctl`:
- `const EMPTY: Self` — No bits set.
- `const MY: Self` — Row address order (mirror Y).
- `const MX: Self` — Column address order (mirror X).
- `const MV: Self` — Row/column exchange (swap axes).
- `const ML: Self` — Vertical refresh order.
- `const BGR: Self` — BGR colour filter order.
- `const MH: Self` — Horizontal refresh order.
- `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Self` — From a raw register value.
- `pub const fn bits(self) -> u8` — The raw register value.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self` — Both sets of bits (usable in `const` context, unlike `|`).
- `pub const fn difference(self, other: Self) -> Self` — `self` without the bits of `other`.
- `pub const fn contains(self, other: Self) -> bool` — Whether all bits of `other` are set.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, BitOr, BitOrAssign

#### fn twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::standard_madctl
`pub const fn standard_madctl(extra: twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl) -> [twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl; 4]`
The common rotation → `MADCTL` mapping for panels whose unmirrored memory is upright: `Deg0: —, Deg90: MY|MV, Deg180: MX|MY, Deg270: MX|MV`, each combined with `extra` (e.g. `Madctl::BGR`).

#### enum twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::InitOp
One entry of a vendor init table.
Variants:
- `Cmd(u8, &'static [u8])` — A command with its parameter bytes.
- `DelayMs(u32)` — Wait this many milliseconds.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::PanelSpec
Description of a MIPI DCS panel model.
Fields:
- `name: &'static str` — Model name (logs, documentation).
- `native_w: u16` — Visible width at `Deg0` orientation of the memory (no `MV`).
- `native_h: u16` — Visible height at `Deg0` orientation of the memory (no `MV`).
- `ram_w: u16` — Controller frame memory width (columns).
- `ram_h: u16` — Controller frame memory height (rows).
- `offset_x: u16` — First visible column with `MX` clear.
- `offset_y: u16` — First visible row with `MY` clear.
- `madctl: [twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl; 4]` — `MADCTL` per `Rotation` (`Deg0`, `Deg90`, `Deg180`, `Deg270`).
- `colmod: u8` — `COLMOD` parameter: `0x55` (or `0x05`) = 16-bit RGB565, `0x66` (or `0x06`) = 18-bit RGB666.
- `invert: bool` — Colour inversion (`INVON`) — many IPS panels need it.
- `align: u8` — Flush areas' x, y, width and height must be multiples of this (`DisplayInfo::align`; 2 for most AMOLED controllers, otherwise 1).
- `sw_rotation: bool` — The controller cannot exchange rows and columns (no usable `MADCTL.MV`): `MADCTL` stays at the `Deg0` entry, `DisplayInfo::hw_rotation` is `false` and the engine rotates in software, so flush areas are in native panel coordinates.
- `brightness: bool` — The controller dims itself with `WRDISBV` (`0x51`; AMOLED/OLED controllers): `DisplayDriver::set_brightness` sends it. `false` for LCD controllers, which are dimmed by their backlight (the driver then answers `Unsupported`).
- `init: &'static [twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::InitOp]` — Vendor init table, run after reset and before `COLMOD`/`MADCTL`/`SLPOUT`/`DISPON`.
Methods of `PanelSpec`:
- `pub const fn format(&self) -> twine_core::ColorFormat` — The pixel format the engine must render for this panel: `ColorFormat::Rgb888` for 18-bit `COLMOD` (`x6`), otherwise `ColorFormat::Rgb565Swapped`.
- `pub const fn bytes_per_pixel(&self) -> usize` — Bytes per pixel sent to the panel (2 or 3).
- `pub const fn hw_rotation(&self, r: twine_core::Rotation) -> twine_core::Rotation` — The rotation done by the controller for display rotation `r`: `r` itself, or `Deg0` for `sw_rotation` panels.
- `pub const fn madctl_for(&self, r: twine_core::Rotation) -> twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl` — The `MADCTL` value for a rotation (always the `Deg0` entry for `sw_rotation` panels).
- `pub const fn logical_size(&self, r: twine_core::Rotation) -> (u16, u16)` — Logical `(width, height)` for a rotation (swapped when its `MADCTL` has `MV`, or for 90°/270° on `sw_rotation` panels).
- `pub const fn offset(&self, r: twine_core::Rotation) -> (u16, u16)` — Column/row offset of the logical origin in controller memory for a rotation: `MX` mirrors the column offset inside `ram_w`, `MY` the row offset inside `ram_h`, `MV` swaps them (the method of mipidsi's `set_address_window`).
- `pub fn window(&self, r: twine_core::Rotation, area: twine_core::Rect) -> Option<([u8; 4], [u8; 4])>` — `CASET` and `RASET` parameters (big-endian inclusive start/end) for an area of the flush coordinate space of rotation `r` (logical, or native for `sw_rotation` panels), or `None` if the area is empty, outside the screen or not a multiple of `align`.
- `pub const fn with_name(self, name: &'static str) -> Self` — Returns a copy with another name.
- `pub const fn with_invert(self, invert: bool) -> Self` — Returns a copy with colour inversion on or off.
- `pub const fn with_bgr(self, bgr: bool) -> Self` — Returns a copy with the `BGR` bit set or cleared in every rotation.
- `pub const fn with_size(self, native_w: u16, native_h: u16, offset_x: u16, offset_y: u16) -> Self` — Returns a copy with another visible size and offset inside the same controller memory.
- `pub const fn with_align(self, align: u8) -> Self` — Returns a copy with another flush alignment.
- `pub const fn with_madctl(self, madctl: [twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::Madctl; 4]) -> Self` — Returns a copy with another `MADCTL` table.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_drivers::mipi_dcs::DcsError<E>
Errors of `MipiDcs`.
Variants:
- `Interface(E)` — The interface (bus or DC pin) failed.
- `ResetPin` — The reset pin failed.
- `BadArea` — The flush area is empty or outside the display, or the buffer is too short for it.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

### mod twine_drivers::mono

Page conversion for monochrome OLED controllers (SSD1306, SH1106).

The engine renders `I1`: row-major, 1 bit per pixel, **most significant bit first**, each
row starting on a byte (`stride = ⌈w / 8⌉`). Page-based controllers store 8 vertically
stacked pixels per byte instead: byte `c` of page `p` holds the pixels `(c, 8p + k)` in bit
`k` (LSB = top). `i1_to_page` converts one page of an `I1` chunk into that layout;
`page_to_i1` is its inverse (tests, simulators).

#### fn twine_drivers::mono::i1_to_page
`pub fn i1_to_page(src: &[u8], stride: usize, width: usize, page: usize, out: &mut [u8])`
Converts rows `8·page … 8·page + 7` of an `I1` chunk (`stride` bytes per row, `width` pixels) into page layout in `out[..width]`.

#### fn twine_drivers::mono::page_to_i1
`pub fn page_to_i1(src: &[u8], stride: usize, width: usize, page: usize, out: &mut [u8])`
Inverse of `i1_to_page`: writes page `page` (`width` bytes of `src`) back into rows `8·page …` of an `I1` buffer with `stride` bytes per row.

#### enum twine_drivers::mono::OledError<E>
Errors of the OLED drivers.
Variants:
- `Interface(E)` — The interface failed.
- `BadArea` — The flush area is outside the panel, not page aligned, or the buffer is too short.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### const twine_drivers::mono::OLED_DPI
`pub const OLED_DPI: u16 = 150`
Default DPI of the small OLEDs (a 0.96" 128 × 64 panel is ≈ 150 dpi).

### mod twine_drivers::rm67162

RM67162 AMOLED controller on quad SPI (`LilyGO` T-Display-S3 AMOLED 1.91": 240 × 536).

| | |
|-|-|
| Reference | `LilyGO` `LilyGo-AMOLED-Series` (`rm67162_cmd`, MIT) |
| Interface | QSPI (`QspiInterface`), vendor runs 75 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x55` → `Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | hardware rotation with `standard_madctl`, RGB order, even flush areas (`align = 2`), brightness via `0x51` |

The init table is the vendor's QSPI table (`rm67162_cmd` of
<https://github.com/Xinyuan-LilyGO/LilyGo-AMOLED-Series>, `src/initSequence.cpp`):
`0xFE 0x00`, `SLPOUT` + 120 ms, page 5 `0x05 0x05` (ELVSS −3.95 V), page 1 `0x73 0x25`
(OVSS −4.0 V), page 0, then `WRDISBV`. The vendor switches the display on at brightness 0 and
raises it afterwards; this table sets `WRDISBV 0xD0` before the generic `DISPON` instead, and
leaves `MADCTL`/`COLMOD` to the generic sequence.

**Wiring**

| Panel pin | Driver argument |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `SCLK`, `SDIO0`–`SDIO3`, `CS` | `bus`, your HAL's quad-SPI implementing `QspiBus` / `AsyncQspiBus` (on ESP32-S3: `twine-esp`) |
| `RESET` | `rst`: `Some(OutputPin)`, or `None` (software reset); some boards route it through an I/O expander that the firmware releases first |
| `TE` | optional, not used |

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

RM67162 vendor init table (`LilyGO` `rm67162_cmd`, see the module docs).

#### static twine_drivers::rm67162::RM67162_240X536

### mod twine_drivers::sh1106

SH1106 monochrome OLED controller (1.3" 128 × 64 modules) over I2C or SPI.

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Sino Wealth SH1106 V2.3 |
| Bus | I2C (`0x3C`/`0x3D`, up to 400 kHz) or 4-wire SPI (up to 4 MHz) |
| Format | `ColorFormat::I1`, `align = 8` |
| Quirks | 132-column memory with the 128 visible columns at offset 2; **no horizontal addressing mode**: each page is written separately (`0xB0 + page`, column low/high nibbles) |

Init follows the `sh1106` crate (MIT/Apache-2.0, <https://github.com/jamwaffles/sh1106>):
display off, clock `0x80`, multiplex 63, offset 0, start line 0, DC-DC on (`0xAD 0x8B`),
segment remap / COM scan direction, COM pins `0x12`, contrast `0x80`, pre-charge `0xF1`,
VCOM deselect `0x40`, resume from RAM, normal, display on. Rotation handling is as for the
`ssd1306` driver (hardware `Deg0`/`Deg180`, software `Deg90`/`Deg270`).

**Wiring**

| Panel pin | Driver argument |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `SDA`, `SCL` (I2C modules) | `I2cInterface::new(i2c, 0x3C)` with an `embedded_hal(_async)::i2c::I2c` |
| `SCK`, `MOSI`, `CS`, `DC` (SPI modules) | `SpiInterface::new(spi_device, dc)` |
| `RES` | not driven by the driver: hold it high (or pulse it low once) from your firmware |

#### const twine_drivers::sh1106::COLUMN_OFFSET
