|-|-|
| Datasheet | Solomon Systech SSD1306 Rev 1.1 |
| Bus | I2C (`I2cInterface`, address `0x3C`/`0x3D`, up to 400 kHz) or 4-wire SPI (`SpiInterface`, up to 10 MHz) |
| Format | `ColorFormat::I1` (1 = lit), `align = 8` (whole 8-row pages) |
| Quirks | 72 × 40 modules (SSD1306B) need the internal current reference and a 28-column offset |

**Init**

The command sequence of the `ssd1306` crate (MIT/Apache-2.0,
<https://github.com/rust-embedded-community/ssd1306>) with its default brightness, sent as one
command stream: display off, clock `0x80`, multiplex `h − 1`, offset 0, start line 0, charge
pump on, horizontal addressing, COM pins (`0x12` for 64/40 rows, `0x02` for 32 rows),
segment remap / COM scan direction for the rotation, pre-charge `0x21`, contrast `0x5F`,
VCOMH auto (`0x40`), resume from RAM, normal (not inverted), scrolling off, display on.

**Rotation**

`Deg0` and `Deg180` are done by the controller (segment remap + COM scan direction,
`hw_rotation = true`). `Deg90`/`Deg270` are not supported by the hardware: the controller
stays at `Deg0`, `DisplayInfo::hw_rotation` is `false` and the engine rotates each chunk
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_drivers::ssd1306::Ssd1306Size
Size of an SSD1306 module.
Variants:
- `Size128x64` — 128 × 64 (0.96", 1.3").
- `Size128x32` — 128 × 32 (0.91").
- `Size72x40` — 72 × 40 (0.42", SSD1306B), columns 28…99 of the controller memory.
Methods of `Ssd1306Size`:
- `pub const fn dimensions(self) -> (u16, u16)` — `(width, height)` in pixels.
- `pub const fn column_offset(self) -> u8` — First visible column in the 128-column memory.
- `pub const fn com_pins(self) -> u8` — `COM` pins hardware configuration (`0xDA` parameter).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

### mod twine_drivers::st7735

ST7735R / ST7735S 128 × 160 TFT controller ("tab" variants of the common 1.8" and 0.96"
modules).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Sitronix ST7735R V2.1 / ST7735S V1.1 |
| Max SPI clock | 15 MHz write (t<sub>scycw</sub> = 66 ns); modules usually work at 20–40 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x05` (16-bit) → `Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | the protective-film tab colour tells the variant: offsets and RGB/BGR differ |

| Spec | Visible | Controller memory | Offset at `Deg0` | Colour order | Inversion |
|------|---------|-------------------|------------------|--------------|-----------|
| `ST7735R_GREENTAB` | 128 × 160 | 132 × 162 | (2, 1) | BGR | off |
| `ST7735R_REDTAB` | 128 × 160 | 128 × 160 | (0, 0) | BGR | off |
| `ST7735R_BLACKTAB` | 128 × 160 | 128 × 160 | (0, 0) | RGB | off |
| `ST7735_80X160` | 80 × 160 (0.96" IPS mini) | 132 × 162 | (26, 1) | BGR | on |

Init tables and rotation mapping follow Adafruit-ST7735-Library (`Rcmd1`, `Rcmd3`,
`setRotation`; BSD license, <https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit-ST7735-Library>), minus
the commands the generic init sends (`SWRESET`, `SLPOUT`, `INVOFF`, `MADCTL`, `COLMOD`,
`DISPON`) and the address commands of `Rcmd2*` (every flush sets its window). Rotation
(Adafruit's values with 90° and 270° exchanged to match the engine's rotation direction):
`Deg0 = MX|MY`, `Deg90 = MX|MV`, `Deg180 = —`, `Deg270 = MY|MV`.

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::st7789

ST7789 / ST7789V 240 × 320 IPS controller and its common module variants.

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Sitronix ST7789V V1.0 |
| Max SPI clock | 15 MHz write per datasheet (t<sub>scycw</sub> = 66 ns); modules usually run at 40–80 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x55` → `Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | IPS glass: colour inversion **on**; RGB order; small panels show a window of the 240 × 320 memory (offsets) |

| Spec | Visible | Offset (`Deg0`) | Typical module |
|------|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| `ST7789` | 240 × 320 | (0, 0) | 2.0"/2.4" IPS |
| `ST7789_240X240` | 240 × 240 | (0, 0); (0, 80) at `Deg180` | 1.3"/1.54" square |
| `ST7789_135X240` | 135 × 240 | (52, 40); (53, 40) at `Deg180` | Lilygo T-Display 1.14" |

Init: after reset the generic sequence (`COLMOD`, `MADCTL`, `INVON`, `SLPOUT`, `DISPON`) is
all the ST7789 needs; the vendor table only adds `NORON` (as mipidsi's `ST7789` model and
Adafruit's `generic_st7789` table do). Rotation uses `standard_madctl`.

**Wiring**

| Panel pin | Driver argument |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `SCK`, `SDI`/`MOSI` (`SDO`/`MISO` is not needed) | the bus of `spi`, an `embedded_hal(_async)::spi::SpiDevice` (use a DMA-capable async one to overlap transfers with rendering) |
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::st7796

ST7796S 320 × 480 TFT controller (3.5"/4.0" SPI modules).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Sitronix ST7796S V1.0 |
| Max SPI clock | 15 MHz write per datasheet; modules commonly run at 40 MHz |
| Format | `COLMOD 0x55` → `Rgb565Swapped` |
| Quirks | most modules have BGR glass and no inversion; use `PanelSpec::with_bgr` / `PanelSpec::with_invert` for others |

Init as mipidsi's `ST7796` model (which reuses its ST7789 sequence): the generic init plus
`NORON`. Rotation uses `standard_madctl`.

**Wiring**

| Panel pin | Driver argument |
|-----------|-----------------|
| `SCK`, `SDI`/`MOSI` (`SDO`/`MISO` is not needed) | the bus of `spi`, an `embedded_hal(_async)::spi::SpiDevice` (use a DMA-capable async one to overlap transfers with rendering) |
| `CS` | the chip select owned by `spi` |
| `DC`/`RS` | `dc`, any `OutputPin` |
| `RESET` | `rst`: `Some(OutputPin)`, or `None` when it is tied to the MCU reset (a software reset is sent instead) |
| `LED`/`BL` | not driven by the driver: switch it (or PWM it) from your firmware |

### mod twine_drivers::touch

Touch controllers implementing `InputDevice` (`Pointer`).

| Module | Controller | Bus | Address | IRQ |
|--------|------------|-----|---------|-----|
| `xpt2046` | XPT2046 / ADS7843 resistive | SPI | — | `T_IRQ`, active low |
| `ft6x36` | Focaltech FT6206/FT6236/FT6336, FT3168 (model flag) capacitive | I2C | `0x38` | `INT`, active low |
| `ft5x06` | Focaltech FT5206/FT5306/FT5406 capacitive | I2C | `0x38` | `INT`, active low |
| `gt911` | Goodix GT911 capacitive | I2C | `0x5D` or `0x14` | `INT`, active low (default config) |
| `cst816s` | Hynitron CST816S capacitive | I2C | `0x15` | `IRQ`, active low pulses |
| `axs5106l` | AXS5106L capacitive | I2C | `0x63` | `INT`, active low |
| `stmpe811` | ST STMPE811 resistive controller | I2C | `0x41` (or `0x44`) | `INT`, active low |

**Power (P1)**

With an interrupt pin, every driver reports `PollHint::Interrupt` and
`read()` performs **no bus transaction** while the pin is inactive and the last state was
released. While pressed it keeps reading until it sees the release. Without an interrupt pin
the engine polls periodically.

**Failures**

Every driver counts **consecutive** failed bus transactions and reports them through
`InputDevice::health`: `Degraded { errors }` after the
first, `Failed` after `with_fail_after(n)` of them (default
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### struct twine_drivers::touch::Axs5106l<I2C, IRQ, RST = twine_drivers::NoPin>
AXS5106L driver implementing `InputDevice` (`Pointer`).
Methods of `Axs5106l`:
- `pub fn new(i2c: I2C, irq: Option<IRQ>) -> Self` — A driver without reset pin; `irq` is the `INT` pin (active low), if wired. Its coordinates are fitted to the display when it is added to the engine (see `for_display`). Touches no bus; never panics.
- `pub fn with_reset_pin<RST: embedded_hal::digital::OutputPin>(self, rst: RST) -> twine_drivers::touch::Axs5106l<I2C, IRQ, RST>` — Adds the reset pin (see `reset`).
- `pub fn with_mount(self, mount: twine_hal::TouchMount) -> Self` — Describes how the touch panel's raw axes sit on the display's native axes (default `TouchMount::ALIGNED`). Composed with the display's rotation whenever the driver is fitted, so set it once, in any order with `for_display`. Never panics.
- `pub fn for_display(self, info: &twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> Self` — Fits the coordinate mapping to the display described by `info` (its rotation, native and logical size), composed with the `with_mount` mount. The engine does this when the driver is added (`Ui::builder(..).input(touch)`, `Engine::add_input`) through `InputDevice::fit_to_display`; call it yourself only when you read the driver without the engine. Never panics.
- `pub fn transform(&self) -> twine_hal::TouchTransform` — The current mapping of raw panel coordinates to the logical screen (`TouchTransform::PASS_THROUGH` until the driver is fitted to a display).
- `pub fn with_fail_after(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Reports the device `Failed` after `n` consecutive bus errors (default `DeviceHealth::DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER`; see `health`).
- `pub fn release(self) -> (I2C, Option<IRQ>, Option<RST>)` — Returns the bus and the pins.
- `pub fn reset(&mut self, delay: &mut impl embedded_hal::delay::DelayNs) -> Result<(), <RST as embedded_hal::digital::ErrorType>::Error>` — Pulses `RST` low for 10 ms and waits 300 ms for the controller to boot (the vendor Arduino library's wait); no-op without a reset pin.
  Errors: The reset pin error.
- `pub fn read_id(&mut self) -> Result<[u8; 3], <I2C as embedded_hal::i2c::ErrorType>::Error>` — Reads the 3 ID bytes (register `0x08`).
  Errors: The I²C bus error.
- `pub fn read_raw(&mut self) -> Result<Option<(u16, u16)>, <I2C as embedded_hal::i2c::ErrorType>::Error>` — Reads the first touch point in raw panel coordinates (`None`: no finger).
  Errors: The I²C bus error.
Implements: Debug, InputDevice, AsyncInputWait

### mod twine_drivers::touch::axs5106l

AXS5106L capacitive touch controller (I2C; 1.47" 172 × 320 IPS modules such as the Waveshare
ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47).

| | |
|-|-|
| Reference | Waveshare ESP32-C6-Touch-LCD-1.47 demo: ESP-IDF component `esp_lcd_touch_axs5106` (Apache-2.0) and Arduino library `esp_lcd_touch_axs5106l` |
| Address | `0x63` |
| Bus speed | I2C up to 400 kHz (the vendor demo's clock) |
| IRQ | `INT`, active low (the demo triggers on the falling edge) |
| Reset | optional `RST` (active low) |
| Rotation | reports panel coordinates (12-bit), mapped to the display by `TouchTransform` (fitted automatically, see module docs) |

A reading is a register write of `0x01` followed by a separate 14-byte read (with a STOP in
between, as the vendor code does): byte 1 holds the number of points (bits 3:0), then per
point 6 bytes starting at byte 2: `XH` (X bits 11:8 in 3:0), `XL`, `YH`, `YL`, two more.
Only the first point is used. `read_id` reads the 3 ID bytes at `0x08`.

On the Waveshare 1.47" board the touch X axis runs opposite to the display's columns:
describe it with `with_mount``(TouchMount { mirror_x: true, .. })`
(the vendor demo mirrors X at rotation 0); every display rotation then works.

### mod twine_drivers::touch::cst816s

Hynitron CST816S capacitive touch controller (I2C; round 1.28" GC9A01 boards and small
watches).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Hynitron CST816S datasheet / register description |
| Address | `0x15` |
| IRQ | `IRQ`, active-low pulses per report; **required**: the chip sleeps when idle and NACKs I2C until touched |
| Reset | optional `RST` (active low) to wake / restart it |
| Rotation | reports panel coordinates (12-bit), mapped to the display by `TouchTransform` (fitted automatically, see module docs) |

A reading reads 6 registers from `0x01`: gesture, finger count, `XH` (bits 11:8 in 3:0),
`XL`, `YH`, `YL`. Because the controller does not answer while asleep, a failed read while
released is reported as "released" and logged at debug level only; only failed reads while
touched (the controller is awake then) count for `health`.

**Wiring**

| Controller pin | Driver argument |
|----------------|-----------------|
| `SDA`, `SCL` | `i2c`, an `embedded_hal::i2c::I2c` (address `0x15`) |
| `INT`/`IRQ` | `irq`: `Some(InputPin)` (`+ Wait` for the async wake-up), or `None` to poll |
| `RST` | not driven by the driver: hold it high from your firmware; the chip sleeps between touches and does not answer then |

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::touch::ft6x36

Focaltech FT6206 / FT6236 / FT6336 (and FT3168) capacitive touch controllers (I2C).

| `RST` | not driven by the driver: hold it high from your firmware |

### mod twine_drivers::touch::gt911

Goodix GT911 capacitive touch controller (I2C, 16-bit register addresses).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | Goodix GT911 datasheet + programming guide |
| Address | `0x5D` or `0x14` (selected by the `INT` level during reset) |
| Bus speed | I2C up to 400 kHz |
| IRQ | `INT`; the default configuration triggers on the falling edge → active low |
| Coordinates | reported in the resolution of its configuration (`0x8048`), scaled to the display's native size and mapped by `TouchTransform` (fitted automatically, see module docs) |

A reading reads the status register `0x814E` (bit 7: buffer ready, bits 3:0: number of
points). When ready and touched, the first point is read at `0x8150` (X low, X high, Y low,
Y high); the status is then cleared by writing `0` — without that the controller stops
reporting. When the buffer is not ready the previous state is kept.

The controller reports points in the X/Y resolution of its configuration (`0x8048`), which
module makers do not always set to the panel's: the CYD 8048S043 ships configured for
480 × 272 on an 800 × 480 display. The driver reads it once (in `probe`, or
before the first sample) and scales points from it to the display's native size; a zero
resolution is taken as native pixels.

`probe` reads the product ID (`0x8140`, `"911"`), the configuration
version (`0x8047`) and the resolution, and logs them.

(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::touch::stmpe811

ST STMPE811 resistive touch-screen controller with ADC (I2C; STM32F429I-DISC1 and many
resistive modules).

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | ST STMPE811 datasheet (`DocID14489`) |
| Address | `0x41` (`ADDR0` high, e.g. F429I-DISC1) or `0x44` |
| Bus speed | I2C up to 400 kHz |
| IRQ | `INT`, open drain, active low (configured by `init`) |
| Coordinates | raw 12-bit ADC values: needs a per-module `Calibration` (default: identity) |

**Init**

Following ST's `STM32Cube` BSP driver `stmpe811.c` (BSD-3-Clause): soft reset, ADC and
touch-screen clocks on (`SYS_CTRL2 = 0x0C`), ADC 12-bit / 80 clocks / internal reference
(`0x49`), ADC clock 3.25 MHz, touch pins to their touch-screen function (`GPIO_AF = 0`),
`TSC_CFG = 0x9A` (4-sample average, 500 µs detect delay and settling), FIFO threshold 1, FIFO
reset, Z fraction 1, 50 mA drive, touch screen on in XYZ mode, clear and enable the
touch-detect interrupt (global, level, active low).

**Reading**

`TSC_CTRL` bit 7 tells whether the panel is touched. While touched, up to 3 samples are
taken from the FIFO (`0xD7`, 4 bytes each: X 12 bit, Y 12 bit, Z 8 bit), filtered with
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

### mod twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046

XPT2046 (ADS7843-compatible) resistive touch controller on SPI.

| | |
|-|-|
| Datasheet | XPTEK XPT2046 (TI ADS7846 compatible) |
| Max SPI clock | 2.5 MHz (125 kHz sample rate); use ≤ 2 MHz, SPI mode 0 |
| IRQ | `T_IRQ`/`PENIRQ`, **active low** while the panel is touched (pull-up needed if the module has none) |
| Quirks | noisy: median of several samples; needs per-module `Calibration` |

**Sampling**

Each reading is one 3-byte SPI transfer `[control, 0, 0]`, the 12-bit result is
`((rx[1] << 8) | rx[2]) >> 3`. Control bytes (12-bit, differential, `PD = 11` = reference
and ADC powered between conversions): `0xB3` Z1, `0xC3` Z2, `0xD3` X, `0x93` Y. A reading
ends with `0xD0` (`PD = 00`) to power down and re-enable `PENIRQ`.

Pressure is `z = z1 + 4095 − z2`; the panel is pressed when `z > z_threshold` (default 400).
Then `samples` (default 5, max 7) X/Y pairs are taken and the median of each axis is
calibrated and clamped to the screen.

**Power (P1)**

With an IRQ pin, `read` returns "released" **without any SPI traffic**
while `T_IRQ` is high and the last state was released; `poll_hint`
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::CMD_Z1
`pub const CMD_Z1: u8 = 0xB3`
Control byte: Z1 (12-bit, differential, powered).

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::CMD_Z2
`pub const CMD_Z2: u8 = 0xC3`
Control byte: Z2.

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::CMD_X
`pub const CMD_X: u8 = 0xD3`
Control byte: X position.

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::CMD_Y
`pub const CMD_Y: u8 = 0x93`
Control byte: Y position.

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::CMD_POWER_DOWN
`pub const CMD_POWER_DOWN: u8 = 0xD0`
Control byte: X with power-down (re-enables `PENIRQ`); ends every reading.

#### const twine_drivers::touch::xpt2046::MAX_SAMPLES
`pub const MAX_SAMPLES: u8 = 7`

### mod twine_drivers::testkit

Recording mock buses for host-side driver tests.

Every mock created from one `Recorder` appends to the same operation log (`BusOp`), so
pin transitions, SPI/I2C traffic and delays interleave exactly as the driver issued them.

- `RecordingSpi`: blocking and async `SpiDevice`. Written bytes become `BusOp::Cmd` (one
  per byte) while the pin named `"dc"` is low, otherwise `BusOp::Data`. Data following a
  `RAMWR` (`0x2C`) / `RAMWRC` (`0x3C`) command is logged as `BusOp::Pixels` (length only);
  the bytes are kept in `Recorder::pixel_bytes`.
- `RecordingPin`: output, input and async `Wait` pin; logs `BusOp::Pin` unless created
  with `Recorder::quiet_pin`. A rising edge on the pin `"wr"` latches the levels of the pins
  `"d0"`…`"d15"` into a `BusOp::Strobe` (i80 parallel bus).
- `RecordingDelay`: blocking and async `DelayNs`, logs `BusOp::DelayUs`.
- `RecordingI2c`: blocking and async `I2c`, logs `BusOp::I2cWrite` / `BusOp::I2cRead`.

Read data comes from responders (`Recorder::set_spi_responder`,
`Recorder::set_i2c_responder`); without one, reads return zeros. Async operations complete
immediately, except that `Recorder::pending_once` makes the next async bus operation
return `Pending` once (to test that a driver starts work on the first poll).
`block_on` is a tiny executor for the async mocks.

#### enum twine_drivers::testkit::BusOp
One recorded bus operation.
Variants:
- `Cmd(u8)` — A command byte (SPI byte written while `dc` is low).
- `Data(Vec<u8>)` — Data bytes of one SPI write (or the transmitted bytes of a transfer).
- `Pixels(usize)` — Pixel data after `RAMWR`/`RAMWRC`: byte count of one SPI write.
- `DelayUs(u32)` — A delay in microseconds.
- `Pin(&'static str, bool)` — A logged pin changed its level (`true` = high).
- `Strobe { dc: bool, value: u16 }` — An i80 write strobe (rising edge of `"wr"`): level of `"dc"` and the latched data pins.
- `I2cWrite { addr: u8, data: Vec<u8> }` — An I2C write.
- `I2cRead { addr: u8, len: usize }` — An I2C read.
- `Wait(&'static str, bool)` — An async wait for a pin level.
- `QspiCmd { instr: u8, addr: u32, data: Vec<u8> }` — A single-line QSPI transaction (register write).
- `QspiPixels { instr: u8, addr: u32, len: usize }` — A quad QSPI transaction (pixel write); the bytes go to `Recorder::pixel_bytes`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display

#### fn twine_drivers::testkit::format_ops
`pub fn format_ops(ops: &[twine_drivers::testkit::BusOp]) -> String`
Formats a log one operation per line (the format of the text fixtures).

#### struct twine_drivers::testkit::MockError
The error of every mock bus (injected with `Recorder::fail_next`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Error, Error

## crate twine_embassy

Documented with the default features.

**twine-embassy**

Runs a Twine UI on an embassy executor: `run` updates the UI and
then sleeps until the UI's next deadline, a channel message (the UI waker) or an input
interrupt. An idle UI costs no CPU at all. `run_with` does the same and reports each step
of the loop (`LoopEvent`) to a callback with the UI, so the application keeps its UI and
display while the loop runs (backlight, panel sleep, faults).

Both runtimes run (`RunUi`):

- `AsyncUi` (`Ui::builder_async`): each frame is rendered while the previous chunk is
  still being transferred by DMA (`AsyncDisplayDriver`), and the loop also wakes on the
  `AsyncInputWait` input's interrupt.
- `Ui` (`Ui::builder`, `Ui::builder_fb`): blocking drivers, e.g. a memory-mapped
  framebuffer (LTDC); input interrupts reach it through its waker (a task awaiting the
  interrupt calls `ui.waker().wake()`).

The loop is a thin adapter like `twine::run::blocking` (bare metal, RTOS, host threads),
with the same events. Applications usually reach this crate through the facade:
`twine::embassy` (feature `embassy`, which also enables `async` and `platform-embassy`).
Its features: `log` / `defmt` (logging backend) and `safety` (the safety profile, forwarded
by the facade; see `docs/safety/profile.md` in the repository).

**Several displays.** A `Ui` with several displays (`UiBuilder::display`,
`Ui::mount_on`) is one UI to the loop: one `run` drives all its displays (one engine, one
waker). An `AsyncUi` drives one async display; for several, run one task per `AsyncUi`
(`run` in each, on the same executor and thread): they share the thread's reactive runtime,
and each update runs only its own UI's channel handlers and bindings, so signals shared
between them update both without cross-talk (`twine_view::UiCore` § Sharing the runtime).

`EmbassyPlatform` (re-exported from `twine-hal`'s `platform-embassy`) is the `AsyncUi`'s
platform over `embassy-time`: its clock and the timer that bounds every display flush with
`EngineConfig::flush_timeout`. `hires_now` is the matching high-resolution timer for
`EngineConfig::hires_timer` (render/flush statistics).

Works with any embassy HAL (embassy-rp, embassy-stm32, esp-hal's `esp-rtos`): the display is
an `AsyncDisplayDriver` (e.g. a `twine-drivers` panel over an async, DMA-backed `SpiDevice`),
and the input waited on is an `AsyncInputWait` device (e.g. a touch controller with its
interrupt pin).

```rust
use twine_embassy::UiBuilderExt;
use twine_view::prelude::*;

fn app(_cx: Scope) -> impl View {
    label("Hello")
}

// Two DMA ping-pong buffers of 40 rows of a 320 px RGB565 panel, sized at compile time.
draw_buffers!(static BUFS: 2 x 40 rows x 320 px @ Rgb565Swapped);

let rt = Runtime::take().expect("runtime already taken"); // keeps the UI in this task
let ui = Ui::builder_async(display)
    .runtime(rt)
    .buffers(BufferMode::partial_double_from(BUFS.take().expect("draw buffers already taken")))
    .input_wait(touch)
    .with_embassy_platform()
    .build(app);
twine_embassy::run(ui).await
```

#### fn twine_embassy::hires_now
`pub fn hires_now() -> twine_core::Instant`
The current `embassy-time` instant as a Twine `Instant` (for `EngineConfig::hires_timer`; its resolution is the embassy tick rate). The same clock as `EmbassyPlatform`.

#### fn twine_embassy::to_embassy
`pub fn to_embassy(t: twine_core::Instant) -> embassy_time::instant::Instant`
Converts a Twine instant (µs since boot) to an `embassy-time` instant.

#### trait twine_embassy::UiBuilderExt
`pub trait UiBuilderExt`
Builder conveniences for embassy, for both runtimes.
Items:
- `type Output` — The builder with its time source set (the clock / platform part of its typestate provided).
- `fn with_embassy_platform(self) -> Self::Output` — Uses `EmbassyPlatform` as the platform: the `AsyncUi`'s clock and flush timer (`AsyncUiBuilder::platform(&EmbassyPlatform)`), or the `Ui`'s clock (`UiBuilder::clock(EmbassyPlatform)`), so the deadlines the UI returns are the `embassy-time` instants `run` sleeps until. Provides the builder's required platform (async) or clock (blocking) part.
Implemented by: twine_view::AsyncUiBuilder<D, W, R, P, B>, twine_view::UiBuilder<S, R, C, B>

#### fn twine_embassy::wait_waker
`pub async fn wait_waker(waker: &twine_reactive::UiWaker)`
Completes when `waker` is set (a channel send or `notify_input` from any context); does not clear it (the next update does).

#### trait twine_embassy::RunUi
`pub trait RunUi`
A UI that `run` and `run_with` can drive: `Ui` and `AsyncUi`.
Items:
- `async fn step(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update (and the frame it renders); returns when to run again.
- `fn waker(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The UI's waker: the loop sleeps until it is set (or a deadline or input interrupt).
- `async fn wait_input(&mut self)` — Completes when an input interrupt asks for the next update (and tells it to read the inputs); never completes for a UI without an interrupt-driven input.
Implemented by: twine_view::Ui, twine_view::AsyncUi<D, W>

#### fn twine_embassy::run
`pub async fn run<U: twine_embassy::RunUi>(ui: U) -> never`
Runs the UI (`Ui` or `AsyncUi`) forever: `run_with` without a callback.

#### fn twine_embassy::run_with
`pub async fn run_with<U, F>(ui: U, on_event: F) -> never where U: twine_embassy::RunUi, F: FnMut(&mut U, twine_view::run::LoopEvent)`
Runs the UI forever, reporting each step of the loop to `on_event` with the UI (see `LoopEvent`): `BeforeUpdate`, the update, then — unless it returned `Wake::Now` — `Idle(deadline)` (or `Inactive(d)` for `Wake::IdleFor`, with `EngineConfig::idle_timeout`), the sleep and `Woken`.

Re-exports in `twine_embassy`:
- `EmbassyPlatform` = `twine_hal::platform::embassy::EmbassyPlatform`
- `LoopEvent` = `twine_view::run::LoopEvent`

## crate twine_embedded_graphics

Documented with features: `drawtarget`.

embedded-graphics adapter for the Twine GUI library, in both directions.

- `EgDisplay` turns any `embedded_graphics_core::draw_target::DrawTarget` — an existing
  embedded-graphics display driver, the embedded-graphics simulator, a framebuffer — into a
  twine `DisplayDriver`. The pixel format follows the target's colour type (`EgColor`:
  `Rgb565`, `Rgb888`, `Gray8`, `BinaryColor`).
- `PainterTarget` (feature `drawtarget`) goes the other way: embedded-graphics primitives,
  fonts and images drawn inside a twine canvas through a `Painter`
  (`painter.as_draw_target::<Rgb565>()` with `PainterExt`).

embedded-graphics: https://docs.rs/embedded-graphics

## crate twine_accel_stm32

Documented with features: `mock`.

STM32 DMA2D (Chrom-ART) draw acceleration for the Twine renderer.

`Dma2d` implements `twine_render::DrawAccel`: attach it to a `Painter`, or hand it to the UI
(`Ui::builder_fb(display).accel(dma2d)`, `Engine::set_accel`), and large fills, image blits and glyph blending run on the DMA2D of
STM32F4/F7/H7 parts while the software renderer handles everything else. The software path
stays complete; whatever DMA2D cannot do returns `AccelResult::Unsupported` and is drawn in
software.

**Layers**

- `Dma2d` holds all register programming and is generic over `Dma2dRegs`, a 32-bit
  register read/write interface.
- `PacRegs` (chip features `stm32f429zi`, `stm32f746ng`, `stm32h743zi`) owns the chip's
  DMA2D (the HAL's handle, one owner at a time) and implements
  `Dma2dRegs` with the `stm32-metapac` register definitions of the chip, and (Cortex-M7,
  feature `dcache`) D-cache maintenance through the core's `SCB`.
- `mock::MockRegs` (feature `mock`) is a recording register file for host tests.

```rust
use twine_accel_stm32::{Dma2d, mock::MockRegs};
use twine_core::{Color, ColorFormat, Opa, Rect};
use twine_render::{DrawBuf, Painter, RenderCaches};

let mut dma = Dma2d::new(MockRegs::new());
let mut caches = RenderCaches::default();
let mut px = vec![0u8; 64 * 64 * 2];
{
    let buf = DrawBuf::new_packed(&mut px, ColorFormat::Rgb565, Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 64, 64)).unwrap();
    let mut p = Painter::new(buf, &mut caches).with_accel(&mut dma);
    p.fill(Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 64, 32), Color::BLUE, Opa::COVER); // programs the DMA2D
} // dropping the painter waits for the transfer
assert_eq!(dma.regs().starts(), 1);
```

On a board, `PacRegs` takes ownership of the HAL's DMA2D handle (at most one `PacRegs`
exists), and the `Ui` takes ownership of the accelerator — nothing to keep or box after
`build`:

```rust
let p = embassy_stm32::init(config);
let regs = PacRegs::new(p.DMA2D).expect("one DMA2D owner");    // F4
// let regs = PacRegs::new(p.DMA2D).expect("..").with_scb(scb); // F7/H7 with the D-cache on
let ui = Ui::builder_fb(display)
    .accel(Dma2d::new(regs).with_timeout(1_000_000))
    /* .runtime(..).platform(..) … */
    .build(app);
```

**Hardware notes**

- Enable the DMA2D clock first (`RCC_AHB1ENR.DMA2DEN` on F4/F7, `RCC_AHB3ENR.DMA2DEN` on H7).
- Buffers must be in memory the DMA2D can reach (not the F4's CCM RAM, not the H7's DTCM).
- Completion is polled (`CR.START`); no interrupt is used.
- Blending rounds differently from the software renderer (±1 per channel).

#### struct twine_accel_stm32::Dma2d<R: twine_accel_stm32::Dma2dRegs>
DMA2D (Chrom-ART) accelerator for STM32F4/F7/H7, implementing `DrawAccel`.
Methods of `Dma2d`:
- `const DEFAULT_MIN_PX: u32` — Default `min_px`: below 256 pixels the software path is faster.
- `pub fn new(regs: R) -> Self` — An accelerator over `regs` (idle; the DMA2D clock must already be enabled).
- `pub fn with_timeout(self, max_polls: u32) -> Self` — Bounds every wait for the hardware to `max_polls` reads of the completion flag (`CR.START`, `FGPFCCR.START` for CLUT loads; at least 1). One poll is one register read, so the bound in time is `max_polls` × (read latency + loop), a few tens of nanoseconds per poll on a 180 MHz Cortex-M4: pick it well above the longest transfer (a full-screen fill), e.g. `1_000_000` polls ≈ tens of milliseconds.
- `pub fn timeout(&self) -> Option<u32>` — The bound set with `with_timeout` (`None`: waits are unbounded).
- `pub fn is_faulted(&self) -> bool` — Whether a wait timed out: the hardware is not used (every operation is drawn in software) until `recover`.
- `pub fn timeout_count(&self) -> u32` — Number of waits that timed out since creation.
- `pub fn recover(&mut self)` — Uses the hardware again after a timeout. Reset the peripheral first (e.g. through its `RCC` reset bit): Twine cannot tell whether a hung DMA2D works again.
- `pub fn with_min_px(self, min_px: u32) -> Self` — Sets the smallest area (in pixels) handled by the hardware.
- `pub fn min_px(&self) -> u32` — The smallest area (in pixels) handled by the hardware.
- `pub fn is_busy(&self) -> bool` — Whether a transfer may still be running (until the next `wait`).
- `pub fn error_count(&self) -> u32` — Number of transfers that ended with an error flag (`TEIF`, `CAEIF`, `CEIF`). Always 0 on correctly configured hardware; each error is also logged.
- `pub fn regs(&self) -> &R` — The register interface.
- `pub fn regs_mut(&mut self) -> &mut R` — The register interface, mutably (waits for the running transfer first; bounded by `with_timeout`).
- `pub fn release(self) -> R` — Waits for the running transfer (bounded by `with_timeout`) and returns the register interface.
Implements: Debug, DrawAccel

#### trait twine_accel_stm32::Dma2dRegs
`pub trait Dma2dRegs`
Access to one DMA2D instance.
Items:
- `fn read(&mut self, reg: twine_accel_stm32::Reg) -> u32` — Reads `reg`.
- `fn write(&mut self, reg: twine_accel_stm32::Reg, value: u32)` — Writes `value` to `reg`.
- `fn clean_dcache(&mut self, addr: usize, len: usize) (provided)` — Writes dirty D-cache lines covering `[addr, addr + len)` back to memory (before the DMA2D reads memory the CPU wrote). Default: no-op.
- `fn clean_invalidate_dcache(&mut self, addr: usize, len: usize) (provided)` — Cleans and invalidates D-cache lines covering `[addr, addr + len)` (before and after the DMA2D writes memory the CPU reads). Default: no-op.
Implemented by: twine_accel_stm32::mock::MockRegs, &mut R

#### enum twine_accel_stm32::Reg
The DMA2D registers used by `Dma2d`, named as in RM0090 §9.5 (STM32F42x/43x), RM0385 §9.5 (STM32F7) and RM0433 §18.6 (STM32H7). The CLUT memories and `LWR`/`AMTCR` are not used.
Variants:
- `Cr` — `DMA2D_CR`: control (mode, start).
- `Isr` — `DMA2D_ISR`: interrupt status (read only).
- `Ifcr` — `DMA2D_IFCR`: interrupt flag clear (write 1 to clear).
- `Fgmar` — `DMA2D_FGMAR`: foreground memory address.
- `Fgor` — `DMA2D_FGOR`: foreground line offset (pixels skipped after each line).
- `Bgmar` — `DMA2D_BGMAR`: background memory address.
- `Bgor` — `DMA2D_BGOR`: background line offset.
- `Fgpfccr` — `DMA2D_FGPFCCR`: foreground PFC control (color mode, alpha mode, alpha, CLUT load).
- `Fgcolr` — `DMA2D_FGCOLR`: foreground color (RGB of A8/A4 foregrounds).
- `Bgpfccr` — `DMA2D_BGPFCCR`: background PFC control.
- `Bgcolr` — `DMA2D_BGCOLR`: background color.
- `Fgcmar` — `DMA2D_FGCMAR`: foreground CLUT memory address.
- `Bgcmar` — `DMA2D_BGCMAR`: background CLUT memory address.
- `Opfccr` — `DMA2D_OPFCCR`: output PFC control (output color mode).
- `Ocolr` — `DMA2D_OCOLR`: output color (register-to-memory fills), in the output color mode.
- `Omar` — `DMA2D_OMAR`: output memory address.
- `Oor` — `DMA2D_OOR`: output line offset.
- `Nlr` — `DMA2D_NLR`: number of lines (`NL`, bits 15:0) and pixels per line (`PL`, bits 29:16).
Methods of `Reg`:
- `const ALL: [twine_accel_stm32::Reg; 18]` — Every register, in address order.
- `pub const fn offset(self) -> usize` — Byte offset of the register from the DMA2D base address (identical on v1 and v2).
- `pub const fn index(self) -> usize` — Index into `Reg::ALL`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

### mod twine_accel_stm32::mock

#### enum twine_accel_stm32::mock::Access

- `CleanInvalidate(usize, usize)` — A D-cache clean + invalidate of `(addr, len)`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_accel_stm32::mock::MockRegs
A DMA2D register file in RAM that records every write and simulates completion.
Methods of `MockRegs`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An idle register file with all registers zero.
- `pub fn with_busy_reads(self, n: u32) -> Self` — Every transfer stays busy for `n` reads of `CR`.
- `pub fn hang(self) -> Self` — Transfers and CLUT loads never complete on their own (a hung DMA2D): only `CR.ABORT` stops them.
- `pub fn set_hang(&mut self, hang: bool)` — Switches `hang` on or off (off: a running transfer completes normally).
- `pub fn aborts(&self) -> u32` — Number of `CR.ABORT` writes so far.
- `pub fn fail_next_transfer(&mut self, flags: u32)` — The next transfer ends with `flags` (e.g. `bits::ISR_CEIF`) set in `ISR`.
- `pub fn log(&self) -> &[twine_accel_stm32::mock::Access]` — Every access so far, in order.
- `pub fn clear_log(&mut self)` — Forgets the recorded accesses.
- `pub fn get(&self, reg: twine_accel_stm32::Reg) -> u32` — Current value of `reg` (no side effects).
- `pub fn last_write(&self, reg: twine_accel_stm32::Reg) -> Option<u32>` — The last value written to `reg`, if any.
- `pub fn starts(&self) -> u32` — Number of transfers started (`CR` writes with `START`).
- `pub fn cr_reads(&self) -> u32` — Number of `CR` reads (polls) so far.
- `pub fn is_running(&self) -> bool` — Whether a transfer is in progress.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Dma2dRegs

### mod twine_accel_stm32::bits

Register bit fields (RM0090 §9.5; v2 on the STM32H7 only adds bits that are not used here).
Cross-checked against the `stm32-metapac` field definitions in this crate's tests.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CR_START
`pub const CR_START: u32`
`CR.START` (bit 0): starts the transfer; hardware clears it when the transfer ends.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CR_ABORT
`pub const CR_ABORT: u32`
`CR.ABORT` (bit 2): aborts the running transfer; hardware clears it with `START`.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CR_MODE_SHIFT
`pub const CR_MODE_SHIFT: u32 = 16`
`CR.MODE` position (bits 17:16 on v1, 18:16 on v2).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MODE_M2M
`pub const MODE_M2M: u32 = 0b00`
`CR.MODE = 00`: memory-to-memory (FG fetch only, no PFC).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MODE_M2M_PFC
`pub const MODE_M2M_PFC: u32 = 0b01`
`CR.MODE = 01`: memory-to-memory with pixel format conversion.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MODE_M2M_BLEND
`pub const MODE_M2M_BLEND: u32 = 0b10`
`CR.MODE = 10`: memory-to-memory with PFC and blending (FG over BG).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MODE_R2M
`pub const MODE_R2M: u32 = 0b11`
`CR.MODE = 11`: register-to-memory (fill with `OCOLR`).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_TEIF
`pub const ISR_TEIF: u32`
`ISR.TEIF` (bit 0): transfer error.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_TCIF
`pub const ISR_TCIF: u32`
`ISR.TCIF` (bit 1): transfer complete.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_CAEIF
`pub const ISR_CAEIF: u32`
`ISR.CAEIF` (bit 3): CLUT access error.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_CTCIF
`pub const ISR_CTCIF: u32`
`ISR.CTCIF` (bit 4): CLUT transfer complete.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_CEIF
`pub const ISR_CEIF: u32`
`ISR.CEIF` (bit 5): configuration error.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::ISR_ERRORS
`pub const ISR_ERRORS: u32`
Error flags of `ISR`.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::IFCR_ALL
`pub const IFCR_ALL: u32 = 0x3F`
`IFCR`: `CTEIF | CTCIF | CTWIF | CAECIF | CCTCIF | CCEIF` (bits 5:0).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CM_ARGB8888
`pub const CM_ARGB8888: u32 = 0x0`
`xPFCCR.CM` / `OPFCCR.CM` = ARGB8888.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CM_RGB888
`pub const CM_RGB888: u32 = 0x1`
Color mode RGB888.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CM_RGB565
`pub const CM_RGB565: u32 = 0x2`
Color mode RGB565.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CM_L8
`pub const CM_L8: u32 = 0x5`
Color mode L8 (8-bit index into the CLUT).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::CM_A8
`pub const CM_A8: u32 = 0x9`
Color mode A8 (8-bit alpha, RGB from `xCOLR`).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::PFCCR_CCM_RGB888
`pub const PFCCR_CCM_RGB888: u32`
`xPFCCR.CCM` (bit 4): CLUT color mode (0 = ARGB8888).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::PFCCR_START
`pub const PFCCR_START: u32`
`xPFCCR.START` (bit 5): starts loading the CLUT; hardware clears it when done.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::PFCCR_CS_SHIFT
`pub const PFCCR_CS_SHIFT: u32 = 8`
`xPFCCR.CS` position (bits 15:8): CLUT size − 1.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::PFCCR_AM_SHIFT
`pub const PFCCR_AM_SHIFT: u32 = 16`
`xPFCCR.AM` position (bits 17:16): alpha mode.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::AM_NO_MODIFY
`pub const AM_NO_MODIFY: u32 = 0b00`
`AM = 00`: keep the pixel's alpha.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::AM_REPLACE
`pub const AM_REPLACE: u32 = 0b01`
`AM = 01`: replace the pixel's alpha with `ALPHA`.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::AM_MULTIPLY
`pub const AM_MULTIPLY: u32 = 0b10`
`AM = 10`: multiply the pixel's alpha by `ALPHA / 255`.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::PFCCR_ALPHA_SHIFT
`pub const PFCCR_ALPHA_SHIFT: u32 = 24`
`xPFCCR.ALPHA` position (bits 31:24).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::NLR_PL_SHIFT
`pub const NLR_PL_SHIFT: u32 = 16`
`NLR.PL` position (bits 29:16): pixels per line.

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MAX_PL
`pub const MAX_PL: u32 = 0x3FFF`
Largest `NLR.PL` (14 bits).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MAX_NL
`pub const MAX_NL: u32 = 0xFFFF`
Largest `NLR.NL` (16 bits).

#### const twine_accel_stm32::bits::MAX_OFFSET
`pub const MAX_OFFSET: u32 = 0x3FFF`
Largest line offset in `FGOR`/`BGOR`/`OOR` (14 bits on v1; v2 has 16, the smaller limit is used everywhere).

## crate twine_sim

Documented with the default features.

**twine-sim**

The desktop simulator of the Twine GUI library:
a native window (winit 0.30 + softbuffer 0.4, pure Rust) showing an **emulated panel** — a
framebuffer in the panel's native pixel format, optionally behind an emulated SPI bus — plus
mouse/keyboard input as twine pointer, keypad and encoder devices, utility hotkeys, and a
headless mode for scripted, deterministic runs in CI.

`twine-sim` is a std-only crate at the top of the crate layering. It depends on `twine-hal` for the driver traits
(its `SimDisplay` is a real `DisplayDriver`) and on the
engine and view crates for the engine and declarative runners.

| Item | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `run`, `run_headless` | declarative apps (`FnOnce(Scope) -> impl View`: a `fn app(cx: Scope) -> impl View` or a closure) with the `Ui` update cycle |
| `run_engine`, `run_engine_headless` | engine apps: an `Engine` on a simulated display, stepped only when it asks to be woken |
| `run_panels`, `run_panels_headless`, `SimPanel`, `PanelLayout`, `PanelCx` | multi-panel apps: several independent `Ui`s (each with its own engine, display, devices and runtime token — e.g. one partition each) side by side in one window; input to the panel under the pointer or the focused one (`panels`) |
| `show_framebuffer`, `show_framebuffer_with_input` | draw raw frames without the engine (with per-frame input: `SimFrame`); window or headless |
| `run_headless_framebuffer` | the same, headless, returning a `HeadlessReport` |
| `SimConfig`, `Headless` | configuration, environment overrides (`TWINE_SIM_*`) |
| `set_title` | change the window title at run time (e.g. to show an example's current settings) |
| `SimDisplay` | emulated panel (formats, bus speed, hardware or software rotation) |
| `SimFramebufferDisplay` | emulated memory-mapped panel for the `Full` / `Direct` buffer modes |
| `SimPointer`, `SimKeypad`, `SimEncoder` | input devices fed by the window or a script |
| `Hotkey` | F1 help, F5–F7 time control (slow motion, pause, single step), F9 screenshot, F10 recording; for engine apps F2 refresh debug, F3 layout bounds, F4 performance overlay, F8 tree dump, F12 next theme mode (`Hotkey::CycleThemeMode`) |
| `script` | the `.twinescript` language of headless runs |

**Environment**

`TWINE_SIM_SCALE=1..4`, `TWINE_SIM_HEADLESS=1`, `TWINE_SIM_SCRIPT=<path>`,
`TWINE_SIM_FRAMES=<n>`, `TWINE_SIM_BUS_HZ=<bits per second>`,
`TWINE_SIM_FORMAT=rgb565|rgb565swapped|rgb888|xrgb8888|argb8888|l8|i1`,
`TWINE_SIM_BUFFERS=single|double|full|direct` (engine apps),
`TWINE_SIM_ROTATION=0|90|180|270` (software rotation by the engine), and `RUST_LOG`
(default `twine=info`; `twine::sim=debug` logs input events and flush times).

```rust
use twine_core::ColorFormat;
use twine_sim::{SimConfig, show_framebuffer};

show_framebuffer(SimConfig::new(320, 240).scale(2), |fb, format, frame| {
    assert_eq!(format, ColorFormat::Rgb565);
    fb.fill((frame % 256) as u8);
});
```

#### const twine_sim::HEADLESS_FRAME
`pub const HEADLESS_FRAME: twine_core::Duration`
Simulated time advanced per headless frame.

#### struct twine_sim::HeadlessReport
What a headless run produced.
Fields:
- `frames: u32` — Frames rendered.
- `sim_time: twine_core::Duration` — Script time at the end (the clock source; unaffected by pausing or slow motion).
- `shots: Vec<PathBuf>` — Every PNG written (script shots, hotkey screenshots, `final.png` last).
- `out_dir: PathBuf` — The output directory.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_sim::SimApp
A simulator application: the emulated display, the input devices, hotkeys and the program that draws frames. Run it with `run` (window or headless, never returns) or `run_headless`.
Methods of `SimApp`:
- `pub fn framebuffer(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, draw: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], twine_core::ColorFormat, u32) + 'static) -> Self` — An app that calls `draw(framebuffer, format, frame_index)` on a full-screen framebuffer in the emulated panel format for every frame and flushes it through the `SimDisplay`.
- `pub fn framebuffer_with_input(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, draw: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], twine_core::ColorFormat, &twine_sim::SimFrame) + 'static) -> Self` — Like `framebuffer`, but `draw` also receives the frame's input (`SimFrame`: keys pressed and clicks since the previous frame, the pointer state).
- `pub fn engine(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, setup: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)) -> Result<Self, twine_sim::SimError>` — An engine app: creates an `Engine` (default configuration plus the simulator's high-resolution timer) with one simulated display — a `SimDisplay` for the partial buffer modes of `SimConfig::buffer_mode`, a `SimFramebufferDisplay` for `Full` and `Direct` — and runs `setup` on it. The engine redraws only what changed and the event loop sleeps while it is idle.
  Errors: `SimError::Engine` when the engine, its display or its input devices cannot be created (for example a colour format whose renderer is not compiled in).
- `pub fn panels(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, panels: Vec<twine_sim::SimPanel>, layout: twine_sim::PanelLayout) -> Result<Self, twine_sim::SimError>` — A multi-panel app (see `crate::panels`): every `SimPanel` gets its own engine (default configuration of its `AppConfig` plus the simulator's high-resolution timer), its own emulated display in `cfg`'s format and bus speed, its own simulated devices (per `SimConfig::input`) and its own `Ui`, mounted on the panel's runtime token; the window shows the panels placed by `layout`. `cfg.width` and `cfg.height` are replaced by the layout's size; the window's title, scale, headless settings and time control are `cfg`'s. Input is routed to the panel under the pointer or the focused panel; each panel's `Ui` wakes the window through its own waker.
  Errors: `SimError::Engine` when a panel's engine or display cannot be created, `SimError::Build` / `SimError::Ui` when a panel's application cannot be mounted.
- `pub fn panel_count(&self) -> usize` — The number of panels of a multi-panel app (0 for other apps).
- `pub fn panel_engine(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&twine_engine::Engine>` — The engine of panel `index` of a multi-panel app (`None` for another app or index).
- `pub fn panel_ui(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&twine_view::UiCore>` — The `UiCore` of panel `index` of a multi-panel app.
- `pub fn panel_inputs(&self, index: usize) -> Option<twine_sim::SimDevices>` — The simulated devices of panel `index` of a multi-panel app (each panel has its own; `inputs` are those of single-panel apps).
- `pub fn focused_panel(&self) -> Option<usize>` — The panel the keyboard and the encoder feed (the last one pressed on; `None` for other apps).
- `pub fn window_size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The window's size in panel pixels (for a multi-panel app: the layout's size).
- `pub fn engine_ref(&self) -> Option<&twine_engine::Engine>` — The engine of an engine app.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut twine_engine::Engine>` — The engine of an engine app, mutably.
- `pub fn set_step_fn(&mut self, f: twine_sim::StepFn)` — Runs `f` instead of `Engine::step` for engine apps (e.g. the declarative `Ui` update cycle); the simulator keeps notifying input changes and waiting for the returned `Wake`.
- `pub fn set_teardown_fn(&mut self, f: twine_sim::TeardownFn)` — Runs `f` with the engine when an engine app is dropped, before the engine (e.g. `UiCore::dispose`, so the application's scopes are disposed with the engine lent).
- `pub fn on_waker(&mut self, sink: Box<dyn FnOnce(Waker)>)` — `sink` receives a waker (usable from any thread) that wakes the window's event loop, e.g. to register it where background tasks signal new data.
- `pub fn inputs(&self) -> twine_sim::SimDevices` — Handles to the simulated input devices.
- `pub fn clock(&self) -> twine_sim::SimClock` — The simulator clock (wall time, or 16 ms per frame when headless).
- `pub fn on_hotkey(&mut self, hotkey: twine_sim::Hotkey, f: Box<dyn FnMut()>)` — Registers a callback for a hotkey (F2–F8, F12 are free for engine runners; F1, F9 and F10 keep their built-in behaviour and additionally run registered callbacks).
- `pub fn frame(&self) -> u32` — Frames rendered so far.
- `pub fn run(self) -> never` — Runs the app — headless when `SimConfig::headless` is set, else in a window — and exits the process: code 0 on window close or headless success, 3 on a script error (printed as `file:line: message`), 1 on other errors.
- `pub fn run_headless(self) -> Result<twine_sim::HeadlessReport, twine_sim::SimError>` — Runs without a window (using `SimConfig::headless`, or `Headless::default`) and returns instead of exiting.
  Errors: `SimError::Io` when the script cannot be read or a PNG cannot be written; `SimError::Script` when the script does not parse.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_sim::SimClock
The simulator clock: wall time since start in a window, exactly 16 ms per frame headless, with time control for animations (hotkeys F5 slow motion ×0.25, F6 pause, F7 single step).
Methods of `SimClock`:
- `pub fn wall() -> Self` — A clock following the wall time from now on (starting at `Instant` 0).
- `pub fn manual() -> Self` — A deterministic clock at `Instant` 0 that only moves with `advance`.
- `pub fn advance(&self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Advances the source of a manual clock by `d` (no effect on a wall clock); the simulator time moves by `d`, `d / 4` in slow motion, or not at all while paused.
- `pub fn set_slow_motion(&self, on: bool)` — Slow motion: time runs at a quarter of the speed (F5).
- `pub fn slow_motion(&self) -> bool` — Whether slow motion is on.
- `pub fn set_paused(&self, on: bool)` — Freezes (`true`) or continues the simulator time (F6). Input is still processed while paused.
- `pub fn paused(&self) -> bool` — Whether the time is paused.
- `pub fn step(&self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Moves a paused clock forward by `d` (F7 steps 16 ms). No effect while running.
- `pub fn wall_duration(&self, d: twine_core::Duration) -> Option<twine_core::Duration>` — The wall time it takes the simulator time to advance by `d` (4 × `d` in slow motion; `None` while paused).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Clock

#### enum twine_sim::SimError
Errors of the simulator runners.
Variants:
- `Script { file: PathBuf, error: twine_sim::script::ScriptError }` — The headless script could not be parsed.
- `Io(Error)` — Reading the script or writing PNGs failed.
- `Window(String)` — The window or event loop could not be created.
- `Engine(twine_engine::EngineError)` — The engine or its display could not be created.
- `Build(twine_view::BuildError)` — The application's views could not be built (see `twine_view::UiCore::mount`).
- `Ui(twine_view::UiError)` — Another error of the declarative runtime (see `twine_view::UiError`).
Implements: Debug, Display, Error, From<twine_engine::EngineError>, From<twine_view::BuildError>, From<twine_view::UiError>, From<Error>

#### struct twine_sim::SimFrame
Per-frame information handed to `SimApp::framebuffer_with_input` programs.
Fields:
- `index: u32` — Frame index (0 for the first frame).
- `time: twine_core::Instant` — Simulator time of the frame (wall time in a window, 16 ms per frame headless).
- `keys: Vec<twine_hal::Key>` — Keys pressed since the previous frame.
- `pointer: Option<twine_hal::PointerData>` — The pointer state (`None` when the pointer device is disabled).
- `clicked: Option<twine_core::Point>` — Where the pointer was released since the previous frame, if it was.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### type twine_sim::StepFn
`pub type StepFn = Box<dyn FnMut(&mut twine_engine::Engine, twine_core::Instant) -> twine_engine::Wake>`
An update function replacing `Engine::step` (see `SimApp::set_step_fn`).

#### type twine_sim::TeardownFn
`pub type TeardownFn = Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)>`
Runs once with the engine when an engine app is dropped, before the engine itself (see `SimApp::set_teardown_fn`). A boxed `FnOnce`: it may own the application's state (e.g. a `UiCore` to dispose).

#### struct twine_sim::Headless
Headless mode: no window, a deterministic clock (16 ms per frame), optional script, PNG output.
Fields:
- `frames: u32` — Frames to render when there is no script (default 60).
- `script: Option<PathBuf>` — A `.twinescript` to execute (see `script`).
- `out_dir: PathBuf` — Where `shot` PNGs and `final.png` are written (default `target/twine-sim/headless/<example-name>/`).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default

#### struct twine_sim::RawKeyHook
Callback of `SimConfig::on_raw_key`: receives the engine and each key pressed on the keyboard, besides the keypad device (for app-level shortcuts that must work whatever is focused).
Fields:
- `0: Box<twine_sim::config::RawKeyFn>`
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_sim::SimConfig
Configuration of the simulator.
Fields:
- `width: u16` — Panel width in pixels (logical, after rotation).
- `height: u16` — Panel height in pixels (logical, after rotation).
- `title: String` — Window title.
- `scale: u8` — Integer window scale, `1..=4`.
- `format: twine_core::ColorFormat` — Emulated panel pixel format (default `Rgb565`).
- `buffer_mode: twine_engine::BufferMode` — The draw buffers of engine apps (default: two 40-row heap buffers, `BufferMode::Alloc(BufferSpec::default())`). `Full` / `Direct` emulate a framebuffer panel; `Partial` / `Alloc` a panel with its own frame memory. Consumed by `SimApp::engine` (the memory moves into the engine).
- `bus_hz: Option<u32>` — Emulated bus throughput in bits per second (`None` = instant flushes).
- `rotation: twine_core::Rotation` — Display rotation.
- `hw_rotation: bool` — `true` (default): rotation is emulated in "hardware" like MIPI `MADCTL` (the window shows the logical screen). `false`: the panel keeps its physical orientation and engine apps rotate in software (the window shows the physical panel).
- `app: twine_view::AppConfig` — The application's configuration (`AppConfig`: engine configuration, theme, motion, channel and queue budgets, fault hook) — the same value the firmware gives `Ui::builder(..).app_config(..)`; set it with `app_config`. The simulator adds its high-resolution timer to the engine configuration. The theme (a `static`: `twine_theme::Lvgl`, `Simple`, `Mono` or a custom `ThemeHook`; default none) is attached when the display is created, before engine apps' `setup` runs and declarative apps are built; `F12` cycles through its modes (`ThemeHook::modes`).
- `input: twine_sim::SimInputs` — Registered input devices.
- `headless: Option<twine_sim::Headless>` — Headless mode when `Some`.
- `mono_colors: (twine_core::Color, twine_core::Color)` — Colors of `0` and `1` bits of an `I1` panel (default black on `#B0C8A0`, "LCD green").
- `fps_limit: Option<u16>` — Frame rate limit of continuously animating apps (default 60, `None` = unlimited).
- `on_raw_key: Option<twine_sim::RawKeyHook>` — Engine apps: called with every key pressed (see `RawKeyHook`).
Methods of `SimConfig`:
- `pub fn new(width: u16, height: u16) -> Self` — A `width × height` panel with defaults: title "twine", scale 1, `Rgb565`, 40-row double buffers, no bus emulation, no rotation, all inputs, windowed, 60 fps.
- `pub fn panel_size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The physical panel size: `width × height`, swapped for a 90°/270° rotation done in software (`hw_rotation == false`). The window and screenshots show the physical panel.
- `pub fn hw_rotation(self, hw: bool) -> Self` — Whether the rotation is emulated in hardware (default) or done by the engine in software (see `SimConfig::hw_rotation`).
- `pub fn engine_config(self, cfg: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — Uses `cfg` for the engine (sets `AppConfig::engine` of `app`; e.g. to give the image cache a budget).
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — The display's theme, a `static` (sets `AppConfig::theme` of `app`). `F12` switches it to its next mode (light → dark → night → high contrast, as far as the theme lists them).
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — The mode the display starts in (sets `AppConfig::theme_mode` of `app`; example: see `theme`).
- `pub fn app_config(self, config: twine_view::AppConfig) -> Self` — Runs the application with `config` — the very `AppConfig` the firmware ships (`Ui::builder(..).app_config(config())`) — so the simulator shows the shipped engine configuration, theme, motion, channel and queue budgets and fault hook. A configured rotation becomes the simulated panel's rotation (`rotation`, emulated in hardware like `MADCTL`); `TWINE_SIM_ROTATION` still overrides it. The window, panel format, buffers and bus emulation stay the simulator's (the engine draws the same pixels with any buffer geometry). Later builder methods refine it.
- `pub fn on_raw_key(self, f: impl FnMut(&mut twine_engine::Engine, twine_hal::Key) + 'static) -> Self` — Calls `f` with the engine for every key pressed (engine apps).
- `pub fn title(self, title: impl Into<String>) -> Self` — Sets the window title.
- `pub fn scale(self, scale: u8) -> Self` — Sets the window scale; values outside `1..=4` are clamped with a warning.
- `pub fn format(self, format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Self` — Sets the emulated panel format; unsupported formats are ignored with a warning (see `SUPPORTED_FORMATS`).
- `pub fn buffers(self, mode: twine_engine::BufferMode) -> Self` — Sets the draw buffers of engine apps: `BufferMode::alloc` (heap partial buffers), caller memory (`BufferMode::partial_double_from` with `draw_buffers!` statics, as on firmware), or `Full` / `Direct` (a framebuffer panel).
- `pub fn bus_hz(self, hz: Option<u32>) -> Self` — Emulates a bus of `hz` bits per second (`None` or 0 = instant).
- `pub fn rotation(self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — Sets the display rotation.
- `pub fn headless(self, headless: Option<twine_sim::Headless>) -> Self` — Runs headless (or windowed with `None`).
- `pub fn mono_colors(self, zero: twine_core::Color, one: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — Sets the colors of `0` and `1` bits of an `I1` panel.
- `pub fn fps_limit(self, fps: Option<u16>) -> Self` — Sets the frame rate limit (`None` = unlimited; 0 is treated as `None`).
- `pub fn from_env(self) -> Self` — Applies the environment: `TWINE_SIM_SCALE`, `TWINE_SIM_HEADLESS=1`, `TWINE_SIM_SCRIPT`, `TWINE_SIM_FRAMES`, `TWINE_SIM_BUS_HZ`, `TWINE_SIM_FORMAT`, `TWINE_SIM_BUFFERS=single|double|full|direct` (the draw buffers of engine apps; partial modes keep the configured rows, default 40) and `TWINE_SIM_ROTATION=0|90|180|270` (the engine rotates in software, the window shows the physical panel: see `hw_rotation`).
- `pub fn from_lookup(self, lookup: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Self` — Like `from_env` with a custom variable lookup (for tests).
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_sim::SimInputs
Which simulated input devices are registered (all by default).
Fields:
- `pointer: bool` — Mouse left button → touch pointer.
- `keypad: bool` — Keyboard → keypad.
- `encoder: bool` — Mouse wheel and middle button → encoder.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### struct twine_sim::FlushStat
Statistics of one flush.
Fields:
- `area: twine_core::Rect` — The flushed area.
- `bytes: usize` — Pixel bytes transferred.
- `started: Instant` — Wall-clock start of the flush.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_sim::SimDisplay
The emulated panel: a framebuffer in the panel's native format, so byte-order and quantisation bugs are visible, with optional bus-speed emulation.
Methods of `SimDisplay`:
- `pub fn new(width: u16, height: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat, rotation: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — A `width × height` panel in `format` (unsupported formats fall back to `Rgb565` with a warning), cleared to zero bytes, without bus emulation.
- `pub fn from_config(cfg: &twine_sim::SimConfig) -> Self` — The panel of `cfg` (size, format, rotation, hardware or software rotation, bus speed, mono colors; flush areas aligned to 8 for `I1`, like page-based mono panels).
- `pub fn with_hw_rotation(self, hw: bool) -> Self` — `false`: the panel keeps its physical orientation and the engine rotates in software (`DisplayInfo::hw_rotation == false`).
- `pub fn panel_size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The physical panel size (see `with_hw_rotation`).
- `pub fn with_bus_hz(self, hz: Option<u32>) -> Self` — Emulates a bus of `hz` bits per second (`None` or 0 = instant).
- `pub fn with_mono_colors(self, zero: twine_core::Color, one: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — Colors of `0` and `1` bits of an `I1` panel.
- `pub fn panel(&self) -> &[u8]` — The raw panel memory (native format, stride = `DisplayInfo::bytes_per_row`).
- `pub fn panel_rgb888(&self) -> Vec<u8>` — The panel as tightly packed 8-bit RGB.
- `pub fn panel_xrgb_into(&self, out: &mut Vec<u32>)` — The panel as `0x00RRGGBB` words, written into `out` (allocation reused).
- `pub fn take_dirty(&mut self) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — The union of the areas that became visible since the last call.
- `pub fn busy_until(&self) -> Option<StdInstant>` — When the oldest flush in flight completes (`None` when idle).
- `pub fn last_flush(&self) -> Option<twine_sim::FlushStat>` — The most recently started flush.
- `pub fn flush_count(&self) -> u64` — Number of accepted flushes.
Implements: Debug, DisplayDriver

#### enum twine_sim::SimDisplayError
Errors of `SimDisplay::begin_flush`. The rejected buffer is returned by the next `poll_flush` (see the `DisplayDriver` contract).
Variants:
- `Busy` — Two flushes are already queued (the engine never has more than two draw buffers).
- `OutOfBounds(twine_core::Rect)` — The area is empty or not fully inside the panel.
- `BufferTooSmall { needed: usize, got: usize }` — The buffer holds fewer bytes than the area needs.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, Error

#### struct twine_sim::SimFramebufferDisplay
An emulated memory-mapped panel (like an LTDC or RGB interface): it hands one or two framebuffers to the engine and "scans out" the presented one. The simulator reads the presented framebuffer back through the engine (`Engine::framebuffer`) to show it. Swaps take effect immediately (no tearing is possible in the simulator).
Methods of `SimFramebufferDisplay`:
- `pub fn new(width: u16, height: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat, rotation: twine_core::Rotation, double: bool) -> Self` — A `width × height` panel in `format` with two (`double`) or one framebuffer. Rotation is emulated in hardware.
- `pub fn presented(&self) -> Option<u8>` — The index of the framebuffer currently shown.
- `pub fn present_count(&self) -> u64` — Number of `present` calls so far.
Implements: Debug, FramebufferDisplay

#### enum twine_sim::Hotkey
A simulator hotkey.
Variants:
- `Help` — F1: print the hotkey table.
- `RefreshDebug` — F2: refresh-area debug overlay.

- `PerfMonitor` — F4: performance monitor.
- `SlowMotion` — F5: slow motion ×0.25.
- `Pause` — F6: pause time.
- `Step` — F7: single-step 16 ms.

- `Screenshot` — F9: screenshot PNG.

- `pub const fn fkey(self) -> u8` — The function key number (`1..=12`).
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<twine_sim::Hotkey>` — Parses `"F1"` … `"F12"`.
- `pub const fn from_winit(key: winit::keyboard::NamedKey) -> Option<twine_sim::Hotkey>` — The hotkey of a winit named key.
- `pub const fn description(self) -> &'static str` — A short description for the help table.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_sim::PanelCx<'a>

- `Row` — Left to right, top-aligned (default).
- `Column` — Top to bottom, left-aligned.

Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_sim::SimPanel
One panel of a multi-panel app: a declarative UI on its own engine and emulated display (see the module docs). Built with `new`, configured with the builder methods, then handed to `SimApp::panels` or `run_panels`, which build its engine and mount the app.
Methods of `SimPanel`:
- `pub fn new<V: twine_view::View>(width: u16, height: u16, rt: twine_reactive::Runtime, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V + 'static) -> Self` — A `width × height` panel running `app` on the runtime `rt` — a partition's token (`Runtime::take_partition`) for independent partitions, or the same token for several panels of one runtime. The application is mounted with the panel's `AppConfig` (`app_config`; default `AppConfig::new`), whose partition is set to `rt`'s. Nothing is built before the app starts.
- `pub fn title(self, title: &str) -> Self` — The panel's name in logs (default: its partition).
- `pub fn app_config(self, config: twine_view::AppConfig) -> Self` — The application's configuration (engine, limits, theme, fault hook, …); the panel's engine also gets the simulator's high-resolution timer.
- `pub fn on_frame(self, hook: impl FnMut(&mut twine_sim::PanelCx<'_>) + 'static) -> Self` — Runs `hook` before every update of the panel (about 60 times per second while the app runs, also while the panel is stopped), with the keys routed to the panel since the last call: host-side code of the simulation, e.g. a sensor feeding a `Latest`, fault injection on keys, or stopping the panel (`PanelCx::set_running`).
- `pub fn size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The panel's size in pixels.
- `pub fn name(&self) -> &str` — The panel's name (`title`).
Implements: Debug

#### fn twine_sim::set_title
`pub fn set_title(title: &str)`
Sets the simulator window title (applied on the window's next tick; headless runs only log it). Call it from the app, e.g. in a `SimConfig::on_raw_key` hook. The title is also logged at `info` level (`twine::sim`).

#### fn twine_sim::init_logging
`pub fn init_logging()`
Initialises `env_logger` with the default filter `twine=info` (`RUST_LOG` overrides). Idempotent.

#### fn twine_sim::show_framebuffer
`pub fn show_framebuffer(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, draw: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], twine_core::ColorFormat, u32) + 'static) -> never`
Shows frames drawn by `draw(framebuffer, format, frame_index)` and never returns.

#### fn twine_sim::show_framebuffer_with_input
`pub fn show_framebuffer_with_input(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, draw: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], twine_core::ColorFormat, &twine_sim::SimFrame) + 'static) -> never`
Like `show_framebuffer`, but `draw` also receives the frame's input (`SimFrame`: keys pressed and clicks since the previous frame, the pointer state).

#### fn twine_sim::run_engine
`pub fn run_engine(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, setup: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)) -> never`
Runs an engine app and never returns: creates an `Engine` with a simulated display (buffer mode, format, rotation and bus speed from `cfg`, after `SimConfig::from_env`), calls `setup` to build the UI imperatively, then steps the engine whenever it asks to be woken — an idle UI leaves the event loop waiting, using no CPU.

#### fn twine_sim::run
`pub fn run<V: twine_view::View>(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> never`
Runs a declarative app and never returns: builds `app` (once) with a `Ui` update cycle on a simulated display (like `run_engine`, after `SimConfig::from_env`) with the pointer, keypad and encoder of `cfg.input` and the application's configuration `cfg.app` (`SimConfig::app_config`: theme, motion, engine configuration, …; no theme by default), then updates whenever the `Ui` asks to be woken — `Wake::Idle` leaves the event loop waiting, using no CPU, until an input or a channel message arrives (channel sends from other threads wake the window). `app` is any `FnOnce(Scope) -> V`: a `fn` item or a closure capturing its configuration; it is called once, when the UI is mounted.

#### fn twine_sim::run_headless
`pub fn run_headless<V: twine_view::View>(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<twine_sim::HeadlessReport, twine_sim::SimError>`
Runs a declarative app headless (with `cfg.headless` or the defaults) and returns a report. The environment is **not** applied. `app` is called once, like in `run`, with the application's configuration `cfg.app` (`SimConfig::app_config`; no theme unless it sets one). No window is opened, so it runs in CI.
Errors: `SimError::Engine` when the engine or the display cannot be created, `SimError::Build` when a widget of `app` cannot be built, `SimError::Script` / `SimError::Io` when the headless script cannot be read or parsed or a PNG cannot be written. Never panics on these.

#### fn twine_sim::run_panels
`pub fn run_panels(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, panels: Vec<twine_sim::SimPanel>) -> never`
Runs a multi-panel app and never returns: one window showing every panel of `panels` side by side (`PanelLayout::Row`), each an independent `Ui` on its own engine, emulated display and input devices (see `panels`). `cfg` gives the title, scale, format, bus speed, input devices and headless settings (after `SimConfig::from_env`); its width and height are replaced by the layout's. Headless runs (`TWINE_SIM_HEADLESS=1`) execute the script, whose coordinates are window coordinates. Exits with code 1 when a panel cannot be built.

#### fn twine_sim::run_panels_headless
`pub fn run_panels_headless(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, panels: Vec<twine_sim::SimPanel>) -> Result<twine_sim::HeadlessReport, twine_sim::SimError>`
Runs a multi-panel app headless (with `cfg.headless` or the defaults) and returns a report instead of exiting. The environment is **not** applied.
Errors: As `SimApp::panels`, and `SimError::Script` / `SimError::Io` for the headless script and output.

#### fn twine_sim::run_engine_headless
`pub fn run_engine_headless(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, setup: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)) -> Result<twine_sim::HeadlessReport, twine_sim::SimError>`
Runs an engine app headless (with `cfg.headless` or the defaults) and returns a report instead of exiting. The environment is **not** applied.
Errors: As `SimApp::engine` and `SimApp::run_headless`.

#### fn twine_sim::run_headless_framebuffer
`pub fn run_headless_framebuffer(cfg: twine_sim::SimConfig, draw: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], twine_core::ColorFormat, u32) + 'static) -> Result<twine_sim::HeadlessReport, twine_sim::SimError>`
Runs `show_framebuffer` headless (with `cfg.headless` or the defaults) and returns a report instead of exiting. The environment is **not** applied.
Errors: As `SimApp::run_headless`.

### mod twine_sim::convert

Conversion of the emulated panel memory to RGB for the window and PNGs.

Deliberately a copy of the logic in `twine-testing` (not a dependency) to keep the simulator
independent of the test crate. Supported panel formats: `Rgb565`, `Rgb565Swapped` (big-endian
bytes), `Rgb888`, `Xrgb8888`, `Argb8888` (alpha ignored, like a real panel), `L8` and `I1`

### mod twine_sim::hotkeys

### mod twine_sim::input

Simulated input devices: mouse → `SimPointer`, wheel + middle button → `SimEncoder`,
keyboard → `SimKeypad`.

Window events (or headless script commands) update a shared `SimInputState`; the devices are
cheap handles over it. All devices report `PollHint::Interrupt`: the simulator wakes the
app on every input event, so no periodic polling is needed.

The mapping functions (`mouse_to_panel`, `WheelAccum`, `map_key`) are pure and tested
without a window.

#### const twine_sim::input::KEY_QUEUE_CAPACITY
`pub const KEY_QUEUE_CAPACITY: usize = 64`
Keypad events kept at most; older ones are dropped (with a warning) when nobody reads them.

#### struct twine_sim::input::SimInputState
The state shared by the simulated devices.
Methods of `SimInputState`:
- `pub fn pointer_press(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point)` — Presses the pointer at `p`.
- `pub fn pointer_move(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point)` — Moves the pointer to `p` (logged at debug while pressed, trace otherwise).
- `pub fn pointer_release(&mut self)` — Releases the pointer (no-op when not pressed).
- `pub fn take_raw_keys(&mut self) -> Vec<twine_hal::Key>` — The keys pressed since the previous call (for `SimConfig::on_raw_key`; the keypad queue itself stays for the keypad device).
- `pub fn take_changes(&mut self) -> twine_sim::input::InputChanges` — The devices whose state changed since the previous call.
- `pub fn take_click(&mut self) -> Option<twine_core::Point>` — The position of the last pointer release since the previous call (a "click").
- `pub fn take_pressed_keys(&mut self) -> Vec<twine_hal::Key>` — Drains the keypad queue, returning the keys pressed since the previous call (for framebuffer runners, where no keypad device reads the queue).
- `pub fn pointer(&self) -> twine_hal::PointerData` — The current pointer state.
- `pub fn key(&mut self, key: twine_hal::Key, pressed: bool)` — Queues a key press or release.
- `pub fn encoder_rotate(&mut self, diff: i16)` — Adds `diff` encoder steps.
- `pub fn encoder_button(&mut self, pressed: bool)` — Presses or releases the encoder button.
- `pub fn release_all(&mut self)` — Releases the pointer and the encoder button (window focus lost: no stuck presses).
- `pub fn queued_keys(&self) -> usize` — Number of queued keypad events.
Implements: Debug, Default

#### struct twine_sim::input::InputChanges
Which simulated devices changed state (the engine is notified for these, like an interrupt line).
Fields:
- `pointer: bool` — Pointer moved, pressed or released.
- `keypad: bool` — Keys queued.
- `encoder: bool` — Encoder rotated, pressed or released.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_sim::input::mouse_to_panel

### mod twine_sim::panels

Multi-panel apps: several independent UIs side by side in one window
(`SimApp::panels`, `run_panels`).

A product can drive several displays from one MCU, each with its own UI — for example a
safety-critical display next to a non-critical one, each in its own **partition**
(`twine_reactive::Runtime::take_partition`, feature `partitions`). A multi-panel app
simulates exactly that: every `SimPanel` is a separate `Ui` with **its own engine**, its own
emulated panel (`SimDisplay`: own flushes, bus timing and dirty areas),
its own simulated input devices and the reactive runtime of the token it was given. The
window only places the panels' pixels side by side (`PanelLayout`); nothing else is
shared, so what one panel does (redraws, faults, slow updates, a stall) never touches
another's engine.

**Input routing.** The pointer goes to the panel under it, in that panel's coordinates; a
press **focuses** the panel and keeps the pointer there until it is released (a drag
leaving the panel stays with it). The keyboard (keypad) and the mouse wheel and middle
button (encoder) go to the **focused** panel — the first one until another is clicked.
Headless scripts route the same way (`tap` a panel to focus it). Engine hotkeys (F2, F3,
F4, F8, F12) act on the focused panel.

**Stepping.** Every tick steps each running panel's `Ui` with the shared simulator clock;
each wakes the window through its own waker. A panel's `on_frame` hook
runs before its update (~60 times per second while any hook is set) with the keys routed
to it (`PanelCx`); it can stop and resume the panel (`PanelCx::set_running`) to
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_sim::panels::PANEL_GAP
`pub const PANEL_GAP: u16 = 4`
Pixels between two panels (and around them) in the window, filled with `GAP_COLOR`.

#### const twine_sim::panels::GAP_COLOR
`pub const GAP_COLOR: u32 = 0x0020_2020`
The colour of the window between the panels (`0x00RRGGBB`).

Re-exports in `twine_sim::panels`:
- `PanelLayout` — same as `twine_sim::PanelLayout`
- `PanelHook` — same as `twine_sim::PanelHook`
- `SimPanel` — same as `twine_sim::SimPanel`
- `PanelCx` — same as `twine_sim::PanelCx`

The cargo target directory: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, else the ancestor of the running executable whose parent holds `Cargo.lock` (`<workspace>/target`), else `./target`.

#### fn twine_sim::paths::sim_dir
