#### fn twine_sim::paths::exe_name
`pub fn exe_name() -> String`
The file stem of the running executable (the example name), or `"sim"`.

### mod twine_sim::script

`.twinescript`: scripted input for headless runs.

One command per line; `#` starts a comment (outside quotes); blank lines are ignored;
integers are decimal (coordinates and wheel steps may be negative).

| Command | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `wait <ms>` | advance the script time |
| `press <x> <y>` / `move <x> <y>` / `release` | pointer |
| `tap <x> <y>` | press, wait 50 ms, release |
| `drag <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <ms>` | press, linear moves every 16 ms, release (takes `ms`) |
| `key <Name>` | press + release of `Key::from_name` (`Enter`, `Up`, `a`, …) |
| `text "<chars>"` | press + release of each character (`\"` and `\\` escapes) |
| `wheel <diff>` | encoder rotation |
| `enc_press` / `enc_release` | encoder button |
| `shot <name>` | write `<out_dir>/<name>.png` |
| `hotkey <F1..F12>` | trigger a simulator hotkey |

#### const twine_sim::script::TAP_MS
`pub const TAP_MS: u64 = 50`
Duration of the press in a `tap` command.

#### const twine_sim::script::DRAG_STEP_MS
`pub const DRAG_STEP_MS: u64 = 16`
Interval of the intermediate moves of a `drag` command.

#### enum twine_sim::script::ScriptCmd
One parsed script command.
Variants:
- `Wait(u64)` — `wait <ms>`.
- `Press(twine_core::Point)` — `press <x> <y>`.
- `Move(twine_core::Point)` — `move <x> <y>`.
- `Release` — `release`.
- `Tap(twine_core::Point)` — `tap <x> <y>`.
- `Drag { from: twine_core::Point, to: twine_core::Point, ms: u64 }` — `drag <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1> <ms>`.
- `Key(twine_hal::Key)` — `key <Name>`.
- `Text(String)` — `text "<chars>"`.
- `Wheel(i16)` — `wheel <diff>`.
- `EncPress` — `enc_press`.
- `EncRelease` — `enc_release`.
- `Shot(String)` — `shot <name>`.
- `Hotkey(twine_sim::Hotkey)` — `hotkey <F1..F12>`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_sim::script::ScriptError
A parse error with its 1-based line number.
Fields:
- `line: usize` — 1-based line number.
- `message: String` — What is wrong.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error

#### fn twine_sim::script::parse
`pub fn parse(src: &str) -> Result<Vec<twine_sim::script::ScriptCmd>, twine_sim::script::ScriptError>`
Parses a whole script.
Errors: The first `ScriptError`, with its line number.

#### enum twine_sim::script::ScriptAction
A timed input or output action derived from a script.
Variants:
- `Press(twine_core::Point)` — Pointer pressed at a point.
- `Move(twine_core::Point)` — Pointer moved.
- `Release` — Pointer released.
- `Key(twine_hal::Key, bool)` — Key pressed (`true`) or released.
- `Wheel(i16)` — Encoder rotation.
- `EncButton(bool)` — Encoder button pressed (`true`) or released.
- `Shot(String)` — Write a screenshot with this name.
- `Hotkey(twine_sim::Hotkey)` — Trigger a hotkey.
Methods of `ScriptAction`:
- `pub fn is_output(&self) -> bool` — Whether the action produces output (applied after the frame at its time is rendered) rather than input (applied before).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_sim::script::schedule
`pub fn schedule(cmds: &[twine_sim::script::ScriptCmd]) -> Vec<(u64, twine_sim::script::ScriptAction)>`
Expands commands into actions with their script time in ms, in execution order.

## crate twine_testing

Documented with features: `ui,engine,render`.

**twine-testing**

Test utilities of the Twine GUI library. This is a std-only crate, at the top of the crate
layering, used as a **dev-dependency** from integration tests (`tests/*.rs`)
of the other crates — never from `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests, where a second copy of the crate
under test would be compiled and types would not match.

Feature-independent parts (always available):

| Item | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `MemoryDisplay`, `FlushRecord`, `leak_buffer` | in-memory `DisplayDriver` recording flushes, with DMA-like latency |
| `MockClock` | manually advanced `Clock` |
| `MockPlatform` | `Platform` and `AsyncPlatform` on simulated time (records waits, counts notifications, simulates interrupt context) |
| `MockPointer`, `MockKeypad`, `MockEncoder`, `MockButton` | scriptable `InputDevice`s |
| `snapshot` | golden images: pixel-exact snapshots against a committed hash manifest (`assert_rgb_snapshot`, `snapshot_config!`, `snapshot::Manifest`) |
| `fuzz` | operation-sequence fuzzing: `fuzz::Bytes`, and with the harness features the tree, input and reactive interpreters (`fuzz` module docs) shared by the property tests and the cargo-fuzz targets |
| `convert` | any supported pixel format → RGB888 |
| `alloc` | `CountingAllocator`, `count_allocs`, `assert_no_alloc_after_seal`, `assert_no_alloc_after_seal_in` (no allocation after `Ui::seal`, per partition) |
| `init_test_logging`, `capture_logs` | `env_logger` for tests, capturing log records |

Harness tiers selected by features (so lower crates can test before higher crates exist):

| Feature | Items |
|---------|-------|
| `render` | `RenderHarness` over the renderer; `gallery`: the renderer's reference drawings (pages of the `render_gallery` example and the renderer snapshot tests) |
| `engine` | `EngineHarness` over a bare engine, `MockDmaDisplay`, `MockFramebufferDisplay`; `scenes`: reference engine scenes (`engine_boxes`, `scroll_list`, …) shared by tests, benchmarks and examples; `theme_coverage`: `assert_theme_covers` (every widget class a UI shows has a recipe in its theme) and the input of `cargo xtask theme-recipes` |
| `ui` (default) | `TestUi` over the declarative UI; per-test ports (`TestUi::channel`, `TestUi::latest`, `TestUi::outbox`: fresh `'static` queues handed to the application instead of global `static`s shared by parallel tests), the shipped configuration (`TestUi::app_config`, `TestUi::limits`), `TestUi::memory_report` and `TestUi::seal` |

```rust
use twine_core::{Color, ColorFormat, Rect};
use twine_hal::{DisplayDriver, DisplayInfo};
use twine_testing::{MemoryDisplay, leak_buffer};

let mut display = MemoryDisplay::new(DisplayInfo::new(8, 8, ColorFormat::L8)).with_latency(2);
let mut buf = leak_buffer(4);
buf.as_mut_slice().fill(255);
display.begin_flush(Rect::from_xywh(0, 0, 2, 2), buf).unwrap();
assert!(display.poll_flush().is_none()); // "DMA" still running
assert!(display.poll_flush().is_some());
assert_eq!(display.pixel(1, 1), Color::WHITE);
```

#### struct twine_testing::MockClock
A clock that only moves when the test says so.
Methods of `MockClock`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A clock at `Instant` 0.
- `pub fn starting_at(start: twine_core::Instant) -> Self` — A clock at `start`.
- `pub fn advance(&self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Moves the time forward by `d` (saturating).
- `pub fn set(&self, t: twine_core::Instant)` — Sets the time. Moving backwards is allowed (for tests of robustness) but logged.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Clock

#### struct twine_testing::EngineHarness
An `Engine` with one display on an in-memory panel, a `MockClock` and helpers to step time, inspect flushes and invalidations, find nodes and compare snapshots.
Methods of `EngineHarness`:
- `pub fn new(w: u16, h: u16) -> Self` — A `w × h` RGB565 display with two 40-row buffers and the LVGL theme in its light mode (`twine_theme::lvgl::THEME`).
- `pub fn set_step_fn(&mut self, f: twine_testing::StepFn)` — Runs `f` instead of `Engine::step` in every `update` (and every helper that updates): the declarative `Ui` installs its update cycle here.
- `pub fn set_teardown_fn(&mut self, f: twine_testing::TeardownFn)` — Runs `f` with the engine when the harness is dropped, before the engine (the declarative `Ui` disposes its scopes here, with the engine lent).
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — Creates the display with `theme` (a `static`) instead of the LVGL theme, starting in its first listed mode (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — Starts the display's theme in `mode` (rebuilds the engine; with `no_theme` it does nothing).
- `pub fn no_theme(self) -> Self` — Uses no theme: nodes have only their own styles and the style defaults (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn format(self, f: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Self` — Uses pixel format `f` for the display (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn buffers(self, b: twine_engine::BufferSpec) -> Self` — Uses heap partial buffers as `b` describes (rebuilds the engine; a framebuffer display set with `framebuffer` goes back to a `MemoryDisplay`). Framebuffer modes are chosen with `framebuffer`.
- `pub fn config(self, c: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — Uses the engine configuration `c` (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn limits(self, limits: twine_core::Limits) -> Self` — Applies `limits` to the engine before its display is added (`Engine::set_limits`; rebuilds the engine), e.g. a small node budget so filling the tree is cheap. In the safety profile they are applied `preallocated`, as the profile requires. Without a call the harness uses `HARNESS_LIMITS`.
  Panics: When `limits` are invalid (`Limits::validate`).
- `pub fn dma(self, polls: u32) -> Self` — Drives the display with a `MockDmaDisplay` whose transfers take `polls` polls, and logs render starts (see `dma_log`).
- `pub fn framebuffer(self, mode: twine_testing::FbMode, present_delay: u32) -> Self` — Uses a `MockFramebufferDisplay` in `mode`, whose swaps take `present_delay` polls.
- `pub fn rotation(self, r: twine_core::Rotation) -> Self` — Software rotation of the panel (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn align(self, a: u8) -> Self` — Flush area alignment of the panel (rebuilds the engine).
- `pub fn dpi(self, dpi: u16) -> Self` — DPI of the panel (`DisplayInfo::dpi`, default 130; rebuilds the engine). Themes and density-independent lengths (`Length::dp`) scale with it.
- `pub fn mount_engine(self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)) -> Self` — Runs `f` on the engine (build the scene).
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> &twine_engine::Engine` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably.
- `pub fn display(&self) -> twine_engine::DisplayId` — The display.
- `pub fn screen(&self) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The active screen.
  Panics: If the harness display was removed from the engine.
- `pub fn clock(&self) -> &twine_testing::MockClock` — The clock (shared with the harness).
- `pub fn now(&self) -> twine_core::Instant` — The current mock time.
- `pub fn update(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One `Engine::step` at the current time. `flushes` and `invalidations` then describe this update only.
- `pub fn advance(&mut self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Advances the clock by `d` in steps of `refr_period`, updating after each step.
- `pub fn run_until_idle(&mut self) -> twine_core::Duration` — Updates (advancing the clock to each requested wake-up) until the engine is idle. Returns the simulated time it took.
  Panics: After 60 simulated seconds, with the tree dump and the pending wake reason.
- `pub fn assert_idle(&mut self)` — Asserts that an update renders nothing and returns `Wake::Idle` (P1).
  Panics: If the update returns anything other than `Wake::Idle` or flushes an area (this is the assertion).
- `pub fn flushes(&self) -> &[twine_testing::FlushRecord]` — The flushes of the last update (partial modes).
- `pub fn invalidations(&self) -> &[(twine_core::Rect, twine_engine::InvalidateReason)]` — The invalidations rendered by the last update's frame (or, when it rendered no frame, those made before it; feature `debug-checks` of the engine).
- `pub fn last_frame(&self) -> twine_engine::RefreshStats` — Statistics of the display's last frame.
- `pub fn tree_dump(&self) -> String` — The whole engine as text (every root of the display).
- `pub fn find_all(&self, q: &twine_testing::Query) -> Vec<twine_engine::NodeId>` — Every node matching `q` (screens and layers of the display).
- `pub fn find(&self, q: twine_testing::Query) -> twine_engine::NodeId` — The single node matching `q`.
  Panics: If none or several match (with the tree dump).
- `pub fn panel_rgb888(&self) -> Vec<u8>` — The panel as 8-bit RGB (physical orientation; for framebuffer modes the presented buffer).
  Panics: If the harness display was removed from the engine.
- `pub fn pixel(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> twine_core::Color` — The panel color at physical pixel `(x, y)`.
- `pub fn memory_display(&self) -> Option<&twine_testing::MemoryDisplay>` — The memory display (partial modes).
- `pub fn framebuffer_display(&self) -> Option<&twine_testing::MockFramebufferDisplay>` — The framebuffer mock (framebuffer modes).
- `pub fn pointer_input(&mut self) -> (twine_engine::InputId, twine_testing::MockPointer)` — The harness pointer (a `MockPointer` with `PollHint::Interrupt`), registered on first use.
  Panics: If the engine refuses the device: the test registered `MAX_INPUTS` devices of its own.
- `pub fn keypad_input(&mut self) -> (twine_engine::InputId, twine_testing::MockKeypad)` — The harness keypad (`MockKeypad`, interrupt driven), registered on first use and attached to the engine's default group (if any at that time).
  Panics: If the engine refuses the device: the test registered `MAX_INPUTS` devices of its own.
- `pub fn encoder_input(&mut self) -> (twine_engine::InputId, twine_testing::MockEncoder)` — The harness encoder (`MockEncoder`, interrupt driven), registered on first use and attached to the engine's default group (if any at that time).
  Panics: If the engine refuses the device: the test registered `MAX_INPUTS` devices of its own.
- `pub fn press(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses the pointer at `p` (notifies the engine) and updates.
- `pub fn move_to(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Moves the (pressed or hovering) pointer to `p` and updates.
- `pub fn release(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Releases the pointer and updates.
- `pub fn tap(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses and releases at `p` (two updates at the same instant).
- `pub fn drag(&mut self, from: twine_core::Point, to: twine_core::Point, dur: twine_core::Duration) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses at `from`, moves linearly to `to` in steps of `read_period` over `dur` (advancing the clock, one update per step) and releases.
- `pub fn key(&mut self, k: twine_hal::Key) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses and releases `k` on the keypad and updates.
- `pub fn key_state(&mut self, k: twine_hal::Key, pressed: bool) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Queues a press (`pressed = true`) or release of `k` and updates.
- `pub fn type_text(&mut self, s: &str) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Types each character of `s` as a `Key::Char` press and release.
- `pub fn encoder(&mut self, diff: i16) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Rotates the encoder by `diff` steps and updates.
- `pub fn encoder_button(&mut self, pressed: bool) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses (`true`) or releases the encoder button and updates.
- `pub fn encoder_click(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — Presses and releases the encoder button (two updates at the same instant).
- `pub fn render_full(&mut self)` — Redraws the whole screen and renders until idle.
- `pub fn assert_snapshot(&mut self, name: &str)` — Redraws the whole screen and compares the panel with the golden image `name` of the crate under test (its entry in `tests/snapshots.toml`, see `snapshot`; the crate is found through the `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `CARGO_PKG_NAME` that cargo sets when running tests).
- `pub fn assert_snapshot_with(&mut self, cfg: &twine_testing::SnapshotConfig, name: &str)` — Like `assert_snapshot` with an explicit configuration.
- `pub fn assert_panel_snapshot(&self, name: &str)` — Compares the panel as it is now (no redraw) with the snapshot `name`, e.g. to capture the effect of one partial frame.
- `pub fn assert_region_snapshot(&mut self, name: &str, r: twine_core::Rect)` — Redraws the whole screen and compares the physical region `r` of the panel.
Implements: Drop, Debug

#### enum twine_testing::FbMode
Framebuffer mode of `EngineHarness::framebuffer`.
Variants:
- `Full` — Two framebuffers with area sync.
- `Direct` — One framebuffer rendered in place.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_testing::HARNESS_LIMITS
`pub const HARNESS_LIMITS: twine_core::Limits`
The harness's limits unless a test sets its own: `Limits::DEFAULT`, except in the safety profile, which refuses limits that are not preallocated and where preallocating the default maxima (65 535 nodes, 64 KiB texts) would make every test reserve megabytes: there the bounds are test-sized (4 096 nodes and handlers, 1 024 animations, 256 timers, 4 KiB texts) and preallocated. Tests that build a `Ui` themselves pass it to `UiBuilder::limits` (or `AppConfig::limits`), so they run in both profiles.

#### enum twine_testing::Query
A node query for `EngineHarness::find` (and `TestUi::find`).
Variants:
- `Text(String)` — The widget's text (`Widget::text`).
- `Id(&'static str)` — The node's test id (`Engine::set_test_id`).
- `Class(&'static str)` — The widget class name.
- `And(Box<twine_testing::Query>, Box<twine_testing::Query>)` — Both queries match.
Methods of `Query`:
- `pub fn matches(&self, engine: &twine_engine::Engine, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> bool` — Whether node `id` matches.
- `pub fn and(self, other: twine_testing::Query) -> twine_testing::Query` — This query and `other`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

Replaces `Engine::step` in `EngineHarness::update` (e.g. the declarative `Ui` cycle).

#### fn twine_testing::profile_limits
`pub const fn profile_limits(limits: twine_core::Limits) -> twine_core::Limits`
`limits` as a test can apply them in either profile: unchanged, except preallocated in the safety profile, which refuses any other (`Limits::validate`). What the harness does with the limits a test gives it; for tests that build a `Ui` with limits of their own. Never panics.

#### fn twine_testing::init_test_logging
`pub fn init_test_logging()`
Initialises logging for tests: `env_logger` output (captured by the test harness, filter from `RUST_LOG`, e.g. `RUST_LOG=twine=debug`) plus the `capture_logs` hook. Safe to call from every test: only the first call has an effect.

#### struct twine_testing::FlushRecord
One flush received by a `MemoryDisplay`.
Fields:
- `area: twine_core::Rect` — The flushed area (screen coordinates).
- `bytes: usize` — Pixel bytes of the area (`stride * height`).
- `buffer_addr: usize` — Address of the draw buffer (`DrawBufferMem::addr`); identifies ping-pong buffers.
- `begin_at: u64` — Value of the display's `poll_flush` call counter when the flush began.
- `end_at: u64` — Value of the `poll_flush` call counter when the buffer was returned (equal to `begin_at` while the flush is still in flight).
- `buffer: u8` — Index of the draw buffer in order of first use (0 = first buffer seen, 1 = second…): a stable name for `buffer_addr`.
- `frame: u32` — Frame number of the flush, filled in by harnesses that know it (0 otherwise).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_testing::MemoryDisplay
An in-memory display: a framebuffer in `info.format` that records every flush.
Methods of `MemoryDisplay`:
- `pub fn new(info: twine_hal::DisplayInfo) -> Self` — A display described by `info`, framebuffer cleared to zero bytes, blocking behaviour.
  Panics: If `info.format` is not supported by `convert`.
- `pub fn with_power_control(self) -> Self` — Supports brightness and sleep (`DisplayDriver::set_brightness`, `DisplayDriver::sleep`): recorded and readable with `brightness` and `is_asleep`. Without it the display answers `Unsupported`, like a driver that does not override them.
- `pub fn with_sleep_settle(self, settle: twine_core::Duration) -> Self` — The settle time `DisplayDriver::sleep` reports (default zero).
- `pub fn with_rotation_control(self) -> Self` — Supports hardware rotation at run time (`DisplayDriver::set_rotation`): the description becomes the rotated logical size with `hw_rotation = true`, and the framebuffer is laid out in logical coordinates from then on (its content is scrambled until redrawn, as on a panel whose `MADCTL` changed).
- `pub fn brightness(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Fraction>` — The brightness last set (`None` before any).
- `pub fn is_asleep(&self) -> bool` — Whether the display was put to sleep (and not woken since).
- `pub fn flushes_while_asleep(&self) -> u64` — Flushes begun while the display was asleep (the engine sends none).
- `pub fn fail_flush_after(&mut self, n: u32)` — Lets the next `n` flushes succeed, then fails every later one with `MemoryDisplayError::Injected` (a bus that breaks down) until `stop_failing`. Replaces any earlier injection.
- `pub fn fail_flush_times(&mut self, n: u32)` — Fails the next `n` flushes with `MemoryDisplayError::Injected`, then lets flushes succeed again (a transient fault). Replaces any earlier injection.
- `pub fn never_complete(self) -> Self` — A display whose flushes never complete: `begin_flush` accepts (and copies) the pixels, but `poll_flush` never hands a buffer back — a hung DMA transfer or a driver that loses buffers. Rejected buffers are withheld too. Undo with `complete_again`.
- `pub fn complete_again(&mut self)` — Hands buffers back again after `never_complete` (the transfer recovered): the next `poll_flush` calls return the held buffers in order.
- `pub fn hang(&mut self)` — Hangs the display now, like `never_complete`.
- `pub fn stop_failing(&mut self)` — Cancels the injected failures: every later flush is processed normally.
- `pub fn failed_flushes(&self) -> u64` — Number of flushes that failed (injected or rejected) since creation.
- `pub fn panel_size(&self) -> (u16, u16)` — The physical panel size: the logical size, with width and height swapped when the display is rotated by 90° or 270° in software (`hw_rotation == false`). Flush areas and the framebuffer use these physical coordinates.
- `pub fn drain_flushes_into(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<twine_testing::FlushRecord>)` — Moves the flush records into `out` (keeping this display's allocation, so a harness that drains every frame does not allocate in steady state).
- `pub fn with_latency(self, polls: u32) -> Self` — Returns buffers on the `polls`-th `poll_flush` call (0 = blocking).
- `pub fn with_max_in_flight(self, n: usize) -> Self` — Allows `n` (≥ 1) buffers in flight at once.
- `pub fn with_mono_colors(self, zero: twine_core::Color, one: twine_core::Color) -> Self` — Colors used for `0` and `1` bits of an `I1` framebuffer (default black, white).
- `pub fn display_info(&self) -> twine_hal::DisplayInfo` — The display description.
- `pub fn framebuffer(&self) -> &[u8]` — The framebuffer bytes (`info.format`, rows of the physical panel width, see `panel_size`).
- `pub fn framebuffer_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [u8]` — The framebuffer, writable: changes what the panel "shows" behind the engine's back, e.g. to simulate a corrupted frame memory for display-integrity tests.
- `pub fn without_read_back(self) -> Self` — Makes the display write-only: `read_back` answers `ControlError::Unsupported`, like a panel without a readable frame memory. (By default a `MemoryDisplay` reads back its framebuffer.)
- `pub fn flushes(&self) -> &[twine_testing::FlushRecord]` — Every flush since creation or the last `take_flushes`.
- `pub fn take_flushes(&mut self) -> Vec<twine_testing::FlushRecord>` — Returns and clears the flush records.
- `pub fn in_flight(&self) -> usize` — Number of buffers currently held for a flush in progress.
- `pub fn poll_count(&self) -> u64` — Number of `poll_flush` calls so far.
- `pub fn to_rgb888(&self) -> Vec<u8>` — The framebuffer as tightly packed 8-bit RGB.
- `pub fn pixel(&self, x: u32, y: u32) -> twine_core::Color` — The color of framebuffer pixel `(x, y)`.
  Panics: If the pixel is outside the screen.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self, c: twine_core::Color)` — Fills the whole framebuffer with `c` (see `convert::write_pixel` for mono formats).
Implements: Debug, DisplayDriver

#### enum twine_testing::MemoryDisplayError
Errors of `MemoryDisplay::begin_flush`. The rejected buffer is returned by the next `poll_flush` (see the `DisplayDriver` contract).
Variants:
- `Busy` — `max_in_flight` flushes are already in progress.
- `OutOfBounds(twine_core::Rect)` — The area is empty or not fully inside the screen.
- `BufferTooSmall { needed: usize, got: usize }` — The buffer holds fewer bytes than the area needs.
- `Injected` — A failure injected with `MemoryDisplay::fail_flush_after` or `MemoryDisplay::fail_flush_times` (nothing was copied).
Methods of `MemoryDisplayError`:
- `pub const fn code(&self) -> u32` — The error's code, as reported by `DisplayDriver::error_code`: `Busy` 1, `OutOfBounds` 2, `BufferTooSmall` 3, `Injected` `INJECTED_CODE`.
- `const INJECTED_CODE: u32` — The code of `MemoryDisplayError::Injected`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, Error

#### fn twine_testing::leak_buffer
`pub fn leak_buffer(len: usize) -> twine_hal::DrawBufferMem`
Creates a 4-byte aligned `len`-byte draw buffer by **leaking** heap memory (tests only).

#### enum twine_testing::DmaEvent
One event of the DMA log (see `dma_log`).
Variants:
- `Begin { buf: u8, area: twine_core::Rect }` — A transfer of `area` from buffer `buf` started (`begin_flush`).
- `Complete { buf: u8 }` — The transfer from buffer `buf` completed (`poll_flush` returned it).
- `RenderStart { buf: u8 }` — The engine started rendering into buffer `buf` (from its render hook).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

Methods of `MockDmaDisplay`:

#### struct twine_testing::MockPlatform
A `Platform` (blocking run loops) and `AsyncPlatform` (`AsyncUi`) on simulated time, for tests: waits do not block, they move a `MockClock`.
Methods of `MockPlatform`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — A platform on a new `MockClock` at `Instant` 0, with no waits recorded and the process-wide notifications made so far already seen (an earlier `notify` does not end its first `wait`). Never panics.
- `pub fn with_clock(clock: twine_testing::MockClock) -> Self` — A platform on `clock` (shared with the caller). Moving the time through `clock` itself does not wake tasks waiting in `poll_wait_until`; use `advance`.
- `pub fn clock(&self) -> &twine_testing::MockClock` — The clock (a clone shares the time).
- `pub fn advance(&self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Moves the time forward by `d` (saturating) and wakes the tasks waiting for a deadline. Never panics (unless a woken task's waker does).
- `pub fn set(&self, t: twine_core::Instant)` — Sets the time (moving backwards is allowed but logged, see `MockClock::set`) and wakes the tasks waiting for a deadline. Never panics (unless a woken task's waker does).
- `pub fn waits(&self) -> usize` — Number of `wait` calls so far (all clones). Never panics.
- `pub fn deadlines(&self) -> Vec<Option<twine_core::Instant>>` — The deadline of every `wait` so far, in order (all clones). Allocates the returned `Vec`; never panics.
- `pub fn yields(&self) -> usize` — Number of `yield_now` calls so far (all clones). Never panics.
- `pub fn notifications() -> u32` — Notifications so far, process-wide (see `MockPlatform`: tests running in parallel add to it, so compare with `>=`). Never panics.
- `pub fn interrupt<R>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` — Runs `f` as if in an interrupt handler: `in_interrupt` returns `true` on this thread until `f` returns (also when it panics).
  Panics: Never by itself; a panic of `f` propagates after the interrupt state is restored.
- `pub fn in_interrupt() -> bool` — Whether the calling thread is inside `interrupt` (the `Platform::in_interrupt` of this platform, callable without naming the trait). Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Clock, Platform, AsyncPlatform

#### struct twine_testing::RenderHarness
A `w × h` buffer in one pixel format plus the renderer caches.
Methods of `RenderHarness`:
- `pub fn new(w: u16, h: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Self` — A buffer cleared to white (opaque for `Argb8888`).
  Panics: If `format` cannot be drawn into or an `I1` width is not a multiple of 8.
- `pub fn with_config(self, cfg: twine_render::RenderConfig) -> Self` — Replaces the caches with ones built from `cfg`.
- `pub fn area(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The screen area of the buffer.
- `pub fn format(&self) -> twine_core::ColorFormat` — The pixel format.
- `pub fn data(&self) -> &[u8]` — The raw buffer bytes.
- `pub fn caches(&self) -> &twine_render::RenderCaches` — The caches (e.g. to read their statistics).
- `pub fn clear(&mut self, c: twine_core::Color)` — Fills the whole buffer with `c` (opaque).
- `pub fn paint<R>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_render::Painter<'_>) -> R) -> R` — Draws with a painter over the whole buffer.
  Panics: If the harness's colour format cannot be drawn into or its renderer is not compiled in, or for an `I1` harness whose width is not a multiple of 8 (see `DrawBuf::new`).
- `pub fn paint_chunked(&mut self, rows: u16, f: impl FnMut(&mut twine_render::Painter<'_>))` — Draws in horizontal strips of `rows` rows, each into a separate strip buffer that starts with the current content and is copied back — like the engine's partial buffers. Used to prove that chunked rendering is pixel-identical to a full render.
  Panics: If the harness's colour format cannot be drawn into or its renderer is not compiled in, or for an `I1` harness whose width is not a multiple of 8 (see `DrawBuf::new`).
- `pub fn rgb888(&self) -> Vec<u8>` — The buffer as 8-bit RGB (`Argb8888` composited over mid gray, `I1` as black/white).
- `pub fn assert_snapshot_with(&self, cfg: &twine_testing::SnapshotConfig, name: &str)` — Compares the buffer with the golden image `name` of `cfg` (its manifest entry), pixel-exact. Usually called through `assert_render_snapshot!`.
Implements: Debug

#### struct twine_testing::SnapshotConfig
Where a crate's manifest, reference cache and artefacts are, and how the run behaves.
Fields:
- `dir: PathBuf` — Directory of the local reference PNG cache (usually `<manifest>/tests/snapshots`).
- `manifest: PathBuf` — The committed manifest (usually `<manifest>/tests/snapshots.toml`).
- `crate_name: String` — Crate name, used for the artefact directory `target/twine-snapshots/<crate_name>/`.
- `ci: Option<bool>` — Override of the `CI` environment variable (`None` = read the environment).
- `mode: Option<twine_testing::snapshot::SnapshotMode>` — Override of `TWINE_SNAPSHOTS` (`None` = read the environment).
Methods of `SnapshotConfig`:
- `pub fn for_crate(manifest_dir: &str, crate_name: &str) -> Self` — The configuration of the crate at `manifest_dir`: cache `<manifest_dir>/tests/snapshots`, manifest `<manifest_dir>/tests/snapshots.toml`, switches read from the environment. Usually created with `snapshot_config!`.
- `pub fn is_ci(&self) -> bool` — Whether the run is in CI (override, else `CI` is set to anything but `""`, `0`, `false`).
- `pub fn mode(&self) -> twine_testing::snapshot::SnapshotMode` — The run's mode (override, else `SnapshotMode::from_env`).
- `pub fn path(&self, name: &str) -> PathBuf` — The cached reference PNG of snapshot `name`.
- `pub fn artifacts_dir(&self) -> PathBuf` — The directory mismatch artefacts are written to: `<target>/twine-snapshots/<crate_name>`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::assert_rgb_snapshot
`pub fn assert_rgb_snapshot(cfg: &twine_testing::SnapshotConfig, name: &str, w: u32, h: u32, rgb: &[u8], tol: twine_testing::Tolerance)`
Compares the `w × h` 8-bit RGB image `rgb` with the manifest entry `name` of `cfg` (see the module docs for the full behaviour).
Panics: On an invalid name (must match `^[a-z0-9_]+$`), an `rgb` of the wrong length, an unreadable manifest, a missing entry (`Check` mode), a mismatch, or I/O errors writing artefacts.

#### struct twine_testing::ThemeCoverage
The theme classes of every themed node of an engine, each once, in the order first met (displays in order, parents first). See `theme_coverage`.
Fields:
- `classes: Vec<twine_testing::theme_coverage::CoveredClass>` — One entry per (display theme, theme class).

- `pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool` — Whether every class has a recipe.
- `pub fn recipes(&self) -> Vec<twine_engine::RecipeRef>` — The recipes in use, each once, in the order first met: the minimal recipe list of the UI (what `cargo xtask theme-recipes` prints).
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, Display

#### fn twine_testing::assert_theme_covers
`pub fn assert_theme_covers(engine: &twine_engine::Engine)`
Asserts that the theme of every display of `engine` has a recipe for every theme class its nodes use (`theme_coverage`): build the product's screens headless (a `TestUi`, an `EngineHarness`) and call it, so a design system's recipe list cannot miss a widget the product shows.
Panics: When a class has no recipe, listing those classes (a test assertion).

#### fn twine_testing::theme_coverage
`pub fn theme_coverage(engine: &twine_engine::Engine) -> twine_testing::ThemeCoverage`
Which recipe styles each theme class of `engine`'s themed nodes (every display with a theme: the nodes of its screens and layers, `Engine::themed_nodes`), as the display's theme answers `ThemeHook::recipe` (the built-in themes answer with their per-class recipes). A theme that styles in code without recipes has all its classes missing. Control-flow wrappers (`ObjFlags::LAYOUT_PASSTHROUGH`: `when`, `for_each`, …) draw nothing and are left out.

#### struct twine_testing::NodeHandle<'a>
A node found by `TestUi::find`.

#### struct twine_testing::TestUi
The high-level test harness: an `EngineHarness` (RGB565 `MemoryDisplay`, `MockClock`, mock pointer, keypad and encoder) whose updates run the declarative `Ui` cycle.
Methods of `TestUi`:
- `pub fn new(w: u16, h: u16) -> Self` — A `w × h` RGB565 display with the default light theme.
- `pub fn in_partition(self, p: twine_core::Partition) -> Self` — Runs the application in partition `p` (ADR-001): the mount uses this thread's runtime of `p` (`Runtime::current_thread_partition`) and puts the engine into `p`, so two `TestUi`s of two partitions on one thread are independent — the way a product runs a critical and a non-critical display. Default `Partition::MAIN`. Builder; before `mount`.
- `pub fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the application runs in (`in_partition`; default `Partition::MAIN`).
- `pub fn channel<T: 'static, const N: usize>() -> &'static twine_reactive::Channel<T, N>` — A fresh `'static` `Channel` for one test: give it to the application through its ports (see `Scope::on_message` § Ports) instead of sharing a global `static` between tests, which the test harness runs in parallel (a value sent by one test would reach another test's UI). Leaks the channel (a few bytes per call; test-only).
- `pub fn latest<T: 'static>(initial: T) -> &'static twine_reactive::Latest<T>` — A fresh `'static` `Latest` holding `initial`, for one test (see `channel`). Leaks the cell.
- `pub fn outbox<T: 'static, const N: usize>() -> &'static twine_reactive::Outbox<T, N>` — A fresh `'static` `Outbox` for one test (see `channel`): the test plays the consumer with `try_recv`. Leaks the outbox.
- `pub fn format(self, f: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Self` — Uses pixel format `f`.
- `pub fn theme(self, theme: &'static dyn twine_engine::ThemeHook) -> Self` — Uses `theme` (a `static`) as the display's theme (and as `AppConfig::theme` after `app_config`), starting in its first listed mode.
- `pub fn mode(self, mode: twine_style::ThemeMode) -> Self` — Starts the display's theme in `mode` (also `AppConfig::theme_mode` after `app_config`). Example: see `theme`.
- `pub fn no_theme(self) -> Self` — Uses no theme (also clears `AppConfig::theme` after `app_config`): widgets draw only their local styles. Never panics.
- `pub fn buffers(self, m: twine_engine::BufferSpec) -> Self` — Uses heap partial buffers as `m` describes (see `EngineHarness::buffers`).
- `pub fn config(self, c: twine_engine::EngineConfig) -> Self` — Uses the engine configuration `c` (also `AppConfig::engine` after `app_config`). Never panics.
- `pub fn app_config(self, config: twine_view::AppConfig) -> Self` — Runs the application with `config` — the very `AppConfig` the firmware gives `Ui::builder(..).app_config(..)` and the simulator `SimConfig::app_config(..)` — so the test sees the shipped engine configuration, theme (`None`: no theme), motion, rotation (the in-memory panel is rotated in software), channel and queue budgets and fault hook. The harness keeps its own panel size, format and buffers (the engine draws the same pixels with any buffer geometry). Call before `mount`; later builder methods refine it, and the mount applies it (over settings a test made on the engine with `mount_engine`). Without it, the harness's defaults stay as they are.
- `pub fn limits(self, limits: twine_core::Limits) -> Self` — Uses `limits` (also `AppConfig::limits` after `app_config`): applied to the harness engine before its display is added, and to the runtime by the mount when an `AppConfig` is set. Rebuilds the engine.
  Panics: When `limits` are invalid.
- `pub fn seal(&mut self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — Seals the mounted application as `Ui::seal` does (`UiCore::seal`: the heap budget is checked, then Twine's allocation guard is sealed for this thread and the UI's partition) and returns the memory report at sealing time. Pair it with `assert_no_alloc_after_seal` around the steady-state updates; unseal with `twine_core::alloc_guard::unseal(partition)` when the test goes on building.
  Panics: Before `mount`.
- `pub fn with_waker(self, waker: &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker) -> Self` — Mounts with the application's own `waker` (typically a `static UiWaker` of the test) instead of one leased from the process-wide pool, like `UiBuilder::waker`.
- `pub fn mount<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Self` — Builds `app` (once) on the display, like `Ui::build`: a default focus group for the keypad and the encoder is created first. Updates then run the `Ui` cycle.
  Panics: When a widget of `app` cannot be created (see `try_mount`).
- `pub fn try_mount<V: twine_view::View>(self, app: impl FnOnce(twine_reactive::Scope) -> V) -> Result<Self, twine_view::UiError>` — `mount`, returning the error (see `UiCore::mount_configured`) instead of panicking.
  Errors: `UiError::Build` when a widget of `app` cannot be created; `UiError::Engine` when the configuration cannot be applied (see `AppConfig::configure_engine`).
- `pub fn mount_engine(self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut twine_engine::Engine)) -> Self` — Runs `f` on the engine (imperative scenes; can be combined with `mount`).
- `pub fn root_scope(&self) -> twine_reactive::Scope` — The root scope of the mounted application.
  Panics: Before `mount`.
- `pub fn waker(&self) -> &'static twine_reactive::UiWaker` — The `Ui`'s waker (set by channel sends).
  Panics: Before `mount`.
- `pub fn update(&mut self) -> twine_engine::Wake` — One update at the current mock time.
- `pub fn advance(&mut self, d: twine_core::Duration)` — Advances the clock by `d` in steps of `refr_period`, updating after each step.
- `pub fn run_until_idle(&mut self) -> twine_core::Duration` — Updates, jumping the clock to each requested wake-up, until the `Ui` is idle. Returns the simulated time it took.
  Panics: After 60 simulated seconds, with a report: running animations, timers, pressed inputs and the tree dump.
- `pub fn press(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point)` — Presses the pointer at `p` and updates.
- `pub fn release(&mut self)` — Releases the pointer and updates.
- `pub fn tap(&mut self, p: twine_core::Point)` — Presses and releases at `p`.
- `pub fn drag(&mut self, from: twine_core::Point, to: twine_core::Point, dur: twine_core::Duration)` — Drags from `from` to `to` over `dur` (one pointer read per `read_period`).
- `pub fn key(&mut self, k: twine_hal::Key)` — Presses and releases `k` on the keypad.
- `pub fn type_text(&mut self, s: &str)` — Types `s` on the keypad (one `Key::Char` press and release per character).
- `pub fn keyboard_type(&mut self, kb: twine_engine::NodeId, s: &str)` — Types `s` by tapping the keys of the on-screen keyboard `kb` (a `Keyboard` node), switching its layout with the mode keys (`abc`, `ABC`, `1#`) when a character is on another layout. `'\n'` taps the new-line key. Each tap is followed by a short wait so a key never counts as a long press or a double click.
  Panics: If `kb` is not a keyboard or a character has no key on any layout.
- `pub fn encoder(&mut self, diff: i16)` — Rotates the encoder by `diff` steps.
- `pub fn encoder_click(&mut self)` — Clicks the encoder button.
- `pub fn find(&self, q: twine_testing::Query) -> twine_testing::NodeHandle<'_>` — The single node matching `q`.
  Panics: If none or several match, listing the tree.
- `pub fn find_all(&self, q: twine_testing::Query) -> Vec<twine_testing::NodeHandle<'_>>` — Every node matching `q`.
- `pub fn node(&self, id: twine_engine::NodeId) -> twine_testing::NodeHandle<'_>` — A handle to node `id`.
- `pub fn tree_dump(&self) -> String` — The whole engine as text.
- `pub fn assert_snapshot(&mut self, name: &str)` — Redraws the whole screen and compares it with the snapshot `name`.
- `pub fn assert_panel_snapshot(&self, name: &str)` — Compares the panel as it is (no redraw, no time passing) with the snapshot `name`, e.g. in the middle of an animation.
- `pub fn assert_region_snapshot(&mut self, name: &str, r: twine_core::Rect)` — Redraws the whole screen and compares region `r` with the snapshot `name`.
- `pub fn assert_idle(&mut self)` — Asserts that an update renders nothing and returns `Wake::Idle`.
- `pub fn last_frame(&self) -> twine_engine::RefreshStats` — Statistics of the application's last frame (a snapshot's full redraw does not count).
- `pub fn invalidations(&self) -> Ref<'_, [(twine_core::Rect, twine_engine::InvalidateReason)]>` — The invalidations rendered by the last update.
- `pub fn flushes(&self) -> Ref<'_, [twine_testing::FlushRecord]>` — The flushes of the last update.
- `pub fn memory_report(&self) -> twine_view::MemoryReport` — What the scene's memory is used for: the engine, the reactive runtime, the command queues and the waker pool (`MemoryReport`; as `Ui::memory_report`, so a test can pin the memory of a scene). Before `mount` only the engine part is filled. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn engine(&self) -> Ref<'_, twine_engine::Engine>` — The engine.
- `pub fn engine_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_engine::Engine` — The engine, mutably.
- `pub fn harness_mut(&mut self) -> &mut twine_testing::EngineHarness` — The underlying engine harness.
Implements: Debug

#### macro twine_testing::assert_render_snapshot!
```rust
macro_rules! assert_render_snapshot {
    ($h:expr, $name:expr) => { ... };
}
```
Asserts a `RenderHarness` snapshot against the calling crate's golden-image manifest (`tests/snapshots.toml`, see `snapshot`).

#### macro twine_testing::snapshot_config!
```rust
macro_rules! snapshot_config {
    () => { ... };
}
```
The `SnapshotConfig` of the calling crate (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `CARGO_PKG_NAME`).

### mod twine_testing::alloc

Allocation counting: `CountingAllocator`, `count_allocs` and
`assert_no_alloc_after_seal`.

Install the allocator in a test binary (one integration test file) that needs it:


Counters are **per thread**, so tests running in parallel do not disturb each other. Without
the global allocator installed, `count_allocs` always reports zero.

#### struct twine_testing::alloc::AllocStats
Allocation statistics of one thread.
Fields:
- `allocs: u64` — `alloc` / `alloc_zeroed` calls.
- `deallocs: u64` — `dealloc` calls.
- `reallocs: u64` — `realloc` calls.
- `bytes: u64` — Bytes requested by `alloc`, `alloc_zeroed` and `realloc` (new size).
- `live: i64` — Live heap bytes: allocated minus freed (a difference of two snapshots is the growth of the heap in between).
- `peak: i64` — The highest `live` reached (the heap high-water mark). In the statistics of `count_allocs`: the highest growth of the heap during the call, transient allocations included.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### fn twine_testing::alloc::current
`pub fn current() -> twine_testing::alloc::AllocStats`
The statistics of the current thread since it started.

#### fn twine_testing::alloc::count_allocs
`pub fn count_allocs<R>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> (R, twine_testing::alloc::AllocStats)`
Runs `f` and returns its result with the allocations it made on this thread (`peak`: the highest heap growth during `f`; it restarts the thread's high-water mark, so nested calls report the outer peak from the inner call on).

#### fn twine_testing::alloc::assert_no_alloc_after_seal
`pub fn assert_no_alloc_after_seal<R>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`
Runs `f` **sealed** and asserts that it allocated nothing: no allocation, reallocation or growth on this thread seen by the `CountingAllocator` (which must be the test binary's global allocator — checked first with a probe allocation), and no growth point noted by Twine's allocation guard (`twine_core::alloc_guard`, which names the site) in `Partition::MAIN`. Returns `f`'s result. For a UI of another partition use `assert_no_alloc_after_seal_in`.
Panics: When the counting allocator is not installed, or when `f` allocated (the message has the allocator's statistics and the last growth point the guard noted).

#### fn twine_testing::alloc::assert_no_alloc_after_seal_in
`pub fn assert_no_alloc_after_seal_in<R>(p: twine_core::Partition, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`
`assert_no_alloc_after_seal` for the UI of partition `p` (ADR-001 § 5.3): seals `p`'s seal domain for `f` and checks the growth Twine noted **in `p`**. The counting allocator still sees every allocation of the thread, whichever partition made it, so run only `p`'s work inside `f`.
Panics: As `assert_no_alloc_after_seal`.

#### struct twine_testing::alloc::CountingAllocator
A global allocator that forwards to `System` and counts calls per thread.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, GlobalAlloc

### mod twine_testing::convert

Pixel format conversion for assertions and snapshots: any supported `ColorFormat` buffer →
8-bit RGB.

Supported formats: every byte-aligned `PixelFormat`
(`Rgb565`, `Rgb565Swapped`, `Rgb888`, `Xrgb8888`, `Argb8888`, `L8`) plus `A8` (shown as gray,
`0` = black) and `I1` (1-bit, MSB first, shown with the two `mono` colors). `Argb8888` is
composited over mid gray `#808080`, so transparency is visible in snapshots. Other formats
panic with a clear message — this is a test-only crate.

#### const twine_testing::convert::ALPHA_BACKGROUND
`pub const ALPHA_BACKGROUND: twine_core::Color = Color::GRAY`
The background `Argb8888` pixels are composited over.

#### fn twine_testing::convert::is_supported
`pub const fn is_supported(format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> bool`
Whether `format` can be converted by this module.

#### fn twine_testing::convert::pixel_color
`pub fn pixel_color(buf: &[u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat, stride: u32, x: u32, y: u32, mono: (twine_core::Color, twine_core::Color)) -> twine_core::Color`
The color of pixel `(x, y)` of a buffer with row pitch `stride` bytes.
Panics: If `format` is unsupported or the pixel lies outside `buf`.

#### fn twine_testing::convert::to_rgb888
`pub fn to_rgb888(buf: &[u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat, w: u32, h: u32, stride: u32, mono: (twine_core::Color, twine_core::Color)) -> Vec<u8>`
Converts a `w × h` buffer (row pitch `stride` bytes) to tightly packed 8-bit RGB (`w * h * 3` bytes).
Panics: If `format` is unsupported or `buf` is shorter than `stride * (h - 1)` + one row.

#### fn twine_testing::convert::write_pixel
`pub fn write_pixel(buf: &mut [u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat, stride: u32, x: u32, y: u32, c: twine_core::Color)`
Writes `c` as pixel `(x, y)` of a buffer in `format` (for filling test displays).
Panics: If `format` is unsupported or the pixel lies outside `buf`.

### mod twine_testing::fuzz

Operation-sequence fuzzing beyond the decoders (R5.S08): interpreters that turn arbitrary
bytes into sequences of API calls and check the library's invariants after every call.

| Interpreter | Operations | Checked after every operation | Feature |
|-------------|------------|-------------------------------|---------|
| `run_tree_ops` | create, delete, move, position, size, flags, states, flex layout, scroll, render steps — on live **and stale** node ids | `Tree::check_invariants`, the node and depth bounds of `Limits`, only `Capacity` faults | `engine` |
| `run_input_ops` | pointer press/move/release, keys, encoder turns and clicks, time, pointer health — on a screen of real widgets | tree invariants, the focused node is alive, faults limited to `InputDevice` (and only after a health change) | `ui` |
| `run_reactive_ops` | scopes (create, dispose), signals, memos, effects, writes, batches, reads — on live **and disposed** handles | live node and scope counts equal the model, no effect left pending, memo values and effect runs equal the model, disposed handles answer `Disposed`; disposing everything returns the runtime to its starting counts | `ui` |

The same functions drive two harnesses: property tests on stable (`proptest` feeding random
bytes; they run with the workspace tests: `twine-testing/tests/fuzz_*.rs`) and the
cargo-fuzz targets `tree_ops`, `input_events` and `reactive_ops` of `fuzz/` (nightly,
coverage-guided; `cargo xtask fuzz <target>`). Decoding never fails: missing bytes read as
zero, so every byte string is a valid program.

A violated invariant panics with the operation index and the operation list, which is what
both harnesses report and shrink.

#### struct twine_testing::fuzz::Bytes<'a>
A reader of fuzz input: each call takes the next bytes; past the end it returns zeros.
Methods of `Bytes`:
- `pub fn new(data: &'a [u8]) -> Self` — A reader over `data`.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether every byte was read.
- `pub fn u8(&mut self) -> u8` — The next byte (0 past the end).
- `pub fn u16(&mut self) -> u16` — The next two bytes, little-endian.
- `pub fn i8(&mut self) -> i8` — The next byte as a signed value.
- `pub fn bool(&mut self) -> bool` — The next byte as a bool (lowest bit).
Implements: Clone, Debug

#### enum twine_testing::fuzz::TreeOp
One mutation of the widget tree. Node operands are indices into the list of nodes the run created (the screen is index 0), taken modulo its length — so they also name nodes that were deleted since: stale ids, which must be ignored with a warning (P7).
Variants:
- `Create { parent: u8 }` — Creates a plain object under `parent`.
- `Delete { node: u8 }` — Deletes `node` (and its subtree).
- `Move { node: u8, parent: u8 }` — Moves `node` under `parent` (refused for cycles, depth and dead nodes).
- `Pos { node: u8, x: i8, y: i8 }` — Sets the position.
- `Size { node: u8, w: i8, h: i8 }` — Sets the size (negative values included).
- `Flag { node: u8, flag: u8, on: bool }` — Sets or clears one of a few flags (`HIDDEN`, `SCROLLABLE`, `FLOATING`, `CLICKABLE`).
- `State { node: u8, state: u8, on: bool }` — Sets or clears one of a few states.
- `Flex { node: u8, kind: u8 }` — Switches the layout: none, flex row, flex column, flex row wrap.
- `Scroll { node: u8, dx: i8, dy: i8 }` — Scrolls by `(dx, dy)`.
- `Step { ms: u8 }` — Lets `ms` milliseconds pass and runs an update (layout and rendering).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_testing::fuzz::TreeRun
What a `run_tree_ops` run did.
Fields:
- `alive: usize` — Nodes alive at the end (screen included).
- `capacity_faults: u32` — `Capacity` faults raised (node or depth bound reached).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::decode_tree_ops
`pub fn decode_tree_ops(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<twine_testing::fuzz::TreeOp>`
Decodes up to 256 tree operations from fuzz input. Never fails.

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::run_tree_ops
`pub fn run_tree_ops(ops: &[twine_testing::fuzz::TreeOp]) -> twine_testing::fuzz::TreeRun`
Runs `ops` on a fresh 96×64 engine with small `Limits` and checks the invariants after every operation (see the module docs). Returns what the run did.
Panics: When an invariant is violated (the message names the operation), or when the library panics.

#### enum twine_testing::fuzz::InputOp
One input event (or the passage of time) delivered through the mock input devices.
Variants:
- `Press { x: u8, y: u8 }` — Pointer pressed at `(x, y)` (may lie outside the screen).
- `Move { x: u8, y: u8 }` — Pointer moved to `(x, y)`.
- `Release` — Pointer released.
- `Key { key: u8 }` — One of the navigation and editing keys, or a character.
- `Encoder { diff: i8 }` — Encoder turned by `diff` steps.
- `EncoderClick` — Encoder button clicked.
- `Wait { ms: u8 }` — `ms` milliseconds pass (timers, long press, animations).
- `PointerHealth { health: u8 }` — The pointer reports `Ok`, `Degraded` or `Failed`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::decode_input_ops
`pub fn decode_input_ops(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<twine_testing::fuzz::InputOp>`
Decodes up to 256 input events from fuzz input. Never fails.

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::run_input_ops
`pub fn run_input_ops(ops: &[twine_testing::fuzz::InputOp])`
Runs `ops` on a 200×150 screen of widgets (button, checkbox, slider, switch, textarea, spinbox, arc in one focus group, default theme) and checks the invariants after every event (see the module docs).
Panics: When an invariant is violated (the message names the event), or when the library panics.

#### enum twine_testing::fuzz::ReactiveOp
One reactive operation. Operands are indices into the run's scopes, signals, memos or effects (modulo their count), so they also name disposed ones.
Variants:
- `Scope { parent: u8 }` — A child scope of `parent`.
- `Dispose { scope: u8 }` — Disposes `scope` (never the root) and everything in it.
- `Signal { scope: u8, value: i8 }` — A signal in `scope` holding `value`.
- `Memo { scope: u8, a: u8, b: u8 }` — A memo in `scope` summing two signals of `scope` or its ancestors.
- `Effect { scope: u8, signal: u8 }` — An effect in `scope` reading one signal of `scope` or its ancestors.
- `Set { signal: u8, value: i8 }` — Writes `value` to `signal`.
- `Batch { first: u8, count: u8, value: i8 }` — Writes several signals in one batch (`count` writes from the following operands).
- `Read { memo: u8 }` — Reads `memo` (or a signal when there is none).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::decode_reactive_ops
`pub fn decode_reactive_ops(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<twine_testing::fuzz::ReactiveOp>`
Decodes up to 256 reactive operations from fuzz input. Never fails.

#### fn twine_testing::fuzz::run_reactive_ops
`pub fn run_reactive_ops(ops: &[twine_testing::fuzz::ReactiveOp])`
Runs `ops` in a fresh root scope of the calling thread's runtime and checks the runtime against a model after every operation; at the end the root is disposed and the runtime must be back at its starting node, scope, queue and registration counts (see the module docs).
Panics: When the runtime differs from the model (the message names the operation), or when the library panics.

### mod twine_testing::mock_input

Mock input devices: `MockPointer`, `MockKeypad`, `MockEncoder`, `MockButton`.

Each mock is a cheap clonable handle over shared state (`Rc<RefCell<…>>`): the test keeps
one handle to drive the device while the engine owns another as its `InputDevice`.
Every mock counts its `read` and `rearm` calls
and has a configurable `PollHint` (default `PollHint::Periodic`) and
`DeviceHealth` (default `DeviceHealth::Ok`, see `set_health`) to simulate a failing
device.

Re-exports in `twine_testing::mock_input`:
- `MockPointer` — same as `twine_testing::MockPointer`
- `MockKeypad` — same as `twine_testing::MockKeypad`
- `MockEncoder` — same as `twine_testing::MockEncoder`
- `MockButton` — same as `twine_testing::MockButton`

### mod twine_testing::scenes

Reference scenes for engine tests, benchmarks and examples (feature `engine`), so every

#### struct twine_testing::scenes::EngineBoxes
Nodes of the `engine_boxes` scene.
Fields:
- `screen: twine_engine::NodeId` — The screen.
- `header: twine_engine::NodeId` — The gradient header bar.
- `card: twine_engine::NodeId` — The card with shadow and radius.

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::set_props
`pub fn set_props(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine, id: twine_engine::NodeId, props: &[twine_style::StyleProp])`
Sets local `Main` properties.

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::styled_box
`pub fn styled_box(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, r: twine_core::Rect, props: &[twine_style::StyleProp]) -> twine_engine::NodeId`
Creates an `Obj` under `parent` covering the absolute rectangle `r`, with the given local properties. The position is stored as `X`/`Y` styles relative to the parent's current content area and the size as `Width`/`Height`, so the box stays in place when the layout runs. The layout is updated before (so that area is current) and after (so the box has its coordinates right away).
Panics: If `parent` does not exist or the node arena is full (see `child_box`): a test fixture fails loudly instead of building a partial scene.

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::child_box

Creates an `Obj` under `parent` at `r` relative to the parent's content area (`X`, `Y`, `Width`, `Height` styles) with the given local properties.
Panics: If the node cannot be created: `parent` does not exist, or the engine's node limit (`Limits::max_nodes`) is reached. A test fixture fails loudly instead of building a partial scene.

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::engine_boxes
`pub fn engine_boxes(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine) -> twine_testing::scenes::EngineBoxes`
The `engine_boxes` example scene on the default display's active screen, laid out for 320 × 240 (it works on any size): a gradient header, a card with shadow, radius and border holding six boxes, a 50 % opacity group, a rotated box and the "player" box.
Panics: If the engine has no default display, the display has no active screen, or a box cannot be created (see `child_box`).

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::scrollbar_style
`pub fn scrollbar_style(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine, id: twine_engine::NodeId, width: i32)`
Styles a node's `Scrollbar` part like a theme would: `width` px thick, 2 px from the edges, rounded, dark gray; blue while the node is scrolled (`State::SCROLLED`).

#### fn twine_testing::scenes::scroll_list
`pub fn scroll_list(e: &mut twine_engine::Engine, parent: twine_engine::NodeId, r: twine_core::Rect, rows: usize, row_h: i32) -> (twine_engine::NodeId, Vec<twine_engine::NodeId>)`
A scrolling list: a white container under `parent` covering the absolute rectangle `r` holding `rows` full-width rows of `row_h` pixels in alternating blue / gray, each clickable and darker while pressed, with a styled vertical scrollbar (see `scrollbar_style`). Returns the container and the rows.

### mod twine_testing::snapshot

Golden-image snapshots: `assert_rgb_snapshot`, `SnapshotConfig`, `Tolerance`, and the
committed hash manifest (`Manifest`, `Digest`).

A crate's references are its **manifest** `tests/snapshots.toml` (committed): one
`Digest` per snapshot — size and XXH64 of the decoded 8-bit RGB pixels (`xxh64`). A test
renders, hashes and compares with the manifest; no image is needed to pass. PNGs exist only
for review: `tests/snapshots/<name>.png` is a **local, git-ignored cache** of the approved
image (written by update runs and by passing runs outside CI when missing), and
`target/twine-snapshots/<crate>/` receives the images of a mismatch or a new snapshot.

| Situation | Behaviour |
|-----------|-----------|
| digest equals the `[approved]` entry | passes |
| digest equals a `[pending]` entry | passes, `PENDING SNAPSHOT <name>` on stderr (awaiting review) |
| no entry | the image goes to `target/twine-snapshots/<crate>/new/<name>.png`; fails, except in a `propose` or `update` run |
| digest differs | `<name>.actual.png` (and, with the cached reference PNG, `<name>.diff.png` plus the count and bounding box of the differing pixels) go to `target/twine-snapshots/<crate>/`; fails — unless the snapshot has a non-exact `Tolerance` and the difference from the cached reference is within it |
| digest differs, tolerant snapshot, no cached reference | not checked (`UNCHECKED SNAPSHOT`); only exact snapshots are evidence |
| `update` run | the image is recorded (and cached); `cargo xtask snapshots --update` makes it the approved entry |

Every assertion leaves a `Record` in `target/twine-snapshots/<crate>/records/`, so
`cargo xtask snapshots` can report the run (matches, pending, new, mismatches, entries no test
used) and change the manifests: `--update` approves every recorded image (the user's
decision after reviewing the diffs), `--propose` adds new images as pending entries, and
`--accept` approves the pending ones. Tests never write a manifest themselves.
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_testing::snapshot::Apply
How `apply_records` changes the manifests.
Variants:
- `Update` — `--update` (the user's approval): every recorded image becomes the approved entry.
- `Propose` — `--propose`: images without an entry become pending entries; nothing else changes.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::ApplyReport
What `apply_records` changed, per manifest.
Fields:
- `added: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>` — Entries added (`(manifest, name)`).
- `changed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>` — Entries whose digest changed.
- `written: Vec<PathBuf>` — Manifests written.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq

#### enum twine_testing::snapshot::Approval
Which block of a `Manifest` an entry is in.
Variants:
- `Approved` — Reviewed and approved by the user (`[approved]`).
- `Pending` — Generated, awaiting the user's review (`[pending]`); compared like an approved entry so it cannot drift, reported by `cargo xtask snapshots` and refused by its `--check`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::Digest
The fingerprint of one image: its size and the XXH64 (seed 0) of its 8-bit RGB pixels, row-major, three bytes per pixel — the decoded pixels, never an encoded file, so a PNG encoder change does not change a digest.
Fields:
- `width: u32` — Width in pixels.
- `height: u32` — Height in pixels.
- `hash: u64` — XXH64 of the RGB bytes.
Methods of `Digest`:
- `pub fn of_rgb(width: u32, height: u32, rgb: &[u8]) -> Self` — The digest of a `w × h` RGB image (`rgb` holds `w * h * 3` bytes; not checked here — `assert_rgb_snapshot` checks it). Never panics.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, FromStr

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::Manifest
A crate's golden-image manifest, `tests/snapshots.toml`: snapshot name → `Digest`, in two blocks, `[approved]` and `[pending]`. Committed; the reference PNGs are not (they are a local cache for diff images).
Fields:
- `approved: BTreeMap<String, twine_testing::snapshot::Digest>` — Approved entries.
- `pending: BTreeMap<String, twine_testing::snapshot::Digest>` — Entries awaiting approval.
Methods of `Manifest`:
- `pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<(twine_testing::snapshot::Digest, twine_testing::snapshot::Approval)>` — The entry `name` and its block (approved first).
- `pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self>` — Reads the manifest at `path`; a missing file is an empty manifest.
  Errors: I/O errors other than "not found", and parse errors (as `InvalidData`).
- `pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>` — Writes the manifest to `path` (creating parent directories).
  Errors: I/O errors.
- `pub fn accept_pending(&mut self) -> Vec<String>` — Moves every pending entry to the approved block; returns their names.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Display, FromStr

#### enum twine_testing::snapshot::Outcome
What one snapshot assertion found (see `Record`).
Variants:
- `Match` — Equal to its approved entry.
- `Pending` — Equal to its pending entry.
- `New` — Not in the manifest (the image is in `new/` of the artefact directory).
- `Mismatch` — Differs from its entry (the assertion failed).
- `Tolerated` — Differs from its entry but within the snapshot's tolerance (checked against the local reference PNG).
- `Unchecked` — A tolerant snapshot that differs from its entry with no local reference PNG to apply the tolerance to: not checked.
- `Updated` — Recorded by an update run.
Methods of `Outcome`:
- `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` — The outcome's word in a record file.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::ParseError
Why a `Digest` or a `Manifest` could not be read.
Fields:
- `line: usize` — 1-based line number (0 for a lone digest).
- `message: String` — What is wrong.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::Record
One snapshot assertion of a test run, written to `<target>/twine-snapshots/<crate>/records/<name>.rec` — one file per snapshot, so tests running in parallel never write the same file. `cargo xtask snapshots` reads them to report the run and, with `--update` / `--propose`, to change the manifests (`apply_records`).
Fields:
- `name: String` — Snapshot name.
- `outcome: twine_testing::snapshot::Outcome` — What the assertion found.
- `digest: twine_testing::snapshot::Digest` — The rendered image's digest.
- `manifest: PathBuf` — The manifest the snapshot belongs to.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::snapshot::apply_records
`pub fn apply_records(records: &[twine_testing::snapshot::Record], how: twine_testing::snapshot::Apply) -> Result<twine_testing::snapshot::ApplyReport>`
Applies a run's records to their manifests (see `Apply`); manifests without a change are not rewritten.
Errors: Reading or writing a manifest.

#### fn twine_testing::snapshot::read_records
`pub fn read_records(snapshots_dir: &Path, skip: &[&str]) -> Vec<twine_testing::snapshot::Record>`
Every record under `snapshots_dir` (`<target>/twine-snapshots`), skipping the artefact directories whose name starts with one of `skip` (e.g. the snapshot module's own self-tests); sorted by manifest and name. Unreadable files are skipped.

#### fn twine_testing::snapshot::xxh64
`pub fn xxh64(data: &[u8], seed: u64) -> u64`
The XXH64 hash of `data` with `seed` (the reference algorithm, little-endian reads, so the value is the same on every host).

#### enum twine_testing::snapshot::SnapshotMode
How a run treats the manifest (environment variable `TWINE_SNAPSHOTS`).
Variants:
- `Check` — Compare; a new or changed image fails (`TWINE_SNAPSHOTS` unset or `check`).
- `Propose` — Like `Check`, but a snapshot without an entry passes and is recorded for `cargo xtask snapshots --propose` (`TWINE_SNAPSHOTS=propose`).
- `Update` — Record every image for `cargo xtask snapshots --update` and refresh the local reference PNGs; nothing fails (`TWINE_SNAPSHOTS=update`).
Methods of `SnapshotMode`:
- `pub fn from_env() -> Self` — The mode named by `TWINE_SNAPSHOTS` (`check`, `propose`, `update`; anything else or unset is `Check`).
- `pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Self` — Parses a mode name (unknown names are `Check`).
- `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` — The value of `TWINE_SNAPSHOTS` selecting this mode.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_testing::snapshot::DiffSummary
Result of comparing two equally sized RGB images.
Fields:
- `count: u32` — Number of differing pixels.
- `bbox: Option<(u32, u32, u32, u32)>` — Bounding box of the differing pixels `(x0, y0, x1, y1)`, half-open.
- `image: Vec<u8>` — The diff image (25 % gray for equal pixels, magenta for differing ones).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_testing::snapshot::diff_rgb
`pub fn diff_rgb(w: u32, h: u32, expected: &[u8], actual: &[u8], max_channel_delta: u8) -> twine_testing::snapshot::DiffSummary`
Compares two `w × h` RGB images pixel by pixel.

Re-exports in `twine_testing::snapshot`:
