## crate twine_build

Documented with features: `font,image`.

**twine-build**

Build-script helpers for Twine applications: assets are compiled on the host, in `build.rs`,
into Rust sources in `OUT_DIR`, so applications commit their sources (translation files,
TrueType fonts, PNG images) and never generated code. Nothing of this crate is linked into
the firmware.

| Concept | Items |
|---------|-------|
| Compile-time translations | `i18n::Translations` (sources and options) → `i18n::Catalog` (checked; `to_rust`, `write_to_out_dir`, `chars`, `number_chars`), `i18n::Format` (Fluent, gettext `.po`, TOML), `i18n::Diagnostic` / `i18n::Error`, CLDR plural rules (`i18n::RULES`) |
| Bitmap fonts (feature `font`) | `font::Font` (TrueType/OpenType file, size, `font::Bpp`, characters, symbols, compression, kerning, subpixels, `font::Hinting`, text `font::Gamma`) → `font::GeneratedFont` (`write_to_out_dir`), `font::describe` |
| Glyph subsetting | `chars::CharSource` (typed ranges `'\u{20}'..='\u{7E}'`, strings, characters, translation catalogs with their numbers' characters), `chars::rust_literal_chars` (the string and character literals of Rust sources), `chars::ranges`, `font::implied_chars` (the Arabic presentation forms and mirrored brackets a font must add) |
| Images (feature `image`) | `image::Image` (file or RGBA pixels, `ColorFormat`, `image::Compression`, dithering, premultiplied alpha, background) → `image::GeneratedImage` (`write_to_out_dir`, `to_tbin`) |
| Errors | `AssetError` (fonts and images) |

The runtime side of the translations is `twine_extra::i18n` (feature `i18n`): the
generated `Key` and `Lang` enums implement its `MessageKey` and `Language` traits, and its
`tr!` macro shows a message in the current language. Generated fonts are
`twine::text::Font` statics and generated images `twine::image::Image` statics.

```rust
[build-dependencies]
twine-build = "0.1"
```

A build script that compiles the translations, a font holding exactly the characters they
(and the application's string literals) use, and an image:

```rust
// build.rs
use twine_build::font::{Bpp, Font};
use twine_build::i18n::Translations;
use twine_build::image::{ColorFormat, Image};

let catalog = Translations::from_dir("i18n").default_language("en").build().unwrap();
catalog.write_to_out_dir("i18n.rs").unwrap();

Font::from_ttf("assets/NotoSansSC-Regular.otf")
    .size(16)
    .bpp(Bpp::Four)
    .chars_from('\u{20}'..='\u{7E}')
    .chars_from(&catalog)
    .chars_from_rust_sources("src")
    .name("TEXT_FONT")
    .build()
    .unwrap()
    .write_to_out_dir("text_font.rs")
    .unwrap();

Image::from_file("assets/logo.png")
    .format(ColorFormat::Rgb565)
    .name("LOGO")
    .build()
    .unwrap()
    .write_to_out_dir("logo.rs")
    .unwrap();
```

and the application includes the generated statics:

```rust
include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/text_font.rs")); // pub static TEXT_FONT: twine::text::Font
include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/logo.rs"));      // pub static LOGO: twine::image::Image
```

The command-line tool `twine` (crate `twine-cli`: `twine font`, `twine image`,
`twine i18n`) is a front end of the same builders, for files that are committed (the
built-in fonts of `twine-assets`). The `include_font!` and `include_image!` macros of the
`twine` facade (feature `include-assets`) run them at compile time without a build script.

#### fn twine_build::sha256_hex
`pub fn sha256_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String`
The SHA-256 digest of `data` as 64 lowercase hex digits (recorded in generated headers).

#### struct twine_build::AssetError
A font or image could not be generated: an invalid option, an unreadable or undecodable input file, or an output that cannot be written.
Methods of `AssetError`:
- `pub fn new(message: impl Into<String>) -> twine_build::AssetError` — An error with a human-readable `message`.
- `pub fn file(path: &Path, message: impl Display) -> twine_build::AssetError` — An error about the file `path`.
- `pub fn message(&self) -> &str` — The message.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error, From<String>, From<&str>

### mod twine_build::chars

Character sets for glyph subsetting: which characters a generated font contains.

A bitmap font only needs the glyphs the application shows. `CharSource` is anything that
names characters — a typed range (`'\u{20}'..='\u{7E}'`), a character, a string, a
translation `Catalog` (every character of every message in every language, and the
characters its numbers are written with) or a list of
those — and `rust_literal_chars` collects the characters of the string and character
literals of Rust sources. A font built from the catalog and the sources carries only the
glyphs it can ever draw, so CJK or Arabic firmware does not pay for thousands of unused
glyphs.

#### trait twine_build::chars::CharSource
`pub trait CharSource`
A source of characters for a generated font (`twine_build::font::Font::chars_from`).
Items:
- `fn add_chars(&self, set: &mut BTreeSet<char>)` — Adds the characters of this source to `set`.
Implemented by: RangeInclusive<char>, char, str, String, twine_build::i18n::Catalog, BTreeSet<char>, [T], [T; N], Vec<T>, &T

#### fn twine_build::chars::ranges
`pub fn ranges(set: &BTreeSet<char>) -> Vec<RangeInclusive<char>>`
The characters of `set` as the fewest ascending inclusive ranges (consecutive code points form one range).

#### fn twine_build::chars::rust_literal_chars
`pub fn rust_literal_chars(src: &str) -> BTreeSet<char>`
The characters of the string and character literals in the Rust source `src`: what an application can show from its own code (labels, button texts, format strings).

#### fn twine_build::chars::rust_source_chars
`pub fn rust_source_chars(path: &Path) -> Result<(BTreeSet<char>, Vec<PathBuf>)>`
The characters of the string and character literals of every `.rs` file under `path` (a file or a directory, searched recursively in name order), with the files read (for `cargo:rerun-if-changed`). See `rust_literal_chars`.
Errors: When `path` or a file or directory below it cannot be read, or a `.rs` file is not UTF-8.

### mod twine_build::font

Bitmap fonts from TrueType/OpenType files (feature `font`): a deterministic generator that
writes a `static` `twine::text::Font` as Rust source.

`Font` is a builder: the source file, the pixel size, the bit depth (`Bpp`), the
characters (`chars_from` — typed ranges, strings, translation
catalogs — and the literals of the application's sources), optional Font Awesome symbols,
compression, kerning, subpixel rendering, `Hinting` and text `Gamma`. `Font::build` rasterizes the glyphs and
returns a `GeneratedFont`, whose `write_to_out_dir`
writes it for `include!` from a build script.



**How a font is generated**

The outlines are grid-fitted with the `FreeType` auto-hinter (`skrifa`; `Hinting::Full` by
default, see `Hinting`) and rasterized (`ab_glyph_rasterizer`; unhinted glyphs with
`fontdue`), trimmed to their inked box and quantized to the bit depth
(`q = (v × max + 127) / 255`). The font carries text-gamma tables (`Gamma`, default
γ = 1.2 dark-on-light / 1.8 light-on-dark) that map the stored levels to opacity when text
is drawn. Kerning comes from the font's `GPOS` pair
adjustments (or its legacy `kern` table), and bitmaps are optionally compressed with LVGL's
RLE scheme. Metrics: `line_height = ceil(ascent) + ceil(-descent)`,
`base_line = ceil(-descent)` (hhea), underline from the `post` table (fallback
`-(descent / 2)` and `max(1, size / 14)`), advances in 1/16 px. The output depends only on
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_build::font::Hinting
Grid-fitting of glyph outlines before they are rasterized (the `FreeType` auto-hinter, as implemented by the pure-Rust `skrifa` crate; the font's own TrueType instructions are not used, so every font is hinted the same way).
Variants:
- `None` — No grid-fitting: the outline as designed (the generator's output before R6.S03).
- `Light` — Vertical-only grid-fitting (as `FT_LOAD_TARGET_LIGHT`): heights snap to the pixel grid, advances and horizontal positions stay unhinted.
- `Full` — Grid-fitting in both directions (as `FT_LOAD_TARGET_NORMAL`, or `_LCD` / `_LCD_V` for subpixel fonts) with hinted, whole-pixel advances (the default).
Methods of `Hinting`:
- `const ALL: [twine_build::font::Hinting; 3]` — Every mode.
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The mode's name as the `twine font --hinting` option and the generated header write it: `none`, `light` or `full`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display, FromStr

#### fn twine_build::font::implied_chars
`pub fn implied_chars(set: &BTreeSet<char>) -> BTreeSet<char>`
The characters the text pipeline may draw for text made of `set`, besides `set` itself (and including it): the contextual presentation forms of each Arabic and Persian letter and the lam-alef ligatures (feature `arabic-shaping` of the runtime shapes text with `twine_text::shape_into`), and the mirrored partner of each bracket (feature `bidi` mirrors brackets in right-to-left runs, `twine_text::mirror`).

#### const twine_build::font::SYMBOL_ALIASES
`pub const SYMBOL_ALIASES: &[(char, char)]`
Symbols that Font Awesome Free 5 does not contain, drawn from another glyph turned 90° clockwise: `NEW_LINE` (U+F8A2, a custom glyph in LVGL's merged font) uses "level-down-alt" (U+F3BE), which turned clockwise is a "↵" return arrow.

#### const twine_build::font::DEFAULT_SIZE
`pub const DEFAULT_SIZE: u16 = 14`
The default pixel size of `Font`: 14 px, the size of Twine's default font.

#### struct twine_build::font::Gamma
The text gamma of a generated font: the strength `γ` of its coverage → opacity curve for dark-on-light and for light-on-dark text, in hundredths (`120` = 1.2). The font stores one 16-entry table per curve, `round(255 · (v / max)^(1 / γ))` (identity at both ends, monotonic); the text renderer picks one per text run from the text and background colors (`twine::text::gamma`), so it costs nothing per pixel.
Methods of `Gamma`:
- `const LINEAR: twine_build::font::Gamma` — No gamma: LVGL's linear mapping (4 bpp `v × 17`) for both polarities.
- `const DEFAULT: twine_build::font::Gamma` — The default: γ = 1.2 for dark-on-light text (sRGB blending already makes it heavy) and 1.8 for light-on-dark text (thin without it). Values settled with the prototype comparison and the regenerated golden images (R6.S03).
- `const MIN: u16` — The smallest strength `Font::build` accepts (0.5).
- `const MAX: u16` — The largest strength `Font::build` accepts (4.0).
- `pub const fn new(dark_on_light: u16, light_on_dark: u16) -> twine_build::font::Gamma` — Curves of strength `dark_on_light / 100` and `light_on_dark / 100` (checked against `MIN`..=`MAX` by `Font::build`).
- `pub const fn dark_on_light(self) -> u16` — The dark-on-light strength in hundredths.
- `pub const fn light_on_dark(self) -> u16` — The light-on-dark strength in hundredths.
- `pub fn table(centi: u16) -> [u8; 16]` — The 16-entry table of strength `centi / 100`: `round(255 · (v / 15)^(100 / centi))`.
- `pub fn tables(self) -> twine_text::TextGamma` — The runtime tables of these curves.
- `pub fn arg(self) -> String` — The `twine font --gamma` form: `linear`, `default`, or `<dark-on-light>,<light-on-dark>` with two decimals (`1.30,2.00`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, FromStr

#### struct twine_build::font::Font
A bitmap font to generate: a builder over the source font file and the options. See the module docs.
Methods of `Font`:
- `pub fn from_ttf(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::font::Font` — A font generated from the TrueType or OpenType file `path` (`.ttf`, `.otf`), with the defaults: `DEFAULT_SIZE` px, `Bpp::Four`, no characters yet, plain bitmaps, kerning on, no subpixels, `Hinting::Full`, `Gamma::DEFAULT`, `pub`, the static named after the file and size (`Montserrat-Medium.ttf` at 16 px → `MONTSERRAT_MEDIUM_16`), paths through the `twine` facade (`twine::text`).
- `pub fn root(self, dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The directory relative paths are read from (default: the current directory).
- `pub fn size(self, px: u16) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The pixel size (em height), 1 to 255 px (checked by `build`).
- `pub fn bpp(self, bpp: twine_text::Bpp) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The bit depth of the coverage values (default `Bpp::Four`): more levels look smoother and cost more flash (a 4 bpp font is about twice the size of a 2 bpp one).
- `pub fn chars_from(self, source: impl twine_build::chars::CharSource) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Adds characters: typed ranges (`'\u{20}'..='\u{7E}'`), characters, strings, a translation `Catalog` (every character of every message, and the digits and signs of each language's numbers) or lists of those (`CharSource`). Call it as often as needed; the font holds the union. `build` adds the forms shaping and mirroring draw for them (`implied_chars`).
- `pub fn chars_from_file(self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Adds the characters of a UTF-8 text file (whitespace ignored), e.g. a list of common CJK characters. Read by `build`.
- `pub fn chars_from_rust_sources(self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Adds the characters of the string and character literals of the Rust sources under `path` (a `.rs` file or a directory, searched recursively) — what the application can show from its own code. See `rust_literal_chars`. Read by `build`.
- `pub fn symbol_fonts<P: Into<PathBuf>>(self, paths: impl IntoIterator<Item = P>) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Merges the glyphs of every Font Awesome `twine::text::Symbol` (`Symbol::is_font_awesome`) from these symbol fonts, searched in order (e.g. Font Awesome Free 5's `fa-solid-900.ttf`, then `fa-brands-400.ttf` for the USB and Bluetooth icons). Symbols are centered vertically on the font's line box. An empty list merges nothing.
- `pub fn format(self, format: twine_text::BitmapFormat) -> twine_build::font::Font` — How bitmaps are stored (default `BitmapFormat::Plain`): plain bitmaps draw fastest, compressed ones (LVGL RLE, with or without the XOR row prefilter) take less flash and are decoded into the glyph cache.
- `pub fn kerning(self, kerning: bool) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Whether to store pair kerning (default `true`).
- `pub fn subpx(self, subpx: twine_text::Subpx) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Subpixel rendering (default `Subpx::None`): horizontal or vertical RGB subpixel glyphs, for displays whose subpixel order is known.
- `pub fn hinting(self, hinting: twine_build::font::Hinting) -> twine_build::font::Font` — Grid-fitting of the outlines (default `Hinting::Full`: crisp stems, whole-pixel advances); `Hinting::None` keeps the outlines and advances as designed. Host-only: the firmware is the same size either way.
- `pub fn gamma(self, gamma: twine_build::font::Gamma) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The text-gamma curves stored with the font (default `Gamma::DEFAULT`; `Gamma::LINEAR` for LVGL's linear coverage mapping). Checked by `build`: each strength within 0.5..=4.0.
- `pub fn name(self, name: &str) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The name of the generated static (a Rust identifier, checked by `build`); its data statics are named after it (`<NAME>_BITMAP`, `<NAME>_GLYPHS`, …).
- `pub fn visibility(self, visibility: &str) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The visibility of the generated static (default `pub`; `""` for private, `pub(crate)`, …).
- `pub fn crate_path(self, path: &str) -> twine_build::font::Font` — The path through which the generated code names the text crate (default `twine::text`, for applications using the `twine` facade; `twine_text` for code that depends on `twine-text` directly).
- `pub fn chars(&self) -> &BTreeSet<char>` — The characters added with `chars_from` so far (files and Rust sources are read by `build`).
- `pub fn static_name(&self) -> String` — The name of the generated static: `name`, or the file stem and size.
- `pub fn command_line(&self) -> String` — The `twine font` command line that generates the same font (recorded in the generated header; characters are written as code-point ranges, and `--crate-path` when it is not the command's default `twine_text`).
- `pub fn build(&self) -> Result<twine_build::font::GeneratedFont, twine_build::AssetError>` — Rasterizes the glyphs and generates the font.
  Errors: An invalid option (a size outside 1..=255, a name that is not a Rust identifier, an invalid crate path or visibility, a gamma strength outside 0.5..=4.0, no characters, more than 65 534 glyphs, a glyph too large for the bitmap format), an unreadable or unparsable input file, or a font the auto-hinter cannot hint.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_build::font::GeneratedFont
A generated font: the in-memory description and its Rust source.
Fields:
- `data: twine_text::encode::FontData` — The font data (a live font for tests: `FontData::leak`).
- `code_points: Vec<char>` — Code point of every glyph id (index 0 = reserved, `'\0'`).
- `source: String` — The Rust source: the data statics and `<visibility> static <NAME>: <crate>::Font`.
- `flash_bytes: usize` — Bytes of static data (bitmaps, descriptors, cmaps, kerning, the font structs).
- `warnings: Vec<String>` — Non-fatal problems: characters missing from the font, clamped kerning values.
- `inputs: Vec<PathBuf>` — Every file read (the font, symbol fonts, character files, Rust sources).
Methods of `GeneratedFont`:
- `pub fn write(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<(), twine_build::AssetError>` — Writes the Rust source to `path` (only when it changed, so dependents are not rebuilt needlessly; the parent directory is created).
  Errors: When the file cannot be written.
- `pub fn write_to_out_dir(&self, file_name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, twine_build::AssetError>` — The build-script convenience: writes the source to `$OUT_DIR/<file_name>`, prints `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for every input and `cargo:warning` for every warning, and returns the path written. Include it with `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/<file_name>"))`.
  Errors: When `OUT_DIR` is not set (not in a build script) or the file cannot be written.
Implements: Clone, Debug

#### fn twine_build::font::build_cmaps
`pub fn build_cmaps(cps: &[char]) -> Vec<twine_text::encode::CmapData>`
Cmaps for glyphs sorted by code point with ids `1..`: runs of ≥ 3 consecutive code points become `Format0Tiny`; the code points between runs are grouped into `SparseTiny` cmaps (a group never spans a run, so its glyph ids stay consecutive, and never exceeds 65 535 code points).

#### fn twine_build::font::describe
`pub fn describe(ttf: &Path, size: u16, hinting: twine_build::font::Hinting, chars: &str) -> Result<String, twine_build::AssetError>`
Glyph metrics of `chars` in the font file `ttf` at `size` px with `hinting`, with each glyph's coverage as ASCII art (`twine font --dump`, a debugging aid): line metrics, unhinted advances, the generated advance and inked box, glyph indices and the kerning to the previous character.
Errors: When the font file cannot be read or parsed, or the auto-hinter fails.

Re-exports in `twine_build::font`:
- `BitmapFormat` = `twine_text::BitmapFormat`
- `Bpp` = `twine_text::Bpp`
- `Subpx` = `twine_text::Subpx`

### mod twine_build::i18n

Compile-time translations: read translation files (Fluent `.ftl`, gettext `.po` or TOML),
check them, and generate the Rust catalog that `twine_extra::i18n` uses at run time — a
`Key` enum (one variant per message), a `Lang` enum (one variant per language) and static
message tables.


In a build script, read a directory with one file per language (`i18n/en.ftl`,
`i18n/de.po`, `i18n/zh.toml`, … — the file stem is the language code) and write the catalog
into `OUT_DIR`:


and include it in the application (in a module of its own):


`twine i18n <dir> -o <file.rs>` (the `twine-cli` tool) does the same from the command
line.

**What is checked**

Errors (the build fails, each with file and line where known): syntax errors and
unsupported constructs; a key or language whose Rust name collides with another; a key
defined twice; a message using an argument the default language's message does not have;
positional arguments that are not `0..n`; more than `MAX_ARGS` arguments; a plural message
without an argument to choose on; a language without a known plural rule (choose one with
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_build::i18n::NUMBERS
`pub const NUMBERS: &[(&str, twine_build::i18n::NumberSymbols)]`
Languages (lower-case tags, `_` read as `-`; full tag first, then the base language) and their symbols.

#### struct twine_build::i18n::NumberSymbols
How one language writes numbers (the generator's copy of the runtime's `NumberFormat`).
Fields:
- `decimal: &'static str` — Decimal separator.
- `group: &'static str` — Grouping separator.
- `primary_group: u8` — Digits of the group next to the decimal separator (0: no grouping).
- `secondary_group: u8` — Digits of the further groups (2 for Indian grouping).
- `min_grouping: u8` — Grouping starts at `primary_group + min_grouping` integer digits.
- `minus: &'static str` — Minus sign (with bidi marks where CLDR has them).
- `percent_prefix: &'static str` — Text before a percentage.
- `percent_suffix: &'static str` — Text after a percentage.
- `zero: char` — Digit zero of the default numbering system.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_build::i18n::ROOT_NUMBERS
`pub const ROOT_NUMBERS: twine_build::i18n::NumberSymbols`
CLDR's root locale (`1,234.5`, `-1`, `12%`, ASCII digits).

#### fn twine_build::i18n::numbers_for
`pub fn numbers_for(code: &str) -> Option<twine_build::i18n::NumberSymbols>`
The symbols of language `code`: the full tag (lower case, `_` read as `-`), then its base language; `None` when neither is known.

#### enum twine_build::i18n::Category
A CLDR plural category (`zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many`, `other`), in CLDR order.
Variants:
- `Zero` — `zero`.
- `One` — `one`.
- `Two` — `two`.
- `Few` — `few`.
- `Many` — `many`.
- `Other` — `other` (every language has it; the catch-all).
Methods of `Category`:
- `const ALL: [twine_build::i18n::Category; 6]` — Every category, in CLDR order.
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The CLDR name (`"one"`, …).
- `pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<twine_build::i18n::Category>` — The category named `name` (`"one"` → `Category::One`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_build::i18n::PluralRules
The plural rule of a group of languages: the runtime function that implements it and the categories it selects.
Fields:
- `name: &'static str` — Name of the runtime rule, `twine_extra::i18n::plural::<name>` (named after a language that uses it). Also what `Translations::plural_rules` takes to choose the rule of a language explicitly.
- `all: &'static [twine_build::i18n::Category]` — Every category the rule selects for some number (integers and decimals), in CLDR order.
- `integer: &'static [twine_build::i18n::Category]` — The categories it selects for integers, in CLDR order (what a gettext `.po` file with integer-only plural forms lists).
- `languages: &'static [&'static str]` — The base language codes (lower case, without region or script) that use the rule.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### const twine_build::i18n::RULES
`pub const RULES: &[twine_build::i18n::PluralRules]`
The rules the generator knows (CLDR 44 cardinal rules, compact-exponent operand `e` = 0). Each one matches a function of `twine_extra::i18n::plural`; a test there checks that the categories listed here are exactly the ones the function selects.

#### fn twine_build::i18n::rules_for
`pub fn rules_for(code: &str) -> Option<&'static twine_build::i18n::PluralRules>`
The rule of language `code` (a BCP 47 tag such as `"pt-PT"` or `"zh_Hant"`): the full tag first (lower case, `_` read as `-`), then its base language.

#### fn twine_build::i18n::rules_named
`pub fn rules_named(name: &str) -> Option<&'static twine_build::i18n::PluralRules>`
The rule named `name` (see `PluralRules::name`).

#### const twine_build::i18n::MAX_ARGS
`pub const MAX_ARGS: usize = 8`
The most arguments a message may have (the runtime's `twine_extra::i18n::MAX_ARGS`).

#### enum twine_build::i18n::Format
The source format of a translation file.
Variants:
- `Fluent` — Fluent (`.ftl`): the subset that compiles to static tables (see the module docs of `Translations`); one select expression per message for plurals.
- `Po` — gettext (`.po`), ID-based: `msgid` is the key, `msgstr` the text with `{name}` placeholders; plural entries list the language's CLDR categories in order.
- `Toml` — TOML (`.toml`): `key = "text"`, tables group keys, a table with `other` is a plural message.
Methods of `Format`:
- `pub fn from_extension(ext: &str) -> Option<twine_build::i18n::Format>` — The format of a file extension (`"ftl"`, `"po"`, `"toml"`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_build::i18n::Dir
A base text direction.
Variants:
- `Ltr` — Left to right.
- `Rtl` — Right to left.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_build::i18n::Diagnostic
One problem found while reading or checking translations.
Fields:
- `file: String` — The file (or inline source name) it is about; empty for the configuration.
- `line: usize` — The 1-based line, or 0 when unknown.
- `message: String` — What is wrong.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display

#### struct twine_build::i18n::Error
The translations could not be built: every problem found.
Fields:
- `diagnostics: Vec<twine_build::i18n::Diagnostic>` — The problems, in the order found.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error

#### struct twine_build::i18n::Translations
The translation sources and options: a builder whose `build` reads, checks and compiles them into a `Catalog`. See the module docs.
Methods of `Translations`:
- `pub fn new() -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — No sources yet; the generated code uses the runtime at `::twine_extra::i18n`.
- `pub fn from_dir(dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — The translation files of directory `dir`: every `<code>.ftl`, `<code>.po` and `<code>.toml` (other files are ignored; one file per language).
- `pub fn dir(self, dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Adds the translation files of directory `dir` (see `from_dir`).
- `pub fn file(self, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Adds one translation file; its stem is the language code (`i18n/de.po` → `de`), its extension the `Format`.
- `pub fn source(self, lang: &str, format: twine_build::i18n::Format, text: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Adds the translations of language `lang` from text (tests, generated sources).
- `pub fn default_language(self, code: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — The default language: it must define every key, every other language falls back to it, and it is `Lang::DEFAULT`. Without this option: the first of `languages`, or the only language.
- `pub fn languages<S: Into<String>>(self, codes: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — The languages to compile, in `Lang` order (others are skipped). Without this option: every language found, the default first, then by code.
- `pub fn font(self, code: &str, path: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — The font of language `code`: `path` is a Rust path to a `&'static`-able `twine_text::Font` (`"crate::fonts::CJK"`, typically a font whose fallback chain covers the language's script), returned by `Lang::font` and `I18n::font`.
- `pub fn base_dir(self, code: &str, dir: twine_build::i18n::Dir) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Overrides the base direction of language `code` (see the module docs for the default).
- `pub fn plural_rules(self, code: &str, rules: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Chooses the plural rule of language `code` by `PluralRules::name` (for languages the generator does not know, or to override).
- `pub fn number_symbols(self, code: &str, symbols: twine_build::i18n::NumberSymbols) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Sets how language `code` writes numbers (for languages the generator does not know, or to override `NUMBERS`).
- `pub fn fallback(self, code: &str, fallback: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Language `code` takes its missing texts from `fallback` first (then from the default language). Without this option a regional language (`de-AT`) falls back to its base language (`de`) when that is compiled too.
- `pub fn strict(self, strict: bool) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — Turns warnings (missing translations, unknown keys, never-chosen plural variants, fuzzy entries) into errors.
- `pub fn runtime_path(self, path: &str) -> twine_build::i18n::Translations` — The Rust path of the runtime module the generated code uses (default `::twine_extra::i18n`).
- `pub fn build(&self) -> Result<twine_build::i18n::Catalog, twine_build::i18n::Error>` — Reads, checks and compiles the translations.
  Errors: Every problem found (see the module docs), with file and line where known.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default

#### struct twine_build::i18n::Catalog
Checked, compiled translations: every key in every language (fallbacks applied), ready to be written as Rust (`to_rust`, `write_to_out_dir`).
Methods of `Catalog`:
- `pub fn languages(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str>` — The language codes, in `Lang` order (the default first unless `Translations::languages` says otherwise).
- `pub fn keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str>` — The key identifiers, in `Key` order (sorted).
- `pub fn warnings(&self) -> &[twine_build::i18n::Diagnostic]` — The warnings (see the module docs); empty with `Translations::strict`.
- `pub fn inputs(&self) -> &[PathBuf]` — The files and directories that were read.
- `pub fn chars(&self) -> BTreeSet<char>` — Every character of every text in every language (arguments excluded): the glyphs the application's fonts need for its translations.
- `pub fn number_chars(&self) -> BTreeSet<char>` — The characters every language writes numbers with: its ten digits (Arabic-Indic in Arabic, Extended Arabic-Indic in Persian, …), decimal and grouping separators, minus sign and percent affixes (`NumberSymbols`) — the glyphs numeric `tr!` arguments and `I18n::number` draw. Formatting marks (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F) are left out: they have no glyph.
- `pub fn preview(&self, lang: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String>` — A readable form of the message `key` in language `lang` (`None` when either is unknown): the text with `{argument}` placeholders, a plural message as `{count -> [one] … | *[other] …}`.
- `pub fn to_rust(&self) -> String` — The generated Rust source (see the crate docs of `twine_extra::i18n` for what it contains).
- `pub fn write(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<()>` — Writes the generated Rust source to `path` (only when it changed, so dependents are not rebuilt needlessly).
  Errors: When the file cannot be written.
- `pub fn write_to_out_dir(&self, file_name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, twine_build::i18n::Error>` — The build-script convenience: writes the catalog to `$OUT_DIR/<file_name>`, prints `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for every input and `cargo:warning` for every warning, and returns the path written.
  Errors: When `OUT_DIR` is not set (not in a build script) or the file cannot be written.
Implements: CharSource, Clone, Debug

### mod twine_build::image

Images from PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF or QOI files (feature `image`): a deterministic converter
that writes a `static` `twine::image::Image` in any `ColorFormat` as Rust source plus a
sidecar file holding the pixel data, optionally RLE- or LZ4-compressed.



Conversion: `A1`…`A8` keep the alpha channel, `L8` the luminance, `I1`…`I8` get a
deterministic median-cut palette (Floyd–Steinberg with `dither`),
`Rgb565*` are rounded or ordered-dithered; `premultiply` premultiplies
`Argb8888` and `Rgb565A8`; `background` composites over an opaque
color first. The output depends only on the inputs (no timestamps), so regenerated files
diff cleanly; the first lines of the source record the equivalent `twine image` command,
the input's SHA-256 and a machine-readable summary (`twine image --info` prints it).

#### struct twine_build::image::Converted
Converted pixel data.
Fields:
- `header: twine_image::ImageHeader` — Header (packed stride).
- `data: Vec<u8>` — Uncompressed data.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_build::image::convert
`pub fn convert(rgba: &[u8], w: u16, h: u16, format: twine_core::ColorFormat, dither: bool, premultiply: bool) -> Result<twine_build::image::Converted, String>`
Converts `w × h` straight-alpha RGBA pixels to `format`.
Errors: If `premultiply` is requested for a format without both color and alpha.

#### fn twine_build::image::flatten
`pub fn flatten(rgba: &[u8], bg: twine_core::Color) -> Vec<u8>`
Composites straight-alpha RGBA pixels over the opaque color `bg`: every channel becomes `(c·a + bg·(255 − a) + 127) / 255` (rounded to nearest) and every alpha 255, so a format without alpha shows `bg` where the source is transparent instead of the color stored there (usually black).

#### fn twine_build::image::luminance
`pub fn luminance(p: twine_build::image::Rgba) -> u8`
Luminance `(r·77 + g·150 + b·29) >> 8`.

#### type twine_build::image::Rgba
`pub type Rgba = [u8; 4]`
An RGBA color.

#### fn twine_build::image::map_to_palette
`pub fn map_to_palette(pixels: &[twine_build::image::Rgba], w: usize, palette: &[twine_build::image::Rgba], dither: bool) -> Vec<u8>`
Maps every pixel to its nearest palette index, optionally with Floyd–Steinberg dithering (errors of all four channels are diffused).

#### fn twine_build::image::median_cut
`pub fn median_cut(pixels: &[twine_build::image::Rgba], n: usize) -> Vec<twine_build::image::Rgba>`
A palette of at most `n` colors for `pixels` (median cut). When the image has at most `n` distinct colors the palette holds exactly those. The palette is sorted and padded with transparent black to `n` entries; the result does not depend on pixel order.

#### enum twine_build::image::Compression
How the pixel data is stored.
Variants:
- `None` — Uncompressed: drawn straight from flash.
- `Rle` — LVGL run-length encoding (decoded into the image cache when drawn).
- `Lz4` — An LZ4 block (needs `twine-image` feature `img-lz4` at run time).
Methods of `Compression`:
- `pub fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The command-line spelling (`none`, `rle`, `lz4`).
- `pub fn compress(self, data: &[u8], format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> Vec<u8>` — Compresses `data` of `format` with this method.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### const twine_build::image::FORMAT_NAMES
`pub const FORMAT_NAMES: [(&str, twine_core::ColorFormat); 16]`
Command-line names of the formats, in `ColorFormat::ALL` order.

#### fn twine_build::image::format_name
`pub fn format_name(f: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> &'static str`
The command-line name of `f` (`rgb565`, `argb8888-premultiplied`, …; see `FORMAT_NAMES`).

#### fn twine_build::image::color_name
`pub fn color_name(c: twine_core::Color) -> String`
The command-line spelling of `c` (`#RRGGBB`, upper case).

#### struct twine_build::image::Image
An image to convert: a builder over the source image and the options. See the module docs.
Methods of `Image`:
- `pub fn from_file(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::image::Image` — An image converted from the file `path` (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF — first frame — or QOI, recognised by content), with the defaults: `ColorFormat::Argb8888`, uncompressed, no dithering, straight alpha kept, `pub`, the static named after the file stem (`logo.png` → `LOGO`), paths through the `twine` facade (`twine::image`).
- `pub fn from_rgba(w: u32, h: u32, pixels: Vec<u8>) -> twine_build::image::Image` — An image converted from `w × h` straight-alpha RGBA pixels (`4 × w × h` bytes, row by row), e.g. drawn by the build script. Named `IMAGE` unless `name`d.
- `pub fn root(self, dir: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> twine_build::image::Image` — The directory a relative input path is read from (default: the current directory).
- `pub fn format(self, format: twine_core::ColorFormat) -> twine_build::image::Image` — The color format of the pixel data (default `ColorFormat::Argb8888`).
- `pub fn compress(self, compression: twine_build::image::Compression) -> twine_build::image::Image` — How the pixel data is stored (default `Compression::None`).
- `pub fn dither(self, dither: bool) -> twine_build::image::Image` — Floyd–Steinberg dithering (indexed formats) or 4 × 4 ordered dithering (RGB565 formats); default off.
- `pub fn premultiply(self, premultiply: bool) -> twine_build::image::Image` — Premultiplies the colors by alpha (`Argb8888`, `Rgb565A8`; sets `ImageFlags::PREMULTIPLIED`); default off.
- `pub fn background(self, bg: twine_core::Color) -> twine_build::image::Image` — Composites the image over the opaque color `bg` before converting: the result is opaque in every format, and formats without alpha show `bg` instead of black where the source is transparent. Not allowed with the alpha-only formats `A1`…`A8` (checked by `build`). Default: alpha kept as is.
- `pub fn name(self, name: &str) -> twine_build::image::Image` — The name of the generated static (a Rust identifier, checked by `build`).
- `pub fn visibility(self, visibility: &str) -> twine_build::image::Image` — The visibility of the generated static (default `pub`; `""` for private, `pub(crate)`, …).
- `pub fn crate_path(self, path: &str) -> twine_build::image::Image` — The path through which the generated code names the image crate (default `twine::image`, for applications using the `twine` facade; `twine_image` for code that depends on `twine-image` directly).
- `pub fn static_name(&self) -> String` — The name of the generated static: `name`, or the file stem.
- `pub fn build(&self) -> Result<twine_build::image::GeneratedImage, twine_build::AssetError>` — Reads (for a file input) and converts the image.
  Errors: An unreadable or undecodable input file, an image wider or taller than 65 535 pixels, an RGBA buffer of the wrong size, premultiplied alpha for a format without both color and alpha, a background for an alpha-only format, a name that is not a Rust identifier, or an invalid crate path or visibility.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### struct twine_build::image::GeneratedImage
A converted image: its header and pixel data, rendered as Rust source by `to_rust` and written with `write` or `write_to_out_dir`.
Fields:
- `header: twine_image::ImageHeader` — Header of the pixel data (`COMPRESSED` set when compressed).
- `data: Vec<u8>` — Uncompressed pixel data.
- `stored: Vec<u8>` — The stored pixel data (the sidecar file's bytes: compressed or not).
- `compression: twine_build::image::Compression` — The compression of `stored`.
Methods of `GeneratedImage`:
- `pub fn sidecar_name(out: &Path) -> String` — The file name of the sidecar holding the pixel data of a source written to `out` (`<out stem>.bin`).
- `pub fn to_rust(&self, out: &Path) -> String` — The Rust source of the image written to `out` (recorded in the header as given): the static includes its pixel data from the sidecar `sidecar_name` next to it.
- `pub fn to_rust_inline(&self) -> String` — The Rust source with the pixel data inline (a byte-string literal) instead of a sidecar file: one self-contained item, as the `include_image!` macro expands to.
- `pub fn summary(&self) -> String` — The machine-readable summary line of the source (`// twine-image: format=… w=… …`).
- `pub fn to_tbin(&self) -> Vec<u8>` — The raw twine binary file (`.tbin`: 12-byte header and the stored pixel data), loaded at run time as `ImageSource::File` (`twine image --bin`).
- `pub fn write(&self, out: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<(), twine_build::AssetError>` — Writes the source to `out` and the pixel data to the sidecar next to it (each only when it changed; the parent directory is created).
  Errors: When a file cannot be written.
- `pub fn write_to_out_dir(&self, file_name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, twine_build::AssetError>` — The build-script convenience: writes the source to `$OUT_DIR/<file_name>` and the sidecar next to it, prints `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for the input file, and returns the path of the source. Include it with `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/<file_name>"))`.
  Errors: When `OUT_DIR` is not set (not in a build script) or a file cannot be written.
- `pub fn inputs(&self) -> &[PathBuf]` — Every file read (the input image, for a file input).
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

Re-exports in `twine_build::image`:
- `Color` = `twine_core::Color`
- `ColorFormat` = `twine_core::ColorFormat`

## crate twine_macros

Documented with features: `assets`.

**twine-macros**

The procedural macros of Twine. Use them through `twine-view` or the `twine` facade
(`use twine::prelude::*;` brings `component` into scope); this crate only runs on the host
while compiling and never reaches firmware — what firmware links is the code the macros
generate.

| Macro | Role |
|-------|------|
| `#[component]` | a component function becomes a view with a props builder: `gauge(rpm).max(8000).redline(6500).padding(4)` |
| `include_font!` (feature `assets`) | a bitmap font generated from a TrueType/OpenType file while the crate compiles: `include_font!(pub static BODY = "assets/Inter.ttf", size = 16, bpp = 4, chars = '\u{20}'..='\u{7E}')` |
| `include_image!` (feature `assets`) | an image converted from a PNG/JPEG/BMP/GIF/QOI file while the crate compiles: `include_image!(pub static LOGO = "assets/logo.png", format = Rgb565)` |

Projects that avoid procedural macros write the same component as a plain function (see
`component` § Without the macro); nothing in Twine requires this crate.

#### macro twine_macros::include_font
`include_font!(…)`
Generates a bitmap font from a TrueType or OpenType file **while the crate compiles** and expands to the `static` `twine::text::Font` (feature `assets`; through the facade, `twine::include_font!` with its feature `include-assets`).
Errors: A compile error for an unknown option or value, an unreadable font file, a character set with no glyph, or anything else `twine_build::font::Font::build` refuses.

#### macro twine_macros::include_image
`include_image!(…)`
Converts an image file (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, QOI) **while the crate compiles** and expands to the `static` `twine::image::Image`, pixel data included (feature `assets`; through the facade, `twine::include_image!` with its feature `include-assets`).
Errors: A compile error for an unknown option or value, an unreadable or undecodable file, or anything else `twine_build::image::Image::build` refuses.

#### macro twine_macros::component
`#[component]`
Turns a function describing a piece of UI into a **component**: a view with a props builder, used exactly like the built-in widgets.
Errors: Unsupported signatures are rejected with a message at the offending part (see Rules), as are unknown `#[component(..)]` or `#[prop(..)]` arguments. A wrong value for a prop is reported by the conversion traits (`` `&str` cannot be used as a property of type `i32` ``).

## crate twine_core

Documented with features: `std`.

**twine-core**

Foundations of the Twine GUI library: integer geometry, fixed-point math and trigonometry,
transforms, colors and pixel formats, opacity, time, generational arenas, a small inline
vector, the dirty-rectangle set, errors, a deterministic RNG and the logging macros.

`twine-core` is the lowest layer: every other Twine crate
builds on it and it depends on no other Twine crate. It is `no_std` + `alloc`, contains no
`unsafe` and no floating-point arithmetic, so results are bit-identical on every target (P5,
P6).

| Module | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `geometry` | `Point`, `Size`, `Rect` (half-open), `Insets`, `Rotation` |
| `math` | `Fx` (16.16), `Angle` (0.1°), `Scale` (256 = 1.0), `Fraction` (255 = 1.0), `AngularSpeed` (°/s), sqrt, sin/cos/atan2, bezier, `udiv255`, `map`, shared 128-bit division (`math::div_rem_i128`) |
| `transform` | `Transform` (2-D affine, fixed point) |
| `color` | `Color`, `Opa`, `ColorFormat`, `PixelFormat` and format marker types, the WCAG `ContrastRatio` |
| `time` | `Instant`, `Duration` (µs) |
| `arena` | `Arena<T>`, generational `Id<T>`, its `Generation` (16-bit; 48-bit in the safety profile, `arena::MAX_GENERATION`, `arena::next_generation`) and packed form `RawId` |
| `small_vec` | `SmallVec` (inline-first vector) |
| `symbol` | `Symbol` (built-in icon glyphs, LVGL `LV_SYMBOL_*`) |
| `rect_set` | `RectSet` (dirty areas, LVGL join policy) |
| `mod@error` | `Error` |
| `fault` | `FaultKind`, `Faults`, `FaultCounts`, `CapacityFault`: failures Twine recovered from, reported to the application |
| `limits` | `Limits`: the memory bounds of an application (enforced as `Capacity` faults, optionally preallocated) |
| `partition` | `Partition`: the identity of a partitioned runtime (one reactive runtime and its UIs; feature `partitions`) |
| `alloc_guard` | sealing per partition: allocation after start-up detected at Twine's growth points (`AllocSite`) |
| `audit` | `Audit`, `AuditSink`, `KeyValues`: machine-readable configuration evidence |
| `crc` | `Crc32`: the CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) checksum of display-integrity checks and digests |
| `validity` | `Validity`, `ValidityStatus`: a value and how far it can be trusted (valid, stale, failed, no data) |
| `rng` | `XorShift32` (deterministic, non-cryptographic) |
| `log` | `trace!`, `debug!`, `info!`, `warn!`, `error!` (log / defmt / none backends) |
| `prelude` | the most used types |

**Units and conventions**

- Pixels are `i32`; `Rect` is **half-open** `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` (LVGL areas are
  inclusive — ported algorithms convert explicitly).
- Opacity is `Opa` (`u8`, 255 = cover); angles are `Angle` in 0.1°, clockwise on screen;
  scale factors are `Scale` (`u16`, 256 = 1.0); fractions of a whole (gradient stops,
  brightness) are `Fraction` (`u8`, 255 = 1.0); angular speeds are `AngularSpeed`
  (`u16`, whole degrees per second); time is `Instant`/`Duration` in µs (`u64`).
- Arithmetic saturates rather than overflowing; invalid arguments log `warn!` and fall back
  to a documented value instead of panicking (P7).

**Features**

- `log` / `defmt`: logging backend (see `log`); `defmt` also derives `defmt::Format` for
  every public type.
- `std`: std-only conveniences.
- `safety`: the safety profile (enabled by the `twine` facade's `safety` feature; see
  `SAFETY_PROFILE` and `docs/safety/profile.md`). Among other things it widens arena
  generations to 48 bits (`Generation`), so no arena slot retires in practice.
- `partitions`: `Partition::COUNT` = 2 partitioned runtimes instead of 1 (ADR-001,
  `docs/design/adr-001-partitioned-runtimes.md`); per-partition seal domains in
  `alloc_guard`. Not implied by `safety`. Without it `Partition` is zero-sized.

```rust
use twine_core::prelude::*;

let area = Rect::from_xywh(10, 10, 100, 50);
let c = Color::mix(Color::RED, Color::BLUE, Opa::P50);
let t = Transform::rotate(Angle::deg(90));
assert_eq!(t.map_point(Point::new(1, 0)), Point::new(0, 1));
assert_eq!(area.size(), Size::new(100, 50));
assert_eq!(c, Color::new(127, 0, 128));
```

#### struct twine_core::Arena<T>
Storage for up to 65 535 live values, addressed by generational `Id`s.
Methods of `Arena`:
- `const MAX_LEN: usize` — Maximum number of live values and of slots. Slot indices are `0..MAX_LEN`, so index `u16::MAX` is never used (see `Id::INVALID`).
- `const ROTATE_PERIOD: u16` — A slot is parked in the FIFO reserve each time its generation reaches a multiple of this (a power of two), so it serves at most this many values in a row (see reuse order).
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — An empty arena (no allocation) of `Partition::MAIN`.
- `pub const fn new_in(p: twine_core::Partition) -> Self` — An empty arena (no allocation) whose growth after a seal is noted in partition `p`'s seal domain (`alloc_guard`): what an owner in partition `p` (a partition's reactive runtime, an engine's tree) uses.
- `pub fn with_capacity(n: u16) -> Self` — An empty arena of `Partition::MAIN` with room for `n` values.
- `pub const fn partition(&self) -> twine_core::Partition` — The partition the arena's growth is noted in (see `new_in`).
- `pub fn set_partition(&mut self, p: twine_core::Partition)` — Moves the arena to partition `p`'s seal domain: its later growth is noted there (the owner calls it when it learns its partition, e.g. `Engine::set_partition`). Never panics.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, v: T) -> Result<twine_core::Id<T>, twine_core::Error>` — Stores `v`, returning its handle; `Error::CapacityExceeded` when 65 535 values are live (or every slot is retired).
  Errors: `Error::CapacityExceeded` when 65 535 values are live or every slot is retired.
- `pub fn reserve(&mut self, n: u16)` — Reserves storage for `n` slots in total — the slot vector and both free lists — so that inserting and removing values never allocates while at most `n` slots are in use (no retirement). Used to preallocate an arena from a `Limits` bound. Does nothing for parts already that large; `n` is capped at `MAX_LEN`. Allocates (once); never panics.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, id: twine_core::Id<T>) -> Option<T>` — Removes and returns the value of `id`; `None` if the id is stale or unknown.
- `pub fn get(&self, id: twine_core::Id<T>) -> Option<&T>` — The value of `id`, if it is live.
- `pub fn get_mut(&mut self, id: twine_core::Id<T>) -> Option<&mut T>` — Mutable access to the value of `id`, if it is live.
- `pub fn get2_mut(&mut self, a: twine_core::Id<T>, b: twine_core::Id<T>) -> (Option<&mut T>, Option<&mut T>)` — Mutable access to two values at once. If `a == b` the result is `(Some, None)`.
- `pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool` — Whether `insert` would fail with `Error::CapacityExceeded`: no free slot is left and the arena already has `MAX_LEN` slots. Lets a caller refuse a value *before* building it (`insert` drops the value it cannot store, which matters when its `Drop` must not run in the caller's context). Never panics.
- `pub fn contains(&self, id: twine_core::Id<T>) -> bool` — Whether `id` refers to a live value.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of live values.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether no value is live.
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (twine_core::Id<T>, &T)>` — Live values with their ids, in slot order.
- `pub fn iter_mut(&mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (twine_core::Id<T>, &mut T)>` — Live values with their ids, mutably, in slot order.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every value. All existing ids become stale (slots are kept and their generations bumped, so no id can ever resolve to a later value).
- `pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize` — Number of slots allocated (live, free and retired).
- `pub fn slot_count(&self) -> usize` — Number of slots in use or ever used (live, free and retired): the high-water mark of the slot storage, at most `capacity`.
- `pub fn bytes_reserved(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes the arena's own storage reserves: the slot vector (each slot holds a `T` inline plus its `Generation`) and the two free-index lists, by capacity. Memory a `T` owns elsewhere (a `Box` inside it) is not included, nor is allocator overhead: this is what the arena asked the allocator for.
- `pub fn retired(&self) -> usize` — Number of **retired** slots: slots that served all `MAX_GENERATION` generations (65 535 by default, ≈ 2.8 × 10¹⁴ in the safety profile) and are never reused (see the generation budget). Each one is dead memory until the arena is dropped; a non-zero value on a device means the arena's working set is too small for its churn (by default) — in the safety profile it stays 0 in practice.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default

#### type twine_core::Generation
`pub type Generation = u16`
The generation of an arena slot (see `Id::generation`), as a plain integer.

#### struct twine_core::Id<T>
A generational handle into an `Arena<T>`: a `u16` slot index plus a `Generation` (16-bit by default, 48-bit in the safety profile).
Methods of `Id`:
- `const DANGLING: twine_core::Id<T>` — A handle that never resolves (index 0, generation 0; generations start at 1).
- `const INVALID: twine_core::Id<T>` — A handle that no `Arena` ever hands out, whatever it stored before: its index (`u16::MAX`) is outside the slot range (an arena has at most `Arena::MAX_LEN` = 65 535 slots, indices `0..=65 534`) **and** its generation is 0 (generations start at 1 and never wrap: a slot retires instead). So it never resolves, is never equal to a live or stale handle, and — unlike `DANGLING`, which only its generation separates from slot 0 — it stays invalid whatever the `Generation` width.
- `pub const fn from_parts(index: u16, generation: twine_core::Generation) -> Self` — The handle of slot `index` at `generation`, for tables that keep generational slots of their own (e.g. `twine-anim`'s timers and animations) and want `Id`'s size, niche and traits. A generation above `MAX_GENERATION` gives `INVALID`. Never panics.
- `pub const fn index(self) -> u16` — Slot index.
- `pub const fn generation(self) -> twine_core::Generation` — Generation of the slot when the handle was created (≥ 1 for real handles; see `Generation` for its width).
- `pub const fn to_raw(self) -> twine_core::RawId` — Packs into a `RawId`: `generation << 16 | index`.
- `pub const fn from_raw(raw: twine_core::RawId) -> Self` — Unpacks a value produced by `Id::to_raw`. In the safety profile a value whose generation is above `MAX_GENERATION` (never produced by `to_raw`) gives `INVALID`.
- `pub const fn cast<U>(self) -> twine_core::Id<U>` — Reinterprets the handle for another element type.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Default, Debug, Display

#### type twine_core::RawId
`pub type RawId = u32`
An `Id` packed into one integer (`Id::to_raw`): `generation << 16 | index`. **`u32`** by default, **`u64`** in the safety profile (16 index bits plus its 48-bit `Generation`).

#### struct twine_core::Color
A 24-bit RGB color (the canonical color type; pixel formats convert from/to it).
Fields:
- `r: u8` — Red channel.
- `g: u8` — Green channel.
- `b: u8` — Blue channel.
Methods of `Color`:
- `pub fn relative_luminance(self) -> u32` — The WCAG 2.x relative luminance of the color in parts per million: `0` for black, `1_000_000` for white (`0.2126·R + 0.7152·G + 0.0722·B` of the linearized sRGB channels). Integer arithmetic; not meant for rendering (see `luminance` for a cheap perceived brightness).
- `pub fn contrast_ratio(self, other: twine_core::Color) -> twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — The WCAG 2.x contrast ratio between this color and `other` (symmetric).
- `const WHITE: twine_core::Color` — `#FFFFFF`
- `const BLACK: twine_core::Color` — `#000000`
- `const RED: twine_core::Color` — `#FF0000`
- `const GREEN: twine_core::Color` — `#00FF00`
- `const BLUE: twine_core::Color` — `#0000FF`
- `const YELLOW: twine_core::Color` — `#FFFF00`
- `const CYAN: twine_core::Color` — `#00FFFF`
- `const MAGENTA: twine_core::Color` — `#FF00FF`
- `const GRAY: twine_core::Color` — `#808080`
- `pub const fn new(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> twine_core::Color` — Creates a color from its channels.
- `pub const fn hex(v: u32) -> twine_core::Color` — From `0xRRGGBB` (higher bits are ignored).
- `pub const fn hex3(v: u16) -> twine_core::Color` — From `0xRGB`; each nibble is expanded ×17 (`0xF` → `0xFF`).
- `pub const fn to_rgb565(self) -> u16` — Packs to RGB565 (truncating the low bits).
- `pub const fn from_rgb565(v: u16) -> twine_core::Color` — Expands RGB565 with bit replication (`r5 → (r5 << 3) | (r5 >> 2)`), so that `from_rgb565(v).to_rgb565() == v` for every `v`.
- `pub const fn luminance(self) -> u8` — Perceived brightness `(r·77 + g·151 + b·28) >> 8` (white → 255).
- `pub const fn mix(fg: twine_core::Color, bg: twine_core::Color, a: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_core::Color` — Blends `fg` over `bg` with alpha `a`, per channel with `mix_channel`.
- `pub const fn lighten(self, lvl: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_core::Color` — Mixes towards white by `lvl`.
- `pub const fn darken(self, lvl: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_core::Color` — Mixes towards black by `lvl`.
- `pub const fn to_u32_argb(self, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> u32` — `0xAARRGGBB` with the given opacity as alpha.
- `pub const fn lerp(a: twine_core::Color, b: twine_core::Color, t: u16) -> twine_core::Color` — Per-channel linear interpolation from `a` to `b` with `t` in `0..=1024`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### enum twine_core::ColorFormat
Pixel formats of images and draw buffers.
Variants:
- `L8 = 0x06` — 8-bit luminance.
- `A1 = 0x0B` — 1-bit alpha only.
- `A2 = 0x0C` — 2-bit alpha only.
- `A4 = 0x0D` — 4-bit alpha only.
- `A8 = 0x0E` — 8-bit alpha only.
- `I1 = 0x07` — 1-bit indexed (2-entry ARGB8888 palette first).
- `I2 = 0x08` — 2-bit indexed (4-entry palette).
- `I4 = 0x09` — 4-bit indexed (16-entry palette).
- `I8 = 0x0A` — 8-bit indexed (256-entry palette).
- `Rgb565 = 0x12` — 16-bit RGB565, little-endian in memory.
- `Rgb565Swapped = 0x1B` — 16-bit RGB565 with bytes swapped (big-endian in memory, for SPI panels).
- `Rgb565A8 = 0x14` — RGB565 plane followed by an 8-bit alpha plane.
- `Rgb888 = 0x0F` — 24-bit, stored B, G, R.
- `Argb8888 = 0x10` — 32-bit with alpha, stored B, G, R, A.
- `Xrgb8888 = 0x11` — 32-bit, alpha byte ignored.
- `Argb8888Premultiplied = 0x1A` — 32-bit with premultiplied alpha.
Methods of `ColorFormat`:
- `const ALL: [twine_core::ColorFormat; 16]` — Every format, in declaration order.
- `pub const fn bpp(self) -> u8` — Bits per pixel of the main plane (`Rgb565A8` → 16).
- `pub const fn has_alpha(self) -> bool` — Whether pixels carry opacity (alpha-only, indexed with ARGB palette, `Rgb565A8`, `Argb8888*`), like LVGL `lv_color_format_has_alpha`.
- `pub const fn is_indexed(self) -> bool` — `I1`, `I2`, `I4`, `I8`.
- `pub const fn is_alpha_only(self) -> bool` — `A1`, `A2`, `A4`, `A8`.
- `pub const fn palette_len(self) -> usize` — Number of palette entries (`I1` → 2 … `I8` → 256; others 0).
- `pub const fn stride(self, width: u32) -> u32` — Bytes per row of the main plane, rounded up to whole bytes (saturating).
- `pub const fn min_stride(self, w: u16) -> u16` — Minimum bytes per row of the main plane for width `w`: `⌈w · bpp / 8⌉` (saturating).
- `pub const fn data_size(self, w: u16, h: u16, stride: u16) -> usize` — Total bytes of a `w × h` image whose main-plane rows are `stride` bytes apart: palette (`palette_len · 4`, indexed formats) + `stride · h` + the `w · h` alpha plane of `Rgb565A8` (its stride is always `w`, LVGL 9 convention). Saturates at `usize::MAX` (reachable on 32-bit targets only, for images near 65 535 × 65 535).
- `pub const fn buf_size(self, w: u32, h: u32) -> u32` — Total bytes of a `w × h` image: palette (4 bytes per entry) + main plane (+ the alpha plane of `Rgb565A8`), saturating.
- `pub const fn from_u8(v: u8) -> Option<twine_core::ColorFormat>` — The format with LVGL discriminant `v`, if supported.
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — Short name, e.g. `"RGB565"`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Display, TryFrom<u8>

#### struct twine_core::Opa
Opacity, stored as `0` (transparent) to `255` (fully covering).
Methods of `Opa`:
- `const TRANSP: twine_core::Opa` — Fully transparent.
- `const COVER: twine_core::Opa` — Fully covering.
- `const P0: twine_core::Opa` — 0 %.
- `const P10: twine_core::Opa` — 10 %.
- `const P20: twine_core::Opa` — 20 %.
- `const P30: twine_core::Opa` — 30 %.
- `const P40: twine_core::Opa` — 40 %.
- `const P50: twine_core::Opa` — 50 %.
- `const P60: twine_core::Opa` — 60 %.
- `const P70: twine_core::Opa` — 70 %.
- `const P80: twine_core::Opa` — 80 %.
- `const P90: twine_core::Opa` — 90 %.
- `const P100: twine_core::Opa` — 100 %.
- `const MIN: twine_core::Opa` — Values `<= MIN` are treated as transparent (LVGL `LV_OPA_MIN`).
- `const MAX: twine_core::Opa` — Values `>= MAX` are treated as covering (LVGL `LV_OPA_MAX`).
- `pub const fn from_raw(raw: u8) -> twine_core::Opa` — The opacity whose 8-bit representation is `raw` (`255` = fully covering).
- `pub const fn raw(self) -> u8` — The 8-bit representation (`Opa::COVER.raw() == 255`).
- `pub const fn pct(p: u8) -> twine_core::Opa` — `p` percent (clamped to 100), rounded: `p · 255 / 100`.
- `pub const fn mul(self, other: twine_core::Opa) -> twine_core::Opa` — Combined opacity `udiv255(a · b)`; `COVER.mul(x) == x` exactly.
- `pub const fn is_transparent(self) -> bool` — `<= MIN`: drawing can be skipped.
- `pub const fn is_cover(self) -> bool` — `>= MAX`: drawing can ignore what is below.
- `pub const fn inverse(self) -> twine_core::Opa` — `255 − self`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, From<twine_core::Opa>

#### trait twine_core::PixelFormat
`pub trait PixelFormat: Copy + 'static`
A byte-aligned pixel format the renderer is monomorphized over.
Items:
- `type Raw: Copy + Default + PartialEq + Debug + 'static` — The in-memory representation of one pixel.
- `const FORMAT: twine_core::ColorFormat` — The runtime tag of this format.
- `const BYTES: usize` — Bytes per pixel (at least 1: the renderer divides by it and asserts this at compile time).
- `fn from_color(c: twine_core::Color) -> Self::Raw` — Converts a color to the raw pixel value.
- `fn to_color(raw: Self::Raw) -> twine_core::Color` — Converts a raw pixel value to a color.
- `fn mix(fg: Self::Raw, bg: Self::Raw, a: twine_core::Opa) -> Self::Raw` — Blends `fg` over `bg` with alpha `a` (see the trait docs for the normative semantics).
- `fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self::Raw` — Reads a pixel from the first `Self::BYTES` bytes of `bytes`.
- `fn write(bytes: &mut [u8], raw: Self::Raw)` — Writes a pixel to the first `BYTES` bytes of `bytes`.
Implemented by: twine_core::color::Rgb565, twine_core::color::Rgb565Swapped, twine_core::color::Rgb888, twine_core::color::Xrgb8888, twine_core::color::Argb8888, twine_core::color::L8

#### struct twine_core::Crc32
A CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) checksum, computed incrementally: `new`, any number of `update`s, then `value`. Two `Crc32` compare equal when their values are equal, so a checksum is also the value type that integrity checks return and compare (`Engine::render_region_to`, frame observers, the audit digest).
Methods of `Crc32`:
- `pub const fn new() -> Self` — A checksum of no data (value `0`).
- `pub fn of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self` — The checksum of `bytes`.
- `pub fn update(&mut self, bytes: &[u8])` — Adds `bytes` to the checksum. O(len), two table lookups per byte.
- `pub fn update_u32(&mut self, v: u32)` — Adds the little-endian bytes of `v` (for checksums of values, e.g. a widget's value).
- `pub const fn value(&self) -> u32` — The checksum of the data added so far.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, Debug, Display, Write

#### enum twine_core::Error
Errors of `twine-core` operations.
Variants:
- `CapacityExceeded` — A fixed-capacity container is full (e.g. an `Arena` with 65 535 live entries).
- `InvalidArgument(&'static str)` — An argument is invalid; the payload names it.
- `OutOfBounds` — An index or coordinate is out of bounds.
- `Unsupported(&'static str)` — The requested feature or format is not supported; the payload names it.
Implements: Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Error, Display

#### struct twine_core::FaultCounts
Saturating per-kind occurrence counters (how often each fault happened since start-up).
Methods of `FaultCounts`:
- `pub const fn new() -> twine_core::FaultCounts` — All counters at zero.
- `pub const fn get(&self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> u32` — The occurrences of `kind`.
- `pub fn add(&mut self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind, n: u32)` — Adds `n` occurrences of `kind` (saturating). Never panics: a counter stops at `u32::MAX`.
- `pub fn total(&self) -> u32` — The occurrences of every kind together (saturating).
- `pub fn kinds(&self) -> twine_core::Faults` — The kinds that occurred at least once.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### enum twine_core::FaultKind
The kind of a fault.
Variants:
- `FlushError = 0` — A display driver failed to start a flush or to present a framebuffer (or the application reported a failed flush with `Engine::report_flush`): the area it was given may not show what was rendered.
- `FlushTimeout = 1` — A display driver did not complete a flush (or a framebuffer swap) within `EngineConfig::flush_timeout`: the display is considered failed.
- `EffectLoopCut = 2` — The reactive runtime cut an effect loop: pending bindings were dropped, so some widget properties may show outdated values.
- `DepthGuard = 3` — The reactive runtime's depth guard triggered (a very deep memo chain): values stay correct, but extra work was done.
- `Capacity = 4` — A bound was reached (a `Limits` field or a fixed capacity): something was not created, was cut or was dropped — never grown.
- `BuildFailed = 5` — The view layer could not build a widget it was asked to build.
- `FormatDisabled = 6` — A display uses a colour format whose renderer is not compiled in.
- `InputDevice = 7` — An input device reported a failure through its health (`InputDevice::health`): it became degraded (some reads failed) or failed (its samples are processed as released). Raised on the transition only, not for every failed read.
- `ChannelOverflow = 8` — A channel into the UI was full: messages were dropped.
- `AccelTimeout = 9` — A draw accelerator (e.g. DMA2D) did not finish an operation within its bound; the operation was drawn in software.
- `DisplayControl = 10` — A display control (brightness, sleep, wake, rotation) requested from the engine was not applied: the driver does not support it, the driver failed, or a rotation does not fit the display's buffers. The display keeps its previous state (except that a display put to sleep stops being drawn even when its driver cannot sleep).
- `DisposedHandle = 11` — A reactive handle (signal, memo, stored value, effect or scope) was used after its scope was disposed, or a node was created in a disposed scope. Raised by the reactive runtime's `no-panic-runtime` feature (implied by the `safety` profile), which skips the write or creation instead of panicking: the value written is dropped, and a creation returns a handle that is not alive. A read that has no value to return still panics after raising the fault (see `twine_reactive::ReactiveError`).
- `MemoCycle = 12` — A memo read itself, directly or through other memos (a dependency cycle). With the reactive runtime's `no-panic-runtime` feature the read returns the memo's previous value instead of panicking (a memo with no previous value still panics after raising the fault); without it, the read panics.
- `ReentrantAccess = 13` — A signal or stored value was written while its value was borrowed by an enclosing access of the same value (e.g. `set` inside `with` on the same signal). With the reactive runtime's `no-panic-runtime` feature the write is skipped instead of panicking.
- `AllocAfterSeal = 14` — Twine allocated heap memory after the application **sealed** it (`alloc_guard::seal`, `Ui::seal`): a growth point that should have been sized at start-up (from `Limits`) grew, or something was created after start-up. The allocation was made (refusing it would lose data or break an invariant); the fault is the evidence that the "no allocation after start-up" claim did not hold.
- `FrameOverrun = 15` — An update used up the time of its step budget (`StepBudget::time`, e.g. `EngineConfig::step_budget`): rendering stopped after the chunk that reached it, and the rest of the frame continues in the next update (`Wake::Now`) — deferred, never dropped. Also raised when an update that deferred nothing still ended past its time (a long layout or binding run, one slow chunk). Measured with the engine's `hires_timer`; at most one record per update.
- `FailSafe = 16` — The application switched a display to its fail-safe screen (`Engine::enter_fail_safe`, `Ui::enter_fail_safe`): from now on the display shows the static screen registered at start-up, and loading any other screen is refused until the application leaves the fail-safe state. Twine raises it so the switch is part of the fault stream and its evidence; the reason is the application's.
- `DisplayIntegrity = 17` — A display-integrity check found that a region of the display does not show what was rendered: the checksum of the pixels read back from the panel (or its framebuffer) differs from the checksum of an independent off-screen re-render of the same region (`Engine::check_region`). What the application does about it (retry, fail-safe screen, reset) is its policy.
- `PartitionViolation = 18` — A partition tried to register for a cross-context source another partition consumes (ADR-001 § 5.5): a `Channel` or `Latest` has one consuming partition — the first one that registered a handler (`on_message`, `on_latest`, `watch`), recorded permanently — and a registration from any other partition is refused (no handler, no wake-up routing) instead of letting two runtimes share the source's waker slot or queue. Recorded in the refused partition's runtime, so only that partition's `Ui` sees it. Fan out to two partitions with one cell per consumer, set by the producer.
Methods of `FaultKind`:
- `const ALL: [twine_core::FaultKind; 19]` — Every kind, in `index` order.
- `const COUNT: usize` — The number of kinds (the length of per-kind tables such as fault counters).
- `pub const fn index(self) -> usize` — The kind's stable index (`0..COUNT`), e.g. for per-kind tables or diagnostic codes.
- `pub const fn from_index(index: usize) -> Option<twine_core::FaultKind>` — The kind with `index`, `None` if out of range.
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The kind's name, as written in the source (`"FlushError"`, …).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Display, From<twine_core::FaultKind>, BitOr<twine_core::FaultKind>, BitOrAssign<twine_core::FaultKind>, FromIterator<twine_core::FaultKind>

#### struct twine_core::Faults
A set of `FaultKind`s (e.g. the faults raised since they were last taken).
Methods of `Faults`:
- `pub const fn empty() -> twine_core::Faults` — No faults.
- `pub const fn is_empty(self) -> bool` — Whether the set holds no kind.
- `pub const fn len(self) -> usize` — The number of kinds in the set.
- `pub const fn contains(self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind) -> bool` — Whether `kind` is in the set.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind)` — Adds `kind`. Idempotent: inserting a kind already in the set changes nothing.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, kind: twine_core::FaultKind)` — Removes `kind`. Removing a kind that is not in the set changes nothing.
- `pub const fn union(self, other: twine_core::Faults) -> twine_core::Faults` — The kinds of both sets. Same as `self | other`.
- `pub fn iter(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = twine_core::FaultKind>` — The kinds in the set, in `FaultKind::index` order.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From<twine_core::FaultKind>, BitOr, BitOr<twine_core::FaultKind>, BitOrAssign, BitOrAssign<twine_core::FaultKind>, FromIterator<twine_core::FaultKind>, Debug

#### struct twine_core::Limits
The memory bounds of an application (see the module docs).
Fields:
- `max_nodes: u16` — Live engine nodes: widgets, screens and every display's four layers (`1..=65 535`, default 65 535). Enforced by `Engine::create` and friends (`CapacityFault::Nodes`). Preallocated: the node arena and the delete scratch.
- `max_tree_depth: u8` — Levels below a root (a screen or layer is level 0, its child level 1, …; `1..=255`, default 255). Bounds the recursion of drawing and layout. Enforced when a node is created or moved (`CapacityFault::TreeDepth`).
- `max_text_len: u16` — Bytes of one widget text (label, checkbox, textarea; `1..=65 535`, default 65 535). A longer text is cut at a character boundary (`CapacityFault::TextLen`). Preallocated: a label's buffers are reserved to this size when it first gets an owned text.
- `max_handlers: u16` — Event handlers registered on engine nodes, all nodes together (default 65 535; `0` allows none). Enforced by `Engine::add_event_handler` (`CapacityFault::Handlers`).
- `max_timers: u16` — Engine timers alive at once (`1..=65 534`, default 65 534). Enforced by `Engine::timer_add` (`CapacityFault::Timers`). Preallocated: the timer table.
- `max_anims: u16` — Engine animations running at once (`1..=65 534`, default 65 534). Enforced by `Engine::anim_start` (`CapacityFault::Animations`). Preallocated: the animation table.
- `max_reactive_nodes: u16` — Live reactive nodes: signals, memos, stored values and effects (`1..=65 535`, default 65 535). Enforced by the reactive runtime (`CapacityFault::ReactiveNodes`). Preallocated: the node arena and the propagation stack.
- `max_scopes: u16` — Live reactive scopes (`1..=65 535`, default 65 535) (`CapacityFault::ReactiveScopes`). Preallocated: the scope arena.
- `max_pending_effects: u16` — Effects waiting to run at once (`1..=65 535`, default 65 535): queued after a write, or deferred until a UI update provides their context (`CapacityFault::PendingEffects`). Preallocated: both effect queues.
- `messages_per_channel: u16` — Messages each channel delivers per `Ui` update (`1..=65 535`, default 16): bounds the work of one update; the rest waits for the next.
- `engine_queue: u16` — Engine commands a `Ui` can queue while it does not hold the engine (default 16; `0` drops every such command). The ring is allocated once, when the `Ui` is built (`CapacityFault::EngineQueue`).
- `max_nav_depth: u8` — Routes on a navigator's stack (`1..=255`, default 255) (`CapacityFault::NavDepth`). Preallocated: the route and page stacks.
- `max_list_items: u16` — Rows of one keyed collection (`1..=65 535`, default 65 535): the rows of a `for_each`, the visible rows of a `virtual_list`. A collection with more items shows the first ones (`CapacityFault::ListItems`); a `for_each` can lower its own bound (`ForEach::max_items`). Preallocated: each collection's row list and reconcile scratch, reserved when it is built (so a keyed change — insert, remove, move — allocates nothing beyond the rows it creates). Size it for the longest list: the reservation is per collection.
- `max_theme_classes: u16` — Nodes with a theme class of their own — a variant (`ButtonVariant::Tinted`) or a role (`.role(&METRIC_TILE)`) set with `Engine::set_theme_class` — all nodes together (default 65 535; `0` allows none). Enforced by `Engine::set_theme_class` (`CapacityFault::ThemeClasses`): the node keeps its widget class's look. Preallocated: the engine's theme-class side table.
- `max_heap_wakers: u16` — Wakers the process-wide waker pool may allocate on the heap once its 4 static slots are leased (default 60, i.e. 64 `Ui`s alive at once; `0` forbids heap wakers). A heap waker is allocated once and never freed (it is reused), so this bounds that memory (`CapacityFault::WakerPool`). Process-wide: the last `Ui` built sets it.
- `heap_budget: Option<usize>` — Heap bytes the `Ui`'s memory report may show (`MemoryReport::heap_bytes`: engine, runtime, queues, waker pool; not the application's own allocations). `None` (default): not checked. Checked when the `Ui` is sealed (`CapacityFault::HeapBudget`); `Some(0)` is invalid.
- `preallocate: bool` — Reserve the storage of the bounded structures up front (default `false`: grow on demand, up to the limits). Required by the `safety` profile. Size the limits for the product: the reservation is made in full (e.g. `max_nodes` × the node slot size).
Methods of `Limits`:
- `const DEFAULT: twine_core::Limits` — The structural maxima, growing on demand (see each field). Not valid in the `safety` profile, which needs `preallocated` limits.
- `pub const fn max_nodes(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_nodes`.
- `pub const fn max_tree_depth(self, n: u8) -> Self` — Sets `max_tree_depth`.
- `pub const fn max_text_len(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_text_len`.
- `pub const fn max_handlers(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_handlers`.
- `pub const fn max_timers(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_timers`.
- `pub const fn max_anims(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_anims`.
- `pub const fn max_reactive_nodes(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_reactive_nodes`.
- `pub const fn max_scopes(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_scopes`.
- `pub const fn max_pending_effects(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_pending_effects`.
- `pub const fn messages_per_channel(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `messages_per_channel`.
- `pub const fn engine_queue(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `engine_queue`.
- `pub const fn max_nav_depth(self, n: u8) -> Self` — Sets `max_nav_depth`.
- `pub const fn max_list_items(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_list_items`.
- `pub const fn max_theme_classes(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_theme_classes`.
- `pub const fn max_heap_wakers(self, n: u16) -> Self` — Sets `max_heap_wakers`.
- `pub const fn heap_budget(self, bytes: Option<usize>) -> Self` — Sets `heap_budget`.
- `pub const fn preallocated(self) -> Self` — Sets `preallocate` to `true`.
- `pub const fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), twine_core::Error>` — Checks the ranges documented on each field, and — in the `safety` profile — that the limits are `preallocated`. The engine, the runtime and the `Ui` builders call it before applying a value.
  Errors: `Error::InvalidArgument` naming the first value out of range. Never panics.
- `pub fn summary(&self) -> twine_core::audit::KeyValues<'_, twine_core::Limits>` — The limits as `limits.<field>=<value>` lines (see `audit` for the format): `Display`, and `defmt::Format` with the `defmt` feature. For the complete configuration of an application use the view layer's `AppConfig::audit_report`. Formatting code is linked only when this is used.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, Audit

- `pub const fn normalized(self) -> twine_core::Angle` — The equivalent angle in `0..3600`.

Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Add, Sub, Neg, Display
