#### struct twine_core::Fraction
A fraction from 0 to 1, stored in 1/255 steps (`255` = 1.0): gradient stop positions, LED brightness and other "how far along" values.
Methods of `Fraction`:
- `const ZERO: twine_core::Fraction` — 0.
- `const HALF: twine_core::Fraction` — ½ (`128`, rounded up like `Fraction::pct``(50)`).
- `const ONE: twine_core::Fraction` — 1.
- `pub const fn from_raw(raw: u8) -> twine_core::Fraction` — The fraction whose 8-bit representation is `raw` (`255` = 1.0).
- `pub const fn raw(self) -> u8` — The 8-bit representation (`Fraction::ONE.raw() == 255`).
- `pub const fn pct(p: u8) -> twine_core::Fraction` — `p` percent (clamped to 100), rounded: `p · 255 / 100`.
- `pub const fn ratio(num: u32, den: u32) -> twine_core::Fraction` — `num / den`, clamped to `0..=1` and rounded. A zero `den` gives `Fraction::ZERO` (no division by zero).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord

#### struct twine_core::Fx
16.16 signed fixed-point number (`Fx::from_raw(1 << 16)` is 1.0).
Methods of `Fx`:
- `const SHIFT: u32` — Number of fractional bits.
- `const ONE: twine_core::Fx` — 1.0
- `const HALF: twine_core::Fx` — 0.5
- `const ZERO: twine_core::Fx` — 0.0
- `const MAX: twine_core::Fx` — Largest value (≈ 32767.99998).
- `const MIN: twine_core::Fx` — Smallest value (−32768.0).
- `pub const fn from_raw(raw: i32) -> twine_core::Fx` — The number whose 16.16 representation is `raw` (`from_raw(1 << 16)` is 1.0).
- `pub const fn raw(self) -> i32` — The 16.16 representation (`Fx::ONE.raw() == 1 << 16`).
- `pub const fn from_int(v: i32) -> twine_core::Fx` — Converts an integer (saturating outside −32768..=32767).
- `pub fn from_ratio(num: i32, den: i32) -> twine_core::Fx` — `num / den`, rounded. `den == 0` returns `Fx::ZERO` and logs a warning.
- `pub const fn to_int_floor(self) -> i32` — Largest integer `<= self`.
- `pub const fn to_int_round(self) -> i32` — Nearest integer, halves rounded away from zero.
- `pub const fn to_int_ceil(self) -> i32` — Smallest integer `>= self`.
- `pub const fn frac(self) -> u16` — Fractional part above the floor, in 1/65536 (always non-negative: `-0.25` → `0.75`).
- `pub const fn abs(self) -> twine_core::Fx` — Absolute value (saturating: `abs(MIN) == MAX`).
- `pub const fn mul(self, o: twine_core::Fx) -> twine_core::Fx` — Product, rounded half away from zero, saturating.
- `pub fn div(self, o: twine_core::Fx) -> twine_core::Fx` — Quotient, rounded half away from zero, saturating. Division by zero saturates to `Fx::MAX` / `Fx::MIN` by the sign of `self` (zero stays zero) and logs a warning.
- `pub const fn saturating_add(self, o: twine_core::Fx) -> twine_core::Fx` — Saturating addition.
- `pub const fn saturating_sub(self, o: twine_core::Fx) -> twine_core::Fx` — Saturating subtraction.
- `pub const fn lerp(a: twine_core::Fx, b: twine_core::Fx, t: u16) -> twine_core::Fx` — Linear interpolation from `a` to `b` with `t` in `0..=1024`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Add, Sub, Neg, Mul, Div, Display

#### struct twine_core::Scale
Scale factor, stored with 256 = 1.0 (LVGL zoom convention).
Methods of `Scale`:
- `const ONE: twine_core::Scale` — 1.0 (no scaling).
- `const ZERO: twine_core::Scale` — 0 (everything collapses to a point).
- `pub const fn pct(p: u16) -> twine_core::Scale` — `p` percent (`100` → 256), truncated; saturates at `u16::MAX` (≈ 256 ×).
- `pub const fn from_raw_256(raw: u16) -> twine_core::Scale` — The scale whose 256-based representation is `raw` (`256` = 1.0, `128` = 0.5).
- `pub const fn raw_256(self) -> u16` — The 256-based representation (`Scale::ONE.raw_256() == 256`).
- `pub const fn apply(self, v: i32) -> i32` — `v · s / 256`, rounded half away from zero, saturating.
- `pub fn inverse_apply(self, v: i32) -> i32` — `v · 256 / s` (truncated towards zero). A zero scale returns `v` and logs a warning.
- `pub const fn to_fx(self) -> twine_core::Fx` — The scale as a fixed-point number (`ONE` → `Fx::ONE`).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Default

#### struct twine_core::Partition
A partition: one reactive runtime and the UIs built on it (see the module docs).
Methods of `Partition`:
- `const COUNT: usize` — The number of partitions: 2 with the `partitions` feature, 1 without. A power of two.
- `const MAIN: twine_core::Partition` — The main partition (index 0): what `Runtime::take()` claims and what a single-partition application uses everywhere.
- `const ALL: [twine_core::Partition; 1]` — Every partition, in index order.
- `pub const fn new(index: u8) -> Option<twine_core::Partition>` — The partition with `index`, or `None` when `index >= COUNT` (without the `partitions` feature: `Some` for 0 only). Never panics.
- `pub const fn index(self) -> u8` — The partition's index (`0..COUNT`). Never panics.
- `pub fn select<T>(self, table: &[T; 1]) -> &T` — This partition's entry of a per-partition table (`[T; COUNT]`): how the runtime selects its state slot and the allocation guard its seal record. The index is an enum below `COUNT`, so this compiles to an address computation (no bounds check, no panic); without the `partitions` feature it is the table's only entry.
Implements: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Debug, Default, Display

#### enum twine_core::AddResult
Result of `RectSet::add`.
Variants:
- `Added` — The rectangle was stored.
- `AlreadyCovered` — An existing rectangle already covers it; nothing changed.
- `ClippedAway` — Nothing remained after clipping to the bounds.
- `Overflowed` — The set was full: everything was replaced by one bounding box.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::RectSet<const N: usize>
Up to `N` dirty rectangles, clipped to `bounds`, never allocating (LVGL's `inv_areas`).
Methods of `RectSet`:
- `pub const fn new(bounds: twine_core::Rect) -> Self` — An empty set whose rectangles are clipped to `bounds`.
- `pub const fn bounds(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — The clip bounds.
- `pub fn set_bounds(&mut self, b: twine_core::Rect)` — Changes the bounds and clears the set.
- `pub fn add(&mut self, r: twine_core::Rect) -> twine_core::AddResult` — Adds a dirty rectangle (see the type docs for the policy).
- `pub fn merge(&mut self)` — Joins pairs of touching/overlapping rectangles while that reduces the covered area (`union.area() < a.area() + b.area()`), until nothing changes. O(n²) per pass.
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &twine_core::Rect>` — The stored rectangles.
- `pub const fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of stored rectangles.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether nothing is dirty.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every rectangle and resets the overflow flag.
- `pub fn bounding_box(&self) -> twine_core::Rect` — Bounding box of all stored rectangles (`Rect::ZERO` if empty).
- `pub fn total_area(&self) -> u64` — Sum of the stored areas (overlaps counted twice), saturating at `u64::MAX`.
- `pub const fn overflowed(&self) -> bool` — Whether an overflow happened since the last `clear`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::XorShift32
Marsaglia xorshift32 generator: tiny, fast and deterministic on every platform.
Methods of `XorShift32`:
- `const DEFAULT_SEED: u32` — Seed used when `0` is given (the all-zero state would be stuck).
- `pub const fn new(seed: u32) -> Self` — Creates a generator; a zero seed is replaced by `Self::DEFAULT_SEED`.
- `pub fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32` — The next 32 random bits.
- `pub fn range(&mut self, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32` — A value in the half-open range `lo..hi`; `lo >= hi` returns `lo`.
- `pub fn next_bool(&mut self) -> bool` — A random boolean.
- `pub fn next_opa(&mut self) -> twine_core::Opa` — A random opacity.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### struct twine_core::SmallVec<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize>
A vector storing up to `N` (≤ 255) elements inline, spilling to the heap when the `N + 1`-th element is pushed. Once spilled it never returns to inline storage (clearing keeps the heap buffer for reuse).
Methods of `SmallVec`:
- `pub fn new() -> Self` — An empty vector (no allocation).
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` — Number of elements.
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — Whether there are no elements.
- `pub fn spilled(&self) -> bool` — Whether the elements live on the heap.
- `pub fn heap_bytes(&self) -> usize` — Heap bytes of the elements: 0 while inline, the heap buffer's capacity once spilled. Allocates nothing; never panics.
- `pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[T]` — The elements as a slice.
- `pub fn as_mut_slice(&mut self) -> &mut [T]` — The elements as a mutable slice.
- `pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, T>` — Iterates over the elements.
- `pub fn push(&mut self, v: T)` — Appends an element; a spill or heap growth after a seal is noted in `Partition::MAIN`'s seal domain (`alloc_guard`). Owners in another partition use `push_in`.
- `pub fn push_in(&mut self, p: twine_core::Partition, v: T)` — Appends an element, noting a spill or heap growth after a seal in partition `p`'s seal domain (the partition of the vector's owner, e.g. a partition's reactive runtime). Never panics.
- `pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>` — Removes and returns the last element.
- `pub fn insert(&mut self, index: usize, v: T)` — Inserts `v` at `index` (`index <= len`), shifting later elements. Out of range: no-op with a warning.
- `pub fn remove(&mut self, index: usize) -> T` — Removes the element at `index`, preserving order. Out of range: returns `T::default()` and logs a warning.
- `pub fn swap_remove(&mut self, index: usize) -> T` — Removes the element at `index`, replacing it with the last one (O(1), order not preserved). Out of range: returns `T::default()` and logs a warning.
- `pub fn retain(&mut self, f: impl FnMut(&T) -> bool)` — Keeps only the elements for which `f` returns `true`, preserving order.
- `pub fn clear(&mut self)` — Removes every element (a spilled vector keeps its heap buffer).
- `pub fn contains(&self, v: &T) -> bool where T: PartialEq` — Whether `v` is an element.
Implements: Clone, Default, Deref, DerefMut, Extend<T>, FromIterator<T>, IntoIterator, IntoIterator, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::Duration
A span of time in microseconds. Arithmetic saturates.

- `pub const fn as_millis(self) -> u64` — Length in whole milliseconds (floor).
- `pub const fn as_millis_u32(self) -> u32` — Length in whole milliseconds, saturating at `u32::MAX`.

- `pub const fn saturating_sub(self, o: twine_core::Duration) -> twine_core::Duration` — Saturating subtraction (floors at zero).

#### struct twine_core::Instant
A point in time: microseconds since an arbitrary epoch (e.g. boot).

#### struct twine_core::Transform
A 2-D affine transform:
Fields:
- `a: twine_core::Fx` — x scale / rotation component.
- `b: twine_core::Fx` — y shear from x (rotation `sin`).
- `c: twine_core::Fx` — x shear from y (rotation `−sin`).
- `d: twine_core::Fx` — y scale / rotation component.
- `tx: twine_core::Fx` — x translation.
- `ty: twine_core::Fx` — y translation.
Methods of `Transform`:
- `const IDENTITY: twine_core::Transform` — The identity transform.
- `pub const fn translate(dx: twine_core::Fx, dy: twine_core::Fx) -> Self` — Translation by `(dx, dy)`.
- `pub const fn scale(sx: twine_core::Fx, sy: twine_core::Fx) -> Self` — Scaling by `(sx, sy)` around the origin.
- `pub const fn rotate(angle: twine_core::Angle) -> Self` — Rotation by `angle` (clockwise on screen) around the origin.
- `pub const fn skew(ax: twine_core::Angle, ay: twine_core::Angle) -> Self` — Skew: `x' = x + tan(ax)·y`, `y' = tan(ay)·x + y`. Where `cos` is 0 the tangent is clamped to `Fx::MAX` (or `Fx::MIN` for a negative sine).
- `pub const fn then(self, next: twine_core::Transform) -> Self` — Composition: apply `self`, then `next`. Never panics: coefficients beyond the 16.16 range saturate.
- `pub const fn around(self, pivot: twine_core::Point) -> Self` — The same transform applied around `pivot` instead of the origin: `translate(−pivot) · self · translate(pivot)`.
- `pub const fn from_rotate_scale(angle: twine_core::Angle, sx: twine_core::Scale, sy: twine_core::Scale, pivot: twine_core::Point) -> Self` — Scale by `(sx, sy)`, then rotate by `angle`, both around `pivot` (LVGL image/layer transform order).
- `pub fn invert(&self) -> Option<twine_core::Transform>` — The inverse transform, or `None` when the determinant is below 1/65536 in magnitude.
- `pub const fn map(&self, x: twine_core::Fx, y: twine_core::Fx) -> (twine_core::Fx, twine_core::Fx)` — Maps a fixed-point coordinate (saturating; never panics).
- `pub const fn map_point(&self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_core::Point` — Maps a pixel coordinate, rounded to the nearest integer.
- `pub fn map_rect_bounds(&self, r: twine_core::Rect) -> twine_core::Rect` — Bounding box of the four mapped corners (see `Rect::corners`), floored/ceiled outwards.
- `pub fn is_identity(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is exactly the identity.
- `pub fn is_translation_only(&self) -> bool` — Whether the transform only translates (no scale, rotation or skew).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default

#### enum twine_core::Validity<T>
A value and how far it can be trusted.
Variants:
- `Valid(T)` — A current value.
- `Stale { value: T, age: twine_core::Duration }` — The last value, older than the consumer allows.
- `Failed` — The source reported a failure (sensor fault, out of range, lost link).
- `NoData` — No value yet (nothing received since start-up).
Methods of `Validity`:
- `pub const fn value(&self) -> Option<&T>` — The value to show: `Some` for `Valid` and `Stale`, `None` otherwise.
- `pub fn value_or(self, fallback: T) -> T` — The value to show, or `fallback` (e.g. the position a bar shows under the cross-hatch).
- `pub const fn is_valid(&self) -> bool` — Whether this is `Valid`.
- `pub const fn status(&self) -> twine_core::ValidityStatus` — How this is shown (`ValidityStatus`).
- `pub fn map<U>(self, f: impl FnOnce(T) -> U) -> twine_core::Validity<U>` — Maps the value, keeping the variant (and the age of a stale value).
- `pub const fn as_ref(&self) -> twine_core::Validity<&T>` — A reference to the value, keeping the variant.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default, From<T>, From<twine_core::Validity<T>>, From<&twine_core::Validity<T>>

#### enum twine_core::ValidityStatus
How a `Validity` is shown: its variant without the value.
Variants:
- `Valid` — The value is current.
- `Stale` — The value is shown but too old.
- `Invalid` — There is no value to show (failed, or no data yet).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, From<twine_core::Validity<T>>, From<&twine_core::Validity<T>>

#### enum twine_core::Rotation
Display rotation, in LVGL's convention: the panel is turned clockwise by this angle and the picture stays upright, so `Deg90` draws logical `(x, y)` on native pixel `(y, w − 1 − x)` (see `Rect::rotate_in`). Software rotation and the panel drivers' hardware rotation (`MADCTL`) follow the same convention. Re-exported by `twine-hal`.
Variants:
- `Deg0` — No rotation.
- `Deg90` — 90° rotation.
- `Deg180` — 180° rotation.
- `Deg270` — 270° rotation.
Methods of `Rotation`:
- `pub const fn swaps_axes(self) -> bool` — Whether the logical width and height are swapped on the physical panel (90° and 270°).
- `pub const fn relative_to(self, base: twine_core::Rotation) -> twine_core::Rotation` — The rotation that is left to do when `base` is already done: `self − base` (mod 360°). The engine uses it when a panel rotates in hardware to `base` and the rest is done in software.
- `pub const fn degrees(self) -> u16` — The rotation in whole degrees (0, 90, 180 or 270).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::Insets

- `top: i32` — Top inset.
- `right: i32` — Right inset.
- `bottom: i32` — Bottom inset.
Methods of `Insets`:
- `const ZERO: twine_core::Insets` — All zero.

- `pub const fn all(v: i32) -> Self` — The same inset `v` on every side.
- `pub const fn hor_ver(h: i32, v: i32) -> Self` — `h` on left and right, `v` on top and bottom.
- `pub const fn horizontal(self) -> i32` — `left + right` (saturating).
- `pub const fn vertical(self) -> i32` — `top + bottom` (saturating).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::Rect
Half-open rectangle `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)`. Empty iff `x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0`.
Fields:
- `x0: i32` — Left edge (inclusive).
- `y0: i32` — Top edge (inclusive).
- `x1: i32` — Right edge (exclusive).
- `y1: i32` — Bottom edge (exclusive).
Methods of `Rect`:
- `const ZERO: twine_core::Rect` — The empty rectangle at the origin.
- `pub const fn new(x0: i32, y0: i32, x1: i32, y1: i32) -> Self` — Creates a rectangle from its edges.
- `pub const fn from_xywh(x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, h: i32) -> Self` — Creates a rectangle from its top-left corner and size (saturating).
- `pub const fn from_origin_size(origin: twine_core::Point, size: twine_core::Size) -> Self` — Creates a rectangle from an origin and a size.
- `pub const fn width(&self) -> i32` — Width, `max(0, x1 - x0)` (saturating).
- `pub const fn height(&self) -> i32` — Height, `max(0, y1 - y0)` (saturating).
- `pub const fn size(&self) -> twine_core::Size` — `width × height`.
- `pub const fn origin(&self) -> twine_core::Point` — Top-left corner.
- `pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` — `true` when the rectangle contains no pixel.
- `pub const fn area(&self) -> u64` — Number of pixels (exact, `0` if empty).
- `pub const fn contains(&self, p: twine_core::Point) -> bool` — Whether the pixel `p` lies inside.
- `pub const fn contains_rect(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> bool` — Whether `other` lies completely inside. An empty rectangle is contained in anything.
- `pub const fn intersects(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> bool` — Whether the two rectangles share at least one pixel.
- `pub const fn intersection(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> Option<twine_core::Rect>` — The common part, or `None` if it is empty.
- `pub const fn union(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> twine_core::Rect` — Bounding box of both. The union with an empty rectangle returns the other one.
- `pub const fn touches_or_overlaps(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> bool` — Whether the rectangles overlap or share (part of) an edge. Touching only at a corner point does not count. Empty rectangles never touch anything.
- `pub const fn translate(&self, dx: i32, dy: i32) -> twine_core::Rect` — Moved by `(dx, dy)` (saturating).
- `pub const fn offset(&self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_core::Rect` — Moved by the vector `p`.
- `pub const fn expand(&self, n: i32) -> twine_core::Rect` — Grows by `n` on every side; a negative `n` shrinks. Shrinking past the center yields an empty rectangle at the center instead of an inverted one.
- `pub const fn inset(&self, i: twine_core::Insets) -> twine_core::Rect` — Shrinks by the given insets (negative insets grow). Clamped to empty at the center.
- `pub const fn outset(&self, i: twine_core::Insets) -> twine_core::Rect` — Grows by the given insets (negative insets shrink). Clamped to empty at the center.
- `pub const fn center(&self) -> twine_core::Point` — Center point, rounded towards negative infinity.
- `pub const fn clamp_point(&self, p: twine_core::Point) -> twine_core::Point` — The nearest pixel inside the rectangle (`x <= x1 - 1`). For an empty rectangle the result is clamped to the top-left corner.
- `pub const fn round_out(&self, align: u8) -> twine_core::Rect` — Rounds `x0, y0` down and `x1, y1` up to multiples of `align` (0 or 1: unchanged). Used for `DisplayInfo::align`.
- `pub fn rows(&self, max_rows: i32) -> twine_core::RowChunks` — Iterates over horizontal bands of at most `max_rows` rows, top to bottom, covering the rectangle exactly. `max_rows <= 0` yields nothing (and logs a warning).
- `pub const fn split_at_y(&self, y: i32) -> (twine_core::Rect, twine_core::Rect)` — Splits at row `y` (clamped into the rectangle) into `(top, bottom)`.
- `pub const fn corners(&self) -> [twine_core::Point; 4]` — Corner coordinates clockwise from the top-left: `(x0,y0) (x1,y0) (x1,y1) (x0,y1)`. These are edge coordinates (`x1`, `y1` exclusive), as used for transforms.
- `pub fn subtract(&self, other: &twine_core::Rect) -> twine_core::SmallRects` — Up to 4 non-overlapping rectangles covering `self \ other` (no allocation).
- `pub const fn rotate_in(&self, rotation: twine_core::Rotation, w: i32, h: i32) -> twine_core::Rect` — Maps a rectangle of a logical `w × h` screen to the physical panel for software rotation (same convention as LVGL `lv_display_rotate_area`; `w`, `h` are the *logical* size): - 90°: `(x, y) → (y, w − 1 − x)` - 180°: `(x, y) → (w − 1 − x, h − 1 − y)` - 270°: `(x, y) → (h − 1 − y, x)`
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_core::RowChunks
Iterator returned by `Rect::rows`.
Implements: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Iterator

#### struct twine_core::SmallRects
Up to four rectangles without allocation (result of `Rect::subtract`). Empty rectangles are never stored.
Implements: Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Iterator, ExactSizeIterator

### mod twine_core::alloc_guard

The allocation guard: detects heap allocation by Twine after start-up ("seal").

A safety case for a fixed-memory product claims that after start-up the UI allocates
nothing: everything it needs was sized from `Limits` and reserved while
the `Ui` was built. Sealing makes that claim checkable at run time:

1. The application builds its UI, then calls `Ui::seal()` (or `seal` directly), which
   seals the UI's `Partition`.
2. From then on, every **growth point** of Twine that is about to allocate — a vector at
   capacity, a new reactive node, a new widget — calls `note` (or `grew`), which counts
   the allocation and remembers its `AllocSite`.
3. The `Ui` turns the count into a
   `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` record at its next
   update (`code` = the last site), through the normal fault stream.

The allocation itself still happens: refusing it would lose data or break an invariant.
The fault is the evidence that the claim did not hold, and where.

**Why a guard instead of an allocator hook**

Twine does not choose the global allocator (platform rule 3), so it cannot see allocations.
The guard is Twine-internal and independent of the allocator: each growth point checks
whether it is about to allocate (`len == capacity`, or a creation that boxes a value) and
only then reads the seal flag, in a `#[cold]` function. Paths that stay within capacity
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite
A growth point of Twine: where an allocation after `seal` happened (the `code` of a `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal` record).
Variants:
- `ArenaSlots = 1` — An `Arena`'s slot storage grew.
- `ArenaFreeList = 2` — An `Arena`'s free lists grew (a value was removed).
- `SmallVec = 3` — A `SmallVec` spilled to the heap or its heap buffer grew.
- `ReactiveNode = 10` — A reactive node (signal, memo, stored value, effect) was created.
- `ReactiveScope = 11` — A reactive scope was created, or a scope's child/node list grew.
- `ReactiveCleanup = 12` — A cleanup was registered on a scope.
- `ReactiveContext = 13` — A context value was provided on a scope.
- `EffectQueue = 14` — An effect queue (pending or deferred) grew.
- `ReactiveEdges = 15` — A dependency edge list (subscribers, sources) grew.
- `ChannelHandler = 16` — A channel handler was registered (`on_message`).
- `ReactiveScratch = 17` — The runtime's propagation stack grew.
- `Waker = 18` — The waker pool allocated a heap waker.
- `Animation = 20` — An animation was started into a full animation table.
- `Timer = 21` — A timer was added into a full timer table.
- `Widget = 22` — A widget (engine node) was created.
- `Handler = 23` — An event handler was registered.
- `FocusGroup = 24` — A focus group was created or a group's member list grew.
- `EngineScratch = 25` — An engine scratch or queue grew (posted events, invalidations, layout, scroll into view, style transitions).
- `DeleteScratch = 26` — The delete scratch (post-order of a deleted subtree) grew.
- `StyleProps = 27` — A style's property list (`StyleBuf`: a node's local style, a shared style) grew: a property was set on it for the first time.
- `ThemeClass = 28` — The engine's theme-class side table (variants and roles, `Engine::set_theme_class`) grew (reserved for `Limits::max_theme_classes` with `preallocate`).
- `Text = 30` — A widget's text buffer grew (label — with its password-mode and shaped copies —, checkbox, span, button-matrix button and popover, owned dropdown/roller options).
- `WidgetBuffer = 31` — A widget's private table grew, or a static table became an owned copy (button-matrix buttons, a span group's spans and line layout).
- `EngineQueue = 40` — A `Ui`'s engine-command ring was (re)allocated.
- `NavStack = 41` — A navigator's route or page stack grew.
- `Reconcile = 42` — A keyed collection's (`for_each`, `virtual_list`) row list or reconcile scratch grew (kept between changes; reserved for `Limits::max_list_items` with `preallocate`).
Methods of `AllocSite`:
- `pub const fn code(self) -> u32` — The stable numeric code.
- `pub const fn from_code(code: u32) -> Option<twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite>` — The site with `code` (`None` for an unknown code).
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The site's name, as written in the source.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocReport
Allocations noted since the last `take`: how many, and the last growth point.
Fields:
- `count: u32` — Allocations noted (saturating).
- `last: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite` — The growth point of the last one.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::seal
`pub fn seal(p: twine_core::Partition)`
Seals partition `p`: from now on every growth point of `p` that allocates is noted (see the module docs). Clears the counts of an earlier seal of `p`. Idempotent apart from that; other partitions are unaffected. Usually called through `Ui::seal`, which also checks the heap budget and seals its own partition. Never panics.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::unseal
`pub fn unseal(p: twine_core::Partition)`
Ends the seal of partition `p` (e.g. before a planned reconfiguration, or at the end of a test). The counts stay readable (`total`). Never panics.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::is_sealed
`pub fn is_sealed(p: twine_core::Partition) -> bool`
Whether partition `p` is sealed (one load).

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::note
`pub fn note(p: twine_core::Partition, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
Notes that the growth point `site` of partition `p` allocates now — when `p` is sealed (one load otherwise). For operations that always allocate (creating a node boxes its value). Never panics.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::grew
`pub fn grew(p: twine_core::Partition, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
Notes that the growth point `site` of partition `p` allocated (its storage just grew) — when `p` is sealed. For the cold branch of a growth point that already knows it grows. Never panics.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::before_push
`pub fn before_push(p: twine_core::Partition, len: usize, cap: usize, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
Notes `site` of partition `p` when a container of length `len` and capacity `cap` is about to grow by one (`len == cap`): the check a growth point makes before a push. Inline; the noting is cold.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::push
`pub fn push<T>(p: twine_core::Partition, v: &mut Vec<T>, value: T, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
`v.push(value)`, noting `site` of partition `p` when the push grows the vector (see `before_push`).

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::push_back
`pub fn push_back<T>(p: twine_core::Partition, q: &mut VecDeque<T>, value: T, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
`q.push_back(value)`, noting `site` of partition `p` when the push grows the queue.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::reserve
`pub fn reserve<T>(p: twine_core::Partition, v: &mut Vec<T>, additional: usize, site: twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocSite)`
Reserves room for `additional` more elements, noting `site` of partition `p` when that allocates.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::take
`pub fn take(p: twine_core::Partition) -> Option<twine_core::alloc_guard::AllocReport>`
The allocations noted in partition `p` since the last call (or since `seal`), clearing them; `None` when there were none. Each `Ui` calls it for its partition at every update and raises `FaultKind::AllocAfterSeal`. Never panics.

#### fn twine_core::alloc_guard::total
`pub fn total(p: twine_core::Partition) -> u32`
Allocations noted in partition `p` since its last `seal` (not cleared by `take`; saturating).

### mod twine_core::arena

Generational arena (`Arena<T>`) with stale-handle detection (`Id<T>`).

#### const twine_core::arena::MAX_GENERATION
`pub const MAX_GENERATION: twine_core::Generation = repr::MAX_GENERATION`
The last `Generation` a slot serves: `u16::MAX` by default, `2⁴⁸ − 2³² − 1` (`0xFFFE_FFFF_FFFF`) in the safety profile. The safety value leaves out the generations whose top 16 bits are all ones, so the handle's niche (`Option<Id>` is as small as `Id`) costs no range worth mentioning.

#### fn twine_core::arena::next_generation
`pub const fn next_generation(g: twine_core::Generation) -> Option<twine_core::Generation>`
The generation after `g`, or `None` when `g` is `MAX_GENERATION` or beyond (the slot must then retire, never wrap). For tables that keep generations of their own (e.g. the animation timeline). Never panics; O(1).

Re-exports in `twine_core::arena`:
- `Generation` — same as `twine_core::Generation`
- `RawId` — same as `twine_core::RawId`
- `Id` — same as `twine_core::Id`
- `Arena` — same as `twine_core::Arena`

### mod twine_core::audit

Configuration evidence: a stable, machine-readable `key=value` dump of everything that bounds
or configures Twine (`Audit`, `AuditSink`, `AuditValue`, `KeyValues`).

A certification or audit file needs the configuration a product actually runs with — every
limit, cache budget, timeout, feature and profile flag — in a form a tool can diff against
the reviewed one. Each configuration type implements `Audit`: it **visits** its entries
(`section`, `key`, `AuditValue`) into an `AuditSink`. Nothing is formatted or allocated
unless a sink does so, and the formatting code is linked only when the application calls
it (pay for what you use).

**Format**

`KeyValues` (`Display`, and `defmt::Format` with the `defmt` feature) writes one entry per
line:


- `section` and `key` are `snake_case` ASCII; a key never changes meaning once released, new
  keys are appended, removed keys are not reused.
- Values: unsigned and signed integers in decimal, `true` / `false`, text verbatim (names
  only, never containing `=` or a line break), and `none` for an absent optional value.
- Units are part of the key (`_us` microseconds, `_bytes` bytes); counts have no suffix.
- The order of the entries is the visiting order and is stable for a given build.

The view layer's `AppConfig::audit_report()` is the complete report of an application
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### enum twine_core::audit::AuditValue<'a>
One configuration value of an audit report.
Variants:
- `Uint(u64)` — An unsigned integer (counts, sizes, durations in the key's unit).
- `Int(i64)` — A signed integer.
- `Bool(bool)` — A flag.
- `Text(&'a str)` — A name (a theme, a mode, an enum variant). Never contains `=` or a line break.
- `Absent` — An optional value that is not set (written `none`).
Methods of `AuditValue`:
- `pub fn from_usize(v: usize) -> Self` — A `usize` as `Uint` (saturating on targets where `usize` is wider than 64 bits).
- `pub fn opt_usize(v: Option<usize>) -> Self` — An optional `usize`: `Uint` or `Absent`.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display

#### trait twine_core::audit::AuditSink
`pub trait AuditSink`
Receives the entries of an audit report (see the module docs for the format).
Items:
- `fn entry(&mut self, section: &str, key: &str, value: twine_core::audit::AuditValue<'_>)` — One entry: `section.key = value`.

#### trait twine_core::audit::Audit
`pub trait Audit`
A configuration that can describe itself to an `AuditSink`.
Items:
- `fn audit(&self, out: &mut dyn twine_core::audit::AuditSink)` — Visits every entry, in a stable order. Never allocates; never panics.
Implemented by: twine_core::Limits

#### fn twine_core::audit::digest
`pub fn digest<T: twine_core::audit::Audit + ?Sized>(report: &T) -> twine_core::Crc32`
The CRC-32 (`Crc32`) of the text `KeyValues` writes for `report` (every `section.key=value` line with its line break, in visiting order), computed without building the text: a short configuration digest to log, display on a service screen or compare with the reviewed configuration's. Never allocates; links the value formatting.

#### struct twine_core::audit::KeyValues<'a, T: twine_core::audit::Audit + ?Sized>
The `section.key=value` text of an `Audit` value (one line per entry): `Display`, and `defmt::Format` with the `defmt` feature.
Fields:
- `0: &'a T`
Implements: Display, Debug

### mod twine_core::color

Colors: the canonical `Color` (RGB888), opacity (`Opa`), the runtime format tag
(`ColorFormat`), typed pixel formats (`PixelFormat`) and the WCAG contrast ratio
(`ContrastRatio`, `Color::contrast_ratio`).

Every blend uses `mix_channel`: `udiv255(fg·a + bg·(255 − a))` — floor division by 255,
exact at `a = 0` and `a = 255`. This formula is normative for deterministic rendering (P6).

#### struct twine_core::color::ContrastRatio
A contrast ratio between two colors as defined by WCAG 2.x: `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` for the relative luminances `L1 ≥ L2`, from 1:1 (equal luminance) to 21:1 (black on white). Stored in hundredths, rounded **down**, so a ratio that compares `>=` a requirement really meets it.
Methods of `ContrastRatio`:
- `const MIN: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — 1:1, two colors of the same luminance.
- `const MAX: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — 21:1, black on white.
- `const WCAG_NON_TEXT: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — 3:1, WCAG 2.x's minimum for large text and for user-interface components and graphical objects (success criteria 1.4.3 and 1.4.11).
- `const WCAG_AA: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — 4.5:1, WCAG 2.x level AA for normal text (success criterion 1.4.3).
- `const WCAG_AAA: twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — 7:1, WCAG 2.x level AAA for normal text (success criterion 1.4.6).
- `pub const fn from_hundredths(hundredths: u16) -> twine_core::color::ContrastRatio` — The ratio `hundredths / 100` (`450` is 4.5:1), clamped to `1:1 ..= 21:1`.
- `pub const fn hundredths(self) -> u16` — The ratio in hundredths (`450` for 4.5:1).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Display

#### struct twine_core::color::A8
8-bit alpha-only format (not a `PixelFormat`; used for masks and glyphs).
Methods of `A8`:
- `pub fn get(row: &[u8], x: usize) -> twine_core::Opa` — The alpha of pixel `x` in `row`; out of range → transparent.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::color::Argb8888
32-bit `0xAA_RR_GG_BB` with straight alpha, little-endian (memory `B, G, R, A`).
Methods of `Argb8888`:
- `pub const fn from_color_opa(c: twine_core::Color, opa: twine_core::Opa) -> u32` — Raw value of `c` with opacity `opa` as alpha.
- `pub const fn alpha(raw: u32) -> twine_core::Opa` — The alpha of a raw value.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### struct twine_core::color::I1
1-bit format, most significant bit first (like LVGL; not a `PixelFormat`).
Methods of `I1`:
- `pub fn get(row: &[u8], x: usize) -> bool` — Bit `x` of `row` (MSB first); out of range → `false`.
- `pub fn set(row: &mut [u8], x: usize, v: bool)` — Sets bit `x` of `row` (MSB first); out of range is ignored with a warning.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### struct twine_core::color::L8
8-bit luminance; converts to gray.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### struct twine_core::color::Rgb565
RGB565, little-endian in memory.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### struct twine_core::color::Rgb565Swapped
RGB565 with swapped bytes: `raw = rgb565.swap_bytes()`, so the **memory bytes are big-endian** and an SPI panel receives the high byte first without a conversion pass.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### struct twine_core::color::Rgb888
24-bit RGB stored as `[B, G, R]` (like LVGL).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### struct twine_core::color::Xrgb8888
32-bit `0xFF_RR_GG_BB` (alpha byte ignored on read, written as `0xFF`), little-endian.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PixelFormat

#### fn twine_core::color::expand_alpha
`pub const fn expand_alpha(v: u8, bpp: u8) -> u8`
Expands a `bpp`-bit alpha to 8 bits (1 → 0/255, 2 → ×85, 4 → ×17, 8 → unchanged).

#### fn twine_core::color::unpack_bits
`pub fn unpack_bits(row: &[u8], bpp: u8, x: usize) -> u8`
Raw value of pixel `x` in a row of `bpp`-bit pixels (1, 2, 4 packed MSB first; 8 = bytes). Other depths and out-of-range pixels return 0.

#### fn twine_core::color::mix_channel
`pub const fn mix_channel(fg: u8, bg: u8, a: u8) -> u8`
Blends one 8-bit channel: `udiv255(fg·a + bg·(255 − a))`.

Re-exports in `twine_core::color`:
- `ColorFormat` — same as `twine_core::ColorFormat`
- `PixelFormat` — same as `twine_core::PixelFormat`
- `Opa` — same as `twine_core::Opa`
- `Color` — same as `twine_core::Color`

### mod twine_core::crc

`Crc32`: the CRC-32 checksum (IEEE 802.3) used for display-integrity checks and digests.

Twine's display-integrity mechanisms (an independent monitor checking what reached the
panel, the off-screen re-render of a safety-critical node, the configuration digest of the
audit report) need one checksum that every part computes the same way, on every target,
without floating point, `unsafe` or allocation. This is the standard CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3,
zlib, PNG, Ethernet: reflected polynomial `0xEDB88320`, initial value and final XOR
`0xFFFF_FFFF`), so a monitor written in another language, or a tool on a host, gets the
same value.

**Size vs speed.** The table holds one nibble (16 × 4 bytes = 64 bytes of flash) instead of
the usual byte table (1 KiB): two lookups per byte, about 4× faster than the bitwise loop
and 16× smaller than the byte table. A checksum is computed only where an integrity check
asks for it (never on the render path unless an observer does it), so the small table is
the better trade on a microcontroller.

Re-exports in `twine_core::crc`:
- `Crc32` — same as `twine_core::Crc32`

### mod twine_core::error

The crate error type.

Re-exports in `twine_core::error`:
- `Error` — same as `twine_core::Error`

### mod twine_core::fault

Faults: the vocabulary every Twine crate uses to report a failure that the library recovered
from but that may leave the display wrong, stale or incomplete (`FaultKind`, `Faults`).

A fault is not an error returned to a caller: it is something that went wrong while Twine was
working on its own (drawing, flushing, running bindings) and that the application must be able
to observe. Twine provides the **mechanism** — every fault is raised, counted and reported
through one hook — and leaves the **policy** to the application: how severe a fault is, how to
react (retry, show a fail-safe screen, reset) and how to report it depends on the product and
the standard it follows, so Twine assigns no severities.

The crates that detect faults record them where they occur (the engine in its fault state,
the reactive runtime in its own); the view layer's `Ui` merges them into one stream.

#### enum twine_core::fault::CapacityFault
The bound named by a `FaultKind::Capacity` record (its `code`): which limit was reached.
Variants:
- `Nodes = 0` — The widget tree is full (`Limits::max_nodes`, at most 65 535): the node was not created. `node` = the parent, if any.
- `EngineQueue = 1` — A `Ui`'s engine command queue was full (`Limits::engine_queue`): engine side effects issued without the engine (a scope disposed or a handle called outside `Ui::update`) were dropped. `display` set; `occurrences` = their number.
- `WakerPool = 2` — The process-wide waker pool was exhausted when a `Ui` was mounted (`Limits::max_heap_wakers`): it got the shared fallback waker instead of its own, so channel and interrupt wake-ups are no longer routed to this UI alone. `display` set.
- `ReactiveNodes = 3` — The reactive runtime's node bound was reached (`Limits::max_reactive_nodes`: signals, memos, stored values and effects): with `no-panic-runtime` the creation was skipped and returned a handle that is never alive (without it, the creation panics). Forwarded by the `Ui`; `occurrences` = the skipped creations.
- `ReactiveScopes = 4` — The reactive runtime's scope bound was reached (`Limits::max_scopes`), as for `ReactiveNodes`.
- `PendingEffects = 5` — More effects waited to run than `Limits::max_pending_effects`: the effects beyond it were not queued (like an effect-loop cut, the bindings concerned may show outdated values until their sources change again). Forwarded by the `Ui`; `occurrences` = the effects not queued.
- `TreeDepth = 6` — A node would have been deeper than `Limits::max_tree_depth` below its root: the creation or move was refused. `node` = the parent.
- `TextLen = 7` — A widget text was longer than `Limits::max_text_len` bytes: it was cut at the last character boundary that fits. `node` = the widget.
- `Handlers = 8` — The engine's event handlers reached `Limits::max_handlers`: the handler was not added. `node` = the node it was for.
- `Timers = 9` — The engine's timers reached `Limits::max_timers`: the timer was not added (its id never resolves).
- `Animations = 10` — The engine's running animations reached `Limits::max_anims`: the animation was not started (its id never resolves).
- `FocusGroups = 11` — More focus groups than the engine's fixed `MAX_GROUPS`: the group was not created.
- `NavDepth = 12` — A navigator's route stack reached `Limits::max_nav_depth`: the push was refused (the current page stays).
- `HeapBudget = 13` — The heap Twine reports for a `Ui` (`MemoryReport::heap_bytes`) exceeded `Limits::heap_budget` when the `Ui` was sealed. `occurrences` = 1; nothing was refused (the memory is in use), the record is evidence.
- `ListItems = 14` — A keyed collection had more rows to show than its bound (`Limits::max_list_items`, or a smaller per-collection bound): the items beyond it were not shown (a `for_each` shows the first ones, a `virtual_list` the first visible ones). `node` = the collection.
- `ThemeClasses = 15` — The nodes with a theme class of their own reached `Limits::max_theme_classes`: the variant or role was not set and the node keeps its widget class's look. `node` = the node.
Methods of `CapacityFault`:
- `const ALL: [twine_core::fault::CapacityFault; 16]` — Every bound, in code order.
- `pub const fn code(self) -> u32` — The stable numeric code (the fault record's `code`).
- `pub const fn from_code(code: u32) -> Option<twine_core::fault::CapacityFault>` — The bound with code `code` (`None` for an unknown code).
- `pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str` — The bound's name, as written in the source (`"Nodes"`, …).
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Display

Re-exports in `twine_core::fault`:
- `FaultKind` — same as `twine_core::FaultKind`
- `Faults` — same as `twine_core::Faults`
- `FaultCounts` — same as `twine_core::FaultCounts`

### mod twine_core::limits

`Limits`: the memory bounds of a Twine application, in one value.

Every structure of Twine that grows with the application — the widget tree, the reactive
graph, event handlers, timers, animations, queues, the navigation stack, keyed lists, the
nodes' theme classes, the waker pool —
is bounded by a field of `Limits`. Reaching a bound is a
`FaultKind::Capacity` fault whose code
(`CapacityFault`) names the field, and the operation is
refused, cut or dropped: **Twine never grows past a limit**. The checks sit at the insertion
points, which already branch on "is there room", so they cost nothing on hot paths.

With `preallocate` the storage of the bounded structures is reserved
up front, when the `Ui` (or the engine and the runtime) is configured, so that staying
within the limits never allocates; together with sealing
(`alloc_guard`, `Ui::seal`) this is the evidence that the application
runs in a fixed amount of memory after start-up.

The view layer's `AppConfig::limits` holds the application's value; the builders apply it to
the engine (`Engine::set_limits`), the reactive runtime (`Runtime::set_limits`) and the
waker pool. `Limits::summary` (and the complete `AppConfig::audit_report`) dump it for
audit evidence.

Re-exports in `twine_core::limits`:
- `Limits` — same as `twine_core::Limits`

### mod twine_core::log

Logging facade: `trace!`, `debug!`, `info!`, `warn!` and `error!`.

The same call syntax works with every backend:


**Backends**

The backend is chosen by cargo features of `twine-core` (the choice is made where the macros
are *defined*, so it applies uniformly to every crate that uses them):

| Features            | Backend | Behaviour |
|---------------------|---------|-----------|
| none                | `none`  | arguments are type-checked but never evaluated; no code is emitted |
| `log`               | `log`   | forwards to `log::log!` with the given target (default `"twine"`) |
| `defmt` (± `log`)   | `defmt` | forwards to `defmt`; **`defmt` wins when both are enabled** |

With `defmt` the `target:` is **dropped** (defmt needs literal format strings and records the
module path itself); messages that need an area start with a short `[area]` prefix instead.
Because defmt's macros expand to `::defmt::…` paths, every crate that enables its own `defmt`
feature must also depend on `defmt` directly:
`defmt = ["dep:defmt", "twine-core/defmt"]`.

Only `{}` and `{:?}` placeholders are portable across backends; every logged type implements
`Display`/`Debug` and, with `defmt`, `defmt::Format`.
(… see the full docs in rustdoc)

#### const twine_core::log::TARGETS
`pub const TARGETS: &[&str]`
The allowed log target strings.

#### const twine_core::log::BACKEND
`pub const BACKEND: &str = "none"`
The compiled logging backend: `"defmt"`, `"log"` or `"none"`.

Re-exports in `twine_core::log`:
- `debug` — same as `twine_core::debug`
- `error` — same as `twine_core::error`
- `error` — same as `twine_core::error`
- `info` — same as `twine_core::info`
- `trace` — same as `twine_core::trace`
- `warn` — same as `twine_core::warn`

### mod twine_core::math

Deterministic integer math: `Fx` (16.16 fixed point), `Angle` (0.1°), `Scale`
(256 = 1.0), `Fraction` (0..=1), `AngularSpeed`, integer square roots, trigonometry,
shared 128-bit division (`div_rem_i128`) and small helpers.

Nothing here uses floating point (P5), so results are bit-identical on every target (P6).

#### const twine_core::math::CUBIC_BEZIER_ONE
`pub const CUBIC_BEZIER_ONE: i32 = 1024`
1.0 in the bezier functions' fixed-point scale (LVGL `LV_BEZIER_VAL_MAX`).

#### fn twine_core::math::bezier3
`pub const fn bezier3(t: u16, u0: i32, u1: i32, u2: i32, u3: i32) -> i32`
One-dimensional cubic Bezier with control values `u0..u3` at time `t` (`0..=1024`, larger values are clamped): `u0·(1−t)³ + 3·u1·(1−t)²·t + 3·u2·(1−t)·t² + u3·t³` (the general Bernstein form of LVGL's `lv_bezier3`, evaluated exactly and rounded once instead of LVGL's per-term truncation).

#### fn twine_core::math::cubic_bezier
`pub fn cubic_bezier(x: i32, x1: i32, y1: i32, x2: i32, y2: i32) -> i32`
CSS-style `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` easing evaluated at `x` (port of LVGL `lv_cubic_bezier`; all values scaled by 1024). Solves `t` for `x` with Newton iterations, falling back to bisection, and returns `y(t)`.

#### struct twine_core::math::SqrtRes
Result of `sqrt`: integer part and an 8-bit binary fraction (`value ≈ i + f/256`).
Fields:
- `i: u16` — Integer part.
- `f: u8` — Fraction in 1/256.
Implements: Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash

#### fn twine_core::math::isqrt64
`pub const fn isqrt64(x: u64) -> u32`
Floor of the square root of `x` (exact digit-by-digit algorithm, no floating point).

#### fn twine_core::math::sqrt
`pub const fn sqrt(x: u32) -> twine_core::math::SqrtRes`
Square root with an 8-bit fraction, like LVGL `lv_sqrt` (bitwise, exact: `i·256 + f = ⌊√x · 256⌋`).

#### fn twine_core::math::sqrt_fx
`pub fn sqrt_fx(x: twine_core::Fx) -> twine_core::Fx`
Square root of a fixed-point number (floor in 1/65536). Negative inputs return zero and log a warning.

#### const twine_core::math::TRIG_MAX
`pub const TRIG_MAX: i32 = 32_767`
Largest value returned by `sin`/`cos` (`sin(90°)`).

#### const twine_core::math::TRIG_SHIFT
`pub const TRIG_SHIFT: u32 = 15`
Shift that normalizes `sin`/`cos` results (`>> TRIG_SHIFT`).

#### fn twine_core::math::atan2
`pub const fn atan2(y: i32, x: i32) -> twine_core::Angle`
Angle of the vector `(x, y)` in `0..3600` (`(0, 0)` → 0). Integer CORDIC in vectoring mode (16 iterations, inputs pre-scaled to 30 bits); accurate to 1 decidegree.

#### fn twine_core::math::cos
`pub const fn cos(a: twine_core::Angle) -> i32`
Cosine scaled to `−32767..=32767` (`cos(a) = sin(a + 90°)`).

#### fn twine_core::math::cos_fx
`pub const fn cos_fx(a: twine_core::Angle) -> twine_core::Fx`
Cosine as fixed point (`cos_fx(0°) == Fx::ONE`).

#### fn twine_core::math::sin
`pub const fn sin(a: twine_core::Angle) -> i32`
Sine scaled to `−32767..=32767` (`>> TRIG_SHIFT` normalizes).

#### fn twine_core::math::sin_fx
`pub const fn sin_fx(a: twine_core::Angle) -> twine_core::Fx`
Sine as fixed point (`sin_fx(90°) == Fx::ONE`).

#### fn twine_core::math::div_rem_euclid_i128
`pub fn div_rem_euclid_i128(a: i128, b: i128) -> Option<(i128, i128)>`
Euclidean quotient and remainder of `a / b`: `(a.div_euclid(b), a.rem_euclid(b))` exactly as `i128::checked_div_euclid` and `i128::checked_rem_euclid` give them (the remainder is in `0..|b|`). `None` when `b == 0` or for `i128::MIN / −1`.

#### fn twine_core::math::div_rem_i128
`pub fn div_rem_i128(a: i128, b: i128) -> Option<(i128, i128)>`
Quotient and remainder of `a / b`, truncated toward zero: `(a / b, a % b)` exactly as `i128::checked_div` and `i128::checked_rem` give them. `None` when `b == 0` or for `i128::MIN / −1` (the quotient does not fit), like those methods.

#### fn twine_core::math::udiv255
`pub const fn udiv255(x: u32) -> u32`
`x / 255` (floor) without a division; exact for every `x <= 65 535`.

#### fn twine_core::math::map
`pub const fn map(v: i32, in_min: i32, in_max: i32, out_min: i32, out_max: i32) -> i32`
Maps `v` from `[in_min, in_max]` to `[out_min, out_max]`, clamped (port of LVGL `lv_map`).

#### fn twine_core::math::clamp
`pub const fn clamp(v: i32, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32`
Clamps `v` into `[lo, hi]`. Unlike `Ord::clamp` it never panics: if `lo > hi` the result is `lo`.

#### fn twine_core::math::lerp_i32
`pub const fn lerp_i32(a: i32, b: i32, t: u16) -> i32`
Linear interpolation `a + (b − a)·t/1024` with `t` in `0..=1024` (values above 1024 extrapolate), rounded half up. `t = 0` gives `a`, `t = 1024` gives `b` exactly.

Re-exports in `twine_core::math`:
- `Fx` — same as `twine_core::Fx`
- `Scale` — same as `twine_core::Scale`
- `Angle` — same as `twine_core::Angle`
- `AngularSpeed` — same as `twine_core::AngularSpeed`
- `Fraction` — same as `twine_core::Fraction`

### mod twine_core::partition

`Partition`: the identity of a partitioned runtime (ADR-001, `docs/design/adr-001-partitioned-runtimes.md`).

A **partition** is one reactive runtime and every `Ui` (engine, displays, inputs) built on
it. Two partitions in one image share no mutable state: each has its own reactive arenas,
effect queue and loop cut, `Limits`, fault stream, seal domain
(`alloc_guard`), step budget, heartbeat, frame observer and fail-safe
screen. A safety-critical display and a non-critical one become independent: a loop cut,
an exhausted bound or a fault in one cannot change what the other shows or when.

The type lives in `twine-core` because both the engine and the reactive runtime need it
(like `Limits`). The runtime's token is the partition's capability
(`twine_reactive::Runtime::take_partition`); this type only names it.

**Feature `partitions`**

Partitions are opt-in. Without the feature `Partition::COUNT` is 1, the type is
zero-sized and every per-partition table has one entry, so an image with one partition
compiles to the code it had before partitions existed (no byte per handle, no slot
selection). With it, `Partition::COUNT` is 2 and a partition is one byte.

Re-exports in `twine_core::partition`:
- `Partition` — same as `twine_core::Partition`

### mod twine_core::symbol

`Symbol`: the built-in icon glyphs (LVGL `LV_SYMBOL_*`), with the exact code points of
LVGL v9 `src/font/lv_symbol_def.h` (MIT licensed, see `THIRD_PARTY.md`).

The Font Awesome symbols are merged into the built-in Montserrat fonts (the font generator
takes its symbol list from `Symbol::ALL`), so a symbol is text: it is an image source
(`ImageSource::from(Symbol::Ok)` in `twine-image`) and it formats into strings without
allocating (`format!("{} Save", Symbol::Save)`, or `text!` in `twine-view`).

`Symbol` is one byte; `Symbol::as_str` is a `const fn` lookup in a static table, so
`Symbol::Ok.as_str()` also works in `const`/`static` tables (keyboard maps, static image
sources).

Re-exports in `twine_core::symbol`:
- `Symbol` — same as `twine_core::Symbol`

### mod twine_core::validity

`Validity`: a value together with how much it can be trusted, and its
`ValidityStatus`.

A display that shows measured data must never show a wrong value as if it were right: a
sensor that stopped reporting, a value that is too old, a failed computation must look
different from a valid reading. `Validity<T>` carries that information from the data source
to the widget: the view layer turns it into the standard look (the value, the value marked
as stale, or dashes with a cross-hatch) and the producer decides only what it knows (a
value, a failure, nothing yet). Freshness is added by the consumer
(`ScopeExt::watch_fresh` in `twine-view`), which knows the time.

Re-exports in `twine_core::validity`:
- `Validity` — same as `twine_core::Validity`
- `ValidityStatus` — same as `twine_core::ValidityStatus`
